EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very deep closed upper low moved through the mid and deep south resulting in a significant severe weather outbreak across the deep south and southeast.  Georgia was on the eastern edge of this outbreak because much of north and central Georgia remained in a wedge of cooler air.  However, a nose of warm, moist air from central and southern Alabama worked its way into the Columbus area of west central Georgia.  Dewpoints in the Columbus area rose into the lower 60s helping to fuel the environment in that region for strong storms.   A strong squall line of thunderstorms from central and southern Alabama worked its way into west central Georgia shortly after noon, spawning a tornado in the Fort Benning area.  The line of thunderstorms weakened considerably as it moved further east into the cooler, more stable air.  Thus, little severe weather was reported further east.|In addition to the severe weather, rainfall of two to four inches across much of north and west Georgia resulted in several street flooding incidents, especially in the Columbus area.  Strong winds, particularly at the higher elevations in the north Georgia counties, resulted in a number of trees being blown down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface low pressure system that lingered around to the Northwest of the U.S. Virgin Islands combined with a mid to upper level trough. The outcome of these systems as they interacted with very moist unstable air and local effects as usual was heavy rain and flooding. The worst of the flooding was reported in St.Croix. The rainfall was of the ���pulsing��� variety with some areas experiencing periods of torrential downpours starting late on October 18th and ending of October 20th.  The flooding in St. Croix, resulted in school and business closings. There were reports of flash flooding throughout the entire island but the worst was in the western suburbs of Christiansted.  VITEMA (Virgin Islands Emergency Management Agency) also reported people trapped in flooded vehicles, road and highway washouts and ���popping��� manhole covers. Although the St. Thomas ASOS monthly rainfall total was close to normal, St. Croix was much wetter than normal.  At the USGS gage at Jolly Hill, St. Croix, on the north side of Fredericksted, the 3 day rainfall total for October 19 through October 21 was 10.22 inches.

In Monroe county, two men were slightly injured when struck by lightning. In Pittsford, the man was working on siding. In Penfield, the man was a cable company employee. Both men were standing on ladders.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved through central Indiana during the afternoon and early evening hours of August 6, 2007.  The main damage was caused by damaging thunderstorm winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and downed power lines at the corner of Brown-Delaware and 11th streets.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck several homes in York County.  Quick responses from homeowners, neighbors, and fire departments kept damages to a minimum.  Homes were struck in York Harbor, York, North Berwick and also in Cape Elizabeth in Cumberland County.  The most severe damage was to a large oceanfront home in York Harbor where lightning put two holes in the roof and ignited a fire which caused heavy damage to an upstairs bedroom.  Damage was estimated at $8000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms containing numerous lightning strikes moved across central Indiana on the afternoon and evening of June 28th.  Lightning struck a barn causing it to catch fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and destroyed a large barn that contained $14,000 worth of hay and farm equipment.  The barn was located near County Road 300 East and County Road 400 South.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms, some containing heavy rain, moved across central Indiana on the evening of June 27th.  The main damage was caused by thunderstorm winds and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Greenfield Police Department and damaged computers, a recorder, and the 911 system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms containing damaging thunderstorm winds and heavy rain moved through central Indiana on the evening of August 24, 2007.  In addition, lightning struck Noblesville High School.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Noblesville High School causing damage to the roof and three classrooms.  Damage was caused by the flames of the fire and the smoke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very hot and humid conditions prevailed across Southern New England on the 27th of June. This in combination with a prefrontal trough aided in the development of scattered thunderstorms during the late afternoon and early evening hours. A few of the storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning injured a person in Palmer. The injuries were reported to be minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level trough and associated cold front move through the region and brought a round of severe weather, mainly to the northern portion of the forecast area. Hail and some wind damage occurred along and north of the Highway 82 corridor during the evening of the 14th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong instability, moderate to strong wind shear, and the approach of a cold front set the stage for a widespread thunderstorm outbreak across Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Rhode Island on the 16th. The main result was wind damage to trees and power lines. This was the most widespread severe thunderstorm event of May 2007.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a large house fire at 41 Bicentennial Drive in Leominster on the 16th. A family pet (dog) was killed in the fire. The fire caused nearly $300,000 in damage to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across southern Nebraska around daybreak.  Lightning apparently damaged a power substation insulator, resulting in power outages.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning apparently struck an insulator at the Beverly, Nebraska substation, resulting in power outages across Dundy and Hitchcock counties for about an hour.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across southwest Nebraska and northwest Kansas during the late morning and afternoon hours.  Dozens of reports of penny to quarter size hail were received, and isolated flash flooding occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning apparently struck a TV antenna and traveled through the electrical system of a home and ignited the wall insulation in the basement.  It took four fire trucks and 13 fire fighters to contain the fire in one hour.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the evening of June 2nd, severe storms moved through central Indiana.  Some of these storms contained 0.75 inch to 0.88 inch hail.  Damaging thunderstorm winds and lightning were also threats from these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power line pole, which fell and subsequently hit and knocked over a tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hail and damaging thunderstorm winds moved across central Indiana throughout the day of August 16, 2007.  Heavy rain also accompanied the severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Union City police department's communication system.     The storm took out the base radio and a couple of computers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved through central Indiana during the afternoon and early evening hours of August 6, 2007.  The main damage was caused by damaging thunderstorm winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a retirement home in Chesterfield.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable atmosphere developed in advance of a cold|front on the 10th. The result was strong instability which|aided in the formation of thunderstorms which produced large|hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm moved through Holden during the late afternoon hours on the 10th. Lightning struck two houses - blowing apart a chimney on one and setting fire to another. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms, some containing heavy rain, moved across central Indiana on the evening of June 27th.  The main damage was caused by thunderstorm winds and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Greater Greenfield Chamber of Commerce building during a brief thunderstorm on the evening of June 27th.  They experienced phone line problems along with other malfunctioning equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed across portions of East Texas during the mid/late afternoon hours of the 27th, producing a large swath of tree, power line, and structural damage. These storms developed well ahead of a cold front that extended from southern and eastern Oklahoma, into central Arkansas, but mainly along a differential moisture boundary that moved south across east Texas, extreme southern Arkansas, and north Louisiana. Strong surface instability, and gust fronts that developed from these storms, focused new shower and thunderstorm development, with several of these storms becoming severe. One longer lived severe thunderstorm developed over eastern Upshur County, then merged with another southward moving band of strong thunderstorms, producing widespread wind damage across eastern Upshur, much of Gregg, and northern Rusk County. The cities of Longview and Kilgore were hit hardest, with numerous trees blown down/uprooted, power lines downed, and trees falling onto homes, with at least one known injury reported. A 53-yr old man was killed on the north side of Longview when lightning struck a tree he was standing near in wake of the storm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 53 year old man was struck and killed by lightning on Cox Lane.  Victim was located approximately 25 feet from a large tree that was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low level jet, remnants of a morning complex of storms from Iowa, and increasing instability all combined to create favorable conditions for damaging winds and isolated supercells. One supercell in particular had a storm motion towards the southeast when the line it was associated with moved mainly eastward. This supercell did produce a tornado in Marshall county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 5300 block of E 100 S in Portland. Heavy damage was reported to the upstairs. A County deputy was able to awake the residents and get them to safety. Damage is estimated at $50,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several severe storms affected western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A sheriff���s deputy received minor injuries from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms caused wind damage across southwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church near Prichard.  The strike started a fire and the church was destroyed by the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning near Wiggins.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning in Wiggins.  The strike caused a fire in the hot water heater.  The fire was contained to a small area.  The home still suffered considerable smoke and water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low over the northeastern Gulf of Mexico along with moist southerly flow over South Florida produced afternoon thunderstorms across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A maintenance building in Lauderhill was destroyed by a fire believed to have been caused by lightning. The 2,000 square foot building was a total loss.||Witnesses reported seeing lightning and looked outside to see the building on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the late evening into the overnight hours. A cloud to ground strike caused injuries to some teenagers attending a concert.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four teenagers were camping at a music festival at a local college and sought shelter under a tree, which was struck by lightning. The teeneages were indirectly injured from the strike. They ranged in age from 14 to 19. Two were admitted to a local hospital in fair conditions, with the other two being treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the heating of the day across portions of northeast Texas. An isolated thunderstorm developed in eastern Bowie County and caused a lightning strike that hit a home west of Texarkana, Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home west of town resulting in a house fire.  Moderate damage was reported.  No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong sea-breeze boundary moved quickly northward out of southeast Texas and southwest Louisiana during the afternoon hours of the 26th.  A strong line of thunderstorms developed along the leading edge of the boundary causing sporadic strong winds that downed a few trees and power lines across portions of northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana.  Cloud to ground lightning was very intense as well and lightning resulted in scattered power outages in southwest Arkansas and northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroyed a power pole and knocked down power lines at the 2900 block of Robertson Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed with the aid of afternoon heating across portions of southwest Arkansas on the 19th of July.  These thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning...one of which did some damage in Columbia County Arkansas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil and saltwater tank about 2 miles north of the La. state line just off Hwy. 79.  Resultant fire spread and burned 8 tanks...three of which completely melted.  Multiple fire agencies on the Louisiana and Arkansas side of the fire needed to be called in to extinguish the fire.  No injuries or evacuations were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours across northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana and quickly became severe producing large hail and damaging thunderstorm gusts. These storms were slow movers and given a very moist atmosphere present at the time across the region...flooding rainfall resulted from the storms across northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana.  A few of these storms developed into southwest Arkansas...producing wind damage as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Benton Fire Department reported two homes struck by lightning and one on fire.  Damage was moderate to extensive.  No report of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours across northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana and quickly became severe producing large hail and damaging thunderstorm gusts. These storms were slow movers and given a very moist atmosphere present at the time across the region...flooding rainfall resulted from the storms across northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana.  A few of these storms developed into southwest Arkansas...producing wind damage as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes were struck by lightning resulting in minor fires.  One home was struck in south Shreveport and the other home in southeast Shreveport.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cool front which moved into north Texas encouraged training of storms over the metroplex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a chemical plant, causing several explosions.  One man was killed in the fire that followed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system interacted with a moist and unstable airmass over north Texas, resulting in large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 4,500 square-foot building was struck by lightning and caught fire.  Damage was sustained to its roof and second floor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong sea-breeze boundary moved quickly northward out of southeast Texas and southwest Louisiana during the afternoon hours of the 26th.  A strong line of thunderstorms developed along the leading edge of the boundary causing sporadic strong winds that downed a few trees and power lines across portions of northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana.  Cloud to ground lightning was very intense as well and lightning resulted in scattered power outages in southwest Arkansas and northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer resulting in power outages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms developed across portions of southwest Arkansas with an unstable and moist airmass in place.  These thunderstorms developed along a residual outflow boundary left over from the previous days convection.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a home in Garland city burning the home to the ground.  There were no residents home at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture fueled late-season thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a drug store.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thundestorms with plenty of lightning rolled through south-central Wisconsin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a commerical peg farm near Sauk City, killing about 1900 pigs.  The exact location of the farm isn't known.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Rockdale Citizen of Conyers reported that lightning struck a home on Georgia Highway 20 entering the house via metallic water and gas lines.  A portion of the floor of the home was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gainesville Times reported that lightning struck several trees on McEver Road, toppling them and causing them to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: June 25th proved to be one of the more significant severe weather days during the month.  This was the result of a strong short wave in westerly flow aloft and a very unstable and moist atmosphere present over the area.  Damaging downburst winds, large hail, and most significantly a number of lightning incidents were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Hall County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a building in the city causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Short lines of severe thunderstorms moved east-northeast through south-central and southeast Wisconsin during the overnight hours.  Some cell movement exceeded 43 kts (50 mph) to the east.  Powerful downburst winds reached hurricane-force at 64 knots or higher (74 mph+), resulting in considerable tree and power-line damage.  Synoptically, a stationary front stretched from northern Iowa to northern Illinois.  Warm, moist, unstable air flowed north over the front in association with an upper-level short-wave trough, resulting in thunderstorm generation.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a church, started a fire, and damaged the church's sound system, computer system, and natural gas lines.  An automated fire-sprinkler system limited the amount of fire damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorm move across areas north of Highway 30 during the afternoon and evening hours of August 6th and the early morning hours of the 7th.  Heavy rains were widespread across these areas, with some isolated wind damage in Buchanan County.  Stephenson County Illinois was hardest hit with rainfall, where totals of three to seven inches fell, which lead to flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused power outages during the early morning hours of August 7th across parts of Jo Daviess County.  A transformer was damaged and needed to be replaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck homes in the Brownsburg and Fishers area as thunderstorms moved through the area during the early hours of November 11, 2007.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Brownsburg during the early morning hours.  The lightning strike set the house on fire and blew out lighting figures and outlets.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northwest flow aloft and a very warm, moist, and unstable lower atmosphere led to scattered afternoon and evening shower and thunderstorm development.  The strongest storms occurred in central sections of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Atlanta-Journal & Constitution reported that a 29-year old male was struck by lightning while doing construction work on a building in the Sandy Springs area.  Co-workers used a forklift to move him to the ground where he was treated by emergency medical technicians.  He was treated on site and then transported to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northwest flow aloft and a very warm, moist, and unstable lower atmosphere led to scattered afternoon and evening shower and thunderstorm development.  The strongest storms occurred in central sections of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Newton Citizen of Rockdale reported that lightning struck a home on Williams Road near Georgia Highway 81.  Extensive damage resulted to the attic.  The four occupants were displaced from their home.  Lightning also knocked out the power line to a home on Georgia Highway 142, but there was no fire reported that this site.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front over northeast Iowa and northern Illinois combined with an unstable air mass to produce thunderstorms during the late afternoon and  evening of June 21st.  The stronger storms produced damaging winds and large hail.  Heavy rain was also common with the storms, which caused some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning splitting it in half.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front over northeast Iowa and northern Illinois combined with an unstable air mass to produce thunderstorms during the late afternoon and  evening of June 21st.  The stronger storms produced damaging winds and large hail.  Heavy rain was also common with the storms, which caused some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning knocking the chimney off and causing some electrical wiring damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was located across central Georgia.  Meanwhile...rich tropical moisture was flowing into the region from the Gulf as Hurricane Humberto moved near the upper Texas coast.  This resulted in the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across central and north Georgia during the afternoon.  While none of these reached severe limits, they did produce frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and locally heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Georgia Department of Transportation reported that lightning struck a transformer on a power pole adjacent to interstate-85 near Fairburn.  This resulted in the attached power line falling down on the interstate.  All lanes of the interstate had to be closed while the line was repaired.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fall cold front was moving through the area from the northwest aided by a vigorous upper-level trough moving through the Ohio Valley into the mid-Atlantic region.  Scattered thunderstorms developed along the cold front during the day and spread southeastward during the afternoon and early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck the attic of a home on Tribble Gates Court within the Gwinnett county portion of Loganville.  Damage was minor to moderate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong late July cold front and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable atmosphere to produce one of the most widespread outbreaks of severe weather seen across the Peachtree City forecast area since mid-April.  The was marked by a mesoscale convective complex which began early in the day across northeast Alabama and quickly spread southeast through west central and into central Georgia during the afternoon.  Numerous reports of large hail were received and wind damage was widespread in the path of the convective complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Times Herald of Newnan reported that lightning struck a tree approximately 50 feet from a home on Tabby Lynch Road.  The lightning travelled underground on a gas line and ignited the home on fire.  The home was declared a total loss.  It took a crew of 12 firefighters 1 1/2 hours to put out the fire.  No one was home at the time of the incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: June 25th proved to be one of the more significant severe weather days during the month.  This was the result of a strong short wave in westerly flow aloft and a very unstable and moist atmosphere present over the area.  Damaging downburst winds, large hail, and most significantly a number of lightning incidents were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee County 911 Center reported that lightning set a structure and a tree on fire near Holly Springs on Hawks Club Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 30th struck two people in Pompano Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, causing a portion of the tree to break off and fall on a house in the 500 block of NW 30th Avenue, just west of the Fort Lauderdale city limits. The impact caused a 50-foot section of ceiling to collapse onto a 2-year-old boy living in the house. The boy suffered cuts and received stitches.||Water also poured into the house from the hole caused by the impact of the tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front over South Florida combined with an upper level shortwave moving east across the Florida peninsula caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop over southern portions of southeast Florida during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a 24-year old man who was laying tile on the roof of a home in western sections of Miramar. The force of the lightning knocked out a second worker, but he regained consciousness and did not require further medical attention.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: June 25th proved to be one of the more significant severe weather days during the month.  This was the result of a strong short wave in westerly flow aloft and a very unstable and moist atmosphere present over the area.  Damaging downburst winds, large hail, and most significantly a number of lightning incidents were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WSB Television of Atlanta reported that a 27-year old male construction worker was killed when struck by lightning.  The individual was working on a house under construction.  He and other workers sought shelter in the structure during the thunderstorm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: June 25th proved to be one of the more significant severe weather days during the month.  This was the result of a strong short wave in westerly flow aloft and a very unstable and moist atmosphere present over the area.  Damaging downburst winds, large hail, and most significantly a number of lightning incidents were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Bartow County Emergency Management Director reported that two structural fires occurred as a result of lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms developed over the southeast Louisiana in an unstable atmosphere as an upper trough moved across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire that severely damaged a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere as an upper level trough approached from the west.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a house in the Lake Sherwood Acres subdivision igniting a fire that caused some damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong late July cold front and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable atmosphere to produce one of the most widespread outbreaks of severe weather seen across the Peachtree City forecast area since mid-April.  The was marked by a mesoscale convective complex which began early in the day across northeast Alabama and quickly spread southeast through west central and into central Georgia during the afternoon.  Numerous reports of large hail were received and wind damage was widespread in the path of the convective complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Carroll County Emergency Management Director reported that a home was struck by lightning causing significant damage to the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably strong cold front was moving rapidly southeast through the eastern states early on the 4th.  This was supported by a very deep polar low intensifying across southeast Canada.  Very warm, humid, and unstable conditions continued in advance of this winterlike cold front.  A squall line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 3rd from the Ohio Valley into the Tennessee Valley.  This squall line continued to race out in advance of the front, reaching far north Georgia around midnight EDT and continued further south into central Georgia as a broken squall line during the early morning hours of the 4th.  Considerable wind damage occurred in association with the squall line across some north Georgia counties.  Several dozen homes were damaged in Hall county, including one blown off its foundation.  Other significant wind damage was noted in Dade and several other north Georgia counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Daily Tribune News of Cartersville reported that lightning struck a home on Euharlee-Five Forks Road.  The resulting fire was quickly contained.  Nonetheless, the home sustained moderate damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Glascock County Emergency Management Director reported that two house fires were started as a result of lightning strikes.  Damage estimates were indeterminate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong late July cold front and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable atmosphere to produce one of the most widespread outbreaks of severe weather seen across the Peachtree City forecast area since mid-April.  The was marked by a mesoscale convective complex which began early in the day across northeast Alabama and quickly spread southeast through west central and into central Georgia during the afternoon.  Numerous reports of large hail were received and wind damage was widespread in the path of the convective complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Upson County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a tree and a transformer in the city.  The transformer was blown and the tree fell down onto the roadway.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a Kroger food store.  Smoke was reported in the building, but damage was determined to be minor by the local fire department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms affected South Florida for the second day in a row due to the interaction of a weak surface trough across Central Florida and a mid to upper level trough over that same area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male construction worker was struck by lightning at a site at 4233 NW 18 Street, just east of Miami International Airport. He was treated at the site and taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms affected South Florida for the second day in a row due to the interaction of a weak surface trough across Central Florida and a mid to upper level trough over that same area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two buildings in the city of Miami. One struck an attic at 3600 NW 18 Street, and another struck a building at 2517 SW 8 Street. Minor damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The upper ridge over the southeast U.S. weakened some as a strong upper trough was moving through the Ohio Valley and northeast U.S.  A weak nearly stationary front was located across the Tennessee Valley.  These systems were close enough to combine with moisture and afternoon heating and instability to produce scattered thunderstorms once again, a few of which became severe and produced marginal severe hail and downbursts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Warren County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home.  The home was completely destroyed from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire in the attic of a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A healthy fall cold front was moving through north Georgia during the afternoon hours.  This combined with ample low-level moisture allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop.  None reached severe limits, but one in Gwinnett county did causing some lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a shed behind a home on Tina Court.  The storage shed was set on fire, causing damage to the structure and lawn equipment stored within.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and badly damaged a home in Colts Neck Township. There were no reported injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 5th that caused lightning damage in Berks County and the Lehigh Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and badly damaged the chimney of a South Whitehall Township home on 34th Street. There was no ensuing fire and no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 5th that caused lightning damage in Berks County and the Lehigh Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two-and-a-half story barn on the Christman Farm on Balthaser Road in Windsor Township. The ensuing fire gutted the structure. It took volunteers about half an hour to control the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 5th that caused lightning damage in Berks County and the Lehigh Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning rod attached to the steeple of Saint John's Lutheran Church in Boyertown absorbed most of the blast from a lightning strike during the late afternoon on the 5th. Nevertheless, the organ and air conditioning controls, one computer and pulpit microphone were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Millville home on Bayberry Court at about 550 p.m. EDT.  It started a fire around the framing of a metal chimney in the living room of the house. Damage was estimated at $25,000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching warm front helped produce severe thunderstorms and also caused some lightning damage across Eastern Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a stereo to explode in a Tilden Township home. About 1,500 homes and businesses lost power throughout the county due to the combination of damaging winds and lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary acted as a focusing mechanism for thunderstorms throughout the day on the 29th in eastern Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at about 930 a.m. EDT and the ensuing fire badly damaged the Whitehall Township municipal building. Heavy rain that also fell exacerbated the damage. More than 150 firefighters assisted in extinguishing the blaze. The roof of the building (a 20 foot by 30 foot section) partially collapsed and damaged several administrative offices, computers and phones. Some records burned. A state of emergency was declared. Damage to the building was estimated as much as one million dollars. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes in Barrett Township started separate house and shed fires. No serious injuries were reported. Lightning also struck an unoccupied hot tub in Brodheadsville (Chestnut Hill Township).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike fried the electrical wiring of a home in Lawrence Township. The lightning initially struck the air conditioning unit and then traveled through the house's wiring.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level trough moved through West Tennessee during the early morning hours of December 28th, 2007. Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with the trough. Some of the thunderstorms became severe and produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Pierce Lane Church of Christ Church in Dyersburg. The lighnting strike produced a fire that resulted in the church being destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroys a home in Lantana, and 4 condos near Crab Orchard.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning, and was fully engulfed in flames. The home was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from heavy rain producing thunderstorms struck a home causing some damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A compact upper low pressure system tracked across eastern Nebraska and western Iowa early in the afternoon on 3/31/07.  Just ahead of this system, from extreme eastern Nebraska into western Iowa, partial sunshine allowed temperatures to climb to around 70 degrees with dewpoints in the 50s, while a bit farther to the west in the Columbus and Norfolk areas, readings were in the 40s.  The contrast in temperatures and dynamics from the upper low helped kick off severe thunderstorms across the area, including at least one short-lived tornado west of Herman, Nebraska.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms that moved across the city caused at least 4 fires in the metro area. Damage to 2 of the homes was estimated at $25,000 and $15,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An outbreak of severe weather occurred across portions of northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana during the early morning hours and afternoon hours of April 25th. This weather was spawned by a strong area of low pressure in the upper levels of the atmosphere across Oklahoma and southern Kansas. Strong shear developed during the day |across the region...resulting in thunderstorms producing large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 101 year old man was killed when a lightning strike ignited a fire at his mobile home in southern Caddo Parish.  Lightning hit a tree by the resident which ran down the trunk and hit part of the trailer where his bedroom was located.  The fire occurred on Moon Beam Road which is off La. Hwy. 169.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulse thunderstorms developed in airmass with low freezing levels creating  large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroyed a barn at Pates Lane when the strike initiated a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong thunderstorms moved east across Orange and Brevard counties producing lightning and small hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was knocked unconscious by lightning while standing next to his personal water craft at Moss Park. He was revived by CPR.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A non-severe thunderstorm produced a lightning strike that killed a high school athlete.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 18-year-old high school student was struck and killed by lightning at a track meet. The lightning strike occurred on the school's campus just before the start of the track meet. Witnesses stated there was little rain, thunder, or lightning prior to the fatal strike. The student was declared dead on arrival at the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convection that resulted from the sea breezes and energy and moisture associated with flow in advance of an approaching upper level trough caused scattered storms across the forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused major damage to a home in Seminole Woods, a subdivision in Palm Coast. A radio antenna and dish were destroyed. Some stucco was removed from the side of the home and numerous holes were noted in the roof. Most of the electronic equipment in the home was inoperable after the strike. The damage amount is an estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate to strong instability resulted from strong afternoon heating. Isolated thunderstorms developed across the northern piedmont along a weak surface boundary.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex and sparked a fire. There was no immediate information on the extent of the damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread rainfall from 1 to 2 inches caused local runoff problems. A southwest flow established itself in the upper levels of the atmosphere, allowing moisture to work its way into the region. A large storm system developed over the central Plains on the 24th and moved northeast toward the Great Lakes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A stray bolt of lightning from an isolated storm entered a house through the telephone line. A 64-year-old man was knocked across his living room. Almost every window was shattered. The television set exploded. The man received a concussion and a damaged eardrum.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire near Elwood.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire which damaged a home near Elwood.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A quasi-stationary front just north of the Altamaha River, the sea breezes, surface based instability and upper level positive differential vorticity advection all merged to spawn scattered severe storms across our forecast area in the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were injured by lightning at the Little Talbot Island picnic area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex storm system took shape at the end of December and brought a round of elevated hail storms to the region. The hail storms occurred as a warm front and deeper moisture surged northward during the early morning hours, generally between 1 and 6 am and were scattered about the forecast area. The hail stones ranged between penny and quarter size and caused little to no damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home sustained heavy damage after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms associated with a persistent upper level low produced heavy rain and flash flooding in the afternoon and evening of July 24.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A father and two sons took shelter under a medium-sized cedar tree at Lost Maples State Natural Area in western Bandera County as a storm approached.  Lightning hit the tree, injuring all three, with the father the most serious.  One son was still able to go for help.  A park ranger and a trained medical responder who was visiting the park came quickly but could not revive the father.  Both of his sons were taken to a hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms also caused damage to a power substation in the northern part of the county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transmission and distributing line near the intersection of F.M. 2143 and Highway 172.  Eight spans of primary wire were destroyed along with insulators.  Puncture holes in the cooling fans also occurred.  Power was knocked out to the Olivia and Port Alto communities.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms accompanied a front moving through Arkansas on the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man in his early 20's was injured by lightning while working outside on a farm. He complained of tingling and numbness and was treated at a hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure center moving across Arkansas brought numerous thunderstorms and locally heavy rain on the morning of the 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: About 325 power outages were reported in the Hot Springs area. Wires were downed in two locations and six transformers had to be replaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough in concert with afternoon instability and the sea breezes spawned scattered severe storms across the forecast area in the evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and injured 3 men and 1 boy after they pulled off on the side of the road and got off their motorcycles.  The 3 men were 32, 25, and 40 years old.  The boy was 13, who required CPR.  All 4 people were taken to Bon Secours Community Hospital in Port Jervis.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface low offshore of the southeast Atlantic seaboard trailed a weak trough across the forecast area. This boundary as well as plentiful moisture and light winds spawned a few slow moving storms across the forecast area in the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an air conditioner at a home in north Arlington on Sanders Road. The strike caused a small fire. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating caused several isolated severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a drilling rig at the Shoal Creek Mine in western Jefferson County.  The lightning ignited methane gas in the mine, and six miners were injured by the subsequent fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating lead to several isolated severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house in Cottondale was significantly damaged by a fire caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper level trough offshore of the Atlantic Coast extended through central Florida and a surface front was stretched across Georgia. A moist and unstable airmass was south of the surface front, and, coupled the sea breezes, contributed to scattered severe storms across Florida in the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Between 1117 and 1126 am, lightning struck a property and a car at 91 Emerson Drive in Palm Coast. Two tires were blown out on the car. At 4 Old  Kings Road in Palm Coast, lightning stuck a building. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough over the eastern United States focused moisture and dynamics over our area. Upper level forcing from the trough along with afternoon instability and the sea breezes spawned widespread severe storms during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at the Moosehaven retirement facility.  The fire department had to remove a 20 x 30 foot section of roof. Forty residents had to be evacuated.  No one was injured. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mean layer southwest flow focused the sea breeze collision across the eastern Florida peninsula during the late afternoon. Isolated severe storms developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire that damaged 5-10 acres but did not endanger any structures along the 700 block of East End Road.  The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved southeast across the Mid-Mississippi Valley during the morning. Short lines of thunderstorms with isolated damaging winds developed in advance of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, sending parts of it crashing onto a mobile home. The mobile home received minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across the southern portion of the region with a few becoming strong and one reaching severe limits.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and caused a power surge to the house adjacent to it. Some interior electrical damage was done. The bark from the tree also exploded and broke out several windows at the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced numerous lightning strikes as they moved southeast across the Lower Ohio Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two persons were injured when lightning struck as they baled hay. The first person was hooking up a tractor to another piece of equipment when the lightning struck, causing burns on the arm. A second person standing further away was knocked unconscious. Neither person was critically injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough tracked through the region triggering scattered severe thunderstorms across east Tennessee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an 80 foot tree causing the electricity to surge into the ground and rupture a nearby home's gas line.  No homes were damaged, only the landscaping was burned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms developed in an unstable airmass in advance of a backdoor front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several reports of structural fires due to lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved southeast across the Mid-Mississippi Valley during the morning. Short lines of thunderstorms with isolated damaging winds developed in advance of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, starting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After an active severe weather day on June 18th, the atmosphere quickly recovered and was able to support additional severe weather which began in the late evening and persisted through the overnight hours. Severe weather during the overnight hours in June is quite rare but does occur on occasion. One of the overnight storms actually produced a rare June tornado! This overnight severe weather was likely a sign and just a taste of what was to come during the day on June 19th. As the overnight/early morning complex of storms shifted east, conditions were set just right for additional storms to redevelop to the west by late morning. The atmosphere recovered once more and became quite unstable in the wake of the morning complex. A very potent disturbance dropped south out of Arkansas and developed a large bow echo complex which plowed south across the forecast area. This bow echo was very efficient at producing severe wind gusts and a large swath of wind damage occurred as the system moved southward across Mississippi into Southeast Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex on North 38th Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning and burned to the ground in Beulah.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in northwest Colorado Springs, jolting a women who was working on a computer inside the house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds in central Maine.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oak tree and followed the roots to underground dog fence, and followed the underground wiring to a garage where it ignited a fire that destroyed the structure.  The structure and a 1996 pickup truck housed inside were a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front set off some thunderstorms over central Kentucky. Although little severe weather was reported, a Jessamine County man was struck and killed by lightning while riding a lawn mower.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two Tallahassee homes were damaged by fire sparked by lightning strikes.

The slow nature of these storms also allowed them to produce locally heavy rainfall with a number of areas seeing 1 to 2 inches in a short amount of time.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes were struck by lighting causing some damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved through North Mississippi during the afternoon and evening hours of July 9th, 2007. The disturbance produced showers and thunderstorms over the area. Some of the thunderstorms produced dangerous lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, about a half mile north of Ripley. The strike produced holes in the siding of the house and caused damage to electrical appliances in the home. In addition to the home, a nearby tree was also struck.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Nevada Appeal newspaper reported that lightning struck a house in Genoa around 5:30 pm PDT.  The lightning strike tore a hole in the roof.  The newspaper article stated that no fire or injuries from the lightning bolt were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A light steering flow and unstable airmass fueled scattered severe storms across the forecast area along the sea breeze fronts and outflow boundaries. Lingering energy from a decaying MCV system across central Florida enhanced convection.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in La Crosse and burned the house to the ground. Pea size hail was also reported. In High Springs at 324 pm, there was another house fire from lightning in the Parker Estates Subdivision. The cost of damage was estimated.
