EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front located over the Great Lakes approached the region from the west late Monday, July 9th. A prefrontal trough well ahead of this front, in conjunction with a lake breeze boundary, and a hot, humid and unstable air mass in place, led to the rapid development of scattered strong to locally severe thunderstorms across portions of eastern New York State and western New England during the late afternoon and early evening hours of Monday.||In addition, some thunderstorms contained locally intense rainfall rates of 2 or more inches per hour.  This led to localized flash flooding in urbanized areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire on Cuyler Avenue in Albany was initiated by a lightning strike, which is believed to have hit an electrical panel on the outside of the house. Once hit, an electrical surge and subsequent fire spread from the basement through the rest of the house. The house sustained severe damage, and partially collapsed.||Two firefighters suffered minor injuries while trying to extinguish the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The approach of a cold front from the west, along with a warm, moist and unstable air mass in place, led to the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across eastern New York and western New England during the afternoon and evening hours of Saturday, August 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Mechanicville around 2105 LST, causing significant damage to the second floor and attic. The back of the house was gutted, and new furniture inside the house was ruined.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm, very moist and unstable airmass, combined with the approach of a weak cold front from the west, led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the evening hours on Friday July 27th. ||Frequent cloud to ground lightning accompanied these thunderstorms, in addition to locally heavy rain and gusty winds. Lightning caused two structure fires in Bennington, destroying one building, and causing approximately $750,000 in damage to another.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vacant house on Harwood Hill Road in Bennington. The house was completely destroyed after the roof collapsed into the second story and continued to burn, subsequently collapsing that level.||State officials recommended that the house be razed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of July 4th and moved east across northern Virginia and western Maryland. Some became severe, producing large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile lounge traveling from Terminal B to the Main Terminal. The lounge had just crossed Taxiway B when a lightning strike caused it to fail. While the lounge operator attempted to re-start the lounge, a second strike traveled through the lounge exiting the chasis by way of the left rear tire. Two windows were blown out and the lounge sustained damage to the tire. The Operator and six passengers were not injured and refused medical treatment at the scene. Information courtesy of Washington Dulles International Airport Management. Damage costs are estimated. |

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms in the Naples area on July 27th caused lightning which damaged a home in Naples.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Naples at 5220 Seahorse Drive. The roof was badly damaged, as well as a room in the back of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on August 2nd. Hot, humid air in place allowed for the development of the thunderstorms. A few of the storms became severe, causing downed trees and tree limbs.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck transformer 3 miles from junction of Highways 315 and 7 towards Dean. Powerlines were also down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved southeast through southern Wisconsin and several thunderstorms along the front became severe.  Large hail up to 1 inch in diameter and powerful wind gusts to around 52 knots (60 mph) were produced.  Dewpoints in the upper 60s to lower 70s resulted in CAPE values of 1500-2000, which was sufficient for severe storm development.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn on Morris Rd., resulting in a fire that destroyed the structure, as well as a 1994 vehicle parked inside.  An adjacent small shed also had a small fire that was quickly extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front approaching from the northwest triggered isolated strong to severe thunderstorms during the early to mid afternoon hours of Sunday July 15th across portions of eastern New York State and western New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole outside the back of the North Adams Regional Hospital around 13:37 EST, which sent an electrical surge throughout the hospital. This melted a wire in the electrical panel inside the hospital that controlled an elevator, making the elevator unserviceable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Yet another weak cold front moved southeast through southern Wisconsin with double-structure in terms of lines of associated storms.  The first line was solid while the second line had scattered storms.  Some of the storms briefly pulsed to severe limits with powerful wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a retail store on a frontage road adjacent to Interstate 94, resulting in a minor fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another in a string of days of severe weather across South Florida as a mid to upper level trough continued to destabilize the atmosphere during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 36-year-old man was killed when lightning struck his tank while scuba diving off the coast near Deerfield Beach. The man had just resurfaced when lightning struck his tank. Frequent lightning and very heavy rain was occurring at the time of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another in a string of days of severe weather across South Florida as a mid to upper level trough continued to destabilize the atmosphere during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two-story house in the 3000 block of Green Turtle Place. A 3-foot hole was left in the roof, and a second floor bedroom caught fire. There were no injuries as no one was home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike during the evening set 14 bales of hay on fire just west of Hooper.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm airmass moved over much of Southern New England on the 9th of July. Instability parameters were quite high, but there was a cap. A weak trough moving in from the west during the afternoon helped to break the cap in a few places, and this allowed for scattered severe thunderstorm development.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Woman was struck by lightning in Ashby. Extent of injuries unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Record setting heat led to an isolated thunderstorm. A barn in Shiawassee Township was destroyed when lightning struck it and set it on fire. Farm equipment and bales of hay were burned in the blaze. Total monetary damage caused by the lightning was estimated at roughly $25K.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of thunderstorms moved across Northern Michigan during the morning hours.  A man in Cheboygan County, while standing in his garage watching the storm, was jolted and shaken up by a lightning strike in his immediate vicinity.  He sought medical treatment later in the day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved across northern Illinois during the late afternoon and evening hours of October 18th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14 year old boy was struck by lightning while riding his bike in an alley near the 6600 block of Archer Avenue.  The boy only suffered minor injuries, including a welt on his back.  Doctors believe he suffered an indirect lightning strike after the bolt hit something near him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably warm airmass was established across Vermont during the early afternoon hours of the 10th. Meanwhile, a mid-level atmospheric disturbance rotated across the area, and this resulted in the development of thunderstorms. One thunderstorm moved across Rutland county, with a lightning strike that struck a sawdust shed at Mill River Lumber on Middle road in Clarendon. The lightning strike completely burned the building and damaged equipment inside as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed rapidly across the four state region on 05/15.  A very unstable airmass was in place across the region ahead of a southward moving cold front and an associated upper level storm system.  The storms produced widespread hail and wind damage across much of the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in town. Minor to moderate damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged a home in Hopewell Township on Caroline Drive during the early morning of the 27th. Odors of smoke and natural gas filled the home. The lightning strike apparently struck the home's natural gas meter. It traveled along the natural gas line into the laundry room (the dryer) and arced between that pipe and a water pipe. The arc generated so much heat that it soldering on both pipes melted and allowed natural gas and water to flow. The lightning also caused extensive damage to the home's electrical system. but no fire occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lighting strikes around 5:00 pm caused a power outage across most of downtown and in the North Business 54 area. At least two area homes also had minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes caused a power outage across most of downtown and in the North Business 54 area. At least 2 area homes also suffered minor damage from lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A teenager was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 15 year old boy was standing near a tree when it was struck by lightning.  The teenager received burns on his back.  His clothes and shoes were ripped off.  A relative standing near the teenager said she saw blue light reflected off of him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved into East Arkansas during the afternoon and evening hours of May 15, 2007. Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the front. Some of the storms produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and power lines on West Walnut Street in Blytheville causing them to fall on a nearby house. Moderate damage was reported to the house, but no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a home in Smith County, Texas during the evening of the May 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Tyler, Texas blasting away part of the homes siding and catching the attic on fire.  The home was at least a 50 percent loss.  There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low pressure system situated to the west brought large scale lift to north Texas. Southerly winds brought deep rich moisture from the Gulf of Mexico. These and other factors caused numerous thunderstorms to develop. Widespread flooding and wind damage followed, as well as a few tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, causing the tree to split and fall on a car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes from thunderstorms that moved across the Omaha area Tuesday morning 4/25/07, caused two separate house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning striked caused an estimated $150,000 in damage to a house near 164th and Page Streets.  Firefighters arrived at around 5 am CDT and found flames on the roof.  The fire spread down a wall and caused considerable damage to the basement.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes from thunderstorms that moved across the Omaha area Tuesday morning 4/25/07, caused two separate house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning striked caused an estimated $60,000 in damage to a house near the 2600 block of 125th Circle. Firefighters arrived around 1030 am CDT and found flames on the roof.  The fire caused extensive damage to the upper level of the house and the rest of the house sustained moderate smoke and water damage. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low pressure system situated to the west brought large scale lift to north Texas. Southerly winds brought deep rich moisture from the Gulf of Mexico. These and other factors caused numerous thunderstorms to develop. Widespread flooding and wind damage followed, as well as a few tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike struck a mobile home and destroyed it.  No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front combined with pockets of moderate instability to help initiate thunderstorms during the late morning and early afternoon hours. A few of the storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Person struck by lighting on Nicholson Street. Extent of injuries unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms ignited off of lake breezes as they pushed inland.  A number of storms produced large hail, especially in Northeast Lower Michigan.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two canoers, one male and one female, were struck by lightning while taking shelter under a tree during a thunderstorm.  The woman was knocked unconscious, and both suffered significant burns.  They were transported to a burn center in Flint to recover.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms moved through central Indiana on the afternoon of 3 April 2007.  The storms produced mostly large hail, with isolated damaging wind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The roof of a home was struck by lightning causing a fire.  Fire crews were able to contain the fire to a bonus room over the garage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire that damaged twelve apartments in an apartment building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms affected parts of northern Arkansas on the 8th. The storms developed ahead of a cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power line, knocking out electricity to about 2200 customers. Gassville and Cotter were affected, as were parts of Mountain Home, Yellville, and Harrison.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed through Arkansas on November 21st. Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, setting it on fire. The second story incurred heavy fire damage, while the first floor suffered water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Powerful storms developed over southern Lake Michigan and moved south across northwest Indiana during the evening hours of August 15th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning, which ignited a fire in the attic.  The house suffered extensive damage, mainly from water.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late night thunderstorms containing frequent lightning caused at least one house fire in the Omaha area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire to house near 153rd and Ida Streets in far northwest Omaha.  The fire damaged the roof and second floor with the first floor and basement sustaining significant smoke and water damage.  The total damage was estimated at $250,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved across northern Illinois during the late evening hours of August 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Peru, which started a fire in the attic causing damage to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into West Tennessee during the evening hours of October 18th, 2007. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the front. Some of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was damaged by a fire started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another in a series of cold fronts brought severe thunderstorms to Kentucky. Most of wind damage that occurred was in the form of downed trees and power lines. Several people were injured, however, when the vehicles or outbuildings they occupied were struck by falling trees or large limbs. A few barns were damaged or destroyed, including one in Bourbon County occupied by four thoroughbred horses. The horses were rescued, and had sustained only minor injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in the Jeffersontown area. The extent of damage is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire on the roof and in the attic of a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms occurred across much of northern Utah, and a man was killed by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 60-year-old male was struck and killed by lightning while camping near Poison Mountain in the Uinta Mountain range. The man, along with his son and brother, sought shelter in a tent. All three people were injured, but only the one died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms developed over sections of southeast Louisiana ahead of a developing strong upper level trough.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at an apartment complex caused a small fire that caused minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulse thunderstorms over Orlando produced lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire that severely damaged a house in Orlando.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms formed over parts of Phoenix with locally strong winds at the airport.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near 51st Ave and Indian School Road. No major damage was reported, but a small attic fire was quickly put out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several strong thunderstorms produced intense lightning in Madison County, with extensive damage to the county jail and EOC.  Very heavy rainfall also caused widespread urban and small stream flooding throughout the county, with 8.3 inches reported at the USFS tower south of Madison.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused extensive damage to the county jail and EOC, with communications down for several hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This event set up as another nice case of elevated convection. On the morning of the 20th, an area of surface low pressure was located near Mobridge, South Dakota, with a warm front arching to the southeast (down into eastern Nebraska). A 35 to 45 knot low level jet set up from central Nebraska into northeast South Dakota, where there was also a tight moisture gradient at 850 mb. Thunderstorms initially flared up near Crookston, MN, and moved northeast at 40 to 50 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an evergreen tree in Barrett, scattering pieces of the tree across several neighboring yards. As the tree fell, it broke multiple windows and damaged the concrete steps to a house. The strike also damaged the electrical systems in three nearby homes. One home lost a microwave, two televisions, and several other smaller appliances.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into West Tennessee during the evening hours of October 18th, 2007. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the front. Some of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four transformers were blown due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This episode of storms dealt with 4 distinct groupings. The first group of storms began near Nashua in southeast Wilkin County (MN) and tracked to the northeast. The second began near Lake Park in western Becker County (MN) and tracked to the east-northeast. The third began near Enderlin in northern Ransom County (ND) and tracked to the east-northeast. And finally, the fourth group of storms formed near Goodridge in northeast Pennington County (MN) and tracked to the east-northeast. These storms appeared to be elevated too, forming near a tight 850 mb moisture gradient and a 35 to 45 knot low level jet. This event also had upper level jet support too.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in south Fargo, tearing a hole through the roof and causing insulation to fall onto the floor. Several light fixtures were knocked out of the ceiling, but no fire was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushing to the coast initiated several strong thunderstorms that produced large hail and numerous lightning strikes across eastern Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike sparked a large crude oil tank fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced a lightning strike that damaged a mobile home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A mobile home was damaged in a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very strong and isolated storms blew up over the western and southwestern CWA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four males struck by lightning at Bear Creek Park.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed and produced lightning and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A light pole was broken in half after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over east central Kansas during the late afternoon hours of April 25th.  No severe weather was reported with these storms, but a cloud to ground lightning strike caused damage to the yard, fence, garage, and portion of a home on a residential property.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in the yard of a home in Ottawa and peeled bark off two sides of the tree.  The bolt traveled into the ground, where it struck a water line, blew the heads off the in-ground sprinkler system in the yard, and traveled along a fence surrounding the yard.  The water line also tracked into the home, where all of the basement windows were blown out, and a few appliances were damaged. There were other isolated reports around town of power outages during the storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man died of a lightning strike on Bowstring Lake on the evening of June 8th. He may have been on his dock when struck. His body was found in the lake the following day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning marine environment was conducive for the formation of funnel clouds. Scattered storms affected coastal communities during the morning hours that produced funnel clouds, very localized street flooding, and frequent lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Home was destroyed by fire caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated streamer thunderstorms forming in the coastal regions moved north towards Houston metro in the early afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike at a Brazoria County golf course, seriously injuring one golfer.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms passing across southeastern Texas produced a lightning-related death and injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 30 year-old male was killed by a lighting strike while standing underneath a tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms passing across southeastern Texas produced a lightning-related death and injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 5 year-old female was injured by a lightning strike of a tree in which the electric charge entered the residence through a satellite dish. A dog inside the home was killed by the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed and produced lightning and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A storage tank was engulfed in flames after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms over the Upper Keys produced heavy rainfall over and a damaging lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the cupola of an unoccupied large oceanfront home in Plantation Key. The strike caused a small fire and damaged plumbing within the roof structure of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over central and south central Texas as an upper level disturbance approached from the west on the morning of Wednesday, the 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike to residential home caused home fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the western areas and moved northeast. The storms produced severe weather along a path from Dawson County to Sherman County. Mainly 3/4 to 1 inch diameter hail occurred with the storms with some gusty winds. A few wind gusts were between 60 and 75 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Evangelical Free Church during a thunderstorm this Monday evening. The lightning strike hit the bathroom vent and went to the basement. It made three holes in the roof and knocked off a big portion of the ceiling. It also knocked nails out of the ceiling and ruined several pieces of electrical equipment. (Source: Ord Quiz Newspaper 4/11/2007).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moved across south-central Nebraska in the late afternoon and evening hours. These storms produced some dime to quarter sized hail and some good rains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the water tower in Sutton. The lightning damaged some radio equipment located on the water tower. Several lightning strikes in the county caused some power and telephone outages. (source: Clay County News).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rogue thunderstorm traversed Thayer County. This storm dumped up to two inches of rain in some parts of the county.  A lightning bolt struck the Courthouse in Hebron. This resulted in minor damage to the county's computer system. County employees in the building remarked how they felt the hair on their arms stand on end and a tingling sensation. This was followed by very bright flash of light and a loud pop that sounded like a gunshot. No injuries occurred in the building. (source: Hebron Journal-Register Newspaper).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning isolated thunderstorms developed and moved northeast across coastal Matagorda County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 52 year old male was struck by lightning and injured while lying on the beach a few miles southwest of the Colorado River mouth.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning isolated thunderstorms developed and moved northeast across coastal Matagorda County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on the 200 block of Peppermint Drive casing a fire. The home was saved with significant roof and upstairs interior burn damage and some lower floor water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough well ahead of a central Texas cold front slowed as it approached the coastal counties. This boundary became the focus for severe thunderstorms along the coast and neighboring inland counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike started a fire that caused moderate damage to a home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over central and south central Texas as an upper level disturbance approached from the west on the morning of Wednesday, the 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike at Richmond Police Department. Lightning struck an antique 1897 flag pole atop building and exploded it into several splinters. One 4 foot section of the pole was reported to have embedded itself in the ground across the street from the police station.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over central and south central Texas as an upper level disturbance approached from the west on the morning of Wednesday, the 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Residential garage fire caused by lightning strike. Home was located on Owens Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed in a very moist and unstable airmass across northwest Louisiana.  These thunderstorms produced strong winds as they decayed along with prolific lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank about 5 miles south of Hwy. 175 near the Hutchinson Plantation in the Caspiana community.  Resultant fire then spread to the neighboring oil tank...destroying both tanks.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that two homes were struck and set on fire by lightning.  One was on Wedgewood Chase Drive and the other on Williamsport Drive near East Jones Bridge Road, of which the roof was completely burned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck and set on fire a home on Primrose Place.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Daily Tribune News of Cartersville reported that lightning struck a home on Lazy Water Drive in Euharlee.  The attic was set on fire and about 75 to 100 percent of the attic was burned.  Other parts of the home also sustained smoke and water damage.  A double-wide mobile home was also struck by lightning in Taylorsville on Old Alabama Road.  This home was a total loss as a result of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Upson County Emergency Management Agency reported that a home was struck and set on fire by lightning in the far western part of the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Record setting temperatures in the mid 90s combined with a cold front dropping into northern New England to produce scattered thunderstorms in northern Massachusetts. Isolated severe thunderstorms with damaging winds moved through sections of Worcester, Middlesex, and Essex Counties during the late afternoon and early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a brush fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the west coast sea breeze front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Seven apartments were damaged by a fire started by a lightning strike on the 3700 block of Winkler Avenue. Firefighters arrived on the scene three minutes after the first call and helped evacuate residents from the building. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moisture from the Gulf of Mexico surged into Arkansas early in September. The moisture content of the atmosphere rose considerably above normal. Then, an upper level low pressure system arrived and caused heavy rainfall and flash flooding to develop on the 4th and 5th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a breaker, causing a power outage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 25 year old man died after he was struck by lightning while working on a barge near Port Arthur, Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 25 year old man was killed when lightning struck him. He was working on a barge near the Motiva Port Arthur dock.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusual mid-August cold front combined with antecedent very hot temperatures in the 95 to 100 degree range and northwest flow aloft to create a very unstable atmosphere.  Thunderstorms developed during mid-afternoon in northwest and west central Georgia and quickly became severe.  Thunderstorm wind damage was the most common occurrence with these storms, but some hail was reported with some of the storms, especially those near the beginning of the event.  Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning was observed with many of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Webster County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a couple of trees and electrical transformers and set them on fire at private residences.  No structural damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak trough across the region triggered isolated strong to severe thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours across the area.  Storm reports comprised of small hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The roof a home on Franklin Road in Blountville was set on fire by lightning from a thunderstorm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A logger was killed by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male was struck and killed by lightning while working on a logging crew.  The sixty-one year old was part of a crew who were working in the forest when the bolt hit.  Emergency personnel were unable to revive him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Monroe County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home in the High Falls area.  The home was completely destroyed from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage in Mobile.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage in the Oakleigh Garden District in Mobile.  The strike started a fire and the garage was destroyed.  Two vehicles in the garage were destroyed by the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced heavy rain with street flooding, high winds, and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm in Winslow produced lightning that blew out a transformer and knocked out power. The storm also produced high winds, local street flooding, and small hail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Jackson County 911 Center reported that a home was set on fire as a result of a lightning strike.  In addition, an individual was injured as a result of a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: While high pressure aloft was once again building over the eastern U.S., a weak front remain draped from northwest Georgia to southeast Georgia.  This front, combined with a very warm, moist, and unstable air mass, again provided the necessary lift for scattered thunderstorms, one of which became severe.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was also once again a problem.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Polk County Fire & Rescue Department reported that lightning struck and set on fire a home on Old Cedartown Road at Morgan Valley Road.  One tree was also blown down three miles east-southeast of Rockmart along Springdale Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck and set on fire a home on Willow Park Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front dropping into northern New England triggered scattered thunderstorms in southwest New Hampshire. Isolated severe thunderstorms with damaging winds moved through Hillsborough County during the late afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a restaurant on Amherst Street, causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Jackson County 911 Center reported that another home was struck and set on fire by lightning in the far southern part of the county near the Oconee county line, just across the border from Bogart.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoonal moisture combined with strong surface heating made for scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms on this date. A few of the thunderstorms achieved severe status.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The steeple of the Newman United Methodist Church was struck twice this day, damaging the steeple, windows, organ, and some other stuff.  Damage amounted to $60,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unseasonably warm high pressure build over the Mid Atlantic ahead of a strong cold front. Scattered thunderstorms developed across western Maryland during the afternoon of September 26th in this warm and unstable air mass. A storm in Washington County produced damaging winds that downed trees and power lines. Lightning was also responsible for an office building fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Newspaper clippings reported an office building fire that was caused by a lightning strike. The building that housed 10 offices is salvagable, but there was significant damage to the top floor and roof and smoke and water damage on the lower floors.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Record setting temperatures in the mid 90s combined with a cold front dropping into northern New England to produce scattered thunderstorms in northern Massachusetts. Isolated severe thunderstorms with damaging winds moved through sections of Worcester, Middlesex, and Essex Counties during the late afternoon and early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage and ignited a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Record setting temperatures in the mid 90s combined with a cold front dropping into northern New England to produce scattered thunderstorms in northern Massachusetts. Isolated severe thunderstorms with damaging winds moved through sections of Worcester, Middlesex, and Essex Counties during the late afternoon and early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wires were reported down due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree next to a house located about 3.5 miles west southwest of Lowden, IA around 10:45 am September 25th.  The tree caught on fire and phone service was interrupted for a while.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree next to a house located about 3.5 miles west southwest of Lowden, IA around 10:45 am September 25th. The tree caught on fire and phone service was interrupted for a while.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over the region ahead of an upper level system.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the 911 tower in Ste. Genevieve.  It knocked out fuses, fried two computer circuit boards and took out all the dispatch phones. Service was not back up til the next day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from early morning thunderstorms over northeast Nebraska caused a house fire in Norfolk.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire in Norfolk causing around $100,000 damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near Pace.  The strike started a fire and the home was destroyed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed during the heating of the day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One house fire and 2 forest fires were started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several severe thunderstorms developed during the heat of the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire on Unicorn drive, in the Coaling community.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tank battery in an open field.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tank battery in an open field just off F.M. 70 and C.R. 63, causing a small explosion and fire.  Roughly 150 barrels of oil were spilled from the tank battery.|

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near Lesterville on August 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an electrical box on a house near Lesterville.  The house caught fire and burned to the ground.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several severe thunderstorms developed during the heat of the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two children sustained minor injuries when they were apparently struck by lightning, at the 4800 block of Caldwell Mill Road in north Shelby County. Both children were knocked to the ground. One got up and was ok, and the other was taken to a local hopital and was later reported to be ok.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid airmass, combined with an approaching upper level trough, contributed to isolated strong thunderstorms across the San Joaquin valley on the 30th and 31st of August.  Late at night on the 30th, a strong thunderstorm knocked out power to over 1500 Avenal residents.  Similarly, 800 customers in Dinuba were without power due to strong thunderstorms. In Visalia, a tree was knocked down by gusty winds and lightning, causing minor property damage on the 30th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small cluster of thunderstorms produced severe weather in Leelanau County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a fire, which destroyed a three-car garage and a boat that was inside, and melted vinyl siding on an adjacent home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hiker was struck by lightning on the southeast face of Mt. Elbert near treeline.  He was treated at the scene by a doctor, complaining of being sore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough over the eastern United States focused moisture and dynamics over our area. Upper level forcing from the trough along with afternoon instability and the sea breezes spawned widespread severe storms during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree in a courtyard near Greenbrier Apartments off of Justina Road in Arlington. The lightning charge then dispersed through an adjacent puddle and killed one man.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable airmass remained in place across Iowa on the evening of the 6th with an east-west boundary lying across the mid section of the state.  CAPE rose to around 4000 J/kg by late afternoon as afternoon highs reached the upper 80s to low 90s, and dew point temperatures were in the mid 70s to low 80s.  The freezing level was very high, between 16,000 and 16,500 feet, reducing the threat of hail even though the CAPE in the hail layer, -10 to -30 C. layer, was in the 500 to 700 J/kg range.  Downdraft cape was significant at around 1200 J/kg.  The lifted index fell to between -4 and -8 C. by late afternoon with an effective shear of 35 to 45 kts across the area.  LCL values were between 750 and 1000 meters.  There was copious amounts of moisture in the atmosphere with between 1.7 to over 2 inches of precipitable water.  Heavy rainfall was the most significant threat.  Heavy rainfall of around 3 inches occurred in Cass County.  The town of Griswold recorded 3.6 inches of rain.  This resulted in flash flooding in the Griswold area.  Reports of 4 feet of water running over the highways were received.  Two to three inches of rain fell in Audubon County, with water running over Highway 173 southeast of Kimballton.  Severe weather was spotty.  Thunderstorms winds downed trees in Cass County from Griswold to about 3 miles northeast of Griswold.  There was also a 60 MPH wind reported northwest of Griswold.  Later in the evening, the thunderstorms moved east into central Iowa.  One storm produced a microburst northwest of Van Meter in Dallas County.  The winds blew in a garage wall and tossed the roof down on a nearby car.  An uninstalled modular home was demolished along with several trees being downed.  As the storms developed east into the metro Des Moines area, lightning struck a house in Urbandale starting it on fire.  There were no injuries.  In addition, lightning struck a garage in Denison, setting it on fire.  The garage was destroyed along with numerous vehicles inside.  Later on, thunderstorms moved across southwest Iowa.  One of the storms struck a chicken barn in Taylor County.  The lightning bolt blew a whole in the electrical box and set the chicken barn on fire.  The barn was destroyed, but fortunately it was empty at the time.  The lightning also knocked out the power at a nearby hog building, killing 700 young pigs due to lack of ventilation when the fans went out.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was struck and killed by lightning, while jogging at Matthews Winters Park in Morrison.  The thunderstorm, which produced numerous lightning strikes, also caused a power outage at Red Rocks Amphitheatre, forcing the cancellation of a concert scheduled later in the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong short wave aloft, combined with daytime heating, brought scattered strong to severe thunderstorms to much of north and central Georgia.  Only isolated storms reached severe limits.  Several discrete lines of strong to severe thunderstorms were observed from mid-afternoon through the early evening hours on the 8th.  Thunderstorms also developed during the afternoon of the 9th as well.  However, the only incident reported on the 9th was a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Daily Tribune of Cartersville reported that lightning struck a home on Ranger Road setting the roof on fire.  Damage was confined to the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms moved across northern Ohio on June 8th.  Lightning from one of the thunderstorms killed a man in Mahoning County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 66 year old male was struck and killed by lightning outside of his house.  His home was on New Buffalo Road approximately two miles northwest of North Lima.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper air disturbance combined with an unseasonably hot and humid air mass to trigger pulse type thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 10th in Delaware. In addition to being prolific cloud-to-ground lightning producers, a couple of thunderstorms also became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike quickly caused a fire at a house on Avalon Road in Georgetown. When firefighters from five separate companies arrived, the rear of the home was already engulfed in flames and the fire had extended to a nearby storage shed. Two people were home at the time of the lightning strike and escaped before being injured. Damage to the home was estimated at $300,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper air disturbance combined with an unseasonably hot and humid air mass to trigger pulse type thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 10th in Delaware. In addition to being prolific cloud-to-ground lightning producers, a couple of thunderstorms also became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: As thunderstorms moved across New Castle County, lightning caused damage to three structures. In Newark, in the Academy Hill Development, a lightning strike started a fire in the basement of one home. The home filled with smoke. It took twenty-five firefighters about forty minutes to extinguish the fire. Damage was estimated at $5,000. In New Castle, a lightning strike punched holes in an Artesian Water Tower on School Lane. It caused the tower to leak. In Delaware City, a lightning strike created a hole in the roof of a home on East Harvest Drive. The ensuing fire consumed a large portion of the roof as well as the master bedroom. Damage was estimated at $150,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved northward during the day of  12/19 and became stationary near the Arkansas/Louisiana border.  An upper level storm system approached the region from the southern plains and provided the dynamics needed for scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to form across all of northeast Texas, southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas and northwest Louisiana.  During the late evening hours of 12/19...the storms initially were elevated in nature...producing large hail.  Towards the overnight and predawn hours of 12/20...the storms across deep east Texas and west central Louisiana became more surface based producing strong and damaging wind gusts and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three family members died in a house explosion as a result of lightning striking near the home.  It was determined that the explosion was caused by a gas leak and the lightning strike.  The blast shattered windows of surrounding homes as well.  Debris from the explosion was found within a 200-foot radius of the home tht was totally destroyed in the blast.  Two other neighboring residents were also injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A combination of a prefrontal outflow boundary drapped across northern Indiana and a MCV from overnight convection across Nebraska the night before provided the focus for convection to develop. In addition, unstable conditions develop during the late morning and early afternoon with SBCAPES of 1500 to 2500 j/kg. Storms began to develop on this boundary during the mid afternoon hours and rapidly became severe. A line of storms associated with the MCV and an approaching trough moved across the northern part of Indiana. This line evolved into several small bowing segments which produced numerous reports of damaging winds and isolated tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire officials were dispatched to a residence in the Harrison Landing subdivision of Warsaw where lightning struck a house. The fire was contained within 30 minutes. No one was injured in the fire. Damage was estimated at around $40,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Brownsburg during the morning hours of November 2nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Brownsburg and started a fire in the house as storms moved through the area.  Large parts of the ceiling fell down and the roof will have to be replaced.  Clothes, bedding, and other items in the house were also damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure area south of the Florida Panhandle provided for a deep southerly flow of moist and unstable air, leading to numerous showers and thunderstorms over South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 49-year-old man was struck and killed by lightning while working on a vegetable farm in rural southern Hendry County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level system ahead of a cold front brought scattered thunderstorms to central Kentucky. Most of the thunderstorms remained below severe limits, but there were some reports of large hail. There was also some unspecified lightning damage to a home in north central Kentucky.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A storm spotter reported unspecified lightning damage to a home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroys a home in Lantana, and 4 condos near Crab Orchard.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is blamed as the cause of a fire that damaged two condos by fire and water, and two other condos with smoke damage. The fire was in the Renegade Mountain region.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of severe thunderstorms formed along a cold front that moved across eastern Nebraska and western Iowa during the late afternoon and evening hours on March 21.  Temperatures climbed into the 70s to around 80 degrees in advance of the front, and dew-points rose into the upper 50s to lower 60s.  This provided the necessary instability to help touch off the severe thunderstorms.  The storms produced mainly nickel to quarter size hail...although a few larger stones were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the gutter of a house causing a fire that caused about $5,000 worth of damage before firefighters brought it under control in about 10 minutes.  The fire was in southwest Omaha.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms associated with warm frontal boundary.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, which burned.  The home was determined to be a near total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very strong Theta-e advection took place over Iowa during the day on the 23rd as a storm system developed over the front range of Colorado and Wyoming.  Low level winds increased to over 50 kts during the day, drawing in considerable moisture north across the colder air at the surface.  I was located north of a surface warm front.  Elevated thunderstorms developed during the day and pushed northeast across the state.  Instability parameters were limited, however 500 J/kg of shear was available in the most unstable layer, with 100 J/kg of that in the -10 to -30 C layer.  The effective zero to 3 km shear was around 25 kts.  Most of the thunderstorms produced one quarter to one half inch diameter hail and a considerable amount of sleet.  There was enough to cover the ground in many places.  One of the storms became severe in Webster County and produced three quarter inch diameter hail.  As the thunderstorms moved through the Cedar Falls area, lightning struck a house there causing a small dormer fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A major winter storm developed over the central U.S. as a strong upper level system move in on the southern jet stream.  The system came through as a bowling ball type event as the upper low first became negatively tilted, then closed off over Iowa.  Low pressure moved across Kansas into northern Missouri, then turned northeast across central into northeast Iowa as it intensified.  The low dropped to about 978 mb as it moved through Iowa.  The low brought a variety of weather to the state, with a blizzard over much of the west half of the state, and thunderstorms with pea to marble size hail over the east half.  As the low passed to the east cold air and high winds overspread the state.  Sustained winds of 30 to 40 MPH were widespread, with occasional gusts to between 50 to 60 MPH were common.  Visibility in rural areas dropped to zero, remaining that way for an extended period of time.  Heavy snowfall occurred over the western part of Iowa with snowfall rates approaching 4 inches per hour at times as the snow was convective in nature.  A large area of Iowa northwest of a a Creston to Mason City line received in excess of 10 inches of snow.  Some of the heavier totals include 18 inches at Estherville, 17 inches at Carroll, 16.8 inches in Estherville, 15.5. inches in Ringsted, and 14 inches in Pocahontas, Atlantic, and Goldfield.  The combination of high winds, heavy snowfall, and the preexisting snow on the ground resulted in roads drifting shut quite rapidly.  Widespread blizzard conditions resulted in numerous road closures over the northwest half of the state.  Interstate 80 was closed westbound at Iowa City to the Nebraska border, and both east and westbound at Des Moines.  Interstate 35 was close both north and southbound at Ankeny to the Minnesota border.  Hundreds of people were stranded in their cars during the height of the blizzard.  The National Guard was called out to conduct numerous SAR missions.  Reports of 5 to 10 foot snow drifts were common across western and northern Iowa, with drifts of 16 feet reported in the Carroll area.  The high winds and wet snow caused additional power outages over parts of the state as well.  An additional 30,000 people lost power during the storm.  Governor Chet Culver declared the remaining 39 counties of the state disaster areas, bringing all 99 counties under disaster declaration.  In addition, a request was made to place 44 Iowa Counties into Federal Disaster Status.  The request was granted, along with two additional counties.  A total of 46 counties received a Presidential Disaster Declaration.  The blizzard was considered the worst blizzard in decades for parts of western Iowa.  In Carroll for example, the blizzard was the worst since the blizzard of 1947.  During the storm in Des Moines, thunderstorms moved across the city.  A woman was struck by lightning outside of Lovejoy Elementary School in Des Moines.  She received minor injuries and reported pain in her arm following the strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low pressure system with a trailing cold front pushed into portions of Southwest Tennessee during the late afternoon hours of 2/24/07. Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the system and produced flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire to begin in a structure located on Paris Avenue in McKenzie.|

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong weather system moved through the southeast United States during the early morning hours of Sunday, February 25th.  While no severe weather was observed or reported within the Peachtree City, Georgia forecast area, a couple of lines of thunderstorms, with occasional lightning and heavy rain, moved through the area during the hours of 2 am and 10 am.  Two lightning-related fires resulted in west central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Newnan Times-Herald reported that lightning struck an outbuilding on 140 Bill Hart Road.  The building housed a cabinet shop.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong weather system moved through the southeast United States during the early morning hours of Sunday, February 25th.  While no severe weather was observed or reported within the Peachtree City, Georgia forecast area, a couple of lines of thunderstorms, with occasional lightning and heavy rain, moved through the area during the hours of 2 am and 10 am.  Two lightning-related fires resulted in west central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Newnan Times-Herald reported that lightning set a home on Bethlehem Church Road on fire.  The lightning actually struck an adjacent tree which caused the lightning to travel through a cable starting a fire in the garage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system lifted northeast into the region from Oklahoma, during the late afternoon and early evening hours on February 28th. The dynamics from this storm system provided the lift for rapid thunderstorm development along and north of a warm front by the early evening hours. There were numerous reports of hail with the storms, as well as some flash flooding. |The most significant severe thunderstorm produced a tornado in Anderson county Kansas, which then tracked east into Linn county Kansas. The EF4 tornado took a nearly 24 mile continuous path, where it caused damage to mainly rural areas. Just north of Blue Mound a single residence, garage, and several farm buildings were completely destroyed. The tornado was historic, since it was the first time anywhere in the country that a tornado was rated as high as EF4, since switching to the new Enhanced Fujita scale February 1st, 2007.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer on the roof of a middle school.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms developed in the Gulf of Mexico far ahead of an approaching cold front. This line caused one lightning injury and wind gusts of 40 to 56 MPH across west central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 38-year-old male landscaper was struck by lightning while planting bushes. Lightning struck and split a nearby tree.  The man was taken to a medical center and was listed in fair condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms during the early morning hours of March 28, 2007|produced numerous lightning strikes over portions of West Tennessee. One lightning strike caused a structure fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a chemical fire to start at the Helena Chemical Plant in Humboldt. The chemical fire destroyed the plant. About 400 to 500 employees of nearby plants as well as some 100 nearby residents were evacuated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scatttered severe storms produced large hail, and one report of a funnel cloud.  A rotating wall cloud was observed by a trained spotter about 6 miles west of the Madison State Capitol. Some of the storms that became supercellur displayed moderate mesocyclones in their updraft towers. Synoptically, a warm front stalled over northern Illinois, resulting in sufficient vertical wind shear that supported rotating updrafts.  However, the depth of the cooler air below the elevated convection prevented actual tornado development.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a city of Fond du Lac home.  There was no fire, but the home's electrical wiring was damaged, and a hole was punched in the roof of a porch.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Upper jet dynamics associated with a 80 to 90 kt jet max combined with surface heating triggered thunderstorms across central and western portions of the piedmont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A two story home in the Tredegar subdivision sustained heavy damage when it was hit by lightning and caught on fire. The entire second floor was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong storms moved across northwest Indiana during the afternoon of September 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A mobile home was struck by lightning, which caused a fire and damaged the mobile home beyond livable conditions.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Non-severe thunderstorms resulted in a lightning stike in DeSoto Parish during the morning of April 17th resulting in a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike along Hwy 84 near Logansport, Louisiana hit a storage tank owned by British Petroleum on the Southern Natural Gas Road.  The fiberglass tank exploded and the local fire department was called in to extinguish the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Non-severe thunderstorms produced a lightning strike which caused a fire in Bossier Parish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt ignited a south Bossier Parish oil tank on the morning of April 10th. The bolt destroyed a tank filled with saltwater and the blast blew the top off a holding tank holding 2000 gallons of oil and water.  No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms struck early Thursday morning on March 1 and later in the afternoon on the same day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Crossville Chronicle stated that lightning struck a TVA transmission line, knocking out power to 24,000 Volunteer Electric Customers (VEC). Power was knocked out in Fairfield Glade, Crab Orchard and the Crossville area until 1033 AM CST.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front approached Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest |Arkansas during the late afternoon hours of Tuesday, April 3rd, in |associated with the tail end of an upper level trough that traversed |southeast across the Mid-Mississippi Valley. Above normal temperatures |and ample low level moisture created strong low level instability  which eventually overcame the capping inversion in place, such that strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and just ahead of the cold front over Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. These severe |thunderstorms eventually backbuilded into Northeast Texas during the |evening hours of the 3rd and into the morning hours of the 4th, |resulting in numerous reports of large hail and strong damaging winds, |with the wind damage reports most common across the western sections of |Northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning resulted in a house fire on County Rd. 246. There were no report of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system remained over west and central Texas for several days.  Numerous shortwaves traveled from this system and over north Texas.  This energy combined with ample moisture to create several rain events over much of the region.  A large amount of rain in a short time triggered flash flooding in many counties.  A few hail and wind reports were received as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of St. John's Lutheran Church.  Minor damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed in advance of a warm front which moved north across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 25 year old man was struck by lightning near the intersection of Columbia and Radcliffe Avenues in University City.  He died from the lightning strike 5 days later on April 29th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread thunderstorms affected central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of June 1, 2007. Some of these thunderstorms developed into pulse severe storms, causing large hail and isolated reports of damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, and injured two individuals inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low level moisture was in place across North Texas as an upper level low pressure system moved into the western half of the state.  Large hail reports along with damaging winds and flash flooding were common throughout this twelve-hour event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Blue Sage Drive and caused damage to the electrical system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep trough along the Rocky Mountains and a stationary front across West Central Texas combined to produce widespread showers and thunderstorms across the region.  With the amount of shear in the environment, several of the storms became supercells and produced mainly hail and an isolated tornado near Sweetwater.  For the most part, they remained elevated above the boundary layer. This was the first widespread outbreak of severe thunderstorms for the early spring storm season.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house off of loop 306 near San Angelo and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The severe weather event that struck the Great Plains on the 28th ranks as the most significant tornado outbreak recorded in the month of March. A pair of tornadic supercells initially erupted along the dryline over the central South Plains during the late afternoon hours, and tracked northeastward across the extreme southeastern Panhandle through the early evening. These two storms produced a total of seven tornadoes in the South Plains region. The hardest hit areas were near Silverton and Antelope Flat in Briscoe County. No injuries were reported.|By late evening, the retreating dryline merged with an advancing Pacific front. This initiated at line of severe storms over the western South Plains that progressed eastward over the region through the early morning hours of the 29th. These storms resulted in widespread reports of large hail up to the size of golfballs and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck a radio antenna near Floydada.  Damage resulting from the lighting strike left local law enforcement without radio communication through the night.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residence in Abilene and damaged the furnace. There were no injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An outflow boundary moved south into Iowa during the morning of the 16th.  Thunderstorms erupted just to the north of the boundary during the afternoon.  As the thunderstorms moved through Humboldt, a 19 year old woman was struck by lightning and injured.  She was taken to hospital complaining of pain and difficulty moving her limbs.  Thunderstorms became numerous over northwest Iowa during the late afternoon in combination with the old outflow boundary and an approaching MCS from South Dakota.  Several of the storms became quite strong with wind gusts of 40 MPH or more and large amounts of small hail.  The shear environment was weak with only 20 kts or so of effective shear.  One storm moved through Pocahontas County and produced nickel size hail near Ware and caused wind damage south of Laurens.  A grain bin was destroyed by the high winds there.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two separate buildings on the same day in Sparta, one of which incurred extensive damage to electrical equipment inside.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of the Museum Complex Building in Sparta, which damaged some electrical equipment inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two separate buildings on the same day in Sparta, one of which incurred extensive damage to electrical equipment inside.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck for the second time in Sparta, this time hitting the Land Conservation Building. Extensive damage occurred to the phone system, computers, printers and copiers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms moved through central Indiana on the afternoon of 3 April 2007.  The storms produced mostly large hail, with isolated damaging wind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a vacant garage at 600 South 7th Street.  The garage was completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The first major severe weather event of the season resulted in widespread reports of wind damage and large hail. This event can be best described as having two parts. The first round of severe storms occurred well in advance of the actual cold front. One batch formed southwest of the Metro-Detroit area, and another formed in the Saginaw valley and thumb regions. A strong supercell moved across Huron County, producing 70 MPH wind gusts and baseball sized hail. A second and final round of storms developed along the cold front with a squall line actually moving from the southwest to the northeast. The squall line raced across the region and produced wind gusts in the 60-70 mph range. Numerous reports of wind damage were received in a swath stretching from a Jackson/Adrian line, northeast to a Flint/Imlay City line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper article reported that a house suffered heavy damage after a lightning strike ignited a fire. Total damages were roughly estimated at $75K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A significant disturbance in northwest flow event provided for scattered to numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours.  Several of the thunderstorms became severe, mainly producing large damaging hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Courier Herald of Dublin reported that lightning struck the Graham Memorial Church of the Nazarene.  Damage was confined to the steeple and inside water damage from heavy rain and fire fighting water hoses.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A significant disturbance in northwest flow event provided for scattered to numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours.  Several of the thunderstorms became severe, mainly producing large damaging hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Kylee Dawn Circle setting the attic on fire.  The attic sustained minor to moderate damage as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot, humid and unstable airmass, interacted with a lake breeze boundary and led to numerous thunderstorms across eastern New York and western New England during the late afternoon hours of Wednesday June 27th, some of which were severe.||In addition, locally very heavy rain led to flash flooding in some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a steel pylon at Alcathys Marina, adjacent to where a 17 year old male was standing. The male was knocked unconscious, and was transported to a nearby hospital. He was pronounced dead the next morning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning non-severe thunderstorm caused two fires at the Wynnewood Refinery. The first fire occurred in a tank housing naptha, a gasoline component. This fire was thought to be contained, before another fire began that evening in a tank containing diesel fuel.  Approximately 70,000 barrels of naptha and diesel were lost in the two day fire. Roads surrounding the refinery were closed due to the massive amounts of smoke coming from the refinery. No injuries were reported with the explosions. The fire burned for at least 2 days before finally extinguishing. Monetary damage amounts were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A convective system which moved through Oklahoma arrived in north Texas around daybreak on the 30th.  Numerous reports of large hail and wind damage were recieved as well as flash flooding.  Storms formed again on the 31st as a strong low level jet helped initiate storms along boundaries left from storms the day before.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Argyle, lightning struck a house in the 800 block of FM 407.  Estimated damages were $200,000. Lightning also struck a hot-water heater at Greenway Patio Homes in Denton.  Lightning started two small fires in Corinth and Shady Shores.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated supercell thunderstorms produced severe weather across Central and South Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck and damaged by lightning on Merimount Avenue in Auburn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary stretched from northern Wisconsin to the Texas panhandle during the evening hours of Wednesday, May 23rd, through the morning hours of May 24th.  Severe storms developed late Wednesday afternoon along the front, and dropped hail up to 1.00 in diameter across portions of northeast Kansas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An official from a local energy company said more than 3,500 customers were left without power after thunderstorms rolled across Hiawatha.  Lightning hitting a power line was stated to be the cause of the outage.

The most impressive of these events was a derecho which moved through North Texas on May 2.  It produced winds in excess of 85 MPH.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked out power to the county's dispatch center, forcing employees to move to another building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms caused large hail and wind damage early in the month.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning produced a house fire on Lake Tuscaloosa.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northwest wind flow aloft drove a cold front into Arkansas from the Plains on the 15th. The front arrived in northwest sections of the state by the early afternoon, and pushed across the region through the evening hours. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms accompanied the front...with some storms becoming severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an electrical substation and set fire to a large transformer.  Power was initially knocked out to a large part of Calhoun County, but some of the power was restored quickly.  The most prolonged power outages occurred in the areas around Highland Industrial Park and Locust Bayou.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The strong upper trough moving through the Ohio Valley continued to cause problems in the southeast for yet another day.  As was the case on the 4th, severe thunderstorms were confined to the far southeast part of the County Warning Area (CWA).  Northwest flow aloft kept isolated thunderstorms going well after dark and into the early morning hours of the 6th.  Renewed, albeit isolated, thunderstorm development occurred in the west central part of the state during the early morning hours before sunrise on the 6th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Laurens County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck three homes in the county.  Damage was minor and confined to electrical wiring damage.  No fires were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system moved northeastward into West Tennessee during the evening hours of May 3, 2007. Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with the upper level low pressure system. Some storms produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Eagle Tree Road in Covington. As a result of the lightning, smoke was coming from the house. In addition, a hole was punched in the roof and the chimney had collapsed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced large hail, damaging winds and very heavy rainfall over the west Texas South Plains during the evening hours of the 28th. Most damage occurred over northern Lynn County, where large hail destroyed young cotton crops. Crops also were damaged in Hockley, Swisher and Terry Counties. Slow storm movements attributed to flash flooding in Lynn and Floyd Counties that stranded motorists and threatened structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike in Floydada damaged the electrical grid and caused an outage that affected more than 1,000 customers for several hours.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a barn on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Daytime heating on May 9, 2007 helped to develop scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a local public housing complex on Rice Street in Forrest City. A fire started and spread to other apartments. No injuries were reported.

One thunderstorm moved across Massena (St. Lawrence county) during the early to mid-afternoon and produced lightning that struck and burned down a church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved across northwest Indiana May 15th, producing significant wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building, which started a fire in the attic.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A school was struck by lightning at Nelson Road, south of Laraway Road, which caused a fire and significant damage to the roof.  A house was struck by lightning near Joliet Highway and Schoolhouse Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms, producing heavy rainfall and dangerous lightning, moved across portions of central Indiana during the afternoon and early evening of June 26, 2007.  The main threat and damage from these storms was caused by flooding and lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was confirmation of two houses being struck by lightning in the Westfield area.  A firefighter was hurt when the ceiling of a house collapsed on him when he was inside the house.  One house sustained substantial damage of $150,000 to $175,000.  The other house had minor damage to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms, producing heavy rainfall and dangerous lightning, moved across portions of central Indiana during the afternoon and early evening of June 26, 2007.  The main threat and damage from these storms was caused by flooding and lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a hotel and three homes in the Fishers area.  At the hotel the lightning hit the telephone and fire alarm system.  A hotel occupant at the time received an electrical shock when he was on the phone during the storm.  Some of the houses reported having holes in the roof of their homes due to the lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread severe weather occurred on this day. Thunderstorms initiated in a warm and humid airmass ahead of a strong cold front moving eastward through the Ohio Valley. One storm produced and EF-0 tornado between Muncy and Hughesville in Lycoming county. In addition, a 24-year-old male was struck by lightning and killed in his driveway in York county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At approximately 630 PM, a 24 year old male was struck by lightning in his driveway in Fairview Township, York County. He died early on June 20th.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn that was subsequently destroyed by a fire. All of the animals escaped, and stored tools were saved.  Only a minor amount of hay was lost.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably warm airmass was located across Vermont during the  afternoon and evening hours of the 10th and continued into the overnight hours of the 11th. Meanwhile, a mid-level atmospheric disturbance rotated across the area, and this resulted in the development of scattered thunderstorms. One thunderstorm moved into Caledonia county around 1 am EDT on the 11th, with a lightning strike that struck a barn on Bible Hill Road in St. Johnsbury. The resultant fire destroyed the barn, some equipment, as well as killed five registered quarter horses, a litter of puppies and a calf.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Daytime heating on May 9, 2007 helped to develop scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. Some of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near Pine Grove, killing 10 cows. The Brangus cattle were huddled under one large oak tree when the lightning bolt struck the tree. The lightning blasted bark from the tree as far as 200 feet away.

Lightning struck the roof of the residence, causing the rafters in the attic to catch fire.  Damage to the home was estimated to be $5000.  The 15,000-gallon fuel tank, which stored diesel gas for farm equipment, was also struck.  The explosion shot the tank an estimated 150 feet in the air and it landed approximately 400 feet from its original location.
