EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving pacific storm system, ejecting from the Desert Southwest, brought a period of unsettled weather to Northeast Colorado.  During the 3-day period from May 3rd to May 5th, locally heavy snow was reported over parts of the Front Range Foothills.  Storm totals included: 15 inches near Conifer, 14.5 inches west of Jamestown, 13.5 inches; 6 miles southwest of Evergreen, and 12.5 inches at Pine Junction.  Severe thunderstorms, producing large hail and several small short-lived tornadoes, occurred during the period as well.  No damage was reported with any of the tornadoes.  ||In addition, lightning struck a residence in Jefferson County.  The roof of the house was hit, causing the attic to catch on fire.  The fire was confined to the one room; there were no injuries.  At Denver International Airport, lightning also struck a United Airlines jet as it was pushing away from the gate.  The passengers were taken off the jet and put on another plane.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a United Airlines jet as it departed the gate at Denver International Airport.

This energy combined with ample moisture to create several rain events over much of the region.  A large amount of rain in a short time triggered flash flooding in many counties.  A few hail and wind reports were received as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front pushed east across east central New York and western New England during the afternoon hours of Tuesday June 5th. The interaction of this strong front, combined with a warm, moist and unstable air mass in place, led to the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across eastern New York and western New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two females, ages 18 and 16, were standing under a tree in Schenectady when lightning struck the tree, injuring both females. The 18 year old female was airlifted to Albany Medical Center for burns to her feet, ankles, legs, stomach, and chest, and may have also had internal injuries, while the 16 year old female suffered superficial wounds to her right arm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low pressure system situated to the west brought large scale lift to north Texas. Southerly winds brought deep rich moisture from the Gulf of Mexico. These and other factors caused numerous thunderstorms to develop. Widespread flooding and wind damage followed, as well as a few tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two transformers were knocked out by lightning.  An electrical worker burned his retinas as an arc came off the wires while he was repairing them.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: June 25th proved to be one of the more significant severe weather days during the month.  This was the result of a strong short wave in westerly flow aloft and a very unstable and moist atmosphere present over the area.  Damaging downburst winds, large hail, and most significantly a number of lightning incidents were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Forsyth County 911 Center reported that two homes and a tree were struck and set on fire by lightning.  The homes were located on Aaron Phosby Road, Astoria Avenue, and Concord Village Lane.  Damage was minor to moderate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms caused wind damage across Northern Franklin and Jefferson counties. A lighting strike in Columbia caused a fire at a business.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lighting strike around 3:00 pm CDT caused a fire at the Creative Photo Photography Studio at 2201 Old Highway 63. Five employees and a dog were able to escape unharmed. The fire is believed to have started in the attic. Damage was estimated at $150,000.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck by lightning while fishing at the edge of a pond.  One was killed and the other injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong northwest flow, a result of an unseasonably deep polar vortex over the northeast U.S. and southeast Canada, combined with several short waves embedded within the northwest flow aloft, to lead to a two-day outbreak of severe thunderstorms.  This was the most significant bout of severe weather north and central Georgia had experienced since mid-April with an almost complete lack of severe weather in May, normally a very active month.  The activity peaked during the afternoon and evening hours, but lingered well overnight on the 11th into the early morning hours of the 12th.  Most of these thunderstorms affected central and east central Georgia.  More widespread severe thunderstorms were observed on the 12th, including much of the Atlanta metropolitan area.  A number of the storms produced large hail, while a lesser amount produced damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a home on Beeblossom Trail.  The resulting fire caused heavy damage to the attic and significant damage to the second floor of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The strong subtropical upper ridge continued over the area.  However, weak disturbances riding around the edges of the upper high combined with strong instability to result in considerable afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms.  A number of these became severe producing hail and damaging winds.  Lightning was particularly significant with this event with a number of lightning-related structural fires reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Harris County 911 Center reported that a power line was down as a result of a lightning strike.  The transformer was also set on fire by the lightning.

Only isolated storms reached severe limits.  Several discrete lines of strong to severe thunderstorms were observed from mid-afternoon through the early evening hours on the 8th. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of heavy rain-producing showers and thunderstorms moved across eastern Iowa and west central Illinois from 12:00 am June 22nd until approximately 6:00 am June 23rd.  This occurred on already saturated ground from heavy rains on June 21st.  The areas from Waterloo, to Cedar Rapids, to Iowa City, to Wapello, to Burlington, to Macomb were affected the most receiving rainfall totals of 4 to 8  inches.  Flash flooding was observed across much of the affected area.  ||Of particular note, near record flooding occurred on the Iowa River near Marengo, IA where the river level rose over 7 feet in under 3 hours.  The 72-hour rainfall total through the morning of June 23rd at the cooperative observation station in Marengo was just over 7.5 inches.||In addition to the flooding, a few of the storms surpassed severe thresholds in Des Moines and Lee Counties in extreme southeast Iowa, producing nickel size hail and a brief EF0 tornado, which damaged a barn and some trees.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An outflow boundary/weak frontal boundary was stretched east to west across the Iowa-Missouri border.  The airmass remained very unstable with temperatures in the mid 90s for highs and dew points in the mid to upper 70s in the vicinity and north of the front.  CAPE reached over 6000 J/kg by the late afternoon with lifted indices in the -10 to -12 C. range.  The shear was between 35 and 45 kts.  A supercell formed in south central Iowa by late afternoon north of the boundary.  The storm was not able to become tornadic in part due to the LCL being quite high at 1500 meters.  The storm did become severe and produced nickel size hail north of Murray in Clarke County.  The CAPE in the hail layer, -10 to -30 C. layer of the atmoshpere, was fairly high at 800 J/kg, however with the freezing level 16,500 feet the hail size was limited.  As the storms moved through Polk County, lightning struck a duplex in Johnston.  It caused a minor fire, but otherwise caused little damage.

One of these thunderstorms generated lightning which caused damage in Chico.

Pieces of flying wood damaged an apartment awning, the roof of a home, and several vehicles.  Another lightning strike on a transformer left 1,800 customers without power for up to four hours.  Additional power outages occurred for 4,300 customers in Tehama County, including the towns of Los Molinos, Gerber and Dairyville.

One of the storms produced damaging winds around 5:20 pm, downing some tree branches in Olin, IA.  Frequent lightning was also noted with the storms, which stuck a transformer and damaged a television, telephones, a refrigerator, and a welder.  A tree was also stuck by lightning, splitting it in half.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An mesoscale convective vortex (MCV, defined as a small low pressure area left behind by previous thunderstorms) arrived in southwest Arkansas on the 2nd. Cool air aloft with the MCV moved over much warmer conditions near the ground, with showers and thunderstorms popping up quickly.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the county courthouse. There was damage to the outside of the building, as well as several computers inside the courthouse.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot, moist air mass allowed some thunderstorms to go over severe limits over central Kentucky.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of showers and thunderstorms, some with moderate to heavy rainfall rates, left behind rainfall totals of 1.5 almost 3 inches in a band from the Madison (Dane Co.) to Milwaukee (Milwaukee Co.).  This resulted in minor small stream/urban flooding in the Madison to Milwaukee corridor.  Numerous roads were flooded at one time or another, but none were closed.  Raw sewage was dumped into Lake Michigan after storm sewers/deep tunnel system filled up in the Milwaukee area.  Specific rainfall totals include 1.84 inches at the UW-Charmany Farm on the southwest side of Madison, 1.80 inches at UW-Whitewater (Jefferson-Walworth county line), 2.48 inches in Elm Grove (Waukesha Co.), and 2.84 inches about 6 miles northwest of downtown Milwaukee.  Most of the rain fell between 2100CST on April 2nd and 0600CST on April 3rd, although some minor road and stream flooding continued until about 1000CST on April 3rd.  Additionally, lightning strikes were responsible for scattered power outages across south-central and southeast Wisconsin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Dozens of power outages resulted from lightning stikes from the city of Monroe to Brodhead.  Either the lines and poles were hit or the transformers were hit.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Supercell thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours, producing severe weather that included tornadoes and very large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was struck by lightning near Emerald Mountain.  The person was working in a house under construction.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered, short lines of thunderstorms produced scattered reports of large hail across south-central and southeast Wisconsin.  On the weather map a surface front extended from northern Iowa through central Illinois.  Mid-level, warm-air advection above a dry, cool, east to northeast surface flow fueled the thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struke a pole-jumper, resulting in a power outage that affected 2000 customers in the city.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved into Iowa from the west and north as an MCS that developed to the west advanced into the state and weakened.  Lightning struck a church in Marshall County shortly after sunrise.  The 106-year-old Sacred Heart Catholic Church in St. Anthony was destroyed by a fire that was touched off by lighting about 0530 CST Friday. By midmorning the roof and much of the walls had collapsed.  No injuries were reported. St. Anthony is located just northwest of Marshalltown.  Seventy firefighters and 24 trucks from fire departments in Clemons, State Center, Zearing, Colo, Nevada, McCallsburg and Albion fought the blaze through late morning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms during the morning and afternoon hours of March 31. 2007 produced dangerous lightning strikes. One in which struck a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire at a house on Shea Road. The fire caused substantial damage to the home. Four firefighters were treated for heat exhaustion and two other firefighters were treated for other injuries. The fire took 4 to 5 hours to put out. The lightning bolt apparently traveled across the top of the house. The house was under construction and was a few weeks from being completed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front passing through Arkansas sparked the development of severe thunderstoms.  There were numerous reports of large hail and a few reports of flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an electric substation and also set fire to a building at the substation.  Power was knocked out to 11,900 customers until power could be rerouted.  The electric utility estimated that it would take three months to repair the damage to the substation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper level disturbance pushed some pulse thunderstorms above severe limits.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two houses were struck by lightning, and had attic damage due to fire.

This resulted in minor small stream/urban flooding in the Madison to Milwaukee corridor.  Numerous roads were flooded at one time or another, but none were closed. Specific rainfall totals include 1.84 inches at the UW-Charmany Farm on the southwest side of Madison, 1.80 inches at UW-Whitewater (Jefferson-Walworth county line), 2.48 inches in Elm Grove (Waukesha Co.), and 2.84 inches about 6 miles northwest of downtown Milwaukee. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large, slow-moving storm system produced severe thunderstorms across NW Kansas, NE Colorado and SW Nebraska.  Tornadoes, large hail and flash flooding were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Time estimated based on newspaper report of other power outages in town.  Owner not home at the time, but returned to find the electric meter on the home destroyed.  A circuit breaker box was burned and hanging from the wall. The strike damaged the underground sprinkler system and destroyed a tree in the yard, which was estimated to have taken the direct lightning strike.  The home's entire electrical system was damaged and a television damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 30th struck two people in Pompano Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman and her toddler-aged daughter were struck by lightning while waiting for a bus. The woman felt electricity in her hands. Both people were able to make it inside of a Wendy's Restaurant and call for help. Paramedics treated the two at the restaurant and convinced them to go to the hospital to be looked at.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably strong mid-level atmospheric disturbance moved across a marginally unstable airmass across northern New York during the early afternoon of the 5th. This resulted in the development of showers and a few scattered thunderstorms, including a severe thunderstorm which moved across the towns of Morrisonville and Beekmantown in Clinton county. This storm produced damaging winds that knocked down tree limbs and power lines, as well as a lightning strike that caused a small fire at a home in Beekmantown.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a small fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the 1st, a cold front moved through the state bringing heavy rain and a few thunderstorms to the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire occurred at the U.S. Forest Service Pleasant Hill District office of the Ozark National Forest. Lightning struck a radio tower and apparently traveled down the tower to a Forest Service office building. The building and equipment inside were destroyed. Siding was melted on an adjacent building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large convective thunderstorm complex moved southeast through southern Wisconsin during the mid-morning hours and gradually diminished in strength.  On the back side of the thunderstorm complex a wake low pressure formed, which resulted in a tight surface pressure gradient.  The tight pressure gradient generated strong gusty southeast winds up to around 40 knots (46 mph).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the golf bag and then a 75-year-old male golfer who was standing under a tree during a thunderstorm.  He was instantly killed.  He was playing at the Odana Golf Course on the southwest side of Madison.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure aloft was firmly entrenched over the area keeping a very hot air mass in place.  Many areas across north and central Georgia had high temperatures in the 100-105 degree range, with a number of record high temperatures recorded.  This combined with a weak cold front draped across north Georgia to result in the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across mainly central Georgia.  The intense heat allowed the storms to linger well past sunset, even into the early morning hours of the 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Crisp County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home starting a fire in the electrical system.  The home sustained at least minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved over northern Oklahoma during the pre-dawn hours of the 23rd. Lightning from one of the thunderstorms caused a fire large tank fire near Waukomis. The tank housed both salt water and crude oil.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tank fire was started by one of numerous lightning strikes from ongoing thunderstorms. The tank contained both salt water and crude oil.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably strong mid-level atmospheric disturbance moved across a marginally unstable airmass across eastern Vermont during the afternoon of the 5th. This caused showers and scattered thunderstorms, including a few severe thunderstorms in Orange and Windsor counties. Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in Ludlow (Windsor county) and other communities in the immediate vicinity. Also, penny size hail fell in Ludlow with nickel size hail in Ascutney (Windsor county) and West Topsham (Orange county). Also, lightning struck a house in Stockbridge (Windsor county).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cluster of thunderstorms July 25, 2007 formed over middle Tennessee from a vorticity lobe circulating around a 500 mb low over northeast Ohio 12Z Wed. July 25.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency Management official said lightning struck a house. There was roof and structural damage to the house, costing about $100k.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced lightning strikes which caused structual damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house under construction was struck by lightning.  The house suffered fire and water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak back door cold front was approaching north and east Georgia from the Carolinas.  Meanwhile...aloft a large upper high remained centered just west of the area.  These features combined with hot afternoon temperatures and a moist low-level air mass to result in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The activity was somewhat more widespread, more intense, and further north than had been observed on several previous days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck near a young girl on Dodd Boulevard in east Rome causing injury.  A home in the area was also set on fire by a lightning strike.  In addition, a power substation in the northern part of the county was struck by lightning with a resulting fire.  Much of the county was left without power as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the area associated with a cold front. Lightning associated with one of the storms killed a man who was in a boat fishing on Canyon Ferry Reservoir.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Man fishing alone in boat on southern Canyon Ferry Resevoir, on east shore across from Silos, struck and killed by lightning around 320 pm MDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms began early in the morning on the 6th, continued most of the day and into the early morning hours of the 7th. An upper level low pressure remained anchored over Colorado during this time period. Surface low pressure was located over southeast Colorado, with a dryline extending south along the Oklahoma and Texas panhandle border. Outflow boundaries were also present from previous thunderstorm activity. These boundaries were important in the formation of thunderstorms throughout the day. Moisture was in abundance that day, along with very strong instability. Wind shear remained quite favorable for supercell thunderstorms. Most of the thunderstorms began over the northwest half of Oklahoma, but moved south and east into the morning and afternoon hours of the 7th.  Large hail, high winds, and tornadoes were common, with flooding rains also present.  One small supercell thunderstorm developed east of the main thunderstorm area during the evening and produced two small tornadoes as it moved to the north. Two other tornadoes occurred in the early morning hours as thunderstorms moving northeast into central Oklahoma interacted with gust front boundaries from previous thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was started after a direct lightning strike. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms, producing hail up to quarter size, and heavy rain; trained across northern portions of the Denver Metropolitan area.  The path of the storms stretched from around Golden to Denver International Airport.  The thunderstorms formed quickly following the passage of a cold front.  ||Some minor street flooding was also reported as hail clogged storm drains.  The hail piled up 4 inches deep at Elitch Gardens amusement park in downtown Denver.  Drivers were caught in up to 3 feet of water in some intersections.  Xcel reported scattered power failures around the Denver metropolitan area. At D.I.A. some brief delays occurred as airlines were forced to pull in their ground crews for safety reasons.  Lightning also struck two homes in Ft. Collins.  No one was hurt in either incident.  The incliment conditions forced the closure of Trail Ridge Road, in Rocky Mountain National Park, due to snow and very poor visibility.||Severe thunderstorms developed further south along the Palmer Divide. Hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter was reported over southern Elbert County.  Hail damage was reported in the towns of Elbert and Limon, where skylights and windows were broken.  Two tornadoes touched down but no structures were damaged.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Flooding rainfall continued to spread across the region on July 9th as the upper trough of low pressure remained parked across our region. Plentiful moisture combined with daytime heating allowed for scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas, northwest Louisiana and northeast Texas resulting in flood producing rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near 79 Sassafras Drive in Magnolia, Arkansas blasting a hole in the yard.  The bolt traveled through water pipes in the home of a local resident.  No occupants were home at the time but two dogs were overcome by smoke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Bermuda high pressure extended across the state with sea breeze induced thunderstorms most active north of Sarasota.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the ground near a 13-year-old boy and he was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm started a house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm created a fire which destroyed a home in Scottsburg.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm caused extensive damage to a neighborhood near Eloy in Pinal County. Meanwhile, southwest of Tucson, lightning struck a suspected illegal immigrant in the Altar Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected illegal immigrant was struck and injured by lightning while traveling through the desert of the Altar Valley near Sasabe. Three of his companions were also shocked when the bolt hit the man who suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced high winds and significant lightning that caused house and tree damage in southwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home causing a fire. The home was a complete loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed on the 30th, ahead of an advancing cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck at a gas well, knocking over a tank and setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Coweta County 911 Center and the Newnan Times Herald reported that lightning struck six structures within the county.  A home was struck on Mike Powers Road, causing moderate damage to the bedrooms, and Pegasus Trace in Thomas Crossroads, causing just minor damage.  A barn on Roy Road off Georgia Highway 16 in the Raymond community was destroyed as a result of a lightning-related fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large convective thunderstorm complex moved southeast through southern Wisconsin during the mid-morning hours and gradually diminished in strength.  On the back side of the thunderstorm complex a wake low pressure formed, which resulted in a tight surface pressure gradient.  The tight pressure gradient generated strong gusty southeast winds up to around 40 knots (46 mph).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire that substantially damaged a 2-story home.

The tight pressure gradient generated strong gusty southeast winds up to around 40 knots (46 mph).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire that substantially damaged a 2-story home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rare and rather strong cold front for July was approaching the area from the northwest during the afternoon of the 11th.  A strong short wave in northwest flow aloft, combined with the cold front and a warm, moist, unstable surface air mass resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms across the area during the afternoon hours.  Abundant cloud cover prevented most of these from becoming severe.  However, as the storms moved into the southern portion of the forecast area, isolated storms produced damaging downburst winds.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was also an issue with some of the thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Morgan County Emergency Management Director reported that two homes were struck by lightning and set on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rare and rather strong cold front for July was approaching the area from the northwest during the afternoon of the 11th.  A strong short wave in northwest flow aloft, combined with the cold front and a warm, moist, unstable surface air mass resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms across the area during the afternoon hours.  Abundant cloud cover prevented most of these from becoming severe.  However, as the storms moved into the southern portion of the forecast area, isolated storms produced damaging downburst winds.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was also an issue with some of the thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Sumter County 911 Center reported that two trees were down as a result of lightning strikes.  The trees were down on Hathaway and Bradley Roads near U.S. Highway 280.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary acted as a focusing mecahnism for thunderstorms throughout the day on the 29th in New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In addition to the wind damage, two homes were damaged by lightning strikes in Medford Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level shortwave in combination with a highly unstable environment resulted in scattered shower and thunderstorm development across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in West Ashley and a transformer was blown out by lightning on Ashley River Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Approximately one mile north of the summit of Poncha Pass in Chaffee County...heavy rain caused one foot of water to flow over the back roads. Quarter size hail occurred in and around Rosita in Custer County.  A few small fires resulted from lightning in La Junta as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes causes small fires in a few buildings.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary acted as a focusing mecahnism for thunderstorms throughout the day on the 29th in New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a fire in the front part of a home on Barberry Court in Woodbridge Township. The front of the home was damaged before fire fighters could extinguish the blaze. In addition siding was removed to help find and battle the fire.|

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An outflow boundary produced by thunderstorms August 7th remained relatively stationary over north central and northeast Kansas through the night.  Convergence near the boundary served to focus convective development by late afternoon as the boundary layer mixed out and destabalized.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn burned down after it was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary acted as a focusing mecahnism for thunderstorms throughout the day on the 29th in New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike in Forked River (Lacey Township) caused a fire that burned and destroyed a shed. Another lightning bolt struck a pole at the intersection of Lakeside Drive and Parker Avenue. Wires dangled downward from it. Between the severe weather and lightning, about 800 homes and businesses lost power in Ocean County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moisture from the Gulf of Mexico advanced rapidly northward on October 17th. A warm front moved into Arkansas and sparked a number of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon. One of these storms spawned an EF1 tornado west of Star City. During the evening, a cold front approaching from the west pushed another area of severe thunderstorms into Arkansas. These storms pushed eastward across the state and continued into the early morning hours of the 18th. In both instances, there was a considerable amount of wind damage, primarily due to very strong winds aloft.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked down a large tree. The tree caused minor damage to the garage of a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms with heavy rain and the usual lightning rolled through the Madison area, resulting in flash flooding and a lightning incident that received considerable media attention.  See the Dane County Flash Flood event for related information.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power-pole, causing the attached power-line to fall onto a water-covered ground around a bus stop.  As a result, three people were electrocuted - two of them while standing in the water waiting for a bus, and another person who got off of the bus.  All three fatalities were indirectly-related to lightning since the people weren't struck by the lightning bolt.  Two other people were injured  and treated for shock at a hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak back door cold front was approaching north and east Georgia from the Carolinas.  Meanwhile...aloft a large upper high remained centered just west of the area.  These features combined with hot afternoon temperatures and a moist low-level air mass to result in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The activity was somewhat more widespread, more intense, and further north than had been observed on several previous days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fulton County 911 Center reported that a home in College Park was set on fire by a lightning strike.  One power line in the area was also down, either the result of lightning or a wind gust.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak back door cold front was approaching north and east Georgia from the Carolinas.  Meanwhile...aloft a large upper high remained centered just west of the area.  These features combined with hot afternoon temperatures and a moist low-level air mass to result in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The activity was somewhat more widespread, more intense, and further north than had been observed on several previous days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The DeKalb County 911 Center reported that a home was struck and set on fire by lightning.  One person in the area was also injured from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Baldwin county worker was struck by lightning as he tried to escape a storm while working near a dirt pit.  He was going to his truck to get out of the storm when he was hit.  He was taken to a local hospital, treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across the region during the afternoon and evening in the vicinity of a nearly stationary frontal boundary. Several of the thunderstorms became severe...producing damaging winds and large hail. A camper at Baxter State Park was killed during the evening after being struck by lightning...with his brother injured by the same lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One camper was killed and his brother injured when lightning struck a tree near their campsite and arced to strike them both where they were sheltering. The incident occurred at the Katahdin Stream Campground in Baxter State Park at some point between 8:00 and 8:15 PM. The surviving brother was hospitalized with first and second degree burns to his feet.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Newton County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a home in the Mansfield area.  Damage was indeterminate.  A few large tree limbs were down in Covington from wind gusts.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain across northern Illinois during the late morning and afternoon hours of August 19th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck in a parking lot, near a hospital causing a power surge which activated pumps in a laundry room, causing a bleach spill.  Several patients had to be relocated away from the fumes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak back door cold front was approaching north and east Georgia from the Carolinas.  Meanwhile...aloft a large upper high remained centered just west of the area.  These features combined with hot afternoon temperatures and a moist low-level air mass to result in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The activity was somewhat more widespread, more intense, and further north than had been observed on several previous days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Carroll County EMA Director reported that lightning struck a home on Carrollton-Villa Rica Highway, Georgia Highway 61, causing damage to the structure.  Another home on Sandhill Hickory Level Road was damaged when a tree fell on the residence as a result of a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak back door cold front was approaching north and east Georgia from the Carolinas.  Meanwhile...aloft a large upper high remained centered just west of the area.  These features combined with hot afternoon temperatures and a moist low-level air mass to result in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The activity was somewhat more widespread, more intense, and further north than had been observed on several previous days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Carroll County EMA Director reported that lightning struck a home on Timber Ridge Trail, just of Georgia Highway 166 west-southwest of Carrollton, causing damage to the structure.  South of Carrollton, just of U.S. Highway 27 on Memory Springs Road, the electrical meter of a mobile home was struck, causing minor damage to the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms with frequent lightning resulted in 87 fire related calls to New Hanover 911 center.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Gorham Ave., heavily damaging the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail, up to 2 inches in diameter.  The most severe weather occurred over southeastern Douglas and southwestern Elbert County, from around Larkspur to Elbert.  Large hail in this location caused extensive damage to vehicles.  A tornado was also observed, but it did no damage.  In Parker, lightning struck a home, causing extensive damage.  The bolt entered the house's electrical system and started a fire when sparks from an overloaded outlet fell into a nearby trash can.  The ensuing fire damaged the attic and top floor.  The strike caused $100,000 in damage and rendered the home uninhabitable for the next 3 months.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front approaching from the west, along with a hot, moist and unstable air mass in place, led to the development of numerous showers and strong thunderstorms across eastern New York and western New England during the mid to late afternoon hours on Friday August 3rd,  into the evening hours. Some thunderstorms became severe during this time period.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the steeple of a church in Brattleboro, at the corner of Main and Grove streets. The damaged area of the steeple was approximately 25 feet tall, and 4 feet wide. Estimated monetary damages from the lightning strike is around $250,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable airmass coupled with a stalled out front was enough to fuel the development of two extremely intense thunderstorms. One of the storms managed to go from Mount Pleasant all the way to eastern Oakland County. The storm in Midland County became so intense that it prompted the issuance of a Tornado Warning. National Weather Service field surveys identified damages consistent with intense straight-line winds associated with thunderstorm downbursts. The Sanford area was hardest hit with many homes suffering damages from falling trees. Many local businesses in Sanford and Midland implemented tornado safety plans, moving customers to designated shelter areas. St Charles in Saginaw County was another area hit hard from downburst winds approaching 80 MPH. Total damages from the entire event approached nearly a quarter of a million dollars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement reported a house struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper air disturbance in the northwest flow behind the cold front still had sufficient moisture to develop strong to severe thunderstorms across Pennsylvania and New Jersey during the afternoon and the evening of the 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck and injured by lightning in the Costco parking lot in Edison Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening of the 10th...a mid-atmospheric disturbance moved along a stationary frontal boundary draped across central Vermont. Numerous thunderstorms developed in Vermont, as well as  New York which then traveled across Vermont. Some of these thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds. Large hail of nickel to quarter size occurred in Norwich, Andover and Weston (Windsor county), as well as East Hardwick (Caledonia county) and several towns in Orleans county. Damaging winds in the form of downed trees occurred in a few communities in Addison, Chittenden and Orleans counties. A severe thunderstorm across Seymour Lake in Morgan (Orleans county) produced golf ball size hail which damaged vehicles and damaging winds that knocked downed trees, flattened utility sheds and damaged boats and docks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house at 525 Forest Dale Road in Brandon and started a fire in the roof and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The same upper low that brought a number of large hail storms to north and central Georgia on June 11th and 12th remained over the northeast, but was shifting slightly further east.  Isolated thunderstorms, a few severe, continued to develop during the afternoon, but were confined primarily to north Georgia on this day.  Several produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning, but only isolated storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Union County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck three structures in the city, including the 911 center.  Damage there was confined mainly to electronic equipment.  Minor damage occurred to the other structures.  In addition to the lightning, pea-sized hail fell for up to five minutes in the city.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching warm front helped produce severe thunderstorms and also caused some lightning damage across northern Delaware.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The combination of lightning strikes and damaging winds caused about 5,200 homes and businesses to lose power across New Castle County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass developed over the Mid Atlantic ahead of a strong cold front on August 25th. Temperatures climbed into the mid 90s by noon. These temperatures combined with high humidity created heat index values around 105. Showers and thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon as the cold front approached the region. Some of these storms became severe, producing large hail and damaging winds that downed trees and power lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Washington County Emergency Management and local newspapers reported that a woman was injured when struck by lightning while tubing on the C&O Canal in southern Washington County. A 27 year old woman was struck by lightning while in the water near the intersection of Keep Tryst Road at Weverton Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The pattern of a broad upper trough in the south central U.S. continued.  This combined with a persistent warm, moist, air mass over the region resulted in yet another afternoon and evening of showers and thunderstorms.  Isolated storms became severe producing damaging downburst winds and marginally severe hail.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was also an issue.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WXIA Television of Atlanta reported that lightning struck a home in the Kennesaw area causing substantial damage to the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm produced lightning damage and hail in northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck several houses around Crestview. No major damage was reported and no one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak frontal boundary in combination with sea breeze and numerous low level boundaries in a highly unstable environment resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old male was struck and killed by lightning while walking along the beach. His mother who was walking with him was also struck by lightning and injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the 12th, a mesoscale convective system moved into Arkansas during the afternoon hours and interacted with a front draped across southern Arkansas. The front became active, with scattered thunderstorms bubbling up and isolated severe weather and flash flooding reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, causing a fire in the laundry room, garage, and attic. It also blew a hole in the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The remnants of Tropical Storm Erin approached Arkansas from the west on August 18th. Ahead of the system, isolated severe storms developed during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Searcy's water treatment plant, damaging the plant's control panel.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved into northern Illinois during the afternoon hours producing severe thunderstorms which moved slowly and produced very heavy rain and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire in the attic, which sustained extensive damage.  The rest of the house was uninhabitable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This event will be remembered for the extreme intensity of large hail it generated. A most unusual hailstorm pounded areas in a 3 mile radius around the city of Durand. Severe hail fell for nearly an hour. At times, the hail was as big as golf balls. Hundreds of homes and vehicles suffered significant damages, totaling nearly 5 million dollars in this area alone. Large hail also caused significant damages to cars in and around the Adrian area. Mostly hail reports were received, but we did get a few wind damage reports from thunderstorm downbursts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported $250K in lightning damages to computer, radio and telephone equipment at county buildings in downtown Adrian.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This event will be remembered for the extreme intensity of large hail it generated. A most unusual hailstorm pounded areas in a 3 mile radius around the city of Durand. Severe hail fell for nearly an hour. At times, the hail was as big as golf balls. Hundreds of homes and vehicles suffered significant damages, totaling nearly 5 million dollars in this area alone. Large hail also caused significant damages to cars in and around the Adrian area. Mostly hail reports were received, but we did get a few wind damage reports from thunderstorm downbursts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported lightning damage to electrical systems at Delphi Automotive Systems. Total property damages were estimated at roughly $50K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and the house caught fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near Milligan shortly after midnight.  The home caught fire and was totally destroyed.  The home had just been rebuilt after being damaged by Hurricane Ivan.  The residents were able to get out of the burning house and were uninjured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High winds from thunderstorms caused tree and power line damage in northwest Florida. The thunderstorms also produced lightning which damaged a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire in the attic which resulted in significant damage to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High winds from thunderstorms caused tree and power line damage in northwest Florida. The thunderstorms also produced lightning which damaged a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man went to his refrigerator to get a drink. As he reached for a metal knob on his cabinet, he saw a flash of light and heard a loud boom.  He was knocked down by the strike.  He was taken to a local hospital and kept overnight and released.  He said he felt sore all over his body.  It was unknown what path the lightning followed into the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in northwest Florida causing significant damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near Navarre causing a fire which resulted in significant damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough extended across the forecast area in a highly unstable and moisture laden environment. Sea breezes as well as upper level divergence enhanced updrafts and severe storms developed across the forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire occurred in Ponte Vedra due to a lightning strike. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough extended across the forecast area in a highly unstable and moisture laden environment. Sea breezes as well as upper level divergence enhanced updrafts and severe storms developed across the forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The 911 center had damage to some consoles due to a lightning strike. Around the same time, a house fire was started in St. Augustine from a lightning strike. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved southeast across the Mid-Mississippi Valley during the morning. Short lines of thunderstorms with isolated damaging winds developed in advance of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage and started a fire that damaged the outside of the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms, producing hail up to quarter size, and heavy rain; trained across northern portions of the Denver Metropolitan area.  The path of the storms stretched from around Golden to Denver International Airport.  The thunderstorms formed quickly following the passage of a cold front.  ||Some minor street flooding was also reported as hail clogged storm drains.  The hail piled up 4 inches deep at Elitch Gardens amusement park in downtown Denver.  Drivers were caught in up to 3 feet of water in some intersections.  Xcel reported scattered power failures around the Denver metropolitan area. At D.I.A. some brief delays occurred as airlines were forced to pull in their ground crews for safety reasons.  Lightning also struck two homes in Ft. Collins.  No one was hurt in either incident.  The incliment conditions forced the closure of Trail Ridge Road, in Rocky Mountain National Park, due to snow and very poor visibility.||Severe thunderstorms developed further south along the Palmer Divide. Hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter was reported over southern Elbert County.  Hail damage was reported in the towns of Elbert and Limon, where skylights and windows were broken.  Two tornadoes touched down but no structures were damaged.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few thunderstorms were able to form, south of a slow moving cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm with minimal lightning, electrocuted a family pet.  A metal wire was attached to 2 trees for a dog run.  Lightning struck one of the trees, killing the dog on the end of his metal leash.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: By mid afternoon on the 21st, an area of surface low pressure was located in southwest North Dakota, with a warm front arching northeast toward Devils Lake (ND) and then southeast toward Detroit Lakes (MN). This front basically held in place through the early evening, and was marked by a strong thermal gradient. At 6 pm CST, Jamestown reported a temperature of 82 degrees, Devils Lake reported 75 degrees, and Minot reported 59 degrees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the steeple of a church in Langdon, causing some shingle and brick damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid-level atmospheric disturbance and accompanying surface trough moved into a very warm and unstable airmass across Vermont during the late afternoon hours of the 27th. Thunderstorms developed along this boundary in the Champlain Valley of New York and intensified as they moved across Vermont. ||There were numerous reports of wind damage in the form of downed trees and power lines across the state, which resulted in thousands without power. Large hail was reported in Caledonia county and lightning struck a house in Brighton (Essex county) that caused a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Derby St. and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved west across much of western and central New Mexico producing heavy rain and hail. Flash flooding occurred in Capitan and lightning caused damage in Santa Fe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in the yard of a Santa Fe residence.  The shock wave from the strike shattered two windows in the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system remained relatively stationary over the Central Plains Saturday through Monday, May 5th through May 7th.  Severe weather swept across Northeast Kansas during the late evening hours the 5th, and the early morning of the 6th.  Hail, strong winds, and tornadoes were all observed over the course of the evening.  An F2 tornado that ripped across Ottawa County killed one woman, and injured one other when their mobile home was demolished.  At least three other people were confirmed to have been injured during the tornado.  NWS Storm Surveys the following day confirmed that damage was created by both tornadoes and strong winds across portions of northeast Kansas, but 6 tornadoes were confirmed. Cloud county qualified for FEMA funds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a power outage for 1,100 customers for nearly 2 hours. A second lightning strike knocked a tree onto powerlines, which knocked out power to 1,375 customers for more than an hour.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating combined with small outflow boundaries and Gulf moisture allowing severe thunderstorms to develop over Archer and Baylor counties. Hail up to nickel size was reported near Seymour in Baylor county. Outflow winds from this storm moved into Archer county, with wind speeds near 70 miles an hour reported. Several tree limbs were blown down as a result. Monetary damages were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree was downed by a lightning strike. The tree was located at Elmwood Avenue near Maplewood Avenue. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning June 23, 2007 during an outdoor festival.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while attending an outdoor festival on June 23, 2007. The 47-year-old Indiana man was among a crowd watching a stage show. A bolt of lightning struck the man, knocking him unconscious. No one else was injured. He was leaning against a motorcycle when the bolt hit his right shoulder and exited out both of his feet according to Sheriff's Deputy Sgt. Durham. He was initially taken to Livingston Regionally Hospital, and then he was transferred to Cookeville Regional Hospital. He died the following day on Sunday June 24. ||The Junebug Boogie festival is held every summer on private property in the Waterloo area of Overton County. It draws motorcycle and music fans from all over the country. It features shows, games, exhibitions, and contests in the open air. The festival ran for four days from June 21 through June 24.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A backdoor cold front and mid-level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass during the afternoon of the 2nd, which resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms across northern New York that moved into Vermont. Some of these thunderstorms were locally severe, which produced damaging winds that knocked down trees and powerlines in South Burlington and Richmond (Chittenden county) as well as Barre (Washington county) and North Williamstown (Orange county). A tin barn was collapsed by thunderstorm winds in Bradford (Orange county). In addition, some of these severe storms produced large hail of 3/4 inch in diameter or greater, including just shy of golf ball size in Moretown (Washnigton county), nickel size hail in South Burlington (Chittenden county) and East Barre (Washington). ||In addition, the bell tower of the Old Brick Church in Williston (Chittenden county) was struck by lightning that caused a fire to the structure. Also, lightning struck a home in South Burlington (Chittenden county) which resulted in a minor fire and structural damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the bell tower of the Old Brick Church in Williston. This caused a subsequent fire that resulted in significant structural damage to the historic church built in 1832.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A backdoor cold front and mid-level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass during the afternoon of the 2nd, which resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms across northern New York that moved into Vermont. Some of these thunderstorms were locally severe, which produced damaging winds that knocked down trees and powerlines in South Burlington and Richmond (Chittenden county) as well as Barre (Washington county) and North Williamstown (Orange county). A tin barn was collapsed by thunderstorm winds in Bradford (Orange county). In addition, some of these severe storms produced large hail of 3/4 inch in diameter or greater, including just shy of golf ball size in Moretown (Washnigton county), nickel size hail in South Burlington (Chittenden county) and East Barre (Washington). ||In addition, the bell tower of the Old Brick Church in Williston (Chittenden county) was struck by lightning that caused a fire to the structure. Also, lightning struck a home in South Burlington (Chittenden county) which resulted in a minor fire and structural damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a single family home on Bluestar Lane, which resulted in a fire that damaged the roof and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms dropped up to 1/2 inch diameter hail and produced lightning.  Lightning struck a tree near Sedro Woolley and the current hit 5 people sheltering under a gazebo next to the tree. All five were taken to the hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Skagit county sheriff reported that 5 people were injured and taken to the hospital after lightning struck a tree near Sedro Woolley and the current hit the five sheltering under a gazebo near to the tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After an extended period of dry conditions, a widespread thunderstorm event during the afternoon and early evening hours brought welcome rain to the area, but unfortunately a number of severe thunderstorms as well.  The thunderstorms were fueled by a stationary front lying across central Georgia combined with a short wave in northwest flow aloft as a large trough developed across the eastern U.S.  Most of the events were characterized by marginal severe thunderstorm wind and hail events.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck the Dacula Fire Station on Old Fountin Road.  Damage was minor and confined to electronic equipment and the phone system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 27 foot sailboat sank near Blackwell Island in Coeur D'Alene after lightning struck the sailboat.  An electrical charge from the lightning also traveled up power lines to a home and blew out two TV's and damaged several electrical sockets.  Other homes and businesses received minor damage.  Lightning struck a business putting a hole in a concrete wall.  About 2,000 power outages resulted from the storm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system dived southeast across Upstate New York and Northeast Pennsylvania, bringing showers and thunderstorms to the area during the afternoon. Scattered thunderstorms produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was on fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system dived southeast across Upstate New York and Northeast Pennsylvania, bringing showers and thunderstorms to the area during the afternoon. Scattered thunderstorms produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were struck by lightning in Hamlin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced damaging winds, hail and lightning to portions of Leon, Calhoun and Wakulla counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas meter on the side of a house in the 500 block of Meadow Ridge Drive.  The meter caught fire and spread to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced damaging winds, hail and lightning to portions of Leon, Calhoun and Wakulla counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a home in the 1700 block of Silverwood Drive.  Part of the roof collapsed.  A firefighter rescued the occupant's cat.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced damaging winds, hail and lightning to portions of Leon, Calhoun and Wakulla counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused signficant damage to a home at Balmoral Drive and Windermere Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system over the Dakotas moved east-southeast through Wisconsin.  It was aided by a strong short wave trough aloft and a cold front dropping southeast.  Short bowing segments of storms generated damaging winds, large hail, and heavy rains that led to localize flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Slinger, and the resultant fire damaged only the living room and electrical wiring.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms rolled across western Maine on the afternoon of July 6, producing numerous reports of large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the chimney of a house in Lewiston and blew it apart.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid and upper level trough moving southward across Florida on July 21st destabilized the atmosphere and set the state for severe afternoon thunderstorms across Southeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the 1500 block of NW 167th Avenue in Pembroke Pines. The attic was filled with smoke and a vent on the home was charred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid and upper level trough moving southward across Florida on July 21st destabilized the atmosphere and set the state for severe afternoon thunderstorms across Southeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The landmark Casa Amado mansion at 455 North County Road which was undergoing renovations was severely damaged by an apparent lightning strike. The mansion was totaled, with damage estimated at $15 million or more. ||The fire department was called in at 1135 PM after calls reporting smoke were received. Storms affected the area sometime around 230 PM, which is the time the lightning strike was believed to have occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms rolled across New Hampshire during the afternoon of July 6, producing numerous reports of large hail and wind damage, and several damaging lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn in Sutton which ignited a fire that destroyed the barn.  A truck, trailer, and hay were also lost in the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hail up to the size of nickels was noted over sections of Custer County, and lightning struck a house in northwest Colorado Springs, setting it on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Woodmen Valley subdivision, and the subsequent fire was put out after an hour.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Upson County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home in town on Thurston Avenue.  Minor damage was reported to the clothes dryer, where the lightning strike occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front near the Georgia/Tennessee line and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable air mass to produce widespread thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe producing hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An amateur radio operator relayed a report of two lightning-related house fires.  The Clayton County Emergency Management Director reported that one of the homes suffered substantial damage when lightning started a fire in the drop ceiling of the basement when it struck a panel box outside of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 20-year old man in Boca Raton during the afternoon of July 30th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 20-year-old male was struck while lightning while playing soccer at Lake Wyman Park in Boca Raton. The victim went to the hospital and died 3 days later. Time of lightning strike is estimated.||A thunderstorm had passed through the park and the victim along with a group of friends took refuge in a park restroom. After the rain stopped, the group went back outside. Lightning struck shortly thereafter, striking the ground near the victim and traveled along the wet grass, entering the victim's left foot. There was a hole in his left shoe and both his socks were burned off.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system over the Dakotas moved east-southeast through Wisconsin.  It was aided by a strong short wave trough aloft and a cold front dropping southeast.  Short bowing segments of storms generated damaging winds, large hail, and heavy rains that led to localize flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 2-story Janesville home was destroyed by a fire after ligntning struck it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad area of weak low pressure aloft persisted across the south central and southeast U.S.  This resulted in a continuation of scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms across the southern states.  Storms on this particular day were all non-severe, although many produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  Isolated storms produced locally heavy rain and wind gusts up to 40 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fayette County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck two homes, one in Peachtree City on Smokey Way and another in Fayetteville on Chateau Drive.  Moderate damage resulted to both structures.  In addition, a person was struck and injured by lightning on Winter Valley Court in Fayetteville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced damaging winds, hail and lightning to portions of Leon, Calhoun and Wakulla counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the 5000 block of Shady View Lane.  The fire spread in the the attic and through the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck five separate homes in Washington Township, a shed and another home in Franklin Township and caused several brush fires in the two townships. The worst reported damage occurred to a home on Jacqueline Place (Franklin Township) that had its chimney destroyed by a lightning strike. Downed wires (by lightning) also caused several traffic light outages. No serious injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Daytime heating produced scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms June 28, 2007. Some of the thunderstorms produced dangerous lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Abbington Wood Subdivision in Bartlett. The lightning strike produced a fire in the home causing severe damage. No injuries occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front located over the Great Lakes approached the region from the west late Monday, July 9th. A prefrontal trough well ahead of this front, in conjunction with a lake breeze boundary, and a hot, humid and unstable air mass in place, led to the rapid development of scattered strong to locally severe thunderstorms across portions of eastern New York State and western New England during the late afternoon and early evening hours of Monday.||In addition, some thunderstorms contained locally intense rainfall rates of 2 or more inches per hour.  This led to localized flash flooding in urbanized areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Park Playhouse at Albany's Washington Park sustained significant damage from a lightning strike, which occurred around 18:30 EST. Estimated damages were around $10,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along the west coast sea breeze front late in the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 53-year-old man was struck by lightning while standing on a pier on the Caloosahatchee River near Freemont Street. He was taken to the hospital and died the next day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: For the fourth consecutive day, strong afternoon thunderstorms affected Southeast Florida. The strongest storms affected Miami-Dade County with flooding and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on SW 13th Street in the Little Gables area was struck by |lightning. The bolt struck a tree before hitting the house, scattering pieces of the roof across the street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from afternoon thunderstorms struck a man in Miami Lakes on July 8th. The man died 5 days later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40-year-old man was struck by lightning while walking door to door along NW 199th Street in Miami Lakes. The man was taken to the Ryder Trauma Center where he died 5 days later.||Light rain was falling at the time of the lightning strike, although there were no dark clouds directly overhead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper air disturbance combined with an unseasonably hot and humid air mass to trigger pulse type thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 10th in eastern Pennsylvania. In addition to being prolific cloud-to-ground lightning producers, a few thunderstorms also became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes across Northampton County caused damage to a few structures. In Bethlehem Township, a house burst into flames after lightning struck a chimney and traveled downward to the gas fireplace. Four fire companies battled the blaze. A firefighter was unhurt after he fell through a ceiling. In Wilson Borough, lightning struck and obliterated a chimney. The debris damaged a minivan parked on Lehigh Street. In Palmer Township, a lightning strike damaged a shed. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several severe thunderstorms caused damage across Central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Dry Creek Road, causing it to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moving across Nebraska helped thunderstorm development ahead of a cold front.  There were isolated reports of severe weather with these storms across the eastern Nebraska and southwest Iowa region, including one tornado near Uehling Nebraska.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Fremont County Sheriff's Department communication tower causing severe damage to nearly everthing electrical in the building.  Total damage to repair or replace the items was estimated at around $100,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms affected parts of South Florida during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 2nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three men were struck by lightning while moving furniture in LaBelle. They were taken to a nearby hospital as a precaution. One of the victims was knocked unconscious for a few minutes, then complained of pain in his chest and throat after regaining consciousness.  Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm, very moist and unstable airmass, combined with the approach of a weak cold front from the west, led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the evening hours on Friday July 27th. ||Frequent cloud to ground lightning accompanied these thunderstorms, in addition to locally heavy rain and gusty winds. Lightning caused two structure fires in Bennington, destroying one building, and causing approximately $750,000 in damage to another.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Green Mountain Christian Center on Harwood Hill Road in Bennington at around 20:55 EST, causing severe damage. One firefighter suffered heat exhaustion while trying to extinguish the blaze, and was sent to the hospital for examination. He was given fluids and then released.||The estimated damages to the church were around $750,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow-moving cold front entered Arkansas, colliding with low-level Gulf moisture that was greater-than-normal for September, as well as some middle and upper level atmospheric moisture from the remains of Pacific Hurricane Henriette. The result was periodic heavy rain and flash flooding from the 7th through the 10th. A cold front moving through the state finally pushed the moisture south of Arkansas on the night of the 10th and the morning of the 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree behind a home, then traveled through a propane gas line to the lower portion of a deck on an enclosed porch. The porch caught fire in two places. There was also some electrical damage inside the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms on July 4th contained frequent lightning which caused damage to several structures. About 10,000 customers lost power in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three homes were struck by lightning in Boynton Beach during a 48-minute period on July 4th. The area affected was between Congress Avenue and Jog Road. ||One home in the 12300 block of Forest Greens Drive suffered about $100,000 in fire and smoke damage to the attic. A second home in the 9700 block of Coronado Lakes Drive suffered about $25,000 in damage when a tower atop the home was struck, with tiles being torn off the roof. ||The third home suffered the most damaged, estimated at $750,000, in the 4100 block of Juniper Terrace. Fire started in the attic and eventually collapsed a portion of the roof. Sixty percent of the roof burned away.||Over 600 lightning strikes were recorded in Palm Beach County between 3 and 5 PM.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms on July 4th contained frequent lightning which caused damage to several structures. About 10,000 customers lost power in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in The Redland, displacing a family of eight. The lightning bolt struck a corner of the house and started a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system over the Dakotas moved east-southeast through Wisconsin.  It was aided by a strong short wave trough aloft and a cold front dropping southeast.  Short bowing segments of storms generated damaging winds, large hail, and heavy rains that led to localize flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an 150-year-old building's TV antenna, resulting in an attic fire.  Damage was limited to the attic and one apartment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak upper level energy interacted with old outflow boundaries and rich tropical moisture.  Lightning was prolific and caused numerous fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and caused significant electrical damage to an SUV travelling on Highway 380, one mile east of Highway 289.  Post analysis found that the lightning bolt entered the vehicle through the radio antenna, caused scorching of the paint under the antenna, and exited through the ABS speed sensors located on the wheel drums.  Significant damage occurred to the vehicle's electronic computer systems, wiring harness and window motors.  Damage to the vehicle was reported at $7,347.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms rolled across New Hampshire during the afternoon of July 6, producing numerous reports of large hail and wind damage, and several damaging lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn in Sunapee iqniting a fire that burned the structure to the ground.  Several pigs were lost in the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at a power plant in the Wausau area caused considerable damage to a power plant there.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 321 megawatt power plant in the Wausau area, causing damage severe enough to keep it off-line until late 2007 or early 2008.  In addition to the cost of repairs to the plant, the utility company will have to pay at least an addition $30 million to purchase power to replace the amount that would have been generated by the plant while repairs are made.  The plant was equipted with a state-of-the-art lightning suppression system that was operational at the time of the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed in southeast New Hampshire and quickly moved into southwestern Maine on the morning of the 27th producing large hail and damaging winds. Lightning struck an abandoned house being used for storage in Sabattus during the early afternoon and burned it to the ground.  An isolated severe thunderstorm also affected Franklin County in northern Maine in the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a smoky fire in an ocean-front home in South Bristol.  The fire struck some nearby trees and apparently entered the home through the electrical system.  The fire smoldered for several hours before it was discovered.  Damage is estimated at $100,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced excessive lighting in the coastal counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in Palm Bay.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure center moving across Arkansas brought numerous thunderstorms and locally heavy rain on the morning of the 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the eastern part of Diaz. Apparently, the resulting fire smoldered for about two hours before the fire was noticed. Visibility was poor at the time, due to fog and continuous rain. By the time the fire alarm was turned in, flames were shooting well above the roof. The house was destroyed, and an elderly couple who lived there lost their lives. The fatalities were a male, 73, and a female, 70. A camping trailer and an all-terrain vehicle, which were parked near the house, were also damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike knocked out power to Hughes Stadium; after hitting a transformer.  It delayed the start of the Colorado State University-Air Force football game.  The outage lasted approximately 10 minutes and affected 135 Xcel customers.  Thunderstorms east and south of Denver also produced hail up to nickel size.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from early morning thunderstorms caused damage in Jefferson.  Lightning struck and ignited a fire that destroyed two outbuildings at a home in the town.  Damage was estimated at $100,000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes from thunderstorms moving through western Maine damaged several structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and ignited a fire that caused an estimated $5000 in damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes from thunderstorms moving through western Maine damaged several structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that consumed a auto repair garage and shed. One vehicle and a mobile home used for storage were damaged in the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local Atlanta television stations reported that lightning struck and set on fire a home in Morrow.  The event was being covered live via a television helicopter.  The Daily Herald of McDonough reported that lightning struck the steeple of Dixon Grove Baptist Churchon Fielder Street in Jonesboro.  There was a small fire at the base of the steeple where it connected to the roof.  In addition, lightning knocked out power to the Clayton State University Campus causing cancellation of all classes for the remainder of the day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An intense thunderstorm developed over the central and southern portions of Huntsville dumping excessive rainfall in a very short period of time. Rainfall amounts over 3 inches were reported via a fairly dense network of automated and manual rain gages in this area.  Peak rainfall rates of up to 6 inches per hour were observed during a 20 minute time span. This led to quick runoff and flash flooding in low lying areas of south Huntsville which impacted several residences about one mile south of downtown.  Flash flooding was also reported on several busy streets.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a small attic fire at a residence.  Total damages unknown and time was estimated.

Rainfall amounts over 3 inches were reported via a fairly dense network of automated and manual rain gages in this area.  Peak rainfall rates of up to 6 inches per hour were observed during a 20 minute time span.
