EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power substation on Chaney Thompson Road causing a power outage affecting 1900 customers.  Lightning also struck a substation in downtown Huntsville affecting 300 customers. Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Milbank and caused some damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Milbank damaging some of the siding, sheet rock, electrical wiring and outlets, and blew a chunk of cement out of the basement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weather disturbance combined with deep moisture and instability to produce severe thunderstorms with damaging winds and large hail over portions of northeast Minnesota from the afternoon hours of September 20 through midday September 21. ||One storm over Pine County brought strong straight line winds that downed numerous trees and braches. Some minor structural damage was observed in Pine City and along County Road 7 just west of town. There was also minor damage to fences, outbuildings, and two baseball fields at Pine City High School.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A garage in Grand Lake Township was destroyed by fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Somersworth igniting a fire in the roof and attic.  The remainder of the home suffered smoke and water damage.  A women and 16-week-old child who were at home at the time were able to escape uninjured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Red Canyon Water Treatment Plant in the Uinta Mountains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Red Canyon Water Treatment Plant and destroyed the transducer.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved through Southeast Michigan during the peak heating of the day and led to another big event, especially for late August. Severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging wind gusts impacted nearly all of Southeast Lower Michigan, including all neighboring marine areas. A couple of storms across the Thumb showed rotation and prompted the issuance of a couple of tornado warnings. No tornadoes were reported. Lightning struck the National Weather Service office during this event, causing total damages in excess of $15K.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The local newspaper reported a home destroyed by fire after being struck by lightning during a violent thunderstorm. Total property damages were estimated at roughly $175K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak back door cold front was approaching north and east Georgia from the Carolinas.  Meanwhile...aloft a large upper high remained centered just west of the area.  These features combined with hot afternoon temperatures and a moist low-level air mass to result in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The activity was somewhat more widespread, more intense, and further north than had been observed on several previous days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fayette County Emergency Management Director reported that at least three homes and one business were struck by lighting resulting in fires and minor to moderate damage to the structures.  A home on New Castle Drive in Fayetteville was a total loss and suffered $275,000 in damages.  Another home on Georgia Highway 314 suffered $100,000 in damages, another on Buckeye Lane $10,000, and minor damage to a business at the Fayette Pavilion Shopping Center about two miles north of Fayetteville.  There were several other lightning related calls to the fire department that evening, but no damage was reported at the other locations.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fayette County Emergency Management Director reported that at least two homes and a work shop sustained damage from lightning strikes and related fires.  A home in the Lakemont Subdivision southwest of Fayetteville on Wind Ridge Dr was a total loss with $450,000 in damages.  Another home on Creek View Trail northwest of Fayetteville was also a total loss with $250,000 in damages.  In addition, a workshop on the east side of the county on Morgan Mill Road was destroyed with $75,000 in damages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong late July cold front and northwest flow aloft combined with a moist and unstable atmosphere to produce one of the most widespread outbreaks of severe weather seen across the Peachtree City forecast area since mid-April.  The was marked by a mesoscale convective complex which began early in the day across northeast Alabama and quickly spread southeast through west central and into central Georgia during the afternoon.  Numerous reports of large hail were received and wind damage was widespread in the path of the convective complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fayette Citizen reported that lightning struck a home in the Wood Creek subdivision just south of the Peachtree City city limits.  Damage to the home was significant.  In addition, three fire fighters sustained minor injuries while fighting the fire.  The Fayette County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning also struck a home on Stone Haven Drive about 5 miles southwest of Fayetteville.  The home was a total loss from the resulting fire.  Another home in the High Grove subdivision near by suffered minor damage from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving into northwest Georgia combined with abundant low-level moisture and instability, provided the impetus for scattered afternoon thunderstorms once again.  While none of these reached severe limits, an lightning incident was reported from Floyd county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home east of Woodstock.  The home suffered minor damage as a result.  There were also several areas without power because of lightning strikes.  One tree was also down just east of Woodstock.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance and associated cold air aloft combined with marginal surface based instability to produce scattered severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike destroyed chimney on a 2 story single family dwelling. Report received by PEMA via the York county 911 center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The pattern of a broad upper trough in the south central U.S. continued.  This combined with a persistent warm, moist, air mass over the region resulted in yet another afternoon and evening of showers and thunderstorms.  Isolated storms became severe producing damaging downburst winds and marginally severe hail.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was also an issue.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett County Emergency Management Director reported that three homes were struck by lightning, one in Lawrenceville on Polarwood Lane Northwest, another on Wildwood Lake Drive Northwest in Suwanee, and a third on Amsterdam Court in Lilburn.  The only one which sustained any significant damage was the one on Wildwood Lane in Suwanee.  The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a tree next to a home on Coteau Place in Lawrenceville.  The tree fell on the roof of the home causing moderate damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning sparking at least three structure or house fires in Colbert County Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and sparked a fire.  Damage estimates were not available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across North Dakota on the 26th, with a hot and humid airmass in place ahead of the front. At 6 pm CST, a surface low was located over southern Manitoba (Canada), just north of Pembina, ND. The cold front stretched to the southwest, back toward Devils Lake (ND) and Bismarck (ND). Ahead of the cold front, temperatures ranged in the low to mid 80s with dew points around 70F. Behind the front, temperatures did not cool significantly, but dew points dropped to the mid 40s. Thunderstorms began to form along and ahead of the cold front by early evening (from northeast ND into south central ND), eventually crossing into northwest Minnesota several hours later. Eight distinct tornadoes occurred over northeast North Dakota and northwest Minnesota during this event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the bell tower of a church in Bejou, igniting a fire in the tower. The fire spread throughout the building, causing a total loss. The building had been recently renovated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms continued off and on through the day on the 22nd.  As an area of thunderstorms moved across the Centerville area of Appanoose County, lightning struck a utility pole along Iowa Highway 5.  The pole fell onto the roadway, hitting a truck.  One person received minor injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper air disturbance in the northwest flow behind the cold front still had sufficient moisture to develop strong to severe thunderstorms across Pennsylvania and New Jersey during the afternoon and the evening of the 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 45-year-old woman was struck by lightning as she was about to enter a restaurant on U.S. Route 9 North in Howell Township. She was pronounced dead about one hour later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning sparking at least three structure or house fires in Colbert County Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage and sparked a fire.  Exact damage estimates were not available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning sparking at least three structure or house fires in Colbert County Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building and sparked a fire at 190 New Bethel Road in Colbert County.  Exact damage estimate was not available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure was located in southeastern Canada during the early morning hours of August 8th. A cold front associated with this area of low pressure was moving across the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley regions during the morning. Well out ahead of this cold front was a surface trough which moved through the Mid Atlantic region during the very early morning hours on August 8th. A very warm and humid air mass was in place, and with some upper-level energy, a round of showers and thunderstorms moved through parts of eastern Pennsylvania and northern New Jersey and produced wind and lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the ensuing fire destroyed a mobile home in Moore Township. The homeowner was seriously injured. The home was located on Jay Lane within the Manufactured Homes Retirement Community on Pennsylvania State Route 512. Damage to the home was estimated at $55,000.|

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong outflow boundary from a thunderstorm resulted in damage to trees and power lines in Whitman and Asotin counties.  Damages were reported in Pullman, Palouse, Albion, and Clarkston.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger thunderstorms that were prolific lightning producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced about 2,300 cloud-to-surface lightning strikes in Sussex County and the nearby waters between 11 p.m. EDT and Midnight EDT. Two lightning strikes caused damage. Lightning struck the chimney of an unoccupied unit of a townhouse complex in Port Lewes. The ensuing fire spread along the exterior of the unit to the adjoining unit in the complex. The residents of that unit were evacuated. Four fire companies battled the blaze. Damage was estimated at $150,000. No serious injuries were reported. In Rehoboth Beach, the fire station and city hall were struck by lightning. The strike fried the 911 system. The combination of wind and lightning caused about 7,000 homes and businesses to lose power in Sussex County. All power was restored by 3 a.m. EDT on the 17th.|

Some of the thunderstorms turned locally severe and also produced lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Frequent cloud to ground lightning associated with a thunderstorm that moved through Metuchen at 5:20 AM EDT on the 8th struck a house.

Another lightning strike caused an abandoned house fire on Frontage Road in Franklin Township. The house was fully engulfed when fire fighters arrived. The house was planned on being razed for an affordable housing development.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front that was approaching northern New Jersey from the Saint Lawrence Valley initiated thunderstorms northwest of the state. These storms caused lightning damage as they moved through Somerset County late in the evening on the 3rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning and the ensuing fire damaged a Bernardsville Borough home on Ballantine Road. The roof was ablaze when firefighters arrived at the scene. The fire caused water and smoke damage to the roof as well as an upper level multi-purpose room and bathroom.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front that was approaching northern New Jersey from the Saint Lawrence Valley initiated thunderstorms northwest of the state. These storms caused lightning damage as they moved through Somerset County late in the evening on the 3rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire totally destroyed one Franklin Township home on Viscaya Court. Residents inside the home escaped unharmed. The fire also damaged the vinyl siding of four nearby homes. One firefighter was injured battling the blaze. Lightning strikes also caused widely scattered power outages throughout the county, mainly in the central part.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in New London which caused damage to its gable roof and electrical wiring. The concussion from the resultant thunder was so loud it pushed in a wall and blew out several windows of the house. Two neighboring houses also had window damage from the concussion. No one was injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms developed across Southeast Florida due to the interaction of a surface trough across the area and northerly flow aloft associated with a weak mid to upper level low.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 54-year-old man was struck and injured by lightning while leaning against a crane outside a business. Lightning apparently struck the crane and the man felt tingling in his left arm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms developed across Southeast Florida due to the interaction of a surface trough across the area and northerly flow aloft associated with a weak mid to upper level low.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Coral Gables Police reported a house fire off Old Cutler Road caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusual summer cold front continued to move southeast through Georgia.  By afternoon it had moved through the northwest corner of the state.  Northwest flow and cold air aloft continued to provide an unstable air mass across the area.  This combined with daytime heating led to scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms once again.  Isolated storms became severe and most produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Times Georgian of Carrollton reported that a weekend type cabin was destroyed by a fire as a result of a lightning strike.  The cabin was declared a total loss.  The fire was not actually discovered until after a midnight by a driver passing by the scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated severe storm produced damaging winds, and started a house fire, in the North Carolina mountains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that destroyed a house in the Clarks Chapel area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front and unstable airmass produced severe thunderstorms with high winds and intense lightning across portions of northwest Wisconsin on August 13. Lightning struck a home in Grantsburg, causing electrical and structural damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, causing electrical damage. The lightning blew out the garage door opener, internet service, cable, telephone, router, two ethernet connections and tripped three circuits, according to the Burnett County Sentinel. The intense lightning storm also caused many small fires to break out in Burnett County, though most were under one acre in size and no property damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front and unstable air mass contributed to very intense thunderstorm development in northeast Minnesota during the afternoon and evening hours of August 27. One particularly severe thunderstorm produced widespread hail damage in the Big Sandy Lake area of Aitkin County, damaging cars, boats, roofs and sidings of homes. A separate thunderstorm produced a lightning strike that caused extensive damage to Queen of Peace Catholic Church in Cloquet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt caused considerable roof and structural damage to the Queen of Peace Catholic Church. Damage to the electrical, phone, and public address system was also noted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms caused power outages and flash flooding in the Holbrook area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked down power lines and caused power outages in Holbrook.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds across portions of southern New Hampshire during the early afternoon of July 15th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were injured by lightning while they picked raspberries.  The lightning traveled along the metal wires that were supporting the plants.  The most severely injured man suffered burns to his arms and feet and was treated at a nearby hospital.  A pregnant woman was taken to the hospital as a precaution and released.  The third person reported tingling in her arms but refused treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of July 11th...a warm and very moist airmass was draped across Vermont. In addition, a slow moving cold front entered Vermont from west to east during the afternoon. This front promoted the development of numerous tropical-like showers and thunderstorms, that repeatedly generated and moved over the same areas of central and eastern Vermont. Localized heavy rainfall exceeded 3 inches within a two hour time frame with some localized storm totals approaching 6 inches across a very hilly or mountainous terrain, which resulted in flash flooding of several communities. The hardest impacted areas included Barre, Randolph, Bethel, Hardwick, Craftsbury and Stockbridge...with washed out roads, flooded basements and homes damaged or destroyed. ||A Presidential Federal Flood Disaster was declared in Washington, Windsor, Orange, Orleans and Caledonia counties with a estimated storm damage total in excess of 3 million dollars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a horse fence that traveled underground to a propane tank, which started a blaze that destroyed a house and barn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper air disturbance in the northwest flow behind the cold front still had sufficient moisture to develop strong to severe thunderstorms across Pennsylvania and New Jersey during the afternoon and the evening of the 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An unoccupied at the time two-story home's roof was struck by a bolt of lightning in Middletown Township. The bolt started a fire in the attic area of the home. Damage was described as moderate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably warm area of high pressure built across the Mid Atlantic in late September. A cold front moved across the region on September 27, triggering numerous showers and thunderstorms across the eastern pan handle of West Virginia. Several of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds that downed trees and power lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported a structure fire due to lightning on Warm Spring Ave in Hedgesville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low over the northeast U.S. was providing a colder northwest flow aloft to the southeast states.  Meanwhile, a weak front had stalled just south of the area.  Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of the 25th and continued into the early morning hours of the 26th.  A similar situation was repeated during the afternoon of the 26th, although the focus had shifted a little further south into central Georgia at that time.  The storms produced intense cloud-to-ground lightning, marginal severe hail, and some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A storm spotter, amateur radio operator, and the Peachtree Citizen reported that lightning struck and set on fire a home in the Honeysuckle Ridge Subdivision near Georgia Highway 74 and Kedron Drive.  A minor fire in the crawlspace resulted.  Another home on Azalea Drive in Peachtree City suffered minor damage when lightning struck a nearby tree and jumped to a handrail and into the house.  Damage was confined to a portion of an interior wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching warm front helped produce severe thunderstorms and also caused some lightning damage across Eastern Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the peak of a three story house on East Main Street in Kutztown. The ensuing fire caused the ceiling to collapse in one apartment before the fire was extinguished. Damage was estimated at $10,000. About 1,500 homes and businesses lost power throughout the county due to the combination of damaging winds and lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pre-frontal clusters of thunderstorms became severe with powerful straight-line winds as they moved east-southeast at anywhere from 35 to 45 knots (40 to 52 mph) to the east-southeast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a blew apart a 60-foot pine tree which was about 30 feet from a residential home.  Part of the generated electrical current fried the home's telephone line.   The time is estimated within a plus or minus 15 minutes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front helped trigger thunderstorms that were  prolific cloud-to-ground lightning producers during the late afternoon and early evening of the 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A series of thunderstorms over a period of three hours produced about 1100 cloud-to-surface lightning strikes in Sussex County and Delaware Bay from 4 p.m. EDT through 7 p.m. EDT on the 16th. About ten structures were struck by lightning in and around Lewes. The worst reported property damage was the ensuing fire that occurred after a lightning strike to a Brighton Drive home. The fire damage was estimated at $50,000. The lightning strike in the Sussex East Mobile Home Park started a shed fire which spread to a home, but was quickly extinguished. Two small fires were started by lightning strikes to homes in the Eagle Point Landing Development. Another lightning strike occurred at an apartment building at the Village of Five Points development. Lightning struck a Home Depot twice on Delaware State Route 1. Lightning also struck the Furniture Galley on Delaware State Route 1 and Practically Yours on U.S. Route 9. No serious injuries were reported with any of the fires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low over the northeast U.S. was providing a colder northwest flow aloft to the southeast states.  Meanwhile, a weak front had stalled just south of the area.  Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of the 25th and continued into the early morning hours of the 26th.  A similar situation was repeated during the afternoon of the 26th, although the focus had shifted a little further south into central Georgia at that time.  The storms produced intense cloud-to-ground lightning, marginal severe hail, and some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local Atlanta broadcast media reported that a house was set on fire by a lightning strike on Oakland Trace near Oglethorpe University.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a severe thunderstorm and lightning damage in Sussex County on the afternoon of the 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a few homes across Sussex County between 330 p.m. EDT and 415 p.m. EDT on the 28th. A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a Kelley Circle home near Seaford. In addition to wind damage elsewhere, lightning struck a home on Clayton Street in Frankford. The ensuing fire damaged the outer wall of the home. Three fire companies assisted in battling the blaze. The worst reported damage occurred to a home struck by lightning in Lewes. Lightning struck a home in the Bay Crossing Community on Anchor Way. Four fire companies fought the ensuing blaze which caused heavy damage to the second floor and roof of the home. No serious injuries were reported with any of the fires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure moved across Ontario and Quebec provinces in Canada on the 9th, while its associated occluded frontal boundaries moved across Vermont during the late morning through early evening hours. Numerous areas of thunderstorms occurred across the region with a wide variety of weather conditions, which included very large hail, damaging winds and several structures struck by lightning. Baseball size hail was reported in Duxbury (Washington county). Lightning struck a house in Barre (Washington county), destroyed a barn in Bakersfield (Franklin county) as well as destroyed one camp and severely damaged another camp in Randolph (Orange county).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a brick chimney at 14 Lauren Avenue in Barre and damaged the chimney.

A portion of the roof and burned and extensive damage resulted to much of the second floor of the home.  The occupants were displaced from their home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure aloft was still the primary weather feature for the area.  However, the center of the high had drifted west of the region, allowing northwest flow aloft to develop over the region. A weak cold front was located across central Georgia.  This provided the focus for scattered afternoon thunderstorms.  A few of these storms became strong to severe, with damaging wind the primary element observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Toombs County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck his home.  While no fire was reported, the refrigerator was rendered inoperative as a result.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Sumter County Emergency Management Director reported that a home was struck by lightning in the city.  Exact damage amounts were not determinable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure moved across the eastern Great Lakes region during the morning of August 25th. A cold front associated with this low pressure system was located in the Ohio Valley. A hot and especially humid airmass was found ahead of this front across the Middle Atlantic region on August 25th. As the front approached, showers and thunderstorms developed and moved across the area. The actual cold front however did not clear the region until the morning of the 26th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A small cluster of thunderstorms moved across Warren County during the evening of the 25th. Lightning produced from these thunderstorms caused 6,000 JCP&L customers to lose power in Warren and Hunterdon Counties.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As low-level moisture spread across north Texas, a cold front moved through during the afternoon and evening hours.  A few reports of severe weather were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused power outages near Lake Bonham.

Lightning struck the steeple of the Great Shepard Christian Fellowship Church in Plainfield Township at 9:50 PM EDT. This resulted in a fire, which caused an estimated $250,000 in damage. In addition, lightning struck a saw mill in Upper Mount Bethel Township, sparking a fire at about 10:15 PM EDT. The saw mill was destroyed, which resulted in $1 million dollars in loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rain-producing showers and thunderstorms moved across eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois during the evening and overnight hours of July 18th.  A bowing segment of thunderstorms pushed east southeast across areas from just south of Waterloo, IA to the Quad Cities producing widespread wind damage, torrential rainfall, and an isolated tornado near Paris, IA.  Rainfall totals ranged between three quarters of an inch to just under 3 inches, but due to saturated soils some flooding problems developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Iwv Rd SW south of Oxford, IA around 2 AM causing a fire.  The homeowner was able to extinguish most of the fire.  Minor fire and smoke damage was reported.  Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late-season surge of monsoon moisture was already in place when the remnant circulation of former Atlantic Hurricane Dean moved over southern Nevada during the pre-dawn hours of August 27th, resulting in major flooding.  Damage figures were not available at this time, but will likely run well into the millions.  In addition, there were 22 swift water rescues in the Las Vegas Valley during the height of the flooding.  Despite the magnitude of the flooding, no deaths or serious injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The same storms which were responsible for major flooding also produced lightning strikes which set fire to at least ten buildings and more than 20 trees.  Damage figure is an estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated pulse thunderstorms produced lightning over central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A school crossing guard was struck and injured by lightning while on duty in Winter Park. He was hospitalized with burns and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed out ahead of a shortwave trough tracking across Wyoming during the afternoon hours of the 17th.  A weak differential heating boundary located in the vicinity of the Kansas/Nebraska border also served as a focus for convective development. Scattered reports of non-severe hail and thunderstorm winds gusts filtered in, along with one report of severe hail and one severe damaging wind gust.  The most damaging report received though, was due to lightning.  One woman in Topeka died several days after being struck by lightning shortly after 4pm on the 17th.  A man was injured when a building next to his was struck by lightning, and the bolt traveled through a wire and into the lamp he had been holding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning near the 2700 block on SW Villa West Dr. in Topeka.  She was originally taken to the hospital with life-threatening injuries, and later passed away as a reult of these injuries. A second man was struck by a lightning bolt in an open air garage next to his home. The bolt struck his house, traveled through a cord, and into the light the man was holding.  He was knocked unconscious, needed to be recussitated, and ended up with injuries to his arm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm, humid and unstable airmass was located across Vermont during the afternoon of the 25th, with temperatures in the upper 80s to lower 90s and dewpoints around 70 degrees. A surface cold front was located across Ontario and Quebec, with a mid-atmospheric disturbance that moved across the North Country during the afternoon and early evening. This triggered numerous thunderstorms in New York, that intensified as they moved across Vermont. An unseasonably strong wind field aloft fueled the development of severe thunderstorms that produced widespread damaging winds and some large hail across central, southern and eastern Vermont. Some of the hardest hit communities included Barre (Washington county), Rutland and vicinity (Rutland county) and Woodstock (Windsor county).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Memorial building, home to town offices including the police department, which caused minor structural damage but did damage many electronic and communication systems within the building.

A surface cold front was located across Ontario and Quebec, with a mid-atmospheric disturbance that moved across the North Country during the afternoon and early evening. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a small hay barn, which started a fire that eventually destroyed the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was located across central Georgia.  An inverted trough was moving west through the eastern Gulf.  These combined to result in the typical summertime afternoon and evening thunderstorms, a few of which became strong to severe.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was particularly significant with the thunderstorms on this day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Barrow County 911 Center reported that two power lines were down as the result of lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was located across central Georgia.  An inverted trough was moving west through the eastern Gulf.  These combined to result in the typical summertime afternoon and evening thunderstorms, a few of which became strong to severe.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was particularly significant with the thunderstorms on this day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Washington County 911 Center reported that lightning started a brush fire along Montgmery Road in the southwest part of the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A typical summertime pattern continued across north and central Georgia as high pressure aloft drifted just west of the area.  The storms were very small, but with high temperatures near 100 across the area, the dissipating storms were capable of wind damage.  Such occurred with one small storm in Oconee county which produced a downburst and brought down a number of trees and power lines in the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Oconee County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a building in the city and set it on fire.  A damage amount was indeterminable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was approaching the area from the northwest as the upper ridge, which had persisted over the area much of the month, retreated back to the west and a weak trough of low pressure developed over the eastern U.S.  As with previous days, thunderstorms developed rapidly during the mid-afternoon and quickly moved south.  However, the activity was in general less numerous and less intense than on previous days.  The main problem this day was cloud-to-ground lightning and gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Alpharetta Fire & Rescue Department reported that a 15-year old male was killed from a lightning strike.  The individual was riding his bicycle with a group of friends in a parking lot at an apartment complex in the vicinity of 500 Governor's Circle.  The group attempted to seek shelter from the thunderstorm under a gazebo.  However, the victim was unable to seek shelter before the incident occurred.  He was found unconscious in the parking lot next to his bicycle and was pronounced dead at North Fulton Regional Hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front dropped southeast from the Great Lakes through central New York and northeast Pennsylvania during the evening. Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the boundary during the afternoon and evening hours. There were numerous reports of large hail and wind damage from these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree and a house were struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure aloft was reasserting itself over the southeast states, a weak front was draped across north Georgia.  This combined with northwest flow aloft, hot surface temperatures, and a very moist and unstable air mass resulted in yet another day of scattered to numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms, several of which became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Forsyth County Emergency Management Director reported that two homes were struck and set on fire by lightning.  One of the homes sustained substantial damage.  Damage to the other home was less severe, but still significant.  Lightning also struck a transformer in the area and left about 5000 residents in the area without power for several hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Erin, the fifth named storm of the 2007 Atlantic Hurricane season, developed quickly over the northeast Gulf of Mexico on the 15th, before moving onshore during the morning hours of the 16th. Erin moved onshore near Lamar, TX as a weak tropical storm, but was quickly downgraded to a tropical depression as it moved over land. The tropical depression moved northwest over the Edwards Plateau toward west Texas. Erin maintained her depression status as it then began to move northeast into southwest Oklahoma between Hollis and Erick during the afternoon hours of Saturday, August 18th. A very tropical airmass was in place along and east of this feature, extending into western and central Oklahoma. Heavy rainfall developed along and east of the center, which moved slowly to the northeast. Low-level wind shear north and east of Erin increased throughout the evening, with several tornadoes reported in Kiowa, Washita, and Grady counties during the late afternoon and early evening hours. Damage was reported east of Hobart, and in Washita county south and east of Cordell. As the evening progressed, a strong low-level jet developed, with additional thunderstorms developing over southwest and central Oklahoma. Remarkably, the center of the tropical depression strengthened between 1 and 7 AM, with a compact area of sustained winds of 35 to 45 MPH concentrated around the center of the depression. Wind gusts of 50 to 80 mph were also reported over parts of central Oklahoma at this time. As with the wind speeds, thunderstorms intensities increased, with two additional tornadoes reported over central Oklahoma Sunday morning. In addition to tornadoes and very strong winds, rainfall rates of over three inches per hour were common, with significant flash flooding reported in numerous counties. Rainfall amounts exceeded five inches over a large area, with some locations receiving eight to ten inches. Rivers and creeks easily exceeded their banks, with water also rising quickly in many towns. Dozens of people were rescued by boat and helicopter as numerous homes and businesses quickly took on water. Unfortunately, six people lost their lives due to the flooding. Monetary values were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning and burned to the ground. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was approaching the area from the northwest as the upper ridge, which had persisted over the area much of the month, retreated back to the west and a weak trough of low pressure developed over the eastern U.S.  As with previous days, thunderstorms developed rapidly during the mid-afternoon and quickly moved south.  However, the activity was in general less numerous and less intense than on previous days.  The main problem this day was cloud-to-ground lightning and gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Americus Times Recorder reported that lightning struck and killed four horses that were grazing in a pasture off Georgia Highway 377 in the central part of the county, south of Americus.  The horses were huddled under a pecan tree when they were struck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms moved through the area producing flooding rains and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at the First Church United in West Liberty, IA on August 8th.  Time estimated.  Electricity and phone services were lost.  One computer was damaged at the church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved through Southeast Michigan during the peak heating of the day and led to another big event, especially for late August. Severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging wind gusts impacted nearly all of Southeast Lower Michigan, including all neighboring marine areas. A couple of storms across the Thumb showed rotation and prompted the issuance of a couple of tornado warnings. No tornadoes were reported. Lightning struck the National Weather Service office during this event, causing total damages in excess of $15K.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the National Weather Service office. Total damages to upper air equipment, Doppler Radar, telephone services, and miscellaneous items were estimated at approximately $16K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms affected much of northern Indiana during the morning hours. One storm produced isolated wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two (2) separate bolts of lightning struck 2 South Bend residences during the morning hours. A house was struck, causing a fire that destroyed the top floor. The 2 occupants of the house were able to escape without injury. Damage is estimated at $80,000. Lightning struck an apartment, causing significant damage to a kitchen and two bathrooms. A woman and her 4 sons were able to escape unharmed. Damage is estimated at $40,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large and intense upper ridge covered most of the southern U.S.  This resulted in maximum temperatures reaching the 100 to 105 range across much of north and central Georgia.  While the atmosphere was very stable, the intense heat combined with low-level moisture resulted in isolated afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  The storms were small and short-lived, but one produced a damaging wind gust in Jones county during the evening.  Cloud-to-ground lightning was also a problem.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Columbus Ledger-Inquirer reported that lightning struck near a school complex causing damage to the fire alarm systems and air conditioners at three schools, Carver Middle School, Harris County High School, and Mulberry Creek Elementary school.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving into northwest Georgia combined with abundant low-level moisture and instability, provided the impetus for scattered afternoon thunderstorms once again.  While none of these reached severe limits, an lightning incident was reported from Floyd county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a tree causing it to fall down onto a home.  Minor damage resulted.  In addition, wind gusts from thunderstorms caused three trees to be blown down in Rome.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms affected much of northern Indiana during the morning hours. One storm produced isolated wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 2200 block of Pleasant Ave in Fort Wayne. The attic suffered moderate damage from the fire, smoke and water, estimated at $20,000. The residents of the house were evacuated by a nearby Kelly Automotive employee who witnessed the bolt of lightning strike the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary across central New York State gradually moved east during Thursday afternoon on September 27th. With a very warm, moist and unstable air mass in place to the east of this boundary, scattered strong to isolated severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern New York State Thursday afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Fourth Street in Hudson Falls at approximately 1745 LST. The lightning is believed to have struck a cable antenna on the roof, which consequently started a fire and then spread.||The fire caused extensive damage to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was blamed for a fire that destroyed a 180-year-old home at Bayville Golf Club.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was blamed for a fire that destroyed a 180-year-old home at Bayville Golf Club.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms moved across eastern Iowa with a few producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Coralville, IA during the late morning hours of August 23rd.  Time estimated.  Firefighters responded at 11:30 am and had the fire under control by 11:45 am.  Fire and smoke damage was confined to the lower level of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was approaching the area from the northwest as the upper ridge, which had persisted over the area much of the month, retreated back to the west and a weak trough of low pressure developed over the eastern U.S.  As with previous days, thunderstorms developed rapidly during the mid-afternoon and quickly moved south.  However, the activity was in general less numerous and less intense than on previous days.  The main problem this day was cloud-to-ground lightning and gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Alpharetta Fire & Rescue Department reported that lightning struck a home and set it on fire.  Fire officials estimated a 30 percent less of the structure as a result of the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Summertime pulse thunderstorms produced hail, wind damage, lightning and funnel clouds over central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A small boat was struck by lightning in the Halifax River. The two people on board were transported to a local hospital with minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck homes in the Brownsburg and Fishers area as thunderstorms moved through the area during the early hours of November 11, 2007.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Fishers during the morning hours and started a fire.  The fire burned part of the chimney.  The fire caused by the lightning also damaged some of the electrical components inside the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed in southeast New Hampshire and quickly moved into southwestern Maine on the morning of the 27th. Lightning struck a home in Alton and caused a fire that destroyed the structure.   A second round of severe storms formed during the afternoon in northern and western New Hampshire. Both morning and afternoon storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a summer home in Alton and caused a fire that destroyed the structure.  In addition to the home, the fire consumed antiques and hardwood furniture.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast moving squall line caused damage in many parts of northern Indiana before clipping portions of Van Wert county. There were reports of damaging winds and intense lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 40 foot oak tree, causing it to drop onto a home at the intersection of Payne and Convoy roads. Significant damage resulted to the home, but no injuries were reported. Damage is estimated at $65,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-dawn thunderstorm convective complex developed over the Northern Plains and moved southeast across southern Wisconsin.  Some thunderstorm cells were severe with downburst winds.  The complex was associated with an upper-level short-wave trough, while at the surface a warm front extended through northern Illinois back to a low pressure over the Dakotas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas-line meter on the side of a residential home.  The resultant fire damaged the living room and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-dawn thunderstorm convective complex developed over the Northern Plains and moved southeast across southern Wisconsin.  Some thunderstorm cells were severe with downburst winds.  The complex was associated with an upper-level short-wave trough, while at the surface a warm front extended through northern Illinois back to a low pressure over the Dakotas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residential home.  The resultant fire severely damaged the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-dawn thunderstorm convective complex developed over the Northern Plains and moved southeast across southern Wisconsin.  Some thunderstorm cells were severe with downburst winds.  The complex was associated with an upper-level short-wave trough, while at the surface a warm front extended through northern Illinois back to a low pressure over the Dakotas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a business structure. The resultant fire caused minor exterior damage and barely any interior damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-dawn thunderstorm convective complex developed over the Northern Plains and moved southeast across southern Wisconsin.  Some thunderstorm cells were severe with downburst winds.  The complex was associated with an upper-level short-wave trough, while at the surface a warm front extended through northern Illinois back to a low pressure over the Dakotas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residential home and damaged its roof, electrical system and telephone line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusual mid-August cold front combined with antecedent very hot temperatures in the 95 to 100 degree range and northwest flow aloft to create a very unstable atmosphere.  Thunderstorms developed during mid-afternoon in northwest and west central Georgia and quickly became severe.  Thunderstorm wind damage was the most common occurrence with these storms, but some hail was reported with some of the storms, especially those near the beginning of the event.  Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning was observed with many of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Troup County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a home and set it on fire.  Damage estimates to the home were indeterminate.  A couple of trees were also struck by lightning causing them to fall.  An electrical transformer was also struck and rendered inoperative by a lightning strike in the same general area.  Finally, fire fighters responded to a grass fire on Stovall Road that was caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Livermore man was injured when he was struck by lightning while taking a shower inside his home.  He reportedly had his hand on the faucet when the lightning struck.   He was hospitalized after the incident.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Four tornadoes moved through portions of Southeast Michigan on August 24th, leading to an estimated $25M in total damages. One long-track tornado cut a path of EF0 to EF2 damage across Livingston, Geneseee, and Oakland Counties. Fenton was the hardest hit area, prompting the Governor of Michigan to declare a state of emergency there. Tornadoes also touched down in eastern Shiawassee County (rated as EF0), northwestern Washtenaw County (rated as EF0), and southwestern Lapeer County (rated as EF1). Thousands of trees were lost to the tornadoes. Although hundreds of homes and buildings were damaged, many destroyed, remarkably only one person was injured (minor cuts from flying glass) and there were no direct fatalities. One man died (indirect) of a heart attack during the cleanup process in Fenton.|In addition to the tornadoes, there were widespread reports of severe thunderstorm wind gusts producing downed trees, limbs, and power lines. The hardest hit areas with respect to severe thunderstorm winds included areas around Flint, Lapeer, St. Clair, Chelsea, Monroe, and many locations in Livingston, Oakland, Macomb, Wayne and Lenawee Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home caught fire during a heavy storm after it was struck by lightning. Total property damages were estimated at roughly $10K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through parts of eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois producing damaging winds and lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused telephone problems for the East Dubuque area during the early morning hours of August 14th.  Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of storms, with isolated severe cells, affected Rock County overight.  This was the 3rd straight night of thunderstorms over Rock County.  Synpotically, a stall frontal boundary stretched from northern Iowa across extreme southern Wisconsin.  Warm, moist air from the south overran the frontal boundary and triggered the thunderstorm cluster.  Mid-level rotation was noted in the stongest cell, but nothing became of it.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The TV antenna of a residential home was struck by lightning.  The home's electrical system and appliances were fried when an electrical current traveled down from the TV antenna.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms produced gusty winds and lightning that caused some damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer and downed some power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front that moved through Delaware on the night of the 10th triggered thunderstorms that caused lightning damage in Sussex County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire caused a shed fire on a property on Reynolds Pond Road east of Ellendale. Damage was estimated at $5,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was draped across North Georgia.  The remnants of Hurricane Humberto tracked from southern Louisiana during the morning, across central Mississippi during the day, and into northern Alabama and northwest Georgia by evening.  Meanwhile, a strong fall cold front was moving rapidly southeast from the central plains.  The right quadrant of the remnants of Hurricane Humberto tracked across northwest Georgia bringing heavy rain to that portion of the state.  Rainfall amounts of four to six inches occurred across the far northwest portion of Georgia, especially in Murray, Whitfield, and northwestern Fannin counties, but average amounts in this area were more in the two to three inch range.  Some roads were flooded as a result.  In addition, during the afternoon heating, a few thunderstorms became severe across north Georgia producing marginally severe hail and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Murray County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck the fire station.  Several radios and computers were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a 47 year old male while fishing on Upper Greenwood Lake.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced lightning that struck a 47 year old male while fishing in a boat over Upper Greenwood Lake in Passaic County, NJ.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger some isolated thunderstorms across northwest New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A father and his daughter were struck and injured by lightning while boating on Lake Hopatcong near Brady Bridge. They were heading for shelter when the father was struck on the top of his head. Burn marks were found. He was in critical, but stable condition. His 8-year-old daughter was struck while hiding under the driver's console. Her injuries were not as serious. The thunderstorm was not a prolific cloud-to-ground lightning producer, there were only 6 recorded cloud-to-ground or cloud-to-water strikes in and around Lake Hopatcong.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front that moved through Delaware on the night of the 10th triggered thunderstorms that caused lightning damage in Sussex County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an ensuing barn fire on a property on Sussex Highway in Greenwood. Damage was estimated at $25,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moving south across Miami-Dade County produced a lightning strike which injured 3 people in Coral Gables.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three roofers working atop a home in Coral Gables were struck by lightning. The three men were knocked unconscious by the lightning bolt, but regained consciousness by the time they were transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a pre-frontal trough during peak  afternoon heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An unoccupied building in Youngsville was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the mountains and foothills during peak diurnal heating and then moved east into the western piedmont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Southern Lunch restaurant on South Railroad Street burning the building down resulting in a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 33-ft marble statue of Jesus at Mother Cabrini Shrine, in the foothills of Golden.  The blast broke off one of the statue's arms and a hand, and also damaged a foot.  The statue was sent from Italy in five stackable sections in 1954.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed as a trough of low pressure in place across central Florida combined with upper level energy passing over the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On a construction site near Brandon, a 52-year-old man sitting in the cab of a crane was injured when lightning struck the crane's boom. The man suffered burns to his face and was unable to see out of his right eye.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Gusty winds lifted tents, snapped flag poles and damaged scenery that had been installed at Town Point Park in downtown Norfolk. Lightning damage 2 homes, one on Long Point Boulevard in Portsmouth, the other on Cascade Drive in Newport News.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Long Point Boulevard was struck by lightning. The resulting fire damage a large part of the roof and caused some structural damage to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed in southeast New Hampshire and quickly moved into southwestern Maine on the morning of the 27th producing large hail and damaging winds. Lightning struck an abandoned house being used for storage in Sabattus during the early afternoon and burned it to the ground.  An isolated severe thunderstorm also affected Franklin County in northern Maine in the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an old abandoned house that was being used for storage and buned it to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper level storm system moved from the desert southwest into west Texas.  Storms developed along a dry line Sunday evening.  The main area of upper level lift along with an attendant Pacific cold front arrived Monday.  As a result, there were several reports of severe weather and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which fell onto a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper level storm system moved from the desert southwest into west Texas.  Storms developed along a dry line Sunday evening.  The main area of upper level lift along with an attendant Pacific cold front arrived Monday.  As a result, there were several reports of severe weather and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A church on Highway 69 South was hit by lightning and burned to the ground.  The fire marshall reported the building was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Gusty winds lifted tents, snapped flag poles and damaged scenery that had been installed at Town Point Park in downtown Norfolk. Lightning damage 2 homes, one on Long Point Boulevard in Portsmouth, the other on Cascade Drive in Newport News.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Cascade Drive was struck by lightning. The resulting fire destroyed the roof and attic, and caused damage to the second story ceiling.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved south and stalled just south of Cape Lookout. During the afternoon the sea breeze slowly pushed inland and thunderstorms developed on the boundary along the south coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A structure fire caused by lightning was reported off Hibbs Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered pulse thunderstorms during the early evening hours produced localized downbursts, one of which produced a few reports of wind damage in DeKalb County in northeast Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local animal park reported that at least nine cows were struck by lightning and killed on Lookout Mountain near Mentone.  Time and location estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning killed a man in Pinecrest on June 21st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a 41-year-old man who was doing landscape work at a home at 10500 SW 62 Ave in Pinecrest. The man was under a tree when the lightning struck. ||It was not raining at the location of the lightning strike, although a thunderstorm was located about 2 to 3 miles to the north. The media reported this incident as dry lightning striking out of a clear sky, although the lightning bolt likely originated out of the side of the nearby storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms with frequent lightning resulted in 87 fire related calls to New Hanover 911 center.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex on Hearthside Drive, heavily damaging it. Heavy rain also caused street flooding on Dawson Street, Medical Center Drive, and parts of College Road. About 1400 customers lost power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong thunderstorms developed across portions of northwest and north central Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours of June 19th. These storms produced lightning which struck a home in Grant Parish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the town of Bentley, Louisiana. The structure suffered moderate damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two men fishing in a boat on Bayou du Large causing minor to moderate injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After an extended period of dry conditions, a widespread thunderstorm event during the afternoon and early evening hours brought welcome rain to the area, but unfortunately a number of severe thunderstorms as well.  The thunderstorms were fueled by a stationary front lying across central Georgia combined with a short wave in northwest flow aloft as a large trough developed across the eastern U.S.  Most of the events were characterized by marginal severe thunderstorm wind and hail events.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a two-story home on Daniel Park Run.  The attic was burned and the remainder of the home suffered moderate to heavy damage from fire and smoke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small cluster of thunderstorms was moving west to east across Macon County on the evening of July 17. A lightning bolt from a thunderstorm|destroyed a feed barn.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A small cluster of thunderstorms was moving west to east across Macon County on the evening of July 17. A lightning bolt from a thunderstorm|destroyed a feed barn. The barn was located at 3716 Akersville Rd. The Lafayette F.D. was on the scene for about 90 minutes trying to put out the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After an extended period of dry conditions, a widespread thunderstorm event during the afternoon and early evening hours brought welcome rain to the area, but unfortunately a number of severe thunderstorms as well.  The thunderstorms were fueled by a stationary front lying across central Georgia combined with a short wave in northwest flow aloft as a large trough developed across the eastern U.S.  Most of the events were characterized by marginal severe thunderstorm wind and hail events.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Spalding County 911 Center reported that lightning strikes caused a couple of power lines to fall down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface pressure ridge axis extended across southern Florida and the west coast sea breeze front was most active from Tampa through Fort Myers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 16-year-old boy and his mother who were vacationing at the beach.  The bolt hit the boy in the chest, knocking him unconscious and shredding his shorts. The boy was taken to the hospital and died four days later on July 24.  The mother also received a jolt and complained of numbness in her feet and radiating pain reaching her chest.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms over Northern Broward County produced lightning which killed    a 24-year-old man.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 24-year-old man was struck and killed by lightning while doing landscape work at a private residence in Parkland. The man was working with three other men when the lightning struck. It was not raining at the time, but there were dark storm clouds in the distance. None of the other men were injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: June 25th proved to be one of the more significant severe weather days during the month.  This was the result of a strong short wave in westerly flow aloft and a very unstable and moist atmosphere present over the area.  Damaging downburst winds, large hail, and most significantly a number of lightning incidents were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a home on Cross Creek Drive.  The resulting fire caused heavy damage to the attic area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across Davis County during the early morning hours of the 16th.  As they moved across the Bloomfield area, lightning struck the chimney of an old school.  It caused minor damage to the building as the chimney was blown apart and the bricks fell on the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Nocturnal convection developed ahead of the main storm system during the morning hours of October 12th. Warm advection ahead of this system caused numerous thunderstorms to train across Central Kansas with flooding reported around Lincoln, Kansas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong mid and upper level shortwave trough moved across the area as it rotated on the back side of a deep closed upper cyclone off the Northeast Coast. The storms reached peaked intensity during peak heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire began when a a lightning strike burned through the upper floor of a 12 unit apartment building of the Rivers Edge apartment complex. The top floor units were destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low pressure system brought thunderstorms and heavy rain to the Mojave Desert.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to an office complex at Eastern Ave. and Horizon Ridge Pkwy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous waves of thunderstorms affected southeast Michigan during the afternoon and evening of June 27, 2007. Severe storms developed along and ahead of a cold front, which dropped south through a very warm and humid airmass. There were numerous reports of wind damage and hail. Saginaw County received two separate rounds of severe weather, producing hail to one-inch in diameter and a number of reports of trees and power poles blown down by winds. Flooding was also a concern, as some areas were repeatedly affected by complexes of storms. Northern Shiawassee County received the worst flooding, with National Weather Service radar estimating up to six inches of rainfall in just a few hours. A golfer in northwest Detroit was struck by lightning and killed after seeking refuge under a tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A golfer was struck and killed by lightning after seeking refuge under a tree at the Rogell Golf Course near 7 Mile and Lahser Roads.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A major, negatively tilted and closed upper trough rotated through the mid-south and southeast U.S. on March 1st.  A 150kt jet was located over the region at 250mb with a strong 50kt low-level jet from central Alabama into central Tennessee.  A wedge of cool air was present over much of north central and northeast Georgia. Rain, which spread over this area early in the day, helped enhance the wedge of cool air.  Little to no severe weather was noted north of the wedge boundary across north Georgia where the air mass remained relatively cool and stable. Meanwhile...a warm, humid air mass was present across much of central and south Georgia where dewpoints had risen well into the 60s during the afternoon.  The strong upper dynamics present over this region combined with the instability just south of the wedge provided a very favorable environment for long lived, strong tornadoes.  A total of 14 tornadoes affecting 17 counties tracked across central and east central Georgia and within the Peachtree City, Georgia county warning area during the late afternoon and evening hours of March 1st.  This was the second greatest number of tornadoes recorded to have occurred in the Peachtree City, Georgia forecast area within a 24-hour period, second only to the 16 tornadoes, affecting 18 counties, associated with Hurricane Katrina on August 29, 2005.  The March 1st tornadoes spanned an area from Stewart county in the far southwest part of the county warning area to Warren county in the far east central portion of the county warning area.  The first tornado touched down in Stewart county at 4:11 pm EST and the last tornado lifted in Marion county at 10:55 pm EST.  By far the hardest hit county was Sumter county, and especially the city of Americus, where hundreds of homes and business, including the regional hospital, were heavily damaged or destroyed.  Additional tornadoes were reported further south in Tallahassee and Jacksonville's, Florida's forecast areas.  Federal disaster assistance had been approved for 1,836 households across the state for a total of $14.2 million.  Another $5.8 million had been approved for public assistance of debris removal and to repair infrastructure.  The Small Business Association also approved $7 million in disaster assistance loans.  Overall damages, however, are estimated to be several hundred million.|Substantial rainfall fell across much of the state, but rainfall amounts of three to five inches were common across central and east central areas.  The heaviest rainfall fell in the Hancock, Putnam, and Baldwin county areas, where some spots received in excess of six inches of rain.  Some flooding was reported in these areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home on Rivermist Drive causing smoke and fire damage to the roof and attic as well as heavy damage to the second floor.  Two adults living in the home escaped without injury.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms were caused by a cold front that extended from northeast Illinois to the southeast part of Oklahoma.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large tree at a farming complex. The lightning traveled down through the roots to a fence, which caught on fire. A propane line on the fence blew out part of an electrical box inside and outside the home on the property.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early March cold frontal passage created isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning striking a home created moderate roof, attic, ceiling and electrical damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A passing upper level low enhanced sea breeze and outflow initiated convection over an unstable and moist airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a small house fire off of Curt Road. The amount of damage was approximated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unusual winter thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning strikes that knocked out power and damaged at least one home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Johnston blowing off vinyl siding and blowing out a basement window.  Several people were in the house at the time of the strike but none were injured.  No fire was started.  Several other locations were without power due to other lightning strikes in the area, including the Lincoln Mall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper level disturbance with associated cold front pushed across the region the afternoon and evening of December 11. Over 2 inches of rain fell in many locations with several reports of minor urban flooding. One house was struck by lightning and burned to the ground.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Chapel Hill and caught fire. The house burned to the ground when the lightning got into the gas lines of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front and squall line transited north Florida on Tuesday, February 26th, 2008.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported one female county employee indirectly struck by lightning while on the phone. EMS treated and released her.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure area tracekd across east Texas and western Louisiana, creating up to 8 inches of rainfall. This resulted in some flash flooding in the Jasper, TX area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church educational building, destroying it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms on the 7th produced a few reports of damaging winds in Houston County and lightning damage to some property in Henry County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two house trailers.  Fire from the trailers spread to a nearby vehicle and grass field.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Newcastle and ignited a fire that destroyed the residence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building used to store hay and ignited a fire that caused major damage to the wooden structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a nearby tree and then followed a gas line into a home in Salem where it ignited a fire.  The fire casued damage to the basement and first floor, however a sprinkler system limited damage on the upper floor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary was positioned over Southeast Georgia with a moist and unstable airmass across the local area in advance of the front. Precipitable water amounts of 2.12 inches were in place and very high surface based instability index values with CAPEs around 3500 J/kg and lifted index values of -9 to -10.  Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across the area during the afternoon and evening along the approaching front , sea breezes and old outflow boundaries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Villas at Ponte Vedra Beach and caused a fire that damaged 19 townhouse rooms in a building. The time of the event was based on lightning data plots. The cost of damaged was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low pressure system lifted northeast across the state during the afternoon of the 2nd.  At the same time, the upper level system lifted northeast and captured the surface feature by the afternoon hours.  Several rounds of thunderstorms rotated in spiral bands across the state.  The atmosphere became unstable during the afternoon with MUCAPE in the 2000 J/kg range and the effective shear around 30 kts.  A band of thunderstorms rotated north into northern Iowa.  The storms produced winds around 60 MPH in parts of northern Iowa.  The highs winds caused some damage to a bar and business in Manly.   Earlier, as the storms moved through central Iowa, lightning struck several power poles in Dallas County, setting them on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck several power poles and set them on fire near the intersection of Highway 44 and P46/El Paso Ave.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moved through the Midlands and produced 1 to 2 inches of rain and some intense lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fifty six year old Brenda F. Baker was struck and killed by lightning while she was taking a break at her job.  A second employee was also struck but only suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stalled front across eastern Ohio. Lightning struck and killed a 60 year old man out tending cows in an open field in Monroe county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported lightning struck and killed a 60 year old man out tending cows in an open field in Lewisville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze thunderstorms produced wind damage in coastal and inland sections of Central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that destroyed at a Marine Learning Center in Wabasso.

The region that experienced the greatest rainfall was across Northeast Louisiana, and West Central Mississippi where 5 to 8 inches fell. The other area of heavy rain was along Interstate 20, through Central and East Central Mississippi. Here, 3 to 6 inches fell. All this heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across the area. The severe weather was more scattered in nature, but what did occur was mainly damaging winds and located across the southern half of the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze thunderstorms resulted in a lightning injury in Winter Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Winter Park man was slightly injured by lightning while setting on his apartment balcony.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An advancing cold front brought a round of severe thunderstorms, with large hail and damaging winds, to Central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A horse was killed by a lightning strike, in the Blairtown Community.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Dingley building in Lewiston and caused a moderate amount of damage to the building's wooden tower.  The building housed the headquarters of the Lewiston School Department.  The lightning also caused damage to the building's phone, electrical, and elevator systems.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Sanford igniting a fire that caused heavy damage to the attic and roof.  The first and second floors sustained water damage.  Damage was estimated at $60,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Sanford igniting a fire that caused heavy damage to the second floor, attic and roof.  Damage was estimated at $100,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms marched across Eastern Upper Michigan early in the morning of the 13th.

The tree was blasted into pieces, and most of the electronic equipment in the admin building was destroyed.  Some electrical damage also occurred in a staff building, not quite an eighth of a mile away.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early summer type pattern developed across the region briefly and brought scattered afternoon thunderstorms to the area. A few of these became severe and brought some damaging winds and a little small hail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe storms popped up during the afternoon of the 24th.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three workers were shocked when their natural gas drilling rig was struck by lightning.  Two workers were taken to nearby hospitals and were treated, kept overnight, and released the next morning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread heavy rainfall and strong to severe thunderstorms affected much of south Mississippi over a two day period. The adverse weather was the result of a series of strong upper level disturbances moving across the lower Mississippi Valley in advance of a strong and slow southward moving cold front.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread heavy rainfall and strong to severe thunderstorms affected much of southeast Louisiana over a two day period. The adverse weather was the result of a series of strong upper level disturbances moving across the lower Mississippi Valley in advance of a strong and slow southward moving cold front.
