EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front advancing from Louisiana into Arkansas triggered thunderstorms in central and southern Arkansas on the afternoon and evening of the 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Arkansas Sky Observatory on Petit Jean Mountain. All the electronics in two telescopes were destroyed, as were some cameras, computers, and other electronic equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An increasingly moist and unstable airmass combined with upper level energy in advance of a remnant MCS complex over Georgia spawned scattered severe storms across the forecast area during the afternoon and evening. Precipitable water values were 1.87 inches on the 12Z Jacksonville sounding with modified surface based CAPEs around 3500 J/kg and lifted indcies of -8 to -9 degrees Celcius.  In addition, 500 mb temperatures cooled to -9 degrees Celcius.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a home in the Hidden Hills subdivision. The strike caused a damaging house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid and upper level trough extended from the Great Lakes south across the lower Mississippi River Valley and a weak shortwave trough was offshore of the southeast U.S. Atlantic Coast. A surface ridge axis was across central Florida. The Jacksonville sounding depicted a precipitable water of over 2 inches and modified afternoon CAPEs were around 2500 J/kg with a lifted index of -10 and 500 mb temperatures of -10 degrees Celcius. Scattered severe storms developed across the area during the afternoon and evening when a passing upper level short wave trough vorticity maxima traversed the moist and unstable airmass as the sea breezes developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old male was struck by lightning while working at a tire store in the Normandy area of Jacksonville. He suffered minor injuries and was taken to the hospital for observation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large and powerful storm system brought several rounds of severe weather to a large section of the Central United States. The Central Plains were hit hard on Thursday, May 1st, while the Mid-South and Lower Mississippi River Valley were impacted on Friday, May 2nd into the early morning hours of May 3rd. As this severe weather episode evolved over the National Weather Service Jackson, MS service area, several tornadoes occurred, along with large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Five air conditioning units were damaged by lightning which struck the Bolivar County Correctional Facility. All the units had to be replaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Our region saw numerous showers and thunderstorms develop during the afternoon hours on May 22nd and push south to north across the area. Scattered storms became severe and produced a mix of hail, damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cluster pulse storms moved through the CSRA and produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Jones Chapel Church at 2322 Thomson Hwy was struck by lightening causing a small fire.  It appears that the church steeple was stuck, causing fire/damage to the steeple and roof structure below it.  Heavy rain at the time minimized the fire spread.  The fire was quickly contained causing minimal damage. Initial damage estimates were $10,000 to the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong low pressure north of the region resulted in a dryline separating warm most air from much drier air across Oklahoma. A cold front caught up to the dryline during the morning hours of January 8th with strong to severe thunderstorms forming on the dryline. The line of thunderstorms originated across northeast Texas and southeast Oklahoma and progressed eastward into southwest Arkansas and northwest Louisiana.  An isolated severe thunderstorm produced some wind damage in the parish and frequent cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree behind a home in the Belle Meade subdivision are causing a gas line to explode in a backyard.  Flames shot 10 to 20 feet into the air and it took firefighters a couple of hours to contain it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which knocked over a power pole near the intersection of Pine Grove Avenue and Forrest Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another in a series of strong weather systems pushed across the area. This one combined with limited moisture and instability and produced isolated severe thunderstorms across southeast portions of the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Powe Road and caused only minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper trough was moving from the mid-south toward the southeast U.S. early on the 26th.  A strong cold front accompanied the upper system.  A squall line of thunderstorms developed after midnight on the 25th across Mississippi and Alabama and reached the Georgia/Alabama border around 5 am EST.  The line of thunderstorms intensified and bowed out just as it was moving in Georgia during the early morning hours.  Wind gusts in excess 60 mph affected many counties as these thunderstorms rolled through the area during the early morning hours, causing extensive wind damage to trees, power lines, and some structures from the west and northwest side of Atlanta toward the Alabama border. In addition, two tornadoes, one an EF3, developed along the stronger part of the line as it moved through Carroll county before daybreak causing extensive damage along their paths.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Rome News Tribune reported that lightning struck a power line adjacent to a barn and workshop setting the structure on fire.  Bales of hay were stored in the barn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours of February 17th, the southern half of the area saw a line of showers and thunderstorms move through. This line brought gusty winds to many areas with scattered severe thunderstorms across the Highway 84 corridor. Scattered wind damage occurred along the southern end of the line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting strike near Oak Grove caused a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep low pressure system moving east across the Great Lakes pushed a strong cold front across the region on late April 20th into early April 21st. Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours across the region and continued into the following morning. High moisture content and training storms lead to flooding across potions of the region with several road closures due to high water. Several storms produced damaging winds that downed trees and power lines. There were also two confirmed tornadoes in Charles and Prince Georges counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper reported that lightning struck a home under construction on Wrights Mill Road in Randallstown.

Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours across the region and continued into the following morning. High moisture content and training storms lead to flooding across potions of the region with several road closures due to high water. EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper reported that a 2-story house on the 770 block of Ricker Road was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving across the Mid Atlantic triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms across portions of northern and central Virginia. Some storms were severe, producing hail to the size of pennies.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Albemarle County Emergency Management reported wires down and a tree on fire in Crozet.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An intense closed upper low was rotating negatively from the southern plains toward the Ohio Valley.  A strong cold front in advance of this system was moving across Mississippi into Alabama during the evening of the 17th.  A wedge cold front was located across north and central Georgia. Very warm, unstable air was present across southern Alabama and southern Georgia, south of the wedge front.  While only marginal instability was present, very strong shear was noted with a 60-70 knot low-level jet evident across Alabama and western and central Georgia.  These systems combined to bring a strong squall line of thunderstorms to west and north Georgia during the mid and late afternoon hours.  Most of the damage associated with this line of thunderstorms was straight-line wind damage.  However, an isolated embedded EF1 tornado within a quasi-linear convective system did occur in west central Georgia in Carroll county.  Meanwhile, along the southern end of the convective line, a long-lived supercell tracked from southern Alabama into southwest Georgia, south of Columbus, and continued on a near 100-mile track across west central and central Georgia from just south of Fort Benning to just northeast of Macon.  Multiple tornadoes, ranging in strength from EF0 to EF1 were reported within broken segments along the track of this supercell, resulting in considerable damage to trees, power lines, and property.  Several injuries were reported during the stronger portion of the tornadic supercell in Taylor and Crawford counties, southwest of Macon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Columbus Ledger-Inquirer reported that lightning struck a home at 506 Avis Court setting fire to the chimney and living room area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level system and evolving surface low moved across the region late on March 3rd. These features combined to bring a potent weather system to the area and a healthy round of severe thunderstorms from late afternoon through around midnight. It was a line of thunderstorms which brought most of the severe weather, but a few supercells did occur just ahead of the line. Ten tornadoes occurred, two of which were strong (EF-2), along with a good deal of wind damage as the line pushed east across Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House was struck by lightning which caused a minor fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system aloft approached from the southern Plains during the evening of March 13th. Cold air surrounded the system, with much warmer conditions near the ground. This created very unstable conditions, with thunderstorms developing.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several grass fires were started across the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system aloft approached from the southern Plains during the evening of March 13th. Cold air surrounded the system, with much warmer conditions near the ground. This created very unstable conditions, with thunderstorms developing.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree caught on fire due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system aloft approached from the southern Plains during the evening of March 13th. Cold air surrounded the system, with much warmer conditions near the ground. This created very unstable conditions, with thunderstorms developing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed across the northern Illinois on April 25th and produced mainly large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Fenview Drive and blew out a four by four foot hole in the roof.  The lightning also started a fire on the cedar shake roof.  The fire was contained to the roof, but the house suffered water damage inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed across the northern Illinois on April 25th and produced mainly large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A utility pole was damaged by a bolt of lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm during the early morning hours produced lightning which knocked out power. No other damage and no injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms which moved across Goodwell Oklahoma during the early morning hours knocked out power to around six hundred and eighty Tri-County Electric customers. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a shed fire on Avalon Road near Georgetown on the 12th. The shed was fully involved with the fire when the two fire companies arrived. Damage was estimated at $1,500. No injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved south through the area triggering showers and thunderstorms.  A few of the storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn in far southwestern Cole county.  It burned to the ground in less than half an hour.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms that developed during the evening of April 3rd across the northern half of northeast Texas, southeast Oklahoma and southwest Arkansas continued into the southern portions of northeast Texas as well as northwest Louisiana in a very unstable atmosphere. These supercell thunderstorms developed into bow echo like appearances due to very strong shear in the lower levels of the atmosphere, producing straight line wind gusts, damaging hail as well as a few tornadoes. Flash flooding was also reported over portions of the region as the storms produced excessive heavy rainfall amounts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning resulted in an explosion at a drilling rig on Highway 9 and Moriah Mountain Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the area triggering showers and thunderstorms.  Some of the thunderstorms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the county courthouse for the fourth time since June 4th of this year.  This time it knocked out part of the 911 capabilities, along with other software and computers throughout the courthouse.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed in advance of a cold front and along a mesoscale  boundary that moved south across Llano and Burnet counties early in the morning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire on Country Trails Lane in the Steiner Ranch area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three homes were struck by lightning as storms passed through central Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Hamilton County and left a charred area in the center of the living room floor.  Firefighters discovered the fire had burned in a cavity located between the first and second levels of the home, producing a large area of charred building material.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three homes were struck by lightning as storms passed through central Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a flexible natural gas line that went to the basement.  The homeowner was treated by medics for smoke inhalation, but was not taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front and deep upper-level trough were moving from the central U.S. into the eastern U.S. on the 11th.  A line of thunderstorms moved into northwest Georgia during the mid afternoon and moved across much of north and west central Georgia during the late afternoon and evening.  Thunderstorm wind damage was the main concern, but there were also several reports of marginally severe hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Dawson county Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a home setting it on fire.  The fire was extinguished by the homeowner with resulting minimal damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A solid line of intense to occasionally severe thunderstorms developed along a southward moving cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused considerable damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated severe thunderstorms developed north of a warm front over central Missouri.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a very large home south of Columbia which ignited a fire in the void between the roof and the peaked ceiling.  Three family members were in the home at the time of the lightning strike & subsequent fire and escaped unharmed.  The fire caused an estimated $100,000 in damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an injury in Richfield.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was injured at the Cove View Golf Course in Richfield when lightning hit a nearby tree and traveled to her. The woman was conscious and breathing when she was taken to a nearby hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and unstable air mass led to the develop of numerous showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Old Highway 431, in the Morrison Crossroads Community, was destroyed by fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was killed and at least two others were injured when lightning struck a tree that they were standing under.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole and ignited a fire at a home in Negaunee on the evening of the 17th. The lightning bolt traveled from the power pole to a metal dryer vent on the side of the house, starting the fire. Negaunee firefighters responded to the blaze and all people inside the house escaped without injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole outside a residence in Negaunee.  The lightning bolt traveled into the residence igniting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across far northern Illinois during the evening hours of July 7th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Ruth Circle but only caused damage to cables and appliances, no fire or structural damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and unstable air mass led to the develop of numerous showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house and barn caught fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze thunderstorms produced lightning across central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a barn fire near De Bary.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary remained just west of the area producing afternoon and evening thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Korey Moore was struck and killed by lightning on Lake Marion near Mill Creek while riding a jet ski.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure was ridging across northern Florida keeping east to southeast winds in place across the local area. An afternoon sea breeze developed and combined with the east coast sea breeze to form several severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging winds around the Tampa Bay area in the early evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas line which sparked a smoldering fire behind a stove in an apartment on the 3300 block of West De Leon Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire in the attic.  The fire was contained, but damage to the home was extensive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across eastern Colorado and northwest Kansas during the late afternoon and early evening hours producing wind damage and an isolated hail report.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three cows were killed by lightning in three separate incidents near this location.  A pasture fire was also started by lightning in the vicinity.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze thunderstorms formed over the Florida interior.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire that destroyed a home and an antique car in the Lake Griffen area.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house to catch fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating caused several severe thunderstorms across central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a tree to fall onto a vehicle, briefly trapping its occupant.  There were no injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sunday afternoon, a cold front moved south into northeast Texas and across southwest and south central Arkansas. Showers and thunderstorms developed along this boundary late in the day. The thunderstorms rapidly become strong to severe with support of a disturbance aloft moving through the region with the winds aloft being from the northwest.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced numerous reports of damaging wind and one tornado across southeast Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning that entered the home through a computer on which she was working during the storm.  She felt a tibgling sensation on her right side and EMS personnel responded to the scene.

The first struck an air conditioner at a car dealership, resulting in a fire in a second floor office.  The second struck a house a few blocks away, entering through the sprinkler system and starting a fire in a laundry room area.  There was no report on the monetary damage caused to the two locations, therefore damage amounts were estimated.

Fire damage was contained to the upper story, however water damage was tremendous. Acting chief of the fire department said about 2,000 gallons of water per minute was used for at least an hour. By 6:51 PM EST the blaze was under control. Firefighters remained on the scene until 9 PM EST.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is believed to have been responsible for major electrical problems at Putnam County Hospital.  Smoke filled the radiology department of the hospital and power flickered. Damage cost is a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and unstable air mass led to the development of showers and thunderstorms in the heat of the afternoon, some of which produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two separate lightning strikes hit 3 people in Wind Creek State Park.  All 3 were injured, and one had to be taken to the hospital.  Another lightning strike destroyed a boat house in the same area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small area of thunderstorms moved rapidly NNE across Red Willow county Nebraska during the late afternoon hours.  Although no severe weather was reported, a lightning strike injured a 9-year old boy in McCook.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 9-year old boy ran outside to retrieve a cardboard box before the storm arrived so it wouldn't blow away.  As he was retrieving the box which was near a yard light, lightning struck the light pole and jumped to a metal button on his coat. He complained of shoulder pain, a tingling sensation in his body and a metal taste in his mouth. He was taken to the hospital where tests were performed, then treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced lightning that struck two golfers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an 80-foot tall ponderosa pine tree and at least one of two golfers on a local golf course. The upper 60 feet of the pine tree was blown apart.  Both men were hospitalized and one was in critical condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early- to mid-evening hours, the Storm Prediction Center upgraded central, and much of southern, Indiana to a moderate risk for severe weather and issued a severe thunderstorm watch for the area effective until 3 AM EST. The atmosphere was extremely unstable and the growth of any developing storms was unimpeded. A roughly west to east frontal boundary stretched from southern Nebraska to central Indiana. Dewpoints in the lower 70s F were in place along the front, contributing to strong instability. A strong shortwave trough skirted the area, enhancing coverage of storms. Winds were expected to be the primary threat, and this is what indeed ending up being the main problem in central Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire from a lightning strike destroyed the roof of a home in the 8300 block of Bighorn Court. The home sustained heavy smoke and water damage throughout. Two other fires, on Key Court and Weathered Edge Drive, were relatively small and contained to the areas where they were started (no damage cost estimates available).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved slowly toward Arkansas from the north to begin July. On the 3rd, the front made it to the Arkansas and Missouri border and stalled. Thunderstorms erupted during the afternoon, with a few storms becoming severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous transformers were out because of lightning strikes. One structure fire was started by an exploding transformer.

The department estimated the fire caused at least $350,000 in damage to the house and contents. The fire was believed to have been burning for some time before it was discovered as evidenced by the entire front of the house, and halfway inside, being engulfed in flames. The owners were at work at the time of occurrence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed mainly across the south and southeast portion of the forecast area. A few of these became severe and produced some hail and wind damage. One cluster of storms lingered across northern Forrest County and caused flash flooding around Hattiesburg.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Bouge Chitto Baptist Church and damaged the steeple.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm created lightning that damaged a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike damaged a home by creating a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very strong and deep upper low in the southern plains swept through the southeast U.S. late on the 31st of January into the 1st of February.  The system took on a negative tilt as it rotated through the southeast U.S.  A strong low-level jet of 60 to 70 mph was noted just in advance of a narrow line of very heavy rain showers and isolated thunderstorms which moved through the west central Georgia area between 1030 pm and 1100 pm EST.  Some of these winds were brought down to the surface with the convective activity, causing wind damage in the Columbus area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Times-Herald of Newnan reported that lightning struck a home on U.S. Highway 27 Alternate starting a fire that caused extensive damage to the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The afternoon sea breeze triggered thunderstorms over coastal Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire caused by lightning destroyed an expensive water front home in Merritt Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal system moved across south central Texas triggering numerous thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was caused by a lightning stirke in the 800 block of Huntington place in south Austin.  There was minor roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe storms affected western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Eight firefighters working to contain a wildfire were treated for burns when lightning struck nearby.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm moist atmosphere continued over the region.  The upper high, which had been suppressing convection during previous days, continued to drift east allowing for a more favorable environment for afternoon pulse thunderstorms to develop.  The atmosphere over the region was slightly more stable because of previous day thunderstorm activity and early morning cloud cover.  However, by late afternoon and evening, isolated pulse thunderstorms began to develop.  One produced a downburst just south of Dublin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning started a forest fire between Wrightsville and Kite in eastern Johnson county.

The structure was completely destroyed by the fire.  This fire was started while a separate lightning sparked fire was ongoing in the woods between Wrightsville and Kite.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front approached the region on July 27th as a strong upper level low pressure system remained over the northeast. Warm and humid air at the surface interacted with cooler air aloft to produce scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours. Many of the storms became severe, producing damaging winds that downed trees and power lines. Large hail to the size of quarters was also reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported a chimney was damaged by a lightning strike. Part of the chimney broke off, falling onto a gas meter and causing a small gas leak.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Under the influence of an unstable airmass and favorable south to southeasterly flow, thunderstorms broke out over eastern Oregon and over the Oregon Cascades, and advanced across the forecast area.  A few of these storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were struck by lightning standing near a house.  Both men were in their 50s to 60s. Both were seriously injured by the strike, and were taken to different medical centers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong thunderstorms developed across southeast Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes caused fires in two mobile homes resulting in severe damage to each one.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms moved across areas of southeast Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a fire in the attic of a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong thunderstorms affected areas of southeast Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Yet another deep trough was digging into the northeast U.S. Northwest flow was becoming increasingly active into the southeast U.S. as a result.  Widespread thunderstorms developed across central Georgia during the afternoon and evening, with isolated thunderstorms in the northern part of the state.  Several of these became severe and produced wind damage and penny to quarter-sized hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Soperton News reported that lightning struck and killed six steer.  The steer were owned by a rodeo company in Texas.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home in the 1000 block of Slash Pine Court just south of Interstate-85 between Suwanee and Lawrenceville.  The resulting fire caused moderate damage to the roof, chimney, and an exterior wall.

The lightning hit the top floor of the hospital professional office building sending pieces of brick falling five stories to the parking lot below.  The falling bricks damaged two cars.  The hospital also lost about 40 percent of its phone service temporarily.  The professional office building of the hospital was evacuated for 15 minutes.

The system became even stronger on the 29th producing widespread severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Laurens County 911 Center reported that lightning strikes resulted in two structural fires in the Cadwell area and a grass fire in the Dexter area.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the north side of Columbia around 5 am.  It caused a fire in the attic of the house which was quickly extinguished.  No injuries were reported, but damage to the house was estimated around $10,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved through the Mid Atlantic during the afternoon and evening of July 4th. This system combined with a weak surface front and heat and humidity to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms during the late afternoon hours. Some of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail in portions of north central Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: King George County Emergency Management reported several lightning-sparked fires, including 2 homes and a business. One person was reportedly struck by lightning through a TV and suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating combined with an approaching cold front created enough lift and instability ahead of it to produce showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a house on fire.

Some of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail in Calvert County. Lightning was also responsible for several fires in Calvert County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported that lightning sparked an attic fire on Parkers Creek Road in Port Republic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours of Tuesday, June 17th, a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) developed over western Oklahoma, and surged southeastward into north Texas after sunrise. This storm system produced widespread 60-70 mph wind gusts across much of north Texas, including Dallas, which then spread into east Texas during the early afternoon hours. Numerous trees and power lines were downed across areas generally along and south of Interstate 20, particularly in the city if Tyler, and also Center, Texas. In fact, trees fell atop several buildings in Center, although no injuries were reported. The storms weakened by early evening, as they spread/developed farther southward into southeast Texas and southwest Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two-story home inside a gated community causing a two-alarm fire in the city of Tyler, Texas.  The home was in the 3500 block of Melanie Court inside the River Oaks community.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms during the late evening hours of July 2nd caused a lightning strike which damaged a grain elevator and building in Shelby County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a grain elevator and started a fire in a nearby office building. There were no injuries.

The home on Candle Berry Drive sustained minor to moderate damage to the basement.  At the other two locations, damage was confined to detached garages, each sustaining moderate damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front and upper level disturbance caused wind damage and dropped large hail as an area of thunderstorms affected the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A four-thousand square-foot house in Justin was burned down after lightning struck it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A developing upper level trough, combined with several weak surface boundaries, led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms during Sunday afternoon and evening on June 22nd, some of which became severe.||Additional isolated severe thunderstorms developed late Sunday night, into the early morning hours of Monday June 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree approximately 2 miles northwest of Rotterdam, resulting in downed powerlines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon thunderstorms moved across portions of the Phoenix metropolitan area.  One cloud to ground lightning strike apparently started a brush fire near the Gila River southwest of Phoenix.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Ethan Fire was sparked by lightning on the 25th, and grew to over 5,000 acres several days later. Estimated cost to fight the fire was about $700,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed with the aid of afternoon heating across portions of northeast Texas and northwest and north central Louisiana.  The atmosphere was very unstable and as a result...thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall and damaging downburst winds across a few locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank on the southeast side of town.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two separate complexes of thunderstorms impacted north Texas causing wind damage as they moved southeast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a tank battery fire near FM 455.  Three firefighter departments battled the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two separate complexes of thunderstorms impacted north Texas causing wind damage as they moved southeast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home south of Decatur was struck by lightning.  Only the phone system was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front slowly approached the region from the southwest early Friday morning on June 6th. Several clusters of thunderstorms developed on the cool side of this boundary during the morning hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is believed to have struck a pole, following the wires into a house on Russell Road in West Albany, igniting a fire within a wall. The fire was extinguished within 15 minutes, but caused damage to a wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered storms returned on the 20th with isolated severe weather and areas of heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An outbuilding burned when it was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large cluster of thunderstorms, known as a mesoscale convective system (MCS), developed near a cold front and swept across much of Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an electrical substation on the northwest side of Pine Bluff. More than 2000 electric customers were without power for more than five hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms over northern Palm Beach on the evening on June 26th caused lightning to strike a car.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning while driving on I-95 in northern Palm Beach County between Indiantown and Donald Ross roads. A female passenger was taken to the hospital for precationary measures. The vehicle was inoperable, likely due to electrical damage caused by the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several boundaries from previous activity remained over the region with very unstable conditions.  This helped to trigger another round of severe thunderstorms and heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The communications tower at the county courthouse in Shelbyville was struck by lightning damaging computers for the 911 system and the sheriff's office, radio consoles, and various other electronic equipment. Damage is estimated around $100,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms over north central Virginia during the afternoon of June 19th. Damaging winds brought down trees near Stanley in Page County. Penny-sized hail occurred near Harrisonburg and in Vienna. Lighting also caused damage to a condominium estate in Alexandria.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Shenandoah County Emergency Management reported a barn destroyed by lightning in the Orkney/Bayes area.

Damaging winds brought down trees near Stanley in Page County. Penny-sized hail occurred near Harrisonburg and in Vienna. Lighting also caused damage to a condominium estate in Alexandria.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported a lightning-sparked fire at a condominium complex. Lightning caused a roof fire at the Alexandria Knolls West condominium. A major electrical panel was destroyed and an explosion went through the adjacent wall, causing severe damage to a unit on the 8th flood.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced damaging winds in a few locations in northwest Iowa from a little before to just after midnight on the night of July 20th and 21st. The greatest damage was in and near Sioux City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and destroyed a large tree and an electrical panel on the side of a house, blowing several breakers and fuse boxes, melting a telephone wire, and damaging other parts of the house's electrical system. The strike also shattered a bedroom window, causing minor cuts from flying glass to two occupants.

Some of this convection initially produced large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts. Eventually...heavy rainfall began across portions of northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana which continued all night and into the morning hours of May 14th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home located at 836 Middle Road in Minden.  Approximately one quarter of the home's roof and structure burned with the remaining portion of the home sustaining smoke and water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of storms moved east from northeast Texas into northwest Louisiana where it met up with a rapidly developing band of showers and thunderstorms.  Some of this convection initially produced large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts. Eventually...heavy rainfall began across portions of northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana which continued all night and into the morning hours of May 14th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil field tank in Caspiana, Louisiana resulting in an explosion.  The explosion blew the tops off two other tanks nearby.

Many roadways across the southern portion of the parish that flooded out late on the 13th remain closed or had to be closed once again as the heavy rainfall continued into the morning hours of the 14th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Green Acres Village Apartments on Airline Drive in Bossier City.  A building that damaged 8 units was heavily damaged and the second floor was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clockwise flow around high pressure in the southwest United States created a northwest wind flow aloft over Arkansas. This drove a cold front toward the region. Precipitation was more organized along and ahead of the front, with scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a barn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Narrative.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Walt Morey Middle School, damaging some of the computer systems.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Narrative.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Firefighters responded to a greenhouse fire, which had been struck by lightning. The greenhouse was completely destroyed, but the nearby home was saved.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved over northwest Iowa shortly after dawn on the 7th.  Lightning struck a house in Estherville.  It resulted in a small fire and the house needed to be evacuated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted northward through the region...triggering showers and thunderstorms.  Some of the storms became severe and/or caused flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old male was struck by lightning in Binder Memorial State Park west of Jefferson City.  The victim was revived by paramedics and airlifted to a local hospital.  He was released from the hospital a week later.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire at the Scottish Inn in Front Royal. The blaze damaged the roof above 2 rooms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early- to mid-evening hours, the Storm Prediction Center upgraded central, and much of southern, Indiana to a moderate risk for severe weather and issued a severe thunderstorm watch for the area effective until 3 AM EST. The atmosphere was extremely unstable and the growth of any developing storms was unimpeded. A roughly west to east frontal boundary stretched from southern Nebraska to central Indiana. Dewpoints in the lower 70s F were in place along the front, contributing to strong instability. A strong shortwave trough skirted the area, enhancing coverage of storms. Winds were expected to be the primary threat, and this is what indeed ending up being the main problem in central Indiana.

The climax of the event was when minor injuries were reported when a tree fell onto a house in Hoke County, trapping 4 individual for more than an hour.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hurricane Gustav was moving west through the eastern Gulf of Mexico. Although the hurricane remained well south of north and central Georgia, the hurricane was so large that the outer most rain bands fired up during the afternoon resulting in scattered thunderstorms across central Georgia.  The thunderstorms produced gusty winds, frequent lightning, and heavy rain.  While none became severe, Upson county did experience a lightning fire and downed power lines as a result of one of these thunderstorms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in southeast Illinois during the afternoon of 9/3, to the northeast of the remnants of Hurricane Gustav. An adult, male was injured by a lightning strike while hunting near a wooded area in southeast Shelby County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An adult male, age unknown, was struck by lightning while hunting at Hidden Springs State Forest. He was transported to a local hospital and treated for his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across portions of northeast Texas and northwest Louisiana along a frontal boundary in association with an upper level disturbance.  Enough instability existed in the late afternoon, early evening hours such that a thunderstorms briefly reached severe criteria across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a salt water disposal tank near mile marker 624 just off Interstate 20 west of Waskom, Texas.  The resulting fire spread to other nearby tanks in the area as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms affected a large part of Arkansas on the 8th.  There were a number of reports of wind damage and an isolated tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An electrical transformer was hit by lightning, which caused a fire in the surrounding trees.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The pattern that began to evolve on March 14th continued and intensified on March 15th.  A stationary front remained draped across north Georgia from near Atlanta to Athens.  South of this front, the air mass was becoming increasingly warm, moist and unstable.  Meanwhile, aloft, a low amplitude, yet vigorous short wave embedded within a fast zonal flow, was tracking rapidly eastward from the mid south into the southeast.  Strong shear and high helicity combined with the unstable air mass and the frontal boundary to allow repeated severe thunderstorms to develop and track eastward along the boundary across north Georgia.  The activity began early in the day as a complex of thunderstorms moved into the area from Alabama and continued until nearly midnight.  As the day progressed, especially during the afternoon, the development of the activity gradually progressed further south and by midnight had reached the south and southeast parts of the state.  Numerous severe thunderstorms and tornadic supercells were observed throughout the day.||Historical records indicate that this was one of the most significant severe weather days for the Peachtree City Weather Forecast Office with more events and warnings than had been observed since May 2003.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Floyd County Emergency Management Director reported that a home at 5229 Rockmart Road in Silver Creek was struck by lightning and completely destroyed from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed between a warm front over northeast South Dakota and a cold front moving into central North Dakota.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an office building and started a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 44-year-old man was injured when he was struck by lightning as he was pumping gas during the late afternoon hours. The man was unconscious for a few minutes and the strike resulting in some blistering.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front that crossed the Tri-State on the 15th, produced some severe thunderstorms across portions of Northeast New Jersey during the afternoon and early evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike produced major house damage at 20 North Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the heating of the afternoon in a very unstable airmass across the region. Storms that developed across southwest Arkansas produced a lightning strike in Sevier County Arkansas that struck the local Fire Department in De Queen, Arkansas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the fire department's radio tower in De Queen, Arkansas.  The electricity from the strike followed the wiring into the wall resulting in a fire inside the local fire department. Moderate damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Hanna made landfall near the North Carolina/South Carolina border at 320AM EDT September 6.  Hanna then moved north/northeast across the Mid-Atlantic states and southern New England September 6 and 7.  Storm total rainfall in southern New England ranged from 2.04 inches in Randolph, MA to 6.56 inches in Nashua, NH.  The highest sustained wind of 27 knots (31 mph) was recorded at Nantucket Airport.  The highest wind gust of 37 knots (43 mph) was recorded at Blue Hill Observatory in Milton, MA.  The lowest sea level pressure was 994.5 mb at Conimicut Lighthouse, RI.  A coastal storm surge of 2 feet above normal tide was experienced at Providence, RI.  No coastal flooding was reported.  Minor wind damage was sustained by nearly every county in southern New England.  Significant wind damage occurred in southern Bristol and southern Plymouth Counties in Massachusetts and southeastern Providence County in Rhode Island.  All of the associated effects of Hanna in Southern New England resulted in no loss of life or injuries and $939K in property damage.  The winds caused $23K in property damage.  Inland flooding resulted in $916K in property damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from an embedded thunderstorm associated with Tropical Storm Hanna struck a house on North Pleasant Street resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very intense upper low was located over the southwest U.S. and lifted northeast during the weekend of the 24th into the morning of the 26th.  The seasons first strong push of deep moisture moved into Iowa on the 25th with surface temperatures warming into the mid 80s and dew points surging into the upper 60s to low 70s.  Precipitable water values were near 1.5 inches.  The dry slot pushed north across the area the previous night as the warm front lifted north.  The primary surface low was located over northern Minnesota.  A cold front extended south from the low into northwest Iowa.  The airmass became very unstable by the mid afternoon hours.  MUCAPE rose to between 4000 and 5000 J/kg.  Lifted indices fell to -8 to -11 C.  There was a considerable amount of both DCAPE at 1000-1500 J/kg and cape in the -10 to-30 C. layer of the atmoshpere, between 400 and 600 J/kg.  The freezing level was around 13,200 feet.  The environment was quite sheared with effective shear in the 40 to 50 kt range.  LCL values were between 1000 and 1500 meters.  The airmass was initially capped.  During the late afternoon hours, a small cluster of thunderstorms formed over north central into northeast Iowa.  The storms became severe very quickly.  Initially, the storms dropped hail up to golf ball in size.  One became a strong super cell and produced a major tornado. This cell, in addition to being tornadic, also produced hail of baseball to softball in size and winds in excess of 90 MPH.  The tornado track was from approximately 2 miles south of Aplington to Parkersburg, then continued to New Hartford and across northern Black Hawk County.  The average path width ranged from 0.6 to 0.7 miles near Parkersburg to just north of New Hartford.  The path constricted to near one quarter mile wide east of New Hartford to north of Waterloo.  The width then increased to near 1.2 miles wide north of Dunkerton before dissipating near the Black Hawk and Buchanan County line.  The tornado was on the ground for approximately 43 miles.  In addition to the main tornado, a satellite tornado was observed by storm chasers and one off duty NWS employee.  It was located south of the main tornado and was on the ground for a little over a mile in Grundy County.  Initial reports indicated 9 fatalities with 7 in Parkersburg (pop 1889) and 2 in New Hartford (pop 637).  There were at least 50 injuries, with 4 of those in critical condition.  Two of the fatalities occurred a few days after the tornado from injuries sustained in the tornado.  The last fatality occurred on 7 Nov.  A 61 year old female sustained injuries in the stairwell of her home when a 2 x 4 was thrown through her right side lung.  She was hospitalized and died several months later of complications.  Significant structural damage occurred across the southern end of Parkersburg and along a path to just north of New Hartford.  Numerous structures completely destroyed from Parkersburg to near New Hartford.  The tornado continued eastward to just north of the Waterloo and Cedar Falls area.  Significant damage also occurred north of Dunkerton where the tornado increased to its greatest path width. This storm also produced substantial straight line wind damage along the southern periphery of the storm just south of the tornado track.  News accounts indicated that a receipt from Parkersburg was found around 1915 CST 3 miles north of Prairie du Chien, WI, 109 miles to the northeast.  Receipits were also found in Clayton County at Elkader, and full scrapbook pages and photos were found in far northeast Bremer County at Sumner.  Preliminary estimates that straight line winds of 90 to 100 MPH occurred with this storm. At 1637 CST, the Waterloo Airport  recorded a 93 MPH wind gust. Survey results suggest that straight line wind damage was the cause of the severe damage at the recreational vehicle dealership north of Cedar Falls.  At least 627 homes were damaged, including 288 homes destroyed in Parkersburg, 88 in New Hartford, 15 in Hazelton and another 50 in Black Hawk County. In addition, 58 had major damage, 33 had moderate damage, 2 were inaccessible, and 93 damaged but able to be occupied. There were also 21 businesses destroyed. Governor Chet Culver declared both Butler and Black Hawk disaster areas with both given the State Declaration.  A Federal Disaster Declaration occurred two days later for both Butler and Black Hawk Counties.  The tornado was rated a low end EF5 by a Quick Response Team (QRT) in portions of Parkersburg and north of New Hartford with peak winds estimated at 205 MPH.  For historical reference, the last F5 tornado to hit Iowa was on 13 June 1976 in Boone and Story Counties in the town of Jordan, with a 21 mile path length.  The last F4 tornado to hit Iowa was in Union, Madison, and Dallas Counties with a 56 mile path length on 8 April 1999.  There was one other smaller tornado during the evening.  A tornado touched down in Clarke County and was on the ground for a short time southeast of Osceola.  After the initial thunderstorm area developed over north central and northeast Iowa, a large complex developed over southeast Nebraska. The two areas of storms filled in to form a squall line by the mid evening hours.  The complex over Nebraska then pushed east and northeast along the squall line.  A considerable amount of severe weather was generated during the evening as this occurred.  Along the squall line, high winds and hail were common with the dominant mode of severe weather being hail of up to golf ball in size.  As the MCS out of Nebraska advanced east, a tail extending south from the centroid took on a bow echo configuration and raced east across Iowa at 65 MPH.  Very high winds occurred with this feature with numerous locations reporting winds of 65 to 85 MPH.  Some of the higher winds included an 85 MPH wind gust in the Winterset area and numerous reports of 75 to 85 MPH winds from Madison, Dallas, Warren and Polk Counties.  Lightning struck a house in Ankeny.  The house was set on fire by the strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Ankeny, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved east across eastern New York and western New England during the late morning through mid afternoon hours of Sunday July 27th. The interaction of this front, and a warm, moist and unstable air mass, led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across the eastern Catskills, mid Hudson Valley region, and the central and southern Taconics.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near Accord at approximately 1300 LST. Significant damage was limited to the den and study areas, with smoke damage throughout the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front that crossed the Tri-State on the 15th, produced some severe thunderstorms across portions of the New York City Metro Area, Long Island, and the Lower Hudson Valley, including a microburst in Southern Westchester County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the steeple of New Rochelle High School, causing significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire in Edmonds, and a funnel cloud was spotted near Lake Lawrence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire that scorched a few nearby trees, and damaged a garage and a storage shed near a home in Edmonds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front provided a focus for severe thunderstorms.  These thunderstorms produced very heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding, hail, and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 42 year old man was hit by lightning while fishing on a jetty.  He was transported to a local hospital, where he later died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms moved from northeastern Wyoming across the northern Black Hills and onto the plains to the east, producing golf ball sized hail and strong wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were injured by lightning at the Glencoe Camp Resort ticket booth.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front acted as a focus for some heavy rains over parts of central Kentucky. Along with this, an upper level system set off some severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning on Harbor Village Drive outside of Georgetown. The strike burned a hole in the roof of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active and very unstable northwest flow continued across the southeast United States as the polar vortex remained very strong in the northeast United States.  A disturbance rotated around the back side of the upper low into the southeast United States during the afternoon and evening.  Multiple complexes of severe thunderstorms developed across north and central Georgia during the mid to later afternoon as a result and moved southeast during the evening hours.  Large hail was the primary severe weather element observed during this outbreak, however an EF2 tornado developed in Cherokee county and caused extensive damage to hundreds of homes.  This was the 45th tornado of the spring season for north and central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that lightning struck a home on Bisland Court setting the structure on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active and very unstable northwest flow continued across the southeast United States as the polar vortex remained very strong in the northeast United States.  A disturbance rotated around the back side of the upper low into the southeast United States during the afternoon and evening.  Multiple complexes of severe thunderstorms developed across north and central Georgia during the mid to later afternoon as a result and moved southeast during the evening hours.  Large hail was the primary severe weather element observed during this outbreak, however an EF2 tornado developed in Cherokee county and caused extensive damage to hundreds of homes.  This was the 45th tornado of the spring season for north and central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Walton Tribune reported that lightning struck a home at 1200 Nicholsville Road.  The house was completely destroyed.  No one was at home at the time and no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning was listed as the probable cause of a fire that destroyed a home in Kingfield.  The fire apparently smouldered for about 12 hours before igniting.  Damage was estimated $200,000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms surged east across portions of south-central and southeast Kansas during the predawn hours on the 27th, as a strong storm system and associated cold front approached from the west. Scattered occurrences of dime size hail and 60 mph winds were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms sparked a house fire in the community of Colony during the predawn hours of the 27th. The residence was completely destroyed. Fortunately, no one was home at the time. Information courtesy of the Iola Register.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three homes were struck by lightning as storms passed through central Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning as storms moved through the area.  When firefighters arrived, they found the home's basement in flames.  It look them about an hour to completely put the fire out.  The blaze originated in the basement utility room.  The basement was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unusual winter thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning that caused several fires, one injury, and damage to trees and telephone poles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Oak Ridge School in Sandwich, Massachusetts. Students were evacuated while firefighters made sure the lightning didn't start a fire, then returned to class.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unusual winter thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning that caused several fires, one injury, and damage to trees and telephone poles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Hanson, lightning strikes shattered telephone poles and put a hole in the road, as well as knocking out power to a number of locations.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A retrograding upper level trough enhanced sea breeze induced storms during the afternoon over Southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Brunswick News documented a lightning strike that killed 3 cows in the Brookman Community on a farm off of U.S. Highway 82. The cows were congregated around a tree, and the tree was struck by lightning.  The lightning current progressed to the cows. Cost of damage was estimated at $1,000/cow.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unusual winter thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning that caused several fires, one injury, and damage to trees and telephone poles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A restaurant in Marlboro was struck by lightning, starting a fire. The fire was contained to the roof but damages were enough that the restaurant was shut down.  One of the restaurant patrons reported being struck by the lightning bolt and was taken by ambulance to the local hospital.  No additional information was available about the victim.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unseasonably warm, moist air was drawn north into the area ahead of a strong cold front that moved from Illinois into Indiana during the evening hours of January 7. Surface temperatures in the 60s and dewpoints in the 50s, as well as strong winds aloft, allowed for the development of a line of strong to severe thunderstorms along the cold front in Illinois. This line progressed east into northwestern Indiana  with reports of wind damage being received. The line quickly weakened as it moved east and transitioned into a heavy rain event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a three car garage attached to a house in the 11000 block of south Michigan Road. When firefighters arrived, the garage was engulfed in flames. Severe damage occurred to the garage and 3 vehicles in it, as well as smoke and water damage to portions of the house. Damage was estimated $90,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A well developed storm system and strong upper level trough pushed through the central sections of the country. A strong surface low developed and lifted into the Great Lakes region and drug a cold front through the south. Ahead of the front, warm and humid conditions moved in and clashed with the eastward moving upper trough. Scattered severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening with a squall line affecting the northern sections of the area. The south half saw a few supercell thunderstorms in advance of the developing line of storms. The storm system produced a mix of large hail, damaging winds, and a couple of tornadoes as it moved across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning and the person inside was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: There were numerous reports of hail and damaging winds as a cold front and upper level shortwave affected the region.  The front had moved east of north Texas by late afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a house fire near Hicks Airfield.  Damage was limited to the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: There were a couple reports of damage as a cold front moved through the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on CR 420, causing heavy damage.  Apparently the lightning struck a television antenna on the left side of the house and followed copper wiring inside the house.  The house had recently been sold and was listed at $289,000.  Two firefighters were treated for minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system aloft approached from the southern Plains during the evening of March 13th. Cold air surrounded the system, with much warmer conditions near the ground. This created very unstable conditions, with thunderstorms developing.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous fires were started across the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mid-level impulse embedded within strong southwest mid-level winds around 60 kt, coupled with south southeast low level flow surging dewpoints into the mid 60s, allowed upstream thunderstorms to reinvigorate, prompting the issuance of a Tornado Watch for southeast portions of North Carolina and northeast portions of South Carolina at 230 am EST.  Mid-level lapse rates of 7 C/km aided in support of increasing instability for surface based storms.  Bulk shear and low level speed shear were both ample for storms to organize with a risk for damaging wind gusts and possible tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 2400 block of Youpon Drive.  The damage was confined to a burned out fuse box.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front along with a strong upper level low produced a squall line that crossed south central Indiana. This set off widespread severe weather, and produced some heavy rains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near the Huntingburg airport.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mid-level impulse embedded within strong southwest mid-level winds around 60 kt, coupled with south southeast low level flow surging dewpoints into the mid 60s, allowed upstream thunderstorms to reinvigorate, prompting the issuance of a Tornado Watch for southeast portions of North Carolina and northeast portions of South Carolina at 230 am EST.  Mid-level lapse rates of 7 C/km aided in support of increasing instability for surface based storms.  Bulk shear and low level speed shear were both ample for storms to organize with a risk for damaging wind gusts and possible tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Garage and mini-van struck by lightning.  Lightning started a fire which took firefighters 20 minutes to extinguish.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active and very unstable northwest flow continued across the southeast United States as the polar vortex remained very strong in the northeast United States.  A disturbance rotated around the back side of the upper low into the southeast United States during the afternoon and evening.  Multiple complexes of severe thunderstorms developed across north and central Georgia during the mid to later afternoon as a result and moved southeast during the evening hours.
