This was the 45th tornado of the spring season for north and central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Morgan County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning started a grass fire near Madison.  The exact location was not provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front pushed northeast from Mississippi into northern Alabama producing widespread rainfall during the afternoon of the 9th.  A squall line then produced another round of heavy rainfall, along with several small bow echoes.  One of these stronger bow echoes resulted in an EF-2 tornado in Jackson County after midnight on the 10th.||Widespread rain amounts of 3 to 5 inches, locally near 6 inches, fell in Madison, Limestone, Morgan, and Lawrence counties resulting in widespread river and local flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The mayor of the city of Hollywood, also a volunteer fire fighter was knocked down by a lightning strike in front of the City Hall building while preparing to go out on an emergency call.  The victim was examined by medical personnel but was found to be not injured.  However, a hole was carved out in his office wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front pushed northeast from Mississippi into northern Alabama producing widespread rainfall during the afternoon of the 9th.  A squall line then produced another round of heavy rainfall, along with several small bow echoes.  One of these stronger bow echoes resulted in an EF-2 tornado in Jackson County after midnight on the 10th.||Widespread rain amounts of 3 to 5 inches, locally near 6 inches, fell in Madison, Limestone, Morgan, and Lawrence counties resulting in widespread river and local flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several house fires were sparked by lightning strikes in Huntsville.  A transformer was damaged by a direct lightning strike just off Winchester Road in north Huntsville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist southerly flow developed over north Florida and southeast Georgia as several convective complexes developed ahead of cold front and upper level trough over the Florida Panhandle. A southwesterly low level jet advected deep moisture off the Gulf of Mexico. This when combined with significant upper level divergence associated with right rear quadrant of the upper jet provided strong large scale lift to support severe convection.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two homes and ignited two brush fires in central Nassau County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low pressure system and associated cold front moved across the region. Thunderstorms developed late in the evening and moved eastward across the northern sections of Maricopa County. Small hail and frequent lightning was observed with the strongest storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning resulted in considerable damage to various electrical and electronic systems at the Pioneer Elementary School in Glendale. A nearby eucalyptus tree was also struck, which resulted in pieces of wood or bark  exploding outward in all directions. Minor damage occurred to one side of a home near the school.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful storm system aloft moved from the southern Rockies into the southern Plains on the 16th. The system dredged abundant moisture northward from the Gulf Coast, with rain becoming widespread. A cold front barreled into the region, with showers and thunderstorms ahead of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Henderson State University area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Warm, moist air ahead of a developing low pressure system produced showers and thunderstorms during the morning hours of February 4, 2008. One of the thunderstorms produced dangerous lightning that caused a fire at a residence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on County Road 112 outside of Tishomingo. The strike produced a fire in the storage shed. The shed was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over southern Iowa during the afternoon of the 17th.  Many of them produced some small hail, mainly pea size around a quarter to half inch in diameter, but no severe weather was reported.  As the storms moved through the Ringgold County area, lightning struck a house in the Sun Valley Lake area.  The house was set on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started it on fire in the Sun Valley area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Englewood during an electrically charged snowstorm.  A gas meter at the home was hit by lightning and burst into flames.  The unusual thunderstorm produced a combination of snow and graupel.  The graupel was up to one half inch in diameter.  Total snow accumulations ranged from 1 to 4 inches across the southern suburbs of Denver.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home during an electrically charged snowstorm. A gas meter at the home was hit by lightning and burst into flames.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved into northwest Oklahoma during the evening of the 4th and moved southeast through the rest of Oklahoma during the early morning and afternoon hours of the 5th. Unseasonably mild temperatures were in place ahead of the cold front, with temperatures more indicative of early February behind the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed along and just ahead of the cold front, especially over the western half of Oklahoma as an upper level disturbance moved overhead. Some of the thunderstorms briefly became severe and produced large hail and brief strong winds. Some damage was reported in Payne county, where monetary damages were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed a bricked fireplace and the electrical wiring in the house. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early on the 5th, a strong storm system approached from the Plains. Ahead of the system, breezy southerly winds provided well above normal temperatures and abundant moisture. Warmth and moisture destabilized the atmosphere and fueled developing thunderstorms. A cold front moved across the state causing numerous severe storms and several tornadoes. One of the tornadoes tracked from Yell County to Sharp County, staying on the ground for 121.84 miles. This track length set a record for the longest tornado path ever recorded in Arkansas. The continuous track was confirmed by two National Weather Service meteorologists who flew the track with the Civil Air Patrol. The final track was based on ground surveys, the Civil Air Patrol flight, and an aerial mapping flight performed for the Arkansas Forestry Commission.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the school campus, causing damage to the school and surveillance system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line moved through central Indiana during the evening hours of January 29th.  Hail, damaging winds, and a tornado occurred with this storm system in central Indiana.  The tornado was rated EF1 and occurred in Marion County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in Westfield.  A firefighter suffered a neck sprain while fighting the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms brought rain, hail and lightning to portions of the Phoenix area on Monday afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started an attic fire in Sun City and a house fire in Glendale.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line with severe weather and several tornadoes moved across north Florida and southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an old structure igniting a fire. Minimal damage was done to the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful storm system aloft moved from the southern Rockies into the southern Plains on the 16th. The system dredged abundant moisture northward from the Gulf Coast, with rain becoming widespread. A cold front barreled into the region, with showers and thunderstorms ahead of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and then the siding on a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front and upper level low pressure system triggered numerous thunderstorms late in the day on the 15th and in the early morning hours of the 16th.  Hail between nickel and golfball-size was a common occurrence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroyed a house on the 5100 block of Iroquis Drive.  The total damage to the 4,600 square foot house and its contents was estimated at $500,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front and upper level low pressure system triggered numerous thunderstorms late in the day on the 15th and in the early morning hours of the 16th.  Hail between nickel and golfball-size was a common occurrence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire at the Paris Independent School District building Saturday afternoon.  The fire was limited to a maintenance area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front was moving into west Georgia during the afternoon.  A weak upper-level disturbance was moving from the mid-south into the mid-Atlantic.  Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in advance of the front during the mid and late afternoon hours and continued into the evening hours ahead of the cold front.  Instability and dynamics were far less impressive than with previous severe events this spring, but sufficient enough for isolated strong thunderstorms to develop across north Georgia. One persistent cell lingered over the Carroll county area of west central Georgia for over an hour producing penny to golf ball-sized hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Times Herald of Newnan reported that lightning struck on or near the county administrative building rendering the phone system inoperable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe storms formed during the morning and evening hours of May 2nd, producing mainly small hail and a few reports of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a high voltage transmission line near the intersection of Stearns Road and Route 59 which knocked out two distribution substations which caused 45,000 customers to loose power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the 23rd, a weak cold front pushed into Arkansas from the Plains and stalled. A southwest wind flow aloft drove a storm system toward the state, with the system interacting with the front. Isolated severe thunderstorms popped up in the western counties during the evening. The system passed over the region late on the 23rd and early on the 24th, with precipitation becoming more widespread.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a natural gas line, causing an explosion. Three residences near the area were evacuated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ingnited a roof fire in Dolington Manor in Lower Makefield Township on the late afternoon of the 21st. The fire quickly spread into the home's attio and second floor and destroyed the upper levels. Heavy fire damage occurred. Firefighters contained the fire to the attic and second floor. Firefighters rescued two family dogs and a cat while battling the blaze. One firefighter suffered a minor burn to his right arm. The 300-year-old stone structure suffered no major structural damage and should remain intact and livable once repairs to the upper floors were done. Twelve different fire compnaies helped battle the blaze.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This is a continuation of the high/strong wind event which began late on January 31st.||A deep, negatively-tilted upper trough was rotating rapidly through the southeast U.S. from the afternoon of January 31st into the early morning hours of February 1st.  A very strong low-level jet of 60-70 mph or greater was noted just above the surface. Surface winds of 45 to 60 mph accompanied this system , particularly as a broad area of showers swept across the area during the evening hours and shortly after midnight.  These winds resulted in a number of trees and power lines being blown down, especially across north Georgia counties.  In advance of this system during the afternoon of the 31st, strong easterly winds across north Georgia, much of which was located in a cold air wedge, caused additional wind damage.||Damage during the early morning hours of the 1st occurred mainly in Dade, Chattooga, Whitfield, Murray, Towns, Dawson, and Lumpkin counties.  Dade, Chattooga, and Murray counties bore the brunt of the damage, where in each county a dozen or more trees and/or power lines were blown down.||In addition, a narrow line of thunderstorms was embedded within a large area of heavy rain accompanying the upper-level system.  This was the same line of thunderstorms that caused wind damage in Columbus during the evening of the 31st.  This line of thunderstorms caused lightning damage in Coweta and Butts county just before and just after midnight, respectively.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The public reported that lightning struck a home causing damage to the structure.  A portion of an outside wall was ripped apart and wires in the electrical circuit breaker box were charred.  However, the structure did not sustain any fire or smoke damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Delray Beach early in the morning setting it on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house around 3 AM in Delray Beach and left a smoldering area in the roof that ignited several hours later. Smoke was first noted in the house at around 1 PM, and the fire was put out by 4 PM.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Marginally severe thunderstorms, mainly producing hail up to the size of nickels.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed three cows.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A single positive cloud to ground lightning strike caused a tree to explode outside of a home in Maple Shade. Pieces of the tree damaged the siding of the home and shattered a bedroom window sending shards of glass onto the bed. The boy was not in the bed at that time. A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through Burlington County at that time.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed across the northern Illinois on April 25th and produced mainly large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Circle Road and caused some smoke and charring in the house, as well as blowing a hole in part of the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A storm system intensified as it moved toward the southeastern states on Saturday Night May 10th and Sunday, May 11th. The combination of warm unstable air and strong wind shear increased the potential for severe thunderstorms and tornadoes across much of the region with a Moderate Risk area issued by the Storms Prediction Center for Sunday. An upper jet axis moved across central Georgia with vertical lift along and north of the jet axis leading to widespread convection over much of southern Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pierce County Fire-Rescue reported a lightning strike caused a brush fire off of Satilla Road. Georgia Forestry crews were dispatched and the blaze was contained.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front gradually moved through the region during the afternoon and evening of the 31st. Ahead of this front, showers and thunderstorms occurred earlier in the day, with another round moving through later in the afternoon and evening with the front itself. Some of the thunderstorms turned locally severe given the unstable air mass that was in place.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm rolled through the Pitman, New Jersey area around midday on the 31st. Several cloud to ground lightning strikes were generated by this thunderstorm. One of the lightning bolts struck a church building in Pitman at 1:05 PM EDT. A fire resulted, which caused some damage to the roof and second floor of the structure. No one was in the building at the time the lightning struck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front gradually moved through the region during the afternoon and evening of the 31st. Ahead of this front, showers and thunderstorms occurred earlier in the day, with another round moving through later in the afternoon and evening with the front itself. Some of the thunderstorms turned locally severe given the unstable air mass that was in place.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Some thunderstorms tracked across Cape May County during the afternoon of the 31st. Frequent cloud to ground lightning was produced by these thunderstorms. One of the lightning bolts struck a pole in Ocean City at about 3:05 PM EDT. As a result of the lightning strike, the pole was brought down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front gradually moved through the region during the afternoon and evening of the 31st. Ahead of this front, showers and thunderstorms occurred earlier in the day, with another round moving through later in the afternoon and evening with the front itself. Some of the thunderstorms turned locally severe given the unstable air mass that was in place.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a home on Ashland Street in Doylestown and started a fire. The occupants were in the house when the roof caught fire. Firefighters from three engine companies assisted in battling the blaze. The couple was not displaced from their home and no injuries occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front gradually moved through the region during the afternoon and evening of the 31st. Ahead of this front, showers and thunderstorms occurred mainly in the afternoon. Some of the thunderstorms turned locally severe given the unstable air mass that was in place.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at a Milton substation damaged some equipment. It caused 1,741 Delmarva Power and Light customers in Milton and another 67 in Harbeson to lose power. The outage last about four and a half hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS developed over northeast Nebraska during the night of the 28th and early morning of the 29th.  The storms progressed east along with an area of strong moisture transport.  They were quite elevated by the time they made their way into northwest and north central Iowa.  A few of the storms intensified a few hours after sunrise and became wind producers.  A wind gust around 70 MPH occurred in the Badger area of Webster County as one of the stronger storms passed.  Just before that time, winds bent the metal on a roof of a building in Badger.  As the thunderstorms moved over the Waterloo area, a person was struck by lightning and injured outside of the Waterloo Post Office.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck and injured one outside of the Waterloo Post Office.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The Elk County 911 Center received a direct lightning strike that disrupted nearly all communications.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Elk County 911 Center sustained a lightening strike that disrupted nearly all communications and damaged or destroyed key equipment. EMA officials said they lost several computers and dispatchers were using portable radios to dispatch emergency crews. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms in southeast Wisconsin generated cloud-to-ground lightning strikes that resulted in structural damage or fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a radio antenna on a home on National Avenue damaged a breadmaker, interior wiring, and electrical outlets.  However , there was no fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms in southeast Wisconsin generated cloud-to-ground lightning strikes that resulted in structural damage or fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck a tree and air conditioning unit of a home in New Berlin.  The current was carried into the basement of the home and the resultant fire was contained mostly in the basement.  Electrical wiring was damaged. Smoke damage was noted elsewhere in the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved slowly north across southeast Missouri during the afternoon. Large clusters of thunderstorms produced very heavy rain and a few reports of large hail. Rainfall amounts averaged from 2 to 4 inches during the 24-hour period, with isolated higher amounts up to 5 inches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while walking home with an umbrella. He received burns and was taken to a St. Louis hospital. He was released within a week.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved over the Mid South on the evening of March 31st and showers and thunderstorms developed across eastern Arkansas. Some of the stronger storms produced large hail and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer at Arkansas State University outside of Kays Hall. 400 students had to be evacuated due to smoke from the transformer.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: North Texas was impacted with a linear mesoscale convective system as well as discrete supercell thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours.  An EF-2 tornado destroyed several homes in the town of Crowley and several other brief tornadoes were reported as well.  Other severe reports included large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning reportedly caused a car fire, melting the cars antenna and battery.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and severe thunderstorms developed along a cold frontal boundary during the afternoon of the 4th over northern Virginia and then moved across the Delmarva Peninsula during the evening of the 4th. In addition to the severe weather, the thunderstorms were prolific lightning producers. Between 8 p.m. EDT and 11 p.m. EDT about 4,700 cloud-to-surface lightning strikes occurred across the Delmarva Peninsula and adjacent coastal waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and an ensuing fire damaged a garage in Trappe.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: North Texas was impacted with a linear mesoscale convective system as well as discrete supercell thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours.  An EF-2 tornado destroyed several homes in the town of Crowley and several other brief tornadoes were reported as well.  Other severe reports included large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and burned a hole in the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two clusters of showers and thunderstorms impacted mainly extreme southeast Kansas and far southwest Missouri. Flash flooding occurred with both clusters. Two to six inches of rain fell on saturated soil conditions, leading to a quick onset of flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a mobile home to burn down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved into Iowa from the west during the early morning hours of the 23rd.  Though the thunderstorms were not severe, a considerable amount of lightning occurred with the storms.  Lightning struck a house in Urbandale around 4 AM CDT.  A bedroom was set on fire, causing minor damage to that area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several factors came into play for a significant severe weather event over the southern half of Oklahoma. A upper level disturbance moved through the central plains, and a cold front moved into the northwest third of Oklahoma by mid afternoon. An area of surface low pressure developed over far southwest Oklahoma, with a dry line extending to the south of this feature. Thunderstorms developed and quickly become severe, producing very large hail. A few tornadoes also occurred. The storms tracked east during the evening hours, with a line of storms also developing along the cold front that moved southeast. Training of thunderstorms over parts of southeast Oklahoma allowed for flash flooding to develop. Only minor damage was reported with all severe weather. Monetary damages were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at a nursing home caused some roof damage. No other damage was reported. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable airmass moved into Iowa during the day on the 29th as a warm front lifted north into the state during the afternoon.  Low pressure approached from the west, along with a cold front so that the triple point was near the western Iowa, eastern Nebraska area by late afternoon.  Thunderstorms erupted quickly during the late afternoon and evening hours in the unstable airmass.  By evening, the low level jet was in the 40 to 60 kt range, feeding moisture into the state and pushing precipitable water values to around 200% of normal, in the 1.5 to 1.8 inch range.  MUCAPE reached 3000 to 3500 J/kg over western Iowa, with lifted indices in the -6 to -10 C. range.  The freezing level was quite high, limiting the hail size somewhat with this event, at 14,300 feet.  The available CAPE in the -10 to -30 C. layer of the atmosphere was in the 300 to 500 J/kg range.  The DCAPE was between 800 and 1000 J/kg.  The environment was highly sheared with 50 to 65 kts of shear available during the event.  The LCL was also quite low, in the 750 to 1250 meter range.  Thunderstorms erupted over western Iowa stretching into north central Iowa first.  It did not take long for the storms to become severe with hail and high winds.  Most of the hail reported was in the pea to marble size, with the larger stones in the nickel to quarter size range.  The primary mode of severe weather was high winds and several tornadoes.  The secondary, but significant threat, was heavy rainfall.  A band of 3 to 5 inches of rain fell between U.S. Highway 30 and U.S. Highway 20 during the event.  The heaviest rainfall total was in Greene County at Jefferson, with 5.90 inches.  Tornadoes began to touch down in western Iowa in Crawford County with two brief touchdowns.  One was west of Dow City, causing roof and shingle damage to a farmhouse there.  The next was east of Denison where a barn roof was removed and a trailer house was destroyed.  A tornado in Carroll County caused damage to 3 farmsteads southeast of Templeton.  A machine shed was completely destroyed and numerous other buildings sustained damage.  Trees also had substantial damage. Two tornadoes touched down in Calhoun County.  One near Farnhamville, tore the roof off of a home and downed power lines.  The second caused damage to trees, outbuildings, and power lines on four farmsteads.  Farther south, a brief touchdown was reported in Dallas County in open fields west of Minburn.  Another tornado touched down in Dallas County later on, west of Adel, and was on the ground for about 4 miles.  A more substantial tornado touched down near Murray in Clarke County with one reported on the ground for about 9 miles.  As the storms moved east, another tornado was on the ground for over 10 miles in Warren and Marion Counties.  The most significant tornado occurred in Marion and Mahaska Counties where an EF2 tornado was on the ground for about 18 miles.  Several homes were damaged along its path, two mobile homes were destroyed, and considerable damage was done to trees in the area.  Up to 10 people were injured with this tornado, mainly in Attica.  The official damage count from this tornado included 5 homes destroyed, 15 with major damage, and another 25 with minor damage.  Many of the storms produced high winds with several reports of winds in the 65 to 75 MPH range.  Considerable tree damage was reported and some structural damage, mainly outbuildings and shingle damage.  Two cars were blown off of the road east of Manning by the high winds.  Building debris was blown onto Highway D60 near Gowrie, causing a brief closure.  High winds in Butler County blew down a machine shed and barn southwest of Aplington, very near to where an EF5 tornado struck just days before.  Extensive damage was done to a farmstead there with some damage done to the house itself as well.  Lightning struck a man in Carroll.  The lightning bolt hit his driveway, blowing out a chunk of concrete out of the driveway and also injured the man.  He was taken to hospital, treated, and released with minor injuries.  Flooding became a significant issue after the heavy rainfall of the previous few days.  Extensive river flooding occurred across the central third of the state.  Record crests were recorded on the Iowa River at Marshalltown.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms erupted along a stalled frontal boundary over the central South Plains of west Texas during the afternoon hours of the 27th. Many of these storms, initially supercells, produced large hail and damaging winds. The activity gradually evolved into a linear complex of storms that propagated southeastward along with the frontal boundary during the late evening. Wind-blown hail damaged more than 2,000 acres of young cotton crops across the area. The worst agricultural damage was generally along the U.S. Highway 87 corridor south of Lubbock.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a structure fire near downtown Lubbock around 16:30 CST. A local business, located in the 600 block of Broadway Avenue, lost equipment in the fire. No injuries were reported. In addition, more than 350 homes and businesses were temporarily without power due to lightning strikes to local utilities.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low pressure system crossed the Mid Atlantic during the afternoon and evening hours of May 8th. This system along with warm temperatures and high dew points triggered numerous strong to severe showers and thunderstorms across the region. Two tornadoes occurred in central Virginia. Several storms produced damaging winds that downed trees and power lines in portions of northern and central Virginia. A few locations reported flooding as storms trained over the same area through the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper reported that lightning caused a fire at a home on the 600 block of Joshua Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A storm system was in the Texas Panhandle during the early evening of the 14th. At the same time, a warm front lifted to the north ahead of the system. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and north of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A hand-built historical house known as Eagle Plantation burned down when struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A band of showers and thunderstorms produced occasional lightning.  A woman in northern Lauderdale County was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 28 year old female was struck by lightning while standing on a carport. The person was ambulanced to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front advancing from Louisiana into Arkansas triggered thunderstorms in central and southern Arkansas on the afternoon and evening of the 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year-old male was stuck and killed by lightning while standing under a large pine tree in the 1800 block of South Jackson Street (about 3 miles west-southwest of downtown Little Rock). Males 13 and 14 years old were injured. The lightning strike occurred just as the storm was moving into the area. Lightning detection equipment showed very few cloud-to-ground strikes with this particular storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike in Olney, from scattered thunderstorms in southeast Illinois, did damage to a building and several autos. The falling debris indirectly injured 3 people.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a 60 foot tall brick chimney in downtown Olney resulted in damage to 16 autos and the roof of the building. Bricks were thrown as far as one block away. Three people were indirectly injured by falling bricks and debris. Ages and genders of the three people were not available. The three injuries were minor, and the people were treated and released at a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused substantial damage to two homes in Leon County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes in the Tower Oaks subdivision off Tower Road were struck by lightning.  Damage to both homes was confined to the roofs and ceilings.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The first widespread severe weather outbreak to affect south-central and southeast Wisconsin occurred on April 25th. It consisted of mostly large hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter, a couple damaging, straight-line wind reports, two tornadoes in Columbia County, and scattered flash flooding due to heavy rains and traning thunderstorm cells. Additionally, lightning struck several buildings and started fires that left damage.  Many power outages were reported thanks to tree branches snapping power lines, and up to 11,000 customers in southern Wisconsin lost power for varying time periods.  Synoptically, low pressure over southeast Minnesota moved northeast with a trailing cold front. Just ahead of the cold front was found strong warm air advection and moisture advection associated with a low-level jet.  Surface dewpoints poked into the mid to upper 60s ahead of the cold front while a favorable jet stream pattern existed aloft.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: During the pre-dawn hours, lightning struck a telephone pole behind the Police Department, damaging an outdoor siren, and several pieces of computer equipment.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and started a fire which caused substantial damage to the residence.

Hail to the size of half dollars fell, and winds to 70 mph were reported across the region. Minor damage was reported, mainly to tree limbs, power lines, and some structures. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moderately unstable, sheared environment was in place across northern Indiana ahead of a cold front. The atmosphere remained capped until the late afternoon and evening hours, when storms began to develop rapidly. Several storms south of a Monon, Indiana to Decatur, Indiana line became strong and even in some instances severe. A few storms exhibited rotation with one tornado confirmed in Wabash County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe storms affected southeast Wisconsin with large hail and strong winds gusting to around 56 knots (65 mph).  Synoptically, low pressure moved northeast through the La Crosse area while a warm front pushed north to a Marquette to Sheboyban county line.  Daytime maximum temperatures reached the 70s while surface dewpoints peaked in the 50s. Clusters or short lines of storms were generated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire to the roof area.

The bolt came through his windshield, and striking him on the shoulder. The vehicle stopped a few blocks away and he regained consciousness long enough to call his father before passing back out. He was treated and released from a local hospital with no serious injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The area's first spring season severe convective weather struck southeastern North Dakota Monday (21st) morning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in north Fargo. The strike blew out many of the home's windows, tore a hole in the roof, and caused water damage in the basement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across east central Minnesota, one of which produced injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An isolated thunderstorm produced a lightning bolt that injured three  construction workers at the Minneapolis International Airport. All three were alert when rescue workers arrived. Two refused medical treatment and one person was taken to Hennepin County Medical Center with minor injuries. Information provided by Minneapolis Star Tribune newspaper.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over eastern North Carlina during the afternoon hours north of a stalled frontal boundary. A few of the storms became severe producing large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people struck by lightning just south of Rodanthe. One person had to be revived by emergency medical technicians.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms formed along a cold front which pushed through northeastern Alabama during the morning hours on March 4th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home sparking a fire destroying the residence.  Exact time and location unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm frontal boundary lifted north across Iowa during the day on the 25th and was located over northern Iowa by the evening hours.  The airmass became very unstable to the south of the front as surface temperatures warmed into the 85 to 90 degree range, and dewpoints rose into the low to mid 70s.  This produced CAPE in the 4500 to 5000 J/kg range and a lifted index of -10 to -15 C.  The atmosphere was weakly sheared with 20 to 25 kts of bulk shear.  The freezing level was relatively low, around to just over 13,000 feet.  A small area of thunderstorms formed over northwest and north central Iowa by the late afternoon and early evening hours.  The storms became more widespread and formed into an MCS, which propagated southeast across the state and became severe.  The storms produced hail, high winds, and some flash flooding.  The primary mode of severe weather with this MCS was hail.  Reports of hail were widespread.  Much of the hail was in the three-quarter to one and one quarter inch range.  There were, however, several reports of large hail.  Three inch diameter hail fell northeast of Madrid in Boone County, with another report of two and one half inch diameter hail about 3 miles southwest of that.  Later on, another two and one half inch hail report was received in Story County.  Much of the larger hail occurred during the early stages of the event with golf ball size hail reported in Story, Dallas, and Marshall Counties as well.  During the late evening hours, golf ball size hail also fell in Polk and Warren Counties as a small area of stronger storms developed within the MCS.  The storms produced gusty winds in most areas as they passed, however much of the wind was below severe levels.  Winds gusted to 60 to 70 MPH during the later part of the severe event in Dallas, Polk and Warren Counties as a beta bow element dropped south across these counties.  Rainfall was very heavy with the storms and did cause some flash flooding.  Water was reported over Highway 17 near the Des Moines River in Dallas County, caused by flash flooding.  Fortunately, the weather had been relatively dry for the previous 2 weeks, so antecedent soil conditions were relatively dry.  Five inches of rain fell west of Polk City in Polk County in a 2 to 3 hour time frame.  There were several reports of rainfall in the 2 to 3 inch range in under three hours.  Although the system was not a tornadic system, there was one report of a funnel cloud in Grundy County.  Lightning struck a house in Polk County.  The house was damaged by the lightning wand it was started on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was damaged due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and injured a young boy along State Road 53 near Madison.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and injured a young boy while has was walking along State Road 53.  He was transported to the hospital in serious condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front brought isolated thunderstorms to the region, with gusty winds and hail being reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A structure fire was caused by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Supercell thunderstorms developed along a nearly stationary frontal boundary across Central and South Central Kansas during the late afternoon hours.  The highly sheared environment lead to the supercells producing tornadoes between Wichita, Kansas and Winfield Kansas. The supercell thunderstorms evolved into a complex of thunderstorms during the early morning hours of June 13th, 2008. The complex of thunderstorms moved slowly over Southeast Kansas producing flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck by lightning and transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary was located to the northwest of Iowa and remained nearly stationary as a shortwave advanced across the state.  The airmass became very unstable with in the 3000 to 4000 J/kg range and lifted indices in the -6 to -9 C. range.  The atmosphere was weakly sheared with 20 to 30 kts of shear.  A fair amount of downdraft CAPE was available at the onset with values in the 800 to 1000 J/kg range.  CAPE in the -10 to -30 C. layer of the atmosphere was somewhat limited, in the 200 to 300 J/kg range and the freezing level was around 14,400 feet.  Considerable moisture transport took place during the evening with precipitable water values rising to between 1.8 and 2 inches.  Thunderstorms initially formed fairly close to the frontal boundary, then propagated south-southeast across the state.  Initially, the storms produced three quarter to one inch diameter hail, along with occasional wind gusts to around 60 MPH.  As the later part of the afternoon and evening hours wore on, the storms transformed into a heavy rain event.  As the storms moved south across central Iowa, rainfall rates were incredible, with one of the storms producing a rainfall rate of 8.5 inches per hour for about 10 minutes.  The area received nearly four and three quarters of an inch of rain northeast of Ames.  There were numerous reports of rainfall in the 2 to 3 inch range, much of it falling in about an hour.  The ground conditions were relatively dry as little rainfall had occurred during the previous 2 weeks.  The heavy rain did not cause major problems in rural areas.  The Des Moines metropolitan area was hard hit with one of the heavier reports in Windsor Heights where 3.54 inches fell, 2.48 of which fell in a 40 minute time span.  This caused extensive ponding of water around the city, in some places nearly 3 feet deep.  Walnut Creek, in Polk County, rose 10 to 11 feet in just 3 hours and crested just over flood stage.  There were numerous other heavy rain reports, including 3.89 inches in the Webster City area, 3.61 inches in Marshalltown, and 3.38 inches in Johnston.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: KWWL reported that lightning struck a home in Waterloo around 1500 CST.  Fire crews were called to the scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another weak wave tracked across the area, allowing numerous storms to develop. Several produced one-quarter to half-inch size hail, but a few better-organized storms produced isolated golf-ball sized hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the corner of one of the apartment buildings in the Indiana Lakes Apartment complex. At least four apartments, all on the third floor, were destroyed. Eight apartments on the second floor suffered extensive water damage and many on the first floor have both smoke and water damage. Luckily, a firewall prevented the fire from spreading to adjacent areas. Damage is estimated at one million dollars for structure and contents. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably hot and humid air mass led to severe thunderstorms occurring across Eastern Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of the 10th. Wind damage was reported in nearly every county in Eastern Pennsylvania. About 185,000 homes and businesses lost power. Power was not fully restored until the night of the 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 19-year-old woman was injured after she was struck by lightning near her Church Road home. The lightning strike struck a tree and then her.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning convection helped stabilize the area until early afternoon when strong heating and an approaching short wave and front set the stage for rapid thunderstorm development. While instability was considered moderate, steep mid-level lapse rates allowed for a favorable profile for large hail and damaging winds. The storms began as very proficient hail producers and evolved into causing wind damage as they evolved.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on State Route 13 in the city of North Manchester, causing extensive damage to the residence. No injuries were reported but damage is estimated at $50,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably hot and humid air mass led to severe thunderstorms occurring across Eastern Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of the 10th. Wind damage was reported in nearly every county in Eastern Pennsylvania. About 185,000 homes and businesses lost power. Power was not fully restored until the night of the 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire in Exeter Township. Lightning struck the roof and the fire began in the upper portion of the house. About seventy-five fire fighters from a half dozen companies helped battle the blaze and contained it in the upper portion of the house. The family and pets escaped unharmed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably hot and humid air mass led to severe thunderstorms occurring across Eastern Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of the 10th. Wind damage was reported in nearly every county in Eastern Pennsylvania. About 185,000 homes and businesses lost power. Power was not fully restored until the night of the 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a house fire on Burning Tree Lane in Lower Macungie Township. When fire fighters arrived, flames were seen through the roof. Five companies helped extinguish the blaze. No injuries were reported. Another lightning strike at the Municipal Building in Whitehall Township did hardly any damage. The same building was struck by lightning in 2007. The combination of damaging winds and lightning caused about 14,000 Pennsylvania Power and Light homes and businesses to lose power in Lehigh County. Metropolitan Edison reported about 12,000 homes and businesses lost power in their service area including Lehigh County. All power was restored by the evening of the 11th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several clusters of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front across mainly northeastern Indiana. The storms interacted with 30 to 40 knots of shear and CAPES in excess of 2000 j/kg, resulting in several reports of damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the corner of the Farm Credit Services office in Bluffton. Employees reported a loud boom, but nothing was apparent immediately. An off duty Bluffton fire fighter in the area noticed smoke from the building and began evacuations of the building and call for personnel. The fire quickly got into the attic and the building was a total loss with damage estimates of at least $250,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent upper level disturbance and associated frontal boundary sparked strong to severe thunderstorms from the mid morning through the afternoon hours of April 23rd across central, south-central and southeast Kansas. Hail as large as golfballs and winds up to 60 mph were reported. Additionally, slow moving and training thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall amounts, particularly across the northern half of Marion County, where excessive runoff caused the North Cottonwood River to overflow its banks, flooding the town of Durham with around 18 inches of water.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms affected south-central Kansas during the evening hours of April 23rd. Lightning struck an electrical line leading to an Arkansas City home, setting a computer area in an upstairs room ablaze. The blaze was contained to the one room. Information courtesy of the Arkansas City Traveler.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sunday afternoon, a cold front moved south into northeast Texas and across southwest and south central Arkansas. Showers and thunderstorms developed along this boundary late in the day. The thunderstorms rapidly become strong to severe with support of a disturbance aloft moving through the region with the winds aloft being from the northwest.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 21 year old male was struck by lightning in the community of Simms, Texas.  The man was working on an oil rig when lightning struck the oil derrick.  The man was treated at a local hospital from burns but was released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across southern New England during the afternoon hours providing a focus for showers and thunderstorms across much of the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two brothers were hospitalized after lightning struck the ground directly in front of them.  Their injuries were non life threatening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved through through the area earlier in the day allowing for warm temperatures over central Indiana.  Severe storms formed in advance of a cold front that moved through later at night.  These storms contained hail and damaging thunderstorm winds.  Three tornadoes also formed with these storms including one that moved through the east side of Indianapolis.  Heavy rain caused flash flooding across many locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One home was completely destroyed fire caused by a lightning strike, while another home received heavy fire damage.

Three tornadoes also formed with these storms including one that moved through the east side of Indianapolis.  Heavy rain caused flash flooding across many locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Fishers causing extensive fire, heat, and smoke damage.  The first floor collapsed into the basement.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and caused a fire to begin on the rear corner of the home.  The winds caught the home next door on fire.  A third house had minor damage from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system tracked northeast from the northern Great Lakes into southeast Canada on Saturday May 31st. A cold front associated with this system tracked east across eastern New York and western New England during the mid to late afternoon hours of Saturday, preceded and accompanied by scattered thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning near Torrington, which started a fire inside one of the walls in the basement. The fire was extinguished by the local fire department.||The basement was badly damaged, with estimated monetary costs of $20,000 to $30,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved across central Indiana during the morning hours on Mother's Day.  During the afternoon hours, winds associated with a strong low pressure system caused damage around the area.  The threats during the morning hours were lightning, thunderstorm winds, and a tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the wall of a church catching the wall on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two police officers, one 38 years old, and the other 54 years old, received a side-flash of current from a lightning strike which hit a parking lot light at a sports complex.  The officers were taken to the hospital, where one was in fair condition, and the other was in good condition.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled front resided across the Mid Atlantic during the afternoon and evening of June 4th, allowing moisture and instability to pool along the boundary. This combined with several strong upper level disturbances resulted in numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Many of these thunderstorms became severe. While penny sized was reported in spots, damaging winds from the thunderstorms was widespread. An EF-0 tornado was also confirmed in the community of Chesapeake Beach in Calvert County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported that lightning struck a home on Sandy Bottom Road, sparking a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of thunderstorms, a few severe, rolled out of northern Kansas and into southeast Nebraska during the late evening hours of May 23rd and the early morning hours of May 24th.  The storms produced strong winds with scattered areas of damage and were fed by a strong low-level jet advecting moisture northward.  Ahead of the severe thunderstorms in southeast Nebraska, heavy rain producing thunderstorms, with isolated embedded severe thunderstorms, caused flash flooding near Platte Center, which is just northwest of Columbus, and wind damage in the Norfolk area.  In addition, indirectly related to the thunderstorms, an area of strong winds of 50 to 60 mph developed in the wake of the thunderstorms.  These winds produced areas of scattered damage, mainly in Lancaster county Nebraska in the middle of the night and in Page county Iowa between about 730 and 830 am.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire that caused an estimated $80,000 damage to a home in Nebraska City.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A closed upper low moved across the Ohio Valley, and a strong jet stream was in place to trigger severe thunderstorms across portions of southwest Virginia, during the afternoon of May 11th. These storms brought hail up to the size of quarters, wind damage, and lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Blacksburg. The bolt struck the dormer, went through a room and hit a galvanized metal water line. This started a fire in the wall. Damages are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning soundings indicated a moist and unstable airmass over the local area with low wind shear and a light southwest steering flow. The precipitable water was 1.76 inches at Jacksonville with around 3000 J/kg of CAPE and a lifted index of -6 degrees Celcius. An upper level low pressure system approached the eastern seaboard during the afternoon which pushed a surface trough over Georgia. This trough in concert with the sea breezes sparked numerous severe storms across the local forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire off of Dyal Road that resulted in 1 fatality and 1 injury. The time of the event was based on radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed quickly across Val Verde County in the unstable environment ahead of an upper level trough moving in from the Western U.S. The line of convection moved to the northeast bringing severe weather to much of the hill country.  Several long track supercells moved across the Austin area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was a lightning strike that caused a house fire on Legends of Hutto Trail near state highway 1660.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Inreasing large-scale lift and instability brought showers and thunderstorms to north Texas.  Flash flooding was the result.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Wind Row Drive and caused a fire which damaged the attic and the second floor.  Extensive water and smoke damage also occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered, weak thunderstorms developed in the warm advection regime ahead of a surface cold front. The storms were not severe, but a teenage girl was injured when a lightning bolt struck near her home, entered the piping, and wounded her.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 15-year-old girl was struck by lightning when a bolt hit near her home, traveled through the steel plumbing, and into the shower nozzle.  The girl was taking a shower at the time she was struck. A single indentation was evident on the girl's knee.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two firefighters were struck by lightning while conducting mop up of a prescribed burn west of Whitefish, MT.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two firefighters, a 25 year old woman and a 29 year old man, members of the Flahtead National Forest were struck by lightning while finishing up a mop up of a prescribed burn west of Whitefish, MT and heading back to their vehicles. The lightning directly hit two nearby trees and injuried the firefighters. The two firefighters were taken to the hospital and listed as in stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was draped across north Georgia early on May 10th with an active northwest flow aloft.  Meanwhile...a vigorous short wave aloft was approaching the area from the southern plains.  The stationary front provided the focus for two rounds of showers and thunderstorms, one early in the morning on the 10th and another in the afternoon.  The activity tracked east-southeast with the upper flow aloft, mainly across north Georgia during the early morning and across central Georgia during the afternoon.  An isolated strong supercell also tracked across the southern part of central Georgia during the evening.  After a lull of convective activity for about four hours, intense multicell thunderstorms tracked into the area from Alabama after midnight and before dawn on the 11th.  As these thunderstorms tracked across west central and central Georgia, 15 tornadoes were identified by subsequent surveys making this the most significant tornado outbreak to affect the area since the Katrina-associated tornadoes on August 29, 2005.  Millions of dollars of property damage were reported as many homes were destroyed from these tornadoes from the western and southern suburbs of Atlanta southeastward across Macon, Dublin, and other counties in east central and southeast Georgia.  Many of these counties were eligible for disaster assistance from the federal government.||In addition to the tornadoes and thunderstorm winds that caused extensive damage in dozens of counties across north and central Georgia during the early morning hours of May 11th, strong gradient winds developed on the back side of the strong cold front that moved through the area as low pressure intensified across the mid-Atlantic region.  The strong winds combined with wet ground resulted in dozens of trees being blown down in some north Georgia counties.  There were also two deaths as a result of downed trees in Barrow and Gwinnett county, all non-thunderstorm-related winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that a two-story home was struck and set on fire by lightning on Freshman Drive.  Damage was confined mostly to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm, moist airmass moved into southern New England providing enough instability for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area.  Several of these storms had very strong winds associated with them, evident in a 69 mph wind gust in Windsor Locks, CT and wind damage across much of western Massachusetts and northern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Quincy Patriot Ledger reported that lightning hit a shed in Sharon starting a fire that spread to an adjacent house.  No one was injured.

Several of these storms had very strong winds associated with them, evident in a 69 mph wind gust in Windsor Locks, CT and wind damage across much of western Massachusetts and northern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck DeCordova Museum.  Unspecified damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical wave over south Florida moved west of the area through the day which brought increased moisture over the area. Drier air from high pressure to the north infiltrated over southeast Georgia. Steering flow was light per a deformation zone over the area. Sea breeze and outflow initiated storms produced heavy rainfall over localized areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 54 year old man was struck by lightning while sitting under a tin frame shelter open that was exposed on three sides. He suffered a minor burn on his right side.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three tornadoes were spawned from supercell thunderstorms that developed over southeast Kansas.  These storms quickly moved into southwest Missouri causing devestating damage to homes, businesses, and trees in Newton, Barry, and Jasper counties.  One tornado, with an intensity that ranged from EF-4 to EF-1, killed 15 people as it tracked through Newton and Barry counties, while another tornado killed one person in Jasper County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught on fire as a result of a lightning strike.  The house was heavily damaged from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the northern portion of the area on May 24th and 25th. A few of these storms became severe and produced a mix of hail and wind damage across the north. Areas around West Point, MS received golf ball sized hail while areas between Brooksville and Macon, MS were hit by 70 to 80 mph winds which caused damage to homes, businesses and downed many trees and power lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck a church on Beamon Road and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms that moved through Central Wisconsin started a house fire in Wood County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck a tree and traveled through a coaxial cable that went into an adjacent house causing a fire in the house.  The fire burned inside walls and in the attic of the house. Fire damage was confined to one of the bedrooms and smoke damage to the home was minimal.  There was some water and roof damage that occurred during process of extinguishing the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure moved northeast through the Northern Plains while a cold front pushed southeast across Wisconsin.  Pre-frontal showers and scattered storms moved northeast through southern Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours.  Lightning accompanied the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a nearly 100-year-old church in/near Genessee on State Highway 83, and the resultant fire destroyed the structure.  The time of this event andn damage amount are broad estimates.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms occurred on July 21st and July 22nd ahead and along an approaching cold front. The front brought cooler air and temperatures into the 80s from July 23 to July 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage which caused a fire. The fire destroyed the garage and its contents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into Arkansas from the Plains late on the 13th. Scattered thunderstorms popped up along and ahead of the front, with a few severe storms noted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the Sills Peninsula at Greers Ferry Lake.  The ensuing fire destroyed the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Outflow boundaries from a Mesoscale Convective Complex in New York state provided a focus for a handful of thunderstorms across northwestern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two houses were struck by lightning in Southington.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across portions of northwest Wisconsin ahead of a complex frontal boundary. Some storms became severe in the late afternoon and produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was caused by a lightning strike. The house was totalled.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Redeveloping strong to severe showers and thunderstorms produce one to 2 inches of rainfall across much of northern Alabama, with locally around 3 inches in some areas over a 2 to 3 hour period. This caused some localized flash flooding in Morgan county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck a house on county road 1545 near its intersection with highway 31 near the Morgan and Cullman county line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was situated across north Georgia.  High pressure aloft had drifted off the east coast and a weak low pressure area was evident aloft over Georgia.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed with daytime heating during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe and produced damaging downburst winds, hail, and frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Paulding County 911 Center reported that two structures were set on fire by lightning.  Damage amounts were not specified.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Polk County 911 Center reported that several structural fires were set in the county by lightning.  Radar shows that the strongest reflectivity affected the western half of the county.  Exact damage amounts were not able to be determined.

Fire emergency crews were dispatched to at least four homes in the area.  One home however, sustained significant damage as the fire reignited several hours after being put out.  The home was a total loss.  No other significant damage was reported at the remaining sites.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous severe thunderstorms developed as a weak upper level trough interacted with a hot and humid airmass across the region. Strong downburst winds were characteristic of many of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire in Stratford.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Harris County 911 Center reported that five brush fires and one structural fire were started from lightning strikes.  No specific damage amount was provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front had drifted into the southeast parts of central Georgia while an active northwest flow continued aloft.  Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in this part of the state and moved south.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Houston County 911 Center reported that a couple of structures were set on fire by lightning strikes.  A couple of trees were also blown down in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two separate complexes of thunderstorms impacted north Texas causing wind damage as they moved southeast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning split an oak tree in two.  Bark was stripped from the tree due to the force of the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced frequent intense lightning that struck a condo complex in Pleasantville.  Lightning blew out windows and ignited a fire that caused 8 families to evacuate.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the upper portion of a condo complex, ignited fires, and displaced at least 8 families.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved across Northeast New Jersey the evening of Tuesday June 10th causing multiple severe thunderstorms across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Charles Street in Livingston was damaged due to being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved across Northeast New Jersey the evening of Tuesday June 10th causing multiple severe thunderstorms across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Lincoln Avenue.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck 3 houses in Hasbrouck Heights.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fayette County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck and set on fire a 4000 square foot home in the Harbor Lakes subdivision off Antioch Road, approximately three miles south-southeast of Fayetteville.  The fire was contained before the home was completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A young girl was struck and killed by lightning at Torreya State Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A young girl was struck and killed by lightning while sitting at a campsite picnic table at Torreya State Park.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms formed during the heat of the afternoon, aided by a weak surface trough that extended from northern Arkansas northeast across the Lower Ohio Valley. Tropical moisture combined with the slow movement of the storms resulted in locally very heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the resulting fire totalled a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong warm air advection took place across Iowa during the overnight hours of the 10th into the morning of the 11th.  CAPE increased to over 3000 J/kg as the lifted index fell to around -7.  A strong low level jet of 50 to 60 kts was in place over the state.  Thunderstorms formed initially over Kansas, then spread northeast into western Iowa.  A wind gust of 65 MPH occurred in Bedford as the storms passed.  Mainly, the storms produced very heavy rainfall. In Taylor County, an inch of rain fell in 30 minutes at Gravity.  For the most part, the storms produced wind gusts of 30 to 45 MPH and pea to marble size hail.  Flash flooding occurred in Crawford County as heavy rains caused the water to rise over the top of U.S. Highway 30.  Rainfall of nearly 2 inches in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Bedford.  Lightning struck a 20 year old male that was working with his father in their yard, killing him.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Massive and historic flash flooding struck central Indiana.  The Great Flood of June 2008 was one of Indiana's costliest natural disasters.  Major roads and interstates flooded.  Heavy rainfall on May 30th allowed streams and rivers to rise.  Additional heavy rainfall on the 3rd and the 4th added to these high levels.  Severe weather brought heavy rainfall on the 6th as well.  The stage was set for historic flooding in portions of central and southern Indiana.  The storms on the 6th exacerbated the situation by laying down a boundary in southern Illinois and southern Indiana.  A moist southerly low level jet rode over this boundary for more than 12 hours continually generating showers and thunderstorms.  Rainfall of two to nearly eleven inches fell across portions of central and southern Indiana.  The impact of the rain was immediate with widespread flash flooding occurring.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Whiteland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed as a weak upper level trough interacted with a hot and humid airmass across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire resulted from a lightning strike in West Milford.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms brought flash flooding and minor wind damage to central Indiana. Lightning also injured an individual as the storms moved through.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A construction worker was injured by lightning striking a crane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several clusters of pulse severe thunderstorms affected north Alabama during the evening hours.  The two strongest storms produced downbursts in Hazel Green in Madison County and in central Colbert County south of Tuscumbia and Muscle Shoals.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ingnited a small tree fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an occupied vehicle at 1430 New Bethel Road.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave trough moved eastward from the Great Lakes into Northern New England, eroding a mid level cap associated with a subtropical ridge over Southern New England.  This allowed widespread showers and thunderstorms to develop over the area resulting in numerous reports of wind damage throughout southern New England and the adjacent marine zones.  ||Despite the amount of damage the storms caused, they did bring some relief from a few days of record high temperatures across New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southern New England was under the favorable left front quadrant of a strong upper level jet as a shortwave moved across the region.  This shortwave provided enough lift in an already unstable atmosphere to produce showers and thunderstorms across much of the area.  Most of the events that occurred were hail though there were a few instances of damaging thunderstorm winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Ridgecrest Road, setting a fire.  Much of the home was damaged by the fire and the resulting smoke and water.  Firefighters were able to put out the blaze, but the home is unlivable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning injured a police officer in the town of Hampton when it struck nearby.  The policeman had stopped a motorist at the time and was asking the motorist for identification information.  The officer was knocked down and momentarily incapacitated by the strike, and then taken to a nearby hospital, where he was checked out and then released.
