EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and started a fire that damage the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated thunderstorms were associated with two lightning strikes that injured two people and killed another.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Methuen couple hiking in a park, took shelter under a tree during a thunderstorm. They were struck by lightning. The couple was transferred to a local hospital where the husband was declared dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated thunderstorms were associated with two lightning strikes that injured two people and killed another.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 49 year old man was walking on the beach when he was struck by lightning and knocked unconscious.  His wife was with him but was unharmed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was situated across north Georgia.  High pressure aloft had drifted off the east coast and a weak low pressure area was evident aloft over Georgia.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed with daytime heating during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe and produced damaging downburst winds, hail, and frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Eatonton Messenger reported that lightning struck Oconee Porter Fireplace and Insulation Building, a warehouse off Sammons Industrial Boulevard on the northwest side of Eatonton, was destroyed when a lightning strike set the roof and piles of insulation on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe Thunderstorm moved from interior sections of South Florida, across portions of the eastern metro areas and into the Atlantic Ocean producing hail, wind and lightning damage, and waterspouts. An estimated 12,000 customers lost power in Palm Beach County during the episode.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A total of 7 homes were struck by lightning across central and southern Miami-Dade County during the late morning and afternoon of June 18th. Damage was primarily to electrical appliances and roofing material.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed across northwest Illinois shortly after sunrise and quickly moved across far northern Illinois during the mid morning hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Yew Tree Court blowing a hole through the roof, knocking siding off of the house and blew out some electrical circuits but no fire was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Outflow boundaries from a Mesoscale Convective Complex in New York state provided a focus for a handful of thunderstorms across northwestern Connecticut and southwestern Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn on Mountain Road was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northwest flow aloft combined with daytime instability to generate scattered strong thunderstorms.  A few of these pulse-type storms became severe producing hail and one elderly man suffered minor injuries from a nearby lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 70 year old man raking the yard suffered minor injuries from a nearby lightning strike.  He received treatment at the hospital before being released several hours later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from afternoon thunderstorms caused damage to at least one house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree that was struck by lightning fell onto a house and briefly trapped its occupants.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several outflow boundaries were located over western and southwest Oklahoma. Strong instability developed near these boundaries by mid to late afternoon, with widespread showers and thunderstorms developing. Several thunderstorms became severe, but moved little through the early evening due to weak upper level winds. Jackson county seemed to take the worst of the thunderstorms, with several rounds of hail and strong winds reported. The slow movement of the thunderstorms and very heavy rain also caused some water problems on area roadways, with several closed for a couple of hours. The thunderstorms finally weakened and moved off to the south by the evening hours. Monetary damages were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning and burned to the ground. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a few severe thunderstorms across central and southern New Jersey during the afternoon and evening of the 29th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire destroyed the landmark Sweetwater Casino Restuarant in Mullica Township. Lightning struck the restaurant's electrical system. When firefighters arrived, the building was engulfed in flames.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed across northeast Pennsylvania in a hot and humid air mass ahead of an approaching cold front. Many of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A truck driver was struck by lightning while driving his truck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a few severe thunderstorms across central and southern New Jersey during the afternoon and evening of the 29th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a polo match in Colts Neck Township. Two men and six horses were knocked unconscious. Lightning struck about 30 seconds into the match. An umpire and a player were working near a horse trailer when the bolt hit and tossed them about ten feet. The umpire suffered a broken arm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms increased to severe strength across northeast Kansas, by the late morning hours of June 2, 2008. The complex continued to move southeast into west central Missouri. Very large hail, damaging thunderstorm winds, and flash flooding, accompanied the storms. Hail sizes were in the half dollar to golfball size range, with baseball size hail reported near Rich Hill. In addition to the large hail, thunderstorm wind gusts estimated between 60 and 80 miles an hour, felled trees and even tore a roof off a home near Trading Post, Kansas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 36 year old female was standing in the doorway of her home, when lightning struck nearby. She was transported to the hospital complaining of deafness.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered bouts of severe weather were generated during the late afternoon and evening, in advance of a cold front which exited Minnesota by the early morning hours of the 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 47 year old male was struck by lightning in his back yard. The victim was unconscious for several hours and admitted to Hennepin County Medical Center. Luckily, he suffered no serious injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered storms returned on the 20th with isolated severe weather and areas of heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire destroyed a sawmill. Lightning struck a power pole, setting fire to the electrical lines, then the electrical boxes, and finally, the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low level boundaries, an unstable airmass, and an upper level disturbance provided the trigger for isolated severe thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening of June 3, across southwest Virginia. One severe thunderstorm produced a brief EF0 tornado in the city of Roanoke. Other severe storms produced hail up to the size of golf balls.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a shed and caught it fire. Damage amounts are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow-moving surface boundary, nearly parallel with the mid-level flow affected  southern Wisconsin during the period of June 7th through June 9th.  A strengthening low-level jet and strong moisture advection produced several rounds of thunderstorms during the period in the vicinity of this boundary.  The atmosphere was very moist with precipitable water values around 2 inches.  Low to mid-level wind flow supported training of flood-producing thunderstorms.  A weak cool front pushed through southern Wisconsin late on the 8th/early on the 9th, finally ending the heavy rainfall.||The heavy rain axis for June 7-9th ran from Sauk County southeast to Milwaukee County, where generally 6 to 9 inches fell on a ground that was totally saturated due to record-setting winter snowfalls and a wet April, 2008.  Several locations topped 10 inches, and Watertown (Jefferson Co.) came in with 13.5 inches, 11.35 inches was measured in Oak Creek (Milwaukee Co.), and Elm Grove in Waukesha County picked up 10.8 inches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, and the current damaged the residents's electrical system, appliances, and televisions.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on a barrier island south of Topsail Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: During a thunderstorm, four people took refuge under a house on Lea Island. A boy was struck by lightning and was killed. Three others were indirectly struck by lightning and were transported to the hospital. They reportedly were not seriously injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Intense lightning at Pawley's Island started many house fires, and injured a firefighter.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple lightning strikes hit 10 homes, setting one ablaze. The homes were in the Debordieu and Prince George Island communities of Pawleys Island.  A firefighter was struck by the lighting while attempting to put out the fire. The strike was channeled through a fire hose, and the firefighter was taken to the hospital with minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Upper-level dynamics were becoming more favorable as an upper level trough was deepening in the mid part of the U.S. and starting to shift eastward.  This combined with a warm and unstable air mass allowed thunderstorms to develop across much of north and central Georgia during the afternoon and evening.  A few of these briefly became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Banks County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning set a barn on fire in the western part of the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An intense upper ridge, which had been drifting eastward across the southeast United States, was beginning to shift east of the region.  This was allowing deep Gulf moisture to surge northward into Georgia.  The presence of the upper ridge had allowed afternoon temperatures to soar into the 95 to 100 degree range.  This resulted in a very unstable atmosphere.  Consequently, isolated to scattered thunderstorms strong to severe thunderstorms developed quickly in the afternoon and continued up until midnight.  Initially the activity was mainly across the northern areas, but developed into central areas during the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Murray County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a home in the Carters Lake area.  No significant damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong upper-level trough was sweeping through the southeast on the 29th accompanied by an unusually strong cold front.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed in advance of the front in two waves, first across central Georgia during the afternoon, followed by another round across north Georgia during the late afternoon and evening.  Damaging straight-line winds occurred with several of the storms, along with frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  Very little hail was reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Henry County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck and set on a fire a home on Dorsey Road.  In addition, there was also a small brush fire in the northwest part of the county also started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was situated across north Georgia.  High pressure aloft had drifted off the east coast and a weak low pressure area was evident aloft over Georgia.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed with daytime heating during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe and produced damaging downburst winds, hail, and frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pulaski County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning strikes ignited two fires in southwest Pulaski county, one to a wheat field and the other to some woods.  Nine acres of a wheat field burned and two acres of woods burned before the fires were extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire east of Guffey, in Park County.  The combination of dry conditions and gusty winds allowed the fire to spread.  It eventually consumed 1,115 acres.  A shed and a camper trailer were also lost in the blaze.  ||Severe thunderstorms produced several small landspout tornadoes in Washington County, and intense thunderstorm winds in Elbert County.  In Weld County near Frederick, strong winds from a dry microburst snapped three utility poles, and downed electrical lines.  As a result, a small fire was started near Interstate 25 and State Highway 52.  The fire damaged irrigation equipment in a nearby field and some power poles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed along several boundaries that were located over Oklahoma. The thunderstorms moved slowly southeast during the afternoon, and continued developing and moving southeast into the overnight hours. Hail to baseball size was reported in Greer county, with several locations reporting hail over golfball size. Winds over 65 mph were also reported in southwest Oklahoma, with mostly tree damage reported. Monetary damages were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 7600 square foot home in the Oak Tree addition in Oklahoma City, burning it to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 100-year-old barn in Litchfield and ignited a fire that caused it to burn to the ground.  Damage to the barn and equipment in the barn was estimated at $100,000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that damaged a shed in Rochester.  The lightning apparently struck a nearby tree and followed the roots to the shed.  The fire damaged the side of the shed and some of the contents.  Damage was estimated at $500.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two-story apartment building in Colebrook and the resultant fire heavily damaged the structure.  Two families were displaced by the fire.  Damage was estimated at $200,000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large cluster of thunderstorms, known as a mesoscale convective system (MCS), developed near a cold front and swept across much of Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is believed to have set fire to a mobile home on Eiler Loop. A 48 year-old man in the home died in the fire. Just a few weeks previously, lightning had struck and burned out the water well on the same property, which is located on top of a hill.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was situated across north Georgia.  High pressure aloft had drifted off the east coast and a weak low pressure area was evident aloft over Georgia.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed with daytime heating during the afternoon and evening.  Several of these became severe and produced damaging downburst winds, hail, and frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Harris County Journal reported that lightning struck a large single-story wood frame home at the corner of Second Street and First Avenue.  The house was completely destroyed from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms with locally heavy rainfall developed across Southeast Arizona resulting in flash flooding, sporadic wind and lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire in a vacant home on the southwest side of Tucson near West Valencia and South Mission Roads.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong upper-level trough was sweeping through the southeast on the 29th accompanied by an unusually strong cold front.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed in advance of the front in two waves, first across central Georgia during the afternoon, followed by another round across north Georgia during the late afternoon and evening.  Damaging straight-line winds occurred with several of the storms, along with frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  Very little hail was reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Forsyth County 911 Center reported that lightning strikes started several house fires in the southern half of the county.  Specific damages were not provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually deep upper low persisted in the northeast U.S., a continuation of the pattern established during the later half of June.  This was allowing a cold front to approach from the north.  This, in combination with ample daytime heating and moisture, allowed for isolated afternoon pulse thunderstorms to develop across many areas of north and central Georgia.  The activity was most numerous and intense across central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Upson County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck a 57 year-old male while in the kitchen of his home.  The individual sustained minor injuries as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind and large hail over parts of Elbert, Lincoln and Weld Counties.  Large hail from golfball to baseball size was reported in Elbert and Lincoln Counties.  Lightning also struck a home in Fort Collins damaging the roof and attic.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A church in Scotland County Missouri burnt down during the late evening of June 12 or early morning hours of June 13.  Lightning is believed to be the cause of the fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike is believed to have sparked a fire that destroyed the Harmony Grove Baptist Church in rural Scotland County during the late evening of June 12 or early morning of June 13.  The fire was reported around 1:30 am, at which time it was in its later stages of burning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved through eastern Iowa, northeast Missouri, and northern Illinois from June 12 through midday June 13 bringing widespread  heavy rains of 1 to 5 inches (with some areas receiving up to around 10 inches), flash flooding, large hail, damaging wind gusts, and two isolated weak tornadoes to the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building starting a fire around 7:40 pm June 12.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms produced heavy rainfall and caused flash flooding as they moved across central Indiana during the afternoon hours and through the overnight time period.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caught the house on fire.  The house was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable situation set up during the afternoon and evening of the 20th as a frontal boundary and remnants of the outflow boundary was established across southern Iowa.  Temperatures warmed into the low to mid 90s across southern Iowa along and just south of the boundary.  Dewpoint readings soared into the mid 70s to low 80s by evening.  This resulted in very unstable CAPE values in the 5000 to 5500 J/kg range, and lifted indices of -10 to -13 C. during the evening.  A low level jet of 40 kts set up while the atmosphere showed fairly strong shear, in the 40 to 55 kt range.  There wasn't as much deep moisture as had been present in previous days with 1.3 to 1.6 inches of precipitable water.  The freezing level remained quite high at around 14,600 feet and CAPE in the -10 to -30 C. layer of the atmosphere was only 300 to 500 J/kg.  Downdraft CAPE was considerable however with 1000 to 1500 J/kg available.  The LCL was also higher than it had been the previous day and was between 1500 and 2000 meters.  During the evening, thunderstorms formed rapidly over northern Nebraska and far southern South Dakota to the north of the boundary.  By late evening, additional development took place across Iowa.  For the most part, these storms remained just below severe levels.  One of them produced one and one quarter inch diameter hail over central Iowa however.  The main event was the MCC from Nebraska.  The MCC moved into Iowa after midnight and produced high winds and hail as it moved through.  A portion of the system became a Derecho over west central Iowa and advanced across the state during the early morning hours.  Winds of 60 to 75 MPH were common, with a few gusts estimated as high as 100 MPH in central Iowa.  A radio tower was blown over by the winds in the Dawson area of Dallas County.  Tree damage was very extensive from the winds with local utilities reporting as many as 200,000 homes were without power following the passage of the system.  In Jamaica, in Guthrie County, 50 percent of the trees in town were damaged with 30 trees completely down.  The roof was damaged at the race track there.  The Guthrie County mobile EOC was tossed 150 feet into a field and roads were impassible.  In Polk County, in Ankeny, 20 tO 30 Black Locust trees of 1 to 2 feet in diameter were snapped or uprooted near the intersection of 35th street and Highway 415.  Winds estimated at 100 MPH in Dawson, in Dallas County, caused considerable damage.  Roads were blocked by trees, with heavy equipment required to clear them.  LP tanks were leaking in town as they were thrown about and damaged by trees.  The grain elevator in town was also damaged.  Bulldozers were also required to clear streets of tree damage in Boone County at Madrid.  In Polk County, at Mitchellville, the roof was taken off of a modular building at the Mitchellville Correctional Facility.  Lightning struck a house west of Nevada in Story County, setting it on fire.  A second house was struck by lightning in Poweshiek County in Montezuma.  Minor damage was reported to the building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House was set on fire due to lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms produced heavy rainfall and caused flash flooding as they moved across central Indiana during the afternoon hours and through the overnight time period.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church and caught the church on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure in combination with the sea breeze and outflow boundaries from earlier convection, resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Hinesville Fire Department reported a lightning strike caused a house fire on Clay Street in Hinesville, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front helped trigger scattered showers and thunderstorns across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. Because of the hot and humid air mass preceding this front, some of the storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the ensuing fire seriously damaged a farm house on the Sunny High Farm off of Pennsylvania State Route 100 in North Coventry Township. The fire began on the first floor in the front of the house. Flames were through the windows when fire fighters arrived. Five fire companies helped battle the blaze. The family dog died; no additional injuries were reported. Damage was estimated at $300,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lee side trough was a focus for showers and thunderstorms, many becoming severe and producing damaging winds and heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the fire department's radio system.  Backup radio systems were online within 5 minutes of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front helped trigger scattered showers and thunderstorns across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. Because of the hot and humid air mass preceding this front, some of the storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a group of swimmers and killed a 17-year-old male in the water at Gouldsboro State Park in Coolbaugh Township. The 17-year-old male and a 24-year-old male were in the water when lightning struck. Two juvenile female companions were along the shore and were knocked to the ground. The ladies were treated at the scene. The 24-year-old male suffered non life threatening injuries, but was briefly hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very warm and more humid air became established across the region by midday on the 26th. Low pressure was located well north of the area in Ontario, and another trough of low pressure was swinging southeast from Michigan. Showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and continued through late evening. With increased moisture across the region, some of the thunderstorms not only became severe, but also caused some flash flooding across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A married couple was struck by lightning while standing outside of their rural Huron County home.  The husband was temporarily knocked unconscious and sustained burns to his ankle.  His 51 year old wife was also knocked unconscious.  She was taken to a nearby hospital where she died early the next day.  Witnesses stated that it had just quit raining and that the sun had just come out at the time of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of an approaching cold front from the west, and an unseasonably hot, humid and unstable air mass in place, led to the development of numerous strong to severe thunderstorms during Tuesday afternoon and evening across eastern New York and adjacent western New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A stucture reportedly caught fire from a lightning strike near Mindenville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a cold front approaching from the west, and a warm and very moist air mass in place, led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across the mid Hudson Valley of eastern New York during the afternoon hours of Saturday June 14th. Some of the thunderstorms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three hikers and a baby were slightly injured by a nearby lightning strike while sitting on a bench at the Mohonk Mountain House near New Paltz. The group were walking on a trail when the thunderstorm started. They then took cover and sat on a bench when lightning struck nearby. Their feet were in water, exacerbating the impact of the nearby lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rain caused dangerous flash flooding and flooding across many locations in central Indiana.  A weak tornado also touched down in Greene County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire, believed to be started by lightning striking a tree parallel to the garage of a house on Westchester Boulevard in Noblesville, was not discovered until hours after initiation. The lightning likely reached the house via a utility line. Fire fighters were called around 5 AM EST by a passerby. Flames were still visible as late as 7 AM EST.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rain caused dangerous flash flooding and flooding across many locations in central Indiana.  A weak tornado also touched down in Greene County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Homeowners of a residence on Montgomery Drive heard thunder, the lights went out, and their living room curtains were ignited. They were able to extinguish the fire using a garden hose from the backyard. Damage was limited to a curtain and a small area of carpeting.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lighting from a nearby thunderstorm struck two children in Douglas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two children were struck by lightning in Douglas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lee side trough was a focus for showers and thunderstorms, many becoming severe and producing damaging winds and heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Marlborough Street, resulting in a power surge that blew several light switches off the wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lee side trough was a focus for showers and thunderstorms, many becoming severe and producing damaging winds and heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Grogan Road, causing a fire that resulted in damage to a large bedroom, as well as knocking out the electricity and phone service to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated pulse severe thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and moved southward.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house suffered considerable damage after a lightning strike sparked a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Officials believe a lightning strike is to blame for a fire which did an estimated $50,000 damage to a south-side Kokomo residence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Officials believe a lightning strike is to blame for a fire which did an estimated $50,000 damage to a south-side Kokomo residence on Springmill Drive. The resident stated lightning hit his attic and when he checked it it was full of smoke. Crews stayed on scene for almost three hours. The house was left in uninhabitable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms moved through southern New Hampshire.  Numerous lightning strikes were observed with these storms, including one that caused damage to a home in Marlborough.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house in Marlborough was struck by lightning.  It resulted in a three foot diameter hole through the wall of the house, melting some wires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck equipment or trees that damaged power lines when they fell.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a fire on South Third Street in Lafayette and reports of other possible strikes were received by fire department dispatch personnel. Power outages occurred around the city with a peak of about 1,500 powerless customers county-wide.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front provided a focus for severe thunderstorms.  These thunderstorms produced very heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding, hail, and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a structure in Camp Squanto, a boy scout camp on the edge of Myles Standish State Forest.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front and low pressure system over northern Kansas lifted northeast into southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa as an unseasonably strong upper level low pressure system lifted from the Rockies into the northern plains.  Severe storms developed over northeast Nebraska during the morning hours of June 5th and after a brief break in the severe weather, additional severe storms developed over southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa by early evening.  The thunderstorms formed into a bow echo as they moved into southwest Iowa and a bookend type vortex on the north end of the bow echo spun up 2 brief tornadoes with another tornado forming on the bow a bit farther east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning apparently struck a house causing a fire that totally destroyed it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated pulse severe thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and moved southward.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on the west side of Houston was damaged by a lightning strike. Fire was contained to the attic area, but smoke and water damage filled the two story home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated pulse severe thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and moved southward.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home suffered some chimney damage from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front helped trigger scattered showers and thunderstorns across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. Because of the hot and humid air mass preceding this front, some of the storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike knocked out power at the Mount Airy Lodge Casino Resort for fourteen hours starting the evening of the 14th. About 800 guests were evacuated from the gaming floor. Some room guests were also evacuated. The casino reopened at Noon EDT on the 15th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southern-based thunderstorms produced a funnel cloud and a far inland lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree in the front yard of a residential home that ultimately generated a fire in the home's garage attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous early afternoon thunderstorms created severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a residential fire that engulfed a majority of the home's roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous early afternoon thunderstorms created severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man on a bicycle suffered very minor injuries when struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front provided a focus for severe thunderstorms.  These thunderstorms produced very heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding, hail, and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure in the lee of the Appalachians in combination with the sea breeze in a highly unstable environment, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across southern South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught on fire in the Wild Dunes Subdivision from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front extending east to west across the Upper Mississippi River Valley was the focus for a significant severe weather event on June 7. Showers and storms redeveloped during the day in the vicinity of the warm front, while a line of storms developed out ahead of the cold front, with these tracking across the region Sunday night. The severe weather activity, aside from heavy rain, was not as widespread compared to Saturday, June 7.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very active severe weather event impacted the South Plains of west Texas during the late afternoon and evening of the 19th. Isolated thunderstorms initially developed along a pre-existing outflow boundary from the central Texas Panhandle southeastward over the northern Rolling Plains. These storms produced large hail, damaging winds, and at least one tornado in northern Cottle County. ||Thunderstorms rapidly became widespread over the South Plains during the evening hours. Many of the storms were severe with large hail up to the size of golf balls and damaging winds in excess of 70 mph. Damage was largely limited to utility poles, lines, and trees. Losses due to agricultural damages, however, were estimated to exceed $1.1 million.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Extremely frequent and vivid cloud-to-ground lightning activity accompanied a severe thunderstorm over the Lubbock vicinity during the late evening of the 19th. The lightning sparked a fire that damaged a home near the intersection of County Road 7610 and south University Avenue around 22:15 CST. By 22:30 CST, a local utility provider reported that approximately 15,000 households across the city were affected by lightning-induced power outages.

This combined with the usual July heat and humidity allowed for pulse thunderstorms to develop as usual. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This episode was the 2nd round of severe storms over southern Wisconsin on July 7th.  A line of storms moved west to east across southern Wisconsin during the evening hours.  Powerful thunderstorm downburst winds were generated which knocked down trees and power-lines that left about 23,000 customers without electrical power.  Additionally, one isolated tornado spun up on the leading edge of the line of storms in southern Green Lake County, where a microburst pushed ahead and enhanced local vorticiy/rotation in a storm cell.  The storms were associated with a short-wave trough at 500 MB moving east through Wisconsin, with a 30 knot low-level jet at 850 MB.  Surface temperatures were in the 80s and surface dewpoints werer around 70.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: LIghting struck and injured a 16-year boy.  He was transfered to  a hospital for medical treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A convective thunderstorm complex that orginated over southern Minnesota moved east/southeast across southern Wisconsin and generated a line of strong to severe storms.  Powerful thunderstorm winds gusting to hurricane-force, large hail, one tornado, and flash flooding were produced by the storms.  Surface dewpoints were in the lower to mid 70s, and CAPE values were 3000 to 4000.  Maximum afternoon temperatures were in the 85 to 90 range.  At least 20,000 customers lost electrical power - 14,000 of them in Sheboygan County alone.

With cold temperatures aloft, hail was the main threat experienced.  However, thunderstorm winds and heavy rainfall also produced some damage and complications, with portions of a few roads closed due to fallen trees or flooding.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front slowly approaching from New York State helped trigger some severe thunderstorms during the evening of the 20th in Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn caught fire after a lightning strike on Devyn Drive in West Pikeland Township. The fire was contained to the barn and two nearby homes were undamaged. The historic barn though was a total loss. Six fire companies assisted in battling the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early- to mid-evening hours, the Storm Prediction Center upgraded central, and much of southern, Indiana to a moderate risk for severe weather and issued a severe thunderstorm watch for the area effective until 3 AM EST. The atmosphere was extremely unstable and the growth of any developing storms was unimpeded. A roughly west to east frontal boundary stretched from southern Nebraska to central Indiana. Dewpoints in the lower 70s F were in place along the front, contributing to strong instability. A strong shortwave trough skirted the area, enhancing coverage of storms. Winds were expected to be the primary threat, and this is what indeed ending up being the main problem in central Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused significant damage to most of the second floor of a large home while water damage was throughout the home. Time of occurrence and damage cost are rough estimates.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold frontal passage triggered severe thunderstorms across New Jersey on the afternoon of the 27th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an electrical fire to a house on Spray Avenue in Atlantic City. The lightning struck a metal chain under the house. The metal provided on conduit to the home's electrical box.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front moved through southern New England and produced a long line of showers and thunderstorms that tracked east across the area.  Much of this line of storms was severe with damaging thunderstorm winds and occasional hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, igniting a gas line, and starting a fire.  The lightning strike also hit a water line coming into the house, which flooded the basement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced large hail, damaging winds, a brief tornado, and flash flooding in northwest Iowa from Sioux City to Storm Lake during the late afternoon and early evening of July 6th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a car, slightly injuring the two occupants, and damaging the car's engine and electrical system.

Due to a moist atmosphere, heavy rains were reported overnight in the range of 1 inch to slightly over 4 inches. Due to a saturated ground, flash flooding was the result.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and started a fire that resulted in roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over Logan and Washington Counties.  The storms produced wind gusts to 60 mph and large hail, up to the size of quarters.  In Aurora, an unoccupied home was struck by lightning causing extensive roof damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home.  The ensuing fire caused extensive roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal system moved through southern New England with the warm front moving through first and increasing low level moisture.  Then the cold front moved through providing a lifting mechanism for showers and thunderstorms to develop.  High levels of moisture contributed to heavy downpours that resulted in flash flooding in Rhode Island and portions of Massachusetts.  All of this coupled with strong wind shear (turning of the winds with height) over southeast Massachusetts and Rhode Island provided the perfect environment for a tornado to form.  ||This particular tornado began as a waterspout over Narragansett Bay and traveled east-northeast reaching land over the southern portion of Warren, Rhode Island.  The tornado continued for 4.2 miles into Swansea, Massachusetts over a mostly continuous track.  Most of the damage sustained was to trees which fell on power lines and houses.  This tornado was rated by a National Weather Service damage survey team as an EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front that ended a week long heat wave also triggered severe thunderstorms across New Jersey during the afternoon and early evening on the 23rd. A power outage caused significant delays and over a one hour shut down (from 430 p.m. EDT until 545 p.m. EDT) of Amtrak train service between Philadelphia and Boston. These outages extended to New Jersey Transit Trains on the Northeast Corridor, North Jersey Shore Line and Midtown Direct Line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: For the second time in one month, the Middlesex Borough Hall was struck by lightning. The first lightning strike on July 11th knocked out communications with other townships for less than an hour. The lightning strike on the 23rd caused phone and internet service to be not available through the afternoon of the 24th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed in a moist and unstable airmass as an upper level disturbance moved across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire that damaged a storage room in a building at Nicholls State University.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed and moved across parts of central Illinois during the early morning hours of 7/7/08.  Locally heavy rainfall of between 2 and 4 inches was observed in a few locations, particularly across DeWitt and Piatt counties. Two thunderstorms, one near Peoria and the other in southern Champaign County produced lightning strikes which caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex near Bradley University setting fire to a third floor apartment ceiling, the attic and the roof. There were no injuries.

Smoke filled the dispatch center at the police headquarters. Equipment was damaged, but no other injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front that ended a week long heat wave also triggered severe thunderstorms across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and early evening on the 23rd. The majority of the wind and lightning damage occurred in southeastern Pennsylvania where PECO Energy reported about 35,000 homes and businesses lost power. A power outage caused significant delays and over a one hour shut down (from 430 p.m. EDT through 545 p.m. EDT) of Amtrak train service between Philadelphia and Boston. Five SEPTA Regional Rail Lines were also affected by the outage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 21-year-old woman and a 3-year-old boy were struck and injured by lightning at the Brookside Swim and Tennis Club in Lower Makefield Township. They were running for shelter and passed under a 50-foot-tall evergreen tree when it was struck by lightning. The lightning traveled down the tree to the ground where it struck the woman. The lightning traveled up her body and exited out her arm to the boy. She suffered a first degree burn from a chain around her neck. The boy had an entrance and exit mark from the lightning and also injured his arm where we was holding onto her neck. The boy never lost consciousness, but the lady went into convulsions and lost consciousness. Both were hospitalized and survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two lines of thunderstorms moved across the Ohio River into central Kentucky on the afternoon and evening of July 8th bringing damaging winds and small hail to the area. Lightning also caused a house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a large house fire in the Lake Forest area.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: An outbuilding received damage due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northwesterly wind flow aloft sent storms into Arkansas on the 22nd.  The approach of a cold front and the hot, humid conditions over the state contributed to the severity of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set the woods on fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire on a young pine plantation off Round Hill Road. Approximately 100 acres burned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure south of the area kept west to southwest winds in place. Deep moisture also in place allowed for numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms to move over the area from the Gulf of Mexico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the garage of a house on North Rehrer Road and started a fire that destroyed the entire house and two cars.

The swath of damage continued into northwestern Indiana where winds of 60 to 80 mph caused several areas of tree damage and some structure damage. One person lost their life when a tree limb fell onto their car in Laporte County.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male was getting out of his boat to take shelter from an approaching thunderstorm when he was hit by lightning.  He was taken to a local hospital and died from his lightning strike injuries a week later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours of 7/21/08, thunderstorms quickly began to develop across Iowa in response to a 30 to 35kt low-level jet and an upper-level disturbance tracking eastward out of the Plains. As they rolled eastward, they began to pick up momentum and soon began producing widespread damaging winds. The storms headed east-southeast into Knox, Fulton, and Peoria counties, where winds between 60 and 70 mph downed numerous trees and powerlines.  Widespread wind damage continued further east in a large swath across Marshall, Woodford, Tazewell, and northern McLean counties where severe winds of 60 to 81 mph were reported. Firefighters rescued 20 people as water quickly rose along creeks, flooded roadways, and stranded motorists.  Three people had to be rescued along Cherry Creek when the bike path flooded. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rare and widespread significant wind event impacted the NWS Jackson, MS forecast area during the evening of Aug 2nd and lasted into the early morning hours of Aug 3rd. Several clusters of storms developed across Northern Mississippi and Northern Alabama during the late afternoon and became further organized as the clusters moved to the south and southwest. Between 8 and 9 pm, a bowing line of storms was located from Oxford to Starkville, growing larger by the minute, and picking up speed as wind gusts between 50 and 70 mph were taking shape.||A large bow echo quickly evolved and raced to the west-southwest, across Mississippi, through the evening at 50 to 60 mph. The line of storms produced widespread severe wind gusts around 60 mph with many locations seeing significant wind gusts between 75 and 80 mph. Tree and power line damage was widespread and significant along the line with the focus and most intense portion of the bow echo located within an axis from Louisville, MS to Jackson, MS to St. Joseph, LA.||Some of the most significant wind damage occurred across Winston, Neshoba, Leake and Scott counties. Here, thousands of trees were downed along with numerous power lines. Many roads were blocked by downed trees, especially across Scott County. Wind gusts across these areas likely peaked between 75 and 85 mph.||The bow echo was re-energized across Madison and Hinds Counties as the line clashed with pre-line storms. The most intense portion of the bow echo was re-focused as it impacted portions of southern Madison and Hinds County. The most intense portion of the line then dove southwest and impacted Copiah, Claiborne, Jefferson, Franklin and Adams Counties. As the line crossed the Mississippi River, the parishes of Tensas and Concordia saw the brunt of the damaging winds. Similar to areas across Central Mississippi, these locations received significant winds between 75 and 85 mph. Thousands of trees and numerous power lines were downed from the winds. Power outages were substantial as many locations were without power for 2 to 4 days.||Looking at this event in a historic perspective, it was likely the most significant and widespread wind event ever in August for our forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low tracked across southern Ontario producing showers and thunderstorms across southern New England.  These storms produced a waterspout and very heavy rains resulting in flash flooding in southeastern Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Laurelcrest Drive was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm, just ahead of an advancing warm front, resulted in wind damage in Westchester County during the morning of the 6th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building on Main Street, causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Florida Highway Patrol trooper was struck by lightning while investigating a crash on interstate 95.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Around 5:30 PM a trooper from the Florida Highway Patrol was investigating a crash on interstate 95 in Palm Beach County when he was struck by lightning. The trooper was able to radio for help and was taken to Bethesda Memorial Hospital along with two other people who were involved in the crash. All three people injured by the strike were later released by the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper trough was located along the east coast of the U.S. and trailed southwestward into central Georgia.  A surface trough was located across central and south Georgia.  The remnants of Hurricane Dolly had been pushed south into central and south Georgia ahead of the trough.  Ample moisture combined with active northwest flow aloft and the surface boundary to allow scattered strong thunderstorms to develop during the late afternoon and evening hours across central and south Georgia.  Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning was observed in these storms, but none reached severe limits.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Telfair County 911 Center reported that lightning ignited a structural fire.  No specific information was provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unstable atmosphere and plenty of sunshine led to widespread severe weather across Southern New England.  Cold upper level temperatures allowed large hail to form and form it did with one report of two inch diameter hail in Marlborough, Massachusetts.  There was heavy rain associated with some of the storms as well which resulted in some urban flooding and some flash flooding in Worcester, Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage on Menthuen Street resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a communications tower in Adel on the 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a communications tower in Adel and burned some components.  The damage caused 200 customers to lose Internet service.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong for August upper air disturbance helped trigger numerous strong to severe thunderstorms across New Jersey. Severe thunderstorms started developing along the warm front in the morning and continued through the afternoon and into the evening until a cold front moved through the state.  ||The large hail storms that occurred contributed to the United States Secretary of Agriculture Edward Schafer declaring ten central and southern New Jersey Counties a natural disaster on September 22nd. Mercer, Monmouth, Burlington, Ocean, Camden, Gloucester, Atlantic, Salem, Cumberland and Cape May Counties were included in the declaration.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A two-and-a-half story barn burned to the ground after being struck by lightning on Pond Lane in Milford.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance, coupled with a passing trough of low pressure at the surface, produced several severe thunderstorms across Southwestern Connecticut, including a microburst near Stratford in Fairfield County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a tree behind the home at 316 Funston Avenue, with the current transferring through its roots, creating a hole in the basement wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong for August upper air disturbance helped trigger numerous strong to severe thunderstorms across New Jersey. Severe thunderstorms started developing along the warm front in the morning and continued through the afternoon and into the evening until a cold front moved through the state.  ||The large hail storms that occurred contributed to the United States Secretary of Agriculture Edward Schafer declaring ten central and southern New Jersey Counties a natural disaster on September 22nd. Mercer, Monmouth, Burlington, Ocean, Camden, Gloucester, Atlantic, Salem, Cumberland and Cape May Counties were included in the declaration.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike struck and damaged an outbuilding on Quilleytown Road in Carneys Point Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low pressure system spawned severe thunderstorms over Middlesex and New London Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Seaside Avenue in Westbrook igniting a small fire, and destroying the chimney.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved through northern Oklahoma during the morning and early afternoon, with several outflow boundaries behind the front. Thunderstorms developed by mid afternoon and continued through the early part of the evening along these boundaries, with several briefly becoming severe. Weak winds aloft and marginal instability allowed for more pulse type storms, with heavy rain and strong winds the main impacts. Some hail was reported as well, but these reports were few and far between. Some damage was reported with the winds, especially in the Oklahoma City metro area. Monetary damages were estimated.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank battery two miles north of Blackwell. An oil tank with 80 barrels of oil exploded as a result. No other damage was reported to the other tanks. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged part of the roof of the Dexter library and damaged most of the computers and radios at the fire station.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong for August upper air disturbance helped trigger numerous strong to severe thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania. Severe thunderstorms started developing along the warm front in the morning and continued through the afternoon and into the evening until a cold front moved through the eastern part of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike amd ensuing fire damaged a townhouse on Rosemont Terrace in Upper Hanover Township. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deepening upper level trough over the southeast region lifted a deep plume of tropical moisture over the forecast area. A strong low level 850 mb jet of 50-55 knots was in place. Backing winds advected instability inland from the Gulf of Mexico across north Florida which coincided with the passing of a second pre-frontal squall line as it tracked across north Florida and Southeast Georgia in the afternoon. Low level storm relative helicities increased to 200-350 M2/S2. Widespread severe storms developed across the forecast area during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer at the corner of Atlantic and Monument Roads. The power lines caught fire and feel onto a car stopped at the traffic light. Two men rescued the driver of the car that was burning. A local gas station had to shut down their pumps due to the lightning fire. The victim did not suffer critical injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wave of low pressure moving along a stationary front located over the Tri-State triggered some severe thunderstorms across Southwestern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on 4th Avenue, causing a small roof fire, damaging the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wave of low pressure moving along a stationary front located over the Tri-State triggered some severe thunderstorms across Southwestern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the garage of a home on the 200 block of Drum Hill Road. The entire garage and all of its contents, including a car, were destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low pressure system spawned numerous severe thunderstorms over the Lower Hudson Valley, New York City Metro, and Long Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 19th century barn on Burdick Road in Milltown, destroying the barn and an antique truck in the barn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon of August 15th a few isolated severe thunderstorms developed along the piedmont trough resulting in wind damage and several home fires from lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes struck by lightning in the Raleigh caught fire resulting in extensive damage to each home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching secondary cold front helped trigger thunderstorms in southeast Pennsylvania on the evening of the 7th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes caused power outages and an apartment fire in eastern Montgomery County. In Montgomery Township, a lightning strike caused an apartment fire at the Avenel Apartments. The fire forced the evacuation of twenty-two apartments in the complex. The fire was contained to the kitchen area of a third floor apartment. Another lightning strike caused about 17,500 PECO Energy homes and businesses to lose power in Montgomery County. Lightning struck the North Wales substation on Sumneytown Road and tripped circuit breakers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low pressure system spawned isolated severe thunderstorms over Northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the house at 102 Sheridan Avenue in Clifton, collapsing the chimney.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low pressure system spawned isolated severe thunderstorms over Northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the house at 484 South Parkway in Clifton, causing the roof to catch on fire, and be destroyed, and caused some damage to the second story of the house as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low pressure system spawned isolated severe thunderstorms over Northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home just southeast of River Edge on Warwick Avenue, destroying the chimney and damaging a near by tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong upper trough was sweeping through the Great Lakes and Northeast from the 2nd into the 3rd of August.  This was pushing an equally unusually strong cold front for early August into the southeast U.S.  This front combined with a very warm humid air mass, partially a result of the lingering remnants of Hurricane Dolly, to result in the development of numerous strong to severe thunderstorms in far north Georgia during the mid to late afternoon hours.  Thunderstorms across north Georgia merged into a near solid arched band of thunderstorms which raced southward during the evening hours into the Atlanta metropolitan area.  Large hail and intense cloud-to-ground lightning accompanied the thunderstorms in north Georgia.  Leading outflow winds produced a wind gust of 71 mph at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport as the thunderstorms came through around 730 pm EDT.  The thunderstorms subsequently diminished as they pushed further south of the Atlanta area, but redeveloped once again into strong to severe thunderstorms during the late evening as the outflow boundary pushed into the Macon area and nearby counties.  Numerous reports of downed trees were received from many north and central Georgia counties as a result of these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that an individual was struck by lightning seven miles southwest of Canton and sustained non life-threatening injuries.  In addition, two homes in the southwest and southern part of the county were struck by lightning and set on fire,  One of the homes was in the Towne Lake Subdivision on Players Court and was totally destroyed.  The Cherokee Tribune reported that up to 134 homes in the area sustained at least minor damage from wind and/or lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front that ended a week long heat wave also triggered severe thunderstorms across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and early evening on the 23rd. The majority of the wind and lightning damage occurred in southeastern Pennsylvania where PECO Energy reported about 35,000 homes and businesses lost power. A power outage caused significant delays and over a one hour shut down (from 430 p.m. EDT through 545 p.m. EDT) of Amtrak train service between Philadelphia and Boston. Five SEPTA Regional Rail Lines were also affected by the outage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Bethel Township police officer and a firefighter were struck and injured by lightning at the Bethel Township fire house on Foulk Road. Lightning struck the building and moved down along its frame. The 22-year-old male officer was standing in the open garage area when he was tossed by the lightning and knocked unconscious. The female firefighter was sitting on the bumper of a fire truck when she was struck. She suffered tingling sensations. Both were hospitalized for observations and released on the 24th. The lightning strike itself damaged the garage door opener, telephone and electronics systems in the fire house.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning struck started a fire at a home on Alden Avenue in Lower Makefield Township. Firefighters quickly extinguished the blaze and rescued the family dog.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few showers and thunderstorms moved into southern New England early Sunday morning from eastern New York. They moved into a more stable atmosphere upon reaching New England, which limited the amount of severe weather that occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house at the intersection of Cabot and Appleton was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A bowing line of severe thunderstorms, known as a Derecho, raced across Iowa and Illinois during the early morning hours of July 21 producing|widespread wind damage in about a 60 mile wide swath just south of Interstate 80.  Winds gusting over 70 miles an hour toppled trees, ripped siding and shingles off homes and businesses, and left much of the region without power.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Delaware County Courthouse at 418 am July 21 damaging the roof, security camera system, elevator, telephone system, and wireless connection to the engineer's office.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced lightning that stuck a man that was working on a fence about 5 miles west of Flagstaff.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was working on a fence when lightning hit nearby or hit the fence. The jolt knocked the man away and ripped the glove off his hand. He had numbness and tingling in his arm. He was transported to the hospital for observation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a fire that burned down a house in Newington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred along and ahead of a cold front as it moved east across Missouri. One of the storms produced a lightning strike that damaged a building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an ambulance building in Mount Vernon. The lightning struck the radio communications tower, then travelled down cables to the building. A small fire was started where electrical lines entered the building. Damage to the building was very minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal system moved through southern New England with the warm front moving through first and increasing low level moisture.  Then the cold front moved through providing a lifting mechanism for showers and thunderstorms to develop.  High levels of moisture contributed to heavy downpours that resulted in flash flooding in Rhode Island and portions of Massachusetts.  All of this coupled with strong wind shear (turning of the winds with height) over southeast Massachusetts and Rhode Island provided the perfect environment for a tornado to form.  ||This particular tornado began as a waterspout over Narragansett Bay and traveled east-northeast reaching land over the southern portion of Warren, Rhode Island.  The tornado continued for 4.2 miles into Swansea, Massachusetts over a mostly continuous track.  Most of the damage sustained was to trees which fell on power lines and houses.  This tornado was rated by a National Weather Service damage survey team as an EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Ephraims Way was struck by lihgtning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching upper level storm triggered numerous showers and thunderstorms across the Tri-State Region. The area was in the warm sector of the surface reflection, with the synoptic cold front to the west and warm front across northern New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree was downed by lightning on Morris Avenue. This tree was reported to have covered the road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With a stationary front parked south of Long Island, an unstable airmass produced thunderstorms in the New York City metropolitan area. Lightning struck a building in Bay Ridge and caused structural damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A four story brick residence was struck by lightning, causing damage to portions of the roof. A two by three foot section of the brick roof was dislodged and fell to the street and sidewalk below. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in two injuries on a golf course.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at a golf course injured two teenage boys.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm frontal boundary across Central Minnesota provided the support for scattered to numerous severe thunderstorms across the region on this date.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Man struck and injured by lightning while accomplishing construction work on the roof of a home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: While the upper low to the northeast of Georgia, across the mid-Atlantic was weakening, a weak upper trough lingered across this region.  This combined with typical July heat and humidity was more than adequate for another afternoon of significant pulse thunderstorms, several of which became severe.  The activity lingered into the early morning hours of the 9th.  There was even one fatality in Banks county in northeast Georgia when a tree fell on a house.  The slow movement and clustering of thunderstorms across north central Georgia in Forsyth, Dawson, and Lumpkin counties prompted flash flood warnings.  A minor flash flood event was observed in Dawson county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Forsyth County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning strikes at several locations caused electrical transformers to blow and resulted in damage to audio equipment at several homes.  However, no structural fires were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front that ended a week long heat wave also triggered severe thunderstorms across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and early evening on the 23rd. The majority of the wind and lightning damage occurred in southeastern Pennsylvania where PECO Energy reported about 35,000 homes and businesses lost power. A power outage caused significant delays and over a one hour shut down (from 430 p.m. EDT through 545 p.m. EDT) of Amtrak train service between Philadelphia and Boston. Five SEPTA Regional Rail Lines were also affected by the outage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire at a Bed, Bath and Beyond store in Upper Merion Township. Lightning struck the roof and made a hole the size of a penny. It penetrated the right front area of the store's displays. The lightning set stacks of towels and other merchandise on fire. The store was evacuated. Eight fire companies battled the blaze and it was contained in a small area of the store. It was declared under control at 7 p.m. EDT. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold frontal passage triggered severe thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania on the afternoon of the 27th. The combination of lightning and damaging winds caused about 62,000 homes and businesses to lose power. Most of the outages (about 49,000) were in PECO Energy's service area in southeast Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman suffered a minor injury when she was shocked by an direct lightning strike in Montgomery Township. She was apparently on a laptop computer when lightning struck nearby. She was shicked, but not seriously injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure was ridging across northern Florida keeping east to southeast winds in place across the local area. An afternoon sea breeze developed and combined with the east coast sea breeze to form several severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging winds around the Tampa Bay area in the early evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building on the 6300 block of South Mac Dill Avenue and started a fire which heavily damaged two units. Water used to put out the fire damaged another two units.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold frontal passage triggered severe thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania on the afternoon of the 27th. The combination of lightning and damaging winds caused about 62,000 homes and businesses to lose power. Most of the outages (about 49,000) were in PECO Energy's service area in southeast Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A series of lightning strikes caused a couple of house fires and other damage across central Bucks County. One firefighter was treated for heat exhaustion. In Hilltown, a home on Paige Trail was struck by lightning on its roof. Smoke spewed from the garage section of the home. Firefighters removed a three foot by three foot section of the roof to help battle the blaze. Five fire companies assisted. The fire was contained to the attic and the second floor master bedroom of the house. In Solebury Township, the chimney of a house on Brighton Way was struck by lightning. The lightning traveled down into the basement where a fire was ignited. Four fire companies battled the blaze for two and a half hours. The fire was contained to one area of the house, but caused heavy smoke damage throughout. The house was expected to be uninhabitable for a few days. Also in Solebury Township, a lightning strike caused a transformer fire. In Warrington Township, another lightning strike damaged a home's chimney. In New Britain Township, lightning struck a PECO Energy substation. U.S. Route 202 was closed as firefighters battled the blaze. One firefighter was treated for heat exhaustion. The combination of damaging winds and lightning strikes caused about 30,000 homes and businesses to lose power in Bucks and Montgomery Counties.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck near a group of eight hikers at Rocky Mountain National Park.  Three of those hikers suffered minor injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe storms affected the Upstate and Northwest Piedmont of South Carolina during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large house on Anchorage Lane, igniting a fire that destroyed much of the roof and the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed mainly over the northern portion of the region and produced scattered wind damage and some hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole in Columbus.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front that ended a week long heat wave also triggered severe thunderstorms across Delaware during the afternoon and early evening on the 23rd. The thunderstorms caused outages to about 9,000 homes and businesses in New Castle County. There were still 6,000 homes and businesses without power at 11 p.m. EDT.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire in the Tenby Chase Development off of Baltimore Road in Hockessin. When firefighters arrived, they saw smoke billowing from the roof. Two people in the home escaped. It was under control within 20 minutes and the fire was contained to the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: There were a few thunderstorms across northeast Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 4th. Lightning from one of them struck a house and caused a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a house fire. The fire burned the attic while the remainder of the house had smoke and water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving frontal boundary pushed east across northern Alabama on October 8th, 2008. Strong southerly winds from the Gulf of Mexico ahead of the front allowed dewpoints to climb to near 65 degrees.  This abundant moisture combined with potent lift (enhanced by a strong wave of low pressure developing along the front) and produced very heavy rainfall and flash flooding in portions of Marshall and Madison counties in northern Alabama.  A few isolated severe storms produced straight lined wind damage as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Huntsville utilities reported that lightning caused a power outage in northeast Huntsville affecting 2000 customers. The outage occurred for about 2 hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure moved over Southeast Georgia allowing scattered strong to severe convection to form in the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported that a top of a tree fell on three power lines due to a lightning strike near the intersection of highway 30 and Keller Road. The power lines fell on the road causing a temporary closing of highway 30 two miles west of Port Wentworth, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shed was hit by lightning in the town of Lynn on November 5, with the shed sustaining damage from the ensuing fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A shed caught fire after it was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a couple of homes near Pensacola.  One of the strikes injured a male.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and knocked it down.  A male, in his middle 70s, was standing near the tree and the strike knocked him down.  He was taken to a local hospital, treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure crossed into west central Minnesota, helping to fuel scattered thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man driving to work in Detroit Lakes on U.S. Highway 10 was struck by lightning. The strike left marks on the vehicle, but the man was not injured. A rear tire was also blown out and the car's generator was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful line of thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the evening hours of August 4th.  Widespread and significant wind damage was reported along with several brief tornadoes on the leading edge of this line of storms.  Close to 550,000 customers lost power during these thunderstorms.  In the City of Chicago, more than 4,400 trees suffered some amount of damage, 161 light poles were damaged and 252 power lines were blown down.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Prairie Street, sparking a fire in the kitchen.  Damage was limited to the stove, a wall, cabinet and a window.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped develop a squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through New Jersey during the morning and early afternoon of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Ocean City MUA pumping station.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large upper level low moved through the Texas panhandle and triggered several rounds of thunderstorms over north Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building as a line of thunderstorms moved through Eastland.  A 3-foot tall concrete staute on a roof was struck by lightning and fell onto a lower part of the building causing more damage.  The debris landed on Main Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the morning hours of August 4th.  Several houses were struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree on N. Ridgeland Avenue, then jumped to electrical wires and into a house.  Several electrical appliances were destroyed and a fire was started in the basement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An advancing cold front, pushing down from the north, helped set off  thunderstorms across Central Alabama, some of which became quite strong.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was struck by lightning on Tabor Cut-off Road, near Noccalula Falls.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped develop a squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through New Jersey during the morning and early afternoon of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing power outage caused school children to be dismissed early from the Voorhees High School on Fairview Avenue in High Bridge Borough. Additional lightning strikes caused about 800 homes and businesses to lose power in neighboring Lebanon Township. All power was restored by 1 p.m. EDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped develop a squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through New Jersey during the morning and early afternoon of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck the chapel's steeple at the Grace Fellowship Church in Bedminster. Sparks and a small piece or two of wood fell to the ground. While smoke spewed from the steeple, damage was limited to a few scorched and broken boards and the building's amplification system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After a nearly week long lull from the daily summer convective activity, scattered thunderstorms, a few severe, developed across the area again.  A weak front, that drifted into the state during the previous weekend, had stalled about halfway across the state.  The front combined with moisture from the extreme outer circulation of hurricane Ike, located near Cuba, and potentially left over residual moisture that drifted over the area from the remnants of hurricane Gustav, provided a favorable environment for scattered thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon and evening hours.  Several of the storms became marginally severe and produced damaging winds.  One storm produced large hail.  Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning was also observed and there were several lightning-related house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Bartow County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a home on Colonial Club Drive and started a fire.  Specific damages were not provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front was approaching north Georgia as a weak upper-level trough skirted across the northern portion of the state.  This combined with residual tropical moisture and daytime heating resulted in scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms, especially in north Georgia.  While none of the thunderstorms became severe, they produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  Lightning struck at least two homes in Bartow county causing minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Daily Tribune of Cartersville reported that lightning struck homes on homes on Vigilant Street and Harris street in Atco.  Damage was minimal in both incidents.
