EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pickens County Progress reported that lightning struck two homes west of Jasper.  A home on Hobson Drive was struck and set on fire causing considerable electrical and smoke damage to the home.  However, the house was apparently not destroyed.  Another home in the 3600 block of Georgia Highway 53 was also struck and set on fire by lightning.  The home was completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front remained across central Georgia as hurricane Ike continued to churn west through the central Gulf of Mexico.  The large scale circulation around Ike continued to bring Atlantic moisture into Georgia.  This combined with the front to produce scattered to numerous afternoon thunderstorms across central Georgia.  Little to no activity occurred in north Georgia.  While none of the thunderstorms were observed to be severe, frequent cloud-to-ground lightning occurred causing several injuries at a football game in Houston county, just south of Macon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Macon Telegraph reported that 12 people, nine adults and three teenagers, were injured when lightning struck a goal post on the football field at Bonaire Middle School during a Thursday evening football game.  The athletic director from the opposing school, Warner Robins, was left in critical condition and transferred to a burn center along with three of the other adults.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped develop a squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through Delaware during the afternoon of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused two-thirds of Dover to lose power for about 90 minutes during the afternoon of the 9th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped develop a squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through New Jersey during the morning and early afternoon of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a two alarm fire at a Kirklin Avenue home in Linwood. The fire began in the electircal system in the house's kitchen. More than forty fire fighters from four municipalities battled the blaze. U.S. Route 9 was closed for 45 minutes. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms over metro Miami-Dade County on September 15th led to lightning striking a construction crane in western Miami-Dade County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a construction crane in western Miami-Dade County while 2 workers were on board.  Both workers were taken to the hospital after the bolt travel down the metal crane and were in good condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface high pressure remained in place across southern Florida with west to southwest winds aloft. Afternoon sea breezes developed each day and thunderstorms formed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries. On June 23, one person was killed and 2 people were injured by lightning while seeking refuge under a tree in DeSoto County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 28 year old man was struck and injured by lightning while wade fishing in the Gulf off of Siesta Key.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface high pressure remained in place across southern Florida with west to southwest winds aloft. Afternoon sea breezes developed each day and thunderstorms formed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries. On June 23, one person was killed and 2 people were injured by lightning while seeking refuge under a tree in DeSoto County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At 4:30 p.m. EDT on June 23, 2008, Employee #1 was working at a ranch, clipping dead limbs off of a palm tree, when a heavy rain and lightning approached. Employee #1 and two coworkers sought refuge under a large 30-ft oak tree. While under the tree, Employee #1 leaned up against the tree. When lightning struck the tree, Employee #1 sustained burns to his hands and feet and was killed. Both coworkers were airlifted to Tampa General Hospital in Tampa, Florida.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface high pressure remained in place across southern Florida with west to southwest winds aloft. Afternoon sea breezes developed each day and thunderstorms formed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries. On June 23, one person was killed and 2 people were injured by lightning while seeking refuge under a tree in DeSoto County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged the top of a chimney on a home in the Grasslands Golf and Country Club.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface high pressure remained in place across southern Florida with west to southwest winds aloft. Afternoon sea breezes developed each day and thunderstorms formed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male was struck and injured by lightning in Chiefland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface high pressure remained in place across southern Florida with west to southwest winds aloft. Afternoon sea breezes developed each day and thunderstorms formed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a 10 to 15 acre brush fire near Tropical Lane and W Miss Maggie Drive. The flames damaged a boat, RV and a camper.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon and evening thunderstorms along the southwest Florida gulf coast caused damage to a home in Marco Island as a result of a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 5 foot concrete wall in front of a Marco Island residence, blowing out 60 to 70 pound chunks of the wall. Some of the concrete traveled about 40 feet into the neighbor���s yard and also into the front of the house. Holes were gouged in the front door. Two gas lamps along the driveway also exploded leaving a hole about a foot in diameter. The bolt also caused damage to the home���s electronics. Total estimated cost of the damage to the concrete wall, lamps, front door, garage, and electronics was around $75,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong push of moist air overspread Iowa during the night of the 5th into the morning of the 6th.  The airmass became very unstable by mid morning with CAPE values over 3000 J/kg and a lifted index between -6 and -9 C.  The atmosphere was weakly sheared with less than 20 kts of shear present.  Thunderstorms formed on a rather isolated basis.  A cell merger took place over northern Adair County, which resulted in a 66 MPH wind gust at the Adair Schoolnet site.  As the storms moved east, lightning struck a church steeple in Dallas County at Dexter. The church was set on fire by the strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong cold front continued to approach Georgia from the northwest.  A cutoff upper low was sinking south into the mid-Atlantic region.  These features combined with typical July heat and humidity across the southeast resulted in scattered to numerous afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms.  The activity was most numerous in the Atlanta metropolitan area and locations east and south of Atlanta.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Upson County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck and set a house on fire just north of Thomaston.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged several homes and a church across South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Dawsey United Methodist Church and burned it to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front helped trigger several severe thunderstorms during the late afternoon and evening of the 16th in New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 47-year-old minister was injured by a lightning strike while at Camp Marcella in Rockaway Township. He was knocked unconscious for about twenty minutes. It was believed the lightning strike created a hole through his hat and entered his body. It exited through his left ankle and blew off a sneaker. He was treated for burns.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few strong to marginally severe thunderstorms impacted southern Missouri the morning of Halloween.  Mainly small hail and frequent lightning was observed with these storms.  One storm impacted 14 students at Buffalo High School.  A lightning strike knocked down a large tree limb which fell on the students causing minor injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fourteen Buffalo High School students were injured from a large tree limb falling to the ground.  This tree limb fell due to lightning striking the tree.  All of the injuries from the students were minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power grid.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power grid and knocked out power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm developed along the inland-pushing sea breeze over the city of Hialeah. Favorable wind profiles along the sea breeze front helped to produce a brief tornado that damaged 8 structures. Other storms which formed along the sea breeze front in Palm Beach County caused  lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Royal Palm complex setting ablaze to a few condominiums. The fire forced residents out of six units as fire spread through the attic and water from the hoses was pumped in damaging lower floors.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled front resided across the Mid Atlantic during the afternoon and evening of June 4th, allowing moisture and instability to pool along the boundary. This combined with several strong upper level disturbances resulted in numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Many of these thunderstorms became severe. While penny sized was reported in spots, damaging winds from the thunderstorms was widespread. An EF-0 tornado was also confirmed in the community of Chesapeake Beach in Calvert County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported that a lightning-sparked fire destroyed a home on Brookstone Way in Hermanville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into the Mid Atlantic region on June 14. With strong afternoon heating, scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of the front in the afternoon and evening. Some of the storms resulted in downed trees and power lines. In Leesburg, Virginia, nickel sized hail was also reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported that a lightning-sparked fire caused minor property damage east of Winchester.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching upper level storm triggered numerous showers and thunderstorms across the Tri-State Region. The area was in the warm sector of the surface reflection, with the synoptic cold front to the west and warm front across northern New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning downed trees and wires, resulting in a car fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A passing upper level low enhanced sea breeze and outflow initiated convection over an unstable and moist airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 21 year old male was struck by lightning near 3500 SW Archer Road. He was rushed to Shands Hospital. The victim was standing under a tree before he was struck.  He suffered extreme burns to half of his body.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The first widespread severe weather outbreak to affect south-central and southeast Wisconsin occurred on April 25th. It consisted of mostly large hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter, a couple damaging, straight-line wind reports, two tornadoes in Columbia County, and scattered flash flooding due to heavy rains and traning thunderstorm cells. Additionally, lightning struck several buildings and started fires that left damage.  Many power outages were reported thanks to tree branches snapping power lines, and up to 11,000 customers in southern Wisconsin lost power for varying time periods.  Synoptically, low pressure over southeast Minnesota moved northeast with a trailing cold front. Just ahead of the cold front was found strong warm air advection and moisture advection associated with a low-level jet.  Surface dewpoints poked into the mid to upper 60s ahead of the cold front while a favorable jet stream pattern existed aloft.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: LIghtning struck a communications tower belonging to the Iowa County Sheriff Department. Radios and computer equipment were damaged.  The time of this event is estimated, since the newspaper article indicated that the event occurred during the morning hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted north of Florida early in the day which increased surface based instability and low level moisture. A passing upper level short wave trough and sea breeze driven outflows boundaries enhanced convection across the state during the late afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a barn and caused a fire. The extent of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe storms affected Upstate South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, which fell on and destroyed 2 vehicles. There was also minor damage to an adjacent home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure was in place across the southern half of the area with upper impulses moving over the area. Numerous showers and scattered thunderstorms formed and moved over the area in this unstable environment.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree in the Fort Myers Villas neighborhood. The strike scorched the tree and scattered debris over fifty feet away, breaking windows on at least five nearby homes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe weather events occurred on July 29th and 30th ahead of a cold  |front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed the communications system, phone system, computers and cameras at the sheriff's office and other Wilson County buildings. The Nave funeral home lost its carport to the lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front that ended a week long heat wave also triggered severe thunderstorms across eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and early evening on the 23rd. The majority of the wind and lightning damage occurred in southeastern Pennsylvania where PECO Energy reported about 35,000 homes and businesses lost power. A power outage caused significant delays and over a one hour shut down (from 430 p.m. EDT through 545 p.m. EDT) of Amtrak train service between Philadelphia and Boston. Five SEPTA Regional Rail Lines were also affected by the outage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike created a three foot hole in the roof of the Allen Township Public Works building. The trusses of the building were not damaged. A canvas was placed over the hole until it was repaired.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms formed during the heat of the afternoon, aided by a weak surface trough that extended from northern Arkansas northeast across the Lower Ohio Valley. Tropical moisture combined with the slow movement of the storms resulted in locally very heavy rain. Some of the moisture was from the remnants of Hurricane Dolly.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple houses were struck by lightning. About one third of the residents in the city were without power due to lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The remnants of Hurricane Dolly that moved inland in the Lower Rio Grande Valley of south Texas, tracked around a large subtropical high centered over north Texas and was drifting across north Georgia.  The deep tropical moisture from the remnants of the hurricane combined with cold air aloft in an active northwest flow on the east side of the southern plains subtropical ridge to result in the development of numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  While the moist adiabatic atmosphere keep most thunderstorms below severe limits, flash flooding in the southwest part of the Atlanta metropolitan area became an issue during the evening as thunderstorms trained over the same areas for several hours.  Four to five inches of rain in Fulton and Douglas county southwest of Atlanta was common during the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Union City Police Department reported that lightning struck and set a tree on fire behind a mobile home in the 7000 block of Goodson Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The daily east coast sea breeze produced thunderstorms over coastal sections of Central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fisherman was struck and injured while standing on the beach at Indian River Shores. He was transported to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm and humid air mass was entrenched across the Mid Atlantic during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 7th. As an upper level disturbance moved across the area, scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed. Damaging winds brought down some trees and power lines across Maryland. The largest diameter hail recorded was quarter-sized, and occurred in Hillandale in Prince Georges County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported a lightning-sparked fire on the 2300 block of Ballenger Creek Pike in Adamstown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated severe thunderstorm resulted in a report of one inch diameter hail.  A lightning strike resulted in a gas well fire in Ensley Center in Newaygo county, resulting in significant damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a gas well fire in Ensley Center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms were pushing back toward the gulf coast on outflow boundaries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning and was on fire on the northbound side of the Sunshine Skyway Bridge.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure at the surface remained across south Florida as an upper trough stayed in place over the eastern U.S. This kept deep southwesterly winds in place over the area. The very moist atmosphere and some upper energy in place allowed for thunderstorms to develop over the coastal waters in the morning and push inland through the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two males were working in a field near the intersection of County Road 337 and County Road 343 when they were struck and injured by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure remained north of the area keeping east to southeast winds in place across the area. An upper level low moved over the state during this time, lowering 500mb temperatures to -9 to -10 degrees Celsius and allowing for numerous hail events with afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Duck Key Court in Carrollwood causing a two-alarm attic fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure remained north of the area keeping east to southeast winds in place across the area. An upper level low moved over the state during this time, lowering 500mb temperatures to -9 to -10 degrees Celsius and allowing for numerous hail events with afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit the railroad crossing at State Road 590 and McMullen Booth Road, causing the crossing's arms to lock in the down position.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of robust, intense severe thunderstorms developed during the morning horurs of June 2nd. Exceptional updrafts evident within these storms and high reflectivities through a deep layer within the thunderstorms (70 dbz to nearly 50,000 ft)produced hail up to the size of softballs at several locations across the county warning area.  The stones caused the most damage on the southwest side of the city of Manhattan, where the airport, numerous businesses, and hundreds of vehicles were pummeled with the large stones. Residents noted that it was so dark under the storms, that they needed a flashlight to see. A newspaper interview noted that one resident reported that gravel was shooting ten feet in the air, driven by the large hail. Farm fields across portions of Franklin County also showed extensive damage. Small animals that were unable to seek shelter also fell victim to the hail stones.  One Manhattan resident reported dead rabbits, squirrels, owls, and quail in his neighborhood. ||The somewhat discrete storms congealed into a convective line as they pushed southeastward across the county warning area, and the primary severe weather threat became strong winds. Residents and law enforcement officers across portions of Douglas, Franklin, Anderson, and Jefferson Counties reported wind gusts in the 60 to 70 mile per hour range. Two individuals in Shawnee County measured wind gusts of 80 miles per hour. Power outages were reported across the city of Topeka, with some residents left without power through that evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman went out for a walk just before ten in the morning , right after the rain associated with severe thunderstorm ended.  She stopped in her yard to pick a weed. Meanwhile, a lightning bolt struck the house across the street, and was felt by her. The bolt left a hole in the roof of the home, and blew several shingles onto the ground.  The woman had an elevated blood pressure, and was taken to a local hospital.  She was sore for several days after the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An ironic twist of fate came to Manhattan the evening of the 17th.  An EF-4 tornado had demolished portions of the Miller Ranch neighborhood in Manhattan just a week before.  One house in the neighborhood sustained no tornado damage.  Non-severe thunderstorms on the 17th brought numerous cloud to ground lightning strikes. One strike struck the untouched home in the Miller Neighborhood. A fire broke out in the attic, and caused several thousands of dollars in damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house that had been spared from the destruction of the EF-4 tornado the week before was struck by lightning.  A fire started in the attic and damaged the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed as the result of an upper level disturbance moving through southern New England.  Unusually cold air in the upper levels aided in the development of large hail within these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 27 year old man was injured inside his home when lightning struck a tree just outside.  Newspaper reports indicate that the man was standing in his doorway when lightning struck the tree about 30 feet away.  The man was transported to Milford Regional Medical Center for observation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered thunderstorms produced some wind damage in the central and eastern midlands taking down some trees and powerlines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes on Kaempfer Circle were struck by lightning causing moderate damage to one and minimal damage to the other.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across southern New England bringing cold air in at the upper levels and producing showers and thunderstorms. The cold air at the upper levels created conditions conducive to the production of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Sturtevant Avenue setting it on fire.  The triple decker house was divided into 5 apartments, all of which had to be evacuated and residents relocated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across southern New England bringing cold air in at the upper levels and producing showers and thunderstorms. The cold air at the upper levels created conditions conducive to the production of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was injured when lightning came through the open garage door and struck her ping pong paddle.  She experienced pain in her right arm, an irregular heart rhythm and the tissue in her throat was burned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across southern New England bringing cold air in at the upper levels and producing showers and thunderstorms. The cold air at the upper levels created conditions conducive to the production of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building on Christie Way, setting one third flood apartment on fire.  The fire damaged a natural gas line which forced the evacuation of 26 apartments.  The damage was repaired and residents were allowed back into their apartments two days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across southern New England bringing cold air in at the upper levels and producing showers and thunderstorms. The cold air at the upper levels created conditions conducive to the production of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Fossen Way setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak west-southwest flow allowed both sea breezes to be active with a collision likely near the U.S. Highway 301 corridor. Mid level dry air was noted as well as moderately cool 500 mb temperatures of -8 degrees C.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Russell Drive was struck by lightning with minimal damage reported. Cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak west-southwest flow allowed both sea breezes to be active with a collision likely near the U.S. Highway 301 corridor. Mid level dry air was noted as well as moderately cool 500 mb temperatures of -8 degrees C.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Buffalo Bill Drive was struck by lightning with minimal damage reported. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a well outside a home in North Yarmouth and is believed to have followed underground wiring to the home where it ignited a fire in the basement.  The fire then completely destroyed the home.  Six people were at the home at the time and all got out safely, but one of the family's dogs perished in the blaze.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across southern New England bringing cold air in at the upper levels and producing showers and thunderstorms. The cold air at the upper levels created conditions conducive to the production of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A police officer was trying to open a garage bay door at the police station when lightning struck nearby, traveled through the ground and the building and shocked him.  He was treated and released from a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system brought heavy rain and a few thunderstorms to the region. Some flash flooding occurred in Mississippi as a result of this rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes were struck by lightning around the Hattiesburg Metro Area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system brought heavy rain and a few thunderstorms to the region. Some flash flooding occurred in Mississippi as a result of this rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a house fire causing major damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving front stretched south of Long Island moved northward, combining with an upper level disturbance to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England. Plenty of moisture was in place across these areas, increasing the chance for heavy rain and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 58 year old man was injured when lightning struck the ground near his home in East Sandwich.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving front stretched south of Long Island moved northward, combining with an upper level disturbance to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England. Plenty of moisture was in place across these areas, increasing the chance for heavy rain and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: New England Cable News reported that a 44 year old man was injured when lightning struck a lamppost at the end of his driveway and travelled under the driveway to where he was standing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front was moving through the area supported by yet another deep trough into the eastern U.S.  A very narrow northeast-southwest oriented line of showers and thunderstorms accompanied the front through north and central Georgia during the day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Times Herald of Newnan reported that lightning struck the Coweta County 911 Center.  Damage to the center was minor and service was only briefly disrupted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm caused a house fire in McCormick County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Mt. Vintage subdivision in Merriwether causing major damage to a 2 story brick home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance which moved through the region produced some thunderstorms during the evening of October 1st and the morning of October 2nd. These thunderstorms produced some gusty winds and quite a bit of lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was damaged by a fire started by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved through the region on October 6th producing some thunderstorms over portions of West Tennessee. These thunderstorms produced quite a bit of lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged parts of First Baptist Church in Paris. The church suffered damage to its chimney, roof, phone system and electrical system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt hit the ground near three people that had stopped riding their motorcycles because of the heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four motorcyclist stopped on the shoulder of a roadway because of the heavy rain.  One of them hid in a near by culvert.  While stopped,  lightning hit the ground near the three cyclists knocking them on the ground.  All three were air lifted to hospitals.  The woman had badly burned feet.  One man was very disoriented.  The third man was unconscious.  The current had entered his feet and exited his head in three places.  He died two days later in the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large scale upper level trough continued over the eastern half of the country with a moist and unstable airmass over the local region. Mid level winds were around 30 to 40 knots with lifted indices near -8 deg C. Storms developed along the sea breezes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck homes in Palm Coast and Flagler Beach. Brush fires were also reported. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that caused damage at a home on Doolie Rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that caused damage at a home on Doolie Rd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms occurred in a brisk southerly wind flow ahead of a cold front over Missouri.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on U.S. Highway 41-A. The lightning damaged several appliances. A telephone line was shredded. The bolt exited the house on the back side, ripping pieces of vinyl siding at the exit point. The house sustained unspecified damage inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms occurred ahead of a cold front as it crossed into western Kentucky.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused considerable damage at the Oak Grove City Hall. Computer equipment used by the police department and city workers was damaged. Lightning struck the communications antenna on the side of the building. The main radio terminal used by emergency dispatchers was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms occurred in a brisk southerly wind flow ahead of a cold front over Missouri.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire. The lightning struck through a television antenna. The antenna connected to the back of the house had scorch marks, and there were burns in wet grass around its base. The home sustained heavy smoke and fire damage. A pet cat died. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moist monsoonal air combined with strong surface heating allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop this day.  While the thunderstorms were not severe, frequent lightning strikes caused structural damage and injuries when one of the thunderstorms moved through an urban area.  Heavy rain led to local urban flooding as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm with frequent lightning caused structural damage...power outages...local urban flooding and one injury.  A McDonald's employee was injured when lightning struck the restaurant while he was unloading the dishwasher.  Full recovery was expected. A manufactured home was partially burned by a fire caused by a lightning strike.  Several intersections in Medford and Central Point were flooding by heavy rain.  More than 14,000 customers lost power at some point during the storm.  All but 891 of those customers had power restored within two hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms during the early morning hours of April 25th created lightning which damaged the water treatment plant in Petersburg.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the water treatment plant in Petersburg. The lightning damaged the automatic control system and security system. There were no injuries and water service was not disrupted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep trough was developing across the eastern U.S. as a large polar high dropped south out of central Canada and a vigorous closed upper low moved from the central U.S. into the southeast.  Warm, moist, unstable air in advance of this system supported the development of widespread showers and thunderstorms.  Marginal severe hail and thunderstorm wind events were observed, but by far the main concern was flooding.  Several creeks and streams exceeded bankfull from this heavy rain event.  The flooding continued into the first few days of March.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Harris County 911 Center reported that a woman was struck by lightning and injured.  No further information was provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike affected the law enforcement dispatch center in Colby.  A communications console was destroyed, the phone system was damaged, and a fire occurred at a generator switch.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep closed low was sweeping through the Great Lakes into the northeast U.S., with a deep trough extending southward toward the Gulf Coast.  A strong polar cold front accompanied the system.  Unseasonably cold air was spreading from the northern plains toward the southeast behind the front as a 1036 millibar surface high moved south from Canada.  A very unstable air mass was noted ahead of the front across the southeast U.S.  However, a complex of thunderstorms which moved east out of central Alabama across central Georgia during the morning hours, greatly stabilized the atmosphere across the area.  Consequently, little severe weather was observed despite the strength of the weather systems tracking across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pike County Journal and Reporter of Zebulon reported that lightning struck a group of 16 cows lying down near a tree at a dairy farm on Kings Road near Meansville.  All of the cows were dead at the scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong shortwave, embedded within northwest flow aloft, combined with a very unstable surface air mass to result in the development of numerous northwest to southeastward moving large hail producing severe thunderstorms...primarily during the afternoon and evening hours.  Many reports of quarter to golf ball-sized hail were received across primarily the northern half of the state during these hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Bibb County Sheriff's Office reported that lightning struck a small shed on Mealer Street and set it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper trough and attendant surface cold front moved through the coastal plain region of North Carolina during the morning hours. The storms produced penny size hail and isolated damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree causing it to hit a house. The house sustained roof damage with a small camper being damaged as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms across the Victoria Crossroads and northern Coastal Bend produced isolated pockets of heavy rainfall. One storm became severe briefly over the city of Victoria.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Victoria 911 call center.  A backup system was used until the main system came back online at 4 AM.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a warm front, resulting in numerous lightning strikes across northeastern portions of New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Power outages were reported in River Edge due to downed power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a warm front, resulting in numerous lightning strikes across northeastern portions of New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Power outages were reported in Ridgewood due to downed power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a warm front, resulting in numerous lightning strikes across northeastern portions of New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Power outages were reported in Paramus due to downed power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Holden Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local law enforcement reported lightning struck a home in Holden Beach.  The strike caused some structural damage and broke some windows.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm producing cloud-to-ground lightning resulted in damage to a utility pole and downed live wires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: KIOD radio reported a lightning strike near 5th and Q Street in McCook.  The utility pole was destroyed and fire units were dispatched to the scene due to downed live wires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lifeguard was struck in his tower by lightning. It burned his jacket and set the tower on fire. He was transported to the hospital and the beaches were closed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper closed low was moving from the mid-south and Mississippi valley region into the mid-Atlantic and southeast U.S.  A strong cold front accompanied the upper system.  A strong low-level jet in advance of these weather systems transported warm, moist Gulf air northward into the region.  With strong dynamics, hence shear, combined with an unusually moist, unstable atmosphere, the atmosphere was primed for a major weather outbreak. One round of thunderstorms passed through north Georgia during the early morning hours.  A few minor severe weather events accompanied this system in northwest Georgia.  Partial clearing followed the morning convection, allowing temperatures to soar into the mid 70s across much of north and central Georgia in advance of the main weather system.  Scattered to numerous discrete supercell thunderstorms developed during mid-afternoon in northwest Georgia and progressed east and southeast across the remaining portions of the county warning area during the evening hours.  Severe thunderstorms and tornadoes lingered into the early morning hours of the 11th across the southern counties of central Georgia.  During the eight hour period from 5 pm EDT on April 10th to 1 am EDT on April 11th, a total of 14 tornadoes were confirmed to have touched down in north and central Georgia causing millions in damages.  While some injuries were observed, no deaths were observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Walton Times reported that the steeple of a church in Gratis was struck by lightning.  While no fire resulted, the sound system and some computers in the church suffered electronic damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep trough was developing across the eastern U.S. as a large polar high dropped south out of central Canada and a vigorous closed upper low moved from the central U.S. into the southeast.  Warm, moist, unstable air in advance of this system supported the development of widespread showers and thunderstorms.  Marginal severe hail and thunderstorm wind events were observed, but by far the main concern was flooding.  Several creeks and streams exceeded bankfull from this heavy rain event.  The flooding continued into the first few days of March.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Schley County Regional 911 Center reported that lightning struck an outbuilding.  The structure was completely destroyed from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong 500 mb shortwave trough and its associated 100-knot mid level jet streak tracked into the Lower Ohio Valley during the afternoon. A deepening surface low moved across central Illinois into Indiana, with a cold front trailing south-southwest into central Arkansas. Low level moisture increased in the warm sector, and along with surface heating,  mixed layer capes rose to near 1000 joules per kilogram. Isolated severe thunderstorms developed ahead of the cold front and tracked rapidly east-northeast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, damaging electrical devices.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Power outages were due to strong thunderstorms in rural LaPaz County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning took out the power to a large portion of LaPaz County this afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A bowing line of thunderstorms increased in intensity as it moved east across western Kentucky into an increasingly unstable atmosphere. Damaging surface winds were enhanced by a strong 50-knot rear-inflow jet feeding into the complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the 911 dispatch center, knocking out the dispatch consoles and phone lines. Lightning was blamed for a nearby garage fire that occurred about the same time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced hail across the Coastal Bend and heavy rainfall across the northern Coastal Bend.  7.17 inches of rain fell during the morning and early afternoon at Port Lavaca and 3.47 at the Aransas Wildlife Refuge.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near the Kings Crossing subdivision, with significant damage reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms across southwest Louisiana caused flooding in the Lake Charles area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an outdoor kitchen in Branch and set the kitchen on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving through the southeastern states caused several strong to severe thunderstorms in central Alabama, with large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire, on Lee County Road 390.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two tornadic supercells developed along a stalled warm front that extended across souther piedmont and coastal plain of North Carolina.|The cells produced 4 tornadoes in Johnston, Nash and Wilson counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a one-story wood and brick house. The home quickly became completely engulfed in flames. Fire Marshall reported the fire source originate from an electrical wall outlet.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Winds associated with thunderstorms caused areas of blowing dust along with spotty minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Transformer fire possibly started by lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late season cold front and outflow boundary allowed a large cluster of storms to develop during the predawn hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was a lightning strike that caused a fire in a home at the 1700 block of Trail of the Woods near the shore of Lake Travis.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck several tanks southeast of Riverton causing at least two to explode.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck four tanks about 15 miles southeast of Riverton causing two to explode and all to rupture. Contents of the containers were spilled on the ground during the incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed across the Northwest Piedmont during the evening hours as a strong mid-level shortwave trough moved across the Appalachians and across the area. The severe thunderstorm wind damage was confined to the Triad.|Lightning associated with the convection was excessive with over 600 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes per hour. Two structures were hit by lightning, with one of the structures being completely destroyed as fire consumed the mobile home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A mobile home in Southmont was totally destroyed when lightning struck the roof and then quickly spread through the entire home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged a home in El Campo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike produced significant damage to a home in El Campo. The lightning struck a tree in the backayrd and traveled along the ground to the home. The sheetrock was destroyed along two interior walls of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms caused several lightning strikes in Austin, two of which started fires at an apartment complex and a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apartment complex was struck by lightning.  There was a resulting fire that caused damage to the complex.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms caused several lightning strikes in Austin, two of which started fires at an apartment complex and a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residence on Encinal Cove and started a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong southern stream short wave was moving from the southern plains toward the southeast.  A cold front remained nearly stationary across the Tennessee Valley and into the Southern Plains.  A long-lived squall line of severe thunderstorms tracked from the mid-south during the morning hours into the southeast by late afternoon, reaching the Georgia border around 5 pm.  The line of thunderstorms weakened quickly as it progressed further eastward into the state, but not before blowing down several hundred trees and power lines, especially in parts of west central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Heard County 911 Center reported that a home was set on fire.  It was not entirely clear whether this was from a lightning strike or a downed tree, but there was considerable cloud-to-ground lightning in the area at the time as a squall line of thunderstorms moved through the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that severely damaged a home on the Isle au Haut.  The house was in the process of being remodeled and was just weeks away from being complete.   The small island community turned out in force to fight the fire which also threatened a 100-year-old island school house nearby.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire in the basement of a home in Freeport causing an estimated $50,000 in damage.  The lightning struck a nearby tree and then travelled through the ground and into the cellar of the home.  The fire was contained to the basement but the rest of the house had smoke damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two teenage baseball players were struck by lightning, but suffered only minor injuries.  The two (along with the rest of the team) had taken shelter in a dugout when the storm approached.  One of the boys was leaning against an electrical outlet when the lightning struck.  The current passed through the two boys and into the ground.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms crossing the northern Outer Banks produced a lightning strike that killed a man in Southern Shores.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck and killed by lightning around 5 pm along the beach at Southern Shores.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms were reported in parts of Mesa.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Mobile home fire likely due to power lines downed by nearby thunderstorms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad upper trough was slowly moving from the central U.S. toward the eastern U.S.  An accompanying cold front and Canadian high pressure system were moving southeast from the central U.S.  Scattered thunderstorms developed during afternoon heating in an increasing moist and unstable atmosphere.  On this particular day, a well defined sea breeze front was observed to move well inland from southeast Georgia during the early and mid-afternoon into northwest Georgia by evening.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms accompanied the sea breeze front as it moved northwest across the state.  A few of these became severe producing penny to quarter-sized hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The public reported that lightning struck a tree at a residence on Walker Circle, just east of Cassville, causing the tree to fall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds over parts of the western Piedmont of North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Nevin Rd, causing extensive damage and causing minor injuries to a firefighter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe stroms produced large hail and damaging winds over the North Carolina mountains.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a house in Brookings, starting a fire which damaged the attic and roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm, moist and unstable environment combined with the afternoon east and west coast sea breeze circulations to allow for severe thunderstorms to develop producing large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house along Old Homeland Road was struck by lightning. It caused a fire that consumed the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front, combined with some upper level support and moderate instability, resulted in thunderstorms forming across portions of northern Indiana. Severe reports were isolated in nature.

The garage was a total loss, with one home suffering severe damage and the other moderate damage. No specific damage estimates were given, but will be assessed at $100,000.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 5000 square foot home was destroyed after being hit by lightning during a strong thunderstorm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon/evening thunderstorms developed on this day.  One of these thunderstorms dropped severe hail on the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A McDonald's employee was injured when lightning struck the building while he was working with the dishwasher.  The employee recovered.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The sea breeze pushing into a highly unstable air mass, resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two structure fires were started by lightning strikes close to U.S. Route 17 near Pooler, Georgia.  One of the fires destroyed a mobile home while the other damaged a single family home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms affected portions of South Texas Thursday March 26th 2009. A few of the storms became severe and produced damaging winds, large hail, and frequent lightning. The worst damage was associated with a supercell thunderstorm that developed over central Live Oak County near George West. The supercell moved east-southeast across the extreme southern portion of Bee County into the northern portions of San Patricio County before weakening. This storm produced a 5 to 10 mile swath of damage mainly due to high winds.||More information on this severe weather episode can be found at http://www.srh.noaa.gov/crp/stories/Mar2609/default.html.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance in combination with the sea breeze in a highly unstable air mass, resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across southern South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported that a man was struck by lightning near a home on Lawson Road.  He was reported to be conscious and alert after being struck, but no other information was available regarding the condition of the victim.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low spawned numerous thunderstorms across portions of northeastern New Jersey. The storms were prolific hail producers. Snow plows were called upon for hail removal across some of the hardest hit areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire on Bailey Avenue in Oakland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave rotating around a deep upper trough over New England acted on warm humid air in place at the surface to allow for supercell thunderstorms to form and track across Northeast New Jersey.  These storms were prolific hail producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Fire Department Headquarters in Teaneck.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the home at 239 Colonial Avenue in Union.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rounds of thunderstorms passing through during the early morning hours of Monday, August 3rd led to the ignition of several structure fires in parts of western Wisconsin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a small fire in a deck planter and damaged a microwave oven.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front helped trigger thunderstorms during the night of July 1st that produced both heavy downpours and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a townhouse fire on Creekside Court in the Christine Hollow Development in Bear. The fire burned the roof of the townhouse and adjacent townhouses also suffered minor damage. The townhome residents were displaced. Damage was estimated at $125,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rounds of thunderstorms passing through during the early morning hours of Monday, August 3rd led to the ignition of several structure fires in parts of western Wisconsin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Oakdale Credit Union was damaged from a fire that apparently was sparked by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An intense supercell developed in western Nebraska during the afternoon and moved south through the evening hours, producing golf ball to softball sized hail and damaging wind gusts to near 80 mph. Millions of dollars in property and crop damage and livestock fatalities and injuries occurred as a result.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Cloud-to-ground lightning started grass fires southwest of Trenton Dam. No known damage to any structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several bands of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across central North Carolina as a a shortwave trough moved across the region. The severe threat quickly |transformed from a hail threat early in the event to a damaging wind episode as shortwave mid-level kinematics increased over the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Child struck by lightning in Bentonville. Injuries unknown but not considered to be serious.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front pushed through Maryland on the 23rd. A southeast flow ahead of the front ushered in plenty of moisture from the Atlantic Ocean. The moisture combined with the warm front triggered showers and thunderstorms. An isolated thunderstorm did become severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured due to a lightning strike close by at the Congressional Golf Course in Bethesda.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 14 year old male was struck by lightning when he ventured outdoors where some tents were pitched.  He made a full recovery.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14 year old male was struck and severely injured by a lightning bolt.  He was going outside where some tents were pitch.  CPR had to be performed as he had not pulse or respiration when rescuers reached him.  Miraculously he made a full recovery after about 2 weeks in the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was struck by lightning. The individual was released after receiving medical attention.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm moist atmosphere interacted with an upper level disturbance and lee side trough to produce a broken line of scattered showers and thunderstorms across central North Carolina. A few of these thunderstorms became severe and produced isolated wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apparent lightning strike caused a house fire in Fayetteville, North Carolina on Tanager Court. The fire took 30 minutes to extinguish and caused extensive damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the 13th, a cold front managed to push into Arkansas from the north before stalling. There was another round of precipitation in the northern and eastern counties early in the day. During the afternoon, the front triggered isolated severe storms in western sections of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning killed 12 cows, three calves, and a bull belonging to the Bergman High School FFA chapter. The cattle had huddled under a large oak tree when the lightning struck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An organized complex of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front as it approached southern Illinois and southeast Missouri during the hottest and most unstable time of day. Very strong instability, coupled with moderately strong mid-level winds, resulted in numerous damaging wind events. Most of the damaging winds were associated with small-scale bows that raced southeast ahead of the main storm complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn, which burned to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in North Platte during the early morning hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the chimney of a home owned by a National Weather Service employee in North Platte.  The lightning blew bricks off the chimney and damaged a water heater near the chimney.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast-moving line of thunderstorms, known as a derecho, rushed across Arkansas on the afternoon of the 12th. Widespread wind damage and one tornado resulted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Seven horses were killed by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A unusually mid-summer broad upper trough was located across the central U.S., with moist and active southwest flow aloft across the southeastern U.S.  A slow moving cold front was approaching the area from the Tennessee Valley.  Waves of isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms continued, even during the nighttime hours, during the last several days of July and into the first few days of August.  One early morning thunderstorm in Carroll county in west central Georgia spawned a lightning-related fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Times Georgian of Carrollton reported that lightning struck a home on Bear Creek Road during the early morning hours as the family inside was sleeping.  The lightning strike caused a fire in the attic, resulting in minor to moderate damage to the structure.  No injuries were reported, however.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved into extreme western Kansas during the early evening hours producing an isolated severe wind gust and lightning which ignited a small grass fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a small grass fire.  Rain from the thunderstorm extinguished the fire before the fire department arrived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of northeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree on Bryantown Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm moist atmosphere interacted with an upper level disturbance and lee side trough to produce a broken line of scattered showers and thunderstorms across central North Carolina. A few of these thunderstorms became severe and produced isolated wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Power lines were reported down across Tilghman Drive in Dunn, North Carolina, from an apparent lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Jupiter man in the head while he was loading his truck to go to work.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Jupiter Heights resident loaded his truck as he prepared to go to work about 7AM. The man was then struck in the head and thrown about 10 feet. The bolt also burned an egg shaped hole in his hat.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS crossed over southeast Georgia during the morning. The remnant upper level short wave trough crossed over northeast Florida during the afternoon which destabilized the atmosphere significantly to yield numerous severe storms in the afternoon and evening. The modified KJAX 12Z sounding indicated surface based lifted indices of -8 and CAPES of 4200 J/kg were possible during maximum heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a barn fire in Jamestown. The barn was completely destroyed, but the barn was not in use and ownership of the property was unknown. Another lightning strike also caused extensive damage to the Ware County Sheriff's Department radio equipment, cameras, computers and gate openers. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of lightning strikes caused minor damage in Canton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a chimney causing damage to the home, which included the water heater and sump pump.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man in an aluminum boat was struck by lightning near the Louisiana Universities Marine Consortium. The man was hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture continued to fuel scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  One storm produced high winds along the Colorado River, and another cluster of storms produced lightning damage in Las Vegas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and set afire two palm trees.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed and intensified over eastern Colorado during the early afternoon hours and moved across southwest Nebraska and northwest Kansas by late afternoon. Numerous reports of strong thunderstorm winds were received which produced minor damage. A few marginally severe hail reports were also received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a pasture fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and moist environment was in place with high pressure ridging across the area. Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries producing strong wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Langley Place causing an attic fire. Quick response kept damage amounts minimal.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalling cold front was settling into northern Florida with pre-frontal energy moving over the area, enhancing thunderstorm development in west to southwesterly flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Bowling Green Elementary School offices, damaging the phone system and fire alarm circuit boards.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused some injuries in the southern foothills of North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and injured 5 workers at a power plant near Cliffside. Although most of the injuries were minor, two people were transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire which destroyed a home east of Charlotte.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, igniting a fire that destroyed much of the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex which moved down the Missouri River during the predawn hours of July 8th spread an outflow boundary into southeast Nebraska.  Lightning from one storm in extreme southwest Iowa caused about a quarter of a million dollars in damage to more than a dozen semi trucks near Pacific Junction.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning apparently started a chain-reaction fire which eventually totally destroyed or significantly damaged 15 semi trucks at a fleet maintenance store near Interstate 29 near Pacific Junction.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the region in association with a frontal system. Some of the storms brought hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding to the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught on fire following a lightning strike along Highway 586.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple lines of scattered thunderstorms pushed into and through Central Indiana during the evening of the 19th and into the early morning hours of the 20th. This event produced one nickel sized hail report, two reports of funnel clouds in Vermillion County, and numerous wind gust and damage reports from across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Greensburg Daily News reported that a historic home near Greensburg was struck by lightning and a fire was started.  Damage to the home was significant.  The time this event occurred was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Central Indiana during the evening hours of the 25th and pushed southeast across the southern half of the state into the 26th.  A wind damage and flash flooding report were observed as these storms passed through the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Bedford Daily Times Mail reported that thunderstorm lightning sparked a house fire on Old Indiana 37 just north of Oolitic.  Some electrical damage was noted in the home.  The time and location of this event are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An old mesoscale convective vortex spawned numerous showers and thunderstorms over western South Carolina. A few of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a storage building on Silver Ridge Rd, destroying the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A waterspout developed over the St. Johns River north of the Buckman Bridge. The waterspout followed the river generally northward to northeast of the Ortega River entrance and south of the Fuller Warren Bridge near downtown Jacksonville before dissipating.
