EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed along sea breeze and outflow boundaries causing lightning damage to a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a house and caused an attic fire that nearly consumed the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalling cold front was settling into northern Florida with pre-frontal energy moving over the area, enhancing thunderstorm development in west to southwesterly flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home and caused a fire that comsumed most of the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalling cold front was settling into northern Florida with pre-frontal energy moving over the area, enhancing thunderstorm development in west to southwesterly flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the boom of a 130 foot drag line crane and injured the man operating the crane on Yonkers Boulevard in Zephyrhills. The man was airlifted to a Tampa hospital and was complaining of tingling in his fingers. It was not raining at the time and it was the first lightning strike anyone saw.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed along the east coast sea breeze during the afternoon hours, resulting in numerous lightning strikes across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A two-story home was struck by lightning in Weston, causing a fire inside the home. Firefighters were able to put out the blaze with only minor damage. All occupants of the home were able to evacuate safely. ||Time is approximate based on radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure moved out of Pennsylvania, south of Long Island and past the Cape and Islands sending warm, moist air into Southern New England.  This resulted in very heavy rainfall, particularly across Cape Cod, where six inches of rain fell in less than three hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were two lightning strikes at Camp Cachalot, a boy scout camp run by the Narragansett Council.  One of them struck near the dining hall where one of the|Scouts was leaning on a metal serving table.  He received a slight shock and, as a cautionary measure, the rescue squad was contacted.  One of the troop leaders accompanied the boy to the hospital where they were met by the parents - he was checked out, found to be OK, and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed over south central Texas on Wednesday August 12, 2009.  Lightning struck a church in Yorktown and caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck the chimney at the rear of the St. Paul Lutheran Church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few thunderstorms produced lightning damage and large hail over south central Upper Michigan on the 14th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning downed a tree near the intersection of Dickinson Boulevard and Wright Street in Kingsford.  The street was blocked to traffic as crews cleaned up the debris.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across Southern New England into an unstable atmosphere, resulting in showers and thunderstorms forming along the front. Some of these storms became severe producing strong, damaging winds and frequent lightning strikes.||A group of nine people sought shelter under a tree at a sports field.  Lightning struck the ground or a fence nearby and the nine felt a shock from the strike.  Only minor injuries were sustained.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Nine people, taking shelter under a tree at Foster Memorial Park, were injured when lightning struck nearby.  Five of the injured refused medical treatment, the other four were transported to a nearby hospital.  There were only minor injuries.  No information was available on their ages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike injured two children who were standing under a tree. Both children were transported to a local hospital with non-life threatening injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck a tree and injured two children that were standing beneath it. The 14 year old male and 12 year old female were both transported to a local hospital with non life threatening injuries. The female was still on the ground when emergency personnel arrived and had burn injuries consistent with a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from an intense thunderstorm started a fire with burned a church to the ground.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze boundaries collided across western Volusia County and resulted in a line of intense thunderstorms with frequent to excessive cloud to ground lightning. Lightning from one of the storms along the line hit a church and started a fire which burned the church to the ground, resulting in a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of lightning strikes caused minor damage in Canton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck a residence home on Rolling Ridge Court, leading to an attic fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough in the lee of the Appalachians in combination with the sea breeze and outflow boundaries from showers and thunderstorms, resulted in scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported that a student was struck by lightning during football practice in Bellville, Georgia.  The individual was taken to a hospital and was reported to be in stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across Southern New England into an unstable atmosphere, resulting in showers and thunderstorms forming along the front. Some of these storms became severe producing strong, damaging winds and frequent lightning strikes.||A group of nine people sought shelter under a tree at a sports field.  Lightning struck the ground or a fence nearby and the nine felt a shock from the strike.  Only minor injuries were sustained.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on North Lane, resulting in a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the southern half of Indiana producing a few reports of small hail and thunderstorm wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning two miles northeast of Pendleton.  No further information on property damage was given.  The time and property damage of this event has been estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across northern Indiana. A 64 year old man was struck by lightning while outside, throwing him across a garage. He escaped with minor injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local newspapers reported a 64 year old man was thrown across his garage when a lightning bolt struck about four feet from where he was standing. He lost consciousness for around five minutes, but awakened and was treated at a local hospital. He was released the next day some lingering speech problems and minor memory lapses.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Central Indiana during the evening hours of the 25th and pushed southeast across the southern half of the state into the 26th.  A wind damage and flash flooding report were observed as these storms passed through the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Rushville Republican reported a church office fire was started due to lightning from an isolated afternoon thunderstorm.  The United Methodist Church District Office building sustained water damage to the kitchen, utility room, and bathroom, as well as minor smoke damage throughout.  A hole, roughly a foot in diameter, was located on the northwest side of the roof.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective complex formed across southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas and northeast Texas during the predawn hours of July 28th and spread southeast towards the Interstate 20 corridor of northeast Texas into northwest Louisiana during the day.  The result was a few reports of wind damage across the region but the main result was excessive heavy rainfall.  This rainfall resulted in numerous flooding reports across the region with several high water rescues reported and water into some homes and businesses.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and resulted in a house fire at 759 Golson Road.  The lightning ran down the satellite wire and dried and cracked the ground beneath it.   From the strike, the fire spread to the carport to the attic and overtook the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A second mid/upper level trough moved down the Florida peninsula during the afternoon hours of June 23. This triggered a second round of severe and damaging thunderstorms over much of south Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two truck drivers were shocked by a nearby lightning strike as they were loading a dump truck in the Golden Gate Estates area. Both men received minor burns on their thighs and complained that their feet were stinging and burning. The injuries were not believed to be serious. One of the men was 22 years old and the other's age was unclear.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorms centered approximately 8 miles northwest of Key West produced a cloud-to-ground lightning strike, injuring one person near the south shore of Key West.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a palm tree near the entrance to White Street Pier in Key West.  The bolt passed from the tree to a 19-year-old male.  The strike survivor remained conscious and was treated at Lower Keys Medical Center for minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front combined with an unstable atmosphere to trigger showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours of the third. Some thunderstorms were severe, producing large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two boys playing baseball during a thunderstorm at Lee Hill Park in Fredericksburg, Virginia. One boy was pronounced dead at Mary Washington Hospital in Fredericksburg and the other boy was in critical condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mid and upper level dry air was in place with a deep northerly flow over the local area. An MCS move across the area during the late afternoon and early evening which spawned scattered severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near the corner of Dunn Avenue and U.S. Highway 1. Extensive structural damage occurred. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Hampstead.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Saint John's Church Road.  The house sustained very minor damage, and a microwave oven was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two airline employees were injured by a lightning strike while loading baggage onto an aircraft.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two AirTran employees were injured by a lightning strike at Orlando International Airport. A bolt of lightning hit near a ramp while workers were loading bags onto a flight. Both workers were transported to area hospitals and were expected to recover. It appears the lightning strike eminated from the anvil of a cluster of storms centered 15 to 20 miles southeast of the airport. The time of the event is approximate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong low level jet stream and abundant moisture for late winter produced scattered, elevated thunderstorms in central Illinois early in the morning. One of these thunderstorms produced a lightning strike which did extensive damage to a home near Decatur.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the west side of Forsyth causing a fire, and extensive damage to the home. There were no injuries, although the family dog had to be rescued by fire personnel.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A bowing line of thunderstorms increased in intensity as it moved east across western Kentucky into an increasingly unstable atmosphere. Damaging surface winds were enhanced by a strong 50-knot rear-inflow jet feeding into the complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning took out power lines at the junction of U.S. Highway 62 and Highway 121.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a power surge at a home on Wetmore Rd, igniting a fire that destroyed the home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced high winds and large hail across portions of southwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an O'Reilly's auto parts store and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weakening pacific storm system moved into Southeast Arizona resulting in scattered showers with a couple of embedded thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected illegal immigrant in the Altar valley was struck by lightning and suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning high-based thunderstorms moved across southeast Nebraska.  One storm produced a lightning strike which caused damage to electrical equipment at the Johnson county Sheriff's office.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused around $25,000 worth of damage to computers, radio and dispatch equipment and the phone system at the Sheriff's office in Tecumseh.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure in the lee of the Appalachians sparked thunderstorm development across the South Carolina Midlands which then propagated along outflow boundaries and intensified when it met up with the sea breeze.  This resulted in numerous strong to severe thunderstorms across southern South Carolina and southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported that a lightning strike started a barn on fire, 3 miles northwest of Saint George, South Carolina.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulse thunderstorms developed across portions of southwest Missouri.  Several of these storms produced damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding.  One man sustained injuries from being struck by lightning on a rural Greene County hay field.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 46 year old man sustained injuries from a lightning strike.  He was loading hay onto a trailer in a hay field near the intersection of Interstate 44 and Mulroy Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A derecho developed across north central Texas into south central Oklahoma during the evening hours of June 10th and move east into the four state region.  This complex of storms moved into an area with extreme instability and the result was widespread wind damage across much of northeast Texas, southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas and northwest Louisiana.  Isolated tornadoes were also reported along the leading edge of the squall line as it moved into northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning apparently struck a tree where 2 horses and 2 mules were standing under during a severe thunderstorm.  The animals were found dead later that night.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produce hail in Charles Mix County, and damaging winds and lightning damage near Sioux Falls during the morning of June 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building, starting a fire. Lightning also struck a day care center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure in the lee of the Appalachians in combination with the sea breeze, resulted in isolated thunderstorm development across southern South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast Media relayed a report of a person struck by lightning at the Ashley Oaks Apartments in West Ashley, South Carolina.  The individual was taken to a local hospital, but the condition of the person was not known.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure in the lee of the Appalachians in combination with the sea breeze, resulted in isolated thunderstorm development across southern South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper article indicated that a house was struck by lightning and caught on fire in Headquarters Plantation off the Maybank Highway in Johns Island, South Carolina.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed in a moist and very unstable atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that spread among oil tanks at an oil production site.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multicell clusters of thunderstorms intensified while spreading east-southeast in advance of a remnant upper level disturbance. A belt of 30 to 40 knot mid-level winds and strong instability supported the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tall white oak tree and may have started a fire at a telephone company switching building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread severe weather affected western South Carolina as a line of storms moved across much of the region. Other severe storms also developed ahead of the line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Catherine St, causing significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong storms with locally heavy rain developed ahead of a cold front on the 6th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole in Danville, briefly knocking out phone lines to 911.  The emergency calls were rerouted to Dardanelle during the outage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong storms with locally heavy rain developed ahead of a cold front on the 6th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree next to a house, then traveled to the house and set it on fire. The house was located in the Cloverdale section of southwest Little Rock.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another day of the wet season in South Florida produce more lightning damage along with hail and high wind gust reports.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked out power to near 1,600 residents of Palm Beach County after it knocked down power lines that cross Golf Street at Military Trail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of northeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike started a house fire at Perry Long Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front and upper level storm system, combined to bring severe thunderstorms and heavy rains to the area, in the evening hours of June 15, 2009, through the early morning hours of June 16, 2009. Large hail, damaging winds, and heavy rains with flash flooding, were observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused damage to a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A derecho developed across north central Texas into south central Oklahoma during the evening hours of June 10th and move east into the four state region.  This complex of storms moved into an area with extreme instability and the result was widespread wind damage across much of northeast Texas, southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas and northwest Louisiana.  Isolated tornadoes were also reported along the leading edge of the squall line as it moved into northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people driving an automobile got out of a truck when the vehicle drove over power lines that were downed from earlier in the evening.  The two adults were electrocuted when the exited the burning vehicle.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A derecho developed across north central Texas into south central Oklahoma during the evening hours of June 10th and move east into the four state region.  This complex of storms moved into an area with extreme instability and the result was widespread wind damage across much of northeast Texas, southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas and northwest Louisiana.  Isolated tornadoes were also reported along the leading edge of the squall line as it moved into northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree adjacent to a trailer house home in Maud, Texas near CR. 1208.  The lightning caused a short in the homeowner's kitchen.  The stove was turned on when the owners arrived home and the electrical damage smoked up their home and damaged a television set inside the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm in advance of a cold front produced a lightning strike across portions of Currituck Sound.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike produced a structural fire and caused scattered power outages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cloud to ground lightning struck a couple of homes in Wilmington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on North Bend Road in Ogden, setting it on fire. Around the same time, another home was struck on Kauri Street in the subdivision of Porters Neck, causing damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of storms over the Gulf of Mexico produced outflows during the morning that converged with the east coast sea breeze during the early afternoon. A moist and unstable airmass was in place, as well as a lingering surface trough across south Georgia. Widespread showers and storms developed. An upper level COL region was over the area which provided very slow storm motion. Doppler radar rainfall estimates generally ranged from 3-5 inches where nearly stationary and back-building cells developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and charred a fence.  The cost of damage was estimated and the timing of the event based on radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe convection developed along a lee side trough across the Midlands of South Carolina and central Georgia, then shifted east into the forecast area during the afternoon and evening as a potent upper level disturbance crossed the area. This convection interacted with the sea breeze (which happened to be pinched rather close to the coast) allowing for additional intensification closer to the coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported several homes were struck by lightning and started on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a residence in Highlands Ranch causing a fire.  The home was not a total loss, but the fire caused extensive damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across southeast Louisiana as a moist and unstable atmosphere prevailed across the region and a weak and nearly stationary frontal boundary was draped across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building resulting in a fire in the attic of the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning was the probable cause of a church fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Garden City Baptist Church early Sunday morning June 28th, setting it on fire.  Half the church was burning, along with part of another building, before the fire fighters arrived. It took five hours to extinguish the blaze, and the church was destroyed.  A fireman injured his ankle in the event.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours.  One person was injured by a lightning strike from one of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Bradley County emergency services reported a man working on a chicken house under construction near Red Clay State Park was stuck by lightning.  It had a metal roof, stilts and no sides.  He did not take a direct hit; however, the hair on the man's head and body were singed.  The man was alert but disoriented when he was taken to the hospital.  He is in stable condition now.  Another man who was nearby reported some hearing issues, but is alright now.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire that destroyed a home in Murrells Inlet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Blackmoor Golf Course subdivision.  The subsequent fire destroyed the home.  There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroyed a house in Jordanville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house off the Pee Dee Highway in Jordanville.  The house burned to the ground. No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and a lightning strike across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike produced a structural fire at Lynnhaven Circle.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of storms over the Gulf of Mexico produced outflows during the morning that converged with the east coast sea breeze during the early afternoon. A moist and unstable airmass was in place, as well as a lingering surface trough across south Georgia. Widespread showers and storms developed. An upper level COL region was over the area which provided very slow storm motion. Doppler radar rainfall estimates generally ranged from 3-5 inches where nearly stationary and back-building cells developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 12 year old male near the Flagler Beach Pier. He was struck unconcious and partially paralyzed. He was air-lifted to a trama center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold low pressure system bought showers and thunderstorms across the Central Valley. Lightning and small hail were reported with these storms, along with a gustnado spotted near Wheatland. A woman was struck by lightning in her home near Marysville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: CHP reported a woman injured when lightning struck power lines and went through a video game system she was playing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms and heavy rainfall affected northeastern California.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Plumas County Sheriff's Department reported that a woman was struck by lightning at her home in Portola.  She was transported by helicopter to the U.C. Davis Medical Center.  She never regained consciousness and died from her injuries on June 11th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifting through central Illinois during the late evening of June 7th produced scattered thunderstorms. One of these thunderstorms produced a lightning bolt which struck a mobile home near Henry and destroyed it.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home near Henry and started a fire. The fire destroyed the mobile home. An occupant of the structure sustained minor burns from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed southward into the region and when combined with the sea breeze and an upper level disturbance, resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across southern South Carolina and southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported that lightning struck a transformer and started a fire along Nash Avenue in Savannah, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a century-old home in Rumford and caused a fire that destroyed the residence.  Damage was estimated at about $200,000.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm developed ahead of a cold front as it moved over Waterbury and produced lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large tree in the back yard of 92 Grassy Hill Road around 4:30 am EST.  It traveled through the ground, blasted a hole through the basement wall, and displaced wooden panels in the interior portions of the house.  The sound was so loud that it damaged the hearing of a woman living in the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over parts of northeast Illinois during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a new auto body repair building on Grinnell Road and started a fire.  The building along with 3 vehicles was completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed over Mid-South during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 15th, 2009 due to daytime heating. The storms died out a couple hours after sunset. Some of the storms became severe with large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two story house causing a fire. The house was totally destroyed by the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface ridge axis was just south of the forecast area with a light southwest flow regime in place over a moist and unstable airmass. High moisture content was also in place which resulted in storms that yielded heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a cabinet store named Henry's Cabinets in St. Marys. Numerous explosions occurred due to lacquer's and other chemicals exploding inside the shop. All persons evacuated safely with no injuries.  The shop was destroyed. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a stalled frontal boundary over far southern Kansas during the evening hours of the 17th. Harper County received 50 to 60 mph winds and up to quarter size hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A teenage boy was struck by lightning in southeast Wichita during the late evening hours of the 17th. The injury was serious for a time, but the boy was later upgraded to good condition. The Wichita Eagle contributed to this report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a school in Yampa.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the South Routt Elementary School and started the building on fire.  The fire and related damage were confined to the gymnasium.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power substation in the early morning hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power substation on the north side of Montrose during the early morning hours, causing minor damage  This caused the electrical power to be down for nearly 1400 residences in northern Montrose County north of the town of Montrose for about 90 minutes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large thunderstorm complex developed over central Missouri during the evening hours.  Numerous reports of large hail were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a woman who was walking across an open field after fishing on one of the lakes at the Rocky Fork Lakes Conservation Area north of Columbia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Local media reported five cattle killed by lightning in rural Live Oak County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved into the Mid-South during the evening of June 9th. Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm killed three calves. The calves were found underneath a cottonwood tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that moved across east-central Wisconsin early in the morning on August 8 produced lightning that struck a home and started a fire in Calumet County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Collins at about 4:30 AM CDT, which started a two story farm house on fire.  The occupants were able to safely evacuate.  The fire did major damage to the structure.  Part of the roof collapsed and a portion of the second floor fell onto the first floor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon convection developed due to the heating of the day.  Plentiful moisture was in place for these random thunderstorms to develop across northwest Louisiana and a few of these storms were prolific lightning producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while standing under the front porch of his home.  Lightning struck a tree adjacent to the porch and ran down the trunk of the tree and struck the man.  He was taken to the nearest hospital and was treated for undisclosed injuries.  A separate lightning strike just minutes earlier hit and killed a dog about 200 yards down the road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the Mid-South during the early morning hours of July 26th, 2009. Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the front. The showers and storms continued into the morning hours before dying out. Some of the storms became severe producing large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caught a house on fire south of Germantown. The house sustained damage from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the Mid-South during the early morning hours of July 26th, 2009. Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the front. The showers and storms continued into the morning hours before dying out. Some of the storms became severe producing large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike produced a fire in a garage. The garage sustained damage from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning killed a swimmer at Wrightsville Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm moved quickly into the Wrightsville Beach area, and lightning struck a young man swimming near the Crystal Pier.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system dropped southeast from the middle Mississippi Valley and into the central Tennessee Valley during the late evening on the 4th.  Frequent lightning was reported with the storms as they rolled into Madison County.   Lightning struck a communications tower sending a surge into a home sparking a fire in the city of Hazel Green.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a communications tower resulting in a power surge which sparked a fire at a residence on Lowe Drive in Hazel Green.  Information on the extent of the fire and damages are not known.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving tropical upper level system brought rainfall to north Texas for 5-6 days. Total rainfall accumulations across north Texas ranged from less than an inch to nearly 15 inches. Most locations picked up 2-10 inches over the entire event. Periods of heavy rainfall and training of echoes resulted in significant flash flooding in some areas. The Salado area sustained significant damage on the 11th when over 10 of rain caused Salado Creek to overflow its banks and flood residential homes. On the 13th, another round of heavy rainfall with totals near 10 caused significant flooding in Ellis County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in Murphy was completely destroyed on the interior by a fire that was started from a lightning strike.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at a home in Murphy that caused minor damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front and a strong upper air disturbance moving across the region resulted in the development of numeorus thunderstorms. A few of the storms were strong to severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two vehicles were struck by lightning with one strike resulting in a minor fire. Three homes were struck by lightning with one resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front and a strong upper air disturbance moving across the region resulted in the development of numeorus thunderstorms. A few of the storms were strong to severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire on a shrimp boat.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire on the southwest side of Colorado Springs.  A firefighter was slightly injured while working the fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening hours, and one produced a lightning stike that destroyed a house east of Woodville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: KJAS radio station reported lightning struck a house on FM 1746 and the resulting fire destroyed the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was located across the Mid-South during the evening hours of July 12th, 2009. A mesoscale convective complex developed along the front and moved into the area during the late evening hours. Showers and thunderstorms from the complex affected the Mid-South through the morning hours of July 13th, 2009. Some of the storms became severe and produced damaging winds and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at the Martin Sprocket & Gear Incorporated Plant. The fire destroyed all the warehouses and ten percent of the plant received heavy smoke damage from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: This event featured mainly large hail reports that came in from the Indianapolis metropolitan area.  A few observations of wind gusts and damage were also reported, along with a couple flash flooding reports from the Indianapolis metro area as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman from Clinton was taken to the hospital for burns after she was struck by lightning.  The Daily Clintonian newspaper reported that she was standing under a tree when the event occurred. She was transported to Union Hospital Clinton and later taken, by ground, to Methodist Hospital in Indianapolis for burns.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system developed along a cold front and moved into the Mid-South during the evening of August 4th, 2009. The remnants of the complex moved southeast over the area into the early morning hours of August 5th, 2009. Some thunderstorms became severe producing large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike struck an apartment complex causing a fire. The apartment complex sustained damage as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Pawleys Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Pawleys Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a trough of low pressure and the inland propagating sea breeze, resulted in the development of numerous thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Print Media reported that a house was damaged by a fire that erupted from a lightning strike in Savannah, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and evening hours of the 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a rapidly-spreading fire that destroyed the Alpine Haus apartment complex.  All residents were safely evacuated, but 52 people were left homeless.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a back-door cold front during max afternoon heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman and a 18-month-old child were struck by lightning in a parking lot of a TJ Maxx in Fayetteville. Officials said the woman was carrying the boy and an umbrella when she was struck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lingering east coast trough dropped southward into the forecast area with steering flow out of the west southwest. A traversing upper level disturbance enhanced convection as well as energy from a remnant MCS which tracked toward the area from the northwest.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an outside garage-type building at a Waresboro residence and caused a fire which resulted in about $15,000 in damages. The building had held an antique tractor, a golf cart and a lot of antiques.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms pushed into Western Indiana during the early evening hours on the 19th.  Also, a few isolated storms were out ahead of the line in Central Indiana.  As the line of storms pushed into the central portion of the state, numerous thunderstorm wind damage and gust observations were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The NBC affiliate in Indianapolis reported that a man was struck by lightning as he and his son were walking from the car to the house, which was located in the 400 block of South Butler Avenue. A nearby tree was also struck and destroyed. The man was rushed to Wishard Hospital, where he was expected to recover.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm developed during afternoon peak heating and produced strong and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Kingwood and caused extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Robinwood Rd on the southeast side of Gastonia. The fire caused significant damage to the attic and a bedroom.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a couple house fires over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a home on Wilson Rd, about two miles east northeast of Brevard, causing damage to the roof and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed in parts of central and eastern Illinois ahead of a strong low pressure area in the upper Midwest, and its associated cold front. One of these thunderstorms produced lightning which caused a fire in Champaign County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A six unit apartment building on the west side of Champaign was struck by lightning, which caused a fire. Walls in one of the apartments were damaged, as well as a furnace. All of the occupants of the building escaped unharmed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon and evening across the Florida peninsula as an upper level trough approached from the Gulf Coast region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 10-year-old male was struck and injured by lightning in Hawthorne. He was hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad cutoff upper low, which had been located over central Texas, was beginning to move very slowly east by the 16th.  This upper low, in combination with unusually deep tropical moisture across the region for mid-September, began an extensive period of showers and thunderstorms with very heavy rain.  The deep tropical moisture was largely the result of a persistent 850 mb flow from the Gulf of Mexico.  The pattern changed very little for nearly a week as the upper low drifted very slowly east, completely cutoff from the main belt of westerlies, which were located well to the north in southern Canada.  The first flash flood event of an extended period of historical and record flooding across north and central Georgia, began on the 15th in Gilmer county.  A few storms became strong to marginally severe as well.||A historical, record, and catastrophic flood event began to unfolded during this period, mostly in the west central Georgia area, including the western and northwestern suburbs of Atlanta.  Major flooding was noted in many other areas of north and central Georgia, including the eastern suburbs of Atlanta, northwest Georgia, and parts of central Georgia.  The culprit was a very stagnant upper atmospheric pattern featuring a weak upper low that developed in early September across south Texas and slowly migrated east-northeast through September 22nd, until a more significant upper trough dropping south into the southern plains finally moved the pesky upper low northeast of Georgia.  In addition, an unusually deep tropical flow was noted throughout this period.  Precipitable water values exceeded 2.0 inches across the area during this time, resulting in extremely efficient rain producing cells.  Persistent heavy rain showers and thunderstorms began to plague the area on the 16th, and persisted daily across parts of north and central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that lightning struck a home in the 4000 block of Palace Court and a business in the 100 block of Luxomni Road.  Both structures suffered minor damage from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A combination of a passing pre-frontal trough and an approaching cold front spawned an isolated severe thunderstorm in Fairfield County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes resulted in two fires in Greenwich. The fires were quickly put out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a strong cold front during the morning hours of October 15th. These storms developed in a very moist airmass with the storms producing copious amounts of rainfall along with some strong and damaging wind gusts.  Trees were downed across some areas with other seeing excessive heavy rainfall that resulted in flash flooding across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced a lightning strike that hit a barn in Valliant, Oklahoma sparking a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching pre-frontal trough along with a passing upper level disturbance caused a squall line to form and move across the Lower Hudson Valley.  The line caused wind damage across portions of the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole in Scotchtown near the intersection of Route 211 and Ballard Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread heavy rainfall and flooding occurred across southeast Kansas and the Missouri Ozarks. The heavy rainfall was associated with several rounds of efficient rain producing stratiform events along a stalled warm front. Isolated convective elements embedded in the system and a few ahead of the system also produce some enhanced rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a cattle rancher as he was checking his cattle. The rancher and one calf were killed from the bolt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful cold front produced numerous severe thunderstorms across Connecticut, Long Island and the Lower Hudson Valley of New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex which started a fire lasting about one hour. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rare slow moving upper level low brought a round of strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of western Montana.  The main threat with these cells was heavy rain and hail.  Hail reached up to an inch in diameter and covered the ground in some locations.  In addition, heavy rain caused flash flooding on the Black Cat burn area, just outside of Missoula.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm that rolled through Anaconda started a roof on fire that was put out by the fire department before extensive damage occurred. The fire burned though the exterior of the roof and down into the insulation, about 20 square feet of the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early afternoon thunderstorms developed in a very unstable airmass across northern Louisiana on the afternoon of September 13th.  These thunderstorms produced a lightning strike which struck a home in Ouachita Parish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The fire department reported that a home in West Monroe caught fire from a lightning strike.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire that resulted in considerable damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire that resulted in considerable damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A passing cold front triggered an isolated severe thunderstorm in Bergen County producing penny size hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The house at 10 Babbitt Bridge Road in Mahwah was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system brought heavy rain and a few thunderstorms to the region. Some flash flooding occurred in Mississippi as a result of this rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in the Oakgrove Community. Some damage was done to the attic area of the house which is located on Buckingham Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A historical, record, and catastrophic flood event unfolded during this period, mostly in the west central Georgia area, including the western and northwestern suburbs of Atlanta.  Major flooding was noted in many other areas of north and central Georgia, including the eastern suburbs of Atlanta, northwest Georgia, and parts of central Georgia.  The culprit was a very stagnant upper atmospheric pattern featuring a weak upper low that developed in early September across south Texas and slowly migrated east-northeast through September 22nd, until a more significant upper trough dropping south into the southern plains finally moved the pesky upper low northeast of Georgia.  In addition, an unusually deep tropical flow was noted throughout this period.  Precipitable water values exceeded 2.0 inches across the area during much of this period, resulting in extremely efficient rain producing cells.  Persistent heavy rain showers and thunderstorms began to plague the area on the 16th, and persisted daily through the 21st across parts of north and central Georgia.||However, the catastrophic flooding unfolded when a sea breeze moving northwest merged with existing outflow boundaries and higher terrain across the western suburbs of Atlanta to result in persistent heavy thunderstorms for a period of at least 12 hours that trained across the same counties west of Atlanta, generally affecting Carroll, Douglas, Paulding and Cobb counties.  As the activity progressed across the state, significant flooding unfolded further east, including Fulton county, and the city of Atlanta, DeKalb, and Gwinnett counties.  Incredible rainfall amounts of 15 to over 20 inches, were observed from northeast Carroll, through much of Douglas, into eastern Paulding and southern Cobb counties.  Rainfall amounts of 10 to 15 inches were noted across parts of Fulton, Dekalb, and Gwinnett.  Rainfall amounts of 8 to 12 inches were noted in other more spotty areas of northwest, north central, and central Georgia during this period.||The excessive rainfall on top of saturated ground resulted in some of the worst flooding ever reported in the Atlanta and north Georgia area.  Eleven deaths were recorded during the event, mostly vehicle related deaths at night from washed out bridges and roads as a result of swollen creeks.  Property damages are estimated to be at least $0.5 Billion, with hundreds of homes and businesses destroyed by flood waters.  Bridges on several state and local highways were washed out and some will take months to even a year to replace.   Eighteen counties (Bartow, Carroll, Chattooga, Cherokee, Cobb, Coweta, DeKalb, Douglas, Fulton, Gwinnett, Heard, Newton, Paulding, Rockdale, Stephens, and Walker) received a presidential disaster declaration as a result of the historic floods.  Twenty-one counties were declared eligible for public assistance, including several central Georgia counties that were affected by flash flooding earlier in the period.||Some of the worst flooding was observed along Sweetwater Creek near the Cobb, Fulton, Douglas county line.  Hundreds of homes were flooded and destroyed as the waters of Sweetwater Creek rose more than 20 feet above flood level.||Many main stem and secondary creeks, streams, and rivers across north and central Georgia, particularly in northwest and west central Georgia, reached record flood levels.  Many of these same creeks, streams, and rivers remained in flood for several days.  In some cases, all time record flood levels were recorded.  The following is a list of new record flood levels set on several creeks, streams, and rivers in north and west Georgia.  Noonday Creek near Woodstock rose to 19.6 feet on the 21st at 530 pm EDT.  The previous record was 16.30 feet set on July 11, 2005.  Nickajack Creek at Mableton reached 19.30 feet on the 22nd at 215 am EDT.  The previous record was 16.60 feet set on July 11, 2005.  The North Fork of Peachtree Creek at Atlanta rose to 18.07 feet on the 21st at 715 pm EDT.  The previous record was 17.70 feet set on September 16, 2004.  Utoy Creek near Atlanta rose to 27.04 feet on the 22nd at 1000 am EDT.  The previous record was 16.86 feet set on May 6, 2003.  The Chattahoochee River at Whitesburg rose to 29.61 feet on the 21st at 745 pm EDT.  The previous record was 29.11 feet on December 11, 1919.  Suwanee Creek at Suwanee rose to 14.30 feet on the 21st at 645 pm EDT.  The previous record was 12.04 feet set on October 5, 1996.  The Yellow River at Lithonia rose to 25.50 feet on the 22nd at 515 am EDT.  The previous record was 17.53 feet set on May 7, 2003.  The Yellow River near Conyers below Milstead rose to 22.54 feet on the 22nd at 500 pm EDT.  The previous record was 16.36 feet set on July 8, 2005.  The Chattahoochee River at Franklin rose to 29.98 feet on the 22nd at 500 pm EDT.  The previous record was 28.40 feet set on December 15, 1919.  The Sweetwater Creek at Austell rose to 30.17 feet on the 22nd at 1000 pm EDT.  The previous record was 21.81 feet on July 12, 2005.||The following rivers reached flood levels that were within the top five all time levels at these locations.  Peachtree Creek in Atlanta rose to 23.89 feet on the 21st at 915 pm EDT.  The all time record is 25.80 feet recorded on December 20th, 1919.  Nancy Creek in Atlanta reached 14.69 feet on the 21st at 930 pm EDT.  The all time record is 15.50 feet on December 1, 1973.  The Chattahoochee River at Vinings reached 28.10 feet on the 22nd at 1200 am EDT.  The all time record is 29.0 feet set on December 10, 1919.  The South Fork of the Peachtree Creek reached 15.21 feet on the 22nd at 1200 am EDT.  The all time record is 29.0 feet set on December 10, 1976.  The Chattahoochee River at Campbellton reached 30.55 feet on the 22nd at 300 pm EDT.  The all time record is 31.60 feet set on December 10, 1919.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Paulding County Emergency Management personnel reported that at least ten lightning strike incidents were documented across the county during the late evening and early morning hours of thunderstorms and flash flooding.  At least two of the lightning strikes resulted in structural fires.  In addition, two Paulding county individuals were electrocuted by lightning in flood waters, but were not killed during the incidents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper-level low pressure area and associated cold front were moving from the mid-south into the southeast U.S.  A backdoor cold front was located across northeast Georgia.  A warm, tropical air mass was present between the advancing cold front to the west and the backdoor front across northeast Georgia.  Upper-level forcing was strong, thanks to the deep upper low moving into the southeast U.S.  These systems combined to bring a 24-hour period of heavy rain and thunderstorms that progressed from northwest to southeast across north and central Georgia.  With this event falling only 6 days after the record and catastrophic flooding that affected west central and north central Georgia on the 20th and 21st, flash flooding was a major concern.  Fortunately, the activity moved through more quickly, but additional flash flooding and river flooding was observed.  In addition, as the afternoon progressed and the activity moved into the central and east central portions of the state, an increasingly warm and unstable air mass was encountered, resulting in several thunderstorms becoming strong to severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Daily Citizen of Dalton reported that lightning struck and set the Rock Building on fire.  This was the site of the first high school in Murray County.  The building was completely destroyed from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface and upper level low supported episodes of thunderstorms within a high shear and low CAPE environment over southeastern Georgia. Thunderstorms with dangerous lightning occurred as this system approached the Atlantic Ocean.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager from Tattnall county reported a lightning strike that ignited a fire which caused a church to be destroyed in Reidsville, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure from southwest Kansas moved northeast into southeast Iowa by the afternoon of the 26th.  A strong push of warm air took place ahead of the low with 850 mb winds around 40 kts pushing into the central U.S.  Surface dew points rose to the mid 50s just south of Iowa during the afternoon with the 50 degree dew points reaching just north of the southern Iowa border.  At the same time, a strong polar high pressure area was poised over northern Manitoba and Saskatchewan.  Sub-zero temperatures reached as far south as the northern South Dakota border during the afternoon.  The atmosphere was marginally unstable with most unstable, elevated, CAPE values in the 500 to 1000 J/kg range in the afternoon.  Shear increased to between 30 and 45 kts with precipitable water values in the three quarters to one inch range over the southeast half of the state.  Thunderstorms in some form occurred through the day.  Over northern Iowa, they produced ice pellets and some small hail.  One half of an inch of ice pellet accumulation occurred in Emmet and Cerro Gordo Counties, with nearly an inch of ice pellet accumulation in Worth County.  These accumulations were the result of thunderstorms.  Thunderstorms were more intense over southeast Iowa.  The freezing level was relatively low, at 8200 feet, resulting in most of the storms producing hail of at least pea size.  Available CAPE was around 200 J/kg at the time.  Penny to quarter size hail fell in central Iowa, across the Des Moines metro area.  Lightning struck an overpass along Interstate 80/35 along the north side of the Des Moines metro area and knocked a chunk of concrete off of it.  The concrete fell onto the windshield of a moving van, smashing through the glass.  The driver was injured and admitted to the hospital with minor injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front accompanied and deep negatively tilted upper trough through the eastern U.S. from the 18th into the 19th.  An unseasonably warm and unstable air mass developed in advance of the cold front during the late afternoon and early evening across north and central Georgia as warm, moist air rode northward into Georgia on a strong low-level jet.  Afternoon temperatures in the 70s and dewpoints in the 60s, combined with strong shear and moderate instability, resulted in the development of numerous supercell thunderstorms from mid-afternoon until a few hours after midnight on the 19th.  Ten tornadoes, ranging in scale from EF0 to EF3 tracked across several north and central Georgia counties.  The worst tornadoes affected the east central Georgia counties of Jasper, Putnam, Hancock, and Jasper.  A death was observed in Hancock county with an EF3 tornado and several injuries were reported from Putnam and Hancock counties.  In addition to the tornadoes, very large hail occurred with several of the thunderstorms, including four-inch diameter hail in Coweta and Fayette counties just south of Atlanta.  Numerous reports of golf ball and larger-sized hail were received.  The event resulted in millions of dollars of damage and the destruction of several homes in north and central Georgia counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Spalding County Emergency Management Director reported that a person was struck and injured by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable air mass developed as early as midday across the central Tennessee Valley.  Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed by late morning producing very heavy rainfall that resulted in isolated flash flooding in northeast Madison County.  A few of these initial storms produced small hail.  As instability increased during the mid to late afternoon, more numerous thunderstorms developed.  Outflow boundary collisions triggered rapid development of new storms which became severe rather quickly in a few instances.  A few reports of large hail and damaging winds were received into the mid evening hours.  Isolated flash flooding occurred again in northeastern Madison County and in the town of Bridgeport in Jackson County where water depth climbed up to two feet.  One person was struck by lightning in the town of Fairview in Cullman County.  Additional thunderstorms moved northwest out of Georgia during the late evening hours producing additional rainfall, but diminished rather quickly after midnight.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person was struck by lightning on CR 1536 in the Fairview area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep and intensifying upper trough was moving from the southwest U.S. into the southeast U.S. from March 27th through the 29th.  Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms preceded the final passage of the upper low on the 29th.  Three to four inches of rain fell across many areas of north and central Georgia during this three-day period.  A number of streams, creeks, and rivers reached or exceeded bankful across north and central Georgia as the result of several days of at least moderate rainfall.  In addition, a number of the thunderstorms became severe on the 29th as the main upper trough moved through the area.  While most of the severe weather was in the form of damaging winds and hail, an isolated tornado was observed in Dooly county during the late morning hours on the 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An amateur radio operator reported that lightning struck a home in Planfield.  The lightning entered the home through the satellite dish mounted the roof.  Heavy rain extinguished the resulting fire.  Damage was minor.
