EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front which followed an unseasonably warm and humid late March afternoon helped trigger severe thunderstorms mainly across central New Jersey during the evening of the 29th. All of the severe weather reports were large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at a Public Service Electric and Gas substation caused power outages in Branchburg Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold winter storm brought 1 to 5 feet of storm total snow accumulation to the higher mountains of the southern Cascades and to the northern Sierra Nevada. Snow levels dropped to near 4000 feet during the latter part of the storm. Gusty winds brought reduced visibilities and broad drifting of snow.||This system also generated thunderstorms in the Central Valley, bringing heavy rain, flash flooding, and other severe effects. Large amounts of hail were reported over Shasta and Glenn Counties, larger than quarter size and more than 6 inches deep in some areas. Flash flooding and slides closed Highway 70 with minor flooding over a number of rural roads. Numerous car accidents from wet roads were reported across the area, as well as trees falling from a combination of wet ground and wind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck a dentist office, damaging a swamp cooler on the roof, the office computer, and the phone system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The seasons first organized severe weather event took place during the late afternoon and evening hours of the 24th.  Very warm and relatively moist air moved into the state on a gusty south wind.  Afternoon temperatures reached the mid 80s to around 90 with surface dew points in the upper 50s to mid 60s.  Precipitable water values were ample in the one to one and one half inch range.  The atmosphere became quite unstable with lifted indices falling to the -5 to -7 C. range and CAPE values around 2000 J/kg.  The freezing level was between 11,500 and 12,000 feet during the event with 25 to 35 kts of effective shear.  A cold front moved into Iowa during the morning of the 24th, and moved slowly southeast during the day.  There was a sharp contrast across the front, with temperatures in the 50s in its wake.  Thunderstorms erupted during the late afternoon along the front and developed southeast as the front moved in a scattered to broken line.  The line produced hail for the most part, with much of it between nickle size and one and one quarter inches in diameter.  One storm became stronger as it moved through Adair County and produced golf ball size hail southeast of Orient.  There was one severe wind gust with this event.  That occurred in Union County northeast of the Creston Airport, with a 60 MPH wind gust.  Additional thunderstorms formed during the late evening over northwest Iowa.  They were not severe, however they produced considerable lightning.  Lightning struck three houses in the town of Graettinger in Palo Alto County.  Minor damage was done to each of the homes as the lightning produced small fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms along the Chugach Mountains occurred the late afternoon and evening of May 26th. Two hikers were struck by lightning in Arctic Valley. One hiker was able to hike out the other required rescue from the Anchorage Fire Department.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two hikers observed the building storm and decided to hike up to the ridge to storm watch. At around 630 PM AKDT lightning struck near them knocking the man and women unconscious. Upon waking up the male companion was 15 feet from his female companion. They called emergency services to facilitate the rescue of the female as she was unable to walk out on her own. The male was able to walk out. His shoes appeared melted and he suffered a cut on his forehead. The female was taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a brick mailbox in Nixa and caused it to explode.  Bricks scattered and one was thrown through the windows of a home.  This specific thunderstorm also produced large hail. Another thunderstorm in Lawrence County produced golf ball size hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement determined that lightning struck a brick mailbox causing bricks to scatter.  One brick was thrown though a window of a house while a couple of vehicles were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of upper level impulses moved over a stationary frontal boundary across north Florida and southeast Georgia producing severe weather and flooding.  This event continued into April 2009.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a roof fire on a Fleming Island home. The family was not in the home at the time and there were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms occurred across a large part of eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening hours of the 10th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank and caused a fire.  The fire burned the oil in the tank and severely damaged the tank itself.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of upper troughs were moving through a large, deep upper trough centered in the mid part of the U.S.  One such upper trough and associated cold front were sweeping through the southeast U.S. on April 1st, with another stronger system on the 2nd.  Widespread heavy rain was observed in central Georgia with the first system.  Several creeks and streams exceeded bankful and several roads and low-lying areas in central Georgia counties, especially around Macon, were flooded.  This evolved into a minor severe weather event during the early morning hours of April 2nd.  A more significant severe weather outbreak was observed when the main upper system and cold front swept into the southeast U.S. late on April 2nd and into the early morning hours of the 3rd.  A narrow line of thunderstorms, with a noteable lack of lightning, produced damaging winds gusts of at least 60 mph as it moved across the Floyd and Calhoun areas of northwest Georgia.  The line weakened considerably as it tracked further eastward into the state after midnight on the 2nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The public reported a lightning strike to a tree at a private residence on Bridge Point Drive.  The tree was destroyed with tree debris scattered all about the immediate adjacent area.  In addition, a light fixture near the tree was blown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The warm front from the previous night lifted north of the state as low pressure pushed northeast out of Kansas across northwest Iowa.  The atmosphere became quite unstable.  Lifted indices fell to -6 to -8, with CAPE values in the 1000 to 2000 J/kg range.  CAPE in the -10 to -30 C. layer of the atmosphere was between 200 and 500 J/kg.  Downdraft CAPE was in the 400 to 700 J/kg range.  The effective shear was between 35 and 55 kts.  The freezing level was consistent with what it had been the previous few events, at 11,900 feet.  Thunderstorms developed in several lines.  The main issue with the thunderstorms was heavy rain as precipitable water values were around 1.6 inches.  The 850 mb feed into the system was between 45 and 55 kts.  Spotty reports of severe wind were received along the line with some relatively minor damage.  Some farm outbuilding damage occurred with the high winds and a few trees were blown over.  The roof and siding were both damaged on a house at Sun Valley Lake in Ringgold County as a brief tornado touched down there.  Part of the roof was actually removed by 80 MPH straight line winds.  Many of the storms produced hail, however it remained below severe limits.  Flooding was widespread with flash flooding reported in several counties.  Rainfall of 4 to 7 inches occurred in a few areas, especially in Guthrie and Audubon Counties.  A band widespread 2 to 4 inch rainfall extended all the way across the CWA from the southwest corner to the northeast in the Waterloo area.   Some of the heavier totals included 8.5 inches in Waterloo, 7.4 inches in Hudson, both in Black Hawk County, and 7 inches in Hardin County in the Whitten area.  Numerous reports of 24 to 36 hour rainfall totals were received. They ranged from 3 1/4 to over 8 inches.  As the thunderstorms were moving east of the area, lightning struck a house in Altoona setting it on fire.  The house was severely damaged.  Nobody was home at the time, however fire fighters were able to save the family dog.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure area moved across central Florida on the afternoon and evening of February 2nd. Thunderstorms associated with the low moved east across south Florida during the evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moving across northern Palm Beach County sparked a fire which destroyed a mobile home in the Suni Sands Mobile Home Park in Jupiter. The owner's dog died in the fire, and the owners were out to dinner when the fire started.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushing through the area brought a line of thunderstorms that caused high winds and two tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apparent lightning strike caused a tree to fall onto and damage portions of a house, a studio building, a garage, and a car.  Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak instability and moderate shear associated with a northward moving warm front allowed a favorable environment for several small clusters of storms to become severe, mainly producing pockets of damaging winds. One storm exhibiting supercell characteristics began producing more focus damage in Wabash County, with a brief tornado developing on the north side of Columbia City in Whitley County. A few hail reports were also received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Firefighters arrived at the residence on East County Road 100 South, east of Monroe to find the front of the house engulfed in flames. Several construction issues made it difficult to fight with the house being a total loss. The damage was estimated at around $100,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep and intensifying upper trough was moving from the southwest U.S. into the southeast U.S. from March 27th through the 29th.  Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms preceded the final passage of the upper low on the 29th.  Three to four inches of rain fell across many areas of north and central Georgia during this three-day period.  A number of streams, creeks, and rivers reached or exceeded bankful across north and central Georgia as the result of several days of at least moderate rainfall.  In addition, a number of the thunderstorms became severe on the 29th as the main upper trough moved through the area.  While most of the severe weather was in the form of damaging winds and hail, an isolated tornado was observed in Dooly county during the late morning hours on the 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Houston County Emergency Management Director reported that a home was struck by lightning of Arena Road between Georgia Highway 129 and U.S. Highway 341.  The home minor damage from the resulting fire.  Lightning was also likely the culprit of a downed power line southwest of Perry near Henderson, but may also have been the result of thunderstorm winds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system moved across north Florida and southeast Georgia dropping heavy rainfall and producing severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A roof fire was ignited by lightning in the eagle Creek sub-division east of U.S. Highway 1. A woman and a young child escaped through a bedroom window after smoke alarms woke the family. Her husband and two other young children escaped through the front door.  A family dog was also rescued and treated with a pet oxygen mask after it was found inside the house. The worst damage from the fire was to the attic above the garage, though smoke penetrated the rest of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of the 26th, thunderstorms developed in eastern Oklahoma and moved into western Arkansas during the overnight hours of the 26th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while on a drilling rig off of Ferguson Valley Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong shortwave, embedded within northwest flow aloft, combined with a very unstable surface air mass to result in the development of numerous northwest to southeastward moving large hail producing severe thunderstorms...primarily during the afternoon and evening hours.  Many reports of quarter to golf ball-sized hail were received across primarily the northern half of the state during these hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a home on Riverwalk Trail just off Annistown Road.  The roof collapsed as as a result of the fire and the home was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong shortwave, embedded within northwest flow aloft, combined with a very unstable surface air mass to result in the development of numerous northwest to southeastward moving large hail producing severe thunderstorms...primarily during the afternoon and evening hours.  Many reports of quarter to golf ball-sized hail were received across primarily the northern half of the state during these hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The 398-foot tall FAA control tower at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport sustained a lightning strike.  Intense cloud-to-ground lightning during a severe thunderstorm had already resulted in a loss of power to much of the airport.  Employees of the tower smelled smoke in the tower immediately following the strike, which required a brief evacuation of the tower.  Ground operations were ceased for several minutes during this thunderstorm as a result, compounding an already bad situation at the world's busiest airport.  In addition, penny to quarter-sized hail fell off-and-on from 806 pm EDT to 852 pm EDT, winds gusts to 42 knots, and nearly 1.5 inches of rain fall during the one-hour period from 8 pm to 9 pm EDT.  Much of the metro Atlanta area reported power outages following these thunderstorms.  Despite the lightning strike to the tower and its impact on airport operations, no significant damages were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several thunderstorms developed across the St. Cloud area the afternoon of May 6th. An individual was working in his backyard at the time one of the thunderstorms moved through and was struck by lightning. The injuries related to the lightning strike caused his unfortunate death six days later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several thunderstorms developed across the St. Cloud area the afternoon of May 6th. An individual was working in his backyard at the time one of the thunderstorms moved through and was struck by lightning. The injuries related to the lightning strike caused his unfortunate death six days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the late afternoon and evening hours of Easter Sunday, a large and strong upper level low clashed into an air mass where high levels of moisture were being pulled northward. This resulted in scattered severe storms which produced penny to half dollar sized hail and damaging winds. Most of the hail occurred across NW portions of the forecast area while the damaging winds occurred across the southern third. All of the convective wind damage occurred within the Highway 84 corridor from Natchez to Laurel as a bowing line of storms moved through this area and downed numerous trees. Some of the winds were as high as 70 or 80 mph across portions of Lincoln, Lawrence, Jefferson Davis, and Covington Counties. In addition to the damaging winds and hail, heavy rain and substantial flash flooding occurred. The heaviest rains fell along and south of the Highway 84 corridor from Brookhaven to Laurel where 4 to 6 inches fell with a few select locations likely reaching 7 inches.||Aside from the convective winds, which occurred from the line of thunderstorms, a wake low wind event occurred across the northeast portion of the forecast area (locations E of I-55 and N of I-20). This wake low occurred as higher surface pressures were held on to by the stratiform rain shield. As the back edge of the rain pushed east, surface pressures are allowed to drop rapidly in response to the main surface low which was located over southern Arkansas. The rapid drop in pressure, forced the winds to increase and shift more out of the east. As this occurred, sustained easterly winds increased to 30 to 45 mph with gusts between 50 and 60 mph. These strong winds downed many trees and caused other minor damage across the northeast portion of the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck and damaged occurred to many electrical appliances.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed north of a warm front resulting in a lightning strike which destroyed a home due to fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in Water Mill was destroyed by fire following a lightning strike to the home. There were no injuries or fatalities. It is estimated that 99 percent of the family's belongings were lost due to the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper closed low was moving from the mid-south and Mississippi valley region into the mid-Atlantic and southeast U.S.  A strong cold front accompanied the upper system.  A strong low-level jet in advance of these weather systems transported warm, moist Gulf air northward into the region.  With strong dynamics, hence shear, combined with an unusually moist, unstable atmosphere, the atmosphere was primed for a major weather outbreak. One round of thunderstorms passed through north Georgia during the early morning hours.  A few minor severe weather events accompanied this system in northwest Georgia.  Partial clearing followed the morning convection, allowing temperatures to soar into the mid 70s across much of north and central Georgia in advance of the main weather system.  Scattered to numerous discrete supercell thunderstorms developed during mid-afternoon in northwest Georgia and progressed east and southeast across the remaining portions of the county warning area during the evening hours.  Severe thunderstorms and tornadoes lingered into the early morning hours of the 11th across the southern counties of central Georgia.  During the eight hour period from 5 pm EDT on April 10th to 1 am EDT on April 11th, a total of 14 tornadoes were confirmed to have touched down in north and central Georgia causing millions in damages.  While some injuries were observed, no deaths were observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Bartow County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck and set a home on fire.  The structure suffered minor damage before the fire was extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to locally severe thunderstorms occurred in Delaware on the morning of the 6th as a warm front moved through the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes caused several homes in Little Creek to lose power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low moving across Southeast Arizona resulted in isolated thunderstorms that produced cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A residence on the Northwest side of Tucson was struck by lightning. A cinder block retaining wall suffered the brunt of the damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper air disturbance created an unstable atmosphere and permitted isolated thunderstorms to form around the greater Philadelphia metropolitan area during the evening of the 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An AirTran jet that was heading for landing at Philadelphia International Airport was struck by lightning. It landed without incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to locally severe thunderstorms occurred in southern New Jersey on the morning of the 6th as a warm front moved through the state. There were numerous reports of pea up to nickel size hail in the central and southern part of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a tree and a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching warm front helped trigger thunderstorms during the evening of the 20th in New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Dennisville (Dennis Township). Lightning strikes also caused power outages in Woodbine and Dennisville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure area combined with a moist and unstable atmosphere produced afternoon thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14 year boy was struck by lightning while standing outside the gymnasium at LaPine High School. He was hospitalized with burns to his chest and ankle areas and also suffered eye injury and a perforated eardrum.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger thunderstorms during the evening of the 21st in Delaware.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the ensuing fire damaged a first floor back room of a house on Gates Circle in Hockessin (Mill Creek Hundred). The fire was under control at 930 p.m. EDT that evening and no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike occurred about 20 miles west of Casper igniting a fire at an oil field.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed or damaged five oil tanks about 20 miles west of Casper near the intersection of county roads 201 and 210. The strike occurred about 1300MST blowing the lid off one tank containing about 400 barrels of crude oil. The fire quickly spread to a nearby tank and burning crude oil ignited the other tanks. Two additional propane tanks were burned but did not explode. A nearly century old storage building at the site was also completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moving south and west across the eastern plains approached the Capitan mountains on May the 20th. Thunderstorms developed ahead of the front producing little rain, but strong winds and numerous lightning strikes. The lightning produced 13 separate fires. The three largest fires burned 44,000 acres of rangeland around Capitan, Arabela and Picacho. At least six ranches received damage by the fires and there was a loss of some livestock.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three major fires consumed around 44,000 acres of rangeland from May 20th into the 24th. The three fires were located north of Capitan, around Arabela and near Picacho. The most significant of these was the Fresquez 2 fire north of Capitan. It burned around 10,000 acres north of Highway 246/48 and six ranches suffered fire damage to various degrees. Burned pasture/grassland was the main fire damage as no structures were damaged. However, several cattle were killed in the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper air disturbance created an unstable atmosphere and permitted isolated thunderstorms to form around the greater Philadelphia metropolitan area during the evening of the 22nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: US Airways flight number 1036, a Boeing 757 jet, was struck by lightning as it was coming in for landing at Philadelphia International Airport. The jet landed safely without incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to locally severe thunderstorms occurred in Delaware on the morning of the 6th as a warm front moved through the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and caused minor damage to the bell tower of the Zion Methodist Church on County Route 382 in Baltimore Hundred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed over central and eastern Maricopa County late in the evening. Strong winds were likely the cause of a large power outage in the East Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was blamed on starting a house fire in Surprise.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system approached western Arkansas during the morning of the 2nd, and spread showers and thunderstorms into the area. Some of these storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree fell on Arkansas Highway 291 due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system approached western Arkansas during the morning of the 2nd, and spread showers and thunderstorms into the area. Some of these storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning and transformers were blown at the University of Arkansas at Monticello.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger strong to severe thunderstorms across northern New Jersey during the late afternoon and early evening of the 24th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four hikers were struck and injured by lightning in the Delaware Water Gap National Recreational Area in Worthington State Forest about one mile south of Sunfish Pond in Pahaquarry Township. Lightning struck the ground first and then traveled to the hikers. Three men and one woman were injured. Two hikers initially were unable to talk after they were struck by lightning. Another hiker suffered a head wound. The injured hikers were taken to Pocono Medical Center in Pennsylvania.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms formed near a warm frontal boundary in northeast Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of the 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in Mertztown (Longswamp Township). The combination of the wind and lightning caused about 1,000 homes and businesses to lose power in thirteen municipalities in Berks County including Reading, Douglassville, Bernville and Kutztown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms formed near a warm frontal boundary in northeast Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of the 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms with frequent lightning struck several homes in Northampton County and caused a couple of fires. About one hundred cloud to ground lightning strikes occurred within a fifteen minute period in the Lehigh Valley. ||In Moore Township, a lightning strike and ensuing fire gutted a home on Countryview Lane. The shell of the house collapsed. Two adults that lived in the house were displaced and two cats died in the house. In Bushkill Township, a family was displaced after a lightning strike and ensuing fire badly damaged a home on Bushkill Center Road. The rear of the home around the kitchen was badly damaged. Two dogs were rescued. Other house fires were reported in Bath and Upper Nazareth Township. In East Allen Township, a family was trapped after a lightning strike downed wires around their home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across Southern New England, triggering showers and thunderstorms.  Warm, moist air and a strong low level jet aided in the development of these storms and several storms became severe, producing hail up to two inches in diameter.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an eight unit condominium building setting fire to the attic.  The fire engulfed the entire building, destroying the condos.  One firefighter suffered from heat exhaustion while trying to extinguish the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm in Eastland County produced small hail. This storm was the right mover of a splitting storm. The thunderstorms developed along a weak shortwave that was moving across the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a power outage throughout Ranger.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms moved across Missouri and Illinois into central and southern Indiana. Storms produced high winds and heavy rain. Rain of 4 to more than 6 inches fell in portions of central and southern Indiana on Wednesday and Thursday morning. This was the biggest rain the area has seen since June 2008. This rain did flood numerous county and a few state roads in central and southern Indiana. At least 4 vehicles attempted to go through flooded roads and did not make it. The biggest rain reported was 6.25 inches on the north side of Bloomington. Monroe���Morgan���Owen���Daviess and southern Marion Counties all had locations that measured 4 or more inches of rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire in the attic of a Shelbyville, Indiana home on South West Street around 1:30 PM EST.  Flames and smoke were visible from the roof.  Firefighters gained access to the fire via the front door as well as by cutting through the roof.  The fire was extinguished with minimal water, causing very little water damage.  Smoke damage was reported to be minimal as well.||Lightning also struck an 80-foot sycamore tree at nearby Bear Chase Golf Course, near Morristown Road, causing it to catch fire and fall.  The time of occurrence was simply described as late in the day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe squall line moved out of Oklahoma and marched across the northeastern counties of north Texas; mainly north and east of Dallas. Wind damage was common with this line of severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the communications tower on top of the Fannin County Jail destroying the radio consoles in the building and disabling the computer system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to locally severe thunderstorms moved across Delaware during the afternoon of the 29th. The thunderstorms preceded a cold front that moved through the Middle Atlantic States during the night of the 29th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire sparked a garage and house fire on Oyster Shell Cove in Salt Pond in Baltimore Hundred. The garage was struck by lightning and the fire then spread to the home. Damage was estimated at $40,000. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms moved across Missouri and Illinois into central and southern Indiana. Storms produced high winds and heavy rain. Rain of 4 to more than 6 inches fell in portions of central and southern Indiana on Wednesday and Thursday morning. This was the biggest rain the area has seen since June 2008. This rain did flood numerous county and a few state roads in central and southern Indiana. At least 4 vehicles attempted to go through flooded roads and did not make it. The biggest rain reported was 6.25 inches on the north side of Bloomington. Monroe���Morgan���Owen���Daviess and southern Marion Counties all had locations that measured 4 or more inches of rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is suspected to be the cause of a house fire, which held ten occupants, occurring at approximately 4 AM EST.  The fire was quickly extinguished by firefighters.  This minimized structural damage but contents were a total loss in one room and the rest of the house sustained extensive heat damage, melting all plastic items.  Property damage cost has been greatly estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms moving ahead of a cold front spawned two tornadoes and produced some damaging winds across the Tampa Bay area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a house causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large MCS rolled through north Texas during the morning hours with most of the severe weather occurring south of Interstate 20. Strong east winds up to 50 mph occurred on the back edge of the precipitation shield resulting in additional wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two-story house between Clifton and Valley Mills. Insulation in the walls caught on fire and was the only damage reported to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms affected areas along and south of the Red River beginning the morning of the 29th into the early morning hours of the 30th. Significant flooding occurred in Montague, Cooke, and Grayson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on US 82 outside of Ringgold was heavily damaged by a fire that was started by a lightning strike. A fireman suffered a broken leg and wrist while fighting the house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thundertorms developed due to strong daytime heating and an approaching cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and ingited a fire which destroyed it. The home was located at 150 Rivendale Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thundertorms developed due to strong daytime heating and an approaching cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at 38 Shoreline Drive and ignited a fire which destroyed it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed along old outflow boundaries from earlier thunderstorms over central Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male jogger was found dead on Crystal Beach. The victim was found with burns on his torso.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful low pressure system tracked from Arkansas into the Ohio Valley, lifting a warm front north during the afternoon, and pushing a cold front through during the evening hours. Two quasi-linear convective systems (QLCS) tracked east through the Tennessee Valley, resulting in two waves of thunderstorms, one which produced lightning damage to a home near Winchester, Tennessee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Petty Lane in Winchester. A gas leak, which was caused by the lightning strike, was ongoing at that time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms affected areas along and south of the Red River beginning the morning of the 29th into the early morning hours of the 30th. Significant flooding occurred in Montague, Cooke, and Grayson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank farm south of Saint Jo.  Three tanks exploded from the lightning strike and the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe hail storms affected the western Piedmont of North Carolina during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a storage shed on S Depot St, igniting a fire that destroyed the building and its contents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the lower Toledo Bend and Sam Rayburn country of deep east Texas during the morning hours of April 18th.  These storms produced occasional cloud to ground lightening which injured a fisherman on the Sam Rayburn Reservoir.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a boat on the Sam Rayburn Reservoir during the morning of April 18th.  The strike threw a fisherman out of the boat and ripped all of his clothes off his body.  A nearby fisherman jumped into the water and rescued the man who was struck and took him to shore where he was transferred to an ambulance.  The man sustained first and second degree burns to 15 percent of his body but recovered.  Witnesses said the lightning bolt was so strong, that other anglers as far as 400 yards away experienced a shock or tingle.  The strike burned the pedestal seat of the mans boat and caused the control unit of a trolling motor to explode.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large MCS rolled through north Texas during the morning hours with most of the severe weather occurring south of Interstate 20. Strong east winds up to 50 mph occurred on the back edge of the precipitation shield resulting in additional wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a roof-top air conditioning unit on the Parsons Building at C.R. Clements/Hollie Parsons Elementary School. Only the A/C unit was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms affected areas along and south of the Red River beginning the morning of the 29th into the early morning hours of the 30th. Significant flooding occurred in Montague, Cooke, and Grayson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire at a kennel at McElroy Street and SH 56 in Southmayd was believed to have been started by a lightning strike. Twenty-four dogs were rescued but an unknown number perished in the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving squall line produced copious amounts of rainfall and severe weather along and south of Interstate 20. An EF-1 tornado damaged 10 buildings in Corsicana including a school.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire in south Arlington.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across eastern Kansas and southern Missouri. Large hail and damaging winds were the primary severe hazards with these storms.  Eventually these storms developed into a squall line near the Highway 13 corridor, and produced wind damage in various locations east of Highway 13.  Perhaps the most significant damage from these storms occurred in the form of a microburst  near the community of Purdy.  One mobile home was destroyed resulting in an injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn caught on fire and burned to the ground from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail in Larimer and Weld Counties.  In Weld County, two weak tornadoes were also reported.  Hail up to golfball size caused heavy crop damage north and east of Greeley, where fields of sugar, beets, pinto beans, corn and carrots were damaged.   The combination of heavy rain and hail shut down several county roads around Greeley, as hail piled in small drifts and overflowed ditches.  Lightning strikes caused damage in Boulder, Superior and at Front Range Airport near Watkins.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and apartment complex, knocking some bricks from a building in the complex.  A water heater was also damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low moved into the Lower Mississippi River Valley from the northern Gulf of Mexico and put deep southwest flow across the area. Numerous thunderstorms developed across the area producing hail and causing a few lightning injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four people standing under a tree were injured when lightning struck the tree. A 52-year old male and a female were seriously injured and transported to the hospital. Two other people refused treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm produced a gust to 66 mph in northern Weld County.  In addition, a lightning strike killed a man in Evans.  A strong thunderstorm produced hail up to the size of nickels in Denver.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was killed by lightning while crossing an open field.  The victim was struck behind the right ear; the bolt then exited out both of his ankles.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front was positioned across central Kentucky during the early morning hours in association with a strong low pressure center over eastern Missouri. As the late evening hours progressed, a strong cold front moved into the mid state as the strong low pressure center moved northeastward into southern Indiana. This all resulted in a severe weather outbreak from the early morning hours through the late evening hours on May 8th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: County's Emergency 911 center located at the Fentress County Jail sustained a direct lightning hit, temporarily knocking out telephone service and causing damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low moved into the Lower Mississippi River Valley from the northern Gulf of Mexico and put deep southwest flow across the area. Numerous thunderstorms developed across the area producing hail and causing a few lightning injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 24-year old female farm worker was struck directly in her back by lightning while picking vegetables in a field and was flown to a Tampa hospital. She suffered first- and second-degree burns to her chest and midsection from the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail in Larimer and Weld Counties.  In Weld County, two weak tornadoes were also reported.  Hail up to golfball size caused heavy crop damage north and east of Greeley, where fields of sugar, beets, pinto beans, corn and carrots were damaged.   The combination of heavy rain and hail shut down several county roads around Greeley, as hail piled in small drifts and overflowed ditches.  Lightning strikes caused damage in Boulder, Superior and at Front Range Airport near Watkins.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a veterinary hospital, damaging an exterior electrical box.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms that moved into parts of central Illinois late in the evening of May 12th created numerous cloud to ground lightning strikes. One lightning strike sparked a house fire in southern Woodford County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a house in Kappa, setting the power lines and part of the house on fire. The kitchen, a staircase and the room above the kitchen were damaged. A man, who was asleep when the fire started, escaped unharmed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Evening thunderstorms on the 28th brought damaging winds, flash flooding and funnel clouds to portions of the Florida Big Bend.  Lightning was blamed for a few house fires in Leon County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Miccosukee Road was destroyed by fire as a result of a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Evening thunderstorms on the 28th brought damaging winds, flash flooding and funnel clouds to portions of the Florida Big Bend.  Lightning was blamed for a few house fires in Leon County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Desoto Farm Road was destroyed by fire as a result of a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe storms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Good View Dr, igniting a fire that rendered the home unlivable. Location is approximate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unstable air, fronts meandering in the state, and areas of low pressure aloft contributed to severe weather, including a few tornadoes.||At Arkansas Post (Arkansas County), the rain contributed to making it the wettest May ever recorded.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, damaging electronic and electrical items in the residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of upper level disturbances, an unstable atmosphere and an approaching cold front produced showers and thunderstorms across portions of Deep South Texas throughout the day May 24th. During the early morning hours, a small thunderstorm complex intensified over the western portion of the Lower RGV before accelerating through Weslaco, La Feria, Brownsville, and South Padre Island then raced into the Gulf. Wind gusts to 50 mph or higher along with brief but frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes caused damage around daybreak.  After a hot and sunny day, another round of storms crossed the Lower Valley during the mid evening, producing more hail and severe wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported that lightning struck a home in Weslaco during an early morning thunderstorm. A fire engulfed the home which was completed destroyed. There were no injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system (MCS) produced a large complex of showers and strong to severe thunderstorms during the afternoon hours. Large hail, damaging wind gusts, and flooding from heavy rainfall occurred with this system.  Also, lightning sparked a fire on the roof of an attic at a church in Falkville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire in the roof and attic of First Faith Church in Falkville.  The fire caused damage to the roof and bell tower.   Smoke and water damage was reported inside the building as a result.  Volunteer firefighters responded to the blaze around 8 am.  One of the responding firefighters suffered an ankle injury after falling from a ladder while working the blaze.  Based on the response time and radar data, an estimated time of occurrence is reported here.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a southward advancing cold front, warm air advection over the cold front, and an approaching shortwave aided in an explosive period that began the afternoon of May 2nd and continued into the morning hours of May 3rd. Several rounds of severe thunderstorms and thunderstorm clusters moved through north Texas in a very unstable environment. A downburst occurred at Valley Ranch in Irving resulting in the collapse of the Dallas Cowboys' bubble practice facility. Flash flooding and flooding became a problem as several clusters of storms produced heavy rainfall over repeated areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning after it first hit a tree and then jumped to him. The lightning stripped the tree of its bark and some of the bark pieces also hit the man. He was not seriously injured but taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening of the 5th, as well as the morning and afternoon of the 6th, an outbreak of severe storms and a few tornadoes occurred across the ArkLaMiss region. There were a number of reports of hail, wind damage, and a few tornadoes across the region. One of the strongest storms moved east across Choctaw County Mississippi. This storm produced an EF1 tornado over the southwest portion of the county. This storm did minor to major damage to five houses, church and several mobile homes. Another strong storm produced an EF1 tornado across northern Noxubee County Mississippi. It had blown an abandoned church of its foundation, overturned a camper and flipped over an 18 wheeler which caused minor injuries. There was also some reports of flash flooding across the northern portion of the ArkLaMiss due to heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning. This caused some fire damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze boundaries collided over coastal Volusia County, resulting in the rapid development of a severe storm near Ormond Beach. This cell then back-built south-southwest along a boundary during the late afternoon, producing a complex of strong to severe cells farther inland. A waterspout developed within the initial severe cell offshore of Ormond Beach and moved onto the beach as a tornado, reaching the adjacent backyard of several homes just beyond the beach. This vortex, or more likely other vorticies associated with the same cell then meandered south along the beach and near-shore Atlantic waters for about ten minutes (about 3 minutes over or near the beach). Early in the evening, another tornado (rated EF0) developed inland over Port Orange and damaged over 150 manufactured/mobile homes before lifting. One person sustained minor injuries from broken glass. Also, between Ormond Beach and Port Orange, a man was struck and injured by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning outside his Holly Hill home while gardening during the beginning of an approaching storm. The man was knocked unconscious for several minutes by the strike and awoke bleeding, and with a numb neck and right leg from the knee down. He also sustained burns inside his mouth and in his eyes. After gaining consciousness, he crawled into his house and his wife called 911. He was then rushed to a local hospital emergency room.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong weather system moved through the central U.S. during the late afternoon of the 3rd through the early morning of the 4th.  The system resembled a winter type system as strong low pressure at the surface developed over Kansas and moved northeast into Missouri.  A large area of thunderstorms developed in the deformation zone north of the low.  A large part of Iowa was affected by the rain with a narrow band of 4 to 7 inch rainfall extending from near the Atlantic area to north of Lamoni. The heaviest report received was nearly 8 inches in Madison County at Orient.  Five to 6 inches of rain fell in parts of Wayne County.  The rain caused flooding of several areas with Clarke, Decatur, Madison, and Wayne Counties affected the most.  Numerous roads were closed by the water with flash flooding reported in Decatur County where 5 to 6 feet of water covered the road.  The flash flooding extended north into Clarke County.  Flash flooding also occurred in Appanoose County, where Highway 2 was flooded west of Centerville.  Flash flooding washed out gravel roads in Wayne and Adair Counties as well with debris thrown onto the roads.  Lightning struck a tree near a house in Creston.  The lightning blasted a hole in the ground at the base of the tree.  Branches and pieces were thrown into a nearby home.  Three screen doors were broken along with several windows in the house.  A nearby garage was also damaged.  Pieces of the tree were blown out about 70 feet from the initial strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a warm front during the morning hours across portions of northeastern New Jersey. These storms produced lightning damage in Passaic county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on 44th Street, resulting in minor structural damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved south into Oklahoma during the evening of the 13th and early on the 14th. Widespread thunderstorms developed over much of the eastern two thirds of Oklahoma. Deep moisture and favorable atmospheric conditions allowed for thunderstorms to become severe along and south of the cold. A strong cap over western Oklahoma didn't allow for much development, although thunderstorms were able to develop west during the late evening hours. All forms of severe weather developed as several supercell thunderstorms developed. Hail up to baseball size, wind gusts over 60 mph, and four tornadoes were reported as the evening progressed. Damage was reported, especially with the tornadoes. The worst damage was reported with a tornado that moved from Gracemont to near Anadarko. Luckily, no injuries were reported with any of the damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck a house near Highway 76 in Pruitt City. The house was destroyed. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a warm front during the morning hours across portions of the Lower Hudson Valley. These storms produced lightning damage in Orange county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A building was struck by lightning in Mechanicstown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a warm front during the morning hours across portions of the Lower Hudson Valley. These storms produced lightning damage in Orange county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house at 65 O'Hare Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low visibility due to dense blowing dust affected many areas betwee Eloy and Apache Junction during the evening hours. Thunderstorms and locally damaging winds were also reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house at Third and Phoenix streets in Florence was struck by lightning, setting the house on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of severe thunderstorms intensified near the Memphis, Tennessee metropolitan area just after 7:00 AM CDT on the 14th.  A bow echo developed with this cluster of storms and accelerated east-southeast across northern Mississippi and into northwest Alabama between 10:00 AM and 11:30 AM CDT.  A brief EF-1 tornado occurred northwest of Moulton in Lawrence county.  Numerous trees and some power lines were knocked down with straight-line winds.  One report of brief flash flooding occurred in the town of Barton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at the intersection of County Road 265 and Blue Hollow Road in Town Creek.  Exact time of lightning strike unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early on the 3rd, clusters of severe storms evolved into a line which produced scattered wind damage as it pushed east along and just north of I-20. An outflow boundary pushed out of this line and provided the focus for the second powerful and significant severe event.||Between 8 am and 1 pm, a Derecho evolved and raced east across the southern half of the forecast area at 60 to 70 mph. A Derecho is defined as a long lived windstorm, usually a large bow echo, which has a width of 40 to 250 miles and covers a long distance, typically one to three states. This large bowing squall line brought intense straight line winds and widespread damage across its swath. Some of the wind speeds within this Derecho ranged between 80 and 95 mph. There were numerous reports of trees down as well as downed power lines, which caused widespread power outages in many locations. Many structures were damaged by either fallen trees or just the wind itself. Scattered reports of hail and a few tornadoes also occurred. One fatality occurred in Jones County as a tree fell through a woman���s mobile home.||During the early predawn hours of May 4th. Isolated severe storms affected northern Forest county with some flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Ross Barnett Reservoir area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck some pine trees close to where four construction workers were standing at Ferris State University, injuring two of them.  An isolated severe thunderstorm brought down several trees two miles north northeast of Fremont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A non severe morning thunderstorm produced lightning that struck pine trees very close to where four construction workers were standing, injuring all of them.  This occurred at Ferris State University in Big Rapids.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave rotating around a deep upper trough over New England acted on warm humid air in place at the surface to allow for supercell thunderstorms to form and track across CT.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at 387 Robinwood Road, causing a large limb to fall on a car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance swung through the area during middle of the afternoon of the 27th, and helped to ignite scattered afternoon thunderstorms. A cold pool aloft also helped to destabilize the atmosphere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in south Grand Forks, which ignited an underground natural gain main. Flames up to ten feet high erupted out of the ground, until the gas line could be shut off.

Damage was reported, especially with the tornadoes. The worst damage was reported with a tornado that moved from Gracemont to near Anadarko. Luckily, no injuries were reported with any of the damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck four homes, sparking a fire that caused substantial damage to the residences. Four firefighters were injured while responding to the fires, although the injuries were not serious. Monetary damage estimates were not available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and early evening of the 16th. Severe storms crossed portions of Central Mississippi and Northeast Louisiana. There was 1 fatality and two injuries from a lightning strike southwest of Yazoo City. There were reports of hail, wind damage, and flash flooding due to heavy rainfall. These storms were due a cold front that moved over the region. The cold front combined with rich gulf moisture and an unstable airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three trees were struck by lighting and fell on some power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening of the 10th, a small outbreak of severe storms occurred across the ArkLaMiss region. There were a number of reports of hail, wind damage, and a few tornadoes across the region. One of the strongest storms moved across Sharkey county. This storm produced an EF1 tornado in the Delta National Forest. Another strong storm produced three injuries in Rankin County, when broken and flying glass from a vehicle injured 3 people. Winds were estimated at 70 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning, which resulted in a fire with minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front, producing a few reports of large hail over the western Piedmont of North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a home in the Bariwood Community, causing significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced a great deal of lightning over Western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Braswell Rd, igniting a fire that damaged a garage apartment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered scattered afternoon and early evening severe thunderstorms across southern Connecticut. In addition to the afternoon storms, three people were struck by lightning while camping in early morning convection.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were struck by lightning while in their tents camping at Webb Mountain Park.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through southeast Pennsylvania during the morning of June 9th. The squall line formed near a warm frontal boundary. In addition to the winds, the thunderstorms were prolific lightning producers. PECO Energy reported about 10,000 homes and businesses lost power that morning in southeastern Pennsylvania because of the combination of mainly lightning and some damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Fielding Drive man was hospitalized after he was shocked by a power surge caused by a lightning strike. Lightning struck the roof of a home on Rabbit Run Road in Willistown Township. It damaged some shingles on the roof as well as a nearby pine tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A north to south line of thunderstorms developed rapidly over central Orange County, including metro Orlando as the west coast sea breeze boundary intersected another mesoscale boundary. A funnel cloud associated with a strong storm tracked just south of Highway 528, then touched down briefly and heavily damaged the roof of a large warehouse. Excessive lightning, nearly 2200 cloud to ground strikes in an hour, affected central Orange County. Lightning struck a apartment complex north of Orlando and started a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building during a severe thunderstorm and started a fire. Nearly 2200 cloud to ground lightning strikes occurred across central Orange County in an hour. The fire damaged eight units, two heavily. Eight families were displaced. Fire fighters working the incident had to pull back and take shelter due to a continuation of excessive lightning once arriving on scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong ridge of high pressure was centered over the southern plains on July 10th.  A shortwave trough rotating around this upper high tracked from near Chihuahua, Mexico into southeast Arizona. This disturbance arrived at peak heating, encouraging the development of scattered thunderstorms. With a relatively dry boundary layer, the primary threat from thunderstorms was damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement reported numerous tree fires started by lightning, centered near the intersection of Golf Links Road and Kolb Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms produced frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes across Volusia County. Two individuals were injured by lightning strikes in separate incidents about 30 minutes apart within Daytona Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man sitting next to a tree in the 1800 block of Biscayne Avenue in South Daytona Beach was struck indirectly by lightning. The man refused treatment at the scene, but was later transported to a hospital by a friend and was admitted in stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms produced frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes across Volusia County. Two individuals were injured by lightning strikes in separate incidents about 30 minutes apart within Daytona Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning within the 1600 block of Dunn Avenue in Daytona Beach. She was in her apartment talking on the telephone at the time of the strike. The woman was transported to a hospital and was admitted in stable condition.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a restaurant parking lot, near the intersection of Wilmot Road and Tanque Verde Road. The tree caught fire and was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small but intense complex of thunderstorms tracked east-southeast clipping far southern middle Tennessee during the late morning and early afternoon of the 10th. Frequent lightning occurred with the strongest storms, sparking a fire that destroyed a cabinet making shop.  A bow echo developed with the cluster of storms as it entered Lincoln County, producing winds of 50 to 60 mph that knocked down numerous trees in southern Lincoln County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire which destroyed a cabinet shop.  The occupants inside escaped harm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small but intense complex of thunderstorms tracked east-southeast into northern Alabama during the late morning and early afternoon of the 10th.  Frequent lightning occurred with the strongest storms, sparking a house fire, a telephone pole fire, and knocking a power pole down. A bow echo developed with the cluster of storms as it entered Limestone and Madison Counties, producing winds of 50 to 60 mph which caused isolated damage in northern Madison County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire at a residence north of Florence.  Location and time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small but intense complex of thunderstorms tracked east-southeast into northern Alabama during the late morning and early afternoon of the 10th.  Frequent lightning occurred with the strongest storms, sparking a house fire, a telephone pole fire, and knocking a power pole down. A bow echo developed with the cluster of storms as it entered Limestone and Madison Counties, producing winds of 50 to 60 mph which caused isolated damage in northern Madison County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked a power pole down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small but intense complex of thunderstorms tracked east-southeast into northern Alabama during the late morning and early afternoon of the 10th. A bow echo developed with the cluster of storms as it entered Limestone and Madison Counties, producing winds of 50 to 60 mph which caused isolated damage in northern Madison County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire on a telephone pole along County Road 91 near the Tennessee River.  The fire blew out the transmitter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable air mass developed as early as midday across the central Tennessee Valley.  Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed by late morning producing very heavy rainfall that resulted in isolated flash flooding in northeast Madison County.  A few of these initial storms produced small hail.  As instability increased during the mid to late afternoon, more numerous thunderstorms developed.  Outflow boundary collisions triggered rapid development of new storms which became severe rather quickly in a few instances.  A few reports of large hail and damaging winds were received into the mid evening hours.  Isolated flash flooding occurred again in northeastern Madison County and in the town of Bridgeport in Jackson County where water depth climbed up to two feet.  One person was struck by lightning in the town of Fairview in Cullman County.  Additional thunderstorms moved northwest out of Georgia during the late evening hours producing additional rainfall, but diminished rather quickly after midnight.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck a person along Good Hop School Road. Other details unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a southward moving frontal boundary across southeast Oklahoma, southwest Arkansas and northeast Texas.  The frontal boundary encountered a moderately unstable airmass with the result being large hail, damaging wind gusts and a few tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on the east side of town doing minor damage.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust to 70 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Darlington Prismatic Electric Fountain in City Park's Lake.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning which caused damage to a home in Wilmington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on the corner of Shinn Creek Lane and Wescott, causing damage to the roof and some of the windows.

PECO Energy reported about 10,000 homes and businesses lost power that morning in southeastern Pennsylvania because of the combination of mainly lightning and some damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the peak of a roof of a home on North Limerick Road in Limerick Township and caught fire. Four fire companies assisted and fought the blaze and confined the fire to one bedroom and attic on one side of the house. The lightning strike also fried the electrical system and meter in the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unstable air ahead of an upper-level low centered just off the coast of Northern California triggered bands of elevated convection which stretched from San Diego to the San Bernardino County deserts. Over 1500 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes were recorded during the event, resulting in one death and multiple injuries. The lightning also started approximately 70 fires, most of which were small and did not result in any damage or injuries. The storms also produced gusty winds and hail, with one cell producing quarter-sized hail in the Del Mar area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A was 40 year old female was struck and killed by lightning around 1530 PST while she was standing under a tree along the 8600 block of Bennett Avenue in Fontana. Some concrete nearby may have also been damaged due to the strike.||Six men were leaning against a metal fence near Electric Avenue and 40th Street in San Bernardino when lightning struck nearby. All six appeared to have suffered electrical burns. Four of the six were administered medical treatment by firefighters as a precaution.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms moved across northern New Jersey during the early morning on the 9th. A more organized squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through southern New Jersey later that morning. The squall line formed near a warm frontal boundary. In addition to the winds, the thunderstorms were prolific lightning producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house in Princeton was struck by lightning and damaged by the ensuing fire. No injuries were reported.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A building in Carteret was struck by lightning. The lightning strike left a small hole in the roof, but no fire developed.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged an Ocean Acres home in Stafford Township. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed preceding a cold front across the Poconos, Lehigh Valley and Bucks County. One thunderstorm in Northampton County caused a lightning related death.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 53-year-old man collapsed and died while doing yard work in his backyard in Bethlehem Township. He was holding an electric trimmer when he was struck by lightning. Medical crews responded, administered CPR, then transported him to Lehigh Valley Hospital Muhlenberg Campus where he was pronounced dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line of strong thunderstorms moved through Delaware during the morning of June 9th. Lightning from the thunderstorms caused a couple of house fires in Rehoboth Beach and Dagsboro.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Rehoboth Beach, a lightning strike and ensuing fire caused about an estimated $250,000 in damage to a house on Coventry Lane in the Rehoboth Beach Yacht and Country Club development. Lightning apparently struck the attic of the home. Six fire companies fought the blaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of supercell thunderstorms developed in western Tennessee during the afternoon hours, dropping southeast into northwestern and north central Alabama during the early to middle evening hours.  These storms produced copious amounts of large hail, some of it over 3 inches in diameter in the Decatur area.  Damaging winds of 65 to 95 mph were estimated, knocking down numerous large trees in the path of these storms.  The strongest estimated winds up to 95 mph occurred in a 16 square mile area affecting portions of Eva, Center Dale, and Gum Pond.  Flash flooding became a problem due to intense rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, particularly in Decatur and Hartselle in Morgan County.  Nearly continuous lightning was reported with these storms.  Observers noticed spectacular anvil crawler and cloud to ground lightning strikes.  Numerous power outages were reported due to power lines being knocked down or due to lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Moores Mill area, causing some minor damage.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Meridianville Road, causing minor damage.
