EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Dagsboro, an attic fire caused by a lightning strike to a home on Westchester Court caused an estimated $1,500 in damage to it before it was extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line of strong thunderstorms moved through the Maryland Eastern Shore during the morning of June 9th. Lightning from the thunderstorms caused outages in Talbot County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike that hit a power line caused outages to about 300 customers in the Easton Utility service area in Easton. Traffic lights were also knocked out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in an unstable air mass ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon hours.  Most of the activity occurred east of interstate 65.  A miniature supercell produced a tornado near the Albertville Airport in Marshall County. Thunderstorm wind damage was also reported in Morgan and Cullman Counties.  Southern and western portions of Marshall county also received two to three inches of rainfall in a short time leading to minor flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in the Union Grove community. No additional details are known.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong thunderstorms moved across northern New Jersey during the early morning on the 9th. A more organized squall line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through southern New Jersey later that morning. The squall line formed near a warm frontal boundary. In addition to the winds, the thunderstorms were prolific lightning producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Pleasant Avenue in Hanover Township. The ensuing fire was contained to the attic, but both the first and second floors of the home sustained smoke and water damage. The fire made the home uninhabitable. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms with intense lightning and torrential rain developed in a southerly flow of moist and unstable air ahead of a cold front over central Missouri and central Illinois.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged the taxiway at Barkley Regional Airport. The lightning left a small pit or pock mark in the pavement, and pieces of asphalt were scattered around.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in a southerly flow of moist and unstable air in advance of a cold front over south central Missouri.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the building that houses control equipment at an electrical substation. Power was interrupted for about 3,600 customers for two to three hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms formed as a result of a short wave moving over a |moist and very unstable atmosphere.  Isolated thunderstorms became |briefly severe.  Late in the evening, additional thunderstorms developed across|north central Texas and southern Oklahoma and moved east towards the interstate|30 corridor.  These storms quickly became severe, producing large hail during|the late night hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An oil tank was struck by lightning on FM 1795 just north of the Kelsey Community.  The tank was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were injured, one seriously, when they were struck by lightning while skeet shooting.  The more seriously injured man was burned when the lightning struck his shotgun, causing it to explode in his hands.  The combination of heavy rain and hail also caused flash flooding in Central Weld County.  Flash flooding was reported over County Road 24 and Two Rivers Parkway near Johnstown.  The water was over 12 inches deep in spots.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow southward moving cold front located over the Leatherstocking Region of New York State during the morning of June 2nd helped trigger thunderstorms along the eastern shore during that afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Bay View couple was homeless after a lightning strike and ensuing fire badly damaged their home. Lightning struck a tree on the property and then jumped to the roof of the home. It took about sixty firefighters ninety minutes to extinguish the blaze. Motorists were detoured near Cecil College as the fire was being fought. No injuries were reported. Damage was estimated at $215,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a water treatment plant in Daggett County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Red Canyon water treatment plant and destroyed the USFS' transducer.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Outflows from thunderstorms, an unstable air mass, and an upper level disturbance moving across Deep South Texas set the stage for more showers and strong to severe thunderstorms moving across portions of the CWA the afternoon of May 27th and into the early morning hours of May 28th. Frequent lightning was common with a large cell in southern Cameron County; the same cell produced large hail, heavy rains, and a prolonged downburst that produced one wind damage event.  ||Another round of storms developed around midnight east of the Sierra Madre and west of Laredo, forming a large complex of thunderstorms which progressed through Deep South Texas after midnight. One set of storms containing a continuous hail core and possible microbursts raced through Zapata, Jim Hogg, Brooks, and Kenedy, Counties while other thunderstorms moved through Starr County and eastward through the Lower Rio Grande Valley.  All storms contained frequent cloud to ground lightning and locally torrential rains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes, associated with continuing strong storms which had earlier produced locally heavy rains and large hail across portions of Jim Hogg, Starr, and Zapata County, moved across the McAllen/Edinburg area during the pre-dawn hours.  One of these strikes started a roof fire by igniting shingles at an estate home.  Within an hour, the blaze had engulfed the entire roof; residents were able to escape unharmed.  Video showed the house, as well as a vehicle, to be a total loss, with replacement estimated to be near $1 million.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A remnant frontal boundary in place across north-central Florida combined with a warm, moist, unstable airmass and the east and west coast sea breeze boundaries to develop numerous thunderstorms across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A restaurant was completely destroyed by a lightning induced fire. The market value of the building was $132,000 while the contents were estimated at $65,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms with heavy downpours and frequent lightning occurred during the morning hours on the 13th along a frontal boundary.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a four story, 20,000 square foot house on Breeding Drive north of Hartselle.  A mother and child were in the home at the time and escaped without injury, as the fire erupted and quickly spread throughout the house.  Tragically, this house was burned to the ground.  In addition, the blaze destroyed two antique cars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted northward into the region during the early morning hours of May 15th, triggering a large complex of thunderstorms across Iowa.  These storms tracked eastward into north-central Illinois producing very heavy rain west of the Illinois River during the morning.  Additional strong to severe thunderstorms developed further south along the warm front in the afternoon.  These storms produced numerous reports of large hail, heavy rainfall, and flash flooding - including a fatality in a vechicle due to high water late in the evening. This was the second heavy rain episode within three days in central Illinois.  There were also isolated reports of wind damage in central Illinois.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole on the east side of Monticello. The lightning strike caused damage to electrical systems and appliances in several homes. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed near a southward moving cold front under marginally strong deep layer wind shear.  The combination of effective shear of 30 to 35 knots and moderate instability supported isolated storms that were near severe levels. Some of the storms produced very heavy rain that caused localized flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A UPS truck driver was struck by lightning as he stepped down from his truck while making a delivery. He was treated and released from the local emergency room.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Middle Tennessee in association with a strong cold frontal passage during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: About 6,000 customers were without power when a lightning strike struck equipment at a power station in Lebannon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that formed along a warm front caused lightning damage in Caroline County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the ensuing fire destroyed an abandoned barn outside of Henderson along Bee Tree Road in Caroline County. A nearby tree was initially struck by the lightning. About twenty-seven fire fighters from four separate companies responded and took about thirty minutes to control the blaze. But, the two story barn was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a line of thunderstorms during the evening of the 21st in Maryland.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused 31 homes to lose power in Preston. Power was restored to all homes by 11 p.m. EDT that evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a line of thunderstorms that moved through southeastern Pennsylvania during the evening of the 21st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several residences were damaged by a lightning strike and then the ensuing fire in Honey Brook. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a line of thunderstorms that moved through New Jersey during the evening of the 21st. There were numerous reports of small hail as the line moved through Camden, Sussex, Warren, Morris, Hunterdon and Somerset Counties. Larger hail fell in Burlington County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire badly damaged a garage in Woodbury Heights.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms erupted during the mid morning hours of the 10th over the plains of eastern New Mexico, southwest Texas, and the western South Plains and Permian Basin. This activity developed as a strong upper air storm system ejected eastward from the Desert Southwest. ||The morning convection produced large hail up to the size of quarters and severe wind gusts as it overspread the western and central South Plains. Thunderstorm activity then pushed eastward during the day and at least one additional storm became severe with large hail near Jayton (Kent County). The only report of damaging weather occurred in Hale County where a lightning strike damaged a tree and broke windows at a residence in Plainview.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local newspaper accounts reported that lightning struck a tree at a residence at the 700 block of Independence Street in Plainview during a thunderstorm that impacted the area on the morning of the 10th. The lightning strike severely damaged the tree and caused pieces of tree bark to fly into and shatter several windows. Event time is estimated, and no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across Southern New England as an upper level low moved across the area.  Weak low level winds resulted in these storms moving very slowly, if at all.  Rainfall rates of up to four inches per hour produced flash flooding, resulting in street closures and basement flooding at several locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a condo at Knollsbrook Condominiums.  The resultant fire spread to two other units.  Three firefighters were treated for heat exhaustion and dehydration while fighting the fire.  One was transported to the hospital.  These injuries were indirectly related to the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave rotating around a deep upper trough over New England acted on warm humid air in place at the surface to allow for supercell thunderstorms to form and track across the Lower Hudson Valley and Long Island.  These storms were prolific hail producers and also caused flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn on Maples Road (at the Maples Farm) in Walkill causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave rotating around a deep upper trough over New England acted on warm humid air in place at the surface to allow for supercell thunderstorms to form and track across the Lower Hudson Valley and Long Island.  These storms were prolific hail producers and also caused flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a shed NW of Circleville causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms were in place across the area. One storm had a lightning strike that hit a home and caused damage to a few others.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One lightning strike caused damage to five homes. One home had a hole in the roof from the strike, another had significant damage and the other three had minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front set up across far southern Wisconsin on the afternoon of June 18th as an upper level disturbance moved eastward into the Upper Midwest.  A line of severe thunderstorms formed in an area of very warm, unstable air and moved through south-central and southeast Wisconsin overnight.  With surface dewpoints near 70, MLCAPE values near 3000 J/kg, and strong wind shear, the storms produced damaging winds, large hail up to 2.75 inches in diameter, dangerous lightning, and a weak tornado. These thunderstorms also dumped very heavy rain up to 4 inches over a relatively short period of time, causing numerous reports of flash flooding across Dane, Waukesha, and Milwaukee counties.  At the height of the storms, about 27,000 households were without electricity in southeastern Wisconsin due to damaged power-lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighthing struck a home shortly after 0200 CST.  The resultant fire damaged an upstairs bedroom.  The homes elecrical system was fried by the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong subtropical ridge, which had been centered over Alabama for the previous three days, was retrograding west as a deep upper low developed off the east coast.  Similar to the June 10th - June 18th period, unstable northwest flow evolved across the area once again.  The pattern allowed a backdoor cold front to push into the area from the northeast, further providing lift in an unstable air mass for thunderstorms.  Scattered severe thunderstorms developed across north central Georgia during the mid-afternoon and quickly moved southeast into central Georgia by evening.  The majority of the severe events occurred in central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Laurens County Fire and Rescue Department reported that lightning set several hundred hay bales on fire in a field in the far northeastern part of the county, north of Dublin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure was ridging across the area at the surface and aloft. Afternoon sea breeze development provided the focus for scattered thunderstorms to form each day producing large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fifteen head of cattle, including 12 cows, two calves, and one bull, all humpbacked Brahmans, were killed when lightning struck the field in which the herd was standing. Time is estimated based off of radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm resulting in a lightning fatality moved across the northwest portions of Billings during the evening hours of July 4th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A line of strong thunderstorms moved into the area west of Billings around 730pm MDT. A lightning strike occurred around 800pm MDT at Castlerock Park where the Celebrate Freedom community gathering was occuring. A visitor (26 year old male resident of Billings) at the celebration was struck in the forehead and died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front produced thunderstorms across portions of northeastern New Jersey. Some of the storms produced lightning and wind damage, as well as large hail and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a house fire at 102 Main Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front produced thunderstorms across portions of northeastern New Jersey. Some of the storms produced lightning and wind damage, as well as large hail and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire at 111 High Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms formed along the east coast sea breeze front as it moved west during the afternoon.  More storms developed along the west coast sea breeze front that remained in the Fort Myers area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 32-year-old male was struck by a bolt from the blue while golfing on the 18th hole at the Spring Lake Golf Resort. The Lorida Fire Department put out a small fire in a nearby tree. It was not raining at the time of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold front moved from the Ohio River Valley during the early morning hours into northern Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours, and upper level disturbances moved in from the northwest, isolated thunderstorms developed across mainly northern portions of Middle Tennessee. Three of these thunderstorms reached severe thresholds, two producing thunderstorm wind damage and one large hail. Other thunderstorms produced lightning that caused major damage to a home in Macon County and an oil well in Overton County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning stike directly hit an oil well off Airport Road in Livingston. It caused the entire lid to bend and fly off.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure was dissipating across the area with high pressure ridging across southern Florida. This kept west to southwest winds in place across the local area and allowed for numerous thunderstorms with heavy rains and a tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 77-year-old man was struck by lightning while standing inside a metal shed and holding the handle on an electrical cart. The hand that was holding the cart where he was struck was numb for a few hours and he was sent to the hospital for testing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold front moved from the Ohio River Valley during the early morning hours into northern Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours, and upper level disturbances moved in from the northwest, isolated thunderstorms developed across mainly northern portions of Middle Tennessee. Three of these thunderstorms reached severe thresholds, two producing thunderstorm wind damage and one large hail. Other thunderstorms produced lightning that caused major damage to a home in Macon County and an oil well in Overton County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a multi-story well constructed brick home at 1106 Hightower Road. It caused an attic fire that lasted from 4 PM to 10 PM. Three fire fighters were transported to the hospital with smoke inhalation and chest pains. They were later released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A boundary across the area triggered scattered severe thunderstorms across east Tennessee during the the afternoon hours.  Damage reports were primarily for damaging thunderstorm winds, but a few hail occurrences were also received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Knoxville News Sentinel newspaper reported a 14 year old girl was struck by lightning as she was entering her home in Luttrell as lightning struck the door she was entering.  She treated and released at a hospital with minor burns on her hand and is expected to fully recover.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the morning hours across southern Louisiana, and continued into the afternoon.  A few storms produced isolated reports of severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: KATC-TV reported a lightning strike caused significant damage to electronic equipment in their studio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the morning hours across southern Louisiana, and continued into the afternoon.  A few storms produced isolated reports of severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: KLFY-TV reported lightning struck their TV tower and briefly knocked the station off the air.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On July 16th, a strong upper atmospheric area of low pressure was located north of the Great Lakes in south central Canada. In addition, a significant mid-level shortwave and associated surface low moved across the eastern Great Lakes, while a warm front and subsequent cold front swept across northern New York and Vermont during the afternoon and evening.||Numerous thunderstorms developed and moved across Vermont, in a moderate to strong unstable atmosphere during the afternoon and evening. In addition there were a few super-cell thunderstorms that produced very large hail, up to 3.3 inches in diameter in Westford (Chittenden county) with numerous reports of damage to vehicles, homes, crop and livestock and a brief EF-0 tornado along the Williamstown-Chelsea town line (Orange county). ||The measured 3.3 inch diameter hail in Westford, also had a circumference of 6.8 inches and has been determined by the State Climate Extremes Committee as the largest recorded hail stone in Vermont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Jet Blue aircraft at the gate, while embarking passengers. The lightning bolt apparently entered the tail section and traveled along the length of the airplane to the gate ramp. No injuries but visible entrance and exit points on aircraft.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A second cold frontal passage in as many days helped trigger strong to severe thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of the 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a three-story Victorian home on East Ridley Avenue in Ridley Park Borough. The fire was confined to the roof, but smoke damage occurred throughout the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast-moving line of thunderstorms, known as a derecho, rushed across Arkansas on the afternoon of the 12th. Widespread wind damage and one tornado resulted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility line and traveled to a house, setting it on fire. The house was severely damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast-moving line of thunderstorms, known as a derecho, rushed across Arkansas on the afternoon of the 12th. Widespread wind damage and one tornado resulted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a boat storage company, setting it on fire. Only the building burned, as there was time to move the boats to safety.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts of 60 to 85 mph, large hail, torrential rainfall, and nearly continuous lightning across much of central and southeast Illinois during the early morning of June 18th. The high winds resulted in multiple power outages, downed trees and power lines, and damage to light poles, outbuildings, and several homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home between Bloomington and Shirley during the early morning hours of June 18th. The lightning ignited a fire in the top floor of the house. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts of 60 to 85 mph, large hail, torrential rainfall, and nearly continuous lightning across much of central and southeast Illinois during the early morning of June 18th. The high winds resulted in multiple power outages, downed trees and power lines, and damage to light poles, outbuildings, and several homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an auto repair shop in Tuscola and started a fire. There was no one present in the building when the fire began.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Airmass thunderstorms produced a few areas of large hail and damaging winds over the North Carolina Mountains during the late afternoon and evening hours. There was also an isolated instance of flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 65-year-old man was struck and killed by lightning on highway 74E just south of Fairview.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold front moved from the Ohio Valley during the early morning hours into Middle Tennessee during the mid afternoon hours, an unstable airmass was already in place across much of the Southeastern U.S. This resulted in development across much of the mid state from the morning through late evening hours of severe thunderstorms, which produced large hail and thunderstorm wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof and started an attic fire in the the Richland Hills Subdivision near Manchester. Exact extent of damage to attic was unkown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a warm and unstable airmass continued across the Northern Cumberland Plateua region, an area of showers and thunderstorms developed during the late morning hours. One of these thunderstorms reached severe thresholds in Fentress County, producing thunderstorm wind damage. Another thunderstorm that developed in Fentress County produced a lightning stike that destroyed four oil tanks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike destroyed an Oil Tank. One of the tanks exploded and flew 300 feet from its original location. Newspaper reported that this one tank broke off a crossmember of a utility pole and severed power and utility lines before coming to rest across the road from its original position. There was only a small amount of oil in the bottom of the tanks, which helped keep a fire that had also broken out due to the lightning strike from spreading to three other tanks in the same area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the evening of June 7th and the morning of June 8th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Bagatelle Lane which started a fire.  While the fire was small, the house suffered extensive smoke and heat damage.  Firefighters also had to remove much of the ceiling throughout the home to remove insulation to prevent the fire from spreading.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the evening of June 7th and the morning of June 8th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two story building on Main Street and caused a fire in the southwest corner of the second level.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large subtropical ridge across Texas was slowly expanding eastward.  In advance of this upper ridge, an unstable northwest flow aloft, with embedded short waves, prevailed across the eastern and southeastern U.S.  This, combined with a continuing warm and very unstable air mass, supported development of several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across the region from late on the 17th through the 18th.  The first round developed around midnight on the 17th and continued through the early morning hours.  The second round occurred during the late afternoon on the 18th.  The storms were generally confined to the eastern parts of the state with all of the storms developing within narrow northwest to southeast oriented bands.  The individual storms were also tracking from northwest to southeast within these bands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Madison County Journal reported that lightning struck and killed an 8-year old quarter horse at a private residence on Fred Goss Road, just southeast of Danielsville.  On Rogers Church Road, just northwest of Danielsville, a home was struck by lightning, which set an inside wire on fall.  Damage was minimal as the fire was quickly extinguished by firefighters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A diffuse frontal system across central Kentucky produced generally garden variety thunderstorms with mainly sub-severe conditions, including small hail and some gusty winds. One person was struck by lightning and killed while standing under a tree in Shelby County, KY.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 44-year old main died Monday, June 15th after being struck by lightning at his workplace on Wednesday, June 10th.  The man was standing outside waiting to be picked up from work when his coworkers heard a very loud boom and looked out to find him laying on the ground beneath the tree.  Coworkers and emergency workers performed CPR on the man but he died five days later due to multiple organ failure according to local news reports.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike knocked a hole in a roof and produced a fire in a house in the Redwing section off General Booth Boulevard.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front helped trigger thunderstorms during the night of July 1st that produced both heavy downpours and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree in the front yard of a Katherine Drive home in Rockaway Township and caused it to explode about 4 a.m. EDT. The tree shrapnel impaled a nearby home's roof and damaged the back window of a car. The cable connection within the home was fried by the lightning strike. All power was restored that afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over western Fresno County during the evening of June 4th, and rapidly grew in intensity. One severe thunderstorm had a reflectivity of 73 dBz, and a VIL (vertically integrated liquid) of 43 g/kg. Hail up to an inch in diameter fell near the town of Helm, and outflow winds were estimated at around 60 mph.||The low finally moved onshore on the 5th, and lifted northeast into northern Nevada that evening. An upper-level trough remained over California, with an unseasonably cold airmass aloft. Upper-level impulses moving through the trough continued the threat of afternoon and evening mountain convection, with isolated light showers drifting over the San Joaquin Valley at times. Temperatures fell to some 10-15 degrees below normal, and stayed well below normal for the next week.||The Grouse wildfire that was sparked by lightning on May 30th continued through the month of June. The ignition time was 1400 PST on May 30th, the location was 3 miles southwest of Yosemite Valley in Mariposa County.  The size of the fire was 3047 acres. The cost to containment was $2.9 million. The containment date was July 13th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement reported tree damage due to lightning near the town of Daulton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm complex developed over Oklahoma during the early morning hours of June 15th, 2009. The complex moved east along a stationary front eventually moving into the Mid-South during the day continuing into the early evening hours on June 15th, 2009. Many storms became severe producing large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck police headquarters in Jackson damaging equipment inside the Jackson-Madison County Emergency Management Operations Center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm complex developed over Oklahoma during the early morning hours of June 15th, 2009. The complex moved east along a stationary front eventually moving into the Mid-South during the day continuing into the early evening hours on June 15th, 2009. Many storms became severe producing large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tornado siren in Lexington causing the siren to become inoperable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois from mid morning through early afternoon, producing numerous reports of hail, heavy rain, flooding and flash flooding.  The City of Chicago reported almost 200 tree emergencies which includes damage to tree limbs, partial trees or entire trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house along Canterbury Drive and started a fire in the bathroom.  The house was declared uninhabitable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure was dissipating across the area with high pressure ridging across southern Florida. This kept west to southwest winds in place across the local area and allowed for numerous thunderstorms with heavy rains and a tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Portmarnock Place in Lakewood Ranch causing the attic to catch fire and consume much of the home.  Damage estimate included structure and contents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of storms from an earlier mesoscale convective system that developed over Southeast Kansas and Southwest Missouri moved east-southeast and affected northern parts of the Mid-South. Strong wind shear combined with very unstable air to support storms with damaging winds along and just ahead of a squall line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas line at a house on the east side of Paris resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several supercell thunderstorms affected the western Carolinas during the afternoon and evening hours, producing very large hail, wind damage and a few weak tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Cedar Lake Farm Rd, igniting a fire that caused significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the evening of June 19th producing widespread wind damage and some flash flooding.  The City of Chicago reported almost 1,000 tree emergencies which includes damage to tree limbs, partial trees or entire trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which fell onto power lines on Crosat Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed along the east coast sea breeze during the afternoon hours, resulting in numerous lightning strikes across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 53-year-old lawn care worker was struck and killed by a lightning strike as he was cutting grass at an apartment building in Coral Springs.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS moved through north Texas causing significant damage to areas generally along and north of Interstate 20. Significant and widespread tree, fence and power line damage was reported along the path of the MCS. In addition, three tornadoes touched down in the northern portions of the DFW Metroplex. Approximately 250,000 people were left without power in the Metroplex and hundreds of flights were grounded or cancelled at DFW and DAL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike is believed to have started a fire that burned the saltwater disposal tanks on Highway 16 South.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved into the state on the 23rd. The front triggered isolated thunderstorms during the heat of the afternoon. A few of the storms were severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire that heavily damaged an office building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms, flash floods and damaging lightning affected parts of southeast Idaho.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a large tree in Taylorsville killed 13 dairy cows who were underneath it for shelter during a thunderstorn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS moved through north Texas causing significant damage to areas generally along and north of Interstate 20. Significant and widespread tree, fence and power line damage was reported along the path of the MCS. In addition, three tornadoes touched down in the northern portions of the DFW Metroplex. Approximately 250,000 people were left without power in the Metroplex and hundreds of flights were grounded or cancelled at DFW and DAL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at the Chatham Creek Apartments on Thomason Circle in Arlington. This was a two-alarm fire. Eight people were displaced from their home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into Arkansas from the northwest on June 3rd, and interacted with low pressure aloft arriving from Oklahoma. These two features headed into a moist and unstable atmosphere. Given some heating, scattered thunderstorms rapidly developed during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike took a chunk of concrete off the side column on North Little Rock High School's midsection tower.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into Arkansas from the northwest on June 3rd, and interacted with low pressure aloft arriving from Oklahoma. These two features headed into a moist and unstable atmosphere. Given some heating, scattered thunderstorms rapidly developed during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A day spa in Conway was damaged by a fire started by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms continued to erupt in an unstable environment behind the MCS that moved through north Texas on the 10th. Training cells moved across the northern portions of the Metroplex and Dallas County resulting in significant flash flooding. Numerous water rescues were needed in the Metroplex. Additional power outages continued with an estimated 500,000 customers in the Metroplex losing power from either the earlier MCS or the flooding storms on the 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a small house fire on Foxcroft Lane in Keller.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over parts of Arapahoe, Elbert, Morgan and Weld Counties.  The combination of intense thunderstorm winds, large hail and heavy rain produced damage to both crops and property.  Extensive flash flooding occurred in and around Fort Morgan.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Six children received minor injuries when lightning struck a nearby tree.  The injuries occurred when they were knocked down by the blast.  None of the children suffered burns or appeared to have been directly hit by the lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late afternoon thunderstorm tracked over Cibolo.  Lightning struck a house and caused a fire, causing significant damage to the residence. Another storm in Val Verde County produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused significant damage due to a resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms continued to erupt in an unstable environment behind the MCS that moved through north Texas on the 10th. Training cells moved across the northern portions of the Metroplex and Dallas County resulting in significant flash flooding. Numerous water rescues were needed in the Metroplex. Additional power outages continued with an estimated 500,000 customers in the Metroplex losing power from either the earlier MCS or the flooding storms on the 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning stike started a house fire in Mesquite. Minimal damage was sustained to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level disturbance continued to track from the south central U.S. toward the eastern U.S. on the north side of a large subtropical ridge in the western Gulf of Mexico.  Scattered thunderstorms developed during the early and mid-afternoon across northwest and north central Georgia and then moved southeast across north and central Georgia during the afternoon and evening.  The disturbance was slightly stronger and the air mass slightly more unstable than on the 11th.  Thus, strong to severe thunderstorms became somewhat more numerous than the previous day, but remained scattered in the north and just isolated in central areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Daily Citizen of Dalton reported that lightning caused serious injuries to a horse located at a private residence on Charlotte Drive in Dalton.  The lightning struck a tree next to which the horse was huddled during the thunderstorm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Four golfers were struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four men were golfing on the seventh green at the Cedar Ridges Golf Course in Rangely when a tree 15 to 20 yards away was struck by lightning.  The charge from the lightning bolt traveled from the tree through the ground and struck the four golfers, blowing the golf clubs out of their hands and leaving them stunned for a period of time.  They heard popping noises on the tops of their heads as the charge exited through their caps.  One of the golfers felt like the hair on his head was on fire.  The tree struck by lightning was split open and a large amount of bark was blown off.  Information in this report was provided by one of the lightning strike victims.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary frontal boundary extending from near Galesburg southeastward to Effingham during the afternoon of July 8th.  Two brief tornado touchdowns were reported in Peoria and Mason counties.  An isolated downburst caused minor wind damage in the town of Neoga in Cumberland County.  In addition, a heavy downpour caused street flooding in Mattoon in Coles County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An employee at WMCI radio in Mattoon was injured when lightning struck the radio station tower. The employee was indoors, working on radio transmission equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS moved through north Texas causing significant damage to areas generally along and north of Interstate 20. Significant and widespread tree, fence and power line damage was reported along the path of the MCS. In addition, three tornadoes touched down in the northern portions of the DFW Metroplex. Approximately 250,000 people were left without power in the Metroplex and hundreds of flights were grounded or cancelled at DFW and DAL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A recently built home on Centerboard Lane near Eagle Mountain Lake was completely destroyed in a fire started by lightning. All new appliances, furniture, and entertainment systems were lost.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm unstable air mass, and several upper level disturbances, helped spark a multi-day period of strong to severe thunderstorms.  Several clusters of thunderstorms, including apparent derechos, caused widespread wind damage and isolated reports of large hail across central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at the Alabama Department of Transportation office in Talladega caused considerable damage, both to the outdoor grounds and to equipment on the inside.  The lightning apparently struck a flag pole in front of the building, and then ran down the pole into the ground.  The underground current created a small ditch and blew out a portion of a concrete sidewalk.  From there it continued into the building, burning down an awning, blowing out a window, and ultimately frying several pieces of computer equipment.  Damage to the grounds was estimated around $2000 to $3000 dollars, with the computer equipment between $10,000 and $20,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms continued to erupt in an unstable environment behind the MCS that moved through north Texas on the 10th. Training cells moved across the northern portions of the Metroplex and Dallas County resulting in significant flash flooding. Numerous water rescues were needed in the Metroplex. Additional power outages continued with an estimated 500,000 customers in the Metroplex losing power from either the earlier MCS or the flooding storms on the 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two lightning strikes hit the Dallas pumping station causing the failure of one of the pumps that is responsible for parts of west Dallas. This failure exacerbated flooding in neighborhoods around Hampton Road and Canada Drive. Some evacuations were performed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms moved south down the Florida peninsula during the early morning hours of June 23 in association with a strong mid level low pressure trough. This cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms swept across southeast Florida during the morning hours causing widespread high winds and damage. Over 30,000 customers lost power in southeast Florida during this morning event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and caused it fall and light on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across Southern New England providing lift for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area.  Strong instability across the state of Connecticut as well as deep layer shear resulted in many of these storms to become severe.  One of these storms produced a weak tornado (EF1) that moved across the community of Wethersfield.  Numerous trees were downed, including one that split a house in half when it fell.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms erupted along the dryline just west of north Texas in the mid afternoon hours. These severe storms merged into a large HP supercell that moved southeast from Comanche County through Lampasas County. Winds up to 70 mph and hail up to baseball size was common with this supercell. A home in Lampasas County sustained significant damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Caradan man was struck by lightning that hit a nearby television pole, traveled through the ground and up his body. He was hospitalized for approximately 24 hours but not seriously injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over western Fresno County during the evening of June 4th, and rapidly grew in intensity. One severe thunderstorm had a reflectivity of 73 dBz, and a VIL (vertically integrated liquid) of 43 g/kg. Hail up to an inch in diameter fell near the town of Helm, and outflow winds were estimated at around 60 mph.||The low finally moved onshore on the 5th, and lifted northeast into northern Nevada that evening. An upper-level trough remained over California, with an unseasonably cold airmass aloft. Upper-level impulses moving through the trough continued the threat of afternoon and evening mountain convection, with isolated light showers drifting over the San Joaquin Valley at times. Temperatures fell to some 10-15 degrees below normal, and stayed well below normal for the next week.||The Grouse wildfire that was sparked by lightning on May 30th continued through the month of June. The ignition time was 1400 PST on May 30th, the location was 3 miles southwest of Yosemite Valley in Mariposa County.  The size of the fire was 3047 acres. The cost to containment was $2.9 million. The containment date was July 13th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A utility pole was struck by lightning and set on fire near Caruthers.

A few strong to severe thunderstorms developed across the region as well, producing strong and damaging wind gusts.  The atmosphere across the region again was very saturated with moisture and with just a little heating and a frontal boundary bisecting the region, scattered to numerous thunderstorms were the result across the region.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front entered the state during night of the 2nd into the early morning hours of the 3rd.  The airmass became unstable ahead of the front, though not as unstable as is typically the case in early August.  CAPE values were in the 2000 to 4000 J/kg range with lifted indices around -6 C.  Precipitable water values were generally three quarters of an inch to one inch.  During the day temperatures warmed into the 80s with dew points generally in the upper 50s to mid 60s.  Dew points pooled just ahead of the front and were between 65 and 70.  The freezing level was quite high, between 14,500 and 15,000 feet.  Thunderstorms developed over southeast South Dakota and northwest Iowa during the evening.  They moved southeast and accelerated to around 50 MPH during the late night and early morning hours.  Many of the storms produced hail, however hail was generally around an inch or less in diameter.  One and one quarter inch diameter hail fell in Clarke County, northeast of Osceola.  One of the stronger clusters of storms produced quarter to golf fall size hail in a swath from Schleswig to Denison in Crawford County.  The hail stripped leaves from trees and caused extensive crop damage.  Strong winds were produced as the storms moved into the northwest part of the Des Moines CWA.  Considerable tree and power line damage occurred in Pocahontas, Humboldt, Webster, and Carroll Counties.  Reports indicated that power was knocked out to about 10,000 homes.  As the storms moved through Story County, lightning struck a house northeast of Nevada.  A power pole was struck and the power line was on the house.  A fire resulted causing some damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass was in place on the 21st ahead of a cold front. This resulted in the development of some thunderstorms from west to east, some of which were strong to locally severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in Penn Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep moisture was lifting back over the area from the south allowing for scattered afternoon thunderstorms to develop along sea breeze and outflow boundaries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two women were struck by lightning during a storm that moved over Cape Coral. One 40-year-old woman felt lightning move through her arm as she was holding an umbrella next to a truck. Another 34-year-old woman felt lightning come through her keyboard while she was on her computer. Both were transported to the hospital in stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms propagated off the mountains and into the Roosevelt area late in the afternoon Saturday.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lake patrol at Roosevelt Lake reported a lightning strike that caused a brief power outage at the marina. A small shed was also damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As of approximately 1730 EST a generally west to east warm front extended from roughly the Kansas City Metro area to near Indianapolis. Storms spread eastward with time across Indiana where ample instability/shear could be found across the central third of the state, an important ingredient for severe weather. Tornado watch number 309 was issued by the Storm Prediction Center at 1840 EST.  Hail, wind, and flood reports were received in Indiana during this watch.  During the 2030 to 2230 EST time frame the radar trend showed some decrease in storm intensity. The National Weather Service in Indianapolis began cancelling portions of the tornado watch in their area of responsibility at 2233 EST in west central Indiana and concluded with cancellation of counties in east central Indiana at 0102 EST on May 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Abundant lightning strikes associated with a squall line apparently started a house fire at approximately 2223 EST in Flora, Indiana.  Three occupants apparently were unable to escape and perished in the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent cold front brought thunderstorms to Fairfield County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the properties at 144 Bennett Street and 35 London Terrace within minutes of each other, causing fires at both locations.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large complex of thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front swept across central Illinois from the late evening of July 24th into the early morning hours of the 25th.  Thunderstorm wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph accompanied the storms, producing widespread wind damage across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a house, causing a fire in the attic. Four people in the house escaped without injury. The fire was contained in the attic and did minor damage to second floor rooms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms moved across Missouri and Illinois into central and southern Indiana. Storms produced high winds and heavy rain. Rain of 4 to more than 6 inches fell in portions of central and southern Indiana on Wednesday and Thursday morning. This was the biggest rain the area has seen since June 2008. This rain did flood numerous county and a few state roads in central and southern Indiana. At least 4 vehicles attempted to go through flooded roads and did not make it. The biggest rain reported was 6.25 inches on the north side of Bloomington. Monroe���Morgan���Owen���Daviess and southern Marion Counties all had locations that measured 4 or more inches of rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is believed to be the cause of a house fire on East County Road 700 South.  A male occupant apparently was able to make it to the back door but not able to open it and was overcome by smoke.  While being treated by emergency personnel he stopped breathing and could not be revived.  Damage cost is grossly estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough induced scattered severe thunderstorms across Northeast New Jersey. Some of the storms also produced very heavy rain which led to flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple buildings in Elizabeth were struck by Lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of high pressure on the 18th was off the Mid Atlantic coast, while a cold front was well off to the west. In between these two systems was a surface trough, which helped to focus showers and thunderstorms within a warm and humid air mass. The thunderstorms, some severe, marched across the region during the evening hours. The combination of high winds and lightning caused about 27,500 homes and businesses to lose power in Berks County and southeastern Pennsylvania. Power was not fully restored until the 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the ensuing fire damaged a home in Lansdowne Borough.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a home, leaving a gaping hole during heavy rain. Firefighters were called about 7 PM EST. The lightning sparked an attic fire that took about 20 minutes to put out, according to the fire chief. The rest of the home had smoke and water damage.  Time of event is approximate.  Damage cost is grossly estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak stationary front was draped across central Georgia, with a moist easterly upslope flow evident north of the stalled front across north Georgia. As was the case much of the summer of 2009, northwest flow aloft remained in place across the southeast U.S. thanks to a mean, nearly stationary trough or upper low anchored across the northeast U.S.  Numerous pre-existing convective outflow boundaries provided ample support for scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop across the region during the afternoon and evening.  While none of the storms became severe, frequent cloud-to-ground lightning was observed with most of the storms.  Two lightning-related fires occurred in the Atlanta metropolitan area during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The John's Creek Herald reported that lightning struck a home on Quail Brook in the John's Creek community, just southeast of Alpharetta.  No specific damage information was provided.

Two lightning-related fires occurred in the Atlanta metropolitan area during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post of Lawrenceville reported that lightning struck a home in the 1800 block of Pine Road igniting two small fires.  The fires were quickly extinguished leaving only minor damage to the structure.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Silverdale Borough and caused a fire. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front arriving from the west late in the day on the 2nd moved into a warm and moist air mass, which resulted in strong to severe thunderstorms across the area, around the Trenton area during the early morning and across a larger area of the state during the late morning and early afternoon of the 2nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning and the ensuing fires destroyed two homes on Jacobs Creek Road and Stevens Oaks Lane within Ewing Township. No injuries were reported, but two dogs and a cat perished within the home on Jacobs Creek Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front arriving from the west late in the day on the 2nd moved into a warm and moist air mass, which resulted in strong to severe thunderstorms across the area, around the Trenton area during the early morning and across a larger area of the state during the late morning and early afternoon of the 2nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a home at the intersection of Argonne Avenue and Claude Street. Damage was confined to the roof and no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An occluded front coupled with shortwave energy moving through associated with a vigorous upper low over the Great Lakes, combined to produce an isolated severe thunderstorm over New London County, CT.  Training of cells also caused severe flash flooding.  Mesonet sites at Cutler Middle School in Mystic and Wheeler Middle/High School in North Stonington reported 6 1/2 inches and 5 3/4 inches of rainfall respectively.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole at the corner of Mason and Lewis Streets in Greenwich.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating and lots of moisture was enough to trigger hit and miss showers and thunderstorms on the 18th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a radio station, destroying the satellite receiver and damaging several other pieces of electronic equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusual weather pattern was in place for July.  A fairly active west to northwest flow was evident across the southern United States with a broad upper low in place across the Great Lakes and New England.  A cold front extended from Texas into the Tennessee Valley and served as a focusing mechanism for shower and thunderstorm development in a warm, moist air mass present to the south of the front across Georgia and Alabama.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed and moved east-southeast across the area during the afternoon and evening hours.  A few of these storms became severe producing damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Troup County 911 Center reported that lightning struck and set a storage building on fire.  The building was located on Teaver Street in the southwest part of La Grange.  While significant damage occurred to the structure, it was not totally destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast-moving line of thunderstorms entered northern Arkansas during the wee hours of the 5th. Initially, mainly hail occurred.  However, as the line swept rapidly southward, wind damage became the main severe weather event, especially from central into eastern Arkansas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A natural gas line was damaged by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several lines of showers and thunderstorms formed in Ohio and West Virginia. Surface dew points were in the low and mid 70s.  The less organized clusters, that were in West Virginia, began to train along a portion of the Interstate 64 corridor during the evening.  This area was already wet from previous rains.  The downpours tended to build west from Putnam County back into Cabell County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Mason County 911 center.  An employee standing outside, was unsure whether the lightning hit the tower, the metal roof, or the lightning rods on top of the roof. ||The lightning knocked out the center's radio and telephone communiciations, as well as its computer and security system.  The center worked out of a mobile unit for about a week.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure approached the region from the Plains, and provided hot and mostly dry weather in the few days leading up to this event. Clusters of storms tended to form to the north of Arkansas around the high. Cool outflow from one of these clusters worked southward toward the Arkansas and Missouri border during the afternoon of the 10th. Storms tapered off in the northern half of Arkansas after midnight, but precipitation became widespread in the southwest.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning killed one cow and two steers on a farm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms over southwest North Dakota resulted in two separate reported damaging lightning strikes during the evening hours of July 7th.  Multiple hay bales were burned resulting in several thousand dollars in damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two separate lightning strikes ignited hay bales near Richardton and Gladstone in Stark County. Eighty bales of hay were lost near Richardton, and one bale of hay was lost near Gladstone.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An old mesoscale convective vortex spawned numerous showers and thunderstorms over western North Carolina. A few of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds. Severe urban flooding developed during the evening hours on the south side of Charlotte.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at a business on W Airline Ave.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A backdoor cold front was edging westward across Georgia as a deep closed upper low remained anchored off the mid-Atlantic coast.  The front served as a focusing mechanism for scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours.  Many of these storms produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  A few became severe and produced marginally severe hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pike County 911 Center reported that a home on Fossett Road was struck by lightning.  No fire was reported and damage was minimal.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak stationary front caused isolated to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms for several days across Central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A female was struck by lightning on Bouldin Dam Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of south central and southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Church was struck by lightning on Sycamore Avenue in Sedley.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The summer of northwest flow aloft continued with a strong subtropical ridge across the southwestern U.S. and a deep upper trough in the northeastern U.S.  A cold front was approaching north Georgia from the Tennessee valley.  Isolated thunderstorms developed across north Georgia during the afternoon and evening producing frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  None of the storms were observed to have become severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett Daily Post reported that lightning struck a two-story home on Castle Royal Drive.  The home sustained significant damage from the resulting fire.  A family of five was displaced as a result of this lightning-related fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of south central and southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A couple of trees were on fire due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced damaging winds and large hail in southwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heating and lots of moisture were enough to trigger hit and miss showers and thunderstorms on the 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Second Street, melting two attic wind turbines and starting a small fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Large-scale atmospheric lift and wind shear associated with a short wave trough combined with an unstable air mass over the region to produce rotating thunderstorms that produced large hail over southern Wisconsin during the afternoon hours of July 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 44-year-old woman was struck by lightning while standing in the doorway of a barn holding the reins of a horse.  She was taken to Beloit Memorial Hospital and treated in the emergency department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front and two storms became severe in Eastland and Johnson County. Lightning also claimed the life of a 19 year old female in Tarrant County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pregnant female at 7:30 pm CDT as she crossed a residential street after exiting her car. The unborn child died soon after the strike and the mother died in the hospital three days later on August 30th at 4:44 PM CDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper trough was digging southward from the Great Lakes toward the southeast.  This was pushing a cold front toward Georgia from the northwest.  Southwest to northeast oriented bands of thunderstorms developed across mainly north central and northwest Georgia during the afternoon and evening.  These thunderstorms brought heavy rainfall of two to four inches in some north central and northwest Georgia counties.  One storm in Gilmer county produced damaging wind gusts.  Considerable cloud-to-ground lightning was observed with these thunderstorms, resulting in several house fires in the north Atlanta metropolitan area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee Tribune reported that lightning struck a home on Eagle Drive in the Towne Lake area near Canton.  A fire resulted, beginning in the floor truss between the first and second floors of the home.  The fire was quickly extinguished.  The home suffered minor damage to the exterior walls.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening hours, and one produced a lightning stike that damaged the Leesville 911 Center.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Public reported the Leesville 911 Center was struck by lightning and knocked offline briefly.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked an oil tank fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited an oil tank approximately 12-ft in diameter and 25-ft high.

These thunderstorms brought heavy rainfall of two to four inches in some north central and northwest Georgia counties.  One storm in Gilmer county produced damaging wind gusts.  Considerable cloud-to-ground lightning was observed with these thunderstorms, resulting in several house fires in the north Atlanta metropolitan area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee Tribune reported that lightning struck a home on Barron Road in the Salacoa Valley area north of Waleska.  The fire burned the kitchen and attic.  The remainder of the home suffered extensive smoke, heat, and water damage.  The contents of the home were ruined.  No injuries were reported, however.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving frontal boundary, caused thunderstorms to last into the night of the 12th across Eastern Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a home on West White Street in Lehighton shattered its chimney and scattered cement blocks fifty feet around the home. One cement block made a ten inch hole in the home's roof. The lightning strike also damaged the electrical wiring within the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary frontal boundary draped along the I-74 corridor triggered slow-moving thunderstorms across east-central Illinois during the evening of August 27th.  Two to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time across western Champaign County, producing flash flooding in the city of Champaign. One thunderstorm produced a lightning strike which damaged a house in the city of Savoy.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm, with very heavy rainfall also produced a lightning strike which started a fire at a house near Savoy. The fire started on the roof and spread to the attic and ceiling of the uppermost floor of the house. Three people were in the house at the time of the lightning strike, and they all escaped uninjured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary in concert with a weak upper level disturbance erupted strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of central and south-central Kansas during the afternoon and evening hours of the 26th. Winds to 60 mph were measured at the Russell Airport in Russell county, and dime to nickel size hail occurred across portions of Harper, Kingman and Reno counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rural home a few miles east of Arkansas City was destroyed by fire after being hit by lightning during the early morning hours. No one was injured. The Winfield Daily Courier contributed to this report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass was in place on the 21st ahead of a cold front. This resulted in the development of some thunderstorms from west to east, some of which were strong to locally severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in Sadsbury Township. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unstable northwest flow aloft persisted across the area.  A cold front continued to slowly approach from the northwest.  However, a pre-frontal trough was located across northeast and north central Georgia.  This feature served as a focusing mechanism for scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon and evening, especially across east central and central Georgia.  A few of the thunderstorms became marginally severe and produced penny-sized hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Emanuel County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a power pole and set it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper trough, located across the eastern U.S., was helping to push a strong cold front into the southeast U.S.  Unseasonably cool air was noted behind the front.  With a warm, humid unstable air mass ahead of the front, scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across northwest Georgia during the afternoon and moved southeast into the remainder of north and parts of central Georgia during the evening hours.  Many of these thunderstorms produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and a few became severe.  Several homes in the Atlanta area were struck by lightning and one person was injured from a lightning strike in Paulding county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Paulding County Emergency Management Director reported that at least nine homes across the county were struck by lightning.  Two of these lightning strikes resulted in fires and damage to the structures.  In addition, one individual approximately three miles north-northeast of New Georgia was injured as a result of a lightning strike.  Lightning also struck a power line approximately three miles north-northeast of New Georgia in the southern part of the county, causing the power line to fall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds at several locations in northwest Iowa during the late afternoon and early evening of August 19th. The reprted wind damage was confined to trees. Damage was also caused by a lightning strike which started a house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire. The fire started in a wall between two rooms, with fire and smoke damage resulting.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level impulse in conjunction with a slow-moving cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms across central Illinois during the afternoon of August 17th.  Despite modest instability, a few of the storms became severe and produced gusty winds. One thunderstorm in Springfield produced a lightning strike which damaged a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house in the city of Springfield was struck by lightning, which caused a fire in the upper level of the structure. Four people were in the house, but they all escaped without injury. The damage was confined to the attic and rooms on the second floor of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning injured a bicyclist in Boulder and sparked a fire in a wheat field near Deer Trail.  A severe thunderstorm also produced strong winds in Arapahoe County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman riding her bike in training for an Ironman Triathalon was struck by lightning.  She was in the 78th mile of a 100-mile training ride when she was hit.  Initially, she lost her vision and couldn't move her arms.  After a short stay in the hospital, she made a full recovery.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning injured a bicyclist in Boulder and sparked a fire in a wheat field near Deer Trail.  A severe thunderstorm also produced strong winds in Arapahoe County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire which charred approximately 1000 acres of wheat stubble.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced heavy rain, large hail and damaging thunderstorm winds over parts of the Urban Corridor and Northeast Plains.  In addition, lightning killed a horse in Boulder County and sparked a fire in Adams County.  Heavy rain also produced a flash flood in Logan County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited two oil tanks near Bennett.  It took 18,000 gallons of water and foam to put out the fires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northwest flow aloft persisted across the area.  Weak disturbances were embedded within the flow.  A cold front was slowly approaching from the northwest as well.  With a warm, unstable air mass in place across the region, yet another day of scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms was observed across north and central Georgia.  A few of the storms became severe producing marginally severe hail.  One or two of the storms produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fox 5 TV of Atlanta relayed a report from the Gwinnett County Fire and Rescue Department of a lightning-related injury to a 15-year old female.  The teenage female was injured by a nearby lightning strike in the 200 block of Club Lakes Parkway of Lawrenceville.  The young female suffered numbness to her back and legs as a result of the lightning strike.  She was transported to a local medical facility, then treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer in Galva, IL around 1214 pm August 7.  A power outage was observed on the southeast side of town.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer in Galva, IL around 1214 pm August 7.  A power outage was observed on the southeast side of town.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced severe weather across northwestern Arkansas during the late afternoon through evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a piano workshop and resulted in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced heavy rain, large hail and damaging thunderstorm winds over parts of the Urban Corridor and Northeast Plains.  In addition, lightning killed a horse in Boulder County and sparked a fire in Adams County.  Heavy rain also produced a flash flood in Logan County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a 2-yr old horse at Colorado Horse Rescue's Longmont farm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical and very unstable airmass was in place across the area. An upper level disturbance moved over the region ahead of a slow moving cold front Friday afternoon on August 21st, triggering widespread severe thunderstorms across Litchfield County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Munger Lane in Bethlehem, near the Morris line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical and very unstable airmass was in place across the area. An upper level disturbance moved over the region ahead of a slow moving cold front Friday afternoon on August 21st, triggering widespread severe thunderstorms across Litchfield County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Milton Road in Litchfield was struck by lightning.

Southwest to northeast oriented bands of thunderstorms developed across mainly north central and northwest Georgia during the afternoon and evening. Considerable cloud-to-ground lightning was observed with these thunderstorms, resulting in several house fires in the north Atlanta metropolitan area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Atlanta-Journal Constitution reported that lightning struck a home on Lenora Church Road at Lee Road, just south of Snellville.  The resulting fire, which started in the bedroom, was quickly extinguished.  However, the remainder of the home suffered extensive heat and smoke damage.  The three occupants escaped uninjured.

Southwest to northeast oriented bands of thunderstorms developed across mainly north central and northwest Georgia during the afternoon and evening. EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Atlanta-Journal Constitution reported that lightning struck a home in the 7000 block of River Island Circle.  A portion of the roof and an exterior wall were set on fire before the fire was extinguished.  The structure suffered minor structural damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms broke out across the Northeast Plains of Colorado.  The hardest hit areas were in Morgan, Logan and Weld Counties.  Hail up to softball size was reported in Morgan County, while hail up to golfball size occurred in Logan and Weld Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a very large tree in southwest Denver.  The tree fell on fences and knocked down power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure ridging across the area allowed for afternoon and evening thunderstorms to develop along sea breeze and outflow boundaries causing strong gusty winds and numerous lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Toys R Us store and caused minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure ridging across the area allowed for afternoon and evening thunderstorms to develop along sea breeze and outflow boundaries causing strong gusty winds and numerous lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure ridging across the area allowed for afternoon and evening thunderstorms to develop along sea breeze and outflow boundaries causing strong gusty winds and numerous lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Delacado Resort on Sunset Beach and caused minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northward moving warm front during the morning of the 9th, helped produce some heavy rain. As the region became entrenched in the warm sector during the day, this helped to ignite thunderstorms through the evening of the 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and the ensuing fire displaced a family of four from their Meadowcrest Lane home in Amity Township. Lightning struck the corner of the home and then traveled through an air duct. It took four fire companies fifteen minutes to extingusih the blaze, but the house suffered smoke and water damage. The damage was estimated at $30,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the northwestern South Plains of west Texas during the evening hours of the 18th. These storms eventually spread southward over the western and central South Plains. At least one isolated storm displayed supercellular structure as it impacted the Dimmitt vicinity in Castro County. This storm produced giant hail and damaging winds. A broad area of strong winds developed in the wake of the convective complex over the western South Plains, and a localized and brief severe gradient wind gust was measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet in Yoakum County. Renewed convective development occurred over the Rolling Plains after midnight CST. Severe storms, including a few supercells, produced large hail over portions of King and Stonewall Counties during the very early morning hours of the 19th. Significant agricultural losses were reported in Stonewall County, where between 1,500 and 2,000 acres of cotton were destroyed near Peacock.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole at the intersection of Slide Road and 98th Street in southwest Lubbock. As a result of the lightning strike, the top of the pole broke off and utility lines fell across 98th Street. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms moved south down the Florida peninsula during the early morning hours of June 23 in association with a strong mid level low pressure trough. This cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms swept across southeast Florida during the morning hours causing widespread high winds and damage. Over 30,000 customers lost power in southeast Florida during this morning event.
