EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm, moist, and unstable airmass was in place over Iowa from 8th into the 9th.  Surface temperatures on the 8th warmed into the upper 80s and 90s, with dew point readings in the 70s.  A weak cold front moved into the state during the evening of the 8th and early morning of the 9th.  There was little thunderstorm development initially as the airmass was capped.  Temperatures at the 700 mb level were +14 to +17 C.   During the early morning hours of the 9th, a short wave lifted northeast out of the southern Rockies.  This resulted in cooling of the mid levels of the atmosphere, thus destabilizing the airmass.  The cold front stall out during the morning of the 9th as a second short wave lifted northast.   Eventually, the front moved south of the state on the night of the 9th.  Overall lifted indices were in the -6 to -10 C range with CAPE values in the 3000 to 4000 J/kg range.  Downdraft CAPE was in the 800 to 1400 J/kg range with 30 to 50 kts of shear available.  CAOE available in the -10 to -30 C layer of the atmosphere was between 300 and 700 J/kg, with a freezing level of 14,000 to 14,500 feet.  The LCL was relatively high across the area ranging from just below 1000 meters to about 1250 meters.  Plenty of moisture was available with precipitable water values between 1.75 and 2.25 inches.  Thunderstorms developed initially over Nebraska and tracked east-northeast into Iowa shortly after sunrise.  One supercell continued to track across the state and produced a swath of wind and hail damage from Sac County east to Black Hawk County.  Additional thunderstorms formed along the cold frontal boundary by mid morning and progressed into the state.  The storms remained below severe levels for several hours, but did become severe by mid afternoon.  A broken like of storms formed with two primary areas tracking east across central and southern Iowa.  These two areas featured mini bow echoes.  The predominant mode of severe weather in the afternoon was high winds.  Several of the storms produced hail, but the hail was sub-severe.  A long lived supercell Thunderstorm tracked across northern Iowa Sunday morning with the Highway 20 corridor receiving the brunt of the damage.  Reports of quarter to golf ball sized hail were common with some hail stones reported to be in excess of two inches approaching the size of a tennis ball.  The hail was wind blown as well, at speeds of 50 to 70 mph, making it extremely damaging and dangerous striping siding off houses and knocking out windows.   A measured wind speed of 68 mph was recorded at a KCCI TV SchoolNet site near Jewell in Hamilton County.   Significant hail damage was received all along the track with areas near Otho, Callender, Radcliffe, Eldora and Grundy Center hit particularly hard.  In Eldora, many homes had windows broken out and tree and power line damage left the city without power. Winds of over 100 MPH toppled a communication tower in Eldora.  A short time before the winds hit Eldora, a 102 MPH wind gust was recorded at the landfill northwest of town.  Wind driven hail of 2 to 3 inches in diameter broke all siding and windows out on the north and west walls of most homes, with hail stones reported landing inside of houses.  Damage in the town of Eldora was expected to be greater than the damage done in the town of Parkersburg by the EF5 tornado a year earlier.  A 150 square mile area of crops was affected in Hardin County.  Total losses were reported on 45,000 acres, with 60% or greater loss on another 55,000 acres.  Hail damage in the Otho to Callender areas was described as the worst seen in 20 years.  MODIS satellite pictures of the crop damage area included in this report.  Estimates of crop damage from this one supercell were over $175,000,000.  Governor Culver declared Hardin County a state disaster area within a day or two of the storm, and declared Webster County a disaster area about a week later.  Formal paperwork was turned in to make 8 Iowa counties federal disaster areas,  They were Calhoun, Grundy, Hamilton, Hardin, Ida, Sac, Webster, and Woodbury.  Following the storms, a shelter was set up for those who felt they should not stay in their homes. Luckily the evening round of storms tracked south. Campers at nearby Pine Lake State Park, gathered for an archery event, were bruised by hail.  There were 22 reports of injuries in Hardin County, 11 serious enough for people to be taken to hospital, but there are no known life threatening injuries.  A second round of severe weather rolled roughly along I-80 between 1630 and 1800 CST, producing a lot of tree and power line damage but apparently little structural damage.  As the storms moved through the metropolitan Des Moines area, winds damaged power lines and knocked out power to 12,000 homes.  One storm produced a wet microburst in Union County.  The winds took the roof and shingles off of a two story brick building near Afton.  The afternoon round of storms produced some hail, but most of the hail was not severe as mentioned above, and was pea size or smaller.  During the morning round of storms, lightning struck a building in Waverly.  The lightning struck an antenna on the building and melted screws all the way down the side of the building, starting a small fire and blowing hole in the wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several factors led to severe hail development across portions of Minnesota Tuesday afternoon, July 21st. These factors included a strong disturbance, a low freezing level, and a weak frontal boundary which caused numerous thunderstorms to develop and produce hail as large as golf ball size. In addition to the hail, frequent lightning strikes led to an individual being struck by lightning under a tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14 year old girl was struck by lightning as she played under a tree during a thunderstorm. She later died at a hospital from her injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another day of the wet season in South Florida produce more lightning damage along with hail and high wind gust reports.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a plumbing stack of a house near the intersection of NW 165 Street and NW 30th Avenue, and a neighbor heard the loud thunder and saw smoke coming from the house. The neighbor then called 911. A fire started in the kitchen and the firefighters put out the fire. No one was home at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another day of the wet season in South Florida produce more lightning damage along with hail and high wind gust reports.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a gas station in Miramar blowing a hole in the roof and knocking out power. The gas station attendant saw the flash and heard the thunder, but was not injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil battery.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil battery, heavily damaging two large oil tanks and other equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms developed near a stalled frontal boundary across the central portions of the state. Isolated events of damaging winds occurred in Bell and Coryell counties. More significant damage occurred to four RVs in Johnson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An unsold house on Jewel Lane near Stillhouse Hollow Lake was destroyed by a fire started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS moved through north Texas causing significant damage to areas generally along and north of Interstate 20. Significant and widespread tree, fence and power line damage was reported along the path of the MCS. In addition, three tornadoes touched down in the northern portions of the DFW Metroplex. Approximately 250,000 people were left without power in the Metroplex and hundreds of flights were grounded or cancelled at DFW and DAL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fort Worth Fire Deparment responded to a total of 7 structure fires during this MCS event: a commercial building on the 1100 block of North Sylvania Avenue, a residence in the 10300 block of Vintage Drive, a residence in the 1800 block of Marlene Drive, a residence in the 3800 block of Buckhorn Place, a residence in the 4500 block of East Loop 820, a residence at Wilbarger Street and Martin Luther King Freeway, and a residence at Shadydell Drive and Boat Club Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A second cold frontal passage in as many days helped trigger strong to severe thunderstorms across the northern half of New Jersey during the evening of the 17th. Thousands of homes and businesses lost power. There were still about 1,000 homes and businesses without power in the hardest hit counties of Hunterdon, Morris and Somerset Counties on the 18th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire in Hanover Township. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and thunderstorms moved from west to east across the region, producing moderate to heavy rainfall during the early morning hours.  Areal Flood Warnings were issued for a number of counties in Central Indiana.  Also, a child was fatally struck by lightning at a Perry Township campground, just south of Indianapolis.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A ten year old boy was killed and two others were injured while fishing at a campground at 4141 West Southport Road, Indianapolis, Indiana.  This was the first death due to lightning in the state for 2009.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure ridging across the area allowed for scattered afternoon thunderstorms to develop along sea breeze and outflow boundaries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck in a soccer field as a church group was in the midst of a game and nearby picnic. This strike was a bolt from the blue as there was no rain in the immediate area.  Radar detected the core of the storm to be six miles to the south of the location.  Eighteen victims were transported to area hospitals where one died from his injuries.  Another nine victims were treated on-site with symptoms consistent with a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm complex that developed north of low pressure in north central Kansas merged with thunderstorms that developed north of a warm front that was along the Kansas and Nebraska border.  With temperatures in the 70s and dew point temperatures around 70 near the front and low, instability was moderately high.  Initially the thunderstorms that developed north of the warm front produced a few large hail reports.  However, as the storms to the west merged with the activity farther east the main severe weather reports consisted of strong winds, especially from one cluster of storms that rolled from Saline and Gage county east into the southeast corner of Nebraska.  Around 12,000 customers lost their power from the storm, mostly from Lincoln and locations southwest through southeast of town.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 50-year-old tree causing it topple onto a house and car causing extensive damage to each.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold frontal system moved southeastward through Middle Tennessee, and upper level disturbances continued to move across the mid state in upper level northwesterly flow, thunderstorms developed during the early morning through afternoon hours. Some of these thunderstorms contained heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding while there was one report of lightning causing damage also.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a three story home at 2225 Austin Bottom Road, causing a blaze in the basement of the home. Details concerning amount of damage to basement of home unknown. No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front retreating to the north and a cold front approaching from the west produced strong to severe thunderstorms across New Jersey during the afternoon and early evening of the 29th. One EF-2 tornado also occurred. The wind damage and lightning resulted in about 57,000 homes and businesses in losing power.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in Sayreville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold front approached and moved through Middle Tennessee during the morning through late evening hours, the atmosphere became increasingly unstable. With the aid of daytime heating and passage of upper level disturbances, thunderstorms developed across the mid state as a result. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging thunderstorm winds, heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding, and lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Norris Body Shop was destroyed when it was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms swept southeastward over the South Plains region of west Texas during the evening hours of the 29th. These storms resulted in widespread severe wind gusts. Damage across the region was generally limited to downed tree limbs and utilities, however, a segment of the convective complex that moved over the extreme southeastern Panhandle produced extreme wind gusts that caused significant structural damage. These winds resulted in the partial collapse of a brick structure in Estelline (Hall County). More significant damage occurred as the winds spread into Childress (Childress County), where a number of buildings were heavily damaged including three local hotels, a hospital, and the high school as measured wind gusts reached 102 mph. Three people were injured and economic losses across the region exceeded $2.2 million.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apartment complex was struck by lightning around midnight CST on the 29th. The strike caused a fire which displaced several tenants. No injuries were reported, but significant damages occurred to the apartment unit.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a frontal system moved northeastward from Middle Tennessee into the Ohio River Valley, the atmosphere became increasingly unstable, and with the influences of daytime heating and passages of upper level disturbances, thunderstorms developed from the early afternoon and lasted well into the evening hours. Several thunderstorms produced damaging thunderstorm winds while two reports of lightning damage occurred also.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: About 200 households lost power in northern portions of Clarksville when the Edgeton substation was struck by lightning.  Power lines and transformers associated with the substation were damaged also.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough followed by a potent cold front caused multiple severe thunderstorms some of which produced flash flooding across Northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a chimney at 309 Ann Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough followed by a potent cold front caused multiple severe thunderstorms some of which produced flash flooding across Northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck 4 persons under a tree outside the Ivy Hill Apartments on Mount Vernon Place, killing one and injuring 3 others.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary draped from northeast to southwest across the state served as the focus for convective development the afternoon of the 25th.  Large hail, with stones to the size of half dollars the largest reported. An exceptionally moist environment also allowed for a copious amount of rain to fall. Several reports of flash flooding were also noted, but no significant damage to property occurred.  One death was noted as a result of the weather during the event. A motorcyclist was struck by lightning as he rode along a local highway. Additional information regarding the fatality is included in the event narrative.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A group of seven motorcyclists riding together as members of the group Bikers Against Child Abuse were struck by lightning just before 5pm on the 25th.  One biker was killed by the strike, and the rider next to him was injured and taken to the hospital, but released later that evening. The other 5 were not injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large subtropical ridge across Texas was slowly expanding eastward.  In advance of this upper ridge, an unstable northwest flow aloft, with embedded short waves, prevailed across the eastern and southeastern U.S.  This, combined with a continuing warm and very unstable air mass, supported development of several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across the region from late on the 17th through the 18th.  The first round developed around midnight on the 17th and continued through the early morning hours.  The second round occurred during the late afternoon on the 18th.  The storms were generally confined to the eastern parts of the state with all of the storms developing within narrow northwest to southeast oriented bands.  The individual storms were also tracking from northwest to southeast within these bands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Johnson County Emergency Management Director reported that a home was struck by lightning just north of Wrightsville causing damage to the structure.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike in Pert Amboy downed a wire. The wire set two vehicles on fires. No injuries were reported.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged the bell tower on top of the Pattenburg United Methodist Church. A gaping hole was made in the top of it.

This resulted in two capstones, estimated to weigh between 250 and 300 pounds, located on the chimney's top brick layer, to topple to the roof below, crashing through it, and causing structural damage. The hole made by the capstone also allowed rainwater to cause further damage inside the school. Total affected area was less than 30 square feet.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms moved southwest to northeast across Port Aransas and Mustang Island between 1:30 PM and 3:00 PM, producing roughly 5-10 cloud to ground lightning strikes per 5 minutes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 63 year old man was struck and killed by lightning on Mustang Island Beach near Port Aransas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that damaged a garage in Sanford.  The lightning struck a tree that was a few feet from the garage and jumped to the corner of the garage roof.  The fire was contained with minimal damage to the garage and its contents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold frontal system moved into Middle Tennessee from western portions of the state and upper level disturbances moved across the mid state in northwesterly upper level flow, thunderstorms formed across the area during the evening hours. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging thunderstorm winds with two reports of lightning strikes causing damage also.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree was struck by lightning, with several large limbs falling to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the region in association with a frontal system. Some of the storms brought hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding to the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 18 year old male was struck by lightning in the Carnes Community.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Evening thunderstorms on the 18th produced reports of large hail, lightning and damaging winds across portions of south central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous lightning strikes damaged fuses in the City of Adel's electrical system.  About 350 electric customers were without power for a few hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms that moved through coastal sections of Maine was responsible for a number of fires in York and Lincoln Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged four homes in the Kennebunk area.  In one incident, lightning struck a tall pine and followed the roots to underground pipes, and then followed the pipes to three separate homes.  In one of the homes, the doors and windows were blown out and the basement filled with smoke.  The two other homes lost appliances and electronic equipment.  In another incident, lightning struck a fourth home, but the damage was minimal.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms that moved through coastal sections of Maine was responsible for a number of fires in York and Lincoln Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and followed the ground to several homes in the immediate area.  The lightning left a large hole where it entered the ground.  Appliances and electronic equipment were damaged or destroyed by the lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms that moved through coastal sections of Maine was responsible for a number of fires in York and Lincoln Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Nobleboro and ignited a fire that destroyed the home.  A homeowner was home at the time and reported sparks throughout the kitchen area.  The fire spread rapidly throughout the structure and destroyed the home.  Damage was estimated at 1.5 million dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms developed across much of southern Arizona. There were no severe weather reports in southeast Arizona, but storms did produce frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a porch of a mobile home in Picture Rocks, creating a fire. The fire spread into the home, causing damage.  One person suffered minor burn injuries to his hands and wrists while attempting to extinguish the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and early evening of the 16th. Severe storms crossed portions of Central Mississippi and Northeast Louisiana. There was 1 fatality and two injuries from a lightning strike southwest of Yazoo City. There were reports of hail, wind damage, and flash flooding due to heavy rainfall. These storms were due a cold front that moved over the region. The cold front combined with rich gulf moisture and an unstable airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three teenagers were struck by lighting on Eagle Bend Road, in southwest Yazoo County. One teenager was seriously injured and passed away a few days later on May 20th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold frontal system moved into Middle Tennessee from western portions of the state and upper level disturbances moved across the mid state in northwesterly upper level flow, thunderstorms formed across the area during the evening hours. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging thunderstorm winds with two reports of lightning strikes causing damage also.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was the result of a lightning strike at 128 Smith Lane. The bolt of lightning struck the side of the house. The bolt hit the phone and electric lines and actually blew a two-foot wide by six-inch deep hole in the yard. Several fire crews arrived on the scene and found the home with thick smoke and fire smoldering in the walls of the home. Firefighters used axes and saws to cut the walls out in order to reach the blaze.|Though the home suffered some smoke and water damage, the house and all of its contents were saved. No injuries were reported during the incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 25-year-old man was struck by lightning as he stood under an overhang of a building to stay dry from a storm.  Both of his sneakers had holes burned in them.  The man was transported to a nearby medical facility for evaluation and then released.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and unstable air mass led to the development of slow moving showers and thunderstorms over several days across Central Alabama.  The slow moving storms caused very heavy rain in some locations, which led to isolated flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house to catch fire, on CR-82 near the Hawk community, resulting in unspecified damages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed ahead of a cold front in a very unstable environment. Large hail fell from the early storms but damaging winds became the main threat as the initial storms merged into an extensive line. A downburst in northwestern Johnson County left 10 homes uninhabitable. Estimated winds in the downburst were 90-100 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a fiberglass tank at a saltwater disposal site starting a blaze. Five tanks were lost in the blaze, and the site had to be monitored by local firefighters until the next morning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed ahead of a cold front in a very unstable environment. Large hail fell from the early storms but damaging winds became the main threat as the initial storms merged into an extensive line. A downburst in northwestern Johnson County left 10 homes uninhabitable. Estimated winds in the downburst were 90-100 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on the 900 block of Condor Drive in Coppell. The brick chimney was damaged but no other information was available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoonal moisture was responsible for a thunderstorm with heavy rain west of Santa Fe, which resulted in water flowing out of an arroyo at a height of two feet.  Lightning from a thunderstorm in Rio Rancho struck and killed a 26 year old man. Six other members of his family sustained injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Jarrod Truesdale, a 26 year old man, was killed by a lightning strike in the parking lot of Rio Rancho High School before a fireworks show.  His wife, 26, was also struck and sustained serious injuries.  Their 4 kids, ranging from 18 months to 7 years in age, as well as the wife's 21 year old sister also sustained injuries.  The family was headed for their vehicle to seek shelter from the storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across mainly the western half of Middle Tennessee as the day progressed in response to deepening surface and aloft southerly flow. This was in association with a developing low pressure system over the central plains. As a result, these areas experienced flooding/flash flooding. One elderly man was killed indirectly by lightning in Marshall County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck a utility pole at the end of a 83 year old man's driveway. The lightning's charge went to the man's house and started a fire, that destroyed most of the home, and also killed the man.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered storms developed across north Texas in an unstable environment with several boundaries lying across the region. Isolated severe weather was reported in Millsap, and a lightning strike damaged a radio station in Keene.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the building that houses KJCR 88.3 Radio Station, starting a fire that heavily damaged the building. All the radio equipment was destroyed including mixing boards and the wiring relay system that sends the signal to the transmitter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A decaying frontal boundary produced widespread showers and strong to severe thunderstorms across northern Alabama.  These storms produced damaging winds and some large hail, primarily along and west of a Madison to Morgan county line. Surface dewpoints in the upper 60s to lower 70s allowed these slow moving storms to produce heavy rainfall causing flash flooding in the Huntsville metro area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire to develop at 2906 Allen Ben Road, which tragically gutted the home. This fire jumped to the house next door at 2904 Allen Ben Road causing damage to the upperstairs portion of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough followed by a potent cold front caused multiple severe thunderstorms and isolated flash flooding in portions of Southeast New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured by a lightning strike at cricket field near Avenue S and East 32nd Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the 4th, showers and thunderstorms were focused in northern Arkansas. Heavy rain fell across parts of the area with a few severe storms developing. Northern and western counties got more rain during the afternoon and evening hours of the 5th and 6th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an electric substation just north of Mountain View. Over 2500 customers lost power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm over northwest New Mexico damaged the radio transmitter on Rabbit Peak southwest of Chama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms over northwest New Mexico during the early morning hours produced a cloud to ground lightning strike that hit the 96.1 FM KZRM Radio transmitter on Rabbit Peak, just west northwest of Chama. The station was off the air for at least three weeks.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front stretched from Hartford, Connecticut across northern Rhode Island to southeast Massachusetts combined with an upper level disturbance to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England. Plenty of moisture was in place across these areas, increasing the chance for heavy rain and flooding.  A 41 year old man was killed when he was struck by lightning while digging for clams in the tidal flats of Little Pleasant Bay near Orleans.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 41 year old man was out digging for quahogs (clams) on the tidal flats of Little Pleasant Bay, a quarter mile east of Sipsons Island when he was struck by lightning and killed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level low continued to meander about the mid-Atlantic region.  A weak cold front was evident from the mid-Atlantic into the southern Appalachians.  A warm, humid air mass continued across Georgia.  The upper low once again provided the support for scattered thunderstorm development across north Georgia during the afternoon and evening hours.  A few of these storms became severe, producing marginally severe hail and damaging wind gusts.  Thunderstorms continued to drift south into east central and central Georgia after midnight, but these remained below severe limits.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Jackson Herald of Jefferson reported that a vacant home on Margie Court was struck by lightning.  The lightning strike resulted in a fire to the attic of the home.  In addition, a 10 by 10 outbuilding in the 2000 block of Jackson Trail Road was also struck by lightning and set on fire.  The structure was completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system tapped into sub-tropical moisture causing hundreds of lightning strikes in thunderstorms around the San Francisco Bay Area, California.  Nearly 50,000 Bay Area residents lost power and dozens of small fires were started.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and surrounding trees in the 300 block of Summit Avenue damaging two 200-foot-tall Redwood trees and a driveway.  Also the lightning fried the television and a video game system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system tapped into sub-tropical moisture causing hundreds of lightning strikes in thunderstorms around the San Francisco Bay Area, California.  Nearly 50,000 Bay Area residents lost power and dozens of small fires were started.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: About 47,000 residents lost power around San Francisco as thunderstorms rolled through the city/county.  The largest outage affected 36,000 customers in parts of Sunset, Glen Park and Park Merced neighborhoods.  One lightning strike hit a power transformer causing it to explode.  Besides the total destruction of the power transformer, two vehicles were damaged at the intersection of Broderick and Sacramento Roads.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the morning and afternoon hours across southwest Louisiana. One storm north of Grand Lake produced lightning which struck a boat on the Intracoastal Waterway, killing one fisherman and injuring another.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two boaters fishing on Black Bayou at the Intracoastal Waterway were struck by lightning. One man was killed and the other suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms occurred over a large part of eastern Oklahoma from the early afternoon hours into the evening hours of the 21st. The continued heavy rain across the area resulted in flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms brought about 1500 recorded lightning strikes to northern California.  One lightning strike injured a woman at a sporting event in Stockton and a number of small wildfires were started across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning while carrying a large umbrella at a softball game at the San Joaquin Regional Sports Complex in Stockton.  Additional reports suggest the lightning hit about 30 feet away from her.  The woman suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large upper level high pressure system was over the U.S. and an upper level trough was pushing offshore of the Atlantic seaboard. A quasi-stationary surface front was across north Florida and became diffuse. Scattered afternoon storms developed over an unstable airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the construction crane on the Flagler Beach Pier. Four workers received a slight electric jolt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late night thunderstorm burned down a home in St. Ignatius from a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in St. Ignatius was completely burned down and destroyed by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mrs. Dawn Yoder of Atmore, Alabama was struck and seriously injured while taking out the garbage at her residence on the morning of July 6th.  She later died on July 8th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Monday morning Dawn Yoder of Atmore was struck by lightning at her home.  She was found 10 to 15 minutes after the lightning strike by her family members and transported to the hospital where she later died on July 8th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms began to develop across portions of southern Minnesota the night of August 7th before midnight. A strong low level jet and deep moisture advection caused several waves of thunderstorms to develop along a line from near Hutchinson Minnesota, to the southern Twin Cities metro area, and into portions of west central Wisconsin. Two to four inches of rainfall was common in a 6 hour period, with locally four to six inches in a narrow band from the southwestern portions of the Twin Cities to portions of West Central Wisconsin, from Prescott to Eau Claire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree which fell on a home in Memomonie, Wisconsin and caused a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a business causing a fire and struck a vehicle injuring a storm chaser.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vehicle, injuring a storm chaser who was filming the storms as they moved through northwest Arkansas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a business causing a fire and struck a vehicle injuring a storm chaser.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a business complex in Bentonville causing a fire that damaged portions of the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid airmass was in place across the region as a weak cold front approached from the Great Lakes Region during Tuesday August 18th, triggering thunderstorms, some of which became severe during the early evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning approximately 5 miles east of Mechanicville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A remnant cold front/outflow boundary moved into Oklahoma during the early morning hours and was located from northwest into southeast Oklahoma. Instability along and near the front allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop by late morning, and continue through the afternoon. Very heavy rainfall accompanied the thunderstorms, but as the thunderstorms became more intense, large hail and damaging winds were reported. The thunderstorms moved into northern Texas by late evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught fire after being struck by lightning. Monetary damage estimates were not available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of severe thunderstorms, with embedded supercells, developed over central Missouri and moved southward across eastern portions of the Springfield County Warning Area. The thunderstorms produced severe winds up to 60mph, baseball size hail and heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damage the radio service and phone lines at the Missouri State Highway Patrol Troop G Headquarters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed in a very unstable airmass across northeast Texas, southwest Arkansas as well as northwest and north central Louisiana. This activity developed along and in the wake of a strong outflow boundary. These storms produced widespread wind damage along with spotty large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home resulting in a fire at the 6000 block of Arden Street in Shreveport.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level low pressure area persisted in the mid-south and was drifting slowly eastward.  A cold front was slowly approaching the area from the west.  Deep tropical moisture was pulled northward in advance of the upper low and cold front.  Widespread showers and thunderstorms were noted in north-south oriented bands...which drifted slowly east across the state during the day.  Some flash flooding was observed, especially in the Atlanta area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported that lightning strikes resulted in three fires in the Johns Creek area of far north Fulton county.  No significant fire-related damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two rounds of severe weather moved through central Kentucky on August 4th. The first produced torrential rainfall in the Louisville Metro area with up to seven inches of rain falling in around two hours time.  This created massive flash flooding issues across much of Jefferson County and caused millions of dollars in damage in Louisville.  This area of rainfall also caused flooding issues in counties just south and east of Jefferson County as well.  The heavy rain and thunderstorms also produced some hail and cloud to ground lightning that caused several fires, including one four-alarm apartment complex fire on the east side of Louisville. Several water rescues were performed as drivers became stranded during the first round of severe weather, which occurred during the morning rush hour.||Later in the afternoon, a line of severe thunderstorms moved into North-Central Kentucky producing damaging winds up to 75 mph along with another round of heavy rainfall which caused another round of flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn burned on Renaker Road due to a lightning strike between Berry and Cynthiana.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered thunderstorms over the North Carolina Mountains starting in the early afternoon hours. The storms organized into a slow moving mesoscale convective system as they moved across the foothills and western piedmont. Quite a bit of wind damage, and some large hail, was produced.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Summit Ridge Ln, causing extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually deep upper trough continued to progress slowly eastward across the eastern United States.  A cold front accompanied the upper trough.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms moved into the area from the west during the morning and continued to develop and increase in aerial coverage and intensity throughout the afternoon and evening.  One storm in Gwinnett county briefly became severe.  In addition, this thunderstorm also produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and several house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WSB Television of Atlanta reported that lightning strikes resulted in two house fires in the Chamblee and Tucker area of northern DeKalb county.  A two story home on Beacon Court and another two-story home on Laurel Post Court both suffered extensive damage from lightning-related fires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually deep upper trough continued to progress slowly eastward across the eastern United States.  A cold front accompanied the upper trough.  Scattered to numerous thunderstorms moved into the area from the west during the morning and continued to develop and increase in aerial coverage and intensity throughout the afternoon and evening.  One storm in Gwinnett county briefly became severe.  In addition, this thunderstorm also produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and several house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WSB Television of Atlanta reported that lightning strikes resulted in at least three house fires in the Lawrenceville area.  House fires were reported on Wildridge Drive in Duluth and San Marcos Drive and Stonebrook Court in Lawrenceville.  Significant damage was reported to the attics of each of the affected homes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated thunderstorm brought heavy rainfall and cloud to ground lightning to Floyd County in Southern Indiana.  A water rescue was performed and lightning caused a house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was started from a lightning strike on Loi Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front passing through the Wisconsin area resulted in at least one lightning stirke with damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home's chimney and started a fire in the attic and roof area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An organized complex of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front as it approached southern Illinois and southeast Missouri during the hottest and most unstable time of day. Very strong instability, coupled with moderately strong mid-level winds, resulted in a few damaging wind events with the initial complex that affected places east of a Dexter to Marble Hill line. In the wake of the initial complex, multi-cell clusters rapidly developed on the upshear side of the cold pool left by the first complex. These clusters produced several large hail events, along with isolated damaging wind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit an electrical substation, knocking out power to 1,100 customers in downtown Poplar Bluff.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the region in association with a frontal system. Gusty winds, small hail, and flash flooding were reported across the region with some of this activity.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house just south of Morton and caused a fire which burned the entire house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass was in place on the 21st ahead of a cold front. This resulted in the development of some thunderstorms from west to east, some of which were strong to locally severe during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In addition to the severe weather, two lifeguards were struck and injured by lightning at Crystal Springs in Vernon Township. They were thrown to the ground by the strike, were dazed, lost their hearing for a short while and had smoking feet.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms tended to be isolated to scattered on the 29th. All of this precipitation was the result of a relentless northwest wind flow aloft bringing storm systems and fronts into Arkansas from the Plains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 52 year-old woman was injured by lightning while selling melons at a roadside stand.  She was holding onto a metal post supporting a tent-like canopy when the lightning struck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass was in place on the 21st ahead of a cold front. This resulted in the development of some thunderstorms from west to east, some of which were strong to locally severe during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to the attic of a home on Birch Street in Boonton sparked a fire. It was brought under control in about fifteen minutes, but the home sustained water and electrical damage. Two firefighters were injured battling the blaze. The family was temporarily relocated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass was in place on the 21st ahead of a cold front. This resulted in the development of some thunderstorms from west to east, some of which were strong to locally severe during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked an underground gas fire at the intersection of Skillman Road and County Route 601 in Montgomery Township. About 200 homes and businesses lost gas service until the blaze was extinguished. The roadway was closed into the evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper low pressure area was meandering through the mid-south.  Warm, moist unstable air remained across the southeast states with a large high pressure system off the mid-Atlantic coast.  Scattered thunderstorms develop during the late afternoon across central Georgia.  Outflow boundaries from these thunderstorms pushed north during the evening, causing additional thunderstorms to develop in north Georgia.  A few of these thunderstorms became strong producing strong winds gusts.  Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning was also observed, resulting in some house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Clayton County 911 Center reported that lightning strikes resulted in two house fires in the Riverdale area.  Specific damages were not provided.  One tree was also blown down by thunderstorm winds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm complex developed ahead of a cold front in northern and central Ohio.  The storms then dropped southeast.   Wind gusts and downpours were the main threat.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were struck by lightning along Elizabeth Township Route 323.  Four people were riding all terrain vehicles, when a downpour had them seek shelter under a tree.  One of the victims said, there was no thunder or lightning. We were just trying to stay dry and the lightning just hit all at once.  One woman was knocked unconscious for about 20 minutes. The 2 females were transported by ambulance to Cabell Huntington Hospital, while the third person did not seek treatment.   The woman that was knocked unconscious checked out of the hospital with no injuries.  The other woman spent 3 days in the hospital undergoing tests.   She was still having vision problems and pain in her hands and feet.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two thunderstorm complexes moved out of southern Kentucky into Middle Tennessee as a result of strong northwesterly flow aloft. The first one moved across the Cumberland Plateau Region during the afternoon hours, while the second one moved across western and central portions of the mid state during the evening hours. Several counties received thunderstorm wind damage, mainly in the form of downed trees and building damage, and one person was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that fell on a 66 year old women, who lives about five miles southwest from Crossville on Lantana Road, as thunderstorms moved through this area.  She was rushed to a regional trauma center after she was rescued. She was trapped underneath the tree for some period of time, but was conscious during the entire event. Extent of injury and condition were not reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical and very unstable airmass was in place across the area. An upper level disturbance moved over the region ahead of a slow moving cold front Friday afternoon, August 21st, triggering widespread severe thunderstorms, mainly south and east of the Capital District.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The SpringHill Suites Hotel in Colonie was struck by lightning, leaving a hole in the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two rounds of severe weather moved through central Kentucky on August 4th. The first produced torrential rainfall in the Louisville Metro area with up to seven inches of rain falling in around two hours time.  This created massive flash flooding issues across much of Jefferson County and caused millions of dollars in damage in Louisville.  This area of rainfall also caused flooding issues in counties just south and east of Jefferson County as well.  The heavy rain and thunderstorms also produced some hail and cloud to ground lightning that caused several fires, including one four-alarm apartment complex fire on the east side of Louisville. Several water rescues were performed as drivers became stranded during the first round of severe weather, which occurred during the morning rush hour.||Later in the afternoon, a line of severe thunderstorms moved into North-Central Kentucky producing damaging winds up to 75 mph along with another round of heavy rainfall which caused another round of flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apartment caught fire after bring struck by lightning off Southside Drive and New Cut Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three rounds of thunderstorms produced wind damage and flash flooding during the afternoon, evening, and overnight hours of August 9th.  The thunderstorms developed as a cold front trailing from low pressure over northeast Wisconsin moved into a hot, humid and unstable air mass in place over southern Wisconsin.  Temperatures warmed to 85 and 90 degrees, with dew-points in the 70s.  Strong unidirectional vertical wind shear produced bowing line segments that caused damaging wind gusts.  The thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall as precipitable water values reached 1.8 to 2 inches.  All together, in just southeast Wisconsin, at least 28,000 customers lost electrical power.  It was reported that 140 power-lines came down due to tree debris, and at least a dozen or two utility poles snapped.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a business building and damaged all inside electronic equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three rounds of thunderstorms produced wind damage and flash flooding during the afternoon, evening, and overnight hours of August 9th.  The thunderstorms developed as a cold front trailing from low pressure over northeast Wisconsin moved into a hot, humid and unstable air mass in place over southern Wisconsin.  Temperatures warmed to 85 and 90 degrees, with dew-points in the 70s.  Strong unidirectional vertical wind shear produced bowing line segments that caused damaging wind gusts.  The thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall as precipitable water values reached 1.8 to 2 inches.  All together, in just southeast Wisconsin, at least 28,000 customers lost electrical power.  It was reported that 140 power-lines came down due to tree debris, and at least a dozen or two utility poles snapped.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and started a fire that resulted in a fair amount of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two rounds of severe weather moved through central Kentucky on August 4th. The first produced torrential rainfall in the Louisville Metro area with up to seven inches of rain falling in around two hours time.  This created massive flash flooding issues across much of Jefferson County and caused millions of dollars in damage in Louisville.  This area of rainfall also caused flooding issues in counties just south and east of Jefferson County as well.  The heavy rain and thunderstorms also produced some hail and cloud to ground lightning that caused several fires, including one four-alarm apartment complex fire on the east side of Louisville. Several water rescues were performed as drivers became stranded during the first round of severe weather, which occurred during the morning rush hour.||Later in the afternoon, a line of severe thunderstorms moved into North-Central Kentucky producing damaging winds up to 75 mph along with another round of heavy rainfall which caused another round of flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a four alarm apartment fire on Hurstbourne Parkway near I-64.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the attic of a home in Tallahassee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near the home and ran up the aluminum porch post to a gas line in the attic.  There were no injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper trough, located across the eastern U.S., was helping to push a strong cold front into the southeast U.S.  Unseasonably cool air was noted behind the front.  With a warm, humid unstable air mass ahead of the front, scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across northwest Georgia during the afternoon and moved southeast into the remainder of north and parts of central Georgia during the evening hours.  Many of these thunderstorms produced frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and a few became severe.  Several homes in the Atlanta area were struck by lightning and one person was injured from a lightning strike in Paulding county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cobb County 911 Center reported that lightning struck a tree and caused it to fall across a road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of an area of low pressure coming from the plains and rich gulf moisture produced some isolated severe weather during the afternoon of the 15th in Leflore County.  The afternoon storms also produced some locally heavy rains in Leflore County, where some flooding was observed around Itta Bena and Schlater.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house burned down after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms and locally heavy rain resulted in damage to roads and buildings in Tacna and Wellton.  Very heavy rain also affected parts of the city of Yuma and Quartzsite in the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near highway 95 and 5E, resulting in a fire. A haystack caught fire at Avenue 30E and County 8th Street after it was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front produced thunderstorms across portions of northeastern New Jersey. Numerous lightning strikes impacted the Hawthorne area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous lightning strikes occurred in Hawthorne.  One strike resulted in a transformer fire.  Eastern Christian High School was impacted by a direct strike on the auditorium. A house was struck, resulting in a two foot gap in the roof.  Two other lightning strikes were reported in town.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cloud to ground lightning from a thunderstorm between Farmington and Bloomfield struck a 24 year old man while he was on his horse, riding along a metal fence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 24 year old man was critically injured when he was struck by lightning while riding his horse along a metal fence. The horse was killed. The man's hat had a four inch hole in it from the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm complex moving through the Minot area resulted in lightning striking and damaging a townhouse.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An early morning lightning strike caused a fire in the attic of a townhouse complex in Minot.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck one house and also knocked out power to street lights.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck one house and also knocked out power to street lights.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent complex of thunderstorms raced across the northwest portion of the forecast area and brought a line severe storms to the Delta region. Several thunderstorms brought damaging winds to portions of southeast Arkansas, northeast Louisiana, and the Delta portion of Mississippi. A couple of tornadoes also occurred during this event with one causing a fatality in Wayside.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck causing ceiling and window damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire in a three-story barn that was used for storing crafts, artwork, and antiques.  Volatile chemicals in the barn helped fuel the fire that destroyed the barn and its contents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms over eastern sections of Palm Beach County produced lightning strikes which affected two houses in the Lake Worth area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit two houses about a block apart from each other at nearly the same time in Lake Worth. A house at 185 Bryn Mawr Drive had roof damage from a fallen tree which knocked a three to four feet wide hole in the living room ceiling and started a small fire in the attic. The hole in the roof allowed rainfall in and that subsequently put out the fire. The other house at 185 Vassar Drive suffered shattered roof tiles and also started a small fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep tropical moisture south of a trough across central Florida produced scattered to numerous thunderstorms along coastal sections of southeast Florida during the early afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A boater was standing in a 14-foot aluminum hull boat when a thunderstorm approached. The man was struck and killed. Two others were with him but in the water, and they were not injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms resulted in a lightning caused grass fire in Moody County, and produced nickel size hail in Lake County in southeast South Dakota during the evening of September 30th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a grass fire which burned over two acres, before being contained by the Brookings Fire Department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small complex of thunderstorms developed ahead of a weakening frontal boundary moving across South Texas, moving across Deep South Texas from west to east during the evening and overnight hours of the 28th into the 29th.  Heavy rainfall and lightning were notable in Jim Hogg County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two transformers were struck by lightning in the city of Hebbronville, reported by the  Jim Hogg County Sheriff Department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the region in association with a frontal system. Gusty winds, small hail, and flash flooding were reported across the region with some of this activity.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged the clubhouse roof and chimney at the Highpoint Apartment Complex in Brandon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary in the area along with a weak area of low pressure combined to produce areas of showers and thunderstorms on the 12th, mainly in the afternoon and evening hours. Some of the storms were prolific lightning producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Bridgewater Court was struck by lightning. The ensuing fire caused major damage to the home and minor damage to the two adjacent homes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms occurred during the afternoon of the 2nd ahead of a pre-frontal trough. One storm's lightning struck a house in Waterbury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at 84 Greystone Road, passed through rock and stone retaining wall, then struck the home at 92 Greystone Road in Waterbury, causing a minor fire, electrical damage, and some cosmetic damage to the exterior.  The force of the strike also caused the dishes to come out of a cabinet at 85 Greystone Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was critically injured when he was struck by lightning while riding his bicycle.  He was nearing a paramedic van when he was hit.  His heart stopped but paramedics quickly responded and were able to resuscitate him.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm over northwest Catron County produced cloud to ground lightning. One of the lightning strikes struck a man who was standing under a 30 foot tall tree to get out of the rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Harry Beggerly, 61, died near Quemado Lake from a lightning strike on the afternoon of August 30, while seeking shelter from the rain under a 30 foot tall tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large pine tree near the Whitaker Suite Building in North Conway and caused damage to electrical equipment, phone lines, afire alarm system and about 13 televisions in buildings in the nearby area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level low continued to meander about the mid-Atlantic region.  A weak cold front was evident from the mid-Atlantic into the southern Appalachians.  A warm, humid air mass continued across Georgia.  The upper low once again provided the support for scattered thunderstorm development across north Georgia during the afternoon and evening hours.  A few of these storms became severe, producing marginally severe hail and damaging wind gusts.  Thunderstorms continued to drift south into east central and central Georgia after midnight, but these remained below severe limits.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fannin County 911 Center reported that a house fire was likely the result of a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the steeple and belfry of an old church that housed the Veterans of Foreign Wars Post in Skowhegan and ignited a fire that caused an estimated $2000 in damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms affected southeast Kansas from the evening hours on the 19th through the early morning hours on the 20th. The storms formed along and ahead of an advancing strong cold front surging southeast across the plains. Thunderstorm winds of 60 to at times 75 mph and hail up to golfball size pummeled portions of southeast Kansas, including the communities of Parsons, Cherryvale, Thayer, Coffeyville, Erie, Neodesha, Peru and Niotaze. Additionally, very heavy rainfall produced flooding and flash flooding across portions of Wilson, Neosho and Montgomery counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a fertilizer plant in downtown Bartlett during the early morning hours on the 20th. Consequently, a large fire erupted, engulfing and eventually destroying the entire plant. No one was injured. Property damage amounts are rough estimates. The Labette Avenue contributed to this report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms affected southeast Kansas from the evening hours on the 19th through the early morning hours on the 20th. The storms formed along and ahead of an advancing strong cold front surging southeast across the plains. Thunderstorm winds of 60 to at times 75 mph and hail up to golfball size pummeled portions of southeast Kansas, including the communities of Parsons, Cherryvale, Thayer, Coffeyville, Erie, Neodesha, Peru and Niotaze. Additionally, very heavy rainfall produced flooding and flash flooding across portions of Wilson, Neosho and Montgomery counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning reportedly struck a grain bin just east of Earlton. Consequently, a fire erupted, engulfing and eventually destroying the bin. No one was injured. Damage amounts are rough estimates. The Chanute Tribune contributed to this report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm affected portions of Surry County during the evening of August 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One male firefighter was part of a water shuttle operation at a house fire in an area with no hydrants. As the firefighter worked near a pond he was struck. He didn't suffer any long term effects from the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm affected portions of Surry County during the evening of August 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An Ararat female volunteer firefighter  was helping fight a house fire when a bolt of lightning struck her helmet Thursday night. She was transported to a nearby hospital but had only minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tornado touched down around 1619 PDT near the southeast corner of Lake Tapps and moved northeast around 36 mph for 16 minutes, lifting off the ground just northeast of Enumclaw.  There was also a lightning strike which damaged a home in Auburn.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree next to a home, causing damage to the home's siding and much of the electronics inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced hail up to the size of golf balls over the eastern of Upstate South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire at the Woodruff High School football stadium, destroying the press box.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of storms developed after dark across metro Phoenix and some produced heavy rain and strong damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in north Phoenix, knocking out many electrical appliances. However, no fire started from this lightning strke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In the early hours on the morning, a lightning strike ignited a fire to hay bales.  Forty-eight large round hay bales were totally lost.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and burned 48 large round hay bales.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The sea breeze pushing into a highly unstable air mass, resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across southern South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported that lightning started a structure fire on Lakewood Drive near Walterboro, South Carolina.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the Mid-South during the early morning hours of July 26th, 2009. Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the front. The showers and storms continued into the morning hours before dying out. Some of the storms became severe producing large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a garage to catch fire. The garage sustained damage from the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a couple house fires over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large home on Pimlico Ln, igniting a fire that caused enough damage to render the home uninhabitable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an automobile in Utah County, causing one injury as well as damage to the SUV.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four people were riding in a late model GMC Yukon SUV south on I-15, when the vehicle was struck by lightning about halfway between Santaquin and Payson. The vehicle immediately stalled. The front passenger was touching the radio/CD player at the moment lightning struck; she became unconscious and stopped breathing. Her husband administered CPR and she was resuscitated, and has since made a full recovery. The vehicle was damaged, with the electrical system and other components having to be replaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms approached the city of Springfield from the west.  This line of storms produced three to six inches of rain over the city causing flash flooding leading to numerous water rescues.  Additional thunderstorms developed across the rest of southern Missouri.  A few of these storms became severe with wind gusts in excess of 60 mph and hail up to the size of golf balls.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning stike caused a house to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail in Larimer and Weld Counties.  In Weld County, two weak tornadoes were also reported.  Hail up to golfball size caused heavy crop damage north and east of Greeley, where fields of sugar, beets, pinto beans, corn and carrots were damaged.   The combination of heavy rain and hail shut down several county roads around Greeley, as hail piled in small drifts and overflowed ditches.  Lightning strikes caused damage in Boulder, Superior and at Front Range Airport near Watkins.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank.  The lid was partially torn off and flames shot out of the tank.  The railing around the tank was also damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance and attendant surface cold front combined to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms across the eastern half of central North Carolina. The unseasonably dry low levels of the atmosphere across central North Carolina created a favorable environment for any thunderstorms that developed to produce damaging winds. Many of the thunderstorms that developed became severe and produced damaging winds across the eastern half of central North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A town home fire was reported on Canvas Drive in Raleigh, North Carolina, which was caused by an apparent lightning strike that that ran in on the natural gas line. Damage to the town home was unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large subtropical ridge across Texas was slowly expanding eastward.  In advance of this upper ridge, an unstable northwest flow aloft, with embedded short waves, prevailed across the eastern and southeastern U.S.  This, combined with a continuing warm and very unstable air mass, supported development of several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across the region from late on the 17th through the 18th.  The first round developed around midnight on the 17th and continued through the early morning hours.  The second round occurred during the late afternoon on the 18th.  The storms were generally confined to the eastern parts of the state with all of the storms developing within narrow northwest to southeast oriented bands.  The individual storms were also tracking from northwest to southeast within these bands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Athens Banner/Herald reported several lightning incidents across eastern Jackson county as strong thunderstorms moved from northwest to southeast shortly after midnight EDT.  The roof of a unit at the Oak Hill Apartments on Old Hull Road in Commerce was set on fire by a lightning strike.  Also, near Commerce, a chicken house on Wilson Road was set on fire and completely destroyed.  Further southeast on Birch Street in Nicholson, a barn was set on fire and destroyed by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary in concert with an approaching upper level disturbance resulted in scattered strong to severe thunderstorms sweeping west to east across areas generally along and west of the Flint Hills during the morning hours of the 17th. Some of the more notable reports include golfball size hail near Russell in Russell County, and wind damage to a mobile home just west of Rosalia in Butler County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14-year-old Hutchinson boy and his mother were struck by lightning standing under a tree shortly before noon on the 17th. The boy was knocked unconscious for a short period of time, but the mother was fine. No serious injuries were incurred. The Hutchinson News contributed to this report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several bands of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across central North Carolina as a a shortwave trough moved across the region. The severe threat quickly |transformed from a hail threat early in the event to a damaging wind episode as shortwave mid-level kinematics increased over the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning resulted in several house fires from Albemarle to New London. The entire town of Albermarle was without power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of upper level impulses moved over a stationary frontal boundary across north Florida and southeast Georgia producing severe weather and flooding.  This event continued into April 2009.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old man was struck by lightning at 1512 Dahlgreen Street. He was treated at the scene by Fire-Rescue and then transported to Baptist South Hospital. During the storm the young man ran outside to bring his dogs in from the storm, when he was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In Logan and Phillips Counties, severe thunderstorms produced large hail, from quarter size to golfball size.  Strong winds also accompanied the storms.  The hardest hit area was in northern Phillips County.   In all, 250 farms were affected by the storms resulting in a 27% crop loss of wheat a 6.3% loss of corn.  Homes were also damaged and windows broken.  In Weld County, a man person was injured by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 41-yr old man was injured when he was struck by lightning on a golf course in Greeley. He was was struck on the 13th hole and suffered burns to his body, but was alert and concious when paramedics arrived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front arriving from the west late in the day on the 2nd moved into a warm and moist air mass, which resulted in strong to severe thunderstorms across the area, around the Trenton area during the early morning and across a larger area of the state during the late morning and early afternoon of the 2nd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two persons were struck and injured by lightning in Northfield.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The evening of August 8th, a very unstable air mass was in place across the upper Midwest with a warm front draped across the Twin Cities area, then eastward across west central Wisconsin. Initially, a strong cap suppressed thunderstorm development until around sunset as a cool front moved across east central Minnesota, and developed a supercell west of Minneapolis, Minnesota.  The storm complex then moved into west central Wisconsin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 45' white pine which fell on a home, and damaged the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper closed low was moving from the mid-south and Mississippi valley region into the mid-Atlantic and southeast U.S.  A strong cold front accompanied the upper system.  A strong low-level jet in advance of these weather systems transported warm, moist Gulf air northward into the region.  With strong dynamics, hence shear, combined with an unusually moist, unstable atmosphere, the atmosphere was primed for a major weather outbreak. One round of thunderstorms passed through north Georgia during the early morning hours.  A few minor severe weather events accompanied this system in northwest Georgia.  Partial clearing followed the morning convection, allowing temperatures to soar into the mid 70s across much of north and central Georgia in advance of the main weather system.  Scattered to numerous discrete supercell thunderstorms developed during mid-afternoon in northwest Georgia and progressed east and southeast across the remaining portions of the county warning area during the evening hours.  Severe thunderstorms and tornadoes lingered into the early morning hours of the 11th across the southern counties of central Georgia.  During the eight hour period from 5 pm EDT on April 10th to 1 am EDT on April 11th, a total of 14 tornadoes were confirmed to have touched down in north and central Georgia causing millions in damages.  While some injuries were observed, no deaths were observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Herald Tribune of Cartersville reported that lightning struck a home on Fairfield Drive and set the structure on fire.  The blaze in the two-story home was confined to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unstable air ahead of an upper-level low centered just off the coast of Northern California triggered bands of elevated convection which stretched from San Diego to the San Bernardino County deserts. Over 1500 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes were recorded during the event, resulting in one death and multiple injuries. The lightning also started approximately 70 fires, most of which were small and did not result in any damage or injuries. The storms also produced gusty winds and hail, with one cell producing quarter-sized hail in the Del Mar area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 31 year old male suffered serious injuries while doing landscape work at a home on Camden Place in San Marcos when lightning struck a palm tree nearby.  He was transported to the hospital in critical condition. His 48 year old brother was treated for minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm, humid and unstable airmass was in place within the warm sector of a low pressure system. Aloft, an upper level low was over the Great Lakes region with disturbances rotating about it. Thunderstorms occurred across Litchfield County during the evening hours with some storms becoming severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in Bantam.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A closed upper level low and pool of unusually cold air in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere moved over the region Tuesday, July 7th, leading to the development of numerous thunderstorms across eastern New York, many of which contained large quantities of hail. The severe thunderstorms developed during the late morning hours, and continued through early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house at 126 Main Street in Altamont late Tuesday afternoon afternoon starting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved rapidly to the northeast across Rapides Parish during the early afternoon hours, producing several reports of wind damage and causing one injury due to lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured by a lightning strike while moving his barbeque pit in his yard.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms across southwest Louisiana formed throughout the day, producing several damaging lightning strikes and one funnel cloud.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Jennings Daily News reported lightning struck an oil tank at the Texas Petroleum Investment Company on East Racca Road, setting it on fire. Smoke from the fire was visible throughout the city of Jennings.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a slow moving cold front approaching from the west, and an abundantly moist and warm air mass in place, led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across eastern New York and western New England during Wednesday afternoon and evening on July 29th.||Some of the thunderstorms were severe, producing isolated damaging winds.  In addition, several clusters of thunderstorms moved slowly, and trained across the same areas for several hours, producing torrential rainfall and resulting in significant flash flooding.||Trained spotters measured rainfall amounts of 4 to 7 inches within the most persistent thunderstorms over a 3 to 6 hour period, particularly near Kinderhook, and adjacent areas of northern Columbia and southern Rensselaer Counties. In addition to widespread flash flooding, the Kinderhook Creek also overflowed its banks, resulting in additional flash flooding.||As a result of the flooding, Amtrak train service was suspended early Thursday morning on July 30th between the Rensselaer Rail Station and Penn Station, in order for track and signal systems to be examined for flood damage in Hudson. The rail service resumed by early Thursday afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Trees and wires were reported down approximately 1 mile north of Woodstock due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The region was under the influence of a departing upper level low and with surface heating the atmosphere became unstable enough for thunderstorm development during the mid afternoon into the early evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was in the backyard of his home wrapping up an extension cord when lightning either struck the ground near him or the cord.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong thunderstorms developed over southeast Texas during the afternoon hours.  One storm moving across Sabine Pass produced a lightning strike that injured 7 people and killed one person.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: All local media reported eight construction workers repairing the roof of a modular home on Bufford Street in Sabine Pass were struck by lightning and injured. One of the workers was critically injured and later died. The home was also set on fire by the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms across southwest Louisiana formed throughout the day, producing several damaging lightning strikes and one funnel cloud.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Jennings Police Department reported lightning struck a home on South Lake Arthur Avenue and set it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on July 6, and continued through the night into the morning hours on July 7.  A few reports of severe weather were received on the 6th, with heavy rainfall and flooding occurring on the 7th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two homes were struck by lightning in Lafayette and both were set on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across central Louisiana during the afternoon and moved westward, with one severe thunderstorm striking the DeRidder area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lake Charles American Press and Cameron Pilot newspapers reported lightning started a fire in the Management Unit 1 region of Sabine National Wildlife Refuge, located in the north-central portion of the refuge. The wildfire continued for nearly two weeks, burning around 4000 acres of marshland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across southwest Louisiana during the afternoon hours and moved southward into the Gulf of Mexico. Several reports of damaging winds and intense lightning were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Cameron Pilot reported lightning started a fire in the Management Unit 2 region of Sabine National Wildlife Refuge, just south of the Wetland Walkway and adjacent to Highway 27 in the far southeast portion of the refuge. The wildfire continued into the following day, burning over 4000 acres of marshland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours across interior southeast Texas, before moving southward into the Gulf of Mexico.  Numerous reports of large hail, damaging winds, and intense lightning were received, with one fatality from a falling tree limb. High winds and lightning combined to knock out power to 11000 customers across southeast Texas.
