These storms were also prolific cloud to ground lightning producers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a backyard tree, then moved onto a powerline which set the roof of a local residence on fire.  There were no report of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Trees were downed by a lightning strike and blocking portions of Qualla Road in Clover Hill Farms Subdivision.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike blew a hole through the roof of a home and traveled through the electrical system on Foxridge Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure aloft triggered numerous showers and thunderstorms across Arkansas on the night of the 22nd and morning of the 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck a natural gas metering station, causing the natural gas to catch fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over parts of northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 23rd producing torrential rainfall and flash flooding in some areas, including parts of Chicago.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Jackson Street which started a fire in the attic and on the second floor.  Damage to the house was estimated at $75,000 and at $25,000 to its contents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over parts of northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 23rd producing torrential rainfall and flash flooding in some areas, including parts of Chicago.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large house on Lincoln Avenue and started a fire in the attic which spread to the second floor.  The house and its contents were a total loss.  No one was home at the time of the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over parts of northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 23rd producing torrential rainfall and flash flooding in some areas, including parts of Chicago.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A church on Division Street was struck by lightning which broke a hole in the steeple tower.  Much of the damage was from heavy rain which entered through the hole.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the morning of July 1st, a series of thunderstorms moved south off of Lake Michigan dropping heavy rain and large hail across portions of northwest Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An employee at a drugstore was using the telephone when lightning struck nearby.  The employee reported feeling a jolt and was taken to the hospital as a precaution.  A dispatcher at the 911 center also reported a jolt after lightning struck the center.  Sparks were reportedly seen inside the center just after the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved across Southern New England, providing enough lift for showers and thunderstorms to develop.  A large area of instability ahead of the front was enough for these storms to become severe, producing large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local television station reported that a 16 year old boy was indirectly struck by lightning.  Lightning struck the ground and traveled into the metal garage door that the boy was touching.  He was transported to the hospital for observation but was reported to be fine.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms developed quickly just after Noon CDT in extreme northwest Alabama, and lasted through around 4 pm.  The storms developed as a weak upper level disturbance tracked southward into the Tennessee Valley.  The environment was conducive for downbursts producing damaging winds.  Isolated large hail up to quarter sized hail was also reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power line at a hotel.  A woman experienced a minor injury and was hospitalized due to a resulting electrical surge.  Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulse storms consolidated into a few multicell clusters late in the afternoon and produced areas of wind damage and large hail as they moved across the upstate.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a moving car on I-26 near mile marker 41, causing significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulse storms consolidated into a few multicell clusters late in the afternoon and produced areas of wind damage and large hail as they moved across the upstate.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck at the Jonesville Fire Dept, causing minor hand injuries to a person inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A ridge of high pressure aloft, which had brought unusually hot weather to Arkansas, shifted to the west of the state. This allowed colder air aloft to move into the state from the northwest, periodically triggering thunderstorms from the 9th through the 13th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured by lightning on the campus of the University of Arkansas Community College at Morrilton. His injuries were not believed to be serious.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from afternoon thunderstorms struck a person in Santa Rosa county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40 year old male was struck by lightning at the intersection of Avalon blvd and Tuscarora trail. After the strike the man noticed his pants were burned...the hairs on his arm singed...and he complained of a severe headache. He was transported to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 24th producing heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in the 5400 block of Switch Grass Lane was uninhabitable after suffering fire damage caused by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 24th producing heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in the 2500 block of Freeland Court was uninhabitable due to fire damage caused by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across parts of far northern Illinois during the mid to late evening hours of July 27th and continued into the early morning hours of July 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire which destroyed the rood of a 2200 square foot home on Glenhurst Court.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the early morning hours of July 24th producing heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire in the attic of a home at 84th and Country Club Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a man standing on a roof on Ono Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level system sparked thunderstorms across Illinois during the early morning hours of the 7th. These moved into northern Indiana during the late morning and continued through the afternoon. Reports of 60 to 70 mph wind gusts and large hail were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management officials reported lightning struck a tree, causing it to fall onto a house. No exact figures were given, but is estimated at $10,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large area of thunderstorms rotated northeast out of Missouri during the evening of the 24th into the early morning of the 25th.  As the storms moved through the Clarke County area, lightning struck at Terrible's Lakeside Casino.  The lightning caused minor damage, however the casino and hotel had to be evacuated due to an electrical fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent squall line of severe thunderstorms raced eastward across the entire southeastern U.S. from the morning of April 4 through the afternoon of April 5, 2011. In a matter of just 30 hours, this squall line brought widespread damaging winds to the Tennessee and Ohio Valleys, southeast Alabama, southwest and south central Georgia, northwest Florida, and the Mid Atlantic States. This system was one of the most prolific severe weather producers to ever impact the nation with widespread straight line wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a large fire in down-town Donalsonville.  The fire consumed the businesses on the east side of Cherry Street and burned about one half of a city block.  Two beauty shops, an insurance agency, a pool hall, a gift shop, and a gym were among the businesses damaged in the fire.  The monetary damage figure provided is a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms developed during the mid afternoon hours in a very moist and moderately unstable air mass with moderate low to mid level wind shear.  Many of the storms produced gusty to damaging winds, some in excess of 60 mph, knocking down several trees and power lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house which caught on fire as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms, including supercells, brought widespread severe weather to the northeastern half of eastern KY during the afternoon and evening hours of May 10th. The primary mode of severe weather on this date was large hail, with some stones as large as baseballs reported in Bath county. Numerous trees were also blown down in several counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit substation at Kemper and power is out at Coal Run Village and various parts of the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical wave moving west across the northern Gulf of Mexico helped produce some thunderstorms, some of which produced hail and damaging winds across southwest Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A ham radio operated reported a trailer was struck by lightning and was on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous pulse-type thunderstorms developed in a regime of weak shear and high instability over the North Carolina foothills and western piedmont. Several of the stroms produced damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in the attic of a home on First Ave Place NW.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated storms produced some lightning damage across inland northeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a structural fire in Citra. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the mid and late afternoon hours on the July 5th, as a weak upper level disturbance aloft drifted south and interacted with strong surface heating/resultant instability and a northwest propagating outflow boundary from an area of showers and embedded thunderstorms over North Central Louisiana. Some of these storms produced marginally severe hail across portions of Southwest Arkansas, but strong damaging winds were the primary result as they downed a number of trees from near Nashville to near the Arkansas/Louisiana line, as they continued south along their own outflow boundary.  This complex of thunderstorms that moved south out of Southwest Arkansas were prolific lightning producers as well as they moved south of the Arkansas/Louisiana line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have struck the top of a supermarket in town.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms developed during the mid afternoon hours in a very moist and moderately unstable air mass with moderate low to mid level wind shear.  Many of the storms produced gusty to damaging winds, some in excess of 60 mph, knocking down several trees and power lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a house on Mount Oak Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture and an upper level low fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  Several storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Anthem area of Henderson, causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire...which destroyed the garage and two vehicles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of thunderstorms developed north of a warm front and trained across portions of northeast Iowa into Southwest Wisconsin during the evening of July 27th into the early morning hours of the 28th. The highest reported rainfall total from these storms was 10.11 inches in Sinsinawa (Grant County). The heavy rain did produce some minor flooding as area streams and rivers came out of their banks for a short period.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a small fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving upper level low and monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  Many storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Kingman, setting it afire.  The home was gutted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving upper level low and monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  Many storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power line at Highway 62 and Dorth Place.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across parts of central Illinois during the morning hours of June 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree was struck by lightning in an alley near Kennedy Drive and North Street.  The tree then fell on to three cars, destroying two of them.  Power lines were also brought down by the falling tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across parts of central Illinois during the morning hours of June 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the chimney of a brick building near La Grange Road and Burlington Avenue.  Bricks and debris were scattered across the street and on sidewalks.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in a warm, humid air mass across the region during the late evening hours. The thunderstorms winds gusting to 60 mph, downed trees and power lines. In North Tonawanda, Niagara County, a home was damaged by a falling tree. Three homes across the area were damaged by lightning-sparked fires. The homes were located in East Pembroke, Wilson and Canandaigua.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful line of severe thunderstorms moved northeast across northern Illinois during the evening hours of June 21st producing damaging winds and widespread wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 5300 block of East Wonder Lake Road and started a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong late summer cold front was moving toward the southeast United States supported by strong northwest flow aloft on the east side of an ever persistent strong subtropical ridge across Texas and the southern plains.  With an unstable, hot surface environment in place across Georgia, the stage was set for scattered thunderstorms.  Activity was a little more widespread than on previous days.  The storms exhibited frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.  A few became strong to severe producing penny to nickel-sized hail and damaging downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The public reported that lightning struck and destroyed a three-foot diameter poplar tree.  The top half of the tree exploded when it was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that developed during the afternoon of July 5th produced large amounts of lightning, some of which caused property damage, including a house in Beaumont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two story house on the west side of Beaumont. The fire quickly spread through the attic, but was put out by firemen who arrived at the scene. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance helped produce thunderstorms that had numerous lightning strikes in southeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A two story home on the west side of Beaumont was struck by lightning. The resulting fire was quickly put out, but not before the home was severely damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front in combination with the inland pushing sea breeze in a moderate to strongly unstable air mass, resulted in scattered thunderstorm development across southern South Carolina and southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Fire Department employee reported that lightning struck a house and started the home on fire at 175 Main Street in Garden City, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving upper level low and monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  Many storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck numerous trees and at least one home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance helped produce thunderstorms that had numerous lightning strikes in southeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Excessive lightning caused a fire at the Stone Hearth Apartments. One unit with eight apartments was on fire and the roof partially collapsed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure area helped produce heavy rain and thunderstorms that caused one house fire in Groves and flooded a home in Port Arthur.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house that was struck by lightning caught fire in Groves. The fire started in the attic of the two story home, and caused considerable water damage on the first floor and fire damage on the second floor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cold, post-frontal showers produced thunderstorms in the northern Willamette Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm early Wednesday evening produced lightning that struck a man riding a tractor near Toliver Road, west of Highway 213 in Molalla, Oregon. The man drove himself to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving upper level low and monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  Many storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, damaging the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system developed over Eastern Arkansas and moved along a stationary front draped across the Mid-South. The system moved into Northern Mississippi where there were several reports of large hail and damaging winds during the late afternoon and early evening hours of June 16, 2011.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex in Southaven starting a fire that destroyed 8 units. A section of the roof collapsed into the structure as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching frontal boundary, seabreeze activity and a mid level shortwave helped to ignite convection across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A midafternoon thunderstorm produced lightning that struck an Oak tree at Allen Benedict Court on Harden Street where 5 landscape and maintenance workers were sitting.  One worker was taken to the hospital with non-life threatening injuries.  The others were treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were injured by a lightning strike while picking blueberries east of South Haven.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple media sources reported a lightning strike injured two males who were picking blueberries at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The last night of the unusual prolonged heat wave brought another round of severe thunderstorms. Surface dew point temperatures continued in the oppressive 70F to 80F range. With the extreme heat, mid level temperatures also remained quite warm. However, the combination of a subtle upper level disturbance and a modest low level jet helped spawn the thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was presumed to have been the source of a house fire. The time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several lightning strikes caused fires and resulted in damage to property in northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A shed and mobile home were damaged from a fire that resulted from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several lightning strikes caused fires and resulted in damage to property in northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two houses struck by lightning in Midway just off Highway 98.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck the bell tower of a church just east of downtown Fort Worth, damaging the tower and sending bricks tumbling to the street below.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the bell tower of the Allen Chapel AME Church on Elm Street, damaging the tower and causing the bricks to tumble onto 1st Street below. The street remained closed for at least 2 days. The church's roof was also damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture lingered over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin, continuing to fuel thunderstorms.  Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked several brush fires near Lake Mead City.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms which weakened across Lake Michigan produced an outflow boundary. This boundary worked into far southern Lower Michigan and interacted with a lake breeze boundary to promote rapid storm development. Reports of damaging winds and some hail were received, but the storms failed to maintain their severity eastward as a large outflow boundary work across and south of the area, cutting off the limited available moisture.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire official reported that a 17 year old female was struck by lightning at a campground while taking a shower. No specific details were given as to the extent of injuries, which are assumed minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Park County during the late afternoon hours of Tuesday July 26. A woman leading a horseback ride in a wooded area at about 530pm in the Chico area was struck by lightning. A man performed CPR on the victim before she was flown to Livingston Memorial Hospital then to Billings Clinic. Another woman was treated at the scene for burns while a 6-year-old girl was treated for minor injuries at the hospital. Two horses were killed in the incident. Lightning strikes were fairly isolated in the region at the time.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Park County during the late afternoon hours of Tuesday July 26. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked down numerous power poles on Two Mile Road at Sunrise Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another push of monsoon moisture fueled more thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Several storms produced flash flooding, and there was also isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and split a tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold storm moved from the Gulf of Alaska through the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin, bringing thunderstorms and strong winds, with spotty damage reported. Heavy snow also likely fell on the unpopulated high mountain peaks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an industrial building at Desert Inn and McLeod, as well as two houses and trees near Nellis AFB.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak low pressure over Georgian Bay moved northeast across the lower Great Lakes and pulled a frontal boundary across the region. Thunderstorms that accompanied the front reached severe limits producing strong winds gusting to 65 mph and large hail. Trees and powers lines were reported down in Orchard Park and near Chaffee in Erie county, near Salamanca in Cattaraugus county, and in Bolivar and Alma in Allegany county. One inch hail was reported in East Aurora where hail accumulated and covered the ground in some sections.  Lightning struck an automobile on Davidson Avenue, Buffalo. The lightning shattered a window. A woman in the vehicle suffered minor injuries from the glass. In Orchard Park, lightning ignited a fire on Stoughton Lane. Damage to the house was extensive, estimated between two and three hundred thousand dollars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across northern Nebraska during the late morning and early afternoon hours on August 23rd.  Lightning from these thunderstorms was the cause of two fires in the Bassett area (Rock County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and burned six hay bales south and east of Bassett.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another push of monsoon moisture fueled more thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Several storms produced flash flooding, and there was also isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole, knocking power out for eight hours in the neighborhood.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and set fire to a power pole along a dirt road near Silver Peak.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of shower and thunderstorms moved off the Appalachians and into central North Carolina during the afternoon. The severe storms produced thunderstorm wind damage across the Central Piedmont with minor structural damage to a couple of outdoor buildings.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire. Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe storms impacted areas south of M-59.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house which caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture and an upper level low fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert.  Several storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and set afire a power pole.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms occurred during the morning hours of the 27th in southern Arkansas. These storms were to the north of an advancing warm front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer and knocked down power lines on N. Gabbert St.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a man at a campground near Big Lake.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 46 year old man was stuck and killed by lightning at a National Forest Campground at a National Forest campground near Big Lake, Arizona.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As the remnants of Tropical Storm Lee tracked along a frontal zone that extended from the southern Appalachians into central Virginia, heavy rain and severe storms spread into central North Carolina. The initial severe weather threat, during the early morning hours, was tornadoes, due to the highly sheared environment associated with the former tropical cyclone. As the day progressed, and the remnant low of Lee continued to weaken, the severe weather threat transitioned to straight line winds, as instability increased with the heating of the day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: According the fire department chief, lightning struck a tree in the backyard and ran underground and came up inside the house and set the house on fire. The kitchen and an enclosed porch were destroyed, with the remainder of the house suffering heavy smoke damage. The home owner was present at the time of the fire, but escaped with any injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of low pressure developed over southeast Louisiana and moved east along a warm front which stretched across southeast Mississippi. This eventually caused a strong cold front to sweep through the region with numerous showers and thunderstorms. This storm system combined with cold temperatures aloft and triggered severe storms that produced quite a bit of hail along with some scattered reports of wind damage. Multiple reports of golf ball sized hail occurred with the largest hail size being tennis ball size. The most intense storm occurred over central sections of Mississippi, roughly across northeast Copiah County and northwest Simpson County. Here, a very intense downburst occurred with winds up to 110 mph which downed dozens of trees. Large hail was wind driven and many trees were stripped of there leaves. Outside of the severe storms, several storms moved over the same locations which resulted in heavy rainfall which led to some flash flooding generally within the I-20 corridor.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire. The fire did severe damage to the house causing a fatality.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front was moving through the region.  It triggered showers and thunderstorms...with numerous reports of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire that destroyed the house.  Fortunately the owners were not home at the time, so no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along an upper shear axis as strong daytime heating |resulted in moderate instability across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 45 year old male died when he was struck by lightning while feeding his livestock.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted northward and positioned just south of the Florida-Georgia state line during the mid afternoon as a pre-frontal squall line of storms moved in from Appalachee Bay. Several low-topped mini-supercells developed across northeast Florida in advance of the squall line. Bowing line segments were noted in the squall line. Low level instability was not quite strong enough to draw mesocyclone rotation down to the surface...but numerous reports of funnel clouds were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire at 3653 Mosswood Court in Mandarin. The cost of damaged was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Surface low pressure moved across north Florida during the day trailing a surface cold front across the area. A few storms fired in the warm sector near the low which produced small hail and some lightning damage in northeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 62 year old make golfer was struck by lightning on the 8th hole of the St. Johns Golf and Country Club golf course. He was transported to the hospital for treatment. The time of the event was approximated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple severe storms affected western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an outbuilding on Lentz Rd, starting a fire that destroyed the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a very unstable atmosphere, weak shear and several outflow boundaries resulted in severe pulse-type thunderstorms across western North Carolina. Some of the storms produced wind damage and large hail as they drifted to the east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17-year-old male was struck by lightning and injured while riding a motorcycle on Brown Mountain Beach Rd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over the southern mountains of North Carolina. The storms caused some lightning damage in Henderson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Solomon Circle, igniting a fire that destroyed most of the home. One person received minor injuries from the lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced a little wind and lightning damage over the western piedmont of North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Wall Ave, starting a fire that damaged the roof and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms gradually increased in coverage and intensity during the afternoon along a weakly convergent cold front moving through the area. The warm sector air mass was characterized by temperatures in the mid to upper 70's, dew points in the lower 60's, and mixed-layer cape values of 1000 to 1500 j/kg. Very strong deep layer wind shear promoted organized storm structures. A bowing line segment that raced east-northeast across southern Illinois clipped Ballard County, KY, where there was isolated wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vacant house on U.S. Highway 60, starting a fire. The fire was mainly confined to the outside walls of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front over Wisconsin generated severe thunderstorms with large hail over portions of western Upper Michigan on the 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and damaged the steeple tower of the Keweenaw Heritage Center at St. Anne's located in Calumet Township on the early morning of the 11th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning associated with an early morning thunderstorm hit a home in Ocoee. The lightning strikes started a fire which destroyed the home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike to a 4000 square foot home started a fire which destroyed the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a propane tank at a water treatment plant, igniting a fire that destroyed some equipment.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a fire that caused an estimated $1 milliion in damage to the Gator Stop Super Truck Stop and Casino.

Several low-topped mini-supercells developed across northeast Florida in advance of the squall line. Bowing line segments were noted in the squall line. Low level instability was not quite strong enough to draw mesocyclone rotation down to the surface...but numerous reports of funnel clouds were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on SW 282nd Street and started a fire which destroyed the home. The cost of property loss was estimated based on an average of home prices in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper level low pressure system moved across the Ozarks causing numerous strong to severe storms to develop with several supercells as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was hit by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm caused lightning damage in Sussex County on the afternoon of the 15th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The roof of a Drake Knoll home in Lewes was struck by lightning and started a fire. Five fire companies battled the blaze that was mainly confined to the roof. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong, potent upper atmospheric system, as well as a developing surface low, raced across the Ohio River Valley during the afternoon of February 5th. This system intensified and moved rapidly across south central New York during the evening (994 mb at 7pm EST) and New England into the Gulf of Maine by early morning of the 6th (980 mb at 1am EST).||This quick-hit storm started around dusk and was largely finished by midnight with snowfall rates up to 3 inches per hour. A heavy wet snowfall (8:1 snow/water ratios) of 6 to 12 inches occurred across the northern third of Vermont, 4 to 8 inches of snow and sleet with some freezing rain across the central third of Vermont and primarily sleet and freezing rain with a few inches of snow across southern Vermont. In addition, there were several organized lines of thunderstorms that contained snow, sleet or freezing rain that moved across the entire state between 830 and 10 pm EST.  ||Snow depths (and Snow water equivalents) after this storm were generally 18 to 30 inches (4 to 6 inches in the valleys with 36 inches or greater (6+ inches) across the higher terrain. This resulted in heavy snow loads and nearly a dozen structure failures of garages, barns and carports. A few of these barn collapses have injured or killed livestock, including in the towns of Chester (Windsor county) and Enosburg Falls (Franklin county) to name a few.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire that eventually destroyed an un-occupied seasonal camp in Addison.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper level low pressure system moved out of the Texas Hill Country and into the Southern Plains/Lower Mississippi Valley during the late evening hours of November 21st and the predawn hours of November 22nd. This storm system was not associated with a frontal boundary...but moisture and shear was significant enough for the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across the region.  A tornado also touched down across Southwest Arkansas as low level shear was maximized by the development of a low pressure center at the surface.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Horatio, Arkansas, burning it to the ground.  There were no reports of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent upper level storm system moved out of the Texas Hill County and into the Southern Plains during the afternoon of November 11th. Deep layer shear and low level shear was significant enough for supercells and mesocyclones during the afternoon and evening hours across the region given the instability in place. Discrete storms developed ahead of a strong cold front and some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts, large hail and tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home west of Homer, Louisiana resulting in a fire and significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary over the region helped to trigger showers and thunderstorms.  Some of the storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building that housed the sales/gift shop of a nursery.  Fire spread rapidly through the building and it is considered a total loss.  No injuries were reported and the other buildings nearby were unharmed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated storms developed across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a cell phone that a 39 year old woman was using at Cosmo Park on the northside of Columbia.  She was taken to a local hospital to be checked out.  She only had some initial numbness in her arm.  She was treated and released the next morning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper low was moving through the northeast United States, while a semi-permanent upper low was located across the southwest United States.  Arctic air enveloped much of the central and southern Plains.  A strong cold front, associated with the northeast U.S. upper low, was sweeping through the southeast U.S.  A large area of showers and thunderstorms accompanied the front.  While none of the thunderstorms became severe, frequent lightning was observed in the stronger storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Johnson County Emergency Managment Director reported that lightning struck a large oak tree adjacent to a residence on Mintons Chapel Road near Kite.  The adjacent structure did not suffer any damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated storms developed over the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a tree and transferred to power lines causing some electrical damage.  Two people were injured by the lightning strike and one had to be briefly hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous short wave was moving rapidly from the south central to the southeast United States, accompanied by a strong Pacific cold front.  Unseasonably warm air, which had prevailed across the southeast U.S. much of the later half of February, combined with strong shear, to support a strong to severe quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) that tracked slowly southeast across the state from mid-afternoon through early evening.  Several tornado warnings were issued, but no tornadoes were reported with this event.  However, several counties across north Georgia received damaging winds and quarter to half-dollars-sized hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gordon County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck an abandoned trailer.  Specific details regarding damages were not provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms produced lightning that caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Centenary Baptist Church.  It burned to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cattle struck by lightning standing near a fence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Twenty one heifers were killed when lightning struck south-southwest of Wibaux.  The heifers were generally lined up along a fence line, but there were six of them that were scattered up to 75 yards away.  Some of the fencing was also knocked down.  There were a total of 51 heifers in the pasture.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak late afternoon seabreeze thunderstorms developed along the Florida west coast. An adult female was struck by lightning from one of the thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 26-year-old female was struck by lightning while standing outside in her driveway next to her vehicle. The incident occurred on Hollywood Avenue in Clearwater. She was transported to the hospital with minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and a lightning strike across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused damage to a house. One person was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms across southwest Louisiana caused lightning that struck and destroyed a home in Calcasieu Parish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An NWS Employee reported a house on Suburban Street was hit by lightning and burned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved into the area triggering showers and thunderstorms.  Some of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a two story house on Clark Lane causing a fire.  No injuries were reported and fortunately the fire department was able to extinguish the flames fairly quickly.  Damage was estimated around $25,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary was in place across central Florida. As the boundary began to lift north drawing in abundant warm moist air over the area, an upper level disturbance moved over the area and a squall line developed and quickly moved across the northern half of the area. Several areas of damaging winds and a tornado resulted from this fast moving line on March 30th. The warm front continued to lift north over northern Florida as a developing low pressure system shifted into the northeastern Gulf of Mexico. As this system moved across northern Florida, the cold front pushed into the local area and another series of squall lines moved across the area through the day on March 31st. Several tornadoes and areas of damaging winds occurred across the greater Tampa Bay area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike took out an electrical substation near the 3500 block of Gaylesburg Court in The Villages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The leading edge of a pre-frontal squall line started to impact southeast Georgia and the Suwannee River Valley of north Florida prior to sunrise. A strong 850 mb SW low level jet of 50-60 kts bisected the Jacksonville county warning area with strong helicities supporting rotating cells during the morning.  Widespread wind damage was reported across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire. The extent of damage was unknown, and the cost of  property damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary was in place across central Florida. As the boundary began to lift north drawing in abundant warm moist air over the area, an upper level disturbance moved over the area and a squall line developed and quickly moved across the northern half of the area. Several areas of damaging winds and a tornado resulted from this fast moving line on March 30th. The warm front continued to lift north over northern Florida as a developing low pressure system shifted into the northeastern Gulf of Mexico. As this system moved across northern Florida, the cold front pushed into the local area and another series of squall lines moved across the area through the day on March 31st. Several tornadoes and areas of damaging winds occurred across the greater Tampa Bay area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire on the 9500 block of County Road 125C just southwest of Lake Miona.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the late morning and early afternoon of April 23rd along and north of a stationary front draped across southeast Illinois. One of the thunderstorms produced a lightning strike which destroyed a shed and its contents in rural southern Shelby County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a propane line and quickly spred to an 8 foot by 12 foot shed. The shed was quickly engulfed in flames and was a total loss. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved onshore from central Lake Michigan into Northwest Lower Michigan.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree, which toppled onto a home, and catching the home on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several supercell thunderstorms produced heavy rain and some hail during the late afternoon and evening hours. These occurred along and north of a nearly stalled warm front which extended across southern portions of north Alabama into east central Alabama.  A few of these storms produced hail and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a house, which was then on fire.  Four people were at home and got out of the house safely.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Mohave Point on the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.  One park visitor was killed and five others were injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning killed a 64-year-old woman visiting the Grand Canyon National Park. It is unclear if the lightning directly hit the victim. Five additional park visitors, ages 45 to 68,  were also injured.  The event took place at Mohave Point.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level short wave disturbance moving over the area combined with a cold front that was settling into the area and allowed for a few thunderstorms with strong gusty winds and a widespread area of two to four inches of rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, causing minor structural damage and igniting a small fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system over the northeast Gulf of Mexico moved northeast across northern Florida and sent a squall line through the area. The thunderstorms brought damaging winds, large hail, minor flooding and a few weak tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning at Central State College in Lecanto, causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved through the area ahead of a cold front and lightning struck a tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and blew pieces of the tree in all directions. No other trees or structures in the vicinity were affected.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A sub-severe line of thunderstorms moved through the southern counties. Lightning struck a house in Leon County and ignited a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near the intersection of Farm-to-Market Road 3175 and Farm-to-Market Road 542. The bolt caused a fire after a gas line ignited. Fire crews from the Centerville Volunteer Fire Department were dispatched to the residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms gradually intensified along and ahead of a cold front from Arkansas into western Kentucky. The storms occurred in a moist and strongly sheared environment, resulting in a combination of line segments and supercells which evolved into a quasi-linear convective system. There were isolated tornadoes, along with a couple small swaths of damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained spotter was taking shelter during a tornado warning with two other individuals. After the storm, while coming out of their place of shelter, lightning struck a few feet above her. The lightning sent showers of sparks and burned a hole in the building she was standing beside. The lightning threw her ten feet from a sidewalk onto a gravel drive, causing some scratches and bruises.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning east of Durango produced significant damage and knocked out power for many area residents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a communications tower near the 8000 foot level on Grassy Mountain between Vallecito and the Forest Lakes subdivision.  The communications tower and nearby facilities were heavily damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system moved across Middle Tennessee during the evening hours on Thursday, February 24th. This system produced several severe thunderstorms, resulting in mainly tornadic and straight line wind damage events across several counties in the mid state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House located on Butt Road in North Central Sumner County was struck by lightning around 430 am. Details concerning any structural damage and associated cost were unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning east of Durango produced significant damage and knocked out power for many area residents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Tri-State Generation and Transmission substation in Bayfield, damaging the station's electronics.  This resulted in a power outage that lasted nearly an hour for over 10,500 residents in eastern La Plata County and Archuleta County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours of April 26 as an upper level trough and cold front approached our region.  Several low topped supercells developed and produced numerous reports of large hail up to around two inches in diameter.  In addition a damage survey team from the NWS Grand Rapids office determined that damage caused near Burnips in Allegan County was due to an EF-0 tornado with top winds near 85 mph that damaged buildings at the Deboer Turkey Farm and trailers around the area.  In Portage, nine people were injured by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Nine people were injured when lightning struck a soccer field in Portage at Westfield Park.  The injured were a mix of adults and students who ranged in age from 12 to 41.  Seven people were transported to area hospitals and two sought treatment on their own.  One man who was injured most seriously went into cardiac arrest before being treated and released from Bronson hospital in Kalamazoo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm produced a destructive lightning strike which hit a house and completely burned it down.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: KY3-TV reported a home completely destroyed by fire likely caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system that moved across northern Illinois from Iowa received plenty of moisture from the Gulf of Mexico.  The abundant Gulf moisture allowed the late-season storm to produce plenty of heavy, wet snow and occasional thundersnow across parts of central and northeast Wisconsin on March 22nd-23rd.  During the two-day period, many locations received more than a foot of snow.  Lightning from the storm destroyed a house in Marathon County.||The high water content of the snow caused more problems than would normally be expected with storms having similar snowfall totals.  In Marathon County, a squad car was stuck in the snow for three hours on the 23rd, and two plow trucks that tried to push it free also became stuck.  Plows in Marathon County not only became stuck in the snow, but several broke down mechanically attempting to clear the snow from the road.  A buildup of hardened snow caused a freight car to derail behind a paper mill in Rhinelander (Oneida Co.) on the afternoon of the 23rd.  The weight of the snow from this storm caused the roof to collapse at a consignment shop on the west side of Green Bay (Brown Co.) on the evening of March 28th.||Some of the highest snowfall totals from across the area included 18.8 inches at Shawano (Shawano Co.), 18.0 inches at Irma (Lincoln Co.), 17.8 inches at Green Bay, 17.0 inches at Peshtigo (Marinette Co.) and Oconto (Oconto Co.), 16.0 inches at Casco (Kewaunee Co.), 14.8 inches at Rhinelander, 14.6 inches near Laona (Forest Co.), 14.5 inches at Sturgeon Bay (Door Co.), 13.5 inches near Big Falls (Waupaca Co.) and 12.1 inches at Mosinee (Marathon Co.).||The 17.8 inches of snow that fell in Green Bay was the most from a single storm in more than 120 years.  It was also the third highest storm total since Green Bay weather records began in 1886.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning fire destroyed a house in the Town of Knowlton.  A woman and her dog were home at the time of the fire but were able to escape without injury.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of quasi-discrete storms intensified as it moved across the Mid Mississippi Valley into a destabilizing atmosphere. A relatively narrow plume of richer low level moisture characterized by upper 50's dew points moved north into southeast Missouri. As an upper level storm system approached the region, cold temperatures aloft fostered hail growth in the stronger storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on County Road 449 north of Sikeston, causing a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure lifted north into Iowa during the day on the 24th.  A weak short wave lifted northeast across the boundary.  Strong thunderstorms fired to the south of Iowa and became enhanced as they interacted with the boundary.  The atmosphere became moderately unstable with CAPE around 1000 to 1500 J/kg and lifted indices fell to around -6 C.  The CAPE in the hail producing level was not all that high, but the freezing level was only 11,000 feet.  Numerous reports of pea to slightly larger size hail were received.  Downdraft CAPE was in the 700 to 1000 J/kg range.  Shear was relatively weak with 20 to 30 kts of shear available.  As the line lifted through central Iowa, which was during peak heating, it intensified.  There were numerous reports of 50 MPH winds all along the line as it extended from west central, through central, into southeast Iowa.  One segment of the line became severe and produced 60 to 70 MPH winds at several locations in central Iowa.  A few funnel clouds were observed as well.  A grain bin and shed were damaged south of Jamaica in Guthrie County.  Scattered tree and outbuilding damage occurred across Dallas, Polk, and into Marshall Counties.  A exit sign was blown down by the high winds south of Woodward in Dallas County.  Lightning struck an accounting building near Charition, blowing out bricks from the building and damaging some electrical components.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the area during the early morning hours of April 11th. Scattered thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper reported a residence in the 300 block of East Stocker Street, in Angola, was struck by lightning, causing an attic fire. The residents were home at the time of the lightning strike and escaped without injuries. An estimated $55,000 in damage was caused to the attic area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Glenridge area, igniting a fire that completely destroyed the home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a night time thunderstorm struck the KNGN radio tower in McCook, Nebraska, damaging the main and backup power sources and knocking the station off the air for several days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Time is estimated from radar.  Newspaper account only mentioned the strike occurred during the overnight hours.  Three separate rounds of thunderstorms moved through the McCook area overnight.  Radar indicated one such storm moved through around midnight CDT time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms moved across parts of northeast and eastern Illinois during the morning hours of May 25th producing a tornado near St. Anne as well as heavy rain and some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A two story, eight unit apartment building was struck by lightning.  The roof was engulfed in flames and the building was a total loss.  All of the 15 occupants were able to exit the building safely and no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep, slow moving, negatively tiltled and highly diffluent upper trough was sweeping from the south central into the southeast U.S. during the April 15th and 16th period.  A strong Pacific cold front accompanied the upper-level trough.  An unseasonably warm, moist and unstable air mass was present across the southeast U.S. in advance of this weather system.  An initial line of strong to severe thunderstorms began to move into northwest Georgia during the late afternoon hours of April 15th.  As the line progressed further into the state, it evolved more in a large area of showers and thunderstorms with discrete supercells across especially central Georgia.  These supercells produced damaging winds, hail, and three tornadoes.  As the event continued into the early morning hours of the 16th, the severity decreased, but widespread rain and thunderstorms, along with isolated severe thunderstorms continued until around daybreak.  In addition to the severe weather events, the prolonged and heavy rain event resulted in flash flooding along north Atlanta metropolitan area creeks and streams.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The public reported that lightning struck a home on Georgia Highway 34 in Franklin setting the house on fire.  The house was completely destroyed by the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad and increasingly diffluent upper trough was digging into the south central U.S. with broad southwest flow increasing across the southeast U.S. on the back side of a subtropical ridge located across the western Atlantic.  This trough eventually set the stage for the historical and catastrophic tornado outbreak that commenced just two days later on the 27th.  On this day, however, the atmosphere across Georgia, being unseasonably warm and humid, supported widespread development of pulse-type thunderstorms.  Several of these storms became strong to severe and produced large hail and damaging downburst winds.  The most significant damage on the east side of Columbus in Muscogee county where a strong downburst blew down several hundred trees and destroyed two trailer homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cherokee County Emergency Management Director reported that lightning struck and set on fire yet a second home in Cherokee county.  This time the incident was five miles east of Woodstock in the far southeast corner of the county.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As an upper-level disturbance interacted with a stationary frontal boundary draped across southern Illinois, thunderstorms developed during the pre-dawn hours of April 9th.  The storms remained along and south of a Winchester...to Taylorville...to Charleston-Mattoon line.  A few of the cells produced hail up to quarter-sized and locally heavy rainfall. One storm produced a lightning strike in Springfield which destroyed a vacant church.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the steeple of a church at 16th and South Grand Avenue in Springfield, starting a fire which quickly engulfed the building. The church was no longer being used, but still contained pews, books and an organ. The building and its contents were a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous severe thunderstorms developed along a dryline as an upper level disturbance approached north Texas. The atmosphere was very unstable and perfectly primed for supercell thunderstorms. The severe weather primarily affected areas south and east of an Erath to Cooke County line due to the positions of the dryline and a southward moving cold front. Hail up to the size of tennis balls and downburst winds up to 80-90 mph occurred across portions of the region. There was also 11 EF-0 tornadoes confirmed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22 year-old male was struck by lightning while working outdoors in Star Harbor. It is believed that lightning struck the tree next to him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold pool of air aloft triggered isolated thunderstorms across northeast New Jersey, with one lightning strike reported near Newark.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Rose Terrace in Cedar Grove, causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe storms developed along a warm front that stretched from Indiana southeast into the Carolinas. An upper level disturbance helped to trigger the storms in the mid-afternoon over southwest Virginia and then developed eastward mainly across the Mountain Empire and the New River Valley. The storms also produced heavy rainfall with several stations in Montgomery County reporting over an inch of rain in a short period, including Christiansburg 1.8S CoCoRaHs 1.61���, Christiansburg 1S COOP 1.56���, Falling Branch IFLOWS 1.46��� and Brush Mtn. IFLOWS 1.26���.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire at a home with significant damage reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold pool of air aloft triggered isolated thunderstorms across southeast New York, with one lightning strike reported in Upper Manhattan.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the top of the building located at 621 West 188th Street, near Wadsworth Avenue in Upper Manhattan.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms erupted overnight ahead of a strong cold front moving through north Texas. These storms developed into a line that moved east and southeast through mainly the eastern half of north Texas. Hail up to the size of ping pong balls was reported with the largest hail stones falling in Watauga. Severe thunderstorm winds also knocked down trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a propane tank on Hwy 19 causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous severe thunderstorms developed along a dryline as an upper level disturbance approached north Texas. The atmosphere was very unstable and perfectly primed for supercell thunderstorms. The severe weather primarily affected areas south and east of an Erath to Cooke County line due to the positions of the dryline and a southward moving cold front. Hail up to the size of tennis balls and downburst winds up to 80-90 mph occurred across portions of the region. There was also 11 EF-0 tornadoes confirmed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house between Commerce and Campbell was struck by lightning and ignited a small fire. The rain put the fire out and damage was limited to television equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong late-season surface low pressure system crossed central Illinois into Lower Michigan on the 19th, bringing a variety of weather to southern Wisconsin. A tight 850 mb to 700 mb baroclinic zone over the region set up a strong frontogenetic response and isentropic lift with a strengthening low level flow ahead of the low...with rain showers and a few strong thunderstorms on the warm side of the system...and heavy wet snow to the north. The precipitation rates were enhanced by elevated instability and a strong dynamic contribution with the vigorous 500 mb short wave trough leading to thunder snow in the northern counties and a severe thunderstorm in Rock County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole, destroying an insulator and caused an electrical wire to break and fall to the ground. 500 homes and businesses were left without power on the east side of Plymouth, until repairs were made and all power was restored around 915 pm CDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large cluster of thunderstorms increased in coverage and intensity as it accelerated eastward into a rapidly destabilizing air mass. The activity was closely related to a mid-level shortwave trough moving across Iowa and Missouri, along with a low level wind maximum. The storms were associated with isolated large hail, damaging winds, and a tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank battery, causing them to explode.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that moved across extreme southern New Jersey exacerbated the ongoing strong synoptic scale southeast winds already in place during the evening of the 16th and produced wind damage. In addition, a lightning strike caused damage to a home in Ocean County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and subsequent fire engulfed a home on Merion Lane in Jackson Township. The house suffered extensive structural damage and a Honda Pilot was also badly damaged. Seven fire companies battled the blaze. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An historic tornado outbreak affected areas from the Deep South to the Mid-Atlantic states April 27-28. A strong tornado touched down in Rabun County late on the 27th, with additional tornadoes affecting the North Carolina foothills during the early morning hours of the 28th. At least three supercell thunderstorms crossed the western Carolinas and northeast Georgia during this time. A greater number of supercells and tornadoes affected areas to the west of the Appalachians. Scattered areas of straight line wind damage and large hail also accompanied the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Finley Forest area, igniting a fire that destroyed the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of the 24th, a stalled frontal boundary extended through northwestern Arkansas and far southeastern Oklahoma. This boundary began to lift to the north with widespread showers and thunderstorms initiating north of the boundary and affecting much of northwestern Arkansas. Recent heavy rains had saturated the ground and the additional heavy rainfall with this activity resulted in widespread flash flooding. Large hail was also observed with the stronger storms. The activity continued into the early morning hours of the 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire. The house was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms initiated over the mountains of North Carolina during the afternoon hours. As the afternoon progressed, several supercell thunderstorms developed which tracked southeast across the foothills and piedmont along a slow moving surface cold front. With unusually steep lapse rates over the region, several of the storms produced large hail. Fortunately the supercells were a little elevated in nature, and only one, brief, weak tornado developed. Still, hail ranging up to the size of a softballs did quite a bit of damage over the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Nine people were injured and several dogs were killed when lightning struck the Burke County Fairgrounds during a dog show.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms moved across parts of northeast and eastern Illinois during the morning hours of May 25th producing a tornado near St. Anne as well as heavy rain and some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on 3rd street in Sandwich was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance and associated dryline approaching from the west interacted with an unstable air mass in place across the eastern half of Kansas, producing numerous strong to severe thunderstorms from the late afternoon on the 19th into the morning on the 20th over primarily central and north-central Kansas. A handful of relatively weak tornadoes touched down over Russell county, along with up to golfball size hail and 60 mph winds across the area. Additionally, very heavy rainfall produced flash flooding over portions of Russell and Lincoln counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire near 29th and Tyler. The fire was brought under control rather quickly, but still produced quite a bit of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance and associated dryline approaching from the west interacted with an unstable air mass in place across the eastern half of Kansas, producing numerous strong to severe thunderstorms from the late afternoon on the 19th into the morning on the 20th over primarily central and north-central Kansas. A handful of relatively weak tornadoes touched down over Russell county, along with up to golfball size hail and 60 mph winds across the area. Additionally, very heavy rainfall produced flash flooding over portions of Russell and Lincoln counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a large oil tank reservoir several miles west of Cheney in rural Kingman county during the early evening hours on the 19th. Strong southeasterly winds hampered the firefighter's efforts, but they eventually extinguished the large fire later that evening. The Cheney Times-Sentinel contributed to this report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the evening of 4 April 2011, a fast moving and intense cold front moved southeast into a very warm, moist and unstable air mass along the Alabama and northwest Florida Gulf Coasts.  Immediately along and ahead of the cold front, a line of severe thunderstorms, already ongoing, moved out of southeast Mississippi during the early evening and progressed across southern Alabama and the western Florida Panhandle through midnight.||In total, there were numerous reports of tree and power line damage as the squall line moved through. There were no known deaths or injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Air conditioning unit took a direct lightning strike resulting in smoke inside a residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the evening of 4 April 2011, a fast moving and intense cold front moved southeast into a very warm, moist and unstable air mass along the Alabama and northwest Florida Gulf Coasts.  Immediately along and ahead of the cold front, a line of severe thunderstorms, already ongoing, moved out of southeast Mississippi during the early evening and progressed across southern Alabama and the western Florida Panhandle through midnight.||In total, there were numerous reports of tree and power line damage as the squall line moved through. There were no known deaths or injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike to a motor home resulted in a small fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance and associated frontal boundary interacted with a moist and unstable air mass to produce a couple rounds of widespread strong to severe thunderstorms across central, south-central and southeast Kansas during the afternoon and evening hours on the 24th. A handful of tornadoes occurred across central Kansas, some of which produced damage and an injury. Straight-line thunderstorm winds of 60 to 80 mph also affected many locations, producing areas of damage. Large hail was not as prevalent, although some stones did reach one inch in diameter.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A small fire at a Great Bend apartment complex was reportedly started by lightning. Property damage amounts are rough estimates.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long lived quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) developed in northern and central Mississippi and tracked eastward through northern Alabama during the early morning hours of the 20th.  A bow echo with a strong meso-vortex produced a long swath of wind damage from southern Franklin across Lawrence, Morgan, Cullman and Marshall counties.  Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped, indicating wind speeds of at least 70 mph or higher.  Trees were toppled onto two homes in Morgan and Cullman counties resulting in two injuries.  As the bow echo continued eastward, numerous reports of trees and damage to small structures were reported.   Following the storms, a meteorological phenomenon known as a wake low developed which produced a short period of damaging non-thunderstorm winds in Marshall County.  A wind gust of 60 mph was registered with this system at the Albertville, Alabama AWOS station (K8A0).  Several power outages were reported through the event.||A mesoscale convective system rolled through northern and central Alabama during the late evening hours of the 20th, and exited shortly after midnight on the 21st. Prolific lightning was generated with mainly elevated thunderstorms within the anvil region of this system across northern Alabama. A line of strong to severe thunderstorms extended south from the upper level circulation center which tracked east from northwest and west central Alabama. The storms produced sporadic thunderstorm wind damage, knocking down several trees in Franklin County. Most of the damage further east were tree limbs that did cause isolated small power outages. Although most areas received one half to one inch of rainfall, there were local amounts of one to just over two inches. This resulted in mostly nuisance minor street flooding, although one road was closed in Franklin County due to more substantial runoff.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a car and set it on fire near the town of Vina.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms produced wind damage and some 3/4 inch hail around the Midlands of South Carolina.  Most of the wind damage was from trees being blown down.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Spotter reported a barn was completely destroyed be fire caused from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep, slow moving, negatively tiltled and highly diffluent upper trough was sweeping from the south central into the southeast U.S. during the April 15th and 16th period.  A strong Pacific cold front accompanied the upper-level trough.  An unseasonably warm, moist and unstable air mass was present across the southeast U.S. in advance of this weather system.  An initial line of strong to severe thunderstorms began to move into northwest Georgia during the late afternoon hours of April 15th.  As the line progressed further into the state, it evolved more in a large area of showers and thunderstorms with discrete supercells across especially central Georgia.  These supercells produced damaging winds, hail, and three tornadoes.  As the event continued into the early morning hours of the 16th, the severity decreased, but widespread rain and thunderstorms, along with isolated severe thunderstorms continued until around daybreak.  In addition to the severe weather events, the prolonged and heavy rain event resulted in flash flooding along north Atlanta metropolitan area creeks and streams.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett County 911 Center reported that at least two homes in the Norcross area were struck by lightning.  One of these, a two-story home, was set on fire and completely destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large outflow boundary initiated by previous showers and thunderstorms over northern Arkansas during the day Monday spread south into the Four State Region during the late afternoon and evening. This boundary helped with the development of showers and thunderstorms that interacted with other isolated and smaller scale outflow boundaries to produce scattered strong to severe thunderstorms that contained locally heavy rainfall, frequent and continuous lightning strikes, and gusty winds of 30 to near 45 mph and isolated higher gusts. These gusts downed trees and power lines. Daytime temperatures were near the century mark Around nightfall the storms went into a decreasing cycle with loss of the afternoon heating. However, during the evening, remnants of a sea breeze boundary spread north across parts of East Texas and lower Northwest and North Central Louisiana and collided with the south bound boundary, allowing storms to increase in intensity as they moved across parts of Louisiana just prior to midnight.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike touched off a fire that killed an elderly couple at their home in Greenwood, Louisiana.  Killed in the fire was Ralph Elliott, 83 and his wife Mary, 83.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over southern West Virginia and eastern Kentucky during the heat and humidity of this June afternoon.  The storms moved northeast into southeast Ohio by the early evening.  Despite the high freezing level, some large hail still occurred.  The rapid temperature drop from near 90 to 70 degrees also helped produced some damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a nursing home, damaging its roof and causing a small electrical fire.  Through the smoke and the water pouring down from the sprinklers, nurses moved several inhabitants to another wing of the building or outside.  A few residents were carried through an open window.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper air disturbance supplied the cold air aloft and an unstable atmosphere to help trigger scattered to numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening of the 19th. Because the air was cold aloft, many of the thunderstorms produced hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a transformer on State Street in East Stroudsburg caused around 1,100 homes and businesses to lose power in Stroudsburg, East Stroudsburg and Delaware Water Gap. All power was restored by 8 p.m. EDT that evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system moved over the Pacific Northwest. Moist and unstable conditions ahead of the low triggered widespread thunderstorms with heavy rainfall and isolated large hail. This combined with the abundant spring snow-pack and wet ground to cause flooding. A 75 yard wide mudslide closed Highway 410 at milepost 87. As the upper low brought colder air. late season heavy snow ended the episode in the Blue Mountains.  Snowfall amounts in inches included Touchet Snotel (7).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a roof fire which damaged a few other rooms of a residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of showers and thunderstorms moved through central and northern New Jersey during the morning of the 30th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike in Brielle downed some wires near Agnes Road and New Jersey State Route 71. About 500 homes and businesses lost power for six and a half hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: North Alabama averted most of the severe weather associated with a large severe weather outbreak across the deep South.  An initial area of elevated thunderstorms followed by a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) moved through during the morning hours ahead of a northward advancing warm front.  The front eventually reached northern Alabama, but persistent rain and thunderstorms through the day limited the instability available to fuel a more widespread severe weather threat during the afternoon and evening hours.   Rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches resulted in brief  flooding of small creeks near Florence and Tuscumbia, and more nuisance minor street flooding elsewhere.||As the strong cold front and upper level trough approached during the evening,   a thunderstorm and meso-cyclone was responsible for knocking a couple of trees down in DeKalb County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole at he intersection of Jefferson Street and U.S. Highway 72.  A live wire fell on a vehicle waiting in the drive-thru line of a fast food restaurant.  No injuries were reported.  Power was knocked out at several businesses and the traffic signal for several hours.
