EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Various synoptic scale and mesoscale features, such as the right entrance region of the upper jet, a short wave moving in aloft, the sea breeze and differential heating boundaries from morning cloud cover.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported a house fire due to a lightning strike along Pine Island View in Mount Pleasant. Extent and cost of damage is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Abundant moisture and hot temperatures allowed for an unstable environment across far southern Lower Michigan. A thermal boundary developed on the edge of a cloud canopy across northern Indiana. This allowed for increased convergence and resulted in isolated pulse thunderstorms developing. Upper level energy moved in during the late afternoon, aiding in some intensification of the storms, mainly in St Joseph and Cass counties where isolated severe weather occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local fire officials and media reported a lightning strike caused an attic fire in the Westchase Apartments complex. Smoke was reported from one of the complexes and the fire was quickly located in the attic. Only one apartment suffered moderate damage when fire crews had to pull the ceiling down to access the area of the fire in the attic. The remaining fire and smoke damage was confined to the attic. No damage estimates were provided, but will be set at $10,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line developed from Montgomery County to Harris County (from about Conroe to just North of the Houston City limit). The showers and thunderstorms developed from many places reaching their convective temperatures in the afternoon, kind of like a classic loaded gun sounding case, when the cap is broken in the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A building fire was caused by a lightning strike at 26 Sawmill Grove Place in the Woodlands. Time estimation via the radar and lightning plot show the strike could've occurred any time between 2-305 pm CST.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms across southeast Texas produced heavy rain and frequent lightning. One fatality occurred due to a lightning strike in Harris County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A utility worker was killed by a lightning strike while trying to repair a power line near the intersection of Miller Road 1 and Miller Road 2. The man was initially revived at the scene but died the next day on July 1st.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level low sagging down the Pacific Northwest Coastline was responsible for drawing moist, unstable air northward into Northern Idaho. A combination of surface heating and shortwave energy ejecting from the low triggered strong thunderstorms over Northern Idaho during the afternoon of July 17th.  Two thunderstorms that afternoon tracked over a similar stretch of Highway 95 just east of Culdesac.  Heavy rainfall from the training thunderstorms, steep terrain, and an overwhelmed culvert were responsible for portions of the hillside at milepost 287, along Highway 95, to washout.  These storms also produced wind gusts around 60 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Non-severe thunderstorms during the early morning of July 17th, produced frequent lightning strikes in and around the Post Falls area.  One bolt struck a man in his car while driving to work. The man did not receive any injuries from the strike however his car's sensors were damaged and he lost all power control while driving, including the brakes. He was able to safely pull the vehicle to the side of the road then noticed the car could not be turned off even without the key in the ignition. Two tires were also blown out from the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level short wave trough moved over the forecast area during the day. This feature combined with a dominant west coast sea breeze over a moist and unstable airmass fueled scattered strong storms with locally heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men working in a bucket truck were struck by lightning at the 8800 block of Moncrief Dinsmore Road around 1 pm. One man was in the truck at the time. Both men were taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across central North Carolina and interacted with moderate to strong instability to trigger scattered showers and thunderstorms. Several of these storms became severe and produced damaging winds and a few isolated severe hail reports.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire at 1345 Legendary Lane was reported from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved across central North Carolina and interacted with moderate to strong instability to trigger scattered showers and thunderstorms. Several of these storms became severe and produced damaging winds and a few isolated severe hail reports.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire was reported at 106 Carterwood Court, caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An amplified ridge over the central U.S. set the stage for scattered to numerous severe storms during the day as several short-wave disturbances dropped southeast across the southern Appalachians while surface conditions became remained very warm and unstable under the intense early July sun. Surface temperatures approached 100F over the piedmont during the afternoon creating steep lapse rates as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was caused by lightning on Gap Trail Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a sea breeze front and also ahead of an approaching cold front, producing pockets of very heavy rain and some wind damage across parts of New Jersey, eastern Pennsylvania, and Delaware during the afternoon and evening of the 22nd.  One of the hardest hit areas was Cumberland and Salem Counties where power was out in some locations until the 24th. Atlantic City Electric reported that roughly 16,000 of its customers lost power at the height of the storm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck and injured a person at Fort Hancock at 2:30 pm EDT on the 22nd. Lightning struck ten other buildings at the Gateway National Recreational Area at Sandy Hook, but no serious damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms over eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania weakened during the morning hours of the 5th.  However, a strong outflow boundary from this convection pushed south.  By late morning, the heating of the unstable air combined with the outflow boundary to trigger additional storms that pushed south across West Virginia, reaching Virginia by mid afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Kanawha Metro 911 building was struck by lightning after most of the rain had already moved south.  Phone lines, radios, and computers were destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms rolled southeast from southeast Missouri and western Tennessee during the evening of the 30th, and through northeast Mississippi into northwest Alabama during the early morning hours of the 31st. The most severe storm produced storm tops well above 60000 feet, and knocked down or snapped several trees along it's path in Colbert and Franklin Counties. Prolific lightning was noted as well, with several power outages reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a house fire on the 800 block of Leanord Road.  Exact time of event unknown.  Extent of damage unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were killed when they sought refuge under a tree during a thunderstorm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men who were playing soccer were killed by a lightning strike while seeking shelter under a tree on the perimeter of the field. A third man was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms caused damaging lightning strikes in the Houston and Pasadena areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A television station reports a man was injured by a lightning strike at the Port of Houston.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The afternoon of Sunday, June 10th, a line of thunderstorms developed along a cold front across western Minnesota, and quickly became severe as they moved to the east-northeast across central and southern Minnesota.  Initially, large hail was the main hazard, but it evolved into severe downburst winds across eastern Minnesota as this line moved to the east.  There was one confirmed report of a tornado in northern Le Sueur County and southern Scott County. ||One area that had significant damage was across southern Ramsay County near Highland Park where numerous trees and large limbs were blown down. Some of the blown down tree limbs caused damage to cars.  Thousands of people lost electrical power as trees and power lines were toppled by severe thunderstorms that rattled through the southern metro area.  Lightning from these thunderstorms across eastern Minnesota struck a home in Apple Valley, and a pole barn in Washington County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a gas meter on one home on 131th Street Southwest. The lightning traveled along the gas line, skipping one house and igniting another house nearby.||One of the homes suffered significant damage as a result of the fire. There were no injuries in the fire, and one other house suffered minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The afternoon of Sunday, June 10th, a line of thunderstorms developed along a cold front across western Minnesota, and quickly became severe as they moved to the east-northeast across central and southern Minnesota.  Initially, large hail was the main hazard, but it evolved into severe downburst winds across eastern Minnesota as this line moved to the east.  There was one confirmed report of a tornado in northern Le Sueur County and southern Scott County. ||One area that had significant damage was across southern Ramsay County near Highland Park where numerous trees and large limbs were blown down. Some of the blown down tree limbs caused damage to cars.  Thousands of people lost electrical power as trees and power lines were toppled by severe thunderstorms that rattled through the southern metro area.  Lightning from these thunderstorms across eastern Minnesota struck a home in Apple Valley, and a pole barn in Washington County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Stillwater Fire Department spent more than three hours extinguishing a pole barn fire on the 12000 block of Lockridge Avenue North Sunday night due to a lightning strike. Damage to a 40-foot-by-50-foot pole barn was estimated at $350,000. ||Fire crews worked on the fire until 1:30 a.m. Monday. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the afternoon.  The lightning from one developing cell increased as it drifted through the Parkersburg vicinity.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: According to employees of the nearby 911 center, a developing thunderstorm started with a big crack of lightning.  An 18 year old boy, a recent high school graduate, was attending a summer church camp.  The boy was struck by lightning while playing left field during a softball game.  The bolt passed through his entire body.  His hair was singed.  His tennis shoes had holes in them.  He fell to his back and was stiff as a board.  He was not breathing and did not have a pulse.  Fellow teammates performed CPR for about 10 to 15 minutes until EMS arrived.  He was taken to a local hospital, then transported to a Morgantown hospital.  Eventually, he was sent to a burn center in Pittsburgh.  A week later he was recovering.  He was to be moved to a rehabilitation center which was closer to home.||Two other players were knocked to the ground during the strike, but were not injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper air disturbance combined with a lee side trof and another hot and humid July day to trigger widely scattered strong thunderstorms across Delaware during the late afternoon and evening of the 15th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire displaced more than a dozen residents in Marhsallton. (Mill Creek Hundred).  Lightning struck the rooftop of a three-story building in the Villages of Clay Creek along Melson Road. The lightning strike also hit a water pipe which hampered efforts to douse the flames.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad ridge over the central U.S. set the stage for scattered to numerous severe storms that developed in the early morning and persisted much of the day and into the night. The storms were triggered by the remains of a mesoscale convective system (MCS) that dropped southeast across the southern Appalachians in the morning hours while strong surface heating created a very unstable air mass as the day progressed. Strong wind shear, steep lapse rates and instability that was approaching 3000 J/kg by mid-morning contributed to the intensity of the storms. The Mountain Empire, New River Valley and Southside Virginia saw most of the activity which featured mainly severe, damaging high winds but also some hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A brush fire was caused by lightning on Tardy Mountain Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the region as an upper level trough and associated surface cold front approached the area from the northwest. Strong heating and high moisture content resulted in a moderately unstable air mass and with the increased low level forcing, as well as increasing upper level dynamics, several of the storms became strong to severe, producing some isolated wind damage. Also, frequent lightning also resulted in a couple of fires, one which completely destroyed a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike struck a home and caused a fire. The former plantation home, which is actually listed on the National Register of Historic Places, was completely destroyed, with only its three chimneys still standing. Damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line developed from Montgomery County to Harris County (from about Conroe to just North of the Houston City limit). The showers and thunderstorms developed from many places reaching their convective temperatures in the afternoon, kind of like a classic loaded gun sounding case, when the cap is broken in the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A detached garage was struck by lightning and destroyed by a fire at 19 West Willowood Court in the Woodlands. Time estimation by radar and lightning plot indicate the strike could've happened any time between 2-305 pm CST.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another strong shortwave swung across the Tennessee Valley on the 3rd.  Meanwhile, a lee side trough remained in place across central Georgia.  These two forcing mechanisms combined with continued strong daytime heating and low level moisture allowed another round of severe pulse convection to form during the afternoon hours.  Several severe thunderstorms developed, with large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast Media stations from Macon reported up to four structures on fire from lightning strikes.  Several units at an apartment complex on Leisure Lake Drive were heavily damaged or destroyed, displacing 16 families.  Before firefighters arrived, three Marines and an Army medic alerted and evacuated many of the residents, including an 87-year-old woman confined to her bed.  No one was injured in the fire, thanks in part to the quick actions of the servicemen.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms resulted in several reports of damaging wind gusts and large hail.  Several trees were blown down.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A construction barn was destroyed by a lightning strike near Rosebush.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a sea breeze front and also ahead of an approaching cold front, producing pockets of very heavy rain and some wind damage across parts of New Jersey, eastern Pennsylvania, and Delaware during the afternoon and evening of the 22nd.  One of the hardest hit areas was Cumberland and Salem Counties where power was out in some locations until the 24th. Atlantic City Electric reported that roughly 16,000 of its customers lost power at the height of the storm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm caused a house fire in Stafford Township at 12:30 pm EDT on the 22nd. The house burned to the ground, but no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front produced showers and thunderstorms, a few of which became severe producing both large hail and gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three children were struck by lightning while playing outside at a Fourth of July party.  Lightning struck the backyard where the children were playing.  The 5 year old, 13 year old, and 14 year old were all transported to Hasbro Children's hospital for non-life threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm produced lightning damage in Wilmington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a tree and a fence on Jackson Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed along the seabreeze front and caused thunderstorm wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: County Sheriffs Office reported a tree was struck by lightning and fell on a house on Allwood Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning squall line moved across the area and produced some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire in the attic of a house.  Damage was mostly contained to the attic and part of the second floor of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through southern New England setting off showers and thunderstorms.  Lightning strikes caused the most damage, hitting tress, houses, and transformers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Dartmouth Street was struck by lightning and caught fire.  Most of the damage was to the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours on July 19th, a convective system moved southeast across southern Ohio and eastern Kentucky. This left behind an outflow boundary that extended from near Madison, Indiana southeast through the Kentucky Bluegrass. A couple of strong storms developed by mid afternoon along this boundary and brought isolated wind damage to the Bluegrass Region. Later that afternoon, scattered severe storms developed under highly unstable conditions across southern Indiana, aided by the approach of a southward moving upper level disturbance. As these storms crossed the Ohio River, they grew upscale into several bowing segments. By evening, two of these segments merged south of Louisville into a squall line that brought widespread damaging winds to much of central Kentucky. Most locations experienced a strong gust front with at least 45 mph winds. Several Kentucky mesonet sites measured winds in excess of 58 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the 3900th block on third street. It started a fire in the basement that eventually consumed the house. Two people did not make it out of the house and died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that developed across the Dakotas early Thursday morning, May 3rd, moved into portions of west-central, and central Minnesota. A few of these storms produced large hail.  These storms caused another thunderstorm complex to develop in east-central Minnesota, and move eastward into west-central Wisconsin during the mid to late morning of May 3rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local authorities indicated that lightning struck a home in Rogers, Minnesota, early Thursday morning, May 3rd.  The lightning started a fire that caused extensive damage to the roof and lesser damage to the second floor of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A little more than a day after a thunderstorm system brought more severe weather to the Rio Grande Valley, the last vestige of very unstable air held forth mainly along and east of Highway 77. Despite unfavorable upper level conditions, the combination of the unstable air with a trigger in the form of a wind shift/dry line which moved within striking distance of Highway 77 allowed a small but potent cluster of thunderstorms to explosively grow initially in northern Willacy County just before 4 PM CDT. These storms would produce south���moving outflows, which added to the dryline trigger. Additional storms would fire in only a half hour, working on the very unstable atmosphere (above right) to increase updraft speed and develop quarter to half dollar sized hail ��� at least ��� between west Harlingen and La Feria and points south between 515 and 545 PM. Once again, there was some damage to vehicles caught in the hail, much containing jagged edges. Many residents caught by surprise by the rapid development moved their vehicles under gas station canopies, car washes, and highway underpasses.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Palm Valley resident reported 5 palm trees set on fire by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms moved along a stationary front and produced damaging winds and large hail across southwest and central Wisconsin in the morning hours of May 3rd. A National Weather Service employee reported a couple of trees knocked down in Holmen (La Crosse). One inch diameter size hail fell in Big Flats (Adams County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and caught a house on fire northwest of Melrose. The house was totally destroyed by the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance interacted with a very warm and humid air mass in place across the region allowing several severe thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon. Wind damage occurred as a result of these storms, in addition to damage as a result of lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning resulting in a fire that burned the house down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance interacted with a very warm and humid air mass in place across the region allowing several severe thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon. Wind damage occurred as a result of these storms, in addition to damage as a result of lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a transformer fire at Jones County Junior College. The fire caused damage to an adjacent building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the region under the influence of a weak shortwave. Most of the rain activity occurred along and east of the I-35 corridor. A few storms in Anderson County grew strong enough in the late afternoon hours to produce large hail. Softball sized hail was reported near Tennessee Colony.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on the 1600 block of Creek Court was struck by lightning. The attic above the garage was damaged by a fire that started as a result of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the region under the influence of a weak shortwave. Most of the rain activity occurred along and east of the I-35 corridor. A few storms in Anderson County grew strong enough in the late afternoon hours to produce large hail. Softball sized hail was reported near Tennessee Colony.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on the 5500 block of Alexander Dr in Fort Worth was struck by lightning. A woman at the home was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Palm City. Significant damage resulted from the strike and subsquent fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home sustained damage estimated at $500,000 due to a fire which started after the home was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance pushed a cold front through southern New England, resulting in showers and thunderstorms.  With plenty of instability available, some of the storms became severe, producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Hyde Park Avenue was struck by lightning, starting a fire.  The second and third floors were engulfed in flames before the fire department was able to put it out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heat and humidity contributed to the development of isolated thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 22nd, resulting in isolated wind damage and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex on Ellis Dr. in Little Rock, starting a fire. Several apartments were destroyed and a few others were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of disturbances pushed through the region, resulting in the development of showers and thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced frequent lightning and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front surged northward through North Mississippi into Southwest Tennessee during the evening hours of April 27th, 2013. As a result, several severe thunderstorms developed behind the front in the very unstable atmosphere. The storms produced damaging winds and large hail. One brief tornado also occurred as two storms merged together.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three horses were struck by lightning and killed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moving through the Missouri Ozarks along with a cold front developed severe storms which produced widespread wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house which caused damage to the kitchen.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance pushed a cold front through southern New England, resulting in showers and thunderstorms.  With plenty of instability available, some of the storms became severe, producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on South Central Street was struck by lightning, igniting a fire in the attic.  It extended to a bedroom and caused significant structural damage and damaged the chimney.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed ahead of an advancing cold front on the afternoon and evening of the 10th. A few tornadoes occurred, and there were also reports of large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a house, burning it to the ground. Three all-terrain vehicles were also destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance and cooling air in the upper levels resulted in steepening mid-level lapse rates, producing showers and thunderstorms.  A warm, unstable environment allowed these storms to become severe, with several storms producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, knocking it down onto a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance and cooling air in the upper levels resulted in steepening mid-level lapse rates, producing showers and thunderstorms.  A warm, unstable environment allowed these storms to become severe, with several storms producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on East Street in Hingham, igniting a fire.  The amount of damage to the home is unknown at this time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed ahead of an advancing cold front on the afternoon and evening of the 10th. A few tornadoes occurred, and there were also reports of large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a multi-family dwelling in Maumelle, starting a fire. There was extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm associated with a trough of low pressure produced lightning damage across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at Kindbird Lane causing extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front on the 29th, and a few of the storms became severe. There was spotty wind damage and a couple of weak tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person inside a house was shocked by lightning. The person was not transported to a hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low pressure system passed by to the northwest of Arkansas on the 25th and 26th. There were numerous reports of hail on the 25th, due to the cold air aloft associated with the low pressure. In many cases, the hail was small but there were great quantities of it. The ground was covered by hail in quite a few places, and hail even piled up on roads in the more extreme cases. After cold air spilled into Arkansas on the back side of the low pressure system, light snow fell in Boone County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home just northeast of Mena. The clothes dryer was destroyed and part of the wall behind the dryer was burned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure tracking out of the Plains was responsible for scattered thunderstorms across central Illinois during the afternoon and evening of May 9th.  One storm produced wind damage to a few structures in rural Coles County, while another caused a lightning strike and ensuing fire in Clay County.  Yet another cell produced a brief tornado in an open field in Christian County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Ten oil tank batteries were ignited by a lightning strike west of Ingraham.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rains caused flooding in northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a small utility shed causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance and cooling air in the upper levels resulted in steepening mid-level lapse rates, producing showers and thunderstorms.  A warm, unstable environment allowed these storms to become severe, with several storms producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a camper, then a shed on Labelle Street, igniting a fire in the shed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With a stationary front inland and High pressure off the coast, very moist air moved in from the south, which combined with a sea breeze, produced some afternoon thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck powerboxes and caused a fire at townhomes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With a stationary front inland and High pressure off the coast, very moist air moved in from the south, which combined with a sea breeze, produced some afternoon thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was struck by lightning and transported to hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms around the Midlands and portions of the CSRA produced large hail, damaging winds, and localized flooding in low lying areas from heavy rains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: EM reported 9 homes were struck by lightning and damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a dissipating nearly stationary front. The thunderstorms produced frequent lightning across Southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An athlete was indirectly affected by lightning during a outdoor practice. Extent of the injuries are unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a dissipating nearly stationary front. The thunderstorms produced frequent lightning across Southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a housing complex near Fort Stewart causing some smoke damage but no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three separate squall line/bowing segments began impacting the Middle Tennessee area around mid day and ending around midnight. These systems produced mostly damaging straight line winds with some hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Celina causing damage. Type of damage was not specifically stated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two distinct lines of thunderstorms developed ahead of a weak boundary during the late afternoon and became more organized toward evening. One line developed across the Genesee Valley and the other across the eastern Lake Ontario Region. Thunderstorm winds downed trees in Ridgeway, Murray, Ogden Center, Ellery Center, Belleville, Croghan, Lowville and near the Chautauqua Institution.  In some areas, scattered power outages were reported as the falling limbs and trees brought down power lines. In Rochester, lighting struck a house igniting a fire and damaging the chimney.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement reported that house was damaged by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level trough across the southern Great Basin ejected out into the Southern Plains during the day on May 21st.  Strong convection developed during peak heating across the region and this convection was aided by moderate to strong instability, excessive deep layer shear and mid level lapse rates.  Add a frontal boundary to the mix and severe thunderstorms became widespread, some of which produced large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning and killed outside an eating establishment during the nighttime hours of May 21st.  She was standing outside adjacent to the restaurant holding an umbrella when she was struck.  According to a Lufkin Police spokesman, lightning entered her upper torso and exited her feet.  A chunk of concrete was blown out of the parking lot in a space to the side of the business where she was hit.|A witness said he was inside the restaurant when he heard and saw an explosion followed by sparks flying off of her and her umbrella.  At first she had stopped breathing, then began again and was put inside an ambulance but she died a short time later at an area hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent upper level disturbance interacted with a very warm and moist air mass on Wednesday afternoon and evening, leading to the development of severe thunderstorms. Widespread large hail and damaging winds occurred, as well as several tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike put a hole in the roof, but did not start a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent upper level disturbance interacted with a very warm and moist air mass on Wednesday afternoon and evening, leading to the development of severe thunderstorms. Widespread large hail and damaging winds occurred, as well as several tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike put a hole in the roof, but did not start a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that developed over western Minnesota during the evening of June 21st, rolled across southeast Minnesota before sunrise on the 22nd. These storms produced high winds and heavy rains. Trees were blown down and a shed moved off its foundation in Rochester (Olmsted County) while more trees were blown down near Lewiston (Winona County). The heavy rain produced street flooding in Rochester.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The corner of a house on the northeast side of Rochester was started on fire by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved northward through Southern New England, resulting in moist southerly flow across much of the area.  Showers and thunderstorms developed across western Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire, producing heavy rainfall towards the end of one of the wettest June's in southern New England history.  This resulted in flash flooding in several locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house at 57 Harkness Road was struck by lightning, which ignited a fire.  The house sustained minor damage before it was extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several waves of low pressure moved across southern Louisiana during the 10th and 11th. Reports of wind damage were received across southeast Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Louisiana Association of Realtors building caught fire due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms developed during the afternoon heating period in a moisture laden atmosphere. Some of these storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 500 block of Craig Avenue. The strike impacted the electrical system of the house and caused a fire that started in the basement.  In addition to damage to the electrical system, the house sustained smoke damage. Firefighting efforts also caused water damage to the house. Damage values are estimated. The two residents in the structure at the time of the strike were able to leave without injury.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An outflow boundary from overnight thunderstorms provided a focus for the development of additional thunderstorms during the morning and early afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in an empty house near Bayou Corne. The home was empty due to sink hole evacuations. Event time estimated based on radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level TUTT retrograde over south Florida with dry air over NE Florida enhancing downdrafts in scattered afternoon thunderstorms...which focused inland due to onshore flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A victim was struck near 74th Terrace and County Road 795 on the north side of Live Oak. Minor injuries were reported and the victim was transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slick roads caused by heavy rain resulted in 2 fatalities in Dallas. Lightning started a fire at a gas well in Somervell County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at a gas well on CR 308 just north of Highway 67 between Glen Rose and Cleburne.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary across northern portions of the forecast area was the focus for afternoon convection on the afternoon of June 23rd. A weak shortwave swinging in from the west helped to increase wind fields aloft and strong heating south of the front produced CAPES in the 1000 to 1500 j/kg range. Large hail and damaging winds were the main threats with these storms, the stronger of which held together long enough to drift into southern portions of the region later in the day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 25-yr-old woman was injured in a lightning strike at Point Sebago Resort.  The woman was standing near a tall pine at the edge of Sebago Lake when lightning struck the tree.  She was reportedly thrown into the air by the strike and was unconscious after landing on  some rocks and a concrete barrier.  She was taken to a nearby hospital for evaluation and treatment.  Two others who were also reportedly thrown into the air were not injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary across northern portions of the forecast area was the focus for afternoon convection on the afternoon of June 23rd. A weak shortwave swinging in from the west helped to increase wind fields aloft and strong heating south of the front produced CAPES in the 1000 to 1500 j/kg range. Large hail and damaging winds were the main threats with these storms, the stronger of which held together long enough to drift into southern portions of the region later in the day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A teenage boy was struck by lightning inside his home.  The lightning reportedly shot across the room, although no details were available concerning what the boy was doing at the time.  He was transported to a nearby hospital for treatment and observation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that was connected to a barbed wire fence on a ranch in Tetonia.  The current from the fence killed 15 cattle lined up next to the fence.   Cost to the rancher was between 15 and 20 thousand dollars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that was connected to a barbed wire fence on a ranch in Tetonia.  The current from the fence killed 15 cattle lined up next to the fence.   Cost to the rancher was between 15 and 20 thousand dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced prolific lightning which caused a fire in northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused house fire and a shed fire due to separate lightning strikes near East Milton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee early on April 27 and continued into the afternoon hours as a weak warm frontal boundary was draped across the region. Some flooding was reported in the Nashville metro area. Additional showers and thunderstorms formed later in the day on April 27 and continued into April 28. Training thunderstorms caused widespread flash flooding. The worst flash flooding was across Houston, Stewart, and Montgomery counties where many homes and businesses were flooded, numerous roads were washed out, and several people were rescued from the flood waters. Several reports of wind damage and large hail were also received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn and an outbuilding were struck by lightning and set on fire on Turkey McCollum Road in Cornersville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Easterly wind flow across the peninsula produces another active afternoon of severe weather across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a shed in a backyard which caused a fire. The house / shed was located on 10th Street SW.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated thunderstorm produced lightning and minor damage in Albertville, Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An isolated thunderstorm produced a lightning strike that produced minor fire damage to a residence in Albertville, Alabama.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall and frequent lightning, that resulted in a home being struck by lightning in north central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a house at the intersection of Sandlin Street and Bethel Road, just east-southeast of Elkmont, Alabama.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal surface trough developed over southern New England, providing a focus for low level convection.  Plenty of instability, as well as a strong upper jet aloft, allowed several of these storms to become severe, producing damaging winds.  A very moist, tropical-like atmosphere resulted in very heavy rainfall which produced flash flooding, mainly across southwestern New Hampshire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an attached garage on Reed Drive in Bedford, NH, starting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two lightning strikes produced a small fire and damaged appliances inside a high-rise condominium in the Coco Plum section of Marathon, Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two lightning strikes occurred to the Bonefish Towers complex in the Coco Plum section of the city of Marathon.  The first bolt was observed to strike a small grouping of palm trees, which were set on fire.  The local fire department extinguished the fire.  A second strike to the main rooftop dryer vent melted the aluminum framing around dryer lint screens on the 4th, 7th, 8th and 9th floors along the southeast corner of the condominum tower.  Laundry rooms exist on all floors of the condominium except the 14th floor penthouse.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Tallahassee and resulted in a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the 200 block of Timberlane Dr and resulted in a fire.  The damage was estimated at $100,000.  This was reported by the City of Tallahassee Fire Department facebook page.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms moving across far northeastern Illinois during the morning of September 19th sparked a fire to a house in Lake Forest.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 300 block of Ravine Park Drive punching a hole in the roof and damaging a third story bedroom.  No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Abnormal heat for early September coupled with an elevated mixed layer resulted in a few strong to severe thunderstorms developing late in the day in western Massachusetts and southwestern New Hampshire.  These storms produced damaging winds, downing several trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree on Locks Village Road was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm resulted in lightning damage in Aloha, Oregon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree hit by lightning fell and damaged two homes in Aloha.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced lots of lightning which caused house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit an oil tank near the Aransas County Airport which caused a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank the the Aransas County Airport on Farm to Market Road 1781. The lightning strike hit a tank with a salt water and crude oil mix sparking a major fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm centered about 6 to 8 miles north of Key West caused injury to a police officer.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A police officer was injured when his motorcycle was struck, possibly indirectly, by lightning.  It was unknown whether the original lightning strike was to a utility pole or directly to the right-hand handlebar of the motorcycle.  The officer was waiting at a traffic signal at Palm Avenue and North Roosevelt Boulevard while returning to the Key West Police Station in order to switch to his assigned car after hearing thunder.  The officer experienced a significant jolt which threw his right arm backward, causing a shoulder injury.  The officer remained conscious and was able to call for rescue service using his own radio.   The officer was admitted for overnight observation and medical testing and did not receive any burns from the lightning strike.  The officer was released shortly thereafter and was expected to return to duty soon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Light ESE steering flow combined with high moisture content and an unstable airmass produced slow moving afternoon thunderstorms that produced locally heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at 139 Lige Branch Lane in the Fruit Cove and Switzerland areas. There were no known injuries, and the cost of damage was estimated since the extent of damage was unknown. The cost of damage is likely grossly underestimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front produced scattered showers and thunderstorms across central and eastern Virginia. Some storms produced strong winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning in Virginia Beach, downing a tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a passing upper level trough combined with active sea breezes, surface instability and high moisture content spawned scattered strong storms which produced locally heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire near Lake City. The time of damage was estimated based on radar and lightning data. The cost of damage was unknown and estimated for the event to be included in StormData.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire that destroyed Finland's only church.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm with intense lightning dropped heavy rain over the Calumet area on the 1st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike blew holes in the steeple of the Keweenaw Heritage Center at St. Anne's Church in Calumet.  The roofing and underlying wood were shattered.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A river guide was struck by lightning while on a river trip in the Grand Canyon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A river guide was struck by lightning while on a river trip in the Grand Canyon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck three people at LeFavre Scenic Overlook along Highway 89 about eight miles north of Jacobs Lake. Two people died and the third person sustained non-life-threatening injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck three people at LeFavre Scenic Overlook along Highway 89 about eight miles north of Jacobs Lake. Two people died and the third person sustained non-life-threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved northward over Southern New England, providing lift for showers and thunderstorms to develop across much of western Massachusetts.  There was enough cold air aloft for some very large hail (for New England) to fall from these storms.  The National Weather Service office in Taunton received several reports of golf ball to almost tennis ball size hail from parts of western Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree outside a house on Colrain Shelburne Road, traveled through the ground and started a fire in the attic of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal surface trough developed over southern New England, providing a focus for low level convection.  Plenty of instability, as well as a strong upper jet aloft, allowed several of these storms to become severe, producing damaging winds.  A very moist, tropical-like atmosphere resulted in very heavy rainfall which produced flash flooding, mainly across southwestern New Hampshire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, then traveled underground, hit an electrical box and started fires in three condos.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man walking along Scott Reservoir near Show Low was hit and killed by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 54 year old man was walking along the south edge of Scott Reservoir with two other people when he was stuck and killed by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A backdoor cold front pushing south through New England produced isolated severe thunderstorms in western and central Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Jeanine Circle, causing damage to the electric service.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused damage to a structure.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a structural fire near the intersection of CR 278 and FM 1361.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorm complexes developed for a second evening over Upstate South Carolina. The storms caused a few areas of flash flooding and knocked down several trees, mainly due to wet ground.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at a 4000 square foot home that completely destroyed the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of multiple lingering convergent boundaries from previous convection, an approaching upper level short wave trough from the NW, and the sea breezes fueled scattered severe storms over an unstable airmass in the afternoon and evening. Gusty winds and heavy rainfall were the main hazards.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The post office was struck by lightning which caused damage. The cost of damage was unknown but estimated so that this event could be included in StormData.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved through the area during the afternoon.  With a warm and moist airmass in place, several showers and thunderstorms developed.  One brought down a tree and resulted in a lightning fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Crisp County Emergency Manager reported that a business was struck by lightning and burned for a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a pole barn to catch fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a pole barn to catch fire, burning to the ground.  The barn was filled with various tools and machinery, which was destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee early on April 27 and continued into the afternoon hours as a weak warm frontal boundary was draped across the region. Some flooding was reported in the Nashville metro area. Additional showers and thunderstorms formed later in the day on April 27 and continued into April 28. Training thunderstorms caused widespread flash flooding. The worst flash flooding was across Houston, Stewart, and Montgomery counties where many homes and businesses were flooded, numerous roads were washed out, and several people were rescued from the flood waters. Several reports of wind damage and large hail were also received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man who was outside in his driveway in the Upper Hurricane Creek community was struck by lightning and injured. The strike knocked him into his home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A backdoor cold front pushing south through New England produced isolated severe thunderstorms in western and central Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three students at the MacDuffie School in Granby were struck by lightning while sitting outside at a picnic table. Two students were knocked unconscious and were hospitalized. The third student was further away when the lightning struck and was not directly hit, suffering less serious effects. The students were 16, 17, and 20 years of age. All of the students reovered from their injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms formed in western Massachusetts during the evening and produced damaging winds. The storms developed in a warm and humid air mass south of a warm front, which remained draped over central New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in Erving which fell and blocked a portion of Route 2.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms formed in western Massachusetts during the evening and produced damaging winds. The storms developed in a warm and humid air mass south of a warm front, which remained draped over central New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a house fire on Haven Hill Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms formed in western Massachusetts during the evening and produced damaging winds. The storms developed in a warm and humid air mass south of a warm front, which remained draped over central New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Church Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the evening of May 22nd, a stationary boundary remained draped across northern New York and Vermont. There was enough low-level instability, as well as disturbances along this boundary to produce scattered and training thunderstorms during the evening hours in the Champlain Valley that produced some hail and localized urban flooding in poor drainage locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an individual...minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary warm front draped across southern New England, coupled with a very moist atmosphere, resulted in showers and thunderstorms across the area for the third day in a row.  Heavy rain fell within these showers and storms and flash flooding occurred, particularly over portions of Rhode Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck near a house on Bay Path Road.  While several homeowners claimed to have experienced electrical problems with the lightning strike, firefighters found no damage within the houses.  Two teenagers (one male, one female) outside manning a yard sale felt the lightning shock.  One (male) declined transportation to the hospital, the other (female) was transported and kept overnight for observation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance had moved over the area, and moisture was present.  This led to the development of thunderstorms across Southeast New Mexico which resulted in severe wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm moved over Lea County and lightning struck a tank battery causing fires west and southwest of Hobbs.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of multiple lingering convergent boundaries from previous convection, an approaching upper level short wave trough from the NW, and the sea breezes fueled scattered severe storms over an unstable airmass in the afternoon and evening. Gusty winds and heavy rainfall were the main hazards.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A residential occurred as a result of a lightning strike. The cost of damage was unknown and estimated so the event could be included in StormData.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough north of Lake Okeechobee combined with local sea breezes to trigger scattered thunderstorms across southwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Greenfield Court and caused a fire which damaged most of the roof. The time of the lightning strike was estimated based on archived radar and lightning data. Fire officials were called to the home at 523 PM, about 45 minutes after the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On Friday, August 9, the upper level ridge axis across the Lower Mississippi River Valley deamplified and ridging stretched from west to east across the Southeast. With weak zonal flow aloft and precipitable water values over 2.00 inches, isolated convection developed during the late afternoon as mesoscale boundaries collided.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the First Church of the Nazarene, causing a fire that destroyed the building. Fire personnel on the scene estimated damages to be greater than $775K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms developed over Southern Ontario and rapidly moved southeast across the Niagara Frontier. The thunderstorms produced damaging winds that downed trees and power lines in Bergholtz.  In Cheektowaga, lightning struck a power transformer in the vicinity of French Road. The media reported live wires down along with power out in the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorms produced a lightning that struck a gas station along I-81.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas station on Interstate 81 at exit 60. Circuit boards on several gas pumps were damaged and had to be replaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two stuctures in Brunswick County with an injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a storage building on the 600 block of Hickory Branches Ln.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two stuctures in Brunswick County with an injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the 200 block of E Wood Lane.  A teenager received a burn from a gaming system inside the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: More scattered showers and thunderstorms formed ahead of a cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An adult male was outside when a bolt of lightning indirectly hit his leg after traveling across some concrete.  He was taken to the hospital and stayed overnight for observation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: More scattered showers and thunderstorms formed ahead of a cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person was struck on Wolfpen Lane, but refused any treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving trough across the central portions of the country helped develop several rounds of severe thunderstorms and flash flooding across the Missouri Ozarks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck by lightning and knocked unconscious at an outdoor rodeo. Both individuals were taken to an area hospital and later released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia under the influence of weak high pressure and significant surface heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Screven County communications center reported that lightning struck a tree which then fell on a car in downtown Sylvania.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of strong thunderstorms developed across central and western portions of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Power lines were reported down on North Lake Drive in Brentwood due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: SW steering flow combined with high moisture content and passing upper level energy fueled scattered afternoon thunderstorms which produced gusty winds and a tornado ENE of Bostwick.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire on South Central Ave in Flagler Beach. There were no injuries.  The cost of damage was estimated for event inclusion in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure moving along a stationary front triggered several severe thunderstorms over southeast Louisiana during the evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a power outage in Gramercy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On Monday, August 12, isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon as a result of diurnal heating. Lightning struck one person in Coosa county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person was injured when struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered diurnal showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours under the influence of weak high pressure and a trough of low pressure east of the Appalachians.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire on Cannon Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms downed trees, limbs, and caused power outages across portions of eastern Kentucky during the overnight hours of June 27, 2013.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large tree which then fell across White Oak Rd/John Rawlings Rd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical afternoon convection produced a report of a funnel cloud and lightning strikes a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home in Breaux Bridge. The resulting fire completely destroyed the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure off the Southeast coast continued to bring deep moisture into the area.  A weak area of low pressure over the Mid-Atlantic allowed disturbances to continue moving across the state, with several showers and thunderstorms developing in the afternoon.  Lightning associated with one of these storms resulted in two house fires in Henry County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Henry County Emergency Manager reported that lightning started two house fires.  The fires were quickly extinguished with little damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An outflow boundary, left behind by previous thunderstorms and extending from northwest to southeast across much of Arkansas, became active again later on the 22nd due to daytime heating. A few severe thunderstorms resulted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A sport utility vehicle was struck by lightning as it was traveling on Interstate 40. The motorist was not injured but the vehicle was disabled.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface front lifted northward over south Georgia with weaker SW steering flow in place. Diurnal heating combined with sea breeze and outflow activity spawned a few severe storms over the area during the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Ocala Star Banner reported that lightning struck a home which blasted a large hole in the roof and caused a fire in the attic of the home. The time of damage was based on radar and lightning data. The cost of damage is likely  not accurate and was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot, humid weather prevailed over Arkansas on the 10th. The approach of a cold front triggered the development of several severe storms during the afternoon and evening. The front was making its way though the state on the 11th, triggering a few severe storms in the southern half of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home near Royal, starting a fire. The home suffered considerable damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot, humid weather prevailed over Arkansas on the 10th. The approach of a cold front triggered the development of several severe storms during the afternoon and evening. The front was making its way though the state on the 11th, triggering a few severe storms in the southern half of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a brush fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper low was in place across the Great Lakes, allowing continued intermittent upper level disturbances to rotate around and affect the Southeast.  A complicated surface pattern in place with multiple boundaries left over from previous days' convection as well as a weak nearly stationary front, combined with ample moisture and high levels of instability provided plenty of focus for thunderstorm development.  Numerous storms did indeed develop, and many of these became severe with mainly damaging winds reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Jasper County Emergency Manager reported that lightning struck a house near Rock Eagle Road.  Smoke was observed but the fire was quickly put out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of squall lines moved through mostly eastern Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours resulting in damaging winds, hail, flash flooding, and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the College Hills Church of Christ and the Snow White Drive In near Lebanon. Firefighters were battling a fire at the church. No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of squall lines moved through mostly eastern Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours resulting in damaging winds, hail, flash flooding, and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at 108 Stockton Drive in Murfreesboro.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level area of low pressure over the eastern Gulf of Mexico caused numerous showers and thunderstorms across the southeast Florida coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two 16-year old males fell from a 25-foot Ficus Tree that was struck by lightning and were injured. Both were transported to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On July 7, 2013 A lightning strike caused the shutdown of the National Telecommunication Authority (NTA) power line system at the Rita substation, disrupting television service. According to NTA MHTV Transmission Supervisor Rayner Peter Jr., the power system and backup generator were damaged.This also disrupted television, internet and cellular phone service in Majuro.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On July 7, 2013 A lightning strike caused the shutdown of the National Telecommunication Authority (NTA) power line system at the Rita substation, disrupting television service. According to NTA MHTV Transmission Supervisor Rayner Peter Jr., the power system and backup generator were damaged.This also disrupted television, internet and cellular phone service in Majuro.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large blocking ridge of high pressure was centered well north and west of the region with thunderstorms developing with the aid of afternoon heating along the periphery of the ridge.  The atmosphere became very unstable during the afternoon of July 11th and once these storms developed, additional thunderstorms developed along residual boundaries from previous storms.  Damaging wind gusts were the main threat from these thunderstorms but large hail was also reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck a powerline and caused a small fire approximately 2 miles south of Lindale, Texas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed across portions of Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon hours of August 13th.  These storms developed in a moderately unstable airmass and with a layer of drier air in the low levels of the atmosphere, once these thunderstorms decayed, they produced pockets of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a battery of tanks ablaze at a gas storage facility on Hwy. 9 south of Arcadia, Louisiana.  A secondary explosion occurred after 8 pm, sending flames as high as 300 feet into the air and forced the closure of Hwy. 9.  In all, about a dozen tanks were set ablaze.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the evening hours that produced frequent cloud to ground lightning resulting in some property damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Traemoor Village Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the evening hours that produced frequent cloud to ground lightning resulting in some property damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have struck a home on Albany Drive in Hermitage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms containing very heavy downpours impacted Middle Tennessee  during the afternoon hours. Flash flooding occurred in Lawrence County as a result.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have struck the 911 call center rendering it without power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of squall lines moved through mostly eastern Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours resulting in damaging winds, hail, flash flooding, and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wilson County Emergency Management reported a house struck by lightning on Holloway Road near Lebanon. The lightning strike caused a small fire in the house. No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical wave along with an upper level low pressure area near Nassau produced scattered showers and thunderstorms across South Florida and the adjacent waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement and the Naples Daily News reported a Pennsylvania woman was injured when a lightning strike occurred near the the Marco Beach Ocean Resort at 480 S. Collier Blvd. She was taken to a local hospital and treated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved through southern New England, providing a focus for a few showers and thunderstorms.  Instability was limited somewhat by cloud cover and weak winds at the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere resulted in slow moving storms.  The atmosphere was very moist with precipitable water levels around 2 inches, this led to very heavy rainfall with storms that developed.  One particular storm became severe over Greenfield and produced a microburst, downing numerous trees through the northwestern part of the city.  It also produced flash flooding in Greenfield.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WCVB-TV Channel 5 in Boston reported that lightning struck a house on Clifton Avenue, setting the garage on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved over southern New England bringing showers and thunderstorms to the region. Precipitable water values over two inches indicated a very moist atmosphere; in addition, weak winds at the mid levels resulted in very slow moving storms. Both of these things led to torrential rainfall and flash flooding.  This is the second day in a row that parts of Kent County received between three and four inches of rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Providence Journal reported that two horses died in a barn fire in Hopkinton caused by a lightning strike.  The horses were 6 and 17 years old.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak mid-to-upper level shortwave swept across the Southern Appalachians early on the 2nd, with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms developing early in the morning. During the day, the remnants of a squall line over the Lower Mississippi Valley pushed into the Southeast.  This combined with the shortwave and daytime heating allowed scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop.  Some thunderstorms reached severe levels with mainly damaging winds, but there were a couple of hail reports as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that a lightning fire destroyed a house on Deville Circle in Suwanee.  No one was injured, but the house was destroyed in a matter of minutes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong area of low pressure sat over the Desert Southwest for two days, bringing heavy rain and snow to portions of the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked out power to 800 customers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over northwestern and west central Arkansas during the late afternoon hours of the 23rd. These storms persisted over the region well into the early morning hours of the 24th. The strongest storms produced strong outflow wind. Lightning from these storms also caused a structural fire in Bentonville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home, resulting in a fire that destroyed it and damaged the adjacent house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The northern extent of a tropical wave over the Bahamas helped to trigger afternoon and evening thunderstorms across south Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A boy who was trying to seek shelter from a thunderstorm underneath a chickee hut at Marriott Beach Resort was injured when a lightning struck the hut. He was taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. The lightning strike also set the chickee hut on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated to scattered, east-to-west moving severe thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours in eastern Middle Tennessee and progressed through the early evening. These storms resulted in multiple wind damage reports across Middle Tennessee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire in the backyard of a home at 2729 Riverbend Drive in the Pennington Bend area of northeast Nashville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front sagging toward the Louisiana and Mississippi coasts aided in the development of strong to severe thunderstorms over the Mississippi coastal counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes damaged 5 golf carts, 3 chargers and a sprinkler system at Whispering Pines Golf Course in Hurley.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed throughout the morning and afternoon of July 26th, ahead of a weak surface front and associated upper level disturbance which moved across the region.  Surface low pressure developed during the early evening hours along the surface front, and enhanced the development of stronger convection across a warm and moderately unstable region in Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. These storms quickly became severe and produced damaging winds which downed trees and power lines across this region before diminishing over extreme North Central Louisiana by late evening. A secondary cluster of severe thunderstorms developed over Northwest Louisiana near this surface low and front, which surged southeast across West Central Louisiana during the late evening and early morning hours of the 26th-27th. Damaging winds again downed trees and power lines across these areas, before weakening prior to sunrise.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Texarkana resulting in a small fire.  There were no report of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front interacting with a hot and humid airmass triggered scattered thunderstorms across portions of central and southeast Illinois during the late afternoon and evening of August 31st.  Most of the storms were confined to locations along and south of a Danville to Taylorville line, where gusty winds downed a few tree branches.  In addition, a lightning strike cause substantial damage to a garage in Flora.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage on East 9th Street in Flora.  The resulting fire caused significant damage to the garage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms knocked over a few trees across Upstate South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 50 year old man was struck by lightning, while working on his truck, under a tree, in the yard. The incident took place Sunday September 1, 2013. The man died Thursday September 5, 2013.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low north of the islands combined with a surface trough and shear line to produce heavy rain and flash flooding over parts of the Aloha State.  There were no reports of serious injuries.  The cost of damages was not available.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and felled a utility pole.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man fishing from a canoe on Big Lake was stuck and killed by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was stuck and killed by lightning while fishing from a canoe on Big Lake.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed over New York and moved into western Massachusetts.  With plenty of diurnal heating resulting in instability, damaging winds occurred with a few of these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Round Hill Road and another on Country Club Way, igniting fires.  No information could be found on the extent of damage to the houses.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed over New York and moved into western Massachusetts.  With plenty of diurnal heating resulting in instability, damaging winds occurred with a few of these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the building, causing electrical damage.  Residents were evacuated briefly while firefighters investigated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough moved into southern New England, providing lift for showers and thunderstorms to develop in a hot and humid atmosphere.  In addition, CAPE up to 2000 J/kg and 30-40 kts of shear provided enough instability and shear for thunderstorms to become severe.  Because of warm air aloft, these thunderstorms mostly produced strong to damaging winds and not large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Tracey Lane, igniting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A short wave mid level trough was lingering over the southeast region. A piece of energy traveled over the area during peak heating and this instability and forcing combined with adequate mean layer moisture and forcing from the sea breezes spawned scattered afternoon and evening severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the St. Augustine Regional Airport runway which caused damage to a 5 foot by 6 foot area of the runway. That section of the runway was closed due to needed repairs. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very hot and unstable airmass prevailed across the Mid-South during the afternoon of June 27, 2013. A weak surface boundary was stretched from Northeast Arkansas into North Mississippi.  A few thunderstorms developed along this boundary in Northeast Arkansas during the late afternoon and eventually formed a mesoscale convective system that traveled southeast across the Memphis Metropolitan area into Northwest Mississippi. A few severe storms occurred with large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire at an apartment complex on West Harrison Street in West Memphis. The fire caused extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough moved into southern New England, providing lift for showers and thunderstorms to develop in a hot and humid atmosphere.  In addition, CAPE up to 2000 J/kg and 30-40 kts of shear provided enough instability and shear for thunderstorms to become severe.  Because of warm air aloft, these thunderstorms mostly produced strong to damaging winds and not large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a house on Morrow Street.  The lightning traveled along the invisible fence line to the house, damaging the invisible fence circuitry.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building in Mansfield, knocking out a fire alarm system.

In addition, CAPE up to 2000 J/kg and 30-40 kts of shear provided enough instability and shear for thunderstorms to become severe. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Elmwood Street, igniting a fire.  The house sustained minor damage.
