In addition, CAPE up to 2000 J/kg and 30-40 kts of shear provided enough instability and shear for thunderstorms to become severe.  Because of warm air aloft, these thunderstorms mostly produced strong to damaging winds and not large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large, multi-family house on Butler Avenue, igniting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused significant damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused significant damage to a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving through the Missouri Ozarks and associated upper level trough over the central portions of the country developed strong to severe thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced marginal severe hail, damaging winds, and heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across the Missouri Ozarks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media reported a house on fire at 218 Prairie Ridge Lane in Ozark which was caused by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike during a thunderstorm destroyed one of three blades on a wind turbine near Dexter (Mower County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed one of three blades on a wind turbine near Dexter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep moisture and southeast winds fueled scattered afternoon thunderstorms over central and southwest Florida that moved northwest towards the coast.  Lightning from one of the storms struck and killed a woman walking on Belleair Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas County emergency management and print and broadcast media reported a 51 year old woman was struck and killed while walking on Belleair Beach.  Print media reported she was walking on the beach with a friend.  When storms started to roll in, the two friends got separated.  After the storms cleared, the friend found the woman's body on the beach. The death was called into the Sheriff's Department at 6:47 PM EDT, so an estimated time of 6:45 PM EDT was used.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A middle to upper level trough moved across Texas providing sufficient lift to produce thunderstorms some of which were severe. These storms produced large hail, a few damaging wind gusts, and minor flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were injured by lightning at a construction site in Austin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along a lee side trough in a warm and unstable airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, causing the tree to fall onto an apartment roof. The roof sustain minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread rain with a few embedded thunderstorms spread across Middle Tennessee during the evening hours of February 23. Lightning from one storm in Humphreys County reportedly struck a food building at the Loretta Lynn Ranch in Hurricane Mills, and the resulting fire destroyed the structure.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning reportedly struck a food building at the Loretta Lynn Ranch in Hurricane Mills, and the resulting fire destroyed the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted northward over the Florida peninsula. During the afternoon, the front combined with an upper level short wave trough combined to trigger scattered severe storms over northeast Florida during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was started by lightning near Manorville Drive and Montsville Ct. The cost of damage was unknown and estimated for inclusion in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A gulf low pressure system developed over the central Gulf of Mexico early in the month and moved into northern Florida on the 4th. The low trailed a cold front to the south with widespread thunderstorms developing ahead of the front and producing frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a stable at RVR Horse Rescue, killing 1 horse and injuring the eye of another.  A time for the lighting strike was estimated at 11:00am EST from radar and lightning archives during the peak of convection over the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convective activity developed early in the afternoon with thunderstorms rapidly developing over West and Southwest Montana in response to an upper trough moving across Northwest Montana into southern Alberta. Though jet streak energy supported the system, convective parameters were not overly impressive. Additionally, precipitable water values were very high across the CWA translating to heavy rain with some isolated to scattered severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms over Glacier Park injured 3 people hiking on the St Mary Falls trail. Time of event is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes started a fire which caused damage in Midway.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a house fire in the town of Midway.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain and lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a shed and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough and surface cold front combined to produce thunderstorms across South Central Texas. Convection started in the northeast during the afternoon of the 2nd then a squall line developed over the western counties later in the evening. A few thunderstorms produced sub-severe hail as the upper level trough moved across on the 3rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire that destroyed a special events facility.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm moved across the southwest and south suburbs of Chicago producing large hail and strong winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A golfer standing near a tree was struck by lightning.  His injuries were not life threatening and he was treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed across central and eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon hours of the 30th, ahead of a dry line over central Oklahoma and along an outflow boundary across northeastern Oklahoma. The storms moved into northwestern Arkansas during the evening, producing some large hail and damaging wind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck and injured by lightning while outside in a parking lot. Both victims were transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front approaching from the west interacted with a very warm and moist tropical air mass.||A corridor of showers and thunderstorms persisted throughout the day Wednesday from Southeastern Kentucky and Southwestern Virginia, northeastward through southeastern West Virginia.  This area intensified and expanded in the afternoon heat. Other thunderstorms developed in the afternoon heat around the lower Ohio River.  A massive complex of thunderstorms expanded and intensified as it moved up the Ohio Valley and approached from the west.  ||Marginally severe wind accompanied the line of thunderstorms through southeast Ohio and across the Ohio River.  The complex weakened while moving further east in West Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An outbuilding caught fire on 20th Street.  Its contents were salvaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated severe storms occurred across Louisiana as a weak disturbance traveled across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a power pole early in the morning of the 23rd near a Eunice business. The surge caused mostly cosmetic damage to the structure, however the surge burned the circuit breaker box and meter resulting in a brief electrical fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms congealed into a squall line ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon. Isolated severe thunderstorms were embedded within the line, mainly over the Northeast NJ Metro area. Heavy rain associated with this line produced flash flooding in Bergen County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a chimney of a house on Finch Road, shorting out circuits and knocking siding off the side of the house. No extensive damage was reported. This was originally reported by a Skywarn Spotter, that was confirmed by a local fire department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across Middle Tennessee. One person was reportedly struck by lightning in Nashville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was reportedly struck by lightning and injured in Sylvan Park. Reported via tspotter on Twitter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance in combination with an unstable airmass contributed to the development of severe thunderstorms across northeast Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a steeple on a church. Half of the steeple was hanging on the church with some debris in the roadway. State Route 2008 was closed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms moved across the western North Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon hours ahead of a cold front. A few of the storms caused straight line wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that then fell on a vehicle on Wilson Lee Blvd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms damaged two homes and an underground pipeline near Sammamish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: South of Issaquah, a tree fell and struck a woman standing on her porch. The woman suffered a broken hip.   A lightning strike sparked a gas leak in a Sammamish neighborhood, it hit a house, then went through the gutter system and ruptured a buried gas line 100 feet away and causing flammable gas to spew into the air.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters and lines of storms produced hail and flooding. In addition several homes and one individual were struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a home fire on the 10500 block of East Aliana Trace Drive in Mission Bend.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak mid-atmospheric disturbance moving across a stationary surface boundary within an unstable, tropical air mass led to numerous showers and thunderstorms with torrential, flooding rains across portions of Vermont. Rainfall rates of 2 inches per hour were observed and detected by Dual-Pol radar. In addition, a woman was struck and injured by lightning in Barre.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A report of a 62 year old woman struck by lightning and taken to the hospital for treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered pulse type strong to severe thunderstorms affected New Jersey during the second half of the afternoon on the 25th. One person was struck and injured by lightning in Hunterdon County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured by an indirect lightning strike on McCan Mill Road in Tewksbury Township. Lightning struck the ground near him and then traveled to him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance triggered thunderstorms that moved across central and north central Wisconsin.  The storms produced isolated severe weather across north central Wisconsin, including large hail, wind damage and heavy rainfall.  The heavy rain in Merrill (Lincoln Co.) caused some street flooding.  Lightning in advance of one of the storms stuck a boy in rural Marathon County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 8 year-old boy was struck by lightning while riding a mini-bike at his uncle's farm in the Town of Rib Falls.  No rain was falling at the time the boy was struck.  He was initially unresponsive and had no pulse, but his father used CPR to revive him and the boy was rushed to the hospital.  The boy suffered ruptured eardrums, scratches on the lenses of his eyes, and second degree burns over more than a quarter of his body.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very unstable airmass on May 19, 2013 led to the development of severe thunderstorms that produced large hail and damaging winds. Temperatures were in the 80s with dewpoints around 70 with a mid level speed maximum rotating around the base of a developing upper low in the Plains states. This increased the deep layer shear during the afternoon and evening hours.  Some of the storms produced golf to baseball size hail and 70 to 80 mph winds.  A trained spotter reported baseball size hail knocked out sky lights at the Walmart store in northeast Keokuk. Golfball to baseball size hail was reported on the north end of the city, with nickel to quarter size hail on the south end of the city.  A downburst produced wind damage in Benton county from the county line 3.5 miles southeast of Blairstown to 2.8 miles southeast of Shellsburg. There was a mile wide swath of near continuous damage to farm outbuildings, tree branches and some power poles. The greatest damage was from 3 miles south of Newhall, where a machine shed and garage were completely destroyed, to about 3 miles northwest of Atkins, where significant damage occurred to outbuildings.  The emergency manager in Buchanan county reported a downburst with winds more than 70 mph struck Independence, Iowa. The northwest side of town sustained the most damage with trees down, power poles snapped and signs blown down.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A garage was struck by lightning at 2640 South Main Street in Burlington resulting in a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters and lines of storms produced hail and flooding. In addition several homes and one individual were struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire in the Silver Ranch subdivision in Katy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple short waves moved across the region while a north flow remained in place. This caused multiple rounds of severe weather with hail, high winds, and a tornado in Louisiana from late during the 9th into the 10th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were fishing in the Lacassine Wildlife Refuge when a storm approached from the east. The two tried to out run the storm in a boat but one was struck by lightning. The struck man died a few days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During an active evening of showers of thunderstorms, damage was reported from two different lightning strikes near Salt Lake City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the top gable of a house in West Jordan; the bolt then traveled about 10 feet and burned part of a satellite dish on the roof of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High Pressure over the Great Basin resulted in moderate northeast flow over southeast Arizona.  With surface dew points in the 30s and 40s, thunderstorms produced gusty winds. Due to recent dry conditions, those winds created areas of blowing dust.  In addition, lightning strikes created at least three separate fires, including one in the Santa Catalina Mountains known as the Prison Wildfire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pair of Palm Trees near 22nd Street and Sarnoff Drive, igniting them and burning one to a cinder. Another palm tree was ignited by lightning near Golf Links Road and Prudence Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters and lines of storms produced hail and flooding. In addition several homes and one individual were struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a man at the intersection of Seamist Drive and Tannehill Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters and lines of storms produced hail and flooding. In addition several homes and one individual were struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a car and set it ablaze at the intersection of Williams Way Blvd. and Highway 59.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical moisture in place across southern New England ahead of a cold front resulted in precipitable water values increasing to 2-2.5 inches (2 to 3 times normal).  The cold front provided enough lift for widespread rain with embedded thunderstorms across all of southern New England.  The high moisture content of the atmosphere resulted in torrential downpours across much of the region, which led to flash flooding in some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the medical office building on the campus of Baystate Mary Lane Hospital in Ware, blowing out the building's electrical panel.  In addition, three people who were on the telephone at the time of the strike reported feeling numbness and a tingling in their arms.  All three walked over to the hospital to be checked out and were fine.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper air disturbance combined with a hot and humid air mass to produce strong to severe thunderstorms across the Maryland Eastern Shore during the second half of the afternoon and early evening on the 24th.  The strongest storms affected Cecil County.  There were also some reports of hail with the thunderstorms as the freezing level aloft was relatively low in height above the ground. Most of the hail was small (less than half an inch).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a store in North East.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During an active evening of showers of thunderstorms, damage was reported from two different lightning strikes near Salt Lake City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A plane belonging to the Utah Air National Guard (a KC-135, which is a large plane that provides in-flight refueling for other aircraft) took off from Salt Lake City International Airport on the evening of May 7, and was struck by lightning about 10 minutes after takeoff. The lightning damaged a communications antenna that stretches from the nose to the tail of the aircraft. In addition to knocking out communications, the antenna became loose and hit against the plane repeatedly, damaging the skin of the aircraft. No one was injured in the incident, and the crew was able to use alternate communications to help them return to the airport and land.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved across southeast Minnesota during the afternoon and evening of May 31st. These storms developed in a complex surface pattern across the Upper Midwest as a pre-frontal surface trough, dry line and cold front all passed through the area. The storms primarily produced large hail, although there were also some wind gusts around 60 mph. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized near Kellogg (Wabasha County) and around Rochester (Olmsted County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree on the southwest side of Rochester causing a nearby natural gas line to start on fire. Firefighters cooled the fire until the utility company clamped off the gas line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank near Erath.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil storage tank on Albert Road near Erath seting the tank on fire. The fire burned through the afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated severe storms occurred across Louisiana as a weak disturbance traveled across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Bayou Ramos power substation near Morgan City that and combined with other issues to cut power to the city through the afternoon. The lightning caused a fault in one of the lines at the substation cutting power from the east side of town. The generators from the other side of the city kicked in, however a natural gas leak feeding the generators was discovered and had to be shut down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved across southeast Minnesota during the afternoon and evening of May 31st. These storms developed in a complex surface pattern across the Upper Midwest as a pre-frontal surface trough, dry line and cold front all passed through the area. The storms primarily produced large hail, although there were also some wind gusts around 60 mph. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized near Kellogg (Wabasha County) and around Rochester (Olmsted County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the southeast side of Rochester causing a fire in the attic. The fire was quickly put out but extensive damage was done to the roof and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching pre-frontal trough, ahead of a cold front, triggered thunderstorms over Northeast New Jersey during the afternoon, causing a lightning strike in Bergen County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to strike a home just north of Glen Rock on Rutland Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An uncapped, unstable atmosphere was in place ahead of an outflow boundary that moved across northern Indiana into northwestern Ohio.  Thunderstorms developed across the area, with the vast majority remaining below severe limits.  One storm produced isolated damage in the Swanton area of Fulton county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was indirectly the cause of structure fire on the 300 block of Wood Street. Fire officials reported that lightning struck a power line near the residence, with the live line impacting the residence and immediately started a fire. The house was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid to upper level low pressure area over Florida combined with a moist east flow to produce periods of torrential downpours and thunderstorms over the course of the day across southeast Florida. Over 2,000 customers were without power in the three-county region of southeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two persons, a 40-year-old man and a 32-year-old woman, were struck by lightning at Aventura Mall close to 10 PM EDT. Both were hospitalized and were released the following day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a dryline and an upper level disturbance produced a few severe thunderstorms across the Big Country and the counties of Brown and San Saba. The storms produced mostly damaging winds and a few reports of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Trinity Church of the Nazarene in the 3300 block of State Street.  A church official estimated the damage to be two hundred and fifty thousand dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across the area and produced large hail and very heavy rain which caused flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was hit by lightning causing a fire and block structure damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High moisture and instability led to thunderstorms developing over parts of southeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a home in Coral Springs. Tiles were removed from the roof, with no other damage or injuries. Time estimated based on lightning archive data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across the region in the form of a squall line of storms. Winds of 60 to 70 mph accompanied this squall line, resulting a widespread wind damage. Large hail also accompanied some of the stronger storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Phillippi Hollow Road. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large haystack just off the pavement on State Highway 487 was ignited by a lightning strike. Fire crews quickly contained the fire, but the nearly 24-foot-tall stack burned completely over the ensuing 24-hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 160-ton haystack was set ablaze by a lightning strike. The fire burned through the night but did not spread beyond the stack. The value of the 190 bales of hay that were burned was estimated at about $35,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A house fire started from a lightning strike resulted in the death of a 79-year-old man near McMillan on the early morning of the 18th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire caused by a lightning strike resulted in the death of a 79-year-old man.  The fire was reported by a storm spotter located one mile away, and it was confirmed by local media.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving upper level low pressure system passed across Virginia during the afternoon and evening.  Cooler temperatures aloft associated with the core of the low provided support for hail-producing thunderstorm.  In addition, light upper level winds made for slower moving storms, which resulted in flooding in some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a home on the 1000 block of Glenwood Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper air disturbance combined with a hot and humid air mass to produce strong to locally severe thunderstorms across central and southern New Jersey during the second half of the afternoon and early evening on the 24th. In addition to locally damaging winds, lightning strikes caused damage and there were several reports of hail with the thunderstorms as the freezing level aloft was relatively low in height above the ground. Most of the hail was very small (less than half an inch).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused minor damage to a home in Shamong Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low moving across the eastern Gulf of Mexico provided increased instability for afternoon showers and thunderstorms.  Several of these storms caused damaging wind gusts.  Additionally, a couple lightning strikes caused fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Florida State watch office reported a lightning strike to an apartment complex started a fire near 4th Street North and 112 Avenue Northeast.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree next to a home in Spread Eagle during the morning, setting the house ablaze.  No one was in the house when the fire started, but the house was destroyed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck a gas line, causing a fire that destroyed the adjacent house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over central Kansas during the late afternoon of the 23rd. These storms moved southeast during the evening and into eastern Oklahoma during the late evening and overnight hours. High amounts of instability and considerable deep layer shear over eastern Oklahoma resulted in the development of a highly organized line of storms. Widespread damaging wind, a tornado, and some large hail resulted across eastern Oklahoma as the line of thunderstorms moved through the region. At least 300,000 people were reportedly without power due to the storms in the area surrounding Tulsa. Some of these outages lasted for nearly a week. In addition, lightning from these storms resulted in a number of structural fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Union 8th Grade Center, igniting a fire that severely damaged the roof of the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper air disturbance combined with  a hot and humid air mass to produce strong to severe thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania during the second half of the afternoon and early evening on the 24th. In addition to locally damaging winds, lightning strikes caused one injury and damaged several homes. There were numerous reports of hail with the thunderstorms as the freezing level aloft was relatively low in height above the ground. Most of the hail was small (half an inch or less in diameter).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing electrical surge started a couple of small basement fires in a home on Half Mile Post in Bethel Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over central Kansas during the late afternoon of the 23rd. These storms moved southeast during the evening and into eastern Oklahoma during the late evening and overnight hours. High amounts of instability and considerable deep layer shear over eastern Oklahoma resulted in the development of a highly organized line of storms. Widespread damaging wind, a tornado, and some large hail resulted across eastern Oklahoma as the line of thunderstorms moved through the region. At least 300,000 people were reportedly without power due to the storms in the area surrounding Tulsa. Some of these outages lasted for nearly a week. In addition, lightning from these storms resulted in a number of structural fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning, resulting in a fire that damaged it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over central Kansas during the late afternoon of the 23rd. These storms moved southeast during the evening and into eastern Oklahoma during the late evening and overnight hours. High amounts of instability and considerable deep layer shear over eastern Oklahoma resulted in the development of a highly organized line of storms. Widespread damaging wind, a tornado, and some large hail resulted across eastern Oklahoma as the line of thunderstorms moved through the region. At least 300,000 people were reportedly without power due to the storms in the area surrounding Tulsa. Some of these outages lasted for nearly a week. In addition, lightning from these storms resulted in a number of structural fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, resulting in a fire that severely damaged it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper air disturbance combined with  a hot and humid air mass to produce strong to severe thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania during the second half of the afternoon and early evening on the 24th. In addition to locally damaging winds, lightning strikes caused one injury and damaged several homes. There were numerous reports of hail with the thunderstorms as the freezing level aloft was relatively low in height above the ground. Most of the hail was small (half an inch or less in diameter).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home on Lindsay Street in Ridley Park. Lightning struck and started a fire in the basement and also traveled along the electrical wiring within the house.  The furniture, electronics and clothing were all damaged within the home. The unharmed family was expected to be displaced for about six months.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance interacted with abundant gulf moisture in place across the region to kick off several severe storms during the period.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree beside a home was struck by lightning, knocking out power to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the evening hours that produced frequent cloud to ground lightning resulting in some property damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have struck a home in the Laguardo area. The lightning strike resulted in a fire that significantly damaged the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable airmass was over South Florida which produced scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 42-year old male crane operator was injured when his crane was struck by lightning in Lauderhill. He was taken to Broward Health Medical Center where he was listed in fair condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple thunderstorms formed along the sea breeze boundary across Long Island, with isolated severe mainly over the eastern end of the island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught on fire due to a lightning strike. Firefighters reported the roof had collapsed by the time of arrival. A dozen firefighters had to be treated for heat exhaustion fighting the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms, with isolated severe thunderstorms embedded, formed along a slow moving cold front pushing through the Tri-State area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, causing the house to fill with smoke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms, with isolated severe thunderstorms embedded, formed along a slow moving cold front pushing through the Tri-State area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in the parking lot of the Bridgeport zoo, causing it to splinter up to 200 yards away across the parking lot.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In addition to flash flooding, a lightning strike from a thunderstorm caused a house fire in Philadelphia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire caused minor damage and no personal injuries to a house on Brown Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance interacted with abundant gulf moisture in place across the region to kick off several severe storms during the period.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a residence on fire just north of the Smithdale community.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy thunderstorms moved through portions of the Northern Idaho Panhandle during the early morning hours of August 10th.  At approximately 0100 PST, lightning struck a house in Althol, ID starting the home on fire.  A lightning bolt also hit a nearby tree killing a doe and her fawn.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A bolt of lightning started a home on fire on Good Hope Road in Althol, ID.  The homeowner got out safely but the fire, fueled by natural gas in the home, destroyed everything inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the day on Sunday, July 7th, a warm, southerly flow around a Bermuda High Pressure area allowed plenty of moisture to stream into eastern New York.  This allowed for an unstable air mass to be in place across the region.  As an upper level shortwave moved from the Ohio Valley towards the Northeast, scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours.  A few of these thunderstorms became severe, producing large hail and damaging winds.  Hail reached the size of golf balls across portions of Columbia County.  During one of the thunderstorms, a man was struck by lightning on a lake beach at a state park in Columbia County.  He went to cardiac arrest, and later died.||In addition, the very moist air mass allowed these thunderstorms to produce very heavy rainfall in a short period of time.  This led to flash flooding in a few locations, including portions of the Mohawk Valley that were still cleaning up from flash flooding earlier in the month and in late June. ||Thunderstorm activity diminished by the evening hours due to the loss of daytime heating, ending the threat for additional severe storms or flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 26 year old man was struck by lightning on a beach at Lake Taghkanic State Park in Gallatin. The man was standing under a tree that was struck by lightning and the lightning traveled through this body.  He went into cardiac arrest, but was resuscitated at the park by emergency personnel.  He was then brought to a hospital in Hudson and transferred to Albany Medical Center where he later died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms, with isolated severe thunderstorms embedded, formed along a slow moving cold front pushing through the Tri-State area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, causing two small fires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak surface ridge remained in place across north Georgia, with a stalled surface boundary draped across central Georgia.  A very warm and moist airmass remained in place across the area.  Another front pushed across the Ohio Valley and into the Appalachians during the day on the 23rd.  Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours, with several reports of damaging winds and isolated flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Houston County Emergency Manager reported a lightning strike to a house on Halindon Drive.  Minor damage occurred from the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms rumbled over parts of western Washington.  One lightning strike damaged a transformer, which knocked out power to customers in Shoreline.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One lightning strike damaged a transformer, which knocked out power to customers in Shoreline.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system over Missouri lead to isolated severe thunderstorms in the afternoon. These thunderstorms produced marginal severe hail and strong gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a house and caused severe damage to the garage and upstair rooms.

The residents were expected to be displaced for about two to five months due to the damaged roof and third floor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the morning and afternoon of the 21st, a large thunderstorm complex moved from the upper Mississippi Valley southeast into the southern Wisconsin and northern Illinois area, producing severe weather and flooding. The complex gradually weakened as it tracked into the northern Wabash Valley during the evening, producing gusty winds to the northwest of Indianapolis before it diminished. This would be the start of an active period for central Indiana, with rain and thunderstorms impacting portions of the area for the rest of the month. The region remained on the fringe of a strong ridge aloft centered over the central Plains with scattered thunderstorms developing as upper level waves tracked along the periphery of the ridge and across the Ohio Valley. The development of an upper low across the region by the end of the month continued the daily threat for rain and thunderstorms. Isolated to scattered severe thunderstorms impacted central Indiana each afternoon and evening from the 22nd through the 27th. Some of the storms moved across the same areas on the 25th and 26th, producing 2 day rainfall totals over 7 inches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WISH-TV reported that an Indianapolis Zoo guard was indirectly hit by lightning Sunday afternoon when a line of storms moved through the area. Around 3:35 p.m., a security guard standing near the administration building was hit by an indirect lightning strike, meaning the charge of the lightning strike made contact, not the bolt. Authorities say the guard was alert and all vital signs were good when he was transported. His injuries are not serious.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wet month led to some minor flooding along the Steinhatchee River in southeast Taylor county.  A house was also struck by lightning in Panama City Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The media reported a house fire started by lightning near the intersection of Hutchison Blvd and Azalea St in Panama City Beach.  Monetary damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Non-severe thunderstorms occurred during the day on July 20th. Lightning struck an apartment complex, setting the structure on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Irving Fire Department responded to a three alarm fire which was caused by lightning. The fire occurred at the Eagle Crest Apartment Homes in Irving.  Three firefighters were injured in the blaze, all with minor burns.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms over the Everglades merged with the sea breeze in the Naples area and led to numerous thunderstorms with heavy rain in the evening hours. In addition to the lightning impacts, a total of 6-10 inches of rain fell in the North Naples area between 8 pm and midnight. This caused significant street flooding in the Quail Run community where about a dozen cars were stranded and had to be towed away, as well as forcing the closure of several area streets.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the exterior wall of an apartment building in East Naples, causing a fire which affected mainly the attic with moderate damage. Crews responded to the fire the following morning. Time of lightning strike estimated based on archived radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved into a very warm airmass and caused isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced strong wind gusts in Travis County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced lightning that struck and disabled the 911 Center in Elgin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved into a very warm airmass and caused isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced strong wind gusts in Travis County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Austin news station reported a house fire was caused by lightning.  The home was on Sierra Oaks in Northwest Hills.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved into a very warm airmass and caused isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced strong wind gusts in Travis County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Austin news station reported that 2 homes were damaged by a fire that was started due to a lightning strike. The homes were located on Carson Creek Road near Highway 71 in Del Valle.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moved into a very warm airmass and caused isolated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced strong wind gusts in Travis County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Austin news station reported a fire at the Hare Krishna Center was caused by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over central Kansas during the late afternoon of the 23rd. These storms moved southeast during the evening and into eastern Oklahoma during the late evening and overnight hours. High amounts of instability and considerable deep layer shear over eastern Oklahoma resulted in the development of a highly organized line of storms. Widespread damaging wind, a tornado, and some large hail resulted across eastern Oklahoma as the line of thunderstorms moved through the region. At least 300,000 people were reportedly without power due to the storms in the area surrounding Tulsa. Some of these outages lasted for nearly a week. In addition, lightning from these storms resulted in a number of structural fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a day care center, resulting in a fire that destroyed it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoonal moisture moved into Utah beginning on July 3, allowing for widespread showers and thunderstorms across the state. Many of these thunderstorms produced strong, gusty winds. Other noteworthy occurrences from these thunderstorms included at least one thunderstorm that helped produce a gustnado, and lightning that ignited fires across the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the wooden turret of a home near Ogden, setting the roof on fire. The fire spread into one of the upstairs rooms before firefighters were able to put out the blaze. Approximately $20,000 worth of damage occurred, mostly to the roof and electrical wiring.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms once again produced pockets of heavy rainfall with one report of a mud slide in a known problem area. However, some of the storms produced strong outflow winds gusts in the Cortez and Durango areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A power pole was struck by lightning and started on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms along a nearly stationary front, dumped heavy rain on parts of southeast Minnesota on August 22nd. The heavy rain produced flash flooding in Rochester (Olmsted County) that snarled the morning commute by flooding numerous intersections and sent water streaming into a Mayo Health building. The storms also produced high winds that damaged several homes and trees in Eyota (Olmsted County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three homes were struck by lightning during a thunderstorm in Rochester. The most serious strike caused minor damage when the electrical system in a home was ignited, resulting in charred outlets and burned window flashing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A monsoon burst pattern developed across central and southern New Mexico as deep moisture combined with a weak upper level disturbance over the area.  Slow-moving thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall across many areas of Catron, Socorro, Lincoln, and Torrance counties.  Several reports of flooded roadways were received across these areas.  Frequent lightning strikes and strong gusty winds were also reported with some of these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car traveling east bound on Interstate 40 three miles east of Moriarty at mile marker 199 with 4 occupants was struck by lightning. One child and one adult were injured and treated at the scene. Car's electronics were destroyed and vehicle towed from scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early afternoon thunderstorm activity created a lightning strike which hit a home and caused damage in the Bulow area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home at 17 Wilderness Way in the Bulow area was struck by lightning. It caused a hole in the roof. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early afternoon thunderstorm activity created a lightning strike which hit a home and caused damage in the Bulow area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in north Jacksonville around 11 am EDT, which sparked an electrical fire inside the home. A trench was visible where the bolt traced the roots to an air-conditioning unit and into the homes electrical circuitry. The cost of damage was estimated at $15K.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze boundary collisions took place along the I-75 corridor. Easterly flow pushed the storms into the Tampa metro area producing strong winds and damage to trees, powerlines and area homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas County Emergency Management relayed a report of a lightning strike to a house in Seminole causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The threat of severe thunderstorms returned for a couple of days in the middle of the month, with both strong, gusty winds and large hail being reported across Utah. In addition, lightning caused multiple fires in northern Utah.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire started at a Salt Lake City green waste storage site, with lightning as the suspected cause of the fire. The fire was contained to a 200-by-300-foot pit where mulch was stored, and firefighters were able to extinguish the blaze before it spread to any adjacent buildings.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms crossed southern Wisconsin during the afternoon hours of July 21st. The storms produced damaging wind gusts as well as hail up to 1 inch. Two people were hurt when their horses were struck by lightning while riding in the Kettle Moraine Forest near Eagle in Waukesha County. The thunderstorms formed in a region of focused warm air advection, with lift aided by vorticity advection from a short wave that tracked across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the ground near a group of horse riders in the Kettle Moraine Forest near Eagle. The lightning traveled through the wet ground and passed through two of the horses and one of the riders. The second rider was injured when thrown from her horse after it was struck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across central Illinois during the morning of July 10th.  One of the storms dropped between 3 and 4 inches of rain in about one hour across southern Logan County and northwest Macon County, leading to flash flooding. Other storms produced damaging wind gusts, resulting in downed trees and flattened corn fields in a few locations.  In addition, lightning strikes caused house fires in both Lincoln and Ogden.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire on the 800 block of North Sherman Street in Lincoln.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The area remained in a warm and humid air mass with afternoon thunderstorms developing rather easily. Most of the storms remained below severe criteria but a few were able to generate enough downburst wind speed for some tree damage. Heavy rainfall also accompanied the storms along with some minor flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church which sustained minor damage and a tree was exploded adjacent to the church. A propane line and fuse boxes in the church were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few discrete thunderstorms formed in a hot and humid air mass ahead of an inland advancing sea breeze boundary.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a grass fire between the towns of Brenham and Washington.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an attic fire in a residential home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an attic fire in a residential home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The threat of severe thunderstorms returned for a couple of days in the middle of the month, with both strong, gusty winds and large hail being reported across Utah. In addition, lightning caused multiple fires in northern Utah.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a cluster of oil storage tanks just outside Altamont, starting a fire at the facility. At least one of the tanks exploded, sending 50-foot-tall flames into the air, and creating a loud boom that woke people in Altamont. One tank was launched outside the containment berm around the well location, and two other storage tanks were engulfed in flames before firefighters reached the site. Once crews shut down the gas line that runs near the well, firefighters were able to put out the fire in less than two hours, and no injuries occurred due to the fire or explosion.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave and associated cold front were approaching from the northwest during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 17th. Very high precipitable water values and very warm temperatures ahead of the front combined with increasing shear to produce numerous severe thunderstorms, mainly during the evening hours. Due to high freezing levels, wind damage and very heavy rain were the main features of these storms as they moved through the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from an early morning thunderstorm struck a 22-ft sailboat at a marina near Moultenborough and ignited a fire which destroyed the boat.  A second boat (a 28-ft runabout) also caught fire and was destroyed.  Both boats sank into Lake Winnipesaukee.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes caused damage in two locations including a shed that was set on fire and at a private residence along Old Court House Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level high over Florida began to weaken on the 12th, and a weak surface front over Tennessee began to shift south during the day. Once again, several showers and thunderstorms developed, and one produced flash flooding in a portion of White County, where flash flooding had occurred on the 11th.  Another thunderstorm briefly reached severe levels with damaging winds in Coweta County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media relayed reports of two people injured by lightning in Summerville.  Wiring in the apartment complex that was struck was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper high was parked squarely over New Mexico. Overnight showers across the Gila region in southwestern NM were responsible for significant rainfall amounts across the Whitewater-Baldy burn scar. This caused some flooding with debris deposits along roads in the area. Afternoon showers and thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain then drifted over the plains and adjacent highlands. Storm motions were generally very slow to the north or northeast. Flooding developed at Los Alamos National Labs as an isolated thunderstorm formed directly overhead and remained nearly stationary for an extended period of time. There was also a lightning injury reported from another isolated storm near Santa Fe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Santa Fe New Mexican ran story about lightning hitting a large cottonwood tree in the Santa Fe Plaza. The bolt hit the tree and sent branches flying into a nearby crowd of people that were gathered in downtown for weekend festivities. Newspaper reporting that at least one man was injured from flying debris while another had breathing problems for a short time.

In addition to locally damaging winds, lightning strikes caused one injury and damaged several homes. There were numerous reports of hail with the thunderstorms as the freezing level aloft was relatively low in height above the ground. Most of the hail was small (half an inch or less in diameter).

Firefighters responded to the fire at 330 PM EDT to the fire already in progress. About 20,000 square feet of the building was completely burned, with the Gym sustaining most of the damage. Damage was estimated at 2 million dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalling cold front helped trigger strong thunderstorms during the second half of the afternoon on the 21st in the southern half of New Jersey.  Also the combination, of the full moon and some of the highest astronomical tides of 2013, caused minor tidal flooding to occur along the New Jersey shore during the evening high tide cycle from the 21st through the 25th. The highest tides (all during the evening high tide cycle on the 22nd) included 6.43 feet above mean lower low water in Atlantic City (Atlantic County), 7.36 feet above mean lower low water in Cape May (Cape May County) and 7.32 feet above mean lower low water in Sandy Hook (Monmouth County). Minor tidal flooding starts at 6.0 feet above mean lower low water in Atlantic City and 6.7 feet above mean lower low water in Cape May and Sandy Hook.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike took down a couple of wires in Bordentown.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured by a lightning strike while working on the Glen Mills Reform School's baseball field in Concord Township.  From 2 p.m. EDT to 3 p.m. EDT there were over 1,000 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes in the local Philadelphia area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very strong Tropical Wave moved over Puerto Rico during July 18, 2013. This wave brought deep topical moisture from the Intertropical Convergence Zone(ITCZ) through the area. These features, in combination with a southeast wind flow and local effects produced torrential rainfall, mainly along the north coast of Puerto Rico. Streamers from El Yunque National Forest developed in the afternoon on July 18, 2013, and were moving very slowly toward the northwest, which affected the San Juan Metropolitan area. The streamers redeveloped over the same area, and brought with it torrential rainfall which led to serious flooding across the San Juan Metro Area. The total rainfall accumulation exceed 9 inches over San Juan. Rainfall totals between 3 to 5 inches were also reported across the North Central section of Puerto Rico. Several reports of flooding were received from the municipalities of San Juan, Carolina, Bayamon and Guaynabo with hundreds of residences and roads affected by the waters. Overall losses were estimated over 1 million dollars across the San Juan Metropolitan area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a balcony and knocked down a power line in Barrio Pajuil.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning low end derecho moved through the region on the 13th which caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop across southeastern Pennsylvania. The derecho moved off the New Jersey coast by late morning leaving a boundary across parts of the region. Later in the day, a strong low pressure system brought a cold front through the region, which sparked off more strong to severe thunderstorms across the area.||In addition to wind, heavy rain was reported with these storms. In general, 1 to 3 inches of rain fell across the state with the heaviest amounts reported across the Lehigh Valley. Rainfall amounts included 1.71 inches in Hellertown (Northampton County), 1.69 inches in South Allentown (Lehigh County), 1.61 inches in Upper Macungie Township and Macungie (Lehigh County), 1.56 inches in Forks Township (Northampton County), 1.23 inches in Jim Thorpe (Carbon County), 1.20 inches in Palmerton (Carbon County), 1.10 inches in Landenburg (Chester County) and 1.02 inches in Alburtis (Berks County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two houses were reported to be struck by lightning in the Broomall section of Marple Township. A house at the Women's Center at Swarthmore College was also struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong mid level trough moved across north Alabama during the evening of July 10th. Strong to severe storms erupted along and ahead of a cold front along the mid level trough. These storms produced scattered wind damage and flash flooding across several areas in north Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in an outbuilding catching fire near the Central community, near Wright, Alabama.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very humid airmass with dewpoints well into the lower 70s was in place over the Lower Ohio Valley during the late morning and early afternoon on July 10th.  A sharpening trough over the western Great Lakes brought moderate mid-level northwest flow over the region during the afternoon hours.  Strong instability and the absence of a cap allowed individual strong storms to develop by early afternoon across northern Kentucky along Interstate 64.  Some of these storms brought localized damaging wind gusts.  A cold pool driven short bowing segment crossed Harrison and Floyd counties in Indiana during the mid afternoon hours, eventually crossing the Ohio River and entering Louisville. This bowing segment brought widespread damaging winds to Louisville, including a 64 mph measured wind gust at Standiford Field in Louisville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local law enforcement relayed a report of a house in Fountain Run damaged by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm associated with a trough of low pressure produced lightning damage across portions of central Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Large tree was partially debarked by a lightning strike.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Florida State watch office reported a house fire started by a lightning strike near Druid Road and Woodside Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong thunderstorms developed during the late morning and afternoon hours across the western Florida Panhandle on July 13.  A few storms became severe producing large hail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A band of thunderstorms moved across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the morning hours of the 5th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, causing a fire that severely damaged it. An elderly woman in the house was killed by the fire after she called 911.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of thunderstorms developed Thursday late afternoon and evening, June 20th, mostly in west central Minnesota, and moved eastward. These storms produced some penny to quarter size hail, but the main event was damaging straight line winds and torrential rainfall during the late evening and overnight period. These storms moved across central and east central Minnesota after midnight, with some redevelopment in far south central Minnesota toward daybreak. ||Flash flooding was observed in portions of west central and central Minnesota where locally three to five inches of rain fell in a short period of time. The towns of Morris, Glenwood, Starbuck, Sauk Centre and Long Prairie were the hardest hit with numerous flooded roadways. ||Wind damage came in two different waves, the first was associated with embedded bow-echoes that moved across central Minnesota, while the second wave came from outflow from previous thunderstorms.||Strong outflow winds from previous thunderstorms affected four counties in central Minnesota, producing a wide area of damage. Winds exceeded 40 mph for nearly two hours in portions of Todd and Stearns Counties.  Peak gusts include 63 mph at Sauk Centre (Stearns County) at 0200, 60 mph in Clearwater (Wright County) at 0240, 55 mph at Rice (Benton County) at 0200, and 54 mph at Long Prairie (Todd County) at 0235.   A business in Long Prairie lost a roof during the height of the high winds. Debris was blown to the south, landing on cars in a parking lot, and numerous trees were blown down around Long Prairie.  Trees and power lines were downed across portions of Todd, Benton, Stearns and Wright Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire in Rosemount, Minnesota. The house fire was a total loss, but no one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning low end derecho moved through the region on the 13th which caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop across eastern Maryland. The derecho moved off the New Jersey coast by late morning leaving a boundary across parts of the region. Later in the day, a strong low pressure system brought a cold front through the region, which sparked off more strong to severe thunderstorms across the area.||In addition to wind, heavy rain was reported with these storms. Most locations saw up to an inch of rain fall, with locally higher amounts of up to 2 inches reported. Rainfall amounts included 1.81 inches in Worton (Kent County), 0.98 inches in Elkton (Cecil County) and 0.88 inches in Greensboro (Caroline County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning at the Plumpton Park Zoo in Rising Sun, MD. She was standing next to a tree that took the bulk of the energy. She was initially in cardiac arrest but regained a pulse and was transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm associated with a trough of low pressure produced lightning damage across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Partially exposed underground gas line was struck by lightning on Songbird Trail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid airmass was in place over the forecast area on the afternoon of June 24th. Convection developed early in the afternoon over eastern New York and western New England and shifted east into the favorable environment across New Hampshire and western Maine through the evening hours. Very weak shear and high precipitable water resulted in pulse type convection with large hail and wet microbursts the main threats. Thirty people were injured by lightning at a Boy Scout Camp near Gilmanton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike injured 29 scouts and 1 leader at Camp Bell Boy Scout Camp on Griswold Scout Reservation near Gilmanton.  All the Scouts were transported to a local hospital and were treated for burns, ranging from minor to serious.  Several of the scouts were retained overnight for observation and treatment.  The Scouts had taken shelter under a tarp strung between trees when lightning struck a tall pine tree about 30 feet away.  The current traveled through the ground to the scouts who were sitting around a table on metal chairs.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sufficient moisture and a series of shortwaves moving through the region allowed for the development of showers and thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts, hail, and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Eagle Lake Baptist Church was struck by lightning resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the late afternoon and evening of June 24th, a bow echo raced across northern Illinois causing widespread wind damage and spawning at least one tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A natural gas transmission facility was struck by lightning resulting in the building catching on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary band of thunderstorms developed across southwest Wisconsin during the evening of June 21st. These storms remained in place until another line of storms pushed in from the west during the early morning hours of the 22nd. Rainfall amounts exceeded six inches with flash flooding reported in parts of Crawford, Grant and Richland Counties. The area in and around Boscobel (Grant County) was hit extremely hard by the flooding. 650 homes were impacted by the flooding with two dozen families displaced, most homes had basements full of water with some having the water reach the first level. Roads in the region had numerous washouts and some bridges were blown out. Rescue crews had to save 54 canoeists who became stranded on the Wisconsin River due to rising waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house in Holmen was struck by lightning. The electrical box, some windows and the roof were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep moisture and strong surface heating set up an environment favorable for strong to severe thunderstorms as a cold front stalled over the region and interacted with an inland moving seabreeze.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A medic was struck by lightning near the Winn Army Community Hospital. The individual was touching a doorknob when the strike sent an electric shock through the trailer he was in.

The derecho moved off the New Jersey coast by late morning leaving a boundary across parts of the region. Later in the day, a strong low pressure system brought a cold front through the region, which sparked off more strong to severe thunderstorms across the area. Atlantic City Electric reported approximately 1774 outages in the region due to the storms.||In addition to wind, heavy rain was reported with these storms. In general, 1 to 2 inches of rain fell across the state with the heaviest amounts reported across the north central and the southern parts of the state. Rainfall amounts included 2.03 inches in Greenwich Township (Cumberland County), 1.92 inches in Holmdel (Monmouth County), 1.75 inches in Bethlehem Township (Hunterdon County), 1.72 inches in Upper Deerfield Township (Cumberland County), 1.71 inches in Wantage (Sussex County), 1.69 inches in Vineland (Cumberland County), 1.67 inches in Andover (Sussex County) and Holland Township (Hunterdon County), 1.62 in Estell Manor (Atlantic County) and Pittsgrove Township (Salem County), 1.60 inches in Edison (Middlesex County) and Franklin Township (Somerset County), 1.59 inches in Bridgewater Township (Somerset County) and Blairstown (Warren County), 1.52 inches in Chatham (Morris County), 1.51 inches in Cranbury (Middlesex County), 1.48 inches in Folsom (Atlantic County) and Woodbine (Cape May County), and 1.45 inches in Washington Township (Warren County).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Twelve soldiers, involved in training exercise, were struck by lightning south of Butts Field on the north side of Fort Carson.  Two soldiers were taken to a hospital in Colorado Springs, one in critical condition.  The other ten soldiers were taken to the base hospital and later released.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms initiated as a mid level shortwave shifted over deep moisture in the southeastern United States. Differential heating boundaries from previous cloud cover provided a focusing mechanism for a few thunderstorms to become severe with damaging wind gusts and heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported a lightning strike caused a house fire along County Home Road. The report was confirmed by a Dorchester County fire chief.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a late Spring cold front as it pushed southeast across north Texas. Isolated minor wind damage occurred around the area late Wednesday night and Thursday morning associated with the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused fires to two homes along Cooke County Road 224 early in the morning of June 6th. Fires destroyed an outdoor storage building, and an unnocupied house near the community of Woodbine.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a late Spring cold front as it pushed southeast across north Texas. Isolated minor wind damage occurred around the area late Wednesday night and Thursday morning associated with the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting started a fire at an apartment complex in North Richland Hills early in the morning of June 6th. Additionally, the storms and lightning strikes caused an estimated 19,000 customers to be without power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough moving through a very warm and unstable air mass provided the focus for scattered severe thunderstorms over north central Upper Michigan during the early morning of the 26th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged electronics equipment in a neighborhood northeast of Negaunee.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level trough moved through north Alabama during the morning, producing heavy rainfall and a few reports of wind damage and flash flooding in northwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and started a fire, producing some light damage to the residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level trough moved through north Alabama during the morning, producing heavy rainfall and a few reports of wind damage and flash flooding in northwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a structure, starting a fire and produced minor damage, on Pine Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak frontal boundary along with several upper level impulses that moved over the Missouri Ozarks resulted in isolated severe thunderstorms that produced large hail, wind damage, and flash flooding. An isolated thunderstorm developed over south Springfield and was nearly stationary for several hours. This storm produced extremely heavy rainfall rates in a localized area causing significant flash flooding over an urban area including water into neighborhoods, homes, and businesses. Numerous streets and low water crossing areas were flooded and impassable. Several high water rescues were performed. The total estimated cost for damage for this particular storm over southern Greene County and south Springfield will be added together in one storm report.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two house fires were started due to lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning low end derecho moved through the region on the 13th which caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop across southeastern Pennsylvania. The derecho moved off the New Jersey coast by late morning leaving a boundary across parts of the region. Later in the day, a strong low pressure system brought a cold front through the region, which sparked off more strong to severe thunderstorms across the area.||In addition to wind, heavy rain was reported with these storms. In general, 1 to 3 inches of rain fell across the state with the heaviest amounts reported across the Lehigh Valley. Rainfall amounts included 1.71 inches in Hellertown (Northampton County), 1.69 inches in South Allentown (Lehigh County), 1.61 inches in Upper Macungie Township and Macungie (Lehigh County), 1.56 inches in Forks Township (Northampton County), 1.23 inches in Jim Thorpe (Carbon County), 1.20 inches in Palmerton (Carbon County), 1.10 inches in Landenburg (Chester County) and 1.02 inches in Alburtis (Berks County).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of thunderstorms developed Thursday late afternoon and evening, June 20th, mostly in west central Minnesota, and moved eastward. These storms produced some penny to quarter size hail, but the main event was damaging straight line winds and torrential rainfall during the late evening and overnight period. These storms moved across central and east central Minnesota after midnight, with some redevelopment in far south central Minnesota toward daybreak. ||Flash flooding was observed in portions of west central and central Minnesota where locally three to five inches of rain fell in a short period of time. The towns of Morris, Glenwood, Starbuck, Sauk Centre and Long Prairie were the hardest hit with numerous flooded roadways. ||Wind damage came in two different waves, the first was associated with embedded bow-echoes that moved across central Minnesota, while the second wave came from outflow from previous thunderstorms.||Strong outflow winds from previous thunderstorms affected four counties in central Minnesota, producing a wide area of damage. Winds exceeded 40 mph for nearly two hours in portions of Todd and Stearns Counties.  Peak gusts include 63 mph at Sauk Centre (Stearns County) at 0200, 60 mph in Clearwater (Wright County) at 0240, 55 mph at Rice (Benton County) at 0200, and 54 mph at Long Prairie (Todd County) at 0235.   A business in Long Prairie lost a roof during the height of the high winds. Debris was blown to the south, landing on cars in a parking lot, and numerous trees were blown down around Long Prairie.  Trees and power lines were downed across portions of Todd, Benton, Stearns and Wright Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire in Minnetonka, Minnesota.  The house was a total loss but no one was hurt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm producing cloud to ground lightning struck a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on South Shore Drive near Longwood Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A bolt of lightning struck a van that was being driven on Interstate 95 in Mims.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A bolt of lightning struck a van that was being driven southbound on Interstate 95 in Mims. The windshield shattered, the engine was disabled, and all four tires were blown out. The front portion of the van then burst into flames. The driver was able to get out of the vehicle safely, with no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that developed over northwest Minnesota during the evening of June 20th, moved across western Wisconsin during the early morning hours of the 21st. These storms produced large hail and winds strong enough to cause damage. Trees were blown down in the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) and a pontoon boat was flipped by the high winds on Lake Onalaska (La Crosse County). Most of the hail that fell was penny to nickel sized. Locally heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in the city of La Crosse and a minor mud slide south of Genoa (Vernon County) that covered part of State Highway 35.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A couple of power poles were struck by lightning in Holmen.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A ferocious line of strong to severe thunderstorms raced through central North Carolina|during the afternoon and into the early evening, uprooting trees and snapping power lines with straight-line wind gusts up to 80 mph. Damage was widespread with numerous trees falling on homes throughout the county warning area. The city of Albermarle, in Stanly County was hardest hit, with approximately 70 homes damaged and at least 3 injuries from trees crashing into and through homes and mobile homes. A University of North Carolina student   also died from injuries received when a large tree fell and landed on top of her on the sidewalk.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning produced a structure fire to a barn on Hesters Store Road.  Monetary damages were estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred during July 21-23 with a few storms becoming severe.  In addition, a few people were struck by lightning on a farm in Decatur county, resulting in 1 fatality and 2 injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Lady Moon Farms, resuling in 1 fatality and 2 injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a trough of low pressure stalled over the region and a passing upper level disturbance triggered a line of severe thunderstorms, which passed across Orange and Putnam Counties.  This line produced heavy rainfall, which resulted in flash flooding in Orange county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Fort Montgomery causing a fire and roof collapse.

A telephone was knocked down near the courthouse.   A trailer at the Sage Hill Travel Center was struck by lightning and destroyed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level shortwave moved southeast across the Tennessee Valley region during the early morning of June 26th. This upper level system produced a cluster of thunderstorms across a portion of southern middle Tennessee, with lightning causing damage to a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, resulting in it falling onto a home along Highway 231 about a mile north of the Tennessee and Alabama border in Lincoln County, Tennessee.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from early morning thunderstorms on June 12th in the Austin area (Mower County) caused a garage to start on fire. No injuries occurred in the fire, but the garage was destroyed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from an early morning thunderstorm destroyed the garage at a home on the east side of Austin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system passing by to the northwest of Arkansas brought two rounds of winter weather from the 20th into the 21st. During the morning of the 20th, light snow, occasionally mixed with sleet, broke out in western Arkansas. Most snowfall was in the 1 to 2 inch range, with spotty totals around 3 inches. Some areas of light snow, sleet, and freezing rain continued into the evening in the northern part of Arkansas, with light rain in the south. Precipitation began to pick up considerably toward dawn on the 21st and continued throughout much of the day. Freezing rain was the predominant precipitation type in the north, while a cold rain fell in the south. Thunderstorms occurred in all sections of the state. In the northern part of Arkansas, an ice storm occurred, with ice accruals generally in the 1/4 to 1/2 inch range. However, there were some totals around 3/4 inch, especially in Stone, Izard, Sharp, and Independence counties. Altogether, about 10,000 power outages were reported. Meanwhile, isolated severe storms with large hail occurred in the south.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning, causing a fire. Due to the amount of lightning in the area, firefighters delayed climbing onto the roof of the house. Four people lived in the house, but no one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few storms developed and moved rapidly east-northeast into northwest and north central Alabama during the morning hours around sunrise.  These storms produced mostly small hail, but a couple produced hail up to quarter sized.  As time wore on and a cold front punched in from the west, the storms evolved into a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) stretching from northeast through central Alabama.  One storm produced a meso-vortex (circulation) resulting in measured winds of 59-62 mph in northern Marshall County, which eventually produced wind damage just west of Rainsville in Dekalb County after the noon hour.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a telephone pole near the Wal-Mart in Guntersville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front across the Virginia Piedmont as it marched into a preceding unseasonably warm air mass.  Although the thunderstorms were not severe, they did produce a considerable amount of lightning causing a house fire in Ringgold, near Danville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Social media outlets and the Danville City web site reported that lightning struck a home in the 5000 block of Kentuk Road in Ringgold.  Lightning traveled into the house via the hot water heater line causing a fire at the structure.  The local fire department quickly extinguished the fire, thus damage was only minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced a lightning strike which hit a building on the southeast side of Springfield.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire caused by a lightning strike destroyed an office building of the Journagan Construction quarry operations near Farm Road 194 and Farm Road 195. Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms developed along an eastward moving Pacific cold front during the very early morning hours. Some of the thunderstorms reached severe limits; generally producing winds up to 65 MPH. The most significant areas of damage that occurred from severe thunderstorms winds was in Luella in Grayson County and in Temple in Bell County. In Luella, 5 homes were damaged from straightline winds that occurred within a bookend vortex on the northern end of the line of thunderstorms. Two homes were nearly destroyed by the winds. In Temple, widespread wind damage was reported in the western portions of the city. In addition, a lightning strike burned a historic church to the ground in Honey Grove in Fannin County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Main Street Presbyterian Church in Honey Grove and the church burned to the ground. The church had been built in 1902.
