EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convection broke out during the afternoon, ahead of a cold front moving southeast through Ohio.  The showers and thunderstorms moved southeast into West Virginia during the evening.  As the convection matured, some stronger wind gusts occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the electric box on the side of a house.  A fire was ignited.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An occluded front moved through West Tennessee during the afternoon hours of February 10, 2013 along with widespread showers and a few thunderstorms. A thunderstorm in Decatur County produced lightning that resulted in a minor injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning while lifting the garage door of a storage unit and suffered a minor injury to her right arm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The dry line became active during the afternoon of May 17th. Only a few storms fired along the dry line across Young and Stephens Counties. However, several reports of large hail, and two tornadoes occurred with these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Young County Emergency Manager reported lightning struck a tank battery, resulting in a fire. No other structures were impacted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large subtropical ridge over the western Atlantic and adjacent southeastern United States pumped unseasonably warm air and rich moisture into the Ohio Valley and Mid-Atlantic. This ring-of-fire pattern of moderate instability and strong deep layer wind shear on the northern periphery of the upper-level ridge was conducive for the development of several early-season thunderstorm complexes (QLCS/MCS). The severe storms with embedded bow echoes moved eastward from the Ohio Valley along and south of a strong low-level frontal zone and produced damaging winds and marginally severe hail in central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a county-owned building next to the Warren Hospital. Damage to the roof was limited to one small hole.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a line of showers and thunderstorms moved west to east across Middle Tennessee during the morning hours of Monday, March 18th, some of these thunderstorms reached severe thresholds, resulting in large hail, thunderstorm wind damage, and the occurence of four different tornadoes. Three of these tornadoes were EF0 rated, with the fourth tornado rated an EF1 tornado, with a path length that went across three different counties. Two lightning strikes on school buildings across the mid state occurred also with these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck in the area of the school's science and vocational buildings around 10 a.m.  Smoke was reported in part of the buildings, but firefighters said no fire was detected. Some electronic equipment was damaged, including the fire alarm system.|No injuries were reported, and students returned to classes within an hour of being evacuated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted north, through southern Ohio, during the morning of the 12th.  Heating and instability increased during the afternoon with dew points reaching the lower 70s during the afternoon.  Disturbances in the mid and upper levels rippled southeast initially.  Addditional disturbances then moved east overnight Wednesday night.||Showers and thunderstorms formed over northern Ohio early on the evening of the 12th, and streaked southeast.   The southern edge of this convection finally sank down into portions of southeast Ohio late at night.   A few storms were severe, causing wind damage. ||Meanwhile, a separate large cluster of showers and thunderstorms moved out of northern Indiana into southeast Ohio during the predawn hours.  The southern edge of that convection became oriented west to east along the fast flow aloft.  Training of showers did cause 1.5 to 2 inches of rain across portions of Jackson, Vinton, Athens, Meigs and northern Gallia Counties.   Due to the relatively dry ground, no serious flash flooding occurred.  Some street flooding was observed in towns such as Athens and Gallipolis.  ||The final round of convection, associated with the cold front, streaked through southeast Ohio during the late morning hours on the 13th.  This caused another brief downpour with pea size hail and wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph.  No significant damage occurred.  Jackson Ohio reported about .9 inches in just over an hour.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A garage was struck, causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front brought scattered strong thunderstorms to central Illinois during the pre-dawn hours of April 16th.  One cell became severe, producing hail up to the size of pennies and some minor wind damage in Sangamon County.  A lightning strike occurred in Springfield, damaging the roof of a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Springfield, creating a hole in the roof.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank 2 miles south-southwest of Clarksburg in Shelby County at about 2:20 PM CDT on April 16th. The lightning caused an explosion that showered debris more than 100 yards away and created a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a funeral home in Burleson, causing a fire in the steeple.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Lucas Blessing Funeral Home on Johnson Avenue in Burleson. The fire was contained in the steeple of the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a structure fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apparent lightning strike started a fire which destroyed a storage building. A car and boat along with tools were in the building and was a total loss. The strike happened near the intersection of Farm Road 203 and Langtry Lane. Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong, negatively tilted upper low pressure area was moving from the central U.S. toward the northeast U.S.  An associated strong cold front extended down the spine of the Appalachians early in the morning.  An unseasonably warm air mass resided across the region in advance of this weather system, responsible for some of the warmest temperatures since the previous early fall across the area.  Afternoon temperatures Thursday afternoon soared to 90 in the Roanoke area.  The very warm temperatures in advance of the strong upper dynamics supported the development of an intense line of thunderstorms or quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) which marched through southern Virginia and northern North Carolina during the early morning hours.  Strong thunderstorm wind gusts blew down a number of trees through the counties bordering North Carolina from Carroll county on the west to Pittsylvania county on the east.  There was also one lightning strike causing considerable damage to a home in Botetourt county, just northeast of Roanoke.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Botetourt View reported that a home in Fincastle sustained significant damage from fire and smoke as a result of a lightning strike.  A portion of the attic and roof of the large two-story home on Brugh's Mill Road were badly damaged by fire from the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A woman east of Pomona was killed by a lightning strike in her front yard.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Howell County Coroner reported that a lightning strike caused the death of a woman near Pomona. Time was estimated by radar and thunderstorms in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon heat and humidity contributed to the development of isolated thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 22nd, resulting in isolated wind damage and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two trees and a gas line at a residence on Arkansas 107. The lightning then traveled along the gas line to a house, damaging the wall behind the kitchen stove.

About 2,200 Jersey Central Power and Light customers lost power that evening, the majority were in Warren County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire destroyed a home and left a family homeless on Brahma Avenue in Bridgewater Township. Lightning struck the home's electrical system and sparked a fire. There was heavy fire damage on the second floor and smoke and water damage throughout the house. Three fire companies took about thirty minutes to extinguish the blaze. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms brought power outages to portions of northwest Montana while a man was injured by lightning in Ravalli county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old male was struck by lightning while changing an irrigation pipe. Injuries were reported as second degree burns.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A substation was severely damaged by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a line of showers and thunderstorms moved west to east across Middle Tennessee during the morning hours of Monday, March 18th, some of these thunderstorms reached severe thresholds, resulting in large hail, thunderstorm wind damage, and the occurence of four different tornadoes. Three of these tornadoes were EF0 rated, with the fourth tornado rated an EF1 tornado, with a path length that went across three different counties. Two lightning strikes on school buildings across the mid state occurred also with these thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike occurred to Fairview Middle School at 7200 Cumberland Drive in Fairview. The lightning strike caused light smoke to come out of a restroom fan along with an unpleasant odor, but no fire resulted. Specific details concerning amount of damage to the restroom fan along with damage to any portions of the school were unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance initiated a few strong to severe thunderstorms. The storms produced large hail, up to softball size, across portions of the Southeast Texas Coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an apartment fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through South Central Texas causing thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced lightning that started a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot, humid weather prevailed over Arkansas on the 10th. The approach of a cold front triggered the development of several severe storms during the afternoon and evening. The front was making its way though the state on the 11th, triggering a few severe storms in the southern half of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree on Horseshoe Mountain in Lake Catherine State Park. Slightly more than an acre burned. A downpour associated with the storm helped to extinguish the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening hours of May 30th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old girl was struck by lightning in O'Brien Park.  Police found her unconscious and not breathing, she was pronounced dead at the scene a short time later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms preceding a cold front during the afternoon of the 11th caused isolated wind damage, mainly in the northern part of New Jersey. Lightning strikes caused power outages in southeastern New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a line of thunderstorms caused about 600 homes and businesses to lose power in Atlantic County with a few dozen additional outages in Cape May and Cumberland Counties. Traffic lights were out along the Black Horse Pike (U.S. Routes 40 and 322) in Egg Harbor Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure tracking along a stationary frontal boundary triggered severe thunderstorms across parts of central Illinois during the afternoon and evening of April 10th.  The storms were most concentrated along and east of I-55, where scattered reports of large hail and damaging winds were reported.  The largest hail stones up to the size of tennis balls occurred near Paris in Edgar County.  In addition to the hail and wind, heavy rain fell across the entire area, leading to flash flooding.  Rainfall totals of 3 to 5 inches were common.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning on County Road 900 North about a half mile east of US-45.  Damage occurred to the vehicle and a large hole was blown into the pavement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Port St. Lucie police officer was injured when lightning struck only 10 to 15 feet away from where he was standing.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Port St. Lucie police officer was injured after lightning struck less than 15 feet away when he was investigating a domestic call at the Saints Golf Course, in the 1500 block of Westmoreland Boulevard. The officer couldn't hear for 45 minutes after the strike and said he could feel the charge leaving his body through his fingertips. The glue that attached the sole and body of his boot melted into his sock. He was held overnight at a hospital, but was released the following day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Flash flooding brought debris and mud down toward Stove Prairie from the High Park Fire burn area.  The debris was washed off of Mt. Ethel and spilled down toward the Stove Prairie area, which is 10 miles west of Bellvue.  A trained weather spotter observed mud and debris flow around both sides of their home and a barn.  One to  one-and-one-half inches of rain fell over the burn area.  Rist Canyon Road was closed because of the flooding; Ford Hill Road was also closed at Stove Prairie.  The damage was confined to the roadways.  In addition, lightning struck down and destroyed a large tree on the CSU Campus.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck down and destroyed a large tree in the Colorado State University annual flower trial garden.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced lightning during the afternoon hours of April 9th and again during the early morning hours of April 10th, igniting 3 separate house fires. The lightning also stuck power lines that caused power outages affecting about 6300 customers in the Milwaukee metropolitan area. The thunderstorms fired up as a low-level jet impinged along an 850 mb baroclinic zone that set up over the area ahead of a 500 mb short-wave, with additional forcing for deep vertical motions provided by a nearly-coupled upper jet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire occurred in the town of New Berlin when the residence was struck by lightning. Only minor damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced lightning during the afternoon hours of April 9th and again during the early morning hours of April 10th, igniting 3 separate house fires. The lightning also stuck power lines that caused power outages affecting about 6300 customers in the Milwaukee metropolitan area. The thunderstorms fired up as a low-level jet impinged along an 850 mb baroclinic zone that set up over the area ahead of a 500 mb short-wave, with additional forcing for deep vertical motions provided by a nearly-coupled upper jet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire occurred in the town of Merton when lightning strike caused a gas line leak, igniting the leaking gas.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire occurred in Waupun when lightning hit near the home and traveled down a metal line to a gas fireplace in the residence, blowing a hole in the fireplace liner and igniting gas fumes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms during typical summer afternoons on June 24th and 25th.  Lightning struck one home in Jackson county and hail was reported in Bay county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire at 2878 Magnolia Blossom Lane in the Indian Springs subdivision east of Marianna.  The Jackson County Floridian newspaper article stated that damages to the house and its contents totaled around $600,000.  The time of the strike was estimated by lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of Thunderstorms occurred during the afternoon and evening of May 29th. A dry line was moving east from west Texas, but the strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of the dry line, producing several reports of gusty thunderstorm winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Denton County Fire marshal reported a house in the 9300 block of Blanco Drive caught fire after lightning struck the roof. The house was severely damaged, causing the home to be temporarily uninhabitable. Due to the fire, the roof is completely gone and the first floor suffered water damage. The siding of a neighboring house was damaged by the heat of the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across central Illinois during the afternoon of May 26th.  Lightning from one of the storms struck a fisherman on the Kaskaskia River near the Lake Shelbyville Dam.  The man was later pronounced dead at the Shelby Memorial Hospital in Shelbyville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 29 year-old fisherman was struck by lightning on the Kaskaskia River near the Lake Shelbyville Dam at around 3:50 PM CDT on Sunday, May 26th.  The man later died at Shelby Memorial Hospital in Shelbyville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level disturbance interacting with a warm and humid airmass helped trigger a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 21st.  A few of the storms produced winds of around 60 mph and hail as large as quarters as they dropped southward through the area.  In addition, lightning caused a structure fire in downtown Lincoln.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike initiated a roof fire at the Oasis Senior Center on the corner of Pulaski and Kickapoo Streets in downtown Lincoln.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm with intense lightning passed across the Hopkinsville area. The storm occurred ahead of a cold front that was crossing Missouri and Illinois.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man received non life-threatening injuries when he was struck by lightning on a golf course. One of his socks was burned. He was transported to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi late on the night of the 18th and early on the morning of the 19th. Strong thunderstorms developed in advance of the front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Gulfport home during the early morning hours. One home was destroyed by the ensuing fire and a second home suffered minor damage to vinyl siding.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system moved along a stalled frontal boundary just south of Long Island, producing showers and thunderstorms, with isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Airmont, causing a man to move across an interior room.  He was not injured. Lightning also tore off shingles and bowed a wall of a neighboring house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front interacted with an existing dry line on the 21st of the month. A line of thunderstorms developed early in the day to the north of the Red River. The line continued to move south and east, moving into increasingly unstable air across north Texas. Numerous reports of large hail and damaging winds were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several fires were started by lightning on the afternoon of May 21st. Two houses suffered fire damage after lightning struck their roof. Another lightning strike destroyed a battery of oil tanks near County Road 208.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable environment coupled with weak forcing along a passing upper-level front led to scattered strong thunderstorms along the East Slopes of the Washington Cascades during the early afternoon hours of June 29th.  Although storm motion was on the order of 20 to 30 miles per hour, cell training across the higher terrain of southeastern Chelan County led to rainfall amounts ranging from one to one and a half inches over the duration of an hour.  The runoff from these storms flowed down Canyons One and Canyon Two into the city of Wenatchee and sewer systems became overwhelmed resulting in flash flooding across southwestern portions of the city.  These storms also fell over portions of the 2012 Peavine burn scar resulting in two known debris flows; one that carried debris from Tronsen Ridge and washed out a section of Upper Tronsen Road and a second that deposited hundreds of trees onto USFS Trails in Devil's Gulch.  Further east closer to the Idaho border, elevated thunderstorms throughout the morning and early afternoon led to numerous lightning strikes and damage to transformers in Spokane.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Spokane's South Hill starting a fire.  Firefighters were able to quickly extinguish the fire but the home did sustain heavy fire damage to a small portion of the attic and to the ceiling in one second floor bedroom.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Extremely powerful severe thunderstorms erupted over Central Kansas in the afternoon, then went on a rampage across South-Central and Southeast Kansas from late in the afternoon through late that evening. Early in the event, the severe thunderstorms produced very large hail, as large as softballs, then evolved into prolific damaging wind producers. Widespread 70-90 mph winds occurred, no doubt causing tremendous damage to trees, many of which were quite large. A few trees were around 20-feet tall with 2-3 foot diameter trunks. Several trees fell onto houses that, in a few cases, caused roof damage. Damage to power lines and power poles was certainly widespread and resulted in numerous power outages. Around 25,000 residences lost power in the Wichita Metro area alone; with around 4,000 still without power as of the 30th. Many houses sustained roof damage, especially in Maize and Northwest Wichita.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A building caught fire. The extent of damage is unknown at this time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning injured four people at Mather Point at the Grand Canyon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At approximately 1:00 p.m. on Monday, July 15 a lightning strike near Mather Point resulted in several visitors reporting injuries to the Grand Canyon Visitors Center. The group of visitors was standing near the Rim when the lightning strike occurred. Four individuals were transported to the South Rim Clinic for evaluation of non-life-threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong ridge of high pressure centered over Utah and eastern Nevada brought hot temperatures to western Nevada on the 28th. The heat set the stage for strong to severe thunderstorms with gusty winds over 50 mph and large hail in the Reno area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Five lightning strikes associated with a severe thunderstorm hit the Washoe County Emergency Operations Center's communications tower. The strikes disabled the primary communications repeater although backups were not disabled.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at 6659 Eagle Ridge RD in Bettendorf, IA around 530 am CDT April 10 causing a fire. Damage was estimated to be about 25,000 dollars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home at 6659 Eagle Ridge RD in Bettendorf, IA around 530 am CDT April 10 causing a fire.  Damage was estimated to be about 25,000 dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable environment coupled with weak forcing along a passing upper-level front led to scattered thunderstorms across the Idaho Panhandle during the morning and early afternoon hours on June 29th.  In the town of Sagle, two men were injured by a lightning strike while they were laying cable in a trench during the storm.  Reports state that lightning hit the electrical line and went through the buried cable.  One victim had entrance and exit woulds and electrical burns to the lower half of his body.  The second victim had no entrance or exit wounds and appeared to have been hit by the strike's ground current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The exact time of the lightning strike was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system passing by to the northwest of Arkansas brought two rounds of winter weather from the 20th into the 21st. During the morning of the 20th, light snow, occasionally mixed with sleet, broke out in western Arkansas. Most snowfall was in the 1 to 2 inch range, with spotty totals around 3 inches. Some areas of light snow, sleet, and freezing rain continued into the evening in the northern part of Arkansas, with light rain in the south. Precipitation began to pick up considerably toward dawn on the 21st and continued throughout much of the day. Freezing rain was the predominant precipitation type in the north, while a cold rain fell in the south. Thunderstorms occurred in all sections of the state. In the northern part of Arkansas, an ice storm occurred, with ice accruals generally in the 1/4 to 1/2 inch range. However, there were some totals around 3/4 inch, especially in Stone, Izard, Sharp, and Independence counties. Altogether, about 10,000 power outages were reported. Meanwhile, isolated severe storms with large hail occurred in the south.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church in Arkadelphia, destroying the steeple and damaging the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An advancing cold front and upper trough brought heavy rain, thunderstorms, and/or flash flooding  to portions of Kauai, Oahu, and Molokai.  The total cost of damages was not available.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike brought down a power line in Kailua in windward Oahu.  The line came to rest on parked vehicles, where a man with a fire extinguisher tried to put out the smoldering debris.  He touched one of the vehicles and was severely shocked by the arcing line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with a cold front moving through the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused damage at the Greenville storm water pumping plant.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from an evening thunderstorm produced an attic fire in a residentail home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused an attic fire at a residential home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms brought large hail and damaging winds to parts of northeast Minnesota on August 26th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pine County Sheriff reported that a male was struck by lightning about 4 miles east-southeast of Sturgeon Lake, MN on Alder Loop in a development called Hogan's Acres.  The individual passed away from his injuries after being taken by ambulance to Mercy Hospital in Moose Lake, MN.  The investigation showed that the 53 year old male victim was standing in a large puddle of water near a tree when the tree and victim were struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Easterly wind flow across the peninsula produces another active afternoon of severe weather across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit the North Greenwood Recreation and Aquatic Center on north Martin Luther King Jr. Road causing a fire in the facility.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped trigger a series of thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania on the 12th.  A line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through the area during the late afternoon and early evening on the 12th caused the majority of the wind and lightning damage. About 3,000 Pennsylvania Power and Light customers lost power in the Lehigh Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a small barn fire in Northampton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall causing numerous flood impacts in Pasco and Hernando Counties. Also, a sub-severe thunderstorm produced a lightning strike causing a brief fire at a local elementary school.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit Mintz Elementary School which caused a brief fire which was quickly put out. No estimate on damage costs to the school was available.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lingering monsoon moisture continued to fuel thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. A few storms produced flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged two major distribution circuits, knocking out power to about 2000 people.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A house south of Zumbro Falls (Wabasha County) was destroyed by a fire likely started from a lightning strike. The fire was reported as numerous thunderstorms with frequent lightning were moving across southeast Minnesota during the evening of October 4th. Two fire departments were on the scene for five hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house south of Zumbro Falls was destroyed by a fire apparently started from a lightning strike. Nobody was home at the time of the fire and two fire departments were on the scene for five hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary led to multiple rounds of thunderstorms which trained over the same areas and produced intense rainfall rates and rainfall totals. Most areas received between one and five inches of rainfall with some localized areas receiving up to 20 inches of rainfall in several days. This caused devastating floods and flash floods with some rivers reaching all time record levels. There were several hundred rescues performed and evacuations of over 500 individuals from their homes across the Missouri Ozarks.  Joint agencies from the federal, state, and local assessed over 18 million dollars in damages to property and infrastructure. Over 380 homes and over 130 businesses were damaged due to the floods.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree struck by lightning fell on power lines at 805 Oaklane Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the evening of October 4th ahead of an approaching warm front. These storms produced locally heavy rains that caused flash flooding to occur across portions of Floyd and Winneshiek Counties. A vehicle became stranded in flood waters near Floyd (Floyd County) with the occupants having to be rescued by emergency personnel. Dime to quarter sized hail also fell near Marble Rock and Charles City (Floyd County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree and power lines were knocked down from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed as a strong shortwave and cold front moved into the region. These storms produced lots of hail up to golf ball sized. One person was struck by lightning in Montague County but survived without significant injuries. Some flash flooding also occurred in Tarrant County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 31-year old male was struck by lightning at the Rednecks with Paychecks event. The lightning struck the tree he was taking cover under and entered his body through his boot. He survived without serious injury.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed as a strong shortwave and cold front moved into the region. These storms produced lots of hail up to golf ball sized. One person was struck by lightning in Montague County but survived without significant injuries. Some flash flooding also occurred in Tarrant County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged an underground cable near Lake Belton that caused the Gatesville Regional Water Intake Structure to lose power. As a result, all Gatesville ISD campuses and less than 100 homes were without water through Monday.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in Colleyville and in Saginaw in Tarrant County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in the 4900 block of Waterford Drive in Colleyville. Flames were coming from the roof when firefighters arrived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot temperatures, combined with dewpoints near 70 degrees, led to the development of scattered strong thunderstorms across southern Kentucky during the afternoon and early evening hours of September 11th. Some of these storms produced up to 2 inches of rain across Simpson County.  A lightning strike injured 5 people.  A couple of storms became severe, producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported 5 injuries from a lightning strike that ended the afternoon racing card at the Kentucky Downs racetrack. Lightning hit a tin pole and traveled down to the ground, shocking 5 people sheltering within a tent. One was transported to a hospital.  The racing board was shorted out with racing cancelled for the rest of the afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved into northwest Indiana during the late morning and early afternoon of September 19th producing deadly lightning.   Later in the afternoon, a supercell developed producing large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man working on a billboard in the 4700 Block of 27th Avenue was struck by lightning and later died from his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms formed due to daily heating over eastern Harrris County. One of these storms produced a lightning strike that caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas tanker truck causing it to fall over in the road, spilling gas. A Shelter in Place order was issued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved into northwest Indiana during the late morning and early afternoon of September 19th producing deadly lightning.   Later in the afternoon, a supercell developed producing large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house at 1180 Jefferson Court was struck by lightning starting a fire which engulfed about 50 percent of the home.  An adult and a 9-month-old child were home at the time of the fire.  The adult was killed and the baby was in critical condition as it was transported to the hospital.  An investigator said that there were no signs that the adult had been struck by lightning and that they died due to smoke inhalation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Prolonged flow from the Gulf of Mexico produced a deep moist layer at the surface with precipitable water values two standard deviations above the mean on area soundings. An upper level trough of low pressure moved out of northern New Mexico and across the Texas Panhandle providing lift to produce showers and thunderstorms. A surface trough was the focus of training storms which produced heavy rainfall that led to major flooding across the Onion Creek and Blanco/San Marcos River watersheds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced a lightning strike that caused a structural fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a lee side trof and an approaching cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms during the day on the 2nd in Eastern Pennsylvania.  While flash flooding caused the majority of the impacts, lightning strikes and severe winds also caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes damaged three homes in Forks Township. The damage was from the lightning strikes themselves as there were no ensuing fires reported.  No serious injuries were also reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a lee side trof and an approaching cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms during the day on the 2nd in Eastern Pennsylvania.  While flash flooding caused the majority of the impacts, lightning strikes and severe winds also caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and caused a fire in the Frankford section of Philadelphia. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A disturbance moved east to initiate thunderstorms that intensified to produce hail up to baseball size. As storms became elevated further northeast to produce strong winds and localized wind damage. The hail broke out windows of homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a wildfire near 1.5 miles east of Dickens that burned pasture land.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several thunderstorms developed within a warm and moist environment as uplift ahead of an approaching shortwave merged with an inland moving seabreeze. Thunderstorms displayed a high lightning count over the region with several structures being stuck and causing a few fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Charleston County 911 call center reported lightning causing a house fire on Cabrill Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several thunderstorms developed within a warm and moist environment as uplift ahead of an approaching shortwave merged with an inland moving seabreeze. Thunderstorms displayed a high lightning count over the region with several structures being stuck and causing a few fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement reported a large oak tree down due to a lightning strike along Jasper Station Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several thunderstorms developed within a warm and moist environment as uplift ahead of an approaching shortwave merged with an inland moving seabreeze. Thunderstorms displayed a high lightning count over the region with several structures being stuck and causing a few fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Charleston County 911 call center reported a tree was hit by lightning and fell on a car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the late morning and afternoon hours on August 7. One storm in Lawrence County produced two reports of minor flooding and lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large tree on Brink Street which caused it to fall across the road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced dangerous cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man and his wife were walking on the beach near South Shore Drive in Surf City when they were struck by lightning.  It appears the man was struck directly, and the woman received only a minor shock.  The man was knocked unconscious, but was revived about six minutes later and taken to the hospital for severe burns.  Days later, he is alive but still recovering from his injuries.  The woman had minor burns and was not hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large thunderstorm complex with embedded severe thunderstorms moved east across southern Wisconsin during the morning hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A dump truck hauling granite was struck by lightning in the southbound lane of highway 41 north of Sherman Road in the Town of Polk. Some of the granite was propelled from the truck. In addition, a 18 inch deep and 3 foot long hole was found in the roadway from the lightning strike. Two vehicles behind the truck suffered wheel and tire damage due to the asphalt debris lying on the highway. No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced dangerous cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a home in Myrtle Grove.  A small fire caused minor roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moving across the area produced lightning that resulted in a minor lightning strike injury in Cullman county, Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms resulted in a lightning strike that caused a minor injury to person on Weaver road, in Albertville, Alabama.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Easterly flow allowed for strong thunderstorms to form late in the evening on the 16th. During the early morning hours on the 17th, these storms moved closer to the coast again producing tree damage and one thunderstorm sparked a house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire to a two-story house in the East Lake Neighborhood. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike downed a couple of power lines in Tallahassee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The public reported a couple of power lines down due to a lightning strike near 1111 High Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southwest flow led to scattered thunderstorms moving through much of West Central and Southwest Florida.  A lightning strike from one of these storms sparked a house fire in Hillsborough county causing minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported an attic fire started by lightning on Lido Drive in Brandon.  Fire crews were able to put the fire out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds along coastal locations. A 40 year old woman and a house sere struck by lightning in Pinellas County in separate incidents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40 year old female was injured by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds along coastal locations. A 40 year old woman and a house sere struck by lightning in Pinellas County in separate incidents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: State emergency management relayed a report of a house struck by lightning with minor damage.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a motorcycle driver near Chehalis, and a home in Puyallup.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning near Shelton.  Another bolt struck a tree that then spread into a nearby apartment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a motorcycle driver near Chehalis, and a home in Puyallup.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and damaged several electrical items inside.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a motorcycle driver near Chehalis, and a home in Puyallup.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 59 year old motorcycle driver was injured when he was struck by lightning while driving on Interstate-5.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front helped trigger a series of thunderstorms across Eastern Pennsylvania on the 12th.  A line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through the area during the late afternoon and early evening on the 12th caused the majority of the wind and lightning damage. About 3,000 Pennsylvania Power and Light customers lost power in the Lehigh Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged a tree in a housing development in Fork Township.

A line of strong to severe thunderstorms that moved through the area during the late afternoon and early evening on the 12th caused the majority of the wind and lightning damage. About 3,000 Pennsylvania Power and Light customers lost power in the Lehigh Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Bern Township and ignited a fire. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flooding across the Navajo Nation. Several communities were impacted by the flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fifteen sheep were killed by lightning.  Time and location are estimates.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Near record warmth and humidity came to an abrupt end as a strong cold front crossed the region. The thunderstorms that preceded and accompanied the front produced damaging winds that downed trees and power lines across the region. Scattered power outages were reported. Hail up to 0.88 inch was also reported. In some areas, downed trees blocked roadways. In Fredonia, lightning sparked a barn fire leaving the structure severely damaged.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a barn on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Pre-frontal trough moved across north central and northeast Alabama early in the morning on September 2 with scattered wind damage and isolated flash flooding reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was suspected to have caused a house fire on Gables Brook Drive. Severe fire damage occurred to the home along with the roof collapsing as per the broadcast media photo and news report. No injuries occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours toward the edge of the Caprock before pushing into the Rolling Plains and far southeastern Texas Panhandle. This activity was in association with a surface trough, a cold front moving out of the Panhandle, and a shortwave trough pushing across the South Plains. Strong winds and large hail accompanied these storms along with a lightning induced fire which produced damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement officials reported a wildfire ignited by a nearby cloud to ground lightning strike west of Paducah. The fire was quickly contained by local fire department personnel and no injuries or significant damage occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms, with embedded severe thunderstorms, formed along a cold front as it pushed through the Northeast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported a building struck by lightning on West Church Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms with embedded severe thunderstorms formed across the southern coast of Long Island ahead of an approaching cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused the Hampton Bays Police Department to lose their communications system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a sea breeze boundary, rich gulf moisture, and daytime heating allowed a few severe storms to develop during the afternoon and evening of the 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Little Sawmill Road. There was no serious damage to the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another surge of monsoon moisture fueled widespread thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Many storms produced flash flooding, and isolated severe weather also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and set fire to a house in the Southern Highlands neighborhood.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low was located over southern Kentucky on the morning of the 19th, with a shortwave trough extending into northern Georgia. Tropical moisture prevailed over Georgia as well.  Widespread showers with embedded thunderstorms developed across a portion of north Georgia early in the morning and moved slowly south. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 7 inches occurred in less than 6 hours prior to 700 AM EST in an area from Dawsonville to Gainesville to Lawrenceville to Roswell. Significant flash flooding occurred with major damage to roads and bridges near Flowery Branch. Another 3 to 7 inches of rain occurred in 6 hours after 700 AM EST in a portion of northwest Georgia from Trenton to LaFayette to Calhoun and Cartersville to Rome and Summerville. Both heavy rain events caused widespread flash flooding and minor river flooding. As the instability increased during the day, the thunderstorms became more intense. Many of the thunderstorms were able to reach severe levels during the afternoon hours, causing primarily wind damage, with only isolated reports of large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pickens County Emergency Manager reported that a house was partially burned down due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the evening of October 4th ahead of warm front that was lifting north out of Iowa. These storms produced locally heavy rains that caused flash flooding to occur across portions of Mower, Fillmore, Winona and Houston Counties. Mud slides closed roads between Pickwick and the city of Winona (Winona County) and washed out a portion of a county road northwest of Lanesboro (Fillmore County). Almost 6 inches of rain fell in about a six hour period in Preston (Fillmore County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole causing a line to fall onto 3 buildings. All three buildings then caught on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A ridge of high pressure was located across the Tennessee Valley during the afternoon hours of September 11th.  Weak perturbations aloft were moving from east to west under the ridge and provided the lift needed for widely scattered thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon hours.  Storms produced strong wind gusts across Northeast Texas.  Some of the storms also produced small hail in Gregg County, Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a rotting tree which caused the tree to fall on a home in Longview, Texas on Oakdale Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northwest flow with upper disturbances aloft dominated the area for this episode. A west to east frontal system lay well to the north, across northern Ohio early Wednesday morning.  The front dropped slowly south during the afternoon. ||The afternoon heating combined with the unstable environment to trigger thunderstorms. |Several convective complexes developed in the afternoon and early evening.  One batch|of storms formed over southeast Ohio.  One individual cell within the southern Ohio complex pulsed to a stronger level as it crossed the Ohio River into northeast Kentucky. The storm became severe near the town of Ashland.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire at a residence on Skyline Drive in Ashland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours due to a stalled frontal boundary overhead. These thunderstorms produces sporadic wind damage around the area and isolated flash flooding near the Lee, Powell and Wolfe County lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree on Little Pittsburg Road, knocking it over onto a power pole and causing the power to go out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed rapidly during the early afternoon of July 25th across portions of southeast Minnesota. These storms produced large hail from the eastern sections of Fillmore County across Houston County before moving into Wisconsin. The largest hail reported was half dollar sized near Lanesboro (Fillmore County). A second round of storms developed in the middle of the afternoon that had winds strong enough to blow down a section of corn near Granger (Fillmore County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ruptured a gas line and started a house fire on the southwest side of Rochester. The damage was limited to the gas line, electrical circuits and charring of the first floor joists.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Nine farm workers working the fields at Grant Family Farms in Wellington were injured by a lightning strike; all were transported to local hospitals.  Two were critically injured. Those two workers were semi-conscious, could not walk, and had muscle weakness and tingling in their hands and feet.  Four other workers had serious injuries and three others had minor injuries.  In addition, a 65-year-old woman was struck by lightning in Rocky Mountain National Park.  She was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.  Heavy rain also produced flash flooding in the Fern Lake and High Park burn area of Larimer County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning injured nine migrant workers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire in Wilmington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on 111 Pitch Pine Court, starting a fire. All indications are that significant damage was done before fire crew could put out the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple of thunderstorms developed on the sea breeze front in central New Jersey during the afternoon of the 9th. One person was struck and injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 48-year-old man was hospitalized after being struck by lightning on the Ocean Beach area of Island Beach State Park.  The man was fishing at the time and it was suspected that the lightning might have initially struck his fishing pole. The man complained about numbness in his legs and was taken to Jersey Shore University Medical Center in Neptune.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lee side trof helped trigger clusters of showers and thunderstorms during the second half of the morning and afternoon. While the greatest impact was flash flooding in the Raritan Basin of New Jersey, lightning and wind damage also occurred.  About 6,000 homes and businesses lost power in the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Springtown Road in Long Valley (Washington Township). No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep moisture allowed for sea breeze thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon.  Some of these storms produced heavy rain and damaging lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Florida State Watch Office reported a house was damaged by lightning in Largo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced lots of lightning which caused house fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moisture from the south and instability from the heatwave brought thunderstorms up along the Sierra Nevada slopes and northern mountains, Monday through Thursday afternoons. Some lower elevations saw showers on Wednesday as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in the afternoon along the Sierra Nevada crest and spread eastward. Witnesses reported a 66-year old female died in a campground after a lightning strike hit the area. No enter/exit woulds reported to confirm a direct hit.  However, evidence would suggest cardiac arrest due to a lightning strike was likely the cause of death.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak easterly winds and deep moisture allowed for sea breeze thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon. Some of these storms produced damaging lightning strikes and wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Florida State Watch Office relayed a report of a house on Alcazar Way in South St. Petersburg that was struck by lightning, causing a fire. Broadcast media reported that the fire only damage one bedroom. Time was estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed along an old outflow boundary and moved into the northern Big Country from the north. These storms resulted in a few damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a tank battery fire near Elbert.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of severe storms developed in an unstable air mass ahead of an advancing cold front. The storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts, at times in excess of 70 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a fire which destroyed a duplex on Wausau's east side. No one was injured in the blaze.  The time of this event was estimated based on news reports and radar data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Flossie, downgraded to tropical depression status as it neared Maui at 1700 HST on the 29th, affected the state from July 28th through the 30th, though high surf continued through the 31st on the Big Island of Hawaii.  The system brought surf of 8 to 15 feet along east-facing shores of most islands, thunderstorms, heavy rain and a flash flood, and wind.  One man was injured by lightning on Maui, and power outages occurred on the Big Island, Maui, and Molokai.  The cost of damages was not available.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning created a five-inch diameter hole in the roof of a home in Kahului.

The largest hail reported was 1.75 inches and the highest estimated wind speed was about 75 MPH.  We had a fatality due to lightning.  A spotter reported over 2 inches of rainfall in just an hour in Jefferson County at the Crooked River Ranch. Some photos were submitted to the office of the standing water and some of the washed out dirt roads in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong push of monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin for several days, peaking on the 25th. Many storms produced flash flooding, and isolated severe weather also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked out power to 186 customers in Bullhead City.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck 6 homes in Keller. Two of the homes caught on fire, and one home on Bourland Rd suffered major roof damage. No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of showers and thunderstorms produced both wind damage and flash flooding across southern new Jersey. The wind damage included an EF0 tornado in Manahawkin (Stafford Township in Ocean County). An isolated severe thunderstorm then occurred during the evening of the 13th in Morris County.  Cloud-to-ground lightning strikes peaked at 6,000 per hour as this complex moved through New Jersey. The thunderstorms caused about 14,500 homes and businesses to lose power on the 13th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike struck the 911 center in Mannington Township and damaged some equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A well defined and progressive nearly cutoff low was positioned over east central Indiana during the afternoon of August 21st.  South and east of this feature, a seasonally strong cyclonic 300mb jet was present, placing central and eastern Kentucky within an area of diffluence aloft.  Strong instability up to 2000 joules developed by mid-afternoon along and east of Interstate 65.  Scattered thunderstorms developed by late morning and strengthen during the afternoon hours.  Training storms produced, within a 2 hour period, a strip of 4 to as much as 5 inches of rain across northern Lincoln and Garrard Counties.  Within this line of storms, lightning struck a barn, killing two people and injuring three others. This has become Kentucky's worst lightning related incident in several years.  Later, a strong storm that briefly displayed supercell characteristics developed over Shelby County.  This storm produced golfball-sized hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tobacco barn near Buckeye, killing two men and injuring 3 others. The men were hanging tobacco at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unstable northwest flow aloft persisted across the region thanks to an equally persistent strong subtropical ridge across the central U.S.  A strengthening upper level storm system was diving southeast from the Great Lakes.  The air mass across the region was unseasonably warm for late August, and as a result was quite unstable.  These factors combined to produce  a few|severe thunderstorms.  The initial thunderstorms developed across far southwest Virginia and southeast West Virginia during the early to mid-afternoon as a result of outflow boundaries from overnight thunderstorms that moved through Kentucky, Tennessee and western West Virginia.  The thunderstorms propagated and developed eastward through the evening, impacting much of the Blacksburg, VA County Warning Area (CWA).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pittsylvania County 911 Center reported that lightning struck and took out a power line and transformer near the 911 Center causing a power disruption at the county facility.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A sea breeze collision over the Florida Gulf Coast allowed for scattered afternoon thunderstorms along the west half of the Florida Peninsula.  Some of these storms produced large hail and damaging lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The National Weather Service Forecast Office in Ruskin, FL was struck by lightning causing widespread damage to electronics across the office.  Several computer motherboards, monitors, security systems, a HAM radio, and internet routers were all damaged.  Time was estimated from the point when several computer systems failed.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Nearly 10,000 customers went without power, including residents in Upper Olinda, from Paia to Kuau, from Huelo to Hana, and along the East Maui coast.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching upper air disturbance coupled with a weak surface trof and hot and humid weather developed a line of strong to isolated severe thunderstorms in southeast Pennsylvania during the early evening of the 7th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and damaged a home in Valley Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved over southern New England bringing showers and thunderstorms to the region.  Precipitable water values over two inches indicated a very moist atmosphere; in addition, weak winds at the mid levels resulted in very slow moving storms.  Both of these things led to torrential rainfall and flash flooding.  Convergence at the surface and a significantly unstable environment resulted in a shower producing a waterspout over the Quabbin Reservoir in New Salem, Massachusetts.  A Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) employee at the reservoir was able to snap several photos of the waterspout and reported that it never moved onto land.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the bell tower at Bethany Congregational Church in Quincy, damaging one of the pinnacles and sending stone debris to the ground and through the ceiling of the church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low level moisture seeped northward into western portions of southern Arizona, leading to scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the house of a trained spotter in Vail, resulting in electrical damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Upper level high pressure was centered over eastern Colorado, allowing adequate moisture to seep north into southern Arizona. Thunderstorms were widespread, but only a couple produced large hail and heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of an apartment building near 29th Street and Craycroft Road. The lightning penetrated the roof's asphalt shingles and caused damage to the cinder block wall below the roof's eave. A nearby palm tree was also ignited by the strike. One resident was knocked over even though he was in a different room, but no one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across Iowa during the predawn and morning hours of the 3rd.  Lightning from one storm stuck the main lodge of the Honey Creek Resort at Rathbun Lake.  There was structural and electrical damage reported from the lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the main lodge of the Honey Creek Resort at Rathbun Lake causing structural and electrical damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm struck a house in Iron County in northwest Wisconsin early in the morning on August 27th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was hit by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The upper high was centered over the Great Basin and continued north to south flow aloft over New Mexico. Storms developed during the mid afternoon hours and tracked southward throughout the day into the evening. Slow storm motions led to flooding across the Whitewater baldy burn scar in southwestern New Mexico.||An Albuquerque couple was struck by lightning while watching Fourth of July fireworks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On July 4th, during a torrential storm, Engine 12 and Rescue 12 of the Albuquerque Fire Dept. were near the area of Eubank and Copper when they heard a very loud lightning strike. Approximately 60-90 seconds later, Engine 12 was dispatched to a residence where a tree had been struck.  Two individuals were injured including a pregnant woman who was two weeks away from her due date.  The 38- week pregnant female and her boyfriend were assessed, treated and transported to a local hospital. The woman underwent an emergency C-section. Days later, mom and dad along with their new baby girl were released from the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Daytime heating helped to touch off scattered showers and thunderstorms in Arkansas on the afternoons of the 11th and 12th. A few storms became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pick-up truck traveling on Interstate 30. No one was injured but the vehicle was disabled.

The wind damage included an EF0 tornado in Manahawkin (Stafford Township in Ocean County). An isolated severe thunderstorm then occurred during the evening of the 13th in Morris County.  Cloud-to-ground lightning strikes peaked at 6,000 per hour as this complex moved through New Jersey. The thunderstorms caused about 14,500 homes and businesses to lose power on the 13th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at the Borough Hall in Manasquan caused damage and disrupted the communication systems in the borough. They were transferred to other facilities.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms occurred across the San Antonio metro area during the late afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 8 year old boy was struck by lightning on the west side of San Antonio in the evening of Thursday September 5th. He, along with another boy, was in a backyard when the lightning strike occurred. The 8 year old was taken to the hospital in critical condition and died September 7th around noon. The other boy survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level trough combined with a warm, unstable air mass and led to the development of a series of thunderstorms across northeast Wisconsin.  Trees were knocked down by strong thunderstorm winds in several locations.  Rainfall amounts ranged from 1 to 4 inches over parts of northern Wisconsin which caused localized flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an electrical regulator on a house, causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist air mass south of a stalled frontal boundary across the northern Gulf of Mexico provided instability for afternoon thunderstorms along the Gulf Coast of Florida. Many of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.  Also, one storm caused lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Police Department building in Largo was struck by lightning, causing a minor fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through northern Indiana during the early morning hours of July 20th. Scattered thunderstorms developed along the front, but remained below severe limits. A report of a residence in Laotto being struck by lightning was received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local media and emergency management officials reported a home in Laotta was struck by lightning around 430 am EDT. A resident of the home was awakened by the noise associated with the lightning strike. Five to ten minutes later smoke and fire was reported. The lightning struck an underground gas line and sparked a fire in the home in the heating ducts. This then spread to the kitchen. Firefighters were able to get the fire quickly under control. Damage was estimated at $20,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms that struck Reno and Kingman Counties on the evening of the 25th produced hail as large as golf balls, gusts around 60 mph and heavy rains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wheat stubble caught on fire. The field fire occurred on Whiteside Road 1/2 mile east of Boundary Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable environment coupled with weak forcing along a passing upper-level front led to scattered strong thunderstorms along the East Slopes of the Washington Cascades during the early afternoon hours of June 29th.  Although storm motion was on the order of 20 to 30 miles per hour, cell training across the higher terrain of southeastern Chelan County led to rainfall amounts ranging from one to one and a half inches over the duration of an hour.  The runoff from these storms flowed down Canyons One and Canyon Two into the city of Wenatchee and sewer systems became overwhelmed resulting in flash flooding across southwestern portions of the city.  These storms also fell over portions of the 2012 Peavine burn scar resulting in two known debris flows; one that carried debris from Tronsen Ridge and washed out a section of Upper Tronsen Road and a second that deposited hundreds of trees onto USFS Trails in Devil's Gulch.  Further east closer to the Idaho border, elevated thunderstorms throughout the morning and early afternoon led to numerous lightning strikes and damage to transformers in Spokane.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer box in an alley behind a residential house, traveled through the lines and blew out a second transformer.  Several homes loss power that afternoon until utility companies were able to replace the transformers.  The transformers were located between Broadway and Boone Streets in west Spokane.  The exact time of the lightning strike was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An intense late night thunderstorm produced locally heavy rainfall and a lot of lightning in the Grand Valley, including a lightning bolt that caused significant damage to a building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The We Kare-A-Lot childcare facility was struck by lightning in the wee hours, igniting a fire in the building which resulted in extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure moving along a stationary front triggered several severe thunderstorms over southeast Louisiana during the evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged one home in the Loranger area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough moved into southern New England, providing lift for showers and thunderstorms to develop in a hot and humid atmosphere.  In addition, CAPE up to 2000 J/kg and 30-40 kts of shear provided enough instability and shear for thunderstorms to become severe.  Because of warm air aloft, these thunderstorms mostly produced strong to damaging winds and not large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a detached garage on Bonnie Avenue, igniting a fire.  There were no vehicles in the garage but there was damage to other household possessions and belongings.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in Colleyville and in Saginaw in Tarrant County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in the 6000 block of Sterling Drive in Colleyville. Flames were coming from the garage when firefighters arrived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak easterly winds and deep moisture allowed for sea breeze thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon. Some of these storms produced damaging lightning strikes and wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Florida State Watch Office relayed a report that an apartment building on Belcher Road in Clearwater was struck by lightning, causing a fire. Time was estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough of low pressure extending across South Florida from Tropical Depression Dorian produced scattered afternoon thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning at the Miami Motorcross Park northwest of Hialeah.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed over central Kansas during the late afternoon of the 23rd. These storms moved southeast during the evening and into eastern Oklahoma during the late evening and overnight hours. High amounts of instability and considerable deep layer shear over eastern Oklahoma resulted in the development of a highly organized line of storms. Widespread damaging wind, a tornado, and some large hail resulted across eastern Oklahoma as the line of thunderstorms moved through the region. At least 300,000 people were reportedly without power due to the storms in the area surrounding Tulsa. Some of these outages lasted for nearly a week. In addition, lightning from these storms resulted in a number of structural fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a hotel, resulting in a fire that damaged the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced 2 to 5 inches of rain in a couple of hours over portions of Columbia County resulting in flash flooding of several streams with water getting into homes and closing roads.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: EM reported lightning struck a home and did moderate damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger strong thunderstorms across the Maryland Eastern Shore during the afternoon and evening of the 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck and injured by lightning where he was standing on Doctor Jack Road in Conowingo. He was taken to Christiana Hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon and moved northeast across north Alabama.  While most of the storms produced winds associated with a gust front of 30 to 40 mph that knocked down small tree limbs, a couple of severe storms knocked down multiple trees resulting in a few power outages.  One storm produced up to quarter inch hail in Madison.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer off of state highway 36 on Elrod Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level trough moved through north Alabama during the morning, producing heavy rainfall and a few reports of wind damage and flash flooding in northwest Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and caught it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed ahead of an advancing cold front on the afternoon and evening of the 10th. A few tornadoes occurred, and there were also reports of large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in the attic of a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable atmosphere led to scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the interior of South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in West Boca was reported to be struck by lightning that damaged several windows, but nobody was injured. The strike occurred about 11 AM EDT in the 9600 block of Lancaster Place. The home's residents requested rescue crews check out the home. Crews found none of the electronics functioned and that several window frames had been separated from the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough of low pressure moved across South Florida producing scattered to numerous afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a roof fire at a home in the 6000 block of Hudson Bay Lane in Lake Worth. Rescue crews arrived at the house and discovered a one-by-two foot hole in the roof of the home and quickly extinguished the fire. There were three people, four cats and one dog inside the home but there were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough of low pressure moved across South Florida producing scattered to numerous afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a roof fire to a home in Loxahatchee. Six people were in the house at the time, and Red Cross assistance was requested. Time based on archived lightning data courtesy of Earth Networks.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused damage to homes in Flagler Beach and near Palm Coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two homes in the Plantation Bay subdivision. The cost of electrical damage was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data. The estimated is likely an underestimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused damage to homes in Flagler Beach and near Palm Coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Grand Haven subdivision which caused damage to the roof and soffits. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data. This estimate is likely an underestimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable atmosphere led to scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the interior of South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 57 year old male died and his 56 year old friend was injured when their boat was struck by lightning on Lake Okeechobee. The two men were boating and decided to dock at the Clewiston boat ramps as a thunderstorm approached. As they were making their way back to Clewiston, lightning struck their boat and both men were knocked unconscious. Some time later, the 56 year old male awoke and called 911 after realizing what happened. Hendry County EMS arrived on the scene and transported the unconscious male to Hendry County Regional Medical Center where he was pronounced dead. The other male was later taken to Palms West Hospital to be treated for his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical wave moved across Cuba enhancing scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms over South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning fatally struck a 35 year old male construction worker who was working on the exterior of a single family home on scaffolding.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon on sea breeze and outflow boundaries and continued through the early evening.  A lightning strike from one of these storms damaged a boat in Central Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The fire department responded to a report of a lightning strike to a boat sitting on a trailer on Rome Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southwest flow fed sea breeze storms moving into the Tampa Bay area late in the afternoon.  One of these storms produced a waterspout that came onshore as a tornado.  Additionally, a couple lightning strikes caused fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pinellas County 911 call center reported minor damage to a shed caused by a lightning strike on Belcher Road in Largo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southwest flow fed sea breeze storms moving into the Tampa Bay area late in the afternoon.  One of these storms produced a waterspout that came onshore as a tornado.  Additionally, a couple lightning strikes caused fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pinellas County 911 call center reported a small fire in a house on Pine Place in Clearwater caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southwest flow led to early afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms over the Nature Coast.  A lightning strike from one of the storms hit a house and sparked a house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported Fire Rescue crews reported to the scene of a house fire in Floral City, FL, believed to be caused by a lightning strike.  No one was home at the time and no injuries were reported.  Damage was estimated to be around $95,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm southerly flow allowed for temperatures to reach well into the 80s to near 90 on Wednesday, July 2nd. In addition, it was rather humid with dewpoints nearing 70 degrees. With the warm and humid conditions in place, the atmosphere became quite unstable during the afternoon and evening hours. ||Well ahead of a cold front, a surface trough was in place across upstate New York and western New England. This caused thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon hours. Many of these storms became severe to the east of southern Vermont across Upstate New York. ||Although no storms were severe across southern Vermont, the thunderstorms did produce a significant amount of cloud to ground lightning. Several fire fighters in Guilford were struck by lightning, but no serious injuries were reported.||The thunderstorms ended by the late evening hours, as nocturnal influences helped wane the development of additional thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Seven fire fighters responding to a structure fire were struck by lightning during a thunderstorm in Guilford.  Although all seven were sent to a hospital with minor injuries, no serious injuries were reported.

Several highway employees were struck by lightning in Rotterdam during a thunderstorm, but luckily escaped serious injury.  ||Although most of the storm ended by the late afternoon hours, a few additional severe storms during during the evening across the western Adirondacks and western Mohawk Valley. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three Rotterdam Highway Department employees were struck by lightning on Curry Road in Rotterdam.  The employees were outdoors loading empty boxes onto a truck during the thunderstorm when they were struck and knocked over.  All three only received minor injuries and escape serious injury.  The employees were sent to a local hospital, but were shortly released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and humid air mass was in place over the region on Thursday, July 3rd.  As a strong cold front approached from the west, a broken line of thunderstorms developed over central New York and moved eastward during the afternoon hours.  Aided by powerful winds aloft, the storms moved from west to east over the region between the late afternoon and early evening hours.  Many of the storms produced strong winds, causing damage to trees and power lines over much of the region.  The most concentrated damage occurred from one particularly severe thunderstorm, which caused intense damage between West Winfield in Herkimer County towards Minden in Montgomery County.  A National Weather Service Storm Survey determined a series of microbursts produced wind damage up to 100 MPH in these areas.  A few of the storms also produced large hail as well.||As the cold front moved through the area by later in the evening, the storms moved east of the region and the threat for severe weather ended.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was reported to have struck a residential propane tank on Court Lane in Claverack.
