EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass was in place on Wednesday, July 23rd, allowing the atmosphere to become quite unstable.  As a cold front approached from the west, clusters of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and early evening hours.  Some of these thunderstorms became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail.  Thunderstorms moved east and weakened by the late evening hours, as the cold front crossed the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large 100 foot pine tree was struck by lightning at the Saratoga Race Course in Saratoga Springs.  Pieces of the downed tree destroyed about a dozen picnic tables and the Dogs and Brews tent.  Some of the debris was scattered nearly 100 feet away from the tree that was struck.  The lightning strike occurred about 20 minutes after the last race of the day had ended and most people had already left the area.  As a result, no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across upstate New York during the early afternoon on Thursday, July 31st.  Ahead of this boundary, the atmosphere was warm and unstable.  A line of showers and thunderstorms developed along the boundary and quickly moved eastward.  One area of the thunderstorms became severe across Saratoga County, producing damaging wind gusts and small hail.  ||The thunderstorms raced eastward into New England by the mid-afternoon, ending the threat for severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that fell onto wires in Salisbury.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of a slow moving cold front, a southerly flow transported plenty of moisture into the region during the day on Tuesday, June 3rd.  With a moist and unstable air mass in place, plenty of slow moving showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the approaching boundary.  Some of these thunderstorms produced very heavy rain in a short period of time.  This led to some flash flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage areas.  In addition, a few of the thunderstorms also produced strong wind gusts, which caused damage to trees and power lines.  By the late evening, the threat for thunderstorms ended, as the frontal boundary pushed through and less humid air moved into the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The local fire department reported that lightning caused a barn to catch fire on Gipp Road in Guilderland.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very moist and humid air mass was in place across the region on Wednesday, June 25th.  As a slow moving cold front approached from the west, bands of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the boundary.  As these showers and thunderstorms repeatedly passed over the same locations, the heavy rainfall led to significant runoff, which caused flash flooding in some areas.  Many roads were closed due to the flooding and some homes were affected by water as well.  In addition, a few of the storms produced wind damage to trees and some damaging lightning strikes.  ||The threat for heavy rainfall and flooding ended late on the evening of June 25th, as the storm's cold front passed through the region from west to east.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Frontal boundaries from a low pressure system tracking through northwest Ontario produced heavy rain and a few severe thunderstorms over south central Upper Michigan from the 4th into the early morning of the 5th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning in Powers but was reported to be conscious and bleeding.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dying thunderstorm complex over Arkansas on the morning of the 8th provided the push for development of thunderstorms over southeast Louisiana during the afternoon hours. Lightning from the storms triggered two house fires in the Baton Rouge area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning striking a roof triggered a fire that produced significant damage to a home on Kenmore Avenue in Baton Rouge.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning striking a roof triggered a fire that produced significant damage to a home on Destrehan Drive in Baton Rouge.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a house and car.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a house and car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture generated thunderstorms that produced numerous reports of large hail, flash flooding, and wind damage across northeast Nevada, primarily in Elko county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a structural fire. Damages are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the region, accompanied by a line of showers and thunderstorms. A lightning strike from one of these storms set fire to a shed in Dunedin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas County Emergency Management reported a fire to a shed in Dunedin, believed to be caused by a lightning strike. The call was received by 911 at 5:08 pm EDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An elongated low pressure moved into the plains on the afternoon of September 9th, 2014.  This low pressure and warm moist air pushing into northern Kansas and southern Nebraska led to the development of severe storms across portions of north and Central Kansas.  The storms produced large hail and some reports of damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Hay bales were struck by lightning and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were struck by lightning as they sat under a tree to avoid a heavy downpour.   One of the men was unconscious and had no pulse when emergency responders arrived. He was immediately taken to Denver Health was listed in critical condition.  The other victim suffered less severe injuries. He was treated at the scene and hospitalized, then released a few hours later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were injured when lightning hit the tree they were sitting under during the downpour.  One man was critically injured, while the other suffered only minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of short waves along with increasing and deepening moisture resulted in isolated severe thunderstorms each day, mainly in the afternoon and evening hours in conjunction with maximum instability due to diurnal heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local media reported that lightning sparked a house fire in Loring Heights.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front combined with an upper level disturbance to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England during the early morning hours of October 8th.  One of these storms produced a microburst in the town of Easthampton in western Massachusetts where numerous trees were downed on the west side of Mount Tom.  Scattered wind damage occurred elsewhere across southern New England.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree 30 feet away from a house on Jason's Lane.  The lightning traveled through the root system to the house, setting it on fire.  The house was deemed a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A ridge of high pressure over the region for the last few weeks was nudged east by a potent upper-level trough coming off the Eastern Pacific. The trough took on a strong negative tilt and passed through during peak heating. An east to west line of strong thunderstorms developed over Northern Oregon and tracked northward through Eastern Washington and Northern Idaho during the late afternoon and early evening. Additional storms continued to develop along the gust front which continued to pickup momentum as it passed into the region into an inverted V environment. Winds between 50 and 60 mph resulted in downed trees and power outages.  The strongest winds were observed between Latah and southern Bonner County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Trained Spotter measured thirty-two hundreths of rain in span of ten minutes under a heavy thunderstorm.  Lightning hit and exploded a nearby telephone pole.  Spotter was located two miles east of Lewiston.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pre-frontal thunderstorms developed over a moist and unstable airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire on East Crystal River Road. The cost of damage was unknown and estimated for inclusion of the event in storm data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper level trough moved out of the Southern Plains and into the Lower Mississippi Valley during the late afternoon and evening hours of October 2nd.   This upper level trough took on a negative tilt as it moved towards the Four State Region, with vigorous lift resulting in the development of severe thunderstorms in a moderately unstable environment.  Strong unidirectional deep layer shear resulted in the convection eventually taking on the shape of a squall line which raced through the region producing widespread wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck multiple oil tanks resulting in and explosion in Chapel Hill near the intersection of FM. 2607 and Smith County Road 223.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms with embedded supercells moved southward out of Kentucky through Middle Tennessee from the late evening hours on October 7 and into the early morning hours on October 8. Several reports of large hail and a few reports of wind damage were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two apartment buildings on Pennington Avenue in east Nashville were struck by lightning and damaged by fire with 40 residents displaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved into Northeast Arkansas during the early evening hours of July 1st, 2014. Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the front. Lightning from the storms struck and killed a teenager and also produced a fire that damaged a municipal airport. In addition, isolated flash flooding occurred after two storms merged together.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building at the Osceola Municipal Airport. As a result, a fire occurred which caused major damage to the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep layer troughing with WSW upper level flow advected moisture inland form the Gulf of Mexico. This moisture feed combined with daytime instability and a front sagging southward over S Ga triggered heavy rainfall potential across the local forecast area. PWAT values were 2.17 to 2.19 inches, and some cells trained across local areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a tower at the Jacksonville Regional Communications Center which caused local dispatch to loose power. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for this event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level disturbance combined with very cold air aloft to produce showers and thunderstorms across much of Southern New England. Many of these storms produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a shed on Bettencourt Road, causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: By the early morning hours of the 4th, an area of surface low pressure had moved into northeast South Dakota, with a warm front extending out to the east. Surface dew point values north of the front ranged in the lower 60s while south of the front they topped out around 70. At 850 millibars, the low level jet pushed juicy air up into southeast North Dakota and west central Minnesota, with drier air to the north. Finally, forty-five to fifty knot westerly winds at 500 millibars provided ample shear to the system. Thunderstorms over western and central North Dakota proceeded east and moved into Barnes County, North Dakota, during the first few hours of the 4th. These storms tracked nearly due east, finally exiting Wadena County, Minnesota, around sunrise. The strongest storms mainly stayed along and south of Interstate 94 in North Dakota and U. S. Highway 10 in Minnesota. These storms trained across the same areas as well, with some spots experiencing large hail or damaging winds two or three times during the event. In addition, heavy rainfall became a problem, resulting in some flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a fire that destroyed one restaurant and badly damaged a second neighboring restaurant.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 10 thousand gallon storage tank near the town of Nursery. This caused the storage tank to catch fire. The tank battery was also burned.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil storage tank near the community of Nursery. This caused a fire that burned the tank and the tank battery.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved through the Missouri Ozarks and caused strong to severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging wind gusts.  Locally heavy rainfall caused minor flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several lightning strikes damaged transformers in downtown Joplin which caused power outages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical monsoon moisture over the region resulted in some weak showers and thunderstorms to develop.  The initial lightning strike from a storm in Las Cruces resulted in 6 people being injured during football practice.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Six people, including several middle school football players were injured from the initial lightning strike from a nearby thunderstorm. No fatalities occurred with this lightning strike, but one student who was closest to the strike suffered significant injuries and was in the hospital for over a week.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved quickly into the Central and Southern Plains providing the necessary lift for scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across Northwest Texas and Western Oklahoma during the evening hours of Sunday, Oct. 12th.  At the surface, a warm front  was rapidly moving northward across East Texas and North Louisiana with low level moisture returning quickly in the wake of the northward moving warm front.  A cold front in association with the upper level trough was rapidly moving eastward through Western Oklahoma and Texas.  Overnight across Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas and Northwest Louisiana, moderate instability was in place with increasing low and mid-level shear as the upper trough approached from the west. Storms eventually erupted ahead of the cold front across Central Oklahoma and Northern Texas, maturing into a squall line as it approached the region during the predawn hours of Monday, Oct. 13th.  As the squall line traversed through the region, widespread wind damage was reported associated with straight line winds.  Several short track, intense tornadoes developed along the leading edge of the squall line as well across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas and Northern Louisiana.  The storms finally exited the region during the afternoon hours of Oct. 13th.  Post-event Storm Surveys determined that 6 tornadoes occurred with this severe weather outbreak, one of which produced 1 fatality and 4 injuries in Little River County, Arkansas.  Another tornado produced widespread damage across Ouachita Parish in Monroe, Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike set an oil well site on fire at the intersection of HG Moseley and Bill Owens Parkway southeast of Wildwood.  Residents had to be evacuated from the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface cold front passed through the region during the afternoon on Thursday, August 7th.  This front was associated with a strong upper level trough, with rather cold temperatures aloft.   As a result, some scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours and several of the storms produced hail. A few of the storms produced severe hail, especially across the Glens Falls-Saratoga Region.  One of the storms also produced damaging wind gusts as well. The threat for storms ended by the late afternoon, as the cold front pushed south and the upper level trough moved away from the area to the east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike downed a tree and wires in South Glens Falls.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms produced a measured wind gust of 64 mph at the South Haven GLERL site and to around 60 mph in Okemos near Lansing.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The media reported that South Shore middle school in Holland was struck by lightning.  There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed along a stationary boundary and produced lightning that struck a house near Varnamtown.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on 2949 Serrano Trail, causing moderate damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure moved offshore allowing the environment to become more unstable and allowing afternoon heating to initiate thunderstorms. A few of these storms became severe producing damaging winds along with lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Boyden Street in Pelham causing a basement fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Olivo Road in Keene which cut a hole in the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure moved offshore allowing the environment to become more unstable and allowing afternoon heating to initiate thunderstorms. A few of these storms became severe producing damaging winds along with lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage on Fox Run Road setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected central and northern parts of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on August 23. Several reports of wind and lightning damage were received.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep trough of low pressure dropped down the Washington Coastline then swung inland into the Inland Northwest during the afternoon of July 23rd. The wave took on a strong negative tilt and moved into a moist and very unstable air mass. The outcome was a widespread severe weather event for Eastern Washington and Northern Idaho producing large hail, flash flooding, and widespread wind damage. Falling trees led to some injuries in Eastern Washington.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structural fire on Double Eagle Road.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning on Locust Street in Swansea, which caused downed wires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Easterly flow allowed for a sea breeze collision along the western half of the Florida peninsula, producing a line of thunderstorms during the afternoon and early evening hours. One of these storms produced a damaging downburst wind gust in Lee County. A lightning strike from another storm struck a house in Pinellas County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas County Emergency Management reported a lightning strike to a house in Saint Petersburg.  Additionally, a tree was also reported to have fallen onto the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the region during the early afternoon. A lightning strike from one of these storms struck a house, causing a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A broadcast media outlet reported that a emergency responders were called to a fire at a house at 1:06PM local time. Neighbors reported hearing and seeing a lightning strike to the home before the fire broke out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers with a few embedded thunderstorms moved from the Gulf into the Tampa Bay area during the afternoon and late evening hours. One storm produced a lightning strike which hit a home in Clearwater.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The state watch office relayed a report from Pinellas County of a lightning strike to a house near Clearwater. Some very minor damage to the home was reported. Thankfully however there were no injuries or fatalities.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across southwest Alabama and caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 911 tower and caused 65 thousand dollars in damage to the tower and phone system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vehicle and injured a person leaning against it.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vehicle and injured a person leaning against it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms across interior southern New England, some of which produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a chimney of a house on Crosby Street in Northampton causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern New Hampshire ahead of a cold front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Valley Street in Manchester was struck by lightning, which ignited a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough of low pressure over the Atlantic along with a tropical wave over the western Caribbean Sea caused scattered afternoon thunderstorms across South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A landscape worker was jolted by a bolt of lightning while riding a lawn mower in Cooper City. The 27-year-old male was knocked unconscious, but regained consciousness by the time he reached the hospital a short time later. No evidence of entry or exit burns were noted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and moist air mass was pulled north from the gulf ahead of a cold front. As a weak surface low pushed across the region a strong short wave also moved across the northern gulf coast. This set up provided support for a few severe thunderstorms in Louisiana, however only one developed in Southeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home of a Southeast Texas doctor setting the roof on fire. Firefighters were able to extinguish the blaze after a neighbor reported it. No one was injured in the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the mountains during the late afternoon. A lightning strike resulted in some minor injuries in northern Oconee County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: EM reported two people sustained minor injuries after lightning struck near them at a campground off Highway 107.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large regional severe weather outbreak affected the Tennessee and lower Mississippi Valleys with a mixture of isolated supercells and multicell line segments impacting Middle Tennessee. One supercell thunderstorm moved rapidly northeast across northwest Perry, Humphreys, eastern Houston, and Montgomery Counties, bringing numerous reports of large hail, wind damage, and one EF1 tornado. Other strong to severe thunderstorms brought wind damage and flash flooding to much of the rest of Middle Tennessee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning at 125 Bethlehem Road. No significant damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on September 3. A few reports of flash flooding and wind damage were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Cookeville Herald-Citizen reported that one person was struck by lightning and injured on Claude Loftis Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across the southern Piedmont during the afternoon. Lightning from one storm caused some structural damage in southern Gaston County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: HAM Radio operator reported lightning struck and damaged a structure at Unity Church Rd and Cedar Creek Ln.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across the mountains, foothills and western Piedmont of North Carolina. A few of the storms became briefly severe, producing localized damaging wind and hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: FD reported lightning struck a house and ignited a fire on Chesnee Highway.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved quickly into the Central and Southern Plains providing the necessary lift for scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across Northwest Texas and Western Oklahoma during the evening hours of Sunday, Oct. 12th. At the surface, a warm front was rapidly moving northward across East Texas and North Louisiana with low level moisture returning quickly in the wake of the northward moving warm front. A cold front in association with the upper level trough was rapidly moving eastward through Western Oklahoma and Texas. Overnight across Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas and Northwest Louisiana, moderate instability was in place with increasing low and mid-level shear as the upper trough approached from the west. Storms eventually erupted ahead of the cold front across Central Oklahoma and Northern Texas, maturing into a squall line as it approached the region during the predawn hours of Monday, Oct. 13th. As the squall line traversed through the region, widespread wind damage was reported associated with straight line winds. Several short track, intense tornadoes developed along the leading edge of the squall line as well across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas and Northern Louisiana. The storms finally exited the region during the afternoon hours of Oct. 13th. Post-event Storm Surveys determined that 6 tornadoes occurred with this severe weather outbreak, one of which produced 1 fatality and 4 injuries in Little River County, Arkansas. Another tornado produced widespread damage across Ouachita Parish in Monroe, Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas tank storage unit and caused it to catch fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a power pole in between Hailey and Ketchum shut down power and also business in Ketchum from 5:35 pm MDT to 8 pm MDT on August 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a power pole in between Hailey and Ketchum shut down power and also business in Ketchum from 5:35 pm MDT to 8 pm MDT on August 12th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system that developed along a frontal boundary helped produce clusters of showers and some strong to locally severe thunderstorms that moved through Eastern Pennsylvania during the early morning of the 19th. Several homes were also struck by lightning.  Approximately 4,500 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes occurred in the Mount Holly warning and forecast area as the thunderstorms moved through. Bucks County suffered the most outages in the area from the combined lightning and wind from the thunderstorms. About 30,000 homes and businesses lost power in the county. This ended the brief hot spell across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and subsequent fire totally consumed an abandoned home along Martin Road in Highland Township. The house was fully consumed by flames when fire crews arrived and it took two companies more than an hour to get the fire under control.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system located over southern Ontario along with surface boundaries in the vicinity of northeast Pennsylvania resulted in severe thunderstorms during the late afternoon and evening hours.  These storms developed in an unstable airmass with severe thunderstorms producing large hail and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two structures were struck by lightning causing minor damage to a church steeple.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system located over southern Ontario along with surface boundaries in the vicinity of northeast Pennsylvania resulted in severe thunderstorms during the late afternoon and evening hours.  These storms developed in an unstable airmass with severe thunderstorms producing large hail and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was on fire on Smith Road due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance aided in producing showers and thunderstorms across southern New England.  While none of these storms were severe, they did produce lightning and two houses were struck by lightning and set on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Bethany Road, setting it on fire.  Firefighters were able to put the fire out quickly, with damage sustained only to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active spring weather scenario unfolded across northern and central New Mexico on the 5th and 6th as gusty winds, mountain snow, and valley showers and thunderstorms impacted the region. Unstable northwest flow and sufficient moisture over the region produced persistent snow showers over the northern high terrain. Seven to 9 inches of fresh snow was reported around Amalia, Red River and Taos Ski Valley.  A man photographing a dust devil near Moriarty was grazed by a lightning strike from a dry thunderstorm.  No reports of high winds were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was grazed by a lightning strike 10 feet away while photographing a dust devil near Moriarty.  The man survived the shock however no details on the extent of his injuries was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning thunderstorm brought a lightning strike to the Citizen's Building on South Main Street in Aberdeen. The lightning strike took out the elevator and phone system on the sixth floor with power disruptions elsewhere.  The fire department was called to the building when a burning smell was noticed with no fire found. A person watched the lightning strike the lightning rod on the top of the building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A narrow line of thunderstorms tracked east across north Alabama during the early morning hours of the 11th.  As the line moved through Huntsville, lightning struck a horse barn at a farm atop Green Mountain.  Tragically, the lightning sparked a fire which killed 12 horses in the barn (due to smoke inhalation), 13 cats and a dog.  Six vehicles were destroyed along with antiques and collectibles stored in the barn.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a horse barn on Green Mountain in Huntsville. The lightning sparked a fire which killed 12 horses in the barn (due to smoke inhalation), 13 cats and a dog. Six vehicles were destroyed along with antiques and collectibles stored in the barn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line moved across northwest Florida during the morning hours of March 16th.  Although no reports of severe weather were received, lightning did damage a home.  In addition, heavy rainfall of 3-5 inches caused some rivers and streams to come out of their banks with areal flooding reported in some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning destroyed a home on Oak Forest Road in the Hiland Park area of Lynn Haven.  Monetary damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong southerly winds gusting as high as 55 mph ahead of a cold front produced minor wind damage, mainly in parts of southeast Massachusetts. Lightning strikes from isolated thunderstorms produced minor damage in northeast Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An isolated lightning strike blew the chimney off a house on Cherry Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong southerly winds gusting as high as 55 mph ahead of a cold front produced minor wind damage, mainly in parts of southeast Massachusetts. Lightning strikes from isolated thunderstorms produced minor damage in northeast Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An isolated lightning strike caused minor damage to the roof of a house on Lakeview Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough moved through the Florida peninsula during the afternoon and early evening hours of the 12th generated a squall line that produced damaging thunderstorm wind gusts and small hail.  Additionally, a lightning strike from the squall line started a fire at an apartment complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Florida Department of Emergency Management relayed a report of a fire started by a lightning strike at an apartment complex. The fire caused smoke damage to 8 units of the apartment building, located near White Swan Drive and Twin Lakes Boulevard. A damage estimate of $10,000 was determined by taking a low end range of average smoke damage claims in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorms produced some urban flash flooding around Valdosta and Albany.  A man was also struck by lightning near Valdosta and subsequently suffered a heart attack and died.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 57 year old male was struck by lightning at a construction site while sheltering under a pole barn.  He then suffered a heart attack and died as a result of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few strong thunderstorms occurred over the San Bernardino and Riverside County mountains overnight on the 21st, with several lightning strikes which started smoldering wildfires. On the 21st, with the onset of offshore winds, two areas ignited into the Strawberry Fire a few miles southwest of Lake Arrowhead, and the North Face Fire in the foothills north of Mount San Jacinto. These fires were quickly extinguished by firefighters, burning no more than a few acres.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning on the 17th eventually ignited the Strawberry Fire just southwest of Lake Arrowhead, with the aid of offshore winds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level weather disturbance and its associated cold front moved across northern Colorado during the late morning and afternoon; spawning several tornadoes, damaging wind, large hail, very heavy rainfall.  Nine tornadoes touched down across northeast Colorado. Three of the tornadoes occurred in Park County, at elevations of 8,000-10,000 feet. The first tornado occurred 8 miles south-southwest of Fairplay; it damaged the roof of a residence and was assigned a rating of EF-1. The second tornado developed 6 miles southeast of Fairplay in open country. The third tornado developed 4 miles west of Lake George; it was given a rating of EF-2. The last tornado caused damage to some homes and overturned several recreational vehicles at an RV park. Several power lines were also downed and some buildings in the town of Lake George were damaged, and trees were also snapped from their bases.  This tornado then passed into Teller County.  ||In Aurora, another tornado touched down near the Blackstone Country Club, it lifted some golf carts and flipped an empty construction trailer. One of the carts was thrown on top of a caddy walking nearby; he was taken to a hospital with minor injuries. It was assigned an EF-1 rating. Five other tornadoes developed over open country across Douglas, Elbert and Weld Counties with little additional damage reported.  In Englewood, lightning struck a tree which damaged two nearby homes and a truck.  Large hail, up to half dollar size, very heavy rain, and minor flooding was also reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in a residential area which caused damage to the two surrounding homes.  Parts of the tree went through the roof and basement of one of the homes as well as the driver-side window of the resident���s truck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms developed along an outflow boundary. There were several reports of large hail and damaging winds as well as heavy rainfall. Also, there were several reports of lightning strikes to structures across the forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a historic church built in the 1880s and caught fire.  It was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few strong thunderstorms occurred over the San Bernardino and Riverside County mountains overnight on the 21st, with several lightning strikes which started smoldering wildfires. On the 21st, with the onset of offshore winds, two areas ignited into the Strawberry Fire a few miles southwest of Lake Arrowhead, and the North Face Fire in the foothills north of Mount San Jacinto. These fires were quickly extinguished by firefighters, burning no more than a few acres.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from the 17th eventually ignited the North Face Fire on the 21st, with the aid of offshore winds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms developed across the region. None of the storms were severe, but a cyclist was struck by lightning causing serious injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Storms moved through the St. Louis metro area.  A cyclist traveling along Maryland Heights Expressway, Highway 141, was struck in the head by a bolt of lightning.  He went into cardiac arrest.  Numerous motorists and paramedics stopped to assist him and were able to revive him, but he was in critical condition.  The 51 year old man has since recovered and was back to work after a month off.  He has hearing loss due to a perforated ear drum, which is where the lightning struck him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An 18-year old male was struck and killed by a lightning strike in Fulton, MO. He was retrieving a book from a pick-up truck when struck.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 18-year old male was killed by a lighting strike while retrieving a book from a pick-up truck.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving area of thunderstorms produced very heavy rain which caused flooding across the western Florida panhandle. The thunderstorms also produced high winds which caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in east Milton causing damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving area of thunderstorms produced very heavy rain which caused flooding across the western Florida panhandle. The thunderstorms also produced high winds which caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A structure fire was caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving area of thunderstorms produced very heavy rain which caused flooding across the western Florida panhandle. The thunderstorms also produced high winds which caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building and caused a fire which injured 1 person.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong storm system brought record flooding along with severe thunderstorms that produced damaging winds and tornadoes to the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper level trough of low pressure over South Florida caused scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two workers were jolted by a lightning strike at the Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport. One of the workers complained of a headache and was transported to a local hospital. The other worker injured his arm when diving to the ground after the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of sub-severe showers and thunderstorms moved through the area during the overnight hours. Lightning associated with the storms struck a house, resulting in minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Officials said lightning struck the side of the home by the garage and traveled down the rain gutter, and into the sprinkler system in the yard.  Fire crews were able to quickly put out the blaze, which mainly damaged part of the garage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across South Florida during the morning producing numerous showers and a few severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck the roof of a home in SW Miami-Dade County on the 5400 block of SW 97 Ct. The bolt damaged the roof and caused a fire in the attic, resulting in moderate damage to the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line moved across southern Georgia during the afternoon hours of March 16th, producing some reports of straight line wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire in Albany.  Monetary damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dry storm system moved through the central California interior on February 18th, bringing a push of cold air that lowered temperatures briefly to near normal. Behind the cold front, gusty winds developed over the mountains and deserts on the 19th. The winds began during the early morning hours, with a gust to 60 mph at Bear Peak in Tulare County, and a gust to 53 mph at Mojave, during the pre-dawn hours. Winds gusted over 45 mph in the eastern Kern County desert during the morning and early afternoon of the 19th, and gusts to 50 mph were recorded in the Piutes.||An upper-level ridge of high pressure returned to California on the 19th behind the departing low-pressure system. High temperatures warmed to above normal for the next several days before the next storm arrived during the afternoon of February 26th. This warming trend peaked with Bakersfield hitting 81 degrees on the 25th, and Fresno reaching 80 degrees. This was the first time either city had seen 80 degrees since November 10th, 2013.||The storm that reached the central California interior on February 26th was the first of two closely-spaced systems. Together, the two storms brought as much as 4 inches of rain to the Southern Sierra Nevada foothills, and over an inch of rain to the Kern County deserts. Fresno had a three-day storm total of 1.11 inch, bringing the total rainfall for February to 2.11 inch. This was 0.08 inch greater than the normal of 2.03 inches and was the first time since December 2012 that Fresno had above-normal rainfall for a month.||The south end of the San Joaquin Valley was rain-shadowed, with Bakersfield receiving only 0.28 inch of rain, almost all of which fell from the second storm on February 28th. The second storm was located off the central California coast, and was impressive on satellite pictures with a tightly-wound structure and a clear center much like the eye of a tropical system. The circulation around the storm produced a southerly wind over the Tehachapi Mountains which funneled through Tejon Pass and down the Grapevine into the south end of the San Joaquin Valley. Winds gusted as high as 89 mph at Grapevine Peak, and to 50 mph at Sunflower Valley on the west side of the Valley. At Buck Rock, in the Sierra Nevada in Tulare County, winds gusted to 66 mph.|Several thunderstorms were spawned by the storms, with the second system being the most potent. Numerous trees were toppled in both the San Joaquin Valley and the Sierra foothills by winds, in many cases pulling down power lines. One thunderstorm at Squaw Valley in the foothills produced a gust estimated at 65 mph, which toppled trees and damaged the roof of a garage. On the Valley floor, there were reports of houses and parked vehicles damaged by falling trees or large limbs. Near Fresno, a tree 3 feet in diameter was toppled.||Street flooding was reported at several locations, not only in the San Joaquin Valley but also in eastern Kern County where the Garlock Road flooded. (Garlock Road is prone to flooding from runoff from the El Paso Mountains.). In Dinuba, water covering the road was estimated at 8 to 12 inches deep. ||In the Southern Sierra Nevada, estimates of new snowfalls were as high as four feet. (These were Snotel observations; a post-storm snow survey had not been conducted at the time of this summary.)||February 2014 was much warmer than normal, and was Fresno���s warmest February on record. Bakersfield tied for its 6th warmest February on record.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused an injury to a man who was in an oil field near Fresno.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Well ahead of a weakening cold front, a narrow band of showers and a few thunderstorms sank southeast through West Virginnia during the late morning and afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a home, then traveled into the garage.  Yet, the surge caused a fire to start in the home's attic.  Fire departments arrived within minutes and contained the fire to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning thunderstorms from a weak upper level disturbance produced lightning strikes that damaged several structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a grass fire on a golf course.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms, associated with an eastward moving cold front, caused significant wind damage across Bell, Harlan, Johnson, and Whitley counties during the afternoon hours of April 28th. The worst of the damage occurred in Harlan county where a storm damage survey revealed that estimated straight line winds of 90 mph downed trees and power lines across the county. Three people were injured in Evarts as a result of the severe winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A county employee was struck by lightning. The person was taken to a hospital but there were no details available on specific injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low near the central Gulf Coast region combined with the sea breezes over a moist and unstable airmass triggered severe storms mainly west of the St Johns River basin during the afternoon and evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed 7 cattle near Starke. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data and is likely incorrect.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms near the Carrollwood area produced hundreds of lightning strikes. One of which sparked a fire at an apartment building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a fire at the Grande Oasis Apartments in Carrollwood. One of the buildings at 8699 Key Royal Ln was evacuated. A total of 18 of the 24 units in the building were damaged. Over 50 residents were displaced from their homes however no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: One round of thunderstorms affected western Arkansas during the morning of the 24th. These thunderstorms moved eastward into eastern Arkansas by afternoon.  Another round of storms developed in western Arkansas during the afternoon and moved to the southeast, exiting the state by late evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and a house in Mena. A small fire started in the house but was quickly extinguished. Power was knocked out for about 45 minutes at the hospital, nursing home, elementary school, and high school.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough and surface cold front combined to bring severe weather on consecutive days May 8 and 9. A short wave trough moved through the long wave pattern on the 8th and caused isolated severe thunderstorms. On the 9th the long wave trough pushed the cold front through causing more widespread storms that produced severe wind gusts, large hail and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck a house causing a fire. There was smoke damage to the kitchen.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, causing a small fire which was quickly put out.  No one was injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front moving southward out of Kentucky spawned numerous showers and thunderstorms throughout Middle Tennessee from the late evening hours on June 4 and continuing throughout the day on June 5. Many reports of damaging winds were received with these storms. In addition, as the front stalled across southwest Middle Tennessee early on June 5, thunderstorms began training across the same areas from Lobelville to Pulaski, dumping up to 8 inches of rain and causing major flash flooding. The flooding damaged numerous roads, homes, and businesses, and resulted in 2 fatalities due to drowning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Trinity Church of the Nazarene on Vultee Boulevard was struck by lightning and destroyed by fire. This was the second time the church had been struck by lightning, as it was previously struck in July 2012.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal squall in and mesolow tracked across southeast Georgia and northeast Florida in several waters of convection through the day. High instability was present, with upper level forcing in place ahead of a long wave trough. The tornado was a associated with the core of a mesolow that tracked ENE inland from the Gulf Coast and over Columbia county and NE over Charlton County. Very heavy rainfall of 4-6 inches occurred over 24 hours with hourly rainfall rates of 2-3 inches in some locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large boat which caused a fire. Significant damage occurred. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated so the event could be included in Storm Data. This estimated value is likely inaccurate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected much of Middle Tennessee from the evening hours on June 6 into and throughout the day on June 7. Numerous reports of wind damage were received, along with a few reports of flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at a residence located at 1906 Herman Street in Nashville, knocking large tree limbs onto an automobile.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning thunderstorms from a weak upper level disturbance produced lightning strikes that damaged several structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike set fire to a structure in Manvel.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small thunderstorm complex moved slowly across Martin County during the early evening of Sunday, April 6th. A lightning bolt struck a sign and blew a hole in the ground, at the Fairmont Municipal Airport. Multiple bulbs were blown out, and the underground transformers and wiring were damaged.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck a sign and blew a hole in the ground, at the Fairmont Municipal Airport. Multiple bulbs were blown out, and the underground transformers and wiring were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved east along and just north of a warm front that was situated near the WI and IL border.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a tree to ignite and a power line was also downed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from morning thunderstorms, started a house fire in Black River Falls (Jackson County) on June 15th. One person lost their life in the resulting fire from smoke inhalation while at least three other homes in the neighborhood also suffered electrical damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An elderly lady died from smoke inhalation after a lightning strike started her house on fire in Black River Falls. At least three other nearby homes also suffered some electrical damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved into Arkansas on the 8th, setting off some thunderstorms in northern Arkansas. These storms sagged into the middle of the state during the evening along with the front. Toward late evening, the front became nearly stationary and rounds of thunderstorms developed along it through the night of the 8th and the morning of the 9th. Excessive amounts of rain fell in parts of western Arkansas, resulting in flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused extensive damage to the communications system at the sheriff's office in Mena.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low combined with monsoonal moisture resulted in widespread lightning over Northwest Oregon and Southwest Washington. The convection was mostly elevated but resulted in power outages and some damage to parts of the Central Willamette Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Abundant lightning resulted in around 1000 PGE customers without power in the Albany and Corvallis area. A public caller reported that a large tree struck from lightning fell onto a home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper air disturbance moved across southeast Louisiana on the afternoon of the 24th. Thunderstorms associated with this disturbance produced several reports of severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local TV station relayed pictures of a fire triggered by a lightning strike at a home in the 3700 block of Rockford Heights. Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Increased upper level dynamics over an unstable and moist airmass triggered scattered strong afternoon thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 19 year old male was struck by lightning sitting in a chair inside an outdoor tent about 2 miles WSW of Palm Coast. The victim has to be resuscitated and hospitalized due to injuries from the lightning strike at least 6 days after the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in a warm, humid airmass ahead of an approaching cold front.  Strong to damaging winds accompanied these thunderstorms resulting in tree damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Eugene Road setting the attic on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours and lingered into the evening across portions of southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms developed along and just south of a nearly stationary front to the north and produced numerous lightning strikes and thunderstorm wind damage reports.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of a slow moving cold front, a southerly flow transported plenty of moisture into the region during the day on Tuesday, June 3rd.  With a moist and unstable air mass in place, plenty of slow moving showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the approaching boundary.  Some of these thunderstorms produced very heavy rain in a short period of time.  This led to some flash flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage areas.  In addition, a few of the thunderstorms also produced strong wind gusts, which caused damage to trees and power lines.  By the late evening, the threat for thunderstorms ended, as the frontal boundary pushed through and less humid air moved into the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning reportedly downed wires on Fishcreek Road and Highwoods Road in Saugerties.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Following a three-week lull in severe thunderstorm activity within the 24-county South Central Nebraska area, a limited severe event unfolded on this Sunday, kicking off what would be a very active month. Although thunderstorms were widespread across nearly all of South Central Nebraska at some point during the day into the early evening, the few known severe-criteria reports originated from the far southwestern counties of Gosper and Furnas between 1230-230 pm CDT. These limited reports were highlighted by quarter size hail in the Johnson Lake and Cambridge areas and also estimated 60 MPH winds near Cambridge. Radar signatures suggested that potentially severe winds might have occurred farther east along and slightly north of the state line from Harlan through Thayer counties, but there were no ground-truth reports to substantiate this. Interestingly, one of the most newsworthy incidents of the day was associated with a non-severe late morning thunderstorm, as a lightning strike sparked a damaging fire in the bell tower of a church in Arapahoe only about an hour after the conclusion of Sunday services. Rainfall-wise, this event brought a much-needed soaking of generally 1-3 to most counties along and south of the Highway 6 corridor. Localized places slightly exceeded 3, including NeRAIN 24-hour totals of 3.14 five miles south-southeast of Deweese and 3.07 two miles east of Stamford. Although impactful flooding issues were held to a minimum, water briefly covered portions of Highway 136 between Oxford and Orleans to a depth of a few inches. ||Fairly weak, non-severe elevated thunderstorms got going early in the day, affecting areas mainly west of a Kearney-Alma line between 8 am-Noon CDT. Then during the 12-3 pm CDT time frame, the initially elevated storms gradually intensified, reached strong to severe levels and became more surface-based in the aforementioned southwestern counties, while general non-severe activity spread eastward across much of South Central Nebraska. Between 3-6 pm CDT, widespread non-severe storms persisted over much of the area, while the northern edge of a more organized convective line centered over north central Kansas tracked eastward along and slightly north of the state line before exiting east of the local area. In the wake of this main batch of convection, a lull ensued for a few hours before another small, weakening quasi-linear storm complex tracked out of western Nebraska into counties such as Dawson, Buffalo and Sherman between 9-11 pm CDT. However, this convection died out with little fanfare before midnight CDT. In the big picture aloft, this event was driven by a series of low amplitude shortwave disturbances ejecting eastward out of the Central Rockies into the Central Plains, along the southeastern periphery of a parent trough shifting eastward from the Northern Rockies. At the surface, a combination of a convectively-driven outflow boundary and synoptic-scale cold front gradually worked southeastward across South Central Nebraska over the course of the day and evening. Although early-day convection and resultant cloud cover kept much of South Central Nebraska from realizing its full potential for low level destabilization, many areas were able to at least briefly realize high temperatures in the 80s F, along with dewpoints in the low-mid 60s. As storms intensified during the afternoon hours, the mesoscale environment featured steep mid level lapse rates, mixed layer CAPE up to around 2000 J/kg and increasing 0-6 kilometer deep layer wind shear of 40-50 knots.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a non-severe storm struck St. Germanus Catholic Church and resulted in a fire that burned a portion of the bell tower. This incident occurred a little more than an hour after Sunday morning worship services ended.
