EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed a 71 year old man while he was out in a field picking blueberries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed a 71 year old man while he was out in a field picking blueberries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very moist and unstable airmass triggered showers and thunderstorms on multiple surface boundaries, with some of the thunderstorms becoming severe. Several rounds of storms produced heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding in portions of Northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A chimney was struck by lightning on Retford Avenue. The chimney was destroyed at the roof lie and resulted in a crack all the way to the basement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical summer time storms developed during the late afternoon of the 21st, isolated strong thunderstorms were a part of that activity over portions of Central Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Concrete Plant and damaged much of the electrical system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on a seasonably hot, muggy day with a few storms becoming severe.  An unusual lightning event occurred in Jackson county where lightning struck a moving vehicle and actually injured the occupant inside.  The vehicle's electrical system was reported to have significant damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning on I-10 near the Grand Ridge exit.  Significant damage occurred to the vehicle and the person inside was transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Residual instability left over from nocturnal convection over Arizona and southeast California moved through southwestern California, helping to initiate showers and thunderstorms over portions of the San Diego County mountains. A separate upper-level low disturbance helped to trigger thunderstorms all the way to the coast and coastal waters during the morning hours. A lightning strike near Encinitas burned the side of a home. Most coastal and valley locations received one-tenth of an inch or less, though a few locations received significantly more, such as 0.57 inch in Del Mar. This disturbance continued to provide enough instability for thunderstorms over the high desert and San Bernardino County mountains, generating up to 0.87 inch. CHP reported flash flooding on Highway 79 at Fink Road and closed the highway at mile marker 46.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a palm tree, which caught fire, burning the side of a home in Encinitas just south of San Elijo Lagoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A single lightning bolt killed cattle at a ranch located in Darby, Montana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A single lightning bolt struck small crab-apple trees at a ranch located on Tin Cup Road, killing all 45 cattle crowded together. The Black Angus cattle consisted of cows, calves and a prize bull that died. A conservative damage estimate calculated by the NWS Missoula office is around $100,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: One man was killed, and four others injured, when they were struck by lightning in Rocky Mountain National Park.  The incident occurred near Rainbow Curve along Trail Ridge Road, not far from where another woman was struck and killed by lightning approximately 26 hours earlier.  Flash flooding was observed in Douglas and Elbert Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning killed one man and injured four others in RMNP.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A combination of upper level disturbances crossing the area along with heating and convergence along the lee trough triggered a band of showers and thunderstorms mainly east of the mountains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Harmony Road setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moving out of the Great Lakes initiated showers and thunderstorms over New York and New England.  Enough instability was present in the region for some of these storms to become severe, producing strong to damaging winds and at least one funnel cloud.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Hudson Road, setting it on fire. News reports indicated the house was a total loss.  In addition, four firefighters were transported to the hospital for heat exhaustion and dehydration.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front provided enough lift in a rather unstable environment to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England. Many of these storms produced strong to damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two women were struck by lightning while walking towards the parking lot from the beach at Crane's Beach in Ipswich.  One was a 61 year old woman from Connecticut, the other a 69 year old woman from Massachusetts.  Both went into cardiac arrest and were given CPR before being transported to Beverly Hospital and then to Massachusetts General Hospital's burn unit. The 61 year old woman died of her injuries the evening of September 6th.  The 69 year old succumbed to her injuries a week later on September 13th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front provided enough lift in a rather unstable environment to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England. Many of these storms produced strong to damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near the intersection of Central Street and Route 28, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lingering monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over southeast Nevada.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a palm tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front draped across central portions of North Texas served as a focus for thunderstorm development on Tuesday afternoon. Meanwhile a second thunderstorm complex advanced from the northwest. Several thunderstorms became severe, namely in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, with damaging winds being the primary occurrence. Flash flooding also occurred in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Much of the western portions of Fort Worth were flooded by flash flood waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning is believed to have been the cause of a large house fire in the 3900 block of West 6th St.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early afternoon thunderstorms produced lightning over southern sections of Pinellas County. A man on a motorcycle was struck by lightning just northeast of Gulfport. Emergency responders were sent to the scene and the man refused to be taken to the hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The state watch office reported a man on a motorcycle was struck by lightning near Gulfport. The man was treated on-scene for his injuries and refused to be taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved east across far southern WI during the morning hours. Lightning struck a home which resulted in a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The roof of a home ignited on fire from a lightning strike. The Fire Department was able to put out the fire without it spreading.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front stalled in Arkansas on the 23rd and remained stationary for several days. Meanwhile, areas of low pressure aloft tracked across the state from time to time. As a result, thunderstorms developed and these storms brought frequent lightning, locally heavy rain, and a few instances of severe weather from the 23rd through the 27th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an ambulance as it traveled along the Martin Luther King Bypass near Carpenter Dam Rd. in the western part of Hot Springs. A person was being transported to the hospital at the time, but no one was injured. However, the lightning strike immediately disabled the vehicle and badly damaged its electrical system. The ambulance had been in service for less than a month.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow-moving upper level low pressure system over the Great Basin pulled abundant moisture north and west into New Mexico.  The combination of deep moisture and instability over eastern New Mexico set the stage for severe thunderstorms beginning by late morning through the late afternoon hours.  Several reports of large hail, strong winds, and heavy rainfall were received.  A large tree in Roswell was blown over onto nearby power lines and a car due to the strong winds.  Pea to quarter size hail accumulated 6 to 12 inches along Interstate 25 between Watrous and Wagon Mound, creating numerous traffic accidents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: State police reported that a man was struck by lightning and killed while riding his motorcycle along U.S. Highway 84 just west of Cimarron at mile post 308 Friday afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours along the Savannah River and moved southeastward across southeast Georgia. The storms developed in the region between the departing Hurricane Arthur to the northeast and a cold front approaching from the west.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike on Tybee Island resulted in minor injuries to three males, two of which were taken to the hospital for treatment of burns. Tybee Island Ocean Rescue reported the injuries and the report was relayed to the National Weather Service by the broadcast media.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Piedmont trough produced thunderstorms with dangerous lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Hogan Court.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Piedmont trough produced thunderstorms with dangerous lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Turnberry Place in Landfall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms formed along and in front of an approaching cold front, with embedded strong to isolated severe thunderstorms that resulted in damaging winds and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck on Elona Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large scale bow echo raced east to northeast across southern WI, causing straight line wind damage in many areas. We Energies reported a maximum power outage of 110000 homes which has not happened since 2005. The outages were due to straight line winds and lightning impacting the power lines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning and killed when he got out of his vehicle on highway 14   to correct the windshield wiper. A line of severe thunderstorms was moving through the area at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and embedded thunderstorms developed across south central Arizona during the early morning hours on September 8th, and as the morning progressed the showers intensified and became more and more widespread. Partially due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Norbert, the storms produced intense rainfall with rainfall rates commonly in excess of 2 inches per hour and in some cases, in excess of 6 inches per hour for short periods of time. By the middle of the morning, most of the central deserts had received over two inches of rain, and many locations across the greater Phoenix metropolitan area picked up between 3 and 6 inches of rainfall. Phoenix Sky Harbor airport received 3.29 inches of rainfall with this event; the rain total set an all time record for any calendar date. The rainfall caused widespread flash flooding followed by flooding; numerous roads were closed. Several freeways were closed, including Interstate 10, as pumping stations failed and lakes several feet deep formed across portions of the freeways. Hundreds of cars were stranded across the greater Phoenix area, many buried to the top of their hoods in flood waters. Hundreds of homes and apartment complexes across the greater Phoenix area were flooded. Heavy rains damaged roofs across the valley, and collapsed the roof of a Fry's grocery store in Tempe. Clearly, the heavy rainfall led to a historic flooding event across south central Arizona on September 8th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and embedded thunderstorms developed across the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the early morning hours on September 8th. Although the thunderstorms were rather isolated, at 0200MST lightning from one of the storms struck a house in south Phoenix. The house was located near 27th Avenue and Baseline Road, at 9624 S 26th Lane in Phoenix. Neighbors reported hearing a large boom at 0200MST when the lightning bolt struck; by the time firefighters arrived the flames were too intense and they were forced to go into a defensive mode. Four children and two adults made it out of the house safely, however the house was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Just after midnight on the morning of the 16th, a line of strong storms crossed south eastward across Interstate 40 near Santa Rosa. This storm produced two lightning strikes that hit a rest area and gas station causing power failures. ||The greatest amount of atmospheric moisture available to date for the summer of 2014 was in place across much of central New Mexico.  Light northwest steering flow aloft beneath an upper level high pressure center building over southwestern New Mexico allowed for locally heavy rainfall.  An area of thunderstorms developed over the southern slopes of the Jemez Mountains forced development farther south into the Albuquerque Metro Area.  These storms developed from northwest to southeast and continually trained over the center of Albuquerque for nearly an hour.  The heaviest rainfall impacted the area from near Montano and Coors southeast across the UNM area, the Albuquerque Sunport, the area around Juan Tabo and Copper, and Mesa del Sol. Significant standing water was reported along Coors Boulevard. Strong flows created impassible conditions along Washington Avenue between Indian School and Constitution.  A frightening YouTube video was posted of the Embudo Canyon flood channel with water battering water beneath of overpass along Interstate 40.  The water was only about 5 feet away from pouring out onto Interstate 40. The most significant flooding occurred around Mesa del Sol where several homes took in water several inches deep.  Many yards in the area reported around 6 inches of standing water.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two lightning bolts just a few seconds apart made direct hits  to the TravelCenters of America just after midnight on July 16th. The strikes caused a power surge which fried circuitry and temporarily knocked 17 fuel pumps out of service. The pumps were not restored to service until the late afternoon during that day as electricians worked to repair the damage caused by the strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of a weak cold front, thunderstorms moved south during the evening hours on the 27th, then slowly weakening in the southern coal field early on the 28th.  Local downpours with 1 to 1.5 inches of rain in an hour fell in parts of Jackson, Cabell, Putnam, Lincoln, Kanawha, Boone, Logan, and Mingo Counties.  The usual street and poor drainage flooding occurred. ||Lightning strikes from these storms did cause some damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an office building off of Teays Valley Road and ignited a fire.  The fire was in the attic. The building sustained smoke and water damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several areas of thunderstorms developed and moved across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the day on the 10th. A home was struck by lightning from one of these storms during the afternoon, resulting in damage to the home. Localized flash flooding also occurred from the excessive rainfall that occurred in some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a home, causing the brick chimney to break apart with pieces falling into the yard and onto the roof. The roof was damaged in several places by the falling bricks. The lightning also damaged a lot of the electrical wiring of the home and damaged some of the support beams of the roof as it passed through the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very humid air mass combined with a passing surface trough to trigger numerous showers and thunderstorms, with embedded strong to severe thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced very heavy rain which led to isolated flash flooding in the Bronx.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were injured when lightning struck a tree they were standing underneath at Orchard Beach. They were rushed to a local hospital. A third man was also struck but was unharmed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front provided enough lift in a rather unstable environment to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England.  Many of these storms produced strong to damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A building on Clearview Circle was struck by lightning, setting the building on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed west of the area before shifting into a warm and moist environment well ahead of a cold front sweeping through the southeastern United States.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Liberty County 911 Call Center reported that lightning struck a tree which then fell down near the intersection of South Main Street and Glenn Bryant Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed west of the area before shifting into a warm and moist environment well ahead of a cold front sweeping through the southeastern United States.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Liberty County 911 Call Center reported one tree down possibly due to lightning along Marchview Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak front in the state helped to spark thunderstorms on the 28th and 29th. Isolated severe weather occurred in the southern part of the state on the afternoon of the 28th. During the evening of the 28th, the front moved slightly back to the north, settling across the middle of the state. During the wee hours of the 29th, very heavy rain began in parts of eastern Arkansas. This rain continued for much of the morning on the 29th as storms repeatedly traveled along the frontal boundary. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches were common in parts of eastern Arkansas, and some totals were in the 8 to 10 inch range. Approximately 35,000 acres of soybeans, corn, and rice were flooded in Prairie, Woodruff, and Monroe counties. Sorghum and winter wheat suffered smaller losses.||Arkansas Governor Mike Beebe declared the following counties eligible for public assistance: Jackson, Monroe, Prairie, and Woodruff. In addition, the governor declared the following counties eligible for individual assistance: Monroe and Woodruff. U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Tom Vilsack declared an agricultural disaster in the following counties: Independence, Jackson, Lonoke, Monroe, Prairie, White, and Woodruff.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire started by lightning destroyed a house. Lightning struck a pine tree behind the house, then traveled along the wiring for an old satellite dish to the house's attic, setting the attic on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small cluster of thunderstorms rapidly became severe over central Bollinger County. This cluster of storms produced very large hail as it tracked east-southeast across central Cape Girardeau County and then into southern Illinois. The storms developed during the heat of the afternoon along a weakening surface trough that extended southward from the Great Lakes region. The storms were aided by a mid-level shortwave trough moving east-southeast toward the Lower Ohio Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several trees and large branches were down due to numerous lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical summer time storms developed during the late afternoon of the 21st, isolated strong thunderstorms were a part of that activity over portions of Central Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One house in the area was struck by lightning the chimney was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A hot and humid air mass in advance of a backdoor cold front resulted in scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Officials reported a vehicle was struck by lightning with the owner standing outside. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: For the second consecutive day, a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms affected central and northern New Jersey during the late afternoon and early evening of the 3rd. About 33,000 homes and businesses lost power throughout the state from the combination of wind damage and lightning strikes. Counties that suffered most of the outages were Cumberland, Hunterdon, Morris, Ocean and Sussex Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire burned a barn to the ground in Frankford Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: For the second consecutive day, a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms affected central and northern New Jersey during the late afternoon and early evening of the 3rd. About 33,000 homes and businesses lost power throughout the state from the combination of wind damage and lightning strikes. Counties that suffered most of the outages were Cumberland, Hunterdon, Morris, Ocean and Sussex Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire damaged a home in Beverly City. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across the region on the 29th. One of the storms produced damaging wind in Franklin County. A man was injured by a lightning strike in Lavaca in Sebastian County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck and injured by lightning while standing on his porch, moving plants indoors out of the weather. The lightning struck a neighbor's tree about 30 yards from his porch. The victim was knocked unconscious and was taken to a nearby hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Upper level trough was positioned over the central U.S. with mid-level winds very weak suggesting slow storm movement. Deep moisture was still in place as precipitable water values ranged from 1.5 to 1.7 inches and surface dewpoints were solidly in the 60's. Another active thunderstorm day occurred with one fatality due to lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local law enforcement reported that a maintenance worker was struck by lightning while outside the middle school in Sells. The individual was flown to a Tucson area hospital and later succumbed to injuries sustained from the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms moving through Western Washington brought lightning, heavy rain and hail. Lightning hit trees in the Fremont and Green Lake neighborhoods, in one case sparking a garage fire.  Power was knocked out in northeast Seattle and crews worked to replace 24 transformers damaged by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Storms moving through Western Washington brought lightning, heavy rain and hail. Lightning hit trees in the Fremont and Green Lake neighborhoods, in one case sparking a garage fire.  Power was knocked out to about 2000 customers in northeast Seattle and crews worked to replace 24 transformers damaged by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail, from quarter to golfball size, and damaging winds across Arapahoe, Boulder, Elbert and Jefferson Counties.  Flash flooding was reported in central Jefferson County.   Heavy rainfall produced street flooding in Denver with some basement flooding reported as well.  The strong winds downed trees and power lines.  One man was injured by a nearby lightning strike in Arvada.  Lightning also sparked a small attic fire in Castle Pines and caused brief electrical outages in Denver.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and sparked a small fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail, from quarter to golfball size, and damaging winds across Arapahoe, Boulder, Elbert and Jefferson Counties.  Flash flooding was reported in central Jefferson County.   Heavy rainfall produced street flooding in Denver with some basement flooding reported as well.  The strong winds downed trees and power lines.  One man was injured by a nearby lightning strike in Arvada.  Lightning also sparked a small attic fire in Castle Pines and caused brief electrical outages in Denver.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a power outage that affected the RTD light rail lines C, D, E, H and W for a short time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong storms occurred during the afternoon of the 11th causing damage and a couple of funnel clouds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a forest fire in the Starks area. The fire was suppressed after a few hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak surface trough sagging south across southern Indiana sparked a thin broken line of thunderstorms during the late afternoon. These storms intensified and brought some strong wind gusts across several counties centered around Fort Knox, which is located in Hardin County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Louisville, starting a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of lines of strong to severe thunderstorms triggered by another lee side trough moved through New Jersey during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. This line not only caused wind and lightning damage, but also caused flash flooding. The greatest impact by the thunderstorms was across the central third of New Jersey. About 30,000 homes and businesses lost power throughout the state with the greatest outages also in the central third of the state. Power was not fully restored until the 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Grove Street in Point Pleasant.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across Arkansas on the 28th, accompanied by scattered thunderstorms. One storm resulted in a lightning fatality in Yell County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 33-year-old man was killed by lightning in a forested area. The man was sitting under a tree, when lightning traveled down the tree, striking the man.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong subtropical ridge of high pressure aloft was centered along the south central Gulf Coastal region.  Some of the hottest weather of the summer season was present across the area at the time with maximum temperatures into the low 90s across the Piedmont, with 80s across the mountains. An upper-level disturbance was tracking through the Great Lakes into the northeastern United States.  This disturbance impinged upon the hot, humid, unstable air mass in place across the region to generate scattered to numerous afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms.  A few of these became severe in the northwest part of the forecast area, particularly in far southeastern West Virginia and adjacent areas of southwest Virginia, producing damaging wind gusts and marginally severe hail along with frequent cloud-to-ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Lynchburg News and Advance along with the Amherst Fire and Rescue Department reported that lightning struck and sparked a fire at a home on Gun Mountain Drive near Amherst.  The home was completely destroyed by the fire.  Nine residents of the home were completely displaced as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front slowly pushed across the area during the afternoon and evening and interacted with deep moisture from Hurricane Arthur tracking up the east coast. This triggered widespread thunderstorms activity with some high winds, hail and heavy rainfall. A Flash Flood Watch was issued early on the 3rd and showers and thunderstorms by mid-afternoon prompted the issuance of several Flood Advisories (FLS) mainly in urban areas including Roanoke and Buena Vista. A Small Stream FLS was issued by late afternoon across parts of Wythe and Grayson counties where radar estimated over 3 inches of rainfall in some basins.  An Urban Flood Warning was issued for the City of Galax, where there were reports of some urban-type flooding.  As the area of heavy rainfall shifted further east a Flash Flood Warning (FFW) was issued for parts of Patrick, Henry, Floyd and Franklin counties at 513 PM. Later information was received that a road was completely washed out by flood waters in eastern Floyd County in an area of 2 to 4 inch rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a house on fire on Williamson Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of lines of strong to severe thunderstorms triggered by another lee side trough moved through New Jersey during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. This line not only caused wind and lightning damage, but also caused flash flooding. The greatest impact by the thunderstorms was across the central third of New Jersey. About 30,000 homes and businesses lost power throughout the state with the greatest outages also in the central third of the state. Power was not fully restored until the 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Wall Township.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Manasquan.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13th across southern Indiana. Some of these storms produced gusty winds and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church just east of Salem, starting a fire. Damage was contained to just a portion of the building, but water and smoke damage was extensive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon heating and produced cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 24 year old male sustained non-life threatening injuries when he was struck by lightning in his yard outside of his home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front and a hot and humid air mass combined to trigger some strong to locally severe thunderstorms over southeast Pennsylvania during the evening of the 2nd.  The thunderstorms caused a ground stop at Philadelphia International Airport that evening and departure delays of over two hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged a home in East Nottingham Township.  No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm struck a tree near Henegar in DeKalb County (northeast AL).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large tree resulting in significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weakening approaching cold front triggered a series of strong to severe thunderstorms during the late afternoon and into the middle of the evening in New Jersey. Hardest hit was Hunterdon County with multiple municipalities that reported downed trees and wires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike and ensuing fire gutted a Wyckoff Mill Condominium building on Powell Court in Hightstown Borough. The lightning struck the roof of the building and started a fire. Seven families were displaced. The fire reached three alarms and fifteen fire companies from seven townships battled the blaze. It took about two hours to get the fire under control. One firefighter hurt his back.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of lines of strong to severe thunderstorms triggered by another lee side trough moved through New Jersey during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. This line not only caused wind and lightning damage, but also caused flash flooding. The greatest impact by the thunderstorms was across the central third of New Jersey. About 30,000 homes and businesses lost power throughout the state with the greatest outages also in the central third of the state. Power was not fully restored until the 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck for separate homes in Neptune. No serious injuries or significant damage occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated strong thunderstorm tracked across Clay County during the evening of August 23rd.  Strong, gusty winds of around 60 mph blew a few large tree branches down in Flora.  In addition, lightning struck a home and caused a small fire in Flora.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the west edge of Flora causing a small fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mean layer high pressure was NW of the area with mean layer flow form the ENE. Sea breeze thunderstorms along the Atlantic coast developed during the early afternoon, and produced some lightning damage in Duval county, including a wildfire near Pumpkin Hill Creek.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a power sub-station at the corner of Old St. Augustine Road near Gran Bay Parkway caused widespread power outages and a transformer fire. About 6000 homes were without power, and traffic lights along several main Southsite Roads were inoperable. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed in an unstable environment aided by diffluence aloft and differential heating. Most of the thunderstorms occurred along a line from Stephenville to Dallas to Cooper. A few of the thunderstorms produced damaging winds that caused minor damage but did tear the roof off one business in Johnson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The local newspaper reported lightning started a fire at Bent Tree Townhomes in Waxahachie. The fire damaged the roof of 4 units, which affected 18 families.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A persistent weather pattern with weak northwest flow over Wisconsin, and cold air aloft, produced slow-moving thunderstorms.  Some storms produced large hail and wind gusts to around 50 mph.  Lightning from one of the storms killed two men working on a tree house in southern Oconto County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm that quickly developed west of Abrams killed two men working on a tree house at a home on County Road E in the Town of Morgan.  The men were struck by lightning from the storm as it passed about two miles to their south.  One of the men, a 27-year-old, was killed instantly.  The other, a 31-year-old, was taken to a Green Bay hospital and died of his injuries on August 6th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An apparent lightning strike caused a fire at the United Methodist Church in Carl Junction. The structure and belongings inside were a total loss. Time was estimated shortly before the fire department was called about the fire. There was tremendous cloud to ground lightning during that time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of short waves in a strong northwesterly upper-level flow pattern, along with moderate to high instability, combined to produce isolated to scattered reports of thunderstorm wind damage across North and Central Georgia each afternoon and evening. Localized flash flooding was reported in Fannin County of North Central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The local media reported that lightning damaged a recreational vehicle and a playground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving frontal boundary, combined with plenty of heat and humidity, led to the development of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Some of the storms were severe and produced damaging winds across parts of central and northeast Massachusetts as well as localized flash flooding. Later at night, thunderstorms with torrential rainfall produced flash flooding near the South Coast and isolated damage from lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Baldpate Road in Boxford which ignited a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving frontal boundary, combined with plenty of heat and humidity, led to the development of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. Some of the storms were severe and produced damaging winds across parts of central and northeast Massachusetts as well as localized flash flooding. Later at night, thunderstorms with torrential rainfall produced flash flooding near the South Coast and isolated damage from lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which caused a large limb to fall on Man Street, partially blocking the roadway.

Some of the storms were severe and produced damaging winds across parts of central and northeast Massachusetts as well as localized flash flooding. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole on Chance Road which brought wires down and ignited a pole fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusual southwest-moving upper disturbance triggered numerous thunderstorms across the South Plains this afternoon and evening. These storms began by mid morning in the Oklahoma Panhandle and at times were severe with very large hail and damaging winds as they moved south-southwest through the Texas Panhandle. Once these storms reached the South Plains, they lost much of their vigor as they consolidated into a large line that only produced two known instances of severe weather. However, this line became more efficient at producing torrential rainfall rates and flooding throughout the South Plains with some locations recording one inch of rain in 15 minutes or less. Parts of Lubbock experienced significant flooding that left at least two dozen cars stranded in high waters. Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and power outages added to the drama as up to 8,000 Lubbock residents were without power during the height of the storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low-level moisture from Tropical Storm (formerly Hurricane) Odile streamed northward ahead of the system, underneath a ridge that was in place. The heat and moisture along a coastal sea breeze combined to produce scattered thunderstorms across the coast, beaches and inland valleys. The strongest storms were in the southern Inland Empire foothills just west of Forest Falls and near Lake Elsinore, and from Kearny Mesa to El Cajon. Rainfall totals were highly variable due to the isolated nature of the thunderstorms, but the heaviest cells on the 16th produced amounts up to one-half, to just over one inch of rain in the coast and valley locations of San Diego and Orange Counties. One to two inches of rain was reported near Lake Elsinore. The San Bernardino County mountains saw generally one-third of an inch or less. A particularly strong storm dumped just over an inch of rain, causing flooding along Balboa Avenue, near Scripps Ranch and Kearny Mesa. The winds were strong enough with these thunderstorms to down several power lines and numerous large trees (across roadways and onto vehicles) in the southern San Diego County valleys (near El Cajon and Mission Valley) and southern Riverside County valleys in Wildomar. Storm survey indicated wind speeds of 60 to 65 mph and Montgomery Field measured 56 mph. The City of San Diego reported 30 buildings damaged and the American Red Cross in Kearny Mesa had significant damage including partial roof collapse.  SDGE reported at least 12 storm-related power outages throughout the city, resulting in more than 6000 customers without power. A few thunderstorms were mountain-focused (near Julian) on the 17th as the remnants of Odile were pushed off to the east and the sea breeze boundary moved well inland.  The storms on the 17th were concentrated over the Riverside and northern San Diego County mountains, generating amounts of one-half of an inch or less. Storm surveys were completed in Wildomar and Kearny Mesa into Mission Valley. Riverside County storm damage was reported at nearly 8 million dollars from the September 7-8 and the 16th events.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near Crestline, resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across north Texas around midday Thursday as a cold front plowed into a warm, moist and unstable air mass in place across the region. Storms began scattered in nature near the Red River and extended south-southwest to just west of the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex along the front. Activity intensified as the front pushed southeast into the Metroplex, with storms becoming severe and producing a large swath of wind damage along the I-20 corridor. Large hail along with damaging winds also occurred in northern portions of the Metro area in Denton County. Storms eventually organized into a squall line, which produced additional areas of wind damage farther south across central and southern portion of the region.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level trough moved out of the Texas Hill Country...towards the region during the late morning, afternoon and evening hours of May 9th. Strong instability developed across the region with peak heating and a strong capping inversion initially during the morning broke during the day. Scattered strong thunderstorms developed as early as mid morning across portions of Northeast Texas.  These storms produced continuous cloud to ground lightning.  A fatality was reported in Nacogdoches County Texas when a man was struck by lightning while standing in close proximity to a tree that was struck.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: According to a press release from the Nacogdoches County Sheriff's Office, NCSO deputies arrived at the home on Shoreline Drive at approximately 11:30 a.m. cdt and discovered the victim lying on the ground in his backyard. A witness reported hearing a loud boom that shook the house. The victim was found in the backyard a few minutes later. The NCSO deputies on the scene noticed that the tree that the man was lying near had clearly been struck by lightning. In addition, the victim had a burn mark on his stomach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon of the 20th and into the early morning hours of the 21st, a large part of the central United States experienced severe weather. Across central Mississippi, severe weather was more sporadic, but portions of the area did see the brunt of the strongest activity.||Portions of the area experienced a combination of damaging winds, hail, a few tornadoes and flash flooding. Damaging winds were more common along the US Highway 82 corridor as the line of storms pushed east. Three weak tornadoes occurred, two in Jones County and the other in Marion County. The most impactful severe weather was from flash flooding as three to six inches of rain fell within a swath extending from Brookhaven to Laurel to Hattiesburg to Columbia. Multiple roads flooded as a result, with the worst flooding outside of West Hattiesburg in Lamar County. Water rescues took place in this area, and about 20 homes had significant water in them.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a gas line along Daisy Drive, causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the region on April 4th and stalled along the northern Gulf Coast. Over the next several days, moisture increased over the region ahead of a strong upper level system. Beginning in the early morning hours of the 6th, bands of showers and thunderstorms moved north across the ArkLaMiss region. This continued through the day as heavy rain fell over some already saturated ground. During the late afternoon and evening hours of the 6th, the stalled front started to move slowly north as a warm front. This occurred as a surface low developed across the Texas coast and began to track northeast. This was able to bring mid 60 degree dew points into the region to just north of the Highway 84 corridor and allow for storms to become more surface based which brought a threat for damaging winds, large hail, and tornadoes.||The most significant impact from this weather system was from the prolonged heavy rainfall. Rainfall totals ranged from a widespread 2-4 inches with a few swaths of 5 to 7 inches. This sort of rainfall produced many instances of flash flooding along with significant river flooding after the rains ended. Multiple roads were washed out in some locations from the copious amounts of rain that fell along with many other roads covered with water. The Strong River at D'Lo, in Simpson County, crested at a record flood stage of 34.3 feet. Due to its close proximity to U.S. Highway 49, flood waters crept across the road and forced closure for a few days. Tallahala Creek at Laurel rose to major flood stage, cresting at 19.36 feet on April 8th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck along Highway 540.

Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed across the area as a result.  A strong cold front moved through the Southeast on the 29th, finally pushing the system out of the Southeast, but not before scattered severe thunderstorms and isolated flash flooding occurred from the widespread 2 to 6 inches of rain that fell over northwest Georgia.  Two weak tornadoes also occurred with this system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wedge cold front was stalled across southwest Virginia into north central North Carolina.  Temperatures behind the wedge front were well below seasonal normals with maximum temperatures only in the 50s.  Meanwhile...a very deep closed upper low (467mb at 500mb) was shifting slowing eastward from the central U.S. into the eastern U.S.  A deep conveyor belt of moisture was spreading northward from the Gulf of Mexico up and over the shallow wedge of cool air. This was a multi-day weather system that culminated with heavy rainfall, flooding, and flash flooding across the Virginia Piedmont during the afternoon of the 30th.  On this day, an early morning thunderstorm sparked a lightning-related fire in rural Surry County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WXII Channel 12 Television of Winston-Salem, North Carolina reported that lightning struck and set on fire the detached carport of a home on Haystack Road in rural north central Surry county.  A vehicle inside the carport was also damaged.  There were no injuries or fatalities to report with the incident.  However, it took nearly two hours to contain the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper low moved into the central United States.  Surface low pressure was located over northwest Kansas into southwest Nebraska during the late afternoon.  A warm front extended from the low across northern Missouri into southern Illinois.  A strong push of moisture took place south of the front with dewpoints rising into the upper 50s to low 60s.  Precipitable water values increased to around 1.3 inches.  The freezing level was relatively low, around 11,000 feet.  The atmosphere was strongly sheared with 50 to 60 kts of shear available.  By the afternoon, the atmosphere became unstable with 1000 to 2000 J.kg of CAPE available.  Downdraft CAPE was quite high in the 700 to 1000 J/kg.  CAPE in the -10 to -30 C layer of the atmosphere was around 200 J/kg.  A strong line of thunderstorms formed on the east edge of the dry slot as it pushed into Iowa.  Thunderstorms remained below severe levels through the morning, however, they intensified as the moved into south central and southeast Iowa.  One tornado touched down in Wapello County before racing northward into Keokuk County.  There were numerous reports of high winds as the line progressed east with winds of 60 to 70 MPH.  Numerous trees were blown down by the high winds.  The roof was taken off of a family medical center in northeast Oskaloosa in Mahaska County.  Major structural damage was reported on a farmstead west of Ottumwa in Wapello County with outbuildings damaged and roof damage to the porch of the farmstead.  Windows were blown out of cars and roofs were blown from buildings on a farmstead east of Cincinnati in Appanoose County.  Ten people were injured, some requiring hospitalization, on the south side of Ottumwa. At least four of the ten were injured when thunderstorms winds lifted debris at an auction on the south side of the city.  One injury was reported in Appanoose County when a woman was struck by debris lifted by strong winds.  Lightning struck a car near Osceola in Clarke County.  It struck the trunk of the car and set the trunk on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning on U.S. 34 near Osceola.  The trunk caught fire.

These storms were hail producers and mainly affected areas primarily along and north of US 380 from Decatur to Sulphur Springs. The worst damage was done in Denton where hail up to the size of softballs caused close to $5 billion in damage. Three tornadoes also occurred with this system; an EF-0 in Collin County, an EF-0 in Hopkins County, and an EF-1 in Hunt County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Denton Record Chronicle reported firefighters from Sanger and Krum battled a gas well fire, which started due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late season cold front and slow moving upper level low moved into the region and pulled deep moisture north across the area. Multiple days of heavy rain occurred causing flooding in portions of South Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from an early morning thunderstorm struck a home in Scott and caught it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful storm system lifted into the central Plains on the afternoon of  April 27, 2014 and brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms to eastern Iowa. Some of these thunderstorms were severe and produced damaging winds in northeast Missouri. Lightning struck the Old Stone Church in St. Francisville and caused a fire that would destroy the building as the line of thunderstorms moved across the region. In addition to the damaging winds, rainfall totals ranged from a half an inch to around 1 inch in a little under an hour.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast Media reported that lightning struck the Old Stone Church in St. Francsville around 4PM CDT on April 27th causing a fire. The church was built in 1853.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sub-severe thunderstorms formed across the peninsula during the early afternoon hours. They produced numerous cloud-to-ground lightning strikes across the area, with two separate lightning fatalities reported.  Additionally, thunderstorm wind damage was reported to a carport.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 71 year old man was fishing in a lake at Edward Medard Park when he was apparently struck and killed by lightning. The man was found face down in the water just after 7 PM with signs of electrocution.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms redeveloped early Monday morning, June 9th across extreme Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Arkansas, as the nocturnal low level jet interacted with the retreating surface front. While these storms were not severe, they did produce an extended period of locally heavy rainfall especially across northern Bowie County Texas, as well as Little River, northern Miller, and southern Hempstead counties in Southwest Arkansas, where surface gauge and radar estimated determined that widespread 3-6+ inches of rain had fallen in 2-3 hours. As a result, flash flooding was observed just west of Texarkana, TX as well as across much of Little River County Arkansas. A tornado was also produced from these storms in Red River County, Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Lindsey Park, sparking a fire which destroyed the home.  Three dogs were fire but the homeowners were not injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of thunderstorms moved across western Wisconsin on April 12th. These storms developed along a very slow moving cold front and primarily produced large hail, although some occasional high winds were also reported. The first round of storms moved in during the mid morning hours with the last of the storms ending during the early evening. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized near Stoddard (Vernon County) and near Viroqua (Vernon County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large retail store in Onalaska. The damage was limited to a portion of the roof. The store had to be evacuated until the fire was extinguished and it was determined that it was safe to be occupied.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A home in Woodburn, Oregon caught on Fire after being struck by lightning. There were also 2000 customers without power in Multnomah and Clackamas Counties from lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple sources reported that lightning struck a residence in Woodburn, OR on the Oregon Golf Association Golf Course causing a significant fire. The second floor of the home was completely destroyed.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning causing a fire. The garage was completely destroyed with heavy smoke damage to the house. Two firefighters were treated at the local hospital with minor injuries sustained while fighting the fire.

One person was killed by lightning, another was injured, and several buildings were reported to be struck.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 31-year-old man was injured when lightning struck him on the practice putting green at White Mountain Golf Course on the north side of Rock Springs. A witness to the incident was able to revive the man with CPR and a defibrillator.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported on a tree that fell onto a house in Tampa. The homeowner reported a loud boom, followed by the tree falling onto a sun room and into a front bedroom, penetrating the ceiling.  Time was estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped to spark off some some strong to locally severe thunderstorms across eastern Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening of the 23rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in West Grove.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep slow moving upper level trough located over the Lower Mississippi Valley led to the development of low pressure, which moved from western Tennessee to just west of Louisville on May 14th. Ahead of this cyclone, ample moisture brought heavy rain and thunderstorms to central Kentucky, beginning during the early morning hours. Shortly after dawn, a line of thunderstorms began to train along a thin strip over  Hancock County, Kentucky, and extending northwards into southern Indiana. Three to as much as 4 inches of rain fell within a 2 hour period, leading to flash flooding. Later in the day, modest instability developed across the Bluegrass Region and east central Kentucky. A couple of waves of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, bringing several rounds of heavy rain and isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lexington media reported that lightning downed a large tree near Cross Keys Road, which fell across several power lines. This brought widespread power outages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system that developed along a frontal boundary helped produce clusters of showers and some strong to locally severe thunderstorms that moved through southern New Jersey during the early morning of the 19th. A couple of homes were also struck by lightning. Approximately 4,500 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes occurred in the Mount Holly warning and forecast area as the thunderstorms moved through. Over 3,000 homes and businesses lost power in the southern half of the state. This ended the brief hot spell across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused smokey conditions in the basement of a home on Birch Street in Vineland. This was one of two homes that were struck by lightning in the city.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper level storm system moved across the region from April 28 into April 29, producing widespread showers and thunderstorms across Middle Tennessee. Several rounds of showers and storms moved across the region throughout the day on April 28, and again late in the day on April 29. Numerous reports of wind damage, flash flooding, large hail, and even one tornado were received from these storms. CoCoRaHS rainfall measurements over these two days ranged from 4 to 6 inches in parts of southwest Middle Tennessee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Cracker Barrel Corporate Office building on Hartmann Drive causing a minor fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a yacht at the Kennedy Point Yacht Club and Marina in Titusville. The lightning strike started a fire that engulfed the yacht and several nearby boats.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a yacht at the Kennedy Point Yacht Club and Marina in Titusville. The yacht caught fire and spread to three adjacent boats. Three of the four boats were a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front wavered in Arkansas for several days from the 5th through the 9th. On several occasions, upper level low pressure systems moved through, sparking thunderstorms in the vicinity of the front. Some severe storms erupted each day, mainly producing damaging winds. However, there were a couple of weak tornadoes on the 6th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable airmass resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low and trailing trough extending from Nevada into Arizona and western NM allowed for numerous storms to develop. Storms moved slowly from south to north and trained over the same areas. With many areas already seeing saturated ground from previous days of rainfall, the potential for flash flooding was exacerbated. Isolated cells began to develop during the late morning hours and increased in coverage and intensity by early afternoon. By 2pm strong cells had developed over the Tajique and Bandelier areas. Cells back-built over the Tajique area, with multiple hours of moderate to sometimes heavy rain.

A bowing segment interacted with this boundary and produced a few straight-line wind damage events from Tattnall County east to Chatham County. Another bowing segment brushed McIntosh County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of a slow moving mid level trough in the Missouri, warm and humid air returned to northeast Kentucky on the 10th.  Sunshine helped temperatures reach into the mid 80s during the afternoon.  An arch of thunderstorms moved northeast out of Tennessee during the late afternoon, through eastern Kentucky and into West Virginia near sunset.  A well defined shelf cloud was observed on the leading edge of the squall line.  Wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph were widespread.  For example, the Tri State Airport near Huntington had a gust to 51 mph at 1909E, a spotter near Leon had a 45 mph gust around 1955E, and Charleston had a 46 mph gust near 2030E.  A few spots received slightly stronger wind gusts.  Electrical power outages occurred.  Cabell County and the Huntington vicinity had about 16,000 customers without electricity.       ||After an overnight and morning lull, more rounds of convection developed during midday on the 11th in southwest Virginia and southern West Virginia.  Those showers and thunderstorms moved northeast through portions of West Virginia during the afternoon.||Additional clusters of showers and thunderstorms moved northeast through West Virginia during the overnight hours of the 11th into the 12th.  Some of these showers were elongated along their movement.  Local rains of 1.5 to 2 inches over wet terrain managed to caused minor flash flooding.||The final round of showers and thunderstorms came during the afternoon and early evening of the 13th, as the surface cold front was moving through.  Some minor urban and poor drainage flooding occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree was struck by lightning.  The tree came down onto a porch of a mobile home.  Three men standing on the porch were trapped beneath the fallen tree.   The local fire department freed the trapped men.  One man suffered a broken collar bone and 5 broken ribs.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm developed in north central Alabama, producing lightning that did some damage to a house after a large tree limb (after being struck by the lightning) fell on it.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked a very large tree limb down onto a home on east upper river road in the Sandy Acres subdivision, near Priceville, Alabama. Winds around 35 mph also damaged a trampoline.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level disturbance movng up the Ohio River Valley combined with a humid air mass to trigger clusters of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northerly flow on the back side of a departing upper level disturbance, combined with hot, humid, unstable air along the Rio Grande to promote several areas of strong to severe thunderstorms. More than an hour of heavy rainfall produced urban flooding in La Joya between 330 and 4 pm, with high water continuing through 430 pm.  The large storm cell surged from northeast Cameron County through Bayview, then on into Brownsville between 4 and 445 pm. Additional cells formed on outflows and continued the heavy rains west of Harlingen through around 6 pm, with between 3.25 and 4.7 inches having fallen. Scattered reports of large hail, urban flooding, frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes, and pockets of wind damage to tree limbs and power lines was common.||The last surge of intense storms occurred just before sunset, as remnant boundaries fired in a small area of southern Starr County, around and just north of Rio Grande City. An intense but brief updraft surged into the storm and resulted in reports of quarter sized hail or larger.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local law enforcement officials reported two house fires started by lightning strikes in the town of Laguna Vista.

Scattered thunderstorms developed, some of which produced localized large hail (greater than an inch in diameter) with isolated damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and downed a tree on Pierce road.

The golfers were leaving the 3rd green at the Powell Golf Club near Garland when lightning struck. The bolt knocked one man to the grass and another to his knees. Both men said it felt like they had been hit from behind or whacked on the side of the head.

Eight units were declared uninhabitable after the blaze, which was controlled in less than an hour. Four nearby townships assisted in battling the blaze. Lightning struck the upper part of the building and started a roof fire.  Other condominium units suffered fire, smoke and water damage.

The storm produced large hail and a brief tornado near Silver City. The tornado caused tree damage along its path. Hail to baseball size was also reported over the Black Hills through Custer State Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt hit a storm chaser as he was filming a storm. The charge traveled to the ground and blew a hole in the pavement. The chaser's car and another car were disabled.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong instability developed during the afternoon of the 21st to the south of a weak boundary sliding south across central Indiana. A shortwave moving across the western Great Lakes contributed to steep low level lapse rates and strong mid-level winds that supported several rounds of strong convection. During the early evening, a southeastward-moving bow echo brought widespread wind damage to the western Bluegrass Region. This initial round of storms produced an outflow boundary that moved west of Louisville and later proved a focus for additional severe storms during the early morning hours.  These additional early morning storms were also supported by a strong low level southwesterly jet. During the early morning hours, a wet microburst developed near Radcliff. This microburst was the beginning of a long-lived bow echo that rapidly moved southeast and brought large hail and widespread wind damage across central Kentucky, including the towns of Elizabethtown, Hodgenville, and Campbellsville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Lexington media reported that lightning struck a church steeple in Georgetown, starting a small roof fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large and powerful complex of thunderstorms moved southeast out of northwest Kansas and across the area during the early morning hours of June 5th, 2014.  This complex of storms was a prolific producer of very large hail up to three and half inches in diameter, especially considering the early morning hours when it occurred.  Damaging wind gusts to 70 mph also occurred with the storms.  As the complex moved southeast, a wake low developed on the north side of the system, producing non thunderstorm wind damage across portions of Central Kansas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The emergency manager reports than an oil well was struck by lightning and caught on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front combined with a series of potent disturbances caused a round of severe thunderstorms across the region. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a shed in Newburgh, creating a fire that resulted in damage to just the shed.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage just southwest of Monroe, resulting in damage to the garage and partial parts of the home on West Mombasha Road.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of an apartment complex sparking a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very dynamic weather pattern was in place over the central U.S. on the 3rd.  A strong short wave moved out of the Rockies onto the Plains during the day.  Thunderstorms formed early in Nebraska and South Dakota.  The storms spread and developed southeast into Iowa during the afternoon and evening.  The airmass became unstable with CAPE values rising to about 2000 J/kg.  Downdraft CAPE rose to to around 1000 J/kg, with about 600 J/kg of CAPE available in the -10 to -30 layer of the atmosphere.  The freezing level was around 14,000 feet.  The atmosphere was highly sheared with 50 to 80 kts of shear available.  A strong 70 to 80 kt mid level jet moved into the area as the low level jet increased to around 60 kts by evening.  Precipitable water values were around 2 inches, which is more than three sigma above seasonal normals.  The LCL level was fairly low, around 1000 meters. Thunderstorms that formed to the west quickly became an upscale MCC as it continue southeast.  The strongest storms formed along the baroclinic zone of the warm front.  Windspread severe weather occurred, but was limited to the far southwest part of the CWA.  Hail and high wind was the mode of severe weather with hail up to baseball size and winds in excess of 80 MPH.  The winds caused considerable structural and tree damage across southwest Iowa.  Whole farm buildings were destroyed in Taylor and Ringgold Counties with winds of 70 to 95 MPH.  Very heavy rainfall also occurred with a band of three to six inches of rain.  Additional damage was done in Adams County when lightning struck a home in the town of Corning. The home was was a total loss from the fire. Spotty flash flooding was reported with some of it significant in Ringgold, Cass,  Adams, Adair, Taylor Wayne, and Decatur Counties.  Flood damage was widespread in Decatur County with the county engineer reporting 25 culverts damage, 12 bridges damaged and water over the road in 40 other locations, up to 2-3' of water at times.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in the city of Corning was a total loss after it burned down following a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted north across the region during the day. Showers and storms developed within the unstable air to its south by the afternoon. Some of these storms increased to severe levels.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and damaged multiple electronic devices. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms intensified along and ahead of a cold front as it pushed south across the Lower Ohio Valley. A very unstable air mass fueled intense thunderstorm development during the late afternoon hours. The initial activity included storms that were discrete and supercellular in nature, with damaging winds and a couple of tornadoes. As storm coverage increased during the evening, the storms merged and evolved into a forward propagating mesoscale convective system across southern parts of western Kentucky. The slow southward movement of the storms resulted in very intense rainfall rates and local flooding. The storms were located within a very moist air mass, with precipitable water values from 1.5 to 1.8 inches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire at an apartment complex was started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slowing moving thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall and flash flooding. There were a few reports of hail and gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A damaging lightning strike hit a large tree on the Ozark Community College campus early Thursday morning. It broke 18 windows in three different dorms on campus. One car was damage by falling tree debris and the phone system in the dorm was severely damaged. Time was estimated by witnesses.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed in the unstable, moisture laden air in advance of an approaching strong cold front. Several of these storms reached severe levels by producing damaging winds and up to golf ball size hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a man.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: For the second day in a row, thunderstorms with heavy rain moved across northeast Iowa. A round of storms developed during the early morning hours of June 19th along a warm front and then a second round developed during the afternoon ahead of an approaching cold front. Radar estimates of 3 to 6 inches were common across southern Winneshiek and Allamakee Counties into the northern portions of Fayette and Clayton Counties. A presidential disaster declaration was signed for the repeated rounds of severe weather that hit northeast Iowa in the middle of June. This disaster declaration included Allamakee, Chickasaw and Fayette Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a minor house fire to occur in Decorah.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed in the unstable, moisture laden air in advance of an approaching strong cold front. Several of these storms reached severe levels by producing damaging winds and up to golf ball size hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a house fire at 509 Sussex St., Lynchburg, VA. Firefighters were able to quickly contain the flames, and there were no injuries to either the residents or the firefighters.  The family of five were displaced due to the damage. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved across South Florida resulting in scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck one of the runways at Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, causing three holes in the asphalt. The holes were rapidly patched up. In the meantime, 27 flights were diverted to other airports.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved across South Florida resulting in scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in North Miami Beach, sparking a fire that caused significant damage to the interior of the home. Five people inside the home at the time of the lightning strike were able to get out in time. Damage to the home is estimated at $50,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surge of monsoonal moisture from northern Mexico generated scattered thunderstorms across Southern California. From these storms, two significant lightning strikes occurred. In Venice Beach, one man was killed and 13 people were injured when lightning struck the water. The other lightning strike occurred on Catalina Island where a golfer was struck and injured by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An isolated thunderstorm moved across the Venice Beach area along the Los Angeles county coast. Lightning struck the water, injuring 13 people and killing one person.
