Over 3,000 homes and businesses lost power in the southern half of the state. This ended the brief hot spell across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a chimney caused an attic fire in a home along Lynn Drive in West Deptford Township. Fire fighters were able to bring the fire under control within 30 minutes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a building in Fairmont, causing significant damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Lumber River Electric Company building at the corner of Main and Red Cross Streets. The resulting fire destroyed the interior of the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A disturbance in the wind flow aloft, along with afternoon heating and instability, helped maintain thunderstorms. They moved through extreme southeast Ohio into West Virginia.  The most power outages occurred in Cabell County with over 7,000 customers affected.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree along Garden Terrace.  The tree fell onto power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On June 1st, thunderstorms with heavy rainfall and small hail occurred across western and north central Nebraska during the afternoon hours.  By early evening, a line of thunderstorms developed and produced damaging winds across portions of western and southwest Nebraska.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two cows were struck by lightning and died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southeast Michigan saw active weather in both the morning and afternoon on Wednesday, June 18th, with the afternoon convection turning severe.  Previous convection during the morning hours had moved to the east and there was enough instability for the thunderstorm complex over southern Wisconsin and northern Illinois to hold together as it crossed Lake Michigan and into Lower Michigan.  This line of storms raced across the state bringing winds, heavy rain, and frequent lightning with numerous reports of trees down, power outages, and local flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms developed late in the afternoon of June 16th across Minnesota and Iowa ahead of warm front and area of low pressure. These storms produced reports of 60 to 70 mph winds as they rolled across northeast Iowa. The area near Westgate (Fayette County) was hit hard with at least three barns blown down, a church roof damaged and numerous trees and power lines were downed. Another cattle barn was blown down south of Brainard (Fayette County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire in Riceville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore flow allowed for the development of early morning showers and thunderstorms. A thunderstorm in Pinellas County produced a lightning strike which sent a man to the hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local TV station relayed a report of a 50 year old man injured by a lightning strike while walking on the beach in Sand Key. He was not struck directly but was very near the strike and was transported to the hospital for non-life threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system that developed along a frontal boundary helped produce clusters of showers and some strong thunderstorms that moved through Delaware during the early morning of the 19th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire in Hockessin (Mill Creek Hundred). No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a pre-frontal trough and a passing short wave triggered an isolated severe thunderstorm over eastern Orange County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning on Union Avenue in Newburgh.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a home in Rosemount, Minnesota during the morning of Friday, July 25th. The home suffered extensive damage as a result of the lightning strike and resultant fire. No one was hurt during the event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a home in Rosemount, Minnesota during the morning of Friday, July 25th. The home suffered extensive damage as a result of the lightning strike and fire. No one was hurt during the event.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The afternoon of Monday, June 16th, two major thunderstorm complexes across Nebraska and South Dakota, congealed into one along the Minnesota, Iowa border from Sioux Falls, eastward along I-90 to Fairmont and Albert Lea. Some of the severe storms moved north of I-90 and produced wind and hail as far north as Mankato, Waseca and Owatonna.  Wind gusts in excess of 60 to 70 mph were clocked in these areas and produced numerous large trees down, power outages, and significant street flooding and erosion due to two to four inches of rainfall in less than two hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a small house fire Monday afternoon, June 16th, on St. Cloud's west side. No one was hurt in the fire at 205-19�� Ave. S. St. Cloud. The fire started after lightning struck an antenna alongside the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The afternoon of Monday, June 16th, two major thunderstorm complexes across Nebraska and South Dakota, congealed into one along the Minnesota, Iowa border from Sioux Falls, eastward along I-90 to Fairmont and Albert Lea. Some of the severe storms moved north of I-90 and produced wind and hail as far north as Mankato, Waseca and Owatonna.  Wind gusts in excess of 60 to 70 mph were clocked in these areas and produced numerous large trees down, power outages, and significant street flooding and erosion due to two to four inches of rainfall in less than two hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home Monday afternoon, June 16th in the 9300 block of Magnolia Lane North, Maple Grove. Lightning struck the attic of the home, caused damage to their roof, and put a 4��2 hole in the side of their home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough continued to dominate the eastern portion of the country on the 20th, but with ridging beginning to build in aloft. A shortwave pushed across the Southeast late in the evening, sparking numerous showers and thunderstorms.  Nearly stationary thunderstorms produced heavy rain over portions of Heard and Troup Counties. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 8 inches occurred primarily just southeast of Franklin. This caused flash flooding on streams and creeks flowing into the Chattahoochee River in southeast Heard County. The flood waters caused the pool elevation on West Point Lake a few miles downstream to rise around one and a half feet.  In this same storm, lightning struck a house, resulting in a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Heard County Emergency Manager reported that a house around two miles southeast of Franklin on Pike Road had major damage from a fire caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure shifted to northern Arizona allowing moist southeast flow into southern Arizona. The first severe thunderstorms of Monsoon 2014 brought gusty outflows producing wind damage and lofting dust into the air. Blowing dust reducing visibility to less than a quarter mile was reported near Safford. Additionally, a haboob started in the Marana area and progressed northwest along Interstate 10 toward Phoenix.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a power pole near Ina Rd. and Oracle Rd. left about 25 residents without power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure shifted to northern Arizona allowing moist southeast flow into southern Arizona. The first severe thunderstorms of Monsoon 2014 brought gusty outflows producing wind damage and lofting dust into the air. Blowing dust reducing visibility to less than a quarter mile was reported near Safford. Additionally, a haboob started in the Marana area and progressed northwest along Interstate 10 toward Phoenix.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning incinerated a palm tree in Saddlebrook.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front helped trigger a series of strong to severe thunderstorms that produced large hail, damaging winds as well as lightning damage and flash flooding during the afternoon and evening of the 15th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused power outages and disrupted 911 communications in Long Hill Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across western Wisconsin during the evening hours of June 28th ahead of a trough of low pressure. Several of these storms produced high winds that caused considerable damage in the city of La Crosse north into Holmen (La Crosse County). Numerous trees and power lines were blown down by winds that gusted to at least 60 mph. At least 7,000 customers in the La Crosse area were without power. The power outage took out street lights and stop lights across much of the city.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole with the electrical surge going into a nearby house and starting a small fire in a La Crosse home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The largest severe weather event to strike Middle Tennessee in the summer of 2014 affected the area during the afternoon hours on August 20. Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms produced numerous reports of wind damage and measured wind gusts up to 75 mph, as well as a few reports of flash flooding. The ASOS at Clarksville Outlaw Field measured a wind gust of 75 mph, which is likely the strongest wind gust ever measured in Clarksville, although historical wind records are incomplete.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Clark Drive in Rural Hill which caused a small fire and minor damage to an upstairs room.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper-level low pressure system dropped southward into the Great Lakes on Sunday July 27, sparking a good deal of severe thunderstorms in the warm, moist, and unstable air in advance of the system. Between 2 p.m. and 8 p.m., severe weather affected nearly all of southeast Michigan.  The initial storm that affected portions of Midland and Bay counties from around 2:15 to 3:15 p.m. was a prolific hail producer, with hail up to 3 diameter (greater than baseball size) recorded near Midland.  Later, another particularly strong storm moved across Oakland County between around 4:30 and 5:15 pm, dropping hail up to 2.50 diameter (tennis ball size) near the Highland/White Lake area, with wind damage reported over central and eastern portions of the county.  The storms produced heavy rainfall as well, with a swath of 1-2 recorded over southern Oakland County.  Wyandotte, in southern Wayne County, picked up 2.67 in 4 hours.  Total damage across Southeast Michigan was estimated to be 100 million dollars from the severe wind and hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Building damage caused by lightning stroke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure remained over northern Arizona. Monsoon storms struck again, but with less potency than the previous day. Only one severe wind report was received, in Santa Cruz County near the international border.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and burned a pair of palm trees in Green Valley.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably strong cold front came through the region on July 2nd. Storms developed along the front, some of which brought damaging winds and some large hail. Behind the front, much cooler and drier air prevailed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning which caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low developed in the eastern Great Lakes, providing enough lift and energy for showers and thunderstorms to develop across southern New England.  With plenty of moisture, shear and instability in the region, some of these storms became severe, producing strong to damaging winds and flash flooding.  This began with a round of showers and thunderstorms in the morning, which mainly resulted in flash flooding.  This was followed with more shower and thunderstorm activity during the afternoon with damaging winds the main effect. ||One of the severe thunderstorms in the morning interacted with the marine front along the coast, allowing it to spin up into a rather brief tornado.  Despite the short path and duration of the tornado, the location in which it touched down, metro Boston, allowed it to do considerable damage before lifting.  Several injuries occurred, mainly from flying debris. This was the first tornado to hit Suffolk County since 1950, when modern record keeping began.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, felling it onto a nearby house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On a hot and humid 14th, thunderstorms moved into the northern half of West Virginia during the afternoon, but did not reach southern counties until the overnight hours. Downpours were common.  Rain amounts of 1.5 to 2.5 inches occurred in many spots, but since the ground was relatively dry, no flooding occurred.||Lightning in the vicinity of a hilltop home in Putnam County between 2300 on the 13th to 0200E on the 14th is suspected of igniting a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large brick house on a hilltop off of Blue Lick Road caught fire and burnt to the ground.  Local and county officials suspect lightning ignited a fire in the attic.  A smoke detector went off alerting the 2 sleeping adults.  They got their 7 year old son and evacuated the house.||By the time fire crews arrived, the home was fully engulfed by flames.  No fire hydrants were located on the hilltop.  The home was a total lose.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very moist and humid air mass was in place across the region on Wednesday, June 25th.  As a slow moving cold front approached from the west, bands of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the boundary.  As these showers and thunderstorms repeatedly passed over the same locations, the heavy rainfall led to significant runoff, which caused flash flooding in some areas.  Many roads were closed due to the flooding and some homes were affected by water as well.  In addition, a few of the storms produced wind damage to trees and some damaging lightning strikes.  ||The threat for heavy rainfall and flooding ended late on the evening of June 25th, as the storm's cold front passed through the region from west to east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning reportedly struck a house on Pells Road in Rhinebeck and caused a fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Todd Road, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level trough of low pressure over the eastern U.S. caused scattered thunderstorms over South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house in the 3000 block of Andrews Ave. in East Naples was hit by lightning, causing a fire inside the home. The family members inside the house got out safely, however at least two pet birds died from the smoke. Fire Officials determined the house was inhabitable from the smoke damage. Time of event was estimated and based on archived lightning data from Earth Systems.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered thunderstorms, with a few severe storms developed over the Piedmont late in the afternoon and during the early evening. Meanwhile, a weakening complex of thunderstorms moved into the Smoky Mountain region, producing areas of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Newspaper reported lightning struck a vacant home on Causby Rd, igniting a fire that completely destroyed the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated severe storms took down trees in Lancaster and Kershaw counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency Manager reported a house fire on Pink Dogwood Road that was caused by lightning which destroyed the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms across interior southern New England, some of which produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was determined to be the cause of a fire that destroyed a 6,500 square foot home on North Farms Road in Northampton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of strong thunderstorms developed in northwest Alabama, producing a few reports of flooding and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local business was struck by lightning, producing some minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning thunderstorms from a weak upper level disturbance produced lightning strikes that damaged several structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire at a two story residential home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The weather changed beginning the evening of January 29th as the first storm in over seven weeks reached the central California interior. Rain and mountain snow moved into the northern half of the region during the late evening of the 29th, spread south through the 30th and tapered off the last day of the month. The storm brought wind gusts as high as 50 mph to the mountains and deserts and the first measurable rain since December 7th to the San Joaquin Valley. Fresno broke its driest start to a calendar year at 28 days; the previous record had been 21 days, set in 1903. Bakersfield���s dry start ended at 29 days, just breaking the old record of 28 days, set in 1963.||The heaviest snow totals occurred in the higher elevations of the Southern Sierra.  For example, 14 inches fell near Devils Postpile, 12 inches just east of Cedar Grove, and 10 inches near Lake Wishon. ||The average high temperature for January at Fresno was 12 degrees above normal, and Bakersfield was 11.3 degrees above normal. However, the very dry, stable airmass over the region allowed for strong radiational cooling most nights. The average low temperatures for Bakersfield and Fresno were less than two degrees above normal.||The well above normal high temperatures more than offset the near-normal lows. January 2014 was the second warmest January on record for both Bakersfield and Fresno.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Weather spotter reported several cloud to ground lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A single cloud to ground lightning strike in the Manayunk section of Philadelphia damaged a transformer and nearby windows.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A single cloud-to-ground lightning strike struck and caused a transformer explosion on Hermit Street in the Manayunk section of Philadelphia. The concussive force of the transformer explosion damaged the windows of at least six homes in the area. One home suffered damage to a dozen windows. The vibrations from the explosion were felt up to one mile away. No serious injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: One round of thunderstorms affected western Arkansas during the morning of the 24th. These thunderstorms moved eastward into eastern Arkansas by afternoon.  Another round of storms developed in western Arkansas during the afternoon and moved to the southeast, exiting the state by late evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Six workers were injured by lightning at a gas well drilling site near Fairview Rd. and Herring Rd. They were all taken to the hospital, but the injuries were not believed to be life-threatening. Radar and lightning data indicated that one storm had moved through the area and had moved away, then a second storm moved into the area and produced the lightning that injured the workers. Both of the storms produced only a small number of cloud-to-ground lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level system moving across the region led to the development of numerous severe thunderstorms across northeast Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours of July 8th. With a tremendous favorable atmospheric wind pattern present, severe thunderstorms resulted in widespread wind damage along with several tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper level wave moved into central New York and resulted in strong thunderstorms that produced copious amounts of hail. One severe thunderstorm produced quarter-sized hail Thursday morning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a structural fire that was confined to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A push of monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a tree fire and also struck a power pole, causing a power outage which, along with the rain, contributed to a multi-vehicle accident which injured one person (indirect).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unstable air was situated over the region south of a warm front and east of an approaching cold front. Showers and storms developed during the late afternoon and continued into the nighttime. A couple of storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and damaged portions of a house along Highway 150 about 0.7 miles east of the intersection with Turner Road. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A powerful upper level storm system moved across the region from April 28 into April 29, producing widespread showers and thunderstorms across Middle Tennessee. Several rounds of showers and storms moved across the region throughout the day on April 28, and again late in the day on April 29. Numerous reports of wind damage, flash flooding, large hail, and even one tornado were received from these storms. CoCoRaHS rainfall measurements over these two days ranged from 4 to 6 inches in parts of southwest Middle Tennessee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning on Lewisburg Pike at Lumsden Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system that developed along a frontal boundary helped produce clusters of showers and some strong to locally severe thunderstorms that moved through southern New Jersey during the early morning of the 19th. A couple of homes were also struck by lightning. Approximately 4,500 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes occurred in the Mount Holly warning and forecast area as the thunderstorms moved through. Over 3,000 homes and businesses lost power in the southern half of the state. This ended the brief hot spell across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and damaged a Jersey Central Power and Light transmission line in the Titusville section of  Hopewell township. About 1,000 of its customers were without power for about twelve hours until the line was repaired.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak front was situated over north central Georgia early in the morning on the 11th.  A weak area of low pressure developed along the front during the day, triggering several showers and thunderstorms.  Lightning struck and injured a woman in Lumpkin County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Lumpkin County Emergency Manager reported that a woman was struck by lightning while trimming hedges at a location off Crawford Falls Road off GA Highway 9.  The woman was transported to the hospital and died as a result of her injuries on July 15, 2014.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of lines of strong to severe thunderstorms triggered by another lee side trough moved through New Jersey during the afternoon and evening of the 14th. This line not only caused wind and lightning damage, but also caused flash flooding. The greatest impact by the thunderstorms was across the central third of New Jersey. About 30,000 homes and businesses lost power throughout the state with the greatest outages also in the central third of the state. Power was not fully restored until the 16th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Jackson Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning thunderstorms from a weak upper level disturbance produced lightning strikes that damaged several structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike set a palm tree on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon sea breeze boundary collisions combined with cool air aloft, allowed for the development of severe thunderstorms that produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local newspaper relayed a report of a lightning strike to a home in the Villages. The home sustained substantial damage. No one was home when the strike occurred and no injuries or fatalities resulted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cut-off low pressure area formed over the southeast states producing scattered showers and thunderstorms over South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported a groundskeeper was struck and injured by a lightning strike in Coral Gables. The 56-year-old man was found unconscious and in cardiac arrest and a defibrillator was used to restore his pulse and breathing. He had burn marks on his clothes but was responsive and talking upon arrival at the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front draped across central portions of North Texas served as a focus for thunderstorm development on Tuesday afternoon. Meanwhile a second thunderstorm complex advanced from the northwest. Several thunderstorms became severe, namely in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, with damaging winds being the primary occurrence. Flash flooding also occurred in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Much of the western portions of Fort Worth were flooded by flash flood waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire on San Andres Drive in Frisco. The estimated loss was $500,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms formed along an old outflow boundary and tracked to the south across the forecast area. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church in Hoyleton, Illinois at approximately midnight.  The fire smoldered in the rafters for several hours before erupting into flames.  The fire department was not called til around 2 am.  Most of the damage was confined to the attic and bell tower, rest of the building sustained major water damage.  No one was in building at the time and no injuries were reported.  The building is considered a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very unstable atmosphere, numerous shortwaves/outflows and plenty of moisture, so storms developed across the area.  Some of the storms produced severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Woodmere Trail Court around 802 pm on June 21st.  It smoldered for several hours. It became fully engulfed in flames by 2 am and that is when it was noticed by neighbors and they called 911.  The family that lives there was out of town for the weekend.  So no injuries reported.  The house was destroyed and damage was estimated around $487,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous strong to severe thunderstorms moved into and developed over the North Carolina mountains during the evening ahead of an unusually strong mid-Summer cold front. Many of the storms exhibited characteristics more typical of organized storms seen in the Spring. While wind damage was the primary impact from the storms, a few instances of large hail were observed. One man was killed when a tree fell on his vehicle near Cherokee.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported lightning struck a barn near the intersection of antioch road and anthony drive, resulting in a significant structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in Beaumont which fell on a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in North Beaumont which then fell on a house damaging the kitchen. Three people were inside the home when the tree fell, but no one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal squall line moved across northeast Florida during the afternoon and early evening hours. A few strong to severe storms produced wind damage, hail as well as funnel clouds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Julington Creek which damaged the fireplace and removed tile from the fireplace wall. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data and the estimated cost of damage is likely inaccurate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving across New York and New England triggered a few showers and thunderstorms across western Massachusetts.  Some tree damage resulted and one house was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Cornell Street, resulting in minor shingle damage and fire damage to the exterior of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level trough moved into the Southern Plains during the afternoon of April 27th.  Strong surface heating resulted in a large amount of instability across the region along and ahead of a dryline which pulled up stationary along or just east of the I-35 corridor of North Central Texas into Central Oklahoma.  Initially...the atmosphere was capped through much of the day but by late afternoon into the evening hours of April 27th...this cap was broken.  Strong upper level shear resulted in the development of supercell thunderstorms along the dryline and these thunderstorms moved eastward into the region.  Large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts were the primary result of these thunderstorms across Northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning ignited a gas well on FM. 95 between Mount Enterprise and Garrison, Texas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front was positioned west-northwest to east-southeast to the south of Iowa.  An upper level disturbance moved into the area as the low level jet increased during the early morning hours of the 20th.  During the pre-dawn hours, the low level jet increased to 35 to 40 kts.  The airmass was unstable with about 2000 J/kg of elevated CAPE available.  CAPE in the -10 to -30 C layer of the atmosphere was near 600 J/kg.  Thunderstorms formed north of the warm front.  A few of them became severe and produced large hail.  Quarter to golf ball size hail fell in Dallas and Polk Counties.  The largest hail fell in De Soto in Dallas County where golf ball size hail was reported.  A car was struck by lightning as a man was driving to work on Iowa Highway 5.  The man was not injured, but about $15,000 in damage occurred to the car.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was struck by lightning as the occupant was driving to work.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unstable airmass was in place across Iowa with afternoon highs reaching well into the 80s, and dewpoint readings in the low to mid 70s.  CAPE rose to 2000 to 3000 J/kg.  Downdraft CAPE was around 900 to 1000 J/kg, with CAPE in the -10 to -30 C layer of the atmosphere in the 600 to 900 J/kg range.  Precipitable water increased to around 1.75 inches.  The freezing level was quite high at around 15,000 feet.  Fairly strong shear was present with 40 to 50 kts of effective shear by late afternoon.  A line of thunderstorms formed ahead of the cold front by late afternoon and moved east across the state through the evening hours.  Hail with the storms was generally quite small.  One inch diameter hail fell in Crawford County in Dow City.  The primary severe events from this system were high winds that occurred as the MCS progressed across the state.  Several locations reported gusts of 60 MPH or higher.  An 80 MPH gust was reported in Guthrie County at Yale and Bayard.  A 71 MPH wind gust occurred in Marion County.  Heavy rainfall was also of significance with flash flooding in Crawford County.  This was caused by a dam failure which flooded Highway 39.  Three inches of rain fell in 50 minutes in Dallas County.  There were numerous reports of around 2 inches of rain falling in Boone and Polk Counties.  Water ponding and low-land flooding was common.  One person was struck by lightning at the Denison Airport.  The person received minor injuries. Funnel clouds were sighted in both Crawford and Boone Counties.  Additional heavy rainfall events are included on 01 September 2014 entry.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person was injured at the airport by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours of the 8th, along a nearly stationary frontal boundary extending across the area. A few of the stronger storms produced large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of disturbances propagating along a stationary frontal boundary resulted in widespread heavy rainfall across parts of northwestern Arkansas. Flash flooding occurred across some areas as a result of the heavy rainfall. An isolated storm also produce strong winds at the Fort Smith Regional Airport.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and injured a 43 year old man, who was taken to the hospital due to his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early season subtropical moisture and daytime heating resulted in scattered afternoon thunderstorms over the mountains of southwest Colorado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two ultramarathon runners from Canada were struck by lightning on Handies Peak at about the 14,050 foot level while competing in the 100-mile Handrock Endurance Run.  Both men incurred minor injuries.  The headlamp of one runner exploded when struck by the lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and humid air mass was in place over the region on Thursday, July 3rd.  As a strong cold front approached from the west, a broken line of thunderstorms developed over central New York and moved eastward during the afternoon hours.  Aided by powerful winds aloft, the storms moved from west to east over the region between the late afternoon and early evening hours.  Many of the storms produced strong winds, causing damage to trees and power lines over much of the region.  The most concentrated damage occurred from one particularly severe thunderstorm, which caused intense damage between West Winfield in Herkimer County towards Minden in Montgomery County.  A National Weather Service Storm Survey determined a series of microbursts produced wind damage up to 100 MPH in these areas.  A few of the storms also produced large hail as well.||As the cold front moved through the area by later in the evening, the storms moved east of the region and the threat for severe weather ended.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was reported to have caused a fire to a home at 14 Temple Street in Gloversville.  The home's roof sustained heavy damage as a result of the fire. Most of the top section of the house was also destroyed, although firefighters were able to prevent it from spreading to other houses.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very moist and humid air mass was in place across the region on Wednesday, June 25th. As a slow moving cold front approached from the west, bands of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the boundary. As these showers and thunderstorms repeatedly passed over the same locations, the heavy rainfall led to significant runoff, which caused flash flooding in some areas. Many roads were closed due to the flooding and some homes were affected by water as well. In addition, a few of the storms produced damaging lightning strikes as well. ||The threat for heavy rainfall and flooding ended late on the evening of June 25th, as the storm's cold front passed through the region from west to east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike downed a tree on Route 43 (Water Street) in Williamstown.  The road was briefly closed as a result of the downed tree, which had to be removed.  The local utility company reported 239 customers without power in the town.

Many roads were closed due to the flooding and some homes were affected by water as well.  In addition, a few of the storms produced wind damage to trees and some damaging lightning strikes.  ||The threat for heavy rainfall and flooding ended late on the evening of June 25th, as the storm's cold front passed through the region from west to east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a transformer to explode at the intersection of State Route 22 and State Route 71 in the town of Hillsdale.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very moist and humid air mass was in place across the region on Wednesday, June 25th.  As a slow moving cold front approached from the west, bands of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the boundary.  As these showers and thunderstorms repeatedly passed over the same locations, the heavy rainfall led to significant runoff, which caused flash flooding in some areas.  Many roads were closed due to the flooding and some homes were affected by water as well.  In addition, a few of the storms produced wind damage to trees and some damaging lightning strikes.  ||The threat for heavy rainfall and flooding ended late on the evening of June 25th, as the storm's cold front passed through the region from west to east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a transformer to explode at the intersection of State Route 66 and Water Street in the town of Ghent.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms rolled across southeast Minnesota during the afternoon of August 4th. A lightning strike from one of these storms hit a transformer in La Crescent (Houston County). The damage from the strike was enough to make a nearby substation unrepairable causing around 3,400 customers to be without power until the following day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a transformer in La Crescent and the resulting damage also took out a nearby substation. Around 3,400 customers were without power until the next day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm southerly flow allowed for temperatures to reach well into the 80s to near 90 on Wednesday, July 2nd.  In addition, it was rather humid with dewpoints nearing 70 degrees.  With the warm and humid conditions in place, the atmosphere became quite unstable during the afternoon and evening hours.||Well ahead of a cold front, a surface trough was in place across upstate New York.  This caused thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon hours.  Many of these storms became severe, producing wind damage to trees and power lines.  A few storms also contained large hail.  In addition, the very humid air mass in place gave the storms the capability of producing very heavy rainfall in a short period of time.  This allowed for a few of the storms to produce flash flooding in urban areas, such as around the Capital Region.  ||In addition, these storms produced a significant amount of cloud to ground lightning.  Several highway employees were struck by lightning in Rotterdam during a thunderstorm, but luckily escaped serious injury.  ||Although most of the storm ended by the late afternoon hours, a few additional severe storms during during the evening across the western Adirondacks and western Mohawk Valley.  These storms ended by the late evening hours, as nocturnal influences helped wane the development of additional thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An unoccupied barn at 251 Alcove Road in Coeymans Hollow was struck by lightning.  The barn burned down as a result of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced lightning damage across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a fire which produced extensive structural damage to a house on Castle Haven Road in Cambridge.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of elevated thunderstorms developed during the morning of the 20th over the ocean and along the coast ahead of an approaching upper-level low. Dynamic lift and monsoonal moisture led to further destabilization and increasing storm intensity with time. The initial band moved inland and organized thunderstorms with prolific lightning persisted over the Inland Empire and Riverside County mountains. The coastal and valley locations of San Diego and Riverside Counties received anywhere from a few hundredths of an inch of rain to one-half of an inch, with the greatest amounts in the Inland Empire and northern San Diego County valleys. The upper low moved across San Diego and Imperial Counties on the 21st, producing intense thunderstorms over the mountains and deserts, as well as a significant dust storm that moved up the Coachella Valley. The mountain locations of San Diego and Riverside Counties received up to one-half of an inch of rain, while the San Diego County deserts received up to 1.30 inches. One-inch hail was reported with thunderstorms in Nuevo and Mount Laguna/Pine Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A spotter reported lightning struck and ignited fires in two palm trees near the community college. The fires were put out. Lightning also struck the technology building on campus, knocking out power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced lightning damage across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a fire which produced electrical damage to an apartment on Willis Street in Cambridge.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm in advance of a cold front produced lightning damage across portions of northeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire in Corolla.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced damaging winds and heavy rain which caused some minor flooding across portions of central, south central, and southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a church fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms dropped southeast across northern Illinois during the evening of June 18th producing marginally severe winds and hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire to a residence in unincorporated St Charles.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms dropped across northern Illinois producing damaging winds and heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire in the attic on Ned Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms dropped southeast across northern Illinois during the evening of June 18th producing marginally severe winds and hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Seneca Drive in unincorporated Wheaton sparking a fire and causing extensive damage.  It is believed that a second lightning strike hit near an aerial truck that three fire fighters were working on causing minor injuries to the fire fighters who were treated and released from the hospital a few hours later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms dropped southeast across northern Illinois during the evening of June 18th producing marginally severe winds and hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on East Weathersfield Way resulting in a fire that caused moderate damage.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Extensive damage was sustained from two separate lines of thunderstorms on Monday, June 30th which was officially determined to be from two separate derecho events from Central Iowa east into Michigan and Ohio. Thunderstorms developed over Iowa during the early afternoon and organized into a forward-propagating quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) and tracked to southern Lake Michigan by early to mid evening. Meanwhile, a second complex of intense thunderstorms developed over central and eastern Iowa and also evolved into a QLCS, tracking across northern Illinois and northwest Indiana late in the evening into the overnight hours. ||Across northern Illinois and northwest Indiana, the first derecho event produced scattered straight-line wind damage, with gusts measured as high as 70 MPH.  The second derecho produced far more extensive damage, with 80 to 90 MPH straight line winds and numerous tornadoes.  Initial post-event surveys cataloged 18 tornadoes across northern Illinois and northwest Indiana, 17 of EF1 intensity and one of EF0 intensity.  Of these 18 tornadoes, 14 were associated with a pair of large mesovortices that traveled along the Kankakee River Valley in Kankakee County, Illinois and Lake, Newton, and Jasper Counties in Indiana.  ||Analysis of Google Earth satellite imagery gathered in spring of 2015 showed numerous additional areas of damage not documented in the original survey efforts.  A thorough analysis of this imagery and synthesis with the original survey information led to a complete reanalysis of the Kankakee Valley tornadoes.  Ultimately, 18 tornado tracks were identified alone in the Kankakee Valley, leading to a total of 22 tornadoes for northern Illinois and northwest Indiana. Of the 18 revised tornadoes, 16 of the paths were determined, in part, using satellite imagery. Further re-examination of the damage also led to a change in rating for several of the damage locations. Of the 18 reanalyzed Kankakee Valley tracks, two were rated EF2, 13 were rated EF1, and three were rated EF0. Additional details on this reanalysis, including the methods used, can be found in the Electronic Journal of Severe Storms Meteorology (Lyza et al. 2019, ���A Multi-Platform Reanalysis of the Kankakee Valley Tornado Cluster on 30 June 2014���).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Schillinger Court caught fire after it was struck by lightning.  The home was deemed uninhabitable due to the damage.
