EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across the northern New York and Vermont during the afternoon of September 9th and developed a broken line of showers and thunderstorms. One isolated thunderstorm was briefly strong enough to produce very localized wind damage in the form of some downed trees in the town of Derby Line in Orleans county Vermont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in North Troy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected much of Middle Tennessee throughout the day on September 14. One report of lightning damage was received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained spotter reported that lightning struck the Iglesia de Cristo Grandview Church on Nolensville Road just south of I-440. Extensive electrical damage occurred to the interior of the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary near the north Alabama area was the focusing mechanism for the development of afternoon to a few strong to severe storms in north central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home near McMullen Cove, off of Little Cove Road at Oakshire Place in southeast Madison county, was struck by lightning with the home declared a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a house on fire in Youngsville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Revere Drive was struck by lightning and caught on fire. All occupants of the home escaped with no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the Missouri Ozarks and developed a few severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man died after being hit by lightning near Seymour. Two horses were also killed by the lightning strike. The man was cultivating a field at the time of the strike. Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front combined with a remnant of an elevated mixed layer (EML) and a significant amount of deep layer shear and instability to produce showers and thunderstorms across southern New England. Many of these thunderstorms became severe, producing strong to damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A utility pole was struck by lightning on North Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active west coast sea breeze merged with the east coast sea breeze and produced numerous thunderstorms over Brevard County. A lightning strike from one of the storms sparked a fire that ultimately destroyed a home in Viera.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Viera, causing a fire to break out that eventually destroyed the residence. A resident who was home at the time reported hearing a large crack of thunder and eventually smelled smoke coming from the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent showers and thunderstorms occurred over the northeastern counties of North Texas where a weak upper level trough was located. The heavy rainfall resulted in some flash flooding north to east of DFW.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was reported on Chaparral Trot in Collin County around 8 am local time. Local fire officials stated lightning hit the peak of the roof sparking a fire in the attic of a two-story home. Fire damage was incurred in the attic and smoke and water damage plagued the rest of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary and a low pressure system moving along it combined to develop thunderstorms that produced damaging wind gusts, large hail and some flash flooding mainly across the northern half of Delaware during the late afternoon and evening of June 1st. As both the low pressure system and frontal boundary sagged southeast, the severe and heavy rain threat ceased.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a Brookside Park house on Marlin Drive. It sparked a fire that caused about $30,000 in damage to the home and rendered it uninhabitable.  The family of four were not injured and were assisted by the Red Cross in finding emergency shelter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning fatality occurred during a round of early morning sub severe storms. A woman was out walking her 2 dogs when lightning struck her and her dogs just outside her home. The dogs died instantly, while she passed away several days later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was out walking her 2 dogs when lightning struck her and her dogs just outside her home. The dogs died instantly, while she passed away several days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike drove a couple out of their home in the south Seattle suburb of Federal Way. ||The lightning late Wednesday afternoon hit a tree in the elderly couple���s front yard and traveled through the root system to the home. The lightning blew out drywall in the house, damaged the gutters and caused a gas line to rupture.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike drove a couple out of their home in the south Seattle suburb of Federal Way.||The lightning late Wednesday afternoon hit a tree in the elderly couple���s front yard and traveled through the root system to the home. The lightning blew out drywall in the house, damaged the gutters and caused a gas line to rupture.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent showers and thunderstorms occurred over the northeastern counties of North Texas where a weak upper level trough was located. The heavy rainfall resulted in some flash flooding north to east of DFW.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was reported on Windmill Hill Lane in DeSoto around 3 pm local time. According to the DeSoto Fire chief, lightning struck the home and caused about $500,000 in damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough meandered over southeast Georgia with a prevailing WSW flow in place. An unstable environment combined with forcing from the sea breezes and the trough produced scattered severe storms in the afternoon with wet downbursts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a semi tractor which caused a brief fire along Interstate 75 near mile marker 364. The time and location are approximate. The cost of damage was unknown but estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary and a low pressure system moving along it combined to develop thunderstorms that produced some damaging winds as well as hail and heavy rain across the Eastern Shore during the late afternoon and early evening of June 1st.  A couple of lightning strikes also caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and damaged a truck on Hambleton Creek Lane in Kingstown. No injuries occurred to the occupants.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms quickly developed across southwest Florida during the afternoon hours. Numerous lightning strikes were observed with these storms, one of which produced a lightning strike which killed one roof worker while injuring another.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men working on a roof were struck by lightning. They stopped working when it began to rain but returned shortly after the rain had stopped. Neighbors said that the lightning strike hit a roofer directly in the head ��� knocking him unconscious. That bolt then transferred to another worker who was just steps away. They were transferred to a local hospital to be treated for their injuries. The man who was struck directly died from his injuries three days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A nearly stationary frontal boundary and a low pressure system moving along it combined to develop thunderstorms that produced some damaging winds as well as hail and heavy rain across the Eastern Shore during the late afternoon and early evening of June 1st.  A couple of lightning strikes also caused damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer on Burchard Sawmill Road and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon over Pinellas County as the sea breeze circulation setup. A lightning strike from one of these storms caused minor damage to a residence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas County Fire and Rescue reported that lightning caused minor damge to a residence in St. Petersburg.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with bands of northeastward moving thunderstorms. Weak to moderate instability and deep, unidirectional southwesterly flow aloft helped to maintain the storms. A 500 mb shortwave trough over the Ozarks moved northeast to the vicinity of the Ohio and Mississippi River confluence by mid-afternoon. A weak surface low pressure center moved northeast from southeast Missouri into south central Illinois.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a small fire at a dealership.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In spite of a cold front clearing the state by the middle of the morning on the 6th, there was still sufficient instability aloft to trigger scattered thunderstorms into the early afternoon across far southern New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at a Middle Township home. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms with intense lightning developed in a broad southerly flow of warm and humid air. Lightning struck a house near Paducah.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in a neighborhood just southeast of the Paducah city limits. The resulting house fire caused extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong afternoon heating and a very moist airmass combined to produce a very unstable atmosphere by the afternoon of the 24th. A weak cold front and an outflow boundary from strong overnight storms across the Tennessee Valley pushed south into the state resulting in widespread strong to severe thunderstorms. Numerous reports of damaging thunderstorm winds and large hail were received, initially across North Georgia, during the afternoon and early evening before moving into portions of Central Georgia during the evening. Heavy rain associated with one severe thunderstorm produced isolated flash flooding in western portions of Gwinnett County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Gwinnett County Emergency Manager reported a nursing home fire caused by lightning on Club Drive in Lawrenceville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms rumbled across northern and western portions of north Texas on May 6. Lightning from one storm caused a house fire in Lewisville, TX.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the 1300 block of Saddleback Lane in Lewisville, TX, damaging the home and destroying 2 cars in the garage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms producing some wind damage, small hail, and eventually flash flooding moved into the western county warning area in the late morning hours. The system intensified and expanded in coverage as it progressed eastward through the afternoon hours resulting in flash flooding for much of the area. The system exited during the late evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a power outage affecting several hundred residents in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A woman was injured while standing on a porch when lightning struck a nearby tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was struck by lightning while standing on the porch of her mobile home on Rustic Lane in Marlborough when lightning struck a tree about 10 feet away. The bolt then traveled down the tree and jumped onto the porch, hitting the woman.  Her young son who was standing next to her was uninjured.  Both were taken by ambulance to a nearby hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were struck by Lightning in Denmark.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were injured when lightning apparently struck the house they were about to enter.  Firefighters were called to a home on Route 160 after a lightning strike knocked down power lines, which fell onto a car with the car���s owner inside it.  Denmark firefighters managed to rescue the man from his car. As a firefighter helped the man up the stairs to his home to wait for paramedics, a second lightning strike hit an antenna on the metal roof of the house. The firefighter and homeowner suffered indirect lightning hits. Both were treated and released from a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning slow moving thunderstorm produced some wind damage and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An oil storage tank truck was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Despite a persistent upper-level ridge over the region, strong afternoon heating resulted in very unstable atmospheric conditions. Scattered to numerous reports of damaging thunderstorm winds were received during the afternoon and evening of the 17th and 18th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An Atlanta television news station reported significant damage to a home on Timberloch Court in Snellville due to a fire initiated by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved south out of the Texas panhandle on May 6th, and was draped across north Texas on the 7th and 8th. The front stalled across the northwestern sections of north Texas and combined to produce severe thunderstorms including large hail, tornadoes, and flash flooding. Flash flooding across Cooke County caused significant impacts, including a late night train derailment.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was likely the cause of a fire that destroyed a 257,000 dollar home in the 10900 block of Rolling Hills Drive.  When firefighters arrived, heavy fire was already visible from the rooftop and the house was declared a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed during the afternoon along a front and strong temperature contrast across southern West Virginia.  A few had downpours with local rain of 1 to 1.5 inches in an hour.  After a dry month of May most areas needed the rain.  However, a downpour in the city of Beckley caused poor drainage street flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near where 3 teenage boys were fishing on a small residential pond.  The location is off of Elverton Road and near the Bridge Haven Golf Course. ||One boy died, the 2 others were injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a warm, moist, and slightly unstable air mass that was in place across northwestern Arkansas. No severe weather occurred but a young man was killed by lightning on Beaver Lake in Benton County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were on a boat fishing when it was struck by lightning. One of the three people died from the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep moisture and weak southwest flow led to morning showers and storms over the coast that moved in towards the coast. A lightning strike from one of these storms sparked a house fire in Lakewood Ranch.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that a fire at a house in Lakewood Ranch was apparently sparked by a lightning strike. Damages were expected to exceed $100,000. Time was estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved through the Florida peninsula during the afternoon and early evening hours. A lightning strike from one of these storms damaged a drinking water facility in Inverness.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Florida Division of Emergency Management relayed a report of a water treatment facility in Inverness that was damaged by a lightning strike, disrupting the drinking water supply to the town. As a result, a boil water notice went into effect and was not lifted until July 20th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front produced areas of thunderstorms with large hail up to the size of quarters and frequent lightning.  One person was killed and another injured by lightning in Muscatine County.  Heavy rain also was common.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Muscatine County Emergency Manager reported a male, age 36, was struck by lightning and killed while riding a horse.  Another male, age 25, was injured.  The horse was also killed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable environment caused scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Aqualane Shores Neighborhood in Naples around 6 PM EDT. Fire-Rescue crews reported heavy smoke and fire coming out of the attic of the two-story house. It took crews close to three hours to extinguish the fire. The house sustained very heavy fire, smoke, heat and water damages with the losses estimated at close to $2 million dollars when factoring both structural and content losses. A firefighter was injured when a section of ceiling collapsed on the second floor, knocking him to the ground and causing shoulder and back injuries. He was transported to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northeast to southwest oriented line of thunderstorms moved east-southeast from west-central Indiana into central Indiana during the morning hours of June 25th. These storms produced a singular wind damage and small hail report. North of these thunderstorms was a large shield of rain caused some flash flooding across northern portions of central Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WTHR reports that a lightning strike around 5:30 AM EDT Thursday is believed to be the cause of a house fire in the 5700 block of North Peppereel Way in McCordsville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms that produced damaging winds, large hail and a tornado affected Eastern Pennsylvania from the middle of the afternoon into the early evening on the 30th. Hardest hit were the Lehigh Valley which experienced a strong microburst and Chester County which experienced a tornado. A state of emergency was declared in Whitehall Township (Lehigh County).  Pennsylvania Power and Light reported about 11,000 of its customers lost power in the Lehigh Valley. Hardest hit by power outages included Whitehall and Catasauqua in Lehigh County and Hanover Township east through Lower Nazareth Township in Northampton County.  First Energy reported 4,000 of its customers lost power in Northampton County. Power was not fully restored until the night of July 1st. Heavy rain also caused some flash flooding in the Lehigh Valley and Poconos.  The most severe thunderstorms formed near a warm frontal boundary that slowly lifted northeast on the 30th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged a home's chimney on Orchard Avenue in Folsom Borough. The bricks fell to the ground, but there were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably warm and moist air mass in advance of a strong late spring cold front ignited scattered thunderstorms across southeast West Virginia. Lightning from one of the storms struck a power pole near Frankford and set it on fire, resulting in power outages for the surrounding area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained storm spotter relayed a report of lightning striking a power pole on U.S. 219 in Frankford.  The lightning set the power pole on fire.  Power was out to a large surrounding area for up to three hours as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms producing very heavy downpours and damaging winds developed over the eastern Edwards Plateau during the afternoon. The storms quickly became strong to severe as they moved over the Hill Country and the Interstate 35 corridor including metro Austin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 3000 block of Palominos Pass near Cedar Park causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across the area and produced frequent lightning. A girl playing volley was struck and later passed away from her injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 12 year old girl playing volleyball on Fort Morgan. There were 7 other near her that were affected by the closeness of the strike. However, only the girl was transported to the hospital. She passed away two days later from her injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms moved through the area. A lightning strike from one storm caused a fire to house in Mulberry.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported on a home in Mulberry that was destroyed by a fire on the 26th that was believed to be caused be a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An MCS rolled through northern Iowa in the AM hours bringing with it numerous reports of high/damaging winds and some hail. The damaging winds brought down large tree limbs, power lines, large trees and damaged chicken and hog facilities. Lightning struck a house in Kossuth County damaging the chimney.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Public reported lightning struck a house and destroyed the chimney.  Photo came from the KCCI ulocal page and time radar estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A passing shortwave disturbance initialized clusters of coastal county thunderstorms that produced severe wind gusts and street flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Evening storms produced lightning that damaged a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house that started a fire on White Rd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the central Black Hills and produced large hail near Silver City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building and started a fire, causing considerable damage. Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe storms developed across the area during the afternoon. This was aided by instability from daytime heating along with various outflow boundaries combined with a moist air mass. The severe storms had produced damage in the form of blown down trees and power lines. There were also some isolated events of hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning on Jimmy Jackson Circle.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed within an upper level trough that was moving across the region ahead of a cold front. One thunderstorm produced damaging winds in Hurst in Tarrant County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was reported around 8 pm local time in Flower Mound. The home was heavily damaged and likely caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep moisture and light flow produced early morning showers and thunderstorms along the Tampa Bay coast. A lightning strike from one of these storms ignited a fire in a condominium building. Thunderstorms later in the afternoon produced a brief lived tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that lightning struck an 8 unit condominium building, causing a small fire in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lee side trough coupled with an unseasonably warm air mass triggered scattered thunderstorms in Eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon on the 27th. A couple of the thunderstorms were severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 52-year-old man was struck by lightning while walking his dog. He was hospitalized, but was expected to survive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms on June 28th caused 3 injuries in St. Louis County.  A 51-year-old father and his 4-year-old daughter were struck and injured by lightning around 2 pm near a baseball field in Cherry, MN, which is near the Iron Range.  The father and daughter were watching the baseball game.  The game was delayed because of the thunderstorm, and the father and daughter were struck as they were walking back to their van.  The father suffered a heart attack and was in critical condition.  He was hospitalized for many days. A 12-year-old boy was critically injured after being struck by lightning at Enger Park Golf Course in Duluth.  The boy was a spectator at a tournament being held at the golf course.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 51-year-old father and his 4-year-old daughter were struck and injured by lightning around 2 pm near a baseball field in Cherry, MN, which is near the Iron Range. The father and daughter were watching the baseball game. The game was delayed because of the thunderstorm, and the father and daughter were struck as they were walking back to their van.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level shortwave trough moved around the longwave low over the Four Corners region. This upper distubance interacted with a surface boundary moving northward as a warm front from South Texas into a very moist airmass. This combination led to thunderstorms that produced heavy rain and isolated severe weather.  A historic flash flood occurred on the Blanco River late Saturday night into Sunday.  Hundreds of homes were destroyed along the river from the City of Blanco down into Wimberley and San Marcos.  The flood wave continued downstream for days affecting residents and homes along the San Marcos and Guadalupe Rivers.  Early estimates show damages in excess of 100 million dollars.  Several people lost their lives due to flash flooding.  A large tornado outbreak occurred this Saturday night producing numerous small brief tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole near the intersection of Lamar Blvd. and Breaker Ln. in Austin and power outages were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning associated with thunderstorms developing along the east coast sea breeze injured a boy fishing in the water at Daytona Beach Shores.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An eleven year old boy from Georgia was struck by lightning while fishing in the ocean in waist deep water. The boy was transported to a nearby hospital and admitted in serious condition. After several days in the hospital, he was released to a rehabilitation center and was recovering.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon sea breeze storms and cool temperatures aloft once again set the stage for strong to severe storms across the Florida Peninsula. One storm produced a lightning strike which caused minor damage to a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit the chimney of a home located on Farrier Trail in Clearwater. Upon arrival, firefighters had to make some small holes in the ceiling of the home to investigate if anything was on fire or not. No fire resulted from the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms on June 28th caused 3 injuries in St. Louis County.  A 51-year-old father and his 4-year-old daughter were struck and injured by lightning around 2 pm near a baseball field in Cherry, MN, which is near the Iron Range.  The father and daughter were watching the baseball game.  The game was delayed because of the thunderstorm, and the father and daughter were struck as they were walking back to their van.  The father suffered a heart attack and was in critical condition.  He was hospitalized for many days. A 12-year-old boy was critically injured after being struck by lightning at Enger Park Golf Course in Duluth.  The boy was a spectator at a tournament being held at the golf course.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 12-year-old boy was critically injured after being struck by lightning at Enger Park Golf Course in Duluth, near the fairway, at about 3:50 pm. The boy was a spectator at a tournament being held at the golf course.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning in Southeast Texas split a large tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A picture was received by KBMT of a large cedar tree being split by lightning in Port Neches.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved south out of the Texas panhandle on May 6th, and was draped across north Texas on the 7th and 8th. The front stalled across the northwestern sections of north Texas and combined to produce severe thunderstorms including large hail, tornadoes, and flash flooding. Flash flooding across Cooke County caused significant impacts, including a late night train derailment.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a group of oil tanks in a field near Whitesboro, TX causing them to explode and destroying all tanks on site.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over northern Volusia County along the east coast sea breeze. Lightning struck and killed a 25-year-old male in Port Orange as he worked outdoors.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 25-year-old male was struck and killed by lightning while working on the roof of a home in the Water's Edge subdivision of Port Orange.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm and unstable air mass brought a few rounds of severe thunderstorms to central Kentucky, starting during the evening hours Thursday June 25th. Isolated storms developed first, producing some sporadic wind damage. Then later that night, a complex of organized storms brought damaging winds, large hail and flash flooding during the early morning hours June 26th. Later that same afternoon, a strong surface low pressure moved across central Kentucky and brought another round of severe storms with damaging winds, large hail and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A broadcast meteorologist relayed a report to the NWS of a house struck by lightning. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slowly northward moving boundary/warm front was draped across the area throughout the day.  By the evening vigorous storms fired up just north of the boundary and continued as the low level jet began to pick up.  Numerous reports of large hail and damaging winds were reported. Fairly quickly after sunset, storms transitioned away from multi-cellular severe to training heavy rain producers over an area NW to SE roughly from Carroll to Bloomfield, including portions of the Des Moines metro.  Resulting rainfall totals exceeded 3 inches in many locations and a few eclipsing 5 and 6 inches.  Widespread flash flooding and eventually river flooding occurred across large portions of the area mentioned above. Precipitable water values were in the 1.5 to 2.2 inch range with the freezing level around 14 to 15 kft across the state throughout the event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Huxley area of Story County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough pushed through the northern plains with an associated cold front extending southward into the central plains. Storms fired along the front to the west of Iowa in the evening and developed into a large MCS as it moved into Iowa. An MCV and a large squall line moved through northern and central Iowa during the overnight hours producing strong, damaging winds and heavy rain. Four brief tornadoes also occurred in central Iowa along the leading edge of the squall line in an area of stronger shear and higher moisture. The tornadoes mainly damaged trees and crops, however one did strike a barn and silo in rural Boone County. Another damaged traffic signals and an Iowa DNR nursery in the Ames area of Story County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the early morning hours starting a fire in the garage and was soon fully engulfed in flames. The house was in a rural area of Polk County. The development also had no fire hydrants.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Daytime heating, outflow boundaries and gulf moisture combined to form a few severe thunderstorms and flash flooding across portions of central Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pasture and killed several horses near Jayess.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm in advance of a frontal boundary produced a lightning strike which injured two adults at Pocahontas Middle School in central Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two adults were struck by lightning and injured at Pocahontas Middle School.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The slow-moving upper level storm system responsible for isolated strong thunderstorms over New Mexico on the 14th edged closer to New Mexico on the 15th. A large subtropical moisture tap and associated upper level jet core ahead of this system moved northeast across eastern New Mexico during the late afternoon and evening hours. Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved northeast over the region, some of which became strong to severe. Quarter size hail was reported at Pep. Unfortunately, a woman traveling to Ruidoso from Albuquerque was struck by lightning while on a motorcycle east of Carrizozo. She died several days later in the hospital. Meanwhile, farther north, enough cold air with the approaching upper level storm system allowed snow to accumulate over the northern mountains. Many high elevation areas in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains reported 2 to 12 inches of wet snow, however impacts were limited due to the very high elevation and relatively warm surface temperatures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Kalina Jinzo, a 40-year mother of three, was struck by lightning and killed while traveling from Albuquerque to Ruidoso on a motorcycle on the 15th. Her husband was also struck but his injuries were not life threatening. The woman died several days later in a Lubbock hospital around the 22nd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike affected five people at a construction site in the northeast part of Colorado Springs.  No one was seriously injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Five men were struck by lightning at a construction site on the northeast side of Colorado Springs...suffering varying degrees of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of an approaching cold front, a warm and humid air mass was in place over northwestern Connecticut on Tuesday, May 19th.  As the cold front approached during the early evening hours, a few scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and moved from west to east across the region.  Some of the thunderstorms became severe, producing damaging winds to trees and power lines.  In addition, two of the thunderstorms produced damaging lightning strikes as well.  ||The threat for thunderstorms ended by the late evening hours, as the cold front passed through the region and drier air moved into the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at a home on Weed Road in Torrington during a thunderstorm.  Although firefighters were initially hampered due to the ongoing thunderstorm, they were able to contain the fire to the attic on the front side of the house.  They had the fire under control within in an hour and a half.  The family was able to go back into the home once the fire was put out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening as a strong upper level disturbance passed across the central Appalachians. Thunderstorm activity was especially enhanced due to strong surface convergence east of the Blue Ridge Mountains as high pressure in the low levels wedged southward from New England, providing easterly wind flow across the Piedmont, with southwesterly winds observed around 3000 feet above the surface.  Upper level ridging across the southeast and mid-Atlantic states supported strong surface heating, which allowed CAPE (Convective Available Potential Energy) values to exceed 2000J/Kg across much of the region.  Mid-level winds across the northern half of the forecast area increased to around 40 knots during the afternoon, aiding in storm organization, while deep tropical moisture across the region pooling ahead of the front aided in producing strong wind gusts due to increased precipitation loading in the downdrafts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike triggered a structure fire on Eggleston Falls Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and thunderstorms spread across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on June 26. A few reports of wind damage were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire occurred at 108 Gallagher Drive in Franklin due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure resided over southern Utah/northern Arizona with weak low pressure over west Texas. This created strong easterly flow over southeast Arizona, which increased to 25-30 kts. Thunderstorms produced large hail, and damaging winds across Santa Cruz and Pima Counties, including Tucson.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and ignited a small fire on the second story of a Sahuarita home.  The lightning also caused a water pipe to burst which subsequently led to ceiling damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe storms developed across the area during the afternoon. This was aided by instability from daytime heating along with various outflow boundaries combined with a moist air mass. The severe storms had produced damage in the form of blown down trees and power lines. There were also some isolated events of hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Jerry Drive was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed during the heat of the afternoon across portions of Central Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Laurelwood subdivision and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early morning squall line moved across northeast Iowa on June 22nd. This squall line produced winds of 60 to 70 mph and at least one tornado. The tornado destroyed one farm house near Maynard (Fayette County) causing injuries to both occupants of the house. Several other nearby farms sustained damage to crops, trees, and barns.  As the squall line moved across northeast Iowa it produced a swath of wind damage starting near Marble Rock (Floyd County) to around Guttenberg (Clayton County). Within this swath, a 65 mph wind gust was measured in Marble Rock that took down trees and power lines, around 17 farms sustained damage across southern Fayette County, and an Amish grocery store was destroyed near Garber (Clayton County). Preliminary damage estimates for Fayette County are in excess of $3 million. Locally heavy rains also produced some flash flooding with 480th Street washed out south of Stacyville (Floyd County) and Waterloo Creek came out of its banks near Dorchester (Allamakee County) within 30 minutes of the rain starting. The State of Iowa Governor issued a disaster proclamation for the following counties: Allamakee, Clayton, Howard, Mitchell and Winneshiek. A federal disaster declaration was made for Allamakee, Chickasaw, Clayton, Fayette, Howard, Mitchell and Winneshiek Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike took out the Decorah eagle web camera.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms produced hundreds of lightning strikes across the Tampa Bay Area during the late evening on Sunday. One lightning strike hit a house in Land O' Lakes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a house in Land O' Lakes and the subsequent fire caused the house to be a total loss. The fire caused the second story to collapse onto the first floor. The home was a vacation property and was vacant at the time so no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced areas of flash flooding on July 3, 2015. The hardest hit areas were Powell, Estill, and Laurel counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed a bull and four cows.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several upper level disturbances crossed the area in the southwesterly flow aloft. These combined with a moist and unstable environment to produce scattered convection, with some of the storms becoming severe. One of the storms produced a microburst, resulting in multiple downed trees and some minor property damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a fire in the attic of 10 Kings Mount Court causing moderate structural damage. Monetary damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure resided over southern Utah/northern Arizona with weak low pressure over west Texas. This created strong easterly flow over southeast Arizona, which increased to 25-30 kts. Thunderstorms produced large hail, and damaging winds across Santa Cruz and Pima Counties, including Tucson.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a man who was walking along a dirt road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A young man died and another was injured when they were struck by lightning at the Spearfish Canyon Disk Golf Course.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved southeast across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on June 29. A few reports of hail and wind damage were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning at 1208 Chickering Road which caused damage to plumbing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually late-season low pressure system combined with unusually early-season deep subtropical moisture to fuel scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Some storms produced flash flooding, and isolated wind damage also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a palm tree near Nellis and Sahara.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large thunderstorm complex developed within the warm sector of a low pressure system that tracked northeast across the St. Louis area. A deep southwesterly flow of tropical moisture provided fuel for the storms. Precipitable water values were approaching two inches. Isolated flash flooding occurred with the strongest and most persistent storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire that caused major damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A boundary was pushing through the state with ongoing convection through central Iowa through the day. As the boundary neared the area, the convection intensified and impacted central and southern Iowa in the evening to early morning hours. Two thunderstorm complexes moved through portions of central and southern Iowa with very heavy rainfall causing flash flooding. The severe thunderstorm complexes produced some hail but mainly strong damaging winds. Precipitable water values were near 2 inches in some areas with deep warm cloud depths during the event. This heavy rainfall further exacerbated conditions as some of the area had just received heavy rainfall in previous days. This led to some extended flooding for a few days and flooding on some area rivers. Several locations reported in excess of 4 inches of rain, while one location in Warren County reported over 7.50 inches of rainfall. The Emergency Manager for Marion County mentioned widespread reports of 8 to 10 inches with one report close to 12 inches of accumulated rainfall over the past few days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vehicle starting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front in the afternoon hours. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts as well as frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A member of the broadcast media reported power lines down on Fox Chase Road due to a tree being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two areas of thunderstorms, one moving north from Virginia and a second line moving east from the higher terrain of Maryland merged over central Maryland early on the 1st. This enhanced the strength of the thunderstorms, one of which remained severe as it crossed Chesapeake Bay.  The western thunderstorms formed ahead of an approaching cold front that moved through the Eastern Shore the middle of that evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a quarter acre wildfire in Stevensville. No property was damaged or injuries occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous eastward moving thunderstorm crossed central Florida during the afternoon. One storm became strong and produced some very localized wind damage in Tavares. Another storm produced lightning which struck and injured two women in Orlando.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two women were struck by lightning in advance of an approaching storm, as they were standing outdoors in the driveway of a home in Orlando. Doctors believe one woman sustained a direct strike to her head. She was transported to a hospital in serious condition, but was able to be released the following day. The second woman was struck indirectly and refused medical treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of strong thunderstorms developed within an inland trough of low pressure and moved southward across southeast South Carolina. These storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported a structure fire due to lightning in the 9 block area of Ashton Cove on Hilton Head Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of strong thunderstorms developed within an inland trough of low pressure and moved southward across southeast South Carolina. These storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported a structure fire caused by lightning in the 20 block area of Ironwood Circle.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of strong thunderstorms developed within an inland trough of low pressure and moved southward across southeast South Carolina. These storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported a structure fire due to lightning in the 600 block area of Dolphin Road on Fripp Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed after midnight following an afternoon where the atmosphere was sufficiently capped. Thunderstorms developed along mesoscale boundaries and produced damaging wind gusts and even some hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A member of the broadcast media relayed a report from the Fire Department of a house that was struck by lightning. Lightning hit the rear of the home and flames eventually came through the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike near Keaau on the Big Island of Hawaii took the roof off a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved across inland southeast Mississippi during the early evening. A lightning strike in Perry County resulted in significant impact to livestock.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Twenty-three cows, nine yearlings, and one bull were killed by a lightning strike Saturday evening in Richton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms in New Jersey during the afternoon and evening on the 21st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two New Jersey state troopers avoided serious injury after their cruiser was struck by lightning in Middle Township on the afternoon of the 21st on the Garden State Parkway near mile-marker 10.9 at a construction site. One officer was taken to the Atlantic City Medical Center. The other officer did not need additional medical attention.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms that formed along a lee side trough moved across eastern Pennsylvania during the evening of the 14th. The thunderstorms caused isolated wind and lightning damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike knocked a tree down onto wires in Lower Saucon Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms that moved through southeast New Jersey during the morning of the 15th caused a lightning fire in Cape May County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire in Seaville. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and thunderstorms spread west to east across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on June 8. Dozens of reports of large hail and wind damage were received, along with localized flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Asheford Trace in Antioch, damaging the upstairs and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of Wednesday, June 3rd, a complex of thunderstorms moved across central Minnesota. Local officials determined that lightning started a fire, and also damaged a gas meter. This occurred in the city of Rice, Minnesota.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local officials determined that lightning started a fire, and also damaged a gas meter in Rice, Minnesota. The damage was limited mostly to the exterior of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Eau Claire in the early morning hours of Monday, June 8th, and caused extensive damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours of Monday, June 8th, lightning struck a home in Eau Claire, Wisconsin. It caused extensive damage, but no one was hurt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: One thunderstorm produced damaging downburst winds and flash flooding in Dallas County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected lightning strike started a house fire near Hillcrest High School in Dallas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread showers and thunderstorms spread across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on June 26. A few reports of wind damage were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire occurred on Strathmore Drive in Franklin due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved southeast across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on June 29. A few reports of hail and wind damage were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house and transformer were struck by lightning at 550 Oak Road near Highway 127, west of Allardt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a remnant feeder band associated with the departing Tropical Depression Bill. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a downburst in Bell County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in the 3300 block of Christie Drive in Killeen.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak front was over south Georgia with prevailing WSW flow pushing the west coast sea breeze inland and triggering afternoon and evening storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A swimmer was indirectly struck by lightning along the 6000 block of A1A South, about 1 mile south of the Crescent Beach ramp. He was ankle deep in water when the event occurred. He was treated at the scene by county fire rescue, then transported to a Jacksonville hospital where he was in serious condition. The extent of injuries were unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two homes on the south side of the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) were damaged by fire after lightning struck a tree that was located between the two homes during a morning thunderstorm on July 24th. Several other homes sustained damage to their gas meters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree located between two homes on the south side of the city of La Crosse. Fires started in both homes from the lightning strike with moderate damage reported. Several other homes sustained damage to their gas meters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous upper-level disturbance tracking through the Upper Midwest interacted with an approaching cold front to trigger scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across central Illinois during the afternoon and evening of August 18th.  Due to increasing low-level wind shear, a number of the storms began to rotate and produce funnel clouds.  One storm produced a weak tornado in Tazewell County just east of Mackinaw.  Other cells created scattered damaging wind gusts of around 60 mph and hail as large as quarters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a mobile home to catch fire in Bartonville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms tracked across central Illinois during the early morning hours of August 19th.  One of the cells produced a lightning strike that caused a house fire in Springfield.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire in Springfield.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the midday hours over north central Alabama.  The line filled in as it moved east across the remainder of northeast Alabama.  Trees were knocked down in a couple locations in Madison County.  Lightning also struck at least two homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Wilshire Cove road, resulting in a fire that moderately damaged the residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and storms moved through the Tampa Bay area producing numerous lightning strikes. The lightning strikes were reported to have caused as many as three separate structure fires across Pinellas County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Florida Department of Emergency Management relayed reports of 3 separate residential structures that sustained lightning strikes. In each case, the fire department was called out to put out small fires. One unit of Lake Seminole Townhomes sustained major damages. In the other two cases, damages were minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving front caused multiple rounds of thunderstorms which led to severe weather and flash flooding across the Missouri Ozarks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a transformer which knocked out power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level ridge dominated over the SE with a surface ridge axis south of the forecast area with a mean layer SW flow in place. A weak surface trough was over south Georgia, and this feature combined with the sea breezes over an unstable and moist airmass produced scattered severe storms during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a mobile home fire. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Spotty thunderstorms developed with afternoon heating across portions of the central Appalachians.  Most of the thunderstorms were weak due to the lack of any upper level support.  However, cloud-to-ground lightning was observed which, in one case, struck a home, causing minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near the intersection of Anderson and Stonehouse Roads, causing minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze storms over an unstable airmass ignited a few strong to severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire after it struck at tree on Hub Bailey Road. The cost of damage was unknown, but estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze storms over an unstable airmass ignited a few strong to severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A small brush fire erupted due to a lightning strike. The fire was contained. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level over south Georgia pushed a dominate west coast sea breeze inland where it intersected the east coast sea breeze along the I-95 corridor in the late afternoon. Scattered severe storms with wet microbursts developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vacant structure in Reddick. The cost of damage was unknown, but was estimated for this event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from an isolated, pulse thunderstorm resulted in numerous injuries on Eglin Air Force Base during a training operation.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck near a battalion of Army Ranger Trainees on Eglin Air Force Base in southern Okaloosa County. Four instructors and 40 trainees were evaluated, and 20 (3 instructors and 17 students) were hospitalized overnight.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a man on a football field in Florence County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 19 year old male on a football field at Carver Elementary school.  He was resuscitated by the Florence City Fire Dept, and was transported to the local emergency room.  He was in serious but stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from an afternoon thunderstorm destroyed a home in Deer Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire that destroyed a home in Deer Park.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across Long Island, NY and raced toward Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts. These storms caused significant wind damage knocking down a significant number of trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Firefly Road, starting two electrical fires.  No one was injured but the house was severely damaged.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was most likely the cause of an apartment fire at the 9700 block of Southbrook Drive. The cost of damage was unknown but estimated for the event to be included in StormData.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe storms produced minor wind damage. A couple damaging lightning strikes also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree where a herd of cattle had taken shelter. The strike killed 11 of the cattle. The estimated loss was between 35 to 40 thousand dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated strong to severe storms produced minor wind damage. A couple damaging lightning strikes also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large home near Republic was destroyed by a fire which was started by a lightning strike. Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning showers and thunderstorms developed and moved very little for several hours resulting in flash flooding across parts of Galveston and Brazoria counties. Rainfall totals of 5 to 7 inches were common, and isolated totals did reach 10 inches in the Bayou Vista area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Light struck and caused a fire at an oil storage tank near Crystal Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level system moved through the Midwest region and produced a squall line of thunderstorms across the Missouri Ozarks. This squall line of storms produced numerous reports of wind damage and a few weak tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike at the Table Rock Dam damaged two of the four hydro-power generating units. These two units remained offline for about 30 days until repaired.  Each turbine unit would normally generate 50,000 Mwh of electricity. Power generated at the hydro-dam was decreased by half of normal capacity. Time was estimated by radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms, with some storms organizing into small clusters, developed across western North Carolina during early-to-mid-afternoon. A few of the storms produced severe weather in the form of damaging wind gusts, mainly over the foothills and Piedmont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Newspaper reported lightning ignited a fire that destroyed a large church on Highway 127 just north of Bethlehem. The structure was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: South to southwest steering flow pushed a more dominant west coast sea breeze inland through the early afternoon over a very unstable airmass which triggered scattered severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home along Avalon Cove Drive. Cost of damage unknown, but estimated for storm data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of weak disturbances aloft interacted with a very moist air mass and triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms. One of these storms resulted in some minor wind damage. Also, a lightning strike injured 18 soldiers during a training activity.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Eighteen soldiers were treated for injuries after lightning struck near where they were training. No soldier was directly struck, but they were taken to the hospital. Ten of the soldiers remained hospitalized overnight.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms associated with a larger cluster of storms advanced southeast through the region. A large number of trees were downed across the area, and some storms produced large hail during the late afternoon and early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was brought down by a lightning strike in King, NC. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms with heavy rain and frequent cloud to ground lightning started structural fires in Brunswick County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at 1806 Evangline Drive in Brunswick County.  The fire burned the entire roof of the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at a house in Surf City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire at 1601 South Shore Drive in Surf City.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread thunderstorm activity across Southern Arkansas during the morning hours of July 4th created a cold pool outflow boundary that moved from east to west across Northern Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours.  A few of these storms were strong to severe producing strong wind gusts and frequent cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at the Cypress Bend Park Resort on Toledo Bend in Sabine Parish around 7 pm on July 4th. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: July rounded out with another shot of monsoon moisture and thunderstorms as high pressure shifted back westward over the Four Corners on the 29th and 30th. The main drivers for storms were terrain and outflow boundary collisions. Scattered thunderstorms occurred mainly over the mountains and deserts with wide-ranging rainfall totals from a few tenths of an inch to locally over 2 inches. Flash flooding occurred in Idyllwild, Timoteo Canyon, Calimesa/Moreno Valley, along with water flowing in the Fish and Vallecito Creeks in Anza Borrego State Park. A few storms went severe, including quarter-sized hail and wind damage in Calimesa and wind damage from a microburst in Palm Desert.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: CHP reported a lightning strike that started a small fire near Interstate 8 and Kitchen Creek Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over interior South Florida and moved west to the greater Naples area during the early evening hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early-season monsoon pattern set up across the southwest U.S., bringing several days of enhanced mid-level moisture from the southeast and enough instability for scattered showers and thunderstorms for the last few days of the month. Scattered thunderstorms developed over the high desert east of the forecast area on the 28th and drifted west, producing lightning and some light rainfall amounts under one-quarter inch (Green Valley Lake won at 0.3 inches) over the San Jacinto Mountains and portions of southwest San Bernardino County, altogether a fairly small coverage area. The 29th saw thunderstorms trying to form over the southern San Diego County Mountains, but quickly dissipating without much effect as they drifted off the mountain crests. A disturbance moving through Baja on the 30th produced an active day of thunderstorms over southern California, reaching all the way to the coast with prolific lightning and rainfall for several areas. Lightning sparked a few small fires near Poway and La Mesa. A few reports of roadway flooding and mudslides came in from the Poway and Ramona areas that day. Amounts were mostly under one-tenth of an inch along the coast, one-tenth to one-half inch in the valleys, and up to three-quarters of an inch in the San Diego County mountains. Other mountain areas were largely missed by this event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: CHP reported lightning striking a wooden power pole with the pole catching on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon of January 3rd, a strong upper level low was moving through the central Plains and a cold front began to move into the region. Across the Lower Mississippi River Valley, peak heating and upper 60s to low 70s dewpoints contributed to decent instability in the developing warm sector in advance of the front. Strong low level wind shear and winds aloft were in place, which made a favorable environment for tornadoes. This helped to support widespread thunderstorms along with a few supercell storms.||A long lived, persistent, storm tracked across the southeastern counties (Lawrence, Jefferson Davis, Covington, Jasper and Lauderdale County) and produced eight tornadoes. Considerable damage occurred in Jasper County, north of Rose Hill, and also near Mount Olive in Covington County and Meehan and Bailey in Lauderdale County. Severe storms moved out of the region by early Saturday evening. The front slowly moved to the east through the area through the evening of January 3rd.||In addition to the severe storms and tornadoes, widespread flooding occurred in southeast Mississippi where 3-5 inches of rain fell. Record amounts of moisture for the month of January were observed in the evening weather balloon sounding at the Jackson International Airport, where precipitable water value of 1.74 inches tied the record last set on January 3, 1973. This led to widespread heavy rainfall and flooding. Water covered some roads and water was entering homes near Bay Springs, with one road washed out nearby.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire along Mississippi Highway 42 West.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from strong thunderstorms resulted in structural damage to a residence in Santa Rosa County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, resulting in roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surge of moisture and unstable air aloft (steep mid level lapse rates) created a favorable environment for strong to severe thunderstorms producing large hail as a weak cold front dropped southeast into the Tennessee Valley.  Although low level wind shear was relatively weak, mid to upper level shear sustained a few supercell thunderstorms that generated the largest hail up to golf ball sized.   The storms developed rapidly during the mid afternoon hours across northern Alabama ahead of the cold front.  As the evening wore on, new storms developed in far northwest Alabama right along the cold front.  These progressed southeast of the area before Midnight.  Unfortunately, one person was injured after being struck by lightning in their residence in Cullman County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 100 foot tower at the Lawrence county, Alabama emergency management/911 facility. EMA officials reported that there was damage to the tornado early warning system and 911 phone lines.

One of the storms became severe across Okaloosa County during the afternoon of June 27th, with lightning damage occurring in Santa Rosa County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a business off Homer Holland Rd. The business suffered smoke damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong seabreeze induced thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and persisted into the evening hours. Most stayed below severe thresholds but still produced some isolated gusty winds leading to some minor damage. One storm produced a lightning strike that hit a home in Pinellas County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas County 911 reported a possible lightning strike that caused a house fire in St. Petersburg. The fire caused damage to the roof of one home. The fire was put out by the homeowners. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure aloft across the southwest United States resulted in broad southwest flow aloft across the Southern Plains into the Lower Mississippi Valley.  Disturbances in this flow rounded the base of the trough and provided the lift necessary for widespread showers and thunderstorms across Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northern Louisiana.  A cold front was located across Northern Texas into Northern Louisiana.  Moderate surface instability coupled with strong deep layer shear allowed the storms that developed to produce strong and damaging wind gusts, large hail and excessive heavy rainfall across portions of Northeast Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Sheriff Office reported a fire to a home in the Cooks Crossing subdivision due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and embedded thunderstorms moved across northwestern Connecticut during the early morning hours of Tuesday, April 21st.  Although the thunderstorms weren't considered severe, cloud to ground lightning struck a home built in the 1800s in the town of Cornwall.  The lightning appeared to hit a nearby tree and then traveled through a trench into an addition on the home.  As a result of the strike, a fire occurred and much of the home was damaged before fire fighters could extinguish the fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike during an early morning thunderstorm struck a home.  The lightning initially hit a nearby tree, with the strike traveling through a trench and into an addition on the home.  A fire occurred, damaging much of the home.
