EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a house in Springfield on West Whiteside Street and caused minor damage to an inside wall of the house. The strike did not start a fire and the time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of strong to severe storms produced large hail and minor wind damage across southern Missouri. Training of storms with heavy rainfall over the same locations led to minor flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a house in the Stonebridge Resort community and caused a house fire. The fire completely destroyed the house and contents inside. There were three cars in the garage that were a total loss as well.  Time was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread severe thunderstorms from the late morning through the evening hours June 20th, produced large hail, damaging winds, and heavy rains.  In addition 4 tornadoes occurred.  One tornado resulted in 2 injuries when a house was destroyed.  Another person was injured by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Officials reported two power lines down and transformer on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surge of moisture and unstable air aloft (steep mid level lapse rates) created a favorable environment for strong to severe thunderstorms producing large hail as a weak cold front dropped southeast into the Tennessee Valley.  Although low level wind shear was relatively weak, mid to upper level shear sustained a few supercell thunderstorms that generated the largest hail up to golf ball sized.   The storms developed rapidly during the mid afternoon hours across northern Alabama ahead of the cold front.  As the evening wore on, new storms developed in far northwest Alabama right along the cold front.  These progressed southeast of the area before Midnight.  Unfortunately, one person was injured after being struck by lightning in their residence in Cullman County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 27 year old female was struck by lightning while leaning against a metal door frame. Victim was transported to a local hospital with non-life threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across South Florida with showers and severe thunderstorms ahead of the front. One of these severe thunderstorms spawned a tornado in Boca Raton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Broward County Sheriff's deputy who was directing traffic in Tamarac was injured after lightning struck a nearby utility box. The lightning struck an Florida Power & Light signal box at the corner of the intersection of University Drive and Southgate Boulevard and that transferred some residual electricity to the deputy.||The deputy felt a tingling and was transported to a nearby hospital for examination. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread severe thunderstorms from the late morning through the evening hours June 20th, produced large hail, damaging winds, and heavy rains.  In addition 4 tornadoes occurred.  One tornado resulted in 2 injuries when a house was destroyed.  Another person was injured by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 42 year old female was struck and killed by lightning while camping at the Pleasant Creek State Recreation Area near Palo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted through during the morning of the 2nd with only a few showers.  Rounds of showers and thunderstorms formed in the lower Ohio River Valley and moved quickly east into northeast Kentucky during the evening hours.  These rounds continued into the morning of the 3rd, before a lull in the early and mid afternoon.  Rain totals of 1.25 to 1.5 inches were common by midday on the 3rd.||Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms moved across during the evening hours. This was ahead of a low pressure wave along a strong cold front.  Dew points were in the upper 50s with temperatures in the low and mid 60s  The evening convection was elongated along the flow in Lawrence County with rain rates of a half inch to an inch in less than an hour.  The headwaters of the Little Fork, a tributary of the Little Sandy River also was hit by this rain.  This water flowed north and caused flooding in Carter County.  ||Rain totals in a 24 to 30 hour time span were on the order of 3 to 4 inches in  Lawrence County.  The mesonet gauge at Louisa went from a total of 1.4 inches of rain at midday on the 3rd, to a total near 4 inches by 2000E.  Their event rain total was 4.2 inches. The heaviest 5 minute rate was around 2 tenths of an inch during the evening.  Flooding along the smaller streams was common.  In its wake, flooding of the larger streams lingered into the 4th.||A major federal disaster was declared in Kentucky. It included Lawrence and Carter Counties in the initial declaration.  The disaster also encompassed the flooding during the 14th and 15th of the month.  See FEMA DR-4217 for more information.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn on Harris Road sustained minor damage after being struck by lightning.  Damage was limited to the electrical panel and about 3 to 4 feet of the adjacent wall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from an early morning thunderstorm on April 9th, struck the Monroe County law enforcement building in Sparta. The strike damaged some of the communication equipment inside the building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit the Monroe County law enforcement building damaging some of the communication equipment inside the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms formed during the heat and instability of the late afternoon and early evening. This was well in advance of a mid level disturbance that followed later that night. Overall though, the rain was needed.  A dry pattern was seen during the first 3 weeks of the month.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was fishing along Racoon Creek off of Route 20 with her boyfriend and 4 year old child.  Lightning hit a tree.  A large branch hit the woman on the head.  She suffered head and back injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The largest severe weather event during the spring of 2015 in Middle Tennessee affected the region during the afternoon and evening hours on April 3. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, including some supercells and bow echoes, developed ahead of a cold front approaching the area, and brought widespread damaging winds, large hail, and one EF0 tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in Antioch was struck by lightning and destroyed in the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front pushed through the Missouri Bootheel during the morning hours with moist and unstable air spreading over the region. An upper level disturbance moving through triggered numerous showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours on May 15, 2015. Lightning near Hayti resulted in a fatality.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in Hayti City Park which then fell on a vehicle. The person inside the vehicle was killed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated, pulse severe thunderstorms developed across southwest and south central Alabama during the afternoon and evening of June 23, 2015.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male and female were struck and killed by lightning as they were attempting to cover a chicken coup which was by a tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Abundant moisture and weak easterly flow caused numerous afternoon thunderstorms over the Florida peninsula. A couple of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and small hail in Polk County, as well as a lightning strike that damaged a moving car.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A broadcast media outlet reported that a car in one of the east bound lanes of Interstate 4 was apparently struck by lightning near Polk City. The driver reported two of the air bags were deployed, the glove box popped open, and power shut down to the car at the time of a bright flash during a thunderstorm. Several burn marks were later found on the car. The driver suffered bruises to her ribcage from the airbags.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of an approaching cold front, a warm and humid air mass was in place over northwestern Connecticut on Tuesday, May 19th.  As the cold front approached during the early evening hours, a few scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and moved from west to east across the region.  Some of the thunderstorms became severe, producing damaging winds to trees and power lines.  In addition, two of the thunderstorms produced damaging lightning strikes as well.  ||The threat for thunderstorms ended by the late evening hours, as the cold front passed through the region and drier air moved into the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike was reported to have downed a tree and power wires in Falls Village.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ahead of an approaching cold front, a warm and humid air mass was in place over eastern New York on Tuesday, May 19th. As the cold front approached during the early evening hours, a few scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and moved from west to east across the region. One of these thunderstorms produced a damaging lightning strike over Columbia County. ||The threat for thunderstorms ended by the late evening hours, as the cold front passed through the region and drier air moved into the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wires were reported down due to a lightning strike on Birch Hill Road in Copake.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With high pressure situated just off the eastern seaboard, a southerly flow allowed for a very warm and humid air mass to move into eastern New York.  Temperatures reached well into the 80s F with dewpoint temperatures into the 60s F as well.  An approaching upper level disturbance, aided by a surface pre-frontal trough, allowed thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon hours.  Although instability was limited due to areas of cloud cover in place, thunderstorms were able to organize into lines.  As a result, some of these thunderstorms became severe, producing damaging winds.  In addition, heavy rain accompanied these thunderstorms, and some flash flooding occurred as well.  As a result of the thunderstorm, power companies reported several thousand customers without power during the height of the storms.||As the upper level disturbance and surface trough moved away, the threat for thunderstorms ended by the early evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house to catch fire on Eastern Avenue in Schenectady.  The home's attic was damaged by fire and smoke and water damage occurred throughout the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough over the central United States and an approaching cold front resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across the north central Gulf Coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the Florida panhandle causing damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a dryline located just west of the CWA in the afternoon hours. These storms eventually merged into a line that continued marching east across most of the region. Winds up to 70-80 mph and hail up to golf ball size were reported with these storms, and a brief EF-0 tornado occurred in Hood County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire on Carmel Drive in Carrollton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms produced large hail across parts of southeast Colorado.  Slow moving storms produced a large amount of hail, which caused flooding and accidents on Colorado Springs area roadways, and flooding also occurred due to clogging of drains. A severe storm produced a short-lived tornado and killed three horses in southeast Baca County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three horses were killed by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms existed at dawn on the 8th in Indiana.  With support for the mid and upper level winds, this mesoscale convective complex maintained its intensity through the morning.  It raced southeast at 50 mph reaching southeast Ohio during the midday time frame.  Most areas saw brief wind gusts of 40 to 45 mph and rains of a quarter to a half inch.  A few areas saw stronger wind gusts.||After a lull, additional rounds of convection moved into southeast Ohio after sunset on the 8th.  Minor flooding occurred in Washington County as a result of the overnight convection.  Rain amounts of 1.5 to 2.5 inches occurred in 24 hours.||Distinct thunderstorm cells formed during the day on the 9th.  On the southern edge of a larger complex, one storm that moved from Athens County through southern Washington County had significant mid level rotation. Yet, no evidence of a tornado was found. ||Widespread showers accompanied the cold frontal passage early on the 10th.  Rain totals of 1 to 1.5 inches were reported that included both the afternoon convection on the 9th and the predawn showers on the 10th.||In the wake of the cold front, drier air finally moved into southeast Ohio during the daylight hours of the 10th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a dwelling.  The house filled with smoke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Upper level low pressure area centered near Baja moved toward West Texas and then slowly across the Permian Basin and the Texas Panhandle, which provided enough lift over the area to produce showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and lightning struck and caused a tank battery fire near Garden City.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.  There were no injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of a stationary frontal boundary, rich gulf moisture, instability and day time heating had triggered some strong to severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a water tower in Terry, creating holes that had to be repaired.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A southeast Minnesota home was damaged from a lightning strike during a late evening thunderstorm on April 8th. The Rochester (Olmsted County) home sustained about $2,500 in damage when lightning hit the natural gas line feeding the house starting a small fire that burned some siding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit the natural gas line to a home on the southwest side of Rochester. A small fire was started that burned some siding and soffit on the exterior of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the runway at Brewton Airport.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the runway at Brewton Airport causing damaging.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough moved through southern New England bringing showers and thunderstorms to the region.  Several of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage on Tipping Rock Road starting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms produced numerous lightning strikes across the Tennessee Valley.  A few resulted in structure fires or damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a tree in the backyard of a Madison home, and traveled over 100 feet and produced damage to the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through southern New England, producing showers and thunderstorms across the region.  Several of these storms became severe producing damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Sandalwood Circle igniting a small fire near the chimney and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Excessive heavy rainfall was widespread across the southern half of Northeast Texas  during the morning hours of May 18th. This convection developed from an upper level disturbance that moved into the region from Central Texas. Moisture was plentiful across the region as the upper level flow was from the southwest. This allowed the disturbance to tap moisture from not only the Eastern Pacific but also the Gulf of Mexico. These storms trained across the same general area resulting in some impressive rainfall totals. The end result was widespread flooding across much of the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Apparent lightning strike struck a window at the Timpson High School and struck a student.  The student suffered a brief injury but lived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms fueled by deep moisture and sea breeze interactions moved through the Tampa Bay area. A lightning strike from one of these storms caused a fire to a condominium.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Print and broadcast media outlets reported that a condominium building in Carollwood was struck by lightning Saturday, that smouldered overnight. The fire burned through a ceiling at one point and triggered the sprinklers, extinguishing the fire. The time of the lightning strike was estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed along a boundary lifting slowly northeast across northern Kentucky into southwest Ohio.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A University of Dayton student, Sean Ferguson, 23 of Pittsburgh, was struck by lightning as he ran across university parking lot C. The student was hospitalized with serious burns and a broken jaw.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered convection developed across the tri-state area with isolated strong to severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike knocked out power to some light poles and telephone service in the Springfield area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous showers and some storms developed within the interaction of a stationary front over the region and upper level disturbances moving along this boundary. A number of the storms produced hail less than an inch in diameter with an isolated report of one inch diameter hail. Damaging winds were produced by one thunderstorm in Yadkin County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck three homes in the Forbush area near the Forsyth County line. The lightning was conducted through the electrical wiring of the homes with one of the homes catching fire. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved eastward out of North Central Texas and into Northeast Texas during the morning hours of May 30th.  This line of storms bowed out as they moved east and produced some wind damage across Northeast Texas and Northwest Louisiana.  Some flash flooding was also produced with these storms as rainfall rates were excessive.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a structural fire in Henderson, Texas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was indirectly struck by lightning while under his truck.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was under his truck when it was struck by lightning.  He sustained only minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The end of May produced very active weather across the state of Utah, with widespread thunderstorms on most days. Several flash floods were observed across southern Utah, and multiple severe thunderstorms occurred across the northern half of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Syracuse, Utah in the morning hours of May 28. The roof of the house caught fire, but was seen and extinguished quickly, leading to only relatively minor roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early season convection resulted in a lighting strike that impacted tens of thousands of Alaskans, from the Southcentral region to the Interior.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike near Houston, AK knocked out power for more than 28,000 people.  |The lightning strike at 5:42 p.m. affected the Intertie between Anchorage and Fairbanks, knocking out power from Willow to as far as North Pole and Salcha. According to Golden Valley Electric Association, strike knocked out 11 substations. |Power was restored to most people by 6:08 p.m., except some in the Cantwell area because of breaker problems in the Healy substation. Power was restored in Cantwell by 11:00 PM.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed late in the evening on April 8th producing marginally severe hail.  There was also a lightning strike in Mount Prospect that set a building on fire the morning of April 9th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a multi-family home on the 400 block of East Lincoln Street causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southwest flow and deep moisture produced several thunderstorms moving up the west coast of the Florida peninsula during the afternoon hours. Wind gusts from these storms caused minor damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media relayed a picture from a viewer of a large tree branch that was knocked down by a lightning strike near the intersection of Highway 54 and Highway 19 just before 7 pm EDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A meandering surface front over the area in concert with the sea breezes and an approaching mid level impulse spawned scattered afternoon thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike in Macclenny injured two. A structure fire was also caused. The cost of damage was unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted north of the Altamaha River Basin in advance of an approaching cold front and parent upper level trough pushing downstream of the MS river valley. Modest instability and shear was in place with supported scattered severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a transformer off of College Avenue. The cost of damage was estimated for the event to be included in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Weak flow and deep moisture produced late morning thunderstorms over Pinellas county. A lightning bolt from one of these storms struck and killed a man in Largo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Florida Emergency Management reported that an 81 year old man was struck and killed while walking near his home in Largo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms preceding a cold front on the evening of the 26th caused lightning damage in Easton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged the Manor House in the Londonderry Retirement Community in Easton. The ensuing fire was limited to the roof and 2nd floor of the 150-year-old building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved across a relatively unstable air mass across eastern New York and Vermont during the afternoon of May 27th. A line of showers and thunderstorms initiated across eastern New York and then proceeded across Vermont. There were several reports of downed trees due to thunderstorm winds in Vermont.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Small boat struck by lightning and severely damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms developed well ahead of an approaching cold front during the late afternoon and evening of May 10th.  Scattered wind damage occurred with the storms, particularly along and south of a Springfield to Danville line.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, which fell on a building behind the fire department in Havana.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms moved through the Midlands of SC and produced some large hail and wind damage...mainly trees taken down.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Sheriff reported a barn struck by lightning in Whitmire burnt to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Marginal Risk (SPC) day produced rather widespread wind damage across west-central Georgia during the late afternoon hours of the 26th.  An EF-1 tornado was confirmed north of Warm Springs in Meriwether county.  An upper level wave moving east from AL/Gulf coast region spawned widespread convection that became an evident QLCS that tracked west to east across GA during the afternoon hours.  The most intense/severe storms were generally south of I-20 and west of I-75.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a natural gas line and caused fires at 2 homes on Poplar Road. Reported by Emergency Management.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed across far west Texas during the early morning hours of May 25th and this cluster of severe thunderstorms evolved into a derecho, moving eastward across the entire state of Texas and eventually into Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northwest Louisiana.  Widespread wind damage was reported across the region during the afternoon and evening hours with flash flooding reported across portions of the region as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a house fire in El Dorado, Arkansas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered clusters of thunderstorms developed across much of western North Carolina during early afternoon and continued into the evening hours. A couple of storms produced brief severe weather in the form of damaging winds, while a cluster of storms produced significant flash flooding in southern portions of the Charlotte metro area for the second evening in a row.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Public reported via Social Media that lightning struck the chimney of a home on Taunton Dr. Debris from the chimney fell on and injured a man and caused damage to the roof and deck of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike injured several hikers as they were descending from the summit of Mt Bierstadt.  Severe thunderstorms produced hail, from quarter to half dollar size, over parts of Arapahoe, Elbert and Weld Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were transported to Denver-area hospitals after a lightning strike 500 feet below the summit of Mt. Bierstadt.  A total of fifteen people were hit by lightning.  Eight adults were were transported from the trailhead, and that three of those were taken to Denver-area hospitals. One of them was in serious condition, the other two had non-life threatening injuries.  A dog was also killed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms continued across southern Utah during the last week of August, with a couple of flash floods reported in far southern Utah. A lightning fatality also occurred in northern Utah during this period of time.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A family was having a picnic in a park in Lehi, Utah, when a thunderstorm moved across the area. Lightning struck a nearby tree, and critically injured a 50-year-old woman. No one else in the party was seriously injured, but the victim passed away in a hospital a few days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed underneath an upper trough axis across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on October 1. Some of thunderstorms repeatedly developed across southern Williamson and northern Maury Counties throughout the afternoon, resulting in a localized area of very heavy rainfall up to 9 inches and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A doctor's office in Spring Hill was struck by lightning. The amount of damage to the office is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rain led to flash flooding across portions of North Central Texas on the 23rd and 24th, with residual flooding lasting through at least the 25th. Rainfall totals in flood damaged areas ranged from 5 to 21+ inches within a 36 hour period. The highest rainfall totals were in Navarro County which suffered significant damage across the entire county. Flood waters derailed a train north of Corsicana and many county and farm-to-market roads were washed away. The flooding in Navarro County persisted for weeks in areas where the water had a very difficult time draining. Rainfall totals near 20 inches also fell in southern Hill County were many roads were covered with water.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a house fire near Judge Dupree Drive and Gentle River Drive in southeast Oak Cliff. The house sustained significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Many storms produced flash flooding, and isolated severe weather also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck three power poles in Amargosa Valley.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper level low fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Many storms produced flash flooding, and isolated severe weather also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a power pole on fire, knocking out power to 1800 customers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed underneath an upper trough axis across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on October 1. Some of thunderstorms repeatedly developed across southern Williamson and northern Maury Counties throughout the afternoon, resulting in a localized area of very heavy rainfall up to 9 inches and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Clara Mathis Drive in Spring Hill around 3:00 PM CDT and started a fire. As emergency crews were fighting the fire, lightning struck the home again around 4:00 PM CDT. The amount of fire damage to the home is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another round of strong thunderstorms formed across Utah for a few days in the middle of October. Severe wind gusts were observed in northwest Utah, while some flash flooding occurred in southern Utah.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Cedar City and started a fire in one corner of the house. Firefighters were able to put out the fire relatively quickly, but not before the residence sustained approximately $8,000 worth of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough slid across the southwestern U.S. and northern Mexico inducing an intensifying surface and low level low pressure trough and increasing southerly flow bringing deep tropical moisture to the area.  Thunderstorms developed over northern Mexico and turned into a mesoscale convective system over Brownsville. Citywide four to seven inches of rain fell within a two to three hour window causing flash flooding across Brownsville. Many roads were inundated with two to three feet of water and dozens of homes and businesses were flooded. The rainfall was accompanied by excessive, nearly continuous cloud to ground lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the KBRO radar dome, damaging circuit boards and rendering the radar inoperable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system brought a round of thunderstorms to the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Significant flash flooding occurred, along with isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning knocked out power to over 4000 customers and set fire to a palm tree between Landers and Twentynine Palms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system brought a round of thunderstorms to the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Significant flash flooding occurred, along with isolated severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to five trees and one power pole in Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave trough located west of Arizona caused scattered showers and thunderstorms for much of the day. Late in the evening, one storm's lightning caused damage to a residence.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 12000 block of North Lost Shadow Court, damaging the roof. The fire which was ignited caused minor smoke damage, mainly in the attic. No one was home at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged the bell tower at the St. Cloud Children's Home that was built in 1924. Although the main brick work wasn't damaged, the main damage occurred with the wooden structure surrounding the bell tower.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged a bell tower at the St. Cloud Children's Home that was built in 1924.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving area of thunderstorms produced several hours of frequent cloud to ground lightning in eastern Iowa the evening of October 20th. The lightning caused several fires in the Iowa City metro area, and caused firefighters to take defensive action against lightning while fighting the structure fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Iowa City's fire department reported that they had three buildings, and one tree set on fire by lightning. Two of the three building fires resulted in fire fighting efforts.  One significant structure fire at 623 E. College St had mutual support called from nearby city departments, and sustained significant fire damage. Fire fighters were forced to take the defensive action of pulling firefighters from ladders, due to the continued frequent lightning in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Record breaking daytime heat in combination with a weak southward sagging cold front and the inland moving sea breeze front produced late afternoon through early evening thunderstorms that became severe. This event included strong damaging winds and hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A car was severely damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong thunderstorms developed in the warm sector across the Lehigh and Susquehanna Valleys and tracked through southern New Jersey during the late afternoon of the 11th. Lightning strikes associated with the line of thunderstorms downed wires and struck a residential building. A warm front had lifted northeast through New Jersey during the morning of the 11th. This permitted sufficient daytime heating to occur ahead of an approaching cold front, yielding a line of strong thunderstorms with numerous lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes downed wires in Chesterfield Township during the late afternoon of the 11th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong thunderstorms developed in the warm sector across the Lehigh and Susquehanna Valleys and tracked through southern New Jersey during the late afternoon of the 11th. Lightning strikes associated with the line of thunderstorms downed wires and struck a residential building. A warm front had lifted northeast through New Jersey during the morning of the 11th. This permitted sufficient daytime heating to occur ahead of an approaching cold front, yielding a line of strong thunderstorms with numerous lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes downed wires in Florence Township during the late afternoon of the 11th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong thunderstorms developed in the warm sector across the Lehigh and Susquehanna Valleys and tracked through southern New Jersey during the late afternoon of the 11th. Lightning strikes associated with the line of thunderstorms downed wires and struck a residential building. A warm front had lifted northeast through New Jersey during the morning of the 11th. This permitted sufficient daytime heating to occur ahead of an approaching cold front, yielding a line of strong thunderstorms with numerous lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Southampton Township. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another round of severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging straight-line winds affected parts of central and northeast Wisconsin during the afternoon of August 2nd.  The most intense storms developed near a surface boundary that stretched from Wausau to Green Bay early in the afternoon.||Some of the first severe storms of the event developed just north of Green Bay, over parts of Oconto County and Marinette County, and produced hail in excess of three inches in diameter.  These storms were part of a larger line of storms that raced eastward across the waters of Green Bay, causing widespread wind damage and knocking out power across much of Door County.||Additional storms developed westward toward the Wausau area.  These storms moved southeast during the late afternoon and produced large hail and damaging winds from Marathon and Wood counties east to Lake Michigan.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire in Suamico.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rainfall of 3 to 8 inches in a few hours caused widespread flash flooding of streets, parks, ditches, homes and businesses, and other low areas in the central and southern parts of Sioux Falls, and just south of the city. Lightning strikes started fires in at least 3 houses during the storm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in the roof of a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northwesterly flow aloft prevailed over Arizona and weakening high pressure was located off the coast of northern Baja California. Scattered thunderstorms began  during the late morning hours and lasted through the early evening. Damaging winds occurred in Marana and flash flooding occurred in Nogales.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck and injured by lightning near Three Points.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved slowly over portions of northern and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon and evening of the 1st. The strongest of these storms rolled through the Santa Rosa area, dropping quarter size hail and producing damaging wind gusts up to 60 mph that caused roof damage to several buildings. The 1.5 to 2 inches of rain that accompanied the storm also caused flash flooding that resulted in one road being closed due to being submerged in water.  Between 1.5 and 3.35 inches of heavy rain also fell near Santa Fe, leading to flash flood waters between 1 and 1.5 feet high making a road impassable. No other significant flooding as a result of heavy rains was reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike led to a fatal motorcycle crash along U.S. Highway 64 near Hopewell Lake. The victim was 37-year old Juan Trujillo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure along the central California coastline coupled with high pressure located over the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles created southwesterly flow over southern Arizona and scattered thunderstorms over Graham, Pinal and Pima Counties. Favorable jet dynamics helped thunderstorms become strong enough to produce gusty winds and areas of flash flooding, mainly in the Tucson Metro area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike shattered a 30-ft tree in the Orange Grove Estates complex.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A teenager was critically injured when he struck by lightning.  He was standing on a hill in an open field.  A thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size near Evergreen.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Juvenile male struck by lightning in field near Town Center Mall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northwesterly flow aloft prevailed over Arizona and weakening high pressure was located off the coast of northern Baja California. Scattered thunderstorms began  during the late morning hours and lasted through the early evening. Damaging winds occurred in Marana and flash flooding occurred in Nogales.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a fire at a residence on N Oracle Rd. in Catalina.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Heavy rainfall of 3 to 8 inches in a few hours caused widespread flash flooding of streets, parks, ditches, homes and businesses, and other low areas in the central and southern parts of Sioux Falls, and just south of the city. Lightning strikes started fires in at least 3 houses during the storm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes on two houses near each other started small fires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level ridge dominated over the SE with a surface ridge axis south of the forecast area with a mean layer SW flow in place. A weak surface trough was over south Georgia, and this feature combined with the sea breezes over an unstable and moist airmass produced scattered severe storms during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire at Wayne Frier Mobile Home Sales at 12788 US Highway 90 West in Live Oak.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably strong storm system lifted northward from Iowa into Minnesota on August 18th. This caused a warm front to lift northward across eastern Iowa and warm and moist air to flood into the region. Showers and thunderstorms developed across eastern Iowa during the afternoon and evening hours. These thunderstorms produced an EF-0 tornado 3 miles northwest of Stanwood in Cedar County. The storms also produced thunderstorm wind damage in Jones and Des Moines Counties along with hail the size of peas. Torrential rains of 2 to 3 inches caused flash flooding in Clinton County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that lightning struck the roof of a home and caused a fire that was quickly extinguished by the fire department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure was located near the four corners region resulting in moderate southerly flow over southeast Arizona. Thunderstorm wind damage occurred in Marana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local police report a tree was struck by lightning near Benson.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of slow-moving thunderstorms developed between Cannon Air Force Base and Clovis during the late afternoon hours. Wet microburst winds and hail slammed Clovis before organizing into an extended line of torrential rainfall from northern Roosevelt County through much of Curry County. Emergency management reported near zero visibility in heavy rain. Fierce lightning struck a duplex home and resulted in a large blaze that severely damaged the home. Nickel to penny size hail was also reported around the city. Minor flooding was observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire crews responded to lightning caused blaze at a duplex home that resulted in significant damage to the property.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Damaging lightning strikes and strong winds recorded.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in a grain field in Declo with 30 foot flames.   40 to 50 acres of a 140 acre field were destroyed by the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper level trough moving across North Florida led to scattered showers and storms across South Florida and local Atlantic.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck house on the 3500 block of SW 123rd Court leading to an attic fire that spread across entire roof. Information via public and broadcast media.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure was located near the four corners region resulting in moderate southerly flow over southeast Arizona. Thunderstorm wind damage occurred in Marana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A palm tree was struck by lightning near the 3500 block of S. Austin Place. This resulted in multiple windows blown out of a nearby duplex.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front that was slowly moving eastward across Iowa. Thunderstorms in Jackson and Scott Counties produced damaging winds estimated to be near 60 mph. A thunderstorm in Louisa County caused a fire at a machine shed from a lightning strike. Brief torrential downpours were reported with several of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire department reported that a lightning strike caught a machine shed on fire about 4 miles east southeast of Wapello. The time of the event was estimated using lightning and radar data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front and leftover daytime instability triggered an area of strong to severe thunderstorms into the central Delmarva Peninsula during the evening of the 24th where damaging wind gusts, lightning strikes, and power outages were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm at 10:48 p.m. EDT caused localized power outages for 51 Delmarva Power customers in the town of Queen Anne. Service was restored to the customers shortly after midnight EDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper level trough moving across North Florida led to scattered showers and storms across South Florida and local Atlantic.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person killed and 2 injured by lightning strike near a group of men sheltering under tree in park in Northeast Miami-Dade County. Exact location and time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In the hours after midnight on the 28th a low pressure system was over portions of central/eastern Nebraska moving toward Iowa.  A warm front extended east out of the surface low into southern Iowa.  With the progression of the surface low, moderate to heavy rainfall began to enter the state.  Areas that reported the greatest storm total amounts began to see rain around the 2 to 3 am hour and onward through the morning and into the early afternoon as the warm front lingered in central Iowa.  In the end, numerous locations reported total rainfall amounts greater than 4 inches with a handful of reports around 6 inches.  The greater totals were in excess of 9 inches and were recorded in Webster and Hamilton counties, with Dayton in Webster county taking the prize at 9.75 inches. The heavy rainfall allowed many rivers in central Iowa to rise above flood stage. Some of the flooding continued into early September. The entry will be continued in the September 2015 report.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree splitting the tree with large limbs down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Dolores and a monsoonal fetch of moisture streamed into southern and central California during the time period. This brought deep moisture into the area which resulted in moderate to heavy rainfall across most of the southern San Joaquin Valley and nearly all of Kern County. Kern County estimates the cost of the emergency response and infrastructure repair  throughout the Kern Operational Area to be approximately 2.7 million dollars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Autospy confirmed Bakersfield man was struck and killed by lightning. The individual was found unresponsive just before 7 PM PDT by a family member.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across Long Island, NY and raced toward Rhode Island. These storms caused significant wind damage across Rhode Island resulting in widespread power outages, knocking down a significant amount of trees, and causing massive traffic delays. Wind gusts were estimated to be between 60 to 80 mph, with T.F. Green Airport reporting a wind gust of 67 mph. In fact, these storms caused more power outages (121,000 customers without power) than Hurricane Sandy (107,000)! Some of the hardest hit areas were Cranston and Charlestown, RI.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Randall Road was struck by lightning, starting a small fire in the basement.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of boundaries in the area and an extremely unstable airmass, led to the development of explosive thunderstorms across the mid Valley, during the late evening and overnight hours (apparent temperatures at McAllen were 100 degrees F at 10 pm (C2T) with the actual temperature at just under 90 F). These thunderstorms produced excessive lightning, quarter to golf ball size hail, strong and gusty winds, and flooding across the mid Valley area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At least five homes were struck by lightning and burned in spots in the McAllen Metro and Weslaco areas, some with considerable damage. Numerous lightning strikes were reported throughout Hidalgo County, resulting in utility pole and tree fires, and more than 30,000 residents without power at the peak of the storms.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure along the central California coastline coupled with high pressure located over the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles created southwesterly flow over southern Arizona and scattered thunderstorms over Graham, Pinal and Pima Counties. Favorable jet dynamics helped thunderstorms become strong enough to produce gusty winds and areas of flash flooding, mainly in the Tucson Metro area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 45-year old tree was struck by lightning. It landed in a woman's backyard when it fell, and no other damage occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An historic severe weather outbreak in northern Michigan, as multiple waves of severe thunderstorms crossed the region. A passing cold front would finally end the activity during the evening hours. This episode featured widespread straight-line wind damage in parts of northwest lower Michigan, and the largest hail on record in northern Michigan in Ogemaw County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were injured by a lightning strike at a campground. They were treated and released from a local hospital later that same day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northward retreating warm front served as the primary focus for convective development. Afternoon heating resulted in destabilization and several storms became severe, with large hail being the primary impact. Isolated flash flooding also occurred. These thunderstorms also had excessive lightning, which resulted in a fatality.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 28 year old male was struck and killed by lightning in the parking lot of a shopping center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced lightning which caused damage in northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A boundary was pushing through the state with ongoing convection through central Iowa through the day. As the boundary neared the area, the convection intensified and impacted central and southern Iowa in the evening to early morning hours. Two thunderstorm complexes moved through portions of central and southern Iowa with very heavy rainfall causing flash flooding. The severe thunderstorm complexes produced some hail but mainly strong damaging winds. Precipitable water values were near 2 inches in some areas with deep warm cloud depths during the event. This heavy rainfall further exacerbated conditions as some of the area had just received heavy rainfall in previous days. This led to some extended flooding for a few days and flooding on some area rivers. Several locations reported in excess of 4 inches of rain, while one location in Warren County reported over 7.50 inches of rainfall. The Emergency Manager for Marion County mentioned widespread reports of 8 to 10 inches with one report close to 12 inches of accumulated rainfall over the past few days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in an environment favorable for severe wet microbursts with high Wet Microburst Severity Index values.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A transformer was blown near the intersection of Apalachee Pkwy and Blairstone.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: For several days, a stalled cold front, combined with abundant moisture from the Gulf of Mexico combined to produce widespread rain and thunderstorms in Texas. Several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms occurred during a four day period, producing flash flooding, and numerous reports of large hail. Tornadoes affected areas in central Texas, from near Lampasas to a deadly tornado in Milam County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck 2 cars on I-35 near Hwy 22 in Hillsboro, TX, causing the airbags to deploy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and storms developed in a moist and unstable atmosphere over South Florida during the afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tour boat captain was struck by lightning on deck of vessel while returning back from Gulf of Mexico through Gordon Pass during stormy weather. Boat captain sustained minor injuries and was held overnight at hospital for monitoring.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home around 11:15 PM EDT, which lead to a house fire. The 3,500-square-foot home suffered extensive damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Diurnal showers and thunderstorms developed with enough instability to produce isolated large hail.  A rather moist environment coupled with slow moving storms resulted in some flash flooding in western Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer, causing a fire on Melville Street at St. James Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably strong cold front passed across the central Appalachians during the evening of June 27th.  Storm intensity increased east of a lee surface trough across the Piedmont of North Carolinas into Virginia.  Heavy precipitation loading occurred with some of the storms due to a very moist atmosphere, where precipitable water values were observed exceeding 1.5 inches.  Damaging wind gusts also occurred due to downward mixing of momentum associated with the 30 to 40 knot mean southwesterly lower and mid tropospheric wind flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home, causing a hot water heater to catch fire that resulted in minor damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms produced hundreds of lightning strikes across the Tampa Bay Area during the late evening on Sunday. One lightning strike hit a house in Land O' Lakes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper reported that a lightning strike caused a fire to a home in Hernando. The residents were not home, and fire crews quickly put out the fire, however, the newspaper reported that damage was estimated at $172,750.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a transformer fire and injured a teenager in the City of Richmond.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a transformer fire and injured a teenager near the intersection of Winnetka Avenue and Edgefield Street off Chamberlayne Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rosemount Fire Department officials said lightning was to blame for a fire that damaged a fourplex on 156th Street early Friday morning in Rosemount. Firefighters arrived to find a fire burning on the exterior of the building���s south side. The fire eventually worked its way inside the building, but firefighters were able to get the flames under control quickly. No injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire was caused by lightning in Rosemount the morning of July 24th. The fire burnt the exterior of a fourplex south side. The fire eventually worked its way inside the building, but firefighters were able to get the flames under control quickly.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a house at 4382 Martin Road in Duluth, MN. The tree caught fire and caused the fire to spread to the house's attic. There were no injuries as the house was unoccupied.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near a house at 4382 Martin Road in Duluth, MN. The tree caught fire and caused the fire to spread to the house's attic. There were no injuries as the house was unoccupied.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a man while he was hiking below the South Rim of The Grand Canyon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while hiking the South Kaibab Trail near Ooh Aah Point (about mile down the trail from the Rim). Paramedics were unable to resuscitate him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorms and heavy rainfall produced 2.5 to around 5 inches of rainfall in a very short amount of time from around Vinton to Bell City. Flooding mainly occurred in the Cities of Sulphur and Lake Charles.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A National Weather Service Employee's home was struck by lightning igniting a small fire in a wall. The fire damaged a wall in the laundry room and shorted out some wiring. The fire department was able keep the fire from spreading.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The remnants of T.S. Erika crossed the forecast area from the Gulf region through the day. High moisture combined with forcing and weak onshore convergence around the remnant low brought waves of heavy rainfall and isolated strong storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Sally B. Mathis Elementary School. School was evacuated due to smoke in the building from a damaged air conditioner unit. The cost of damage was unknown but estimated for StormData.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Overnight thunderstorms and an associated lightning strike caused the cross atop St. Helena���s Catholic Church to crash to the ground. The cross was made of limestone, which had been on the church for 75 years. Damage also occurred on the  marble steps at the entrance to the church. Nobody was hurt, though the impact of the falling rubble could be heard as far as two blocks away.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed the cross atop St. Helena���s Catholic Church which crashed to the ground and caused more damage to the marble steps.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad upper trough of low pressure over the eastern U.S. caused scattered afternoon thunderstorms across South Florida. A few strong storms produced small hail in eastern Palm Beach county, as well as a funnel cloud over Broward county. Lightning strikes  started fires in two Miami-Dade County homes and resulted in about 3,700 customers losing power in Aventura, including at Aventura Mall. Traffic lights were out at several intersections along Biscayne Boulevard in northeast Miami-Dade County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected lightning strike lead to a fire at an apartment in the Playa Lago Condominiums in the Tamiami neighborhood of Miami. Neighbors reported hearing loud thunder, then seeing smoke and flames coming from the affected apartment. Fire damage was confined to one apartment, but several others received water damage. No one was home at the time of the fire and no injures were reported. Information from NBC6. Time of event estimated and based on data from lightning detection network.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad upper trough of low pressure over the eastern U.S. caused scattered afternoon thunderstorms across South Florida. A few strong storms produced small hail in eastern Palm Beach county, as well as a funnel cloud over Broward county. Lightning strikes  started fires in two Miami-Dade County homes and resulted in about 3,700 customers losing power in Aventura, including at Aventura Mall. Traffic lights were out at several intersections along Biscayne Boulevard in northeast Miami-Dade County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected lightning strike lead to a fire at a duplex home Sweetwater. The occupant of the home reported hearing a loud boom then smelling smoke shortly thereafter. The occupants of the home safely evacuated and the fire left the home uninhabitable. Information from WSVN. Time of event estimated and based on data from lightning detection network.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Subtropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Linda brought widespread showers to most of the area, deserts included. The first isolated thunderstorm developed on the 6th in San Diego County as a moisture surge in monsoon warm upper level flow arrived. Intense heavy rain from thunderstorms occurred on the 7th with flash flooding in several locations including Victorville and Forest Falls. A swift water rescue in Victorville was successful, but another incident in Forest Falls had one rescue but a drowning occurred when a 30-year-old couple crossed Mill Creek and were swept away. Most areas received between a few hundredths to one-third of an inch of rain, with a few upslope areas of the San Bernardino Mountains receiving up to around one inch. Additional thunderstorms developed on the 8th by noon over the mountains and quickly spread into the Inland Empire and Orange County, as well as near I-15 in San Diego County. Locally heavy rain and several trees and poles were downed in the Riverside area including a small dust storm. Several hail reports, mostly nickel-sized, but a few larger. Activity decreased on the 9th with only isolated thunderstorms formed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: CHP reported a lightning-started brush fire along Highway 38 near Onyx Peak.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep and moist southerly wind flow led to an active afternoon of thunderstorms across parts of southeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage roof of a home in Jupiter Landings. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Florida Power & Light officials responded and found a damaged rafter under the shingles, a charred electrical line and blown circuit.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad upper trough of low pressure over the eastern U.S. caused scattered afternoon thunderstorms across South Florida. A few strong storms produced small hail in eastern Palm Beach county, as well as a funnel cloud over Broward county. Lightning strikes  started fires in two Miami-Dade County homes and resulted in about 3,700 customers losing power in Aventura, including at Aventura Mall. Traffic lights were out at several intersections along Biscayne Boulevard in northeast Miami-Dade County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: SUV traveling along I-95 near Griffin Road exit was disabled by lightning strike on rear of vehicle. A hole the size of a quarter was found in the rear of the vehicle beneath the back windshield and the electrical system in the car was destroyed. No injuries were reported and vehicle was towed from scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fallen tree caused damage to a camper in Van Riper State Park after it was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fallen tree caused damage to a boat, a pickup truck and a camper awning in Van Riper State Park after it was struck by lightning.  No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough of low pressure over the Florida peninsula generated scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 29-foot boat at a marina on the Miami River near NW 17th Avenue which started a fire and caused significant damage to the boat. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed in an environment favorable for severe wet microbursts with high Wet Microburst Severity Index values.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck by lightning and injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in an environment favorable for severe wet microbursts with high Wet Microburst Severity Index values.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused several power outages in Chipley.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough of low pressure over the southeast U.S. caused scattered afternoon thunderstorms over Southeast Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected lightning strike hit a large tree, causing portions of the tree to fall onto a parked car. The back windshield of the car was damaged along with driver's side door. Additional damaged was caused by the falling tree to a wooden fence in between two homes. The fallen tree also resulted in a road blockage for several hours along Mayo Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper trough of low pressure over the northeastern Gulf of Mexico caused scattered showers and thunderstorms across South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman working at Palm Beach International Airport was apparently struck by lightning on the tarmac and was taken to the hospital. Lightning data from the National Lightning Detection Network showed a lightning strike at the airport at the reported time of the emergency call.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front pushed south across the Red River Tuesday Night and was accompanied by a broken line of showers and storms as it  encroached on the Interstate 20 corridor early Wednesday morning. As a cluster of storms moved across the Dallas-Fort Worth area, lightning struck and set fire to an apartment complex in Irving, damaging 16 units.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms rolled across the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex early morning on Wednesday September 9th. Lightning from one storm struck an apartment complex, setting fire to it and damaging 16 units. No injuries were reported, but 27 people were displaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak push of monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. A few storms produced flash flooding and strong winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two transformers, knocking out power to about a quarter of Kingman.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm with infrequent lightning produced a strike which struck a construction crane at Hobe Sound and injured two workers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm with infrequent lightning produced a strike which hit a construction crane and injured two nearby workers. The two men were transported to a nearby hospital with non life-threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable airmass caused scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue reported damage to a Wellington Petco roof with debris from the lightning strike on the ground. Store is located at 920 S. State Road 7. There were no injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning associated with a strong thunderstorm struck a home in Winter Garden and caused a fire that nearly destroyed the home. A short time later, another thunderstorm became locally strong over the Kissimmee Airport, with microbust winds damaging a hanger building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Shadowmoss Drive in Winter Garden and started a fire which destroyed most of the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rural Black River Falls (Jackson County) house was damaged when it was hit by a lightning strike during the evening of September 17th. The lightning struck the house's TV antenna and traveled into the house blowing out a section of an interior and exterior wall and causing damage to the electrical wiring in the house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a rural Black River Falls home striking the house's TV antenna and then traveling into the house. A hole was blown into an interior wall of a second floor bedroom where a mattress and box springs caught on fire. A wall stud was blown apart causing a hole in an exterior wall and numerous outlets and light switches throughout the house had their covers blown off or charred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening across the Piedmont and foothills of western North Carolina. A few of the storms produced brief severe weather in the form of large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported a person in the Oak Hill community received minor injuries after being struck by lightning while talking on a cell phone plugged into a wall charger.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front across the North Carolina Piedmont and foothills during the late afternoon. Some of the storms organized into a line or clusters and produced localized damaging winds into the evening hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported two people were injured due to lightning strike on Yorkmount Ridge Ln.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Ample, deep moisture along with afternoon heating produced a moderately unstable atmosphere across the region. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced large hail in North Georgia during the early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Overlook Trail causing an attic fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A procession of thunderstorm complexes moved slowly eastward across southwest Kentucky. These storms occurred ahead of a slow-moving upper level disturbance that tracked from the central Plains to the Lower Missouri Valley. The storms were fed by a very moist southwest flow in the low levels of the atmosphere. Surface dew points were in the lower 70's. The intensity and duration of the storms resulted in locally very heavy rainfall from three to four inches in some places.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a substation near Cadiz, causing several circuits to go down. About 12,000 utility customers lost power for up to an hour. Power went out throughout all of Cadiz and parts of three other counties.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed 10 cows standing under a tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Ten cows were killed when a pine tree they were standing under was struck by lightning.  According to the 2010 farming and ranch guide, the average value of a cow is  about $1.58 per pound.  The average cow weighs about 2,400 pounds.  Thus the damage loss is estimated at about $37,920.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: July rounded out with another shot of monsoon moisture and thunderstorms as high pressure shifted back westward over the Four Corners on the 29th and 30th. The main drivers for storms were terrain and outflow boundary collisions. Scattered thunderstorms occurred mainly over the mountains and deserts with wide-ranging rainfall totals from a few tenths of an inch to locally over 2 inches. Flash flooding occurred in Idyllwild, Timoteo Canyon, Calimesa/Moreno Valley, along with water flowing in the Fish and Vallecito Creeks in Anza Borrego State Park. A few storms went severe, including quarter-sized hail and wind damage in Calimesa and wind damage from a microburst in Palm Desert.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A spotter in Lucerne Valley reported a lightning strike onto power lines causing a power outage across a section of the Lucerne Valley area to the southeast of town. A transformer was burned out and tripped a number of circuit breakers on the nearby power grid causing the outage for over an hour in some locations.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms developed during the evening hours of July 12th over Minnesota. As these storms move southeast during the early morning hours of the 13th, they strengthened over central Wisconsin and started producing damaging winds. A mesonet reporting station near Necedah (Juneau County) measured a 62 mph wind gust and trees were blown down in Arkdale and Petenwell County Park (Adams County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house located near Lake Camelot sustained significant fire and water damage from a fire started by a lightning strike. The lightning strike also damaged the phone lines of a neighboring house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm along a frontal boundary produced a lightning strike which caused a house fire across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire in Smithfield.

As the boundary neared the area, the convection intensified and impacted central and southern Iowa in the evening to early morning hours. Two thunderstorm complexes moved through portions of central and southern Iowa with very heavy rainfall causing flash flooding. The severe thunderstorm complexes produced some hail but mainly strong damaging winds. Precipitable water values were near 2 inches in some areas with deep warm cloud depths during the event. This heavy rainfall further exacerbated conditions as some of the area had just received heavy rainfall in previous days. This led to some extended flooding for a few days and flooding on some area rivers. Several locations reported in excess of 4 inches of rain, while one location in Warren County reported over 7.50 inches of rainfall. The Emergency Manager for Marion County mentioned widespread reports of 8 to 10 inches with one report close to 12 inches of accumulated rainfall over the past few days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a telephone pole starting a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms tracked through much of central Nebraska on this Friday evening, north of Interstate 80. While many of the storms were strong, only one turned severe. Quarter size hail was reported in Sherman county around 9 p.m. CST. A lightning strike from a different storm snapped off a very large tree limb in Valley county, severely damaging two vehicles in the town of Ord.||A low pressure system was over the Canadian Prairies. These storms formed along and ahead of the associated cold front that was slowly advancing through the Northern and Central Plains. In the upper levels, the flow was generally west-southwest across the United States, with low amplitude. A subtropical high over the Gulf Coast, and a trough was over the West, with a closed low over Saskatchewan. The near-storm environment was characterized by surface temperatures in the upper 80s, with dewpoints in the lower to middle 70s. With mid-level lapse rates near 7.5 deg C/km, instability of significant with MLCAPE between 3000 and 4000 J/kg. Deep layer shear was around 35 knots.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, breaking off a large limb approximately 20 inches in diameter. This limb landed on 2 vehicles, causing significant damage to the cab of a pickup and the passenger compartment of a car.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms moved southward out of Kentucky along the I-65 corridor during the afternoon hours on July 28. These storms caused widespread wind damage across the eastern half of the Nashville metro area, resulting in tens of thousands of power outages including the Nashville International Airport. The BNA ASOS at the Nashville International Airport measured a peak wind gust of 54 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Hendersonville Medical Center. No significant damage was reported with normal operations continuing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a trough of low pressure produced damaging winds, large hail, two funnel clouds, and heavy rain across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small tornado touched down during the evening of July 16th southwest of Osage (Mitchell County). The tornado damaged three farms along its path where it flipped and damaged a garage, destroyed a barn and damaged house siding from flying debris. In addition, several trees and powerlines were downed and crops were damaged.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A machine shed was set on fire from a lightning strike southeast of New Haven.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of an unseasonably hot and humid air mass, an approaching cold front and strong winds aloft caused a squall line of severe thunderstorms to move through southern New Jersey during the very late afternoon and early evening of the 23rd. Estimated wind gusts as high as around 85 mph knocked down thousands of trees and caused structural damage to homes and vehicles, mainly from fallen trees. Four direct injuries were reported. Many roadways were closed because of downed trees into the 24th. Hardest hit were Burlington, Camden, Atlantic and in particular Gloucester County. Gloucester County declared a state of emergency. The region suffered approximately 31 million dollars in property damage and was declared a presidential disaster area.  A couple of severe thunderstorms also occurred in northwest New Jersey during the afternoon of the 23rd. While there was one report of a funnel cloud and a waterspout in Barnegat Bay, no confirmed tornadoes occurred.||The severe thunderstorm forced suspension of all PATCO commuter regional rail service in the Philadelphia suburbs as well as the New Jersey Transit Line between Philadelphia and Atlantic City. PATCO service was partially restored on the afternoon of the 24th with full service back on the 25th. Philadelphia to Atlantic City service was not restored until the 26th.||About 410,000 homes and businesses in southern New Jersey lost power.  The 280,000 customers that lost service in the Atlantic City Electric's service area represented a greater number than what occurred during Superstorm Sandy (220,000) and the Derecho of 2012 (206,000). The utility reported that several high transmission lines, five substations, twenty other transmission lines, hundreds of poles as well as 372 incidents of wire damage occurred. The utility received assistance from repair crews as far away as Ohio and New England. About 210,000 of its customers were still without power on the morning of the 24th, 180,000 the afternoon of the 24th, 121,500 the afternoon of the 25th, 84,000 the morning of the 26th and 48,000 the evening of the 26th. Thunderstorms on the 27th slowed restoration efforts and full restoration did not occur until the 30th. Public Service Electric & Gas reported 130,000 of its customers lost power. Full restoration occurred on the 26th. The utility's substations in Collingswood, Maple Shade, Medford and Southampton were damaged. Because of the prolonged power outages, water and ice distribution centers were opened and the American Red Cross assisted with displaced families. ||In Gloucester County, two comfort stations were opened by the Red Cross.  The worst wind damage occurred from Greenwich Township east through Mantua Township. About 11,000 homes and businesses were still without power on the morning of the 28th. In Camden County, the county dispatch office fielded ten times the normal call volume for assistance. The County Public Safety Office fielded 3,522 calls vs 2,432 calls for the entire duration of Superstorm Sandy. Hardest hit was the central part of the county from Gloucester Township east through Cherry Hill and Voorhees Township. In Burlington County, Evesham and Medford Townships were hardest hit.||Crop damage impacted mainly Camden and Gloucester Counties. Most of the initial damage was physical in nature to buildings, facilities and ditches. The impact of the wind on the crops themselves will not be known for months. The lack of hail cut down on the overall crop damage. Verizon cell phone service was also lost in parts of southwest New Jersey on the 23rd and restored by the 24th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Paulsboro refinery was struck by lightning which caused a loss of power. The refinery then off gassed. No evacuations were needed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper level system moved through northeast Alabama during the mid afternoon, producing a strong thunderstorm that resulted in lightning damage in DeKalb County, Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and damaged a home on County Road 505 in DeKalb County, Alabama.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Double barrel cold fronts helped trigger a series of showers and thunderstorms across southeast Pennsylvania during the morning of the 15th. Lightning struck a home in Orange County and injured a girl inside. The strike also started a small fire within the home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home within eastern Orange County and started a small fire. A teenager inside the home, using a computer was injured from the lightning strike. The girl was transported to a local hospital, where she was treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of slow moving thunderstorms moved across Indiana during the early morning hours July 12th and slowly tracked into southern Indiana shortly before dawn. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain fell in a 1 to 2 hour time frame, resulting in flash flooding across parts of the area. The system was also accompanied by an intense amount of lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained spotter reported that lightning struck the Sulphur Pentecostal Church. According to the Crawford County emergency manager, the church was destroyed and determined to be a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A boundary was pushing through the state with ongoing convection through central Iowa through the day. As the boundary neared the area, the convection intensified and impacted central and southern Iowa in the evening to early morning hours. Two thunderstorm complexes moved through portions of central and southern Iowa with very heavy rainfall causing flash flooding. The severe thunderstorm complexes produced some hail but mainly strong damaging winds. Precipitable water values were near 2 inches in some areas with deep warm cloud depths during the event. This heavy rainfall further exacerbated conditions as some of the area had just received heavy rainfall in previous days. This led to some extended flooding for a few days and flooding on some area rivers. Several locations reported in excess of 4 inches of rain, while one location in Warren County reported over 7.50 inches of rainfall. The Emergency Manager for Marion County mentioned widespread reports of 8 to 10 inches with one report close to 12 inches of accumulated rainfall over the past few days.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an LP tank and freon line starting a fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set fire to a power pole.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Considerable moisture from Hurricane Dolores to the south, along with monsoon moisture from the southeast resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms over most of the HSA for the 17th-19th. Rainfall ranged from one-half of an inch up to around 4 inches, including a record 1.71 inches at Lindbergh Field on the 18th (July 18 single-day and July monthly total). The San Diego River at Fashion Valley had 2 crests above monitor stage, 7.7 feet on the 18th and 8.8 feet on the 19th. The heavy rain resulted in a debris flow in the burn scar of Silverado Canyon, as well as flash flooding in Moreno Valley, Perris, and La Mesa on the 19th and a wet microburst in Tierrasanta on the 18th. The rain also caused the first Los Angeles Angels baseball game rain-out since 1995, and a rare 2-hour rain delay at the San Diego Padres baseball game. Over 2000 lightning strikes reported on July 18, some starting small brush fires. Microburst wind damage occurred in Tierrasanta, along with additional damage from a haboob in the Anza Borrego SP and wind damage from a thunderstorm in Palm Desert.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: CHP reported a lightning fire near the intersection of Dillon Rd. and Fargo Canyon Rd. northeast of Indio.
