EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late season storm brought showers, thunderstorms, and high elevation snow to the region. Thunderstorms brought heavy rain, copious amounts of small and accumulating hail, funnel clouds, and even a weak tornado to interior northern California.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local media reported that a man's home was struck by lightning on the afternoon of May 18. Media crews posted photos and video footage of damage to the owner's home which was estimated to be at least five thousand dollars worth of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two rounds of storms moved over the region from the early morning hours to late afternoon. The first round developed shortly after midnight along an elevated warm front moving northward from the Red River Valley into southwest Missouri. The second round of storms, associated with a meso-scale convective system, developed over western Kansas during the late afternoon of the 21st and moved across southwestern Missouri from mid-morning through late afternoon on the 22nd. Rainfall accumulations over an inch and a half occurred for some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home resulting in a fire that caused moderate damage to a home and garage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Arthur, which was moving over the outer banks of North Carolina, was forecast to continue moving northeastward off the Mid-Atlantic coastline. At the same time, the tail of Arthur, basically a trough of low pressure, extended into the southeastern portion of the country. This also combined with a mid to upper level area of low pressure moving into the Tennessee Valley and a trough of low pressure moving into the eastern Gulf of Mexico which allowed for a south southwesterly flow across South Florida. This allowed for the Gulf coast sea breeze to push inland as the east coast sea breeze remained pushed up against the east coast. This eventually lead to the development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across all of South Florida. The primary impacts with these storms were heavy rainfall and associated flooding, frequent lightning strikes, small hail, and gusty winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported a house fire due to a lightning strike near the corner of Ridge Dr and East Ave near North Naples. The family had safely evacuated the home by the time crews arrived on scene. Naples Fire-Rescue Department confirms a lightning strike hit the roof of a home, causing the flames. Damage totals are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: May 22nd - 24th, 2020 was an active few days with two main time frames of severe weather, and scattered severe weather reports punctuated elsewhere within these few days. The highlight of this period was damaging straight-line winds across Montague, Cooke and Grayson Counties with an EF-1 tornado in Bowie (Montague County) on May 22nd. These storms formed along an outflow boundary and front combined across our northwestern counties. The second significant round of convection was scattered diurnal storms on the 24th that produced a few instances of large hail. This second event occurred ahead of an upper level trough that set the stage for severe weather in the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was determined to be the cause of a house fire on Ignatius in Frisco.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On May 16th, a shortwave trough moved eastward across Texas providing an opportunity for thunderstorms to develop in a very unstable and moist environment. Several convective boundaries were in play, but the main event revolved around the line of storms that bowed out and produced strong winds and frequent lightning.  One early morning lightning strike burned down a large portion of a condominium complex on South Padre Island, leaving several million dollars in damage behind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike resulted in a structure fire at Gulfport Condominiums on South Padre Island. The fire was reported around 7 AM CDT. Time of strike was estimated by radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe weather outbreak occurred during the evening hours of April 8th. A line of severe thunderstorms moved through central Indiana intitially causing large hail and damaging winds. As the storms progressed, the hail threat gradually decreased with wind speeds rapidly increasing. In addition to widespread 60 to 70 mph winds, the line of storms had several mesovortices that led to areas of enhanced winds up to 90 mph and produced an EF-1 tornado in Mooresville, IN.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire department was responding to two fires in southern Johnson County that were started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cut off upper low slowly moved across Texas and produce multiple days of stormy weather. One lightning fatality occurred and wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A construction worker was building an outdoor kitchen in the Diamond D Ranch Subdivision near China when he was struck by lightning. He was hospitalized for 2 week before passing in early June.

Later on the 28th, a deep upper level trough in the Southern Plains allowed convection to initiate along a southward moving cold front. This line of severe storms produced damaging winds and severe hail in North and Central Texas overnight and into the morning of April 29th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A bowing line of severe thunderstorms tracked from western into central North Dakota during the evening of Tuesday, July 7th. Slightly after midnight CDT, July 8th, storms out ahead of the main bowing segment entered the Barnes/Griggs county area. Eventually the main bowing segment tracked through Griggs and Steele counties before weakening. North of the main bowing segment, strong winds also tracked through portions of Benson and Ramsey counties. After 3 am CDT, a second bowing line of storms took shape over Richland County, North Dakota, which tracked through Otter Tail County, Minnesota. This segment also produced very strong winds.

A motorist passing by witnessed the strike, called 911 and performed CPR on the victim until emergency officials arrived. The man was taken to a hospital and was improving later in the day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable summertime weather pattern allowed for the development of scattered showers and storms. A single storm increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds which downed trees.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14-year-old boy was struck in the chest by lightning while he and his family were walking from the beach to their hotel.  The boy had numerous burns and a hole in his shoe where the lightning exited his body.  He was put on a ventilator and did survive the strike.  The family was on vacation from Houston.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure and a very moist and unstable airmass led to clusters of thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning with a fire affecting the roof and attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A short-wave trough approached the region aloft while a pre-frontal trough moved into the area at the surface. producing severe thunderstorms in the afternoon. Dewpoints were between 70 and 75, providing ample moisture. With only marginal shear, the storms were slow-moving and produced torrential downpours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Farmington, lightning struck a pole on Main Street, bringing down the pole and wires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Dominant west coast sea breeze converged with east coast sea breeze near the St. Johns River basin. A moist airmass with PWAT near 2 inches and high low level instability produced a few strong to pulse severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Putnam EOC was struck by lightning. There was about $5k in damage. The time of damage was based on lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast moving Mesoscale Convective System raced south out of central Mississippi and spread damaging winds across southeastern Louisiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Smoke in a home due to a lightning strike in Pass Christian near Menge avenue and Fahrion Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving frontal boundary was draped across upstate New York and southern New England on July 22 with multiple waves of low pressure tracking along it. The mid-Atlantic was left in a warm sector air mass south of this front. This led to a very hot and humid day on July 22 with air temperatures rising into the 90s and dew point values near 70. This caused strong instability to develop. Shear values were not overly impressive, but an approaching shortwave disturbance from the Midwest did help to increase shear late in the day. This disturbance also served as forcing for convection to develop in the warm and unstable air mass. Widespread thunderstorm development occurred, with storms eventually developing into a mostly solid squall line. This line of storms produced numerous reports of wind damage across eastern Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Delmarva.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Breckenridge Dr in the Sicklerville section of Winslow Twp. This resulted in a fire which left the home uninhabitable due to smoke and water damage. No injuries were reported. Time estimated from lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the Ohio Valley along a slow moving boundary.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four workers were injured from a lightning strike at the Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developing during peak summertime heating. Some of the storms became briefly severe with damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to the 911 center damaged multiple radios.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convection initiated over the North Carolina mountains and foothills by midday and then spread east into the North Carolina Piedmont during early to mid afternoon. The first storms of the day produced some damaging downbursts with convection then becoming outflow dominated. By the late early evening, the combination of slow moving and training convection resulted in isolated flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near Lake Wheeler Road and Penny Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level low combined with strong afternoon heating resulting in a moderately unstable atmosphere to produce isolated strong to severe thunderstorms in the afternoon and early evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Hall County Emergency Manager reported a house struck by lightning in the 2000 block of Jack Bryant Circle with minor damage in the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the heat of the afternoon across the Pennyrile region of western Kentucky. Isolated strong winds, frequent lightning, and very heavy rain accompanied the storms. A weak low pressure system over the Tennessee Valley contributed to the formation of the storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening hours, isolated to scattered thunderstorms moved through central Indiana causing widespread tree damage to portions of Carroll county.  More isolated damage occurred across other portions of central Indiana.  Storms remained nearly stationary in west central Indiana where over 4 inches of rain fell.  Flash flooding occurred in Sullivan county which led to US 41 to remain closed for several hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Twelve apartments were damaged  due to a fire that was caused by a lightning strike. Heavy fire damage caused portions of the roof to collapse onto the ceiling above the second floor apartment units. A number of off-duty firefighters were called in to assist to put out the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low triggered severe thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire Department sent to Laurel Hill Drive for burning smell due to house struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low triggered severe thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Fox Hill Road in Warwick.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low triggered severe thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and damaged a small section of a fence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several clusters of strong to severe storms developed during the late afternoon and evening in a hot and unstable summer time environment. A few of these storms became severe and produced wind damage and lots of lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a telephone pole along Lassiter Mill Road, which caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm in advance of a weak frontal boundary produced a lightning strike which caused a house fire across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a house fire on Beach Haven Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving backdoor cold front drifted southwest through the mid-Atlantic region on July 6. Meanwhile, a shortwave vorticity impulse, one of several in a series, moved across the region during the day. A very hot and humid air mass was present ahead of the backdoor cold front, leading to the development of strong to extreme instability over the region. The approaching upper level disturbance allowed for the development of moderate wind shear over the region. Combined with the front, it also acted as a trigger mechanism for convection. Severe thunderstorms developed by early afternoon over eastern PA and southern and central New Jersey. These storms produced strong outflow boundaries which served to initiate additional severe convection. The result was a ring of fire in which outflow steadily propagated outward in all directions. This caused severe weather to spread radially outward from its origin near Philadelphia to much of New Jersey, other portions of eastern Pennsylvania, and Delmarva.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A structure fire due to a lightning strike was reported on Amandas Teal Dr.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low triggered severe thunderstorms across Southern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike to power pole resulting in power lines down causing power outages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system and its associated cold pool aloft led to the development of scattered thunderstorms, one of which caused a lightning injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 23 year old woman was injured by a lightning strike very near her house, while she was turning on a lamp on an enclosed porch on Depot Street in Bellingham.  She was treated and released by a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving cold front in a warm and humid air mass triggered strong to severe thunderstorms across Southern Connecticut.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a small electrical fire in a home in Bethel, CT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms occurred in the heat of the afternoon north of a weak surface boundary extending from western Tennessee to South Carolina. One of the storms produced a lightning strike that killed a construction worker in Evansville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A construction worker on the roof of a building was struck by lightning. The individual was a 34-year-old male who was on top of a tall building in downtown Evansville. The lightning hit the roof, causing damage about the size of a softball. The individual was near the damage site when he was struck. He received a burn mark on his chest but no other obvious injuries. The man was admitted to a hospital and then passed away two days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and storms formed on the south side of an area of low pressure that was moving eastward through New England. Some of these storms reached severe levels and produced damaging winds that brought down trees and blew off a barn roof.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in the 13000 block of Francisco Road and set it on fire. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Nearby Mesoscale Convective Systems across Alabama and the northern Gulf coast spread outflow boundaries that sparked clusters of severe thunderstorms across coastal and southern Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Home on fire due to lightning strike in the Magnolia Springs Subdivision off Canal Road near I-10.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved into the region and stalled out along the I-70 corridor. Numerous showers and storms developed along the boundary. Some of the storms became severe with reports of damaging winds and large hail. Also, a couple of the storms dropped very heavy rainfall causing flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: As storms were moving through the region, four men were struck by lightning while at Marquette Park in the Dutchtown neighborhood of St. Louis. Deep tropical moisture was in place with precipitable water values near record values in the 2.0-2.4 inch range. These ingredients produced a few strong storms with localized flooding rainfall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving through Central New York sparked showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 23rd. Some of these storms became severe and produced mainly tree damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck a tree and wires, which caused a fire off of Old Vestal Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front moved southeast into the region. Showers and storms developed ahead and along this feature, with some of the storms increasing to severe levels, producing damaging winds and large hail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With an area of high pressure centered near the Four Corners, drier air began to move into western New Mexico. Meanwhile, an upper-level trough that moved through northeastern New Mexico provided the lift necessary for a round of afternoon thunderstorms. As the thunderstorms moved southeast off the higher terrain, they increased in coverage and intensity. A few severe thunderstorms were observed in southeastern New Mexico where strong winds and thunderstorm wind damage were reported. The drier mid-level air that moved into western portions of the state was responsible for virga and gusty winds, and the Albuquerque Sunport recorded a 61 mph wind gust.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The heat/humidity energized the environment on the 29th, and this happened as a cold front slowly approached from Missouri. Ahead of the front, strong to severe thunderstorms popped up in northern Arkansas in the afternoon. There was an estimated 60 mph wind gust just northeast of Damascus (Van Buren County) and a 70 mph gust at Alicia (Lawrence County). Trees were blown down at the latter location, and also at Lynn (Lawrence County). As storms dropped to the south toward Little Rock (Pulaski County), a building on a school campus was struck by lightning in Pulaski Heights (Pulaski County). This started a fire that damaged the roof.||Later in the evening, the focus shifted to the west. A storm near Boothe (Scott County) cranked out golf ball size hail at the intersection of Highways 23 and 71. Trees were pushed onto Highway 28 just east of Hon (Scott County) and Mena (Polk County).||Two to more than four inches of rain fell in west central Arkansas. Since this part of the state had already been pounded with deluge after deluge in August, the soil was saturated and could not hold much liquid. A flash flood event unfolded in a hurry, and it was serious. Water was over Highway 23 at Elm Park (Scott County). Several roads were under water and impassible at Mena (Polk County). At the airport just southeast of town, 2.74 inches of rain fell in an hour. People on all-terrain vehicles were stranded by high water at Wolfpen Gap Campground just west of Big Fork (Polk County). Sections of Highways 270 and 27 were flooded near Mount Ida (Montgomery County).||Early on the 31st, the sky opened again in the west. Many roads were inundated with water at Waldron (Scott County). Flooding was also experienced on Highway 298 near Story (Montgomery County), and along several thoroughfares in Hot Springs (Garland County).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A prolonged and oppressive heat wave swept the Central Coast and Bay Area for almost a week from August 14th to August 19th with widespread record breaking temperatures observed across the region. This was caused by a strong high pressure system over the Desert Southwest that expanded westward into California. This dome of heat brought hot temperatures to the area for several days. Multiple days of triple digit afternoon highs were recorded inland with some coastal locations even reaching the mid 90s. Several days of hot and dry weather further dried fuels over the area increasing fire danger. During this event, a surge of monsoonal and tropical moisture from a former Tropical Storm advected northward with sufficient instability to generate multiple high based and dry thunderstorms that produced several thousand lightning strikes over the Greater Bay Area. Many locations saw wind gusts of 40-50 mph with isolated areas seeing gusts of 60-75 mph. This prompted the San Francisco Bay Area forecast office to issue a rare severe thunderstorm warning. These lightning strikes in combination with gusty and erratic outflow winds sparked hundreds of wildfires across the state of California. Several smaller fires combined to form complexes some of which are now among the largest wildfires in state history. Most of which were still actively burning at the end of August. Hundreds of thousands of acres have been burned with several hundred structures destroyed as well as a handful of deaths and injuries. Tens of thousands of residents were also forced to evacuate. Additionally, all of these wildfires burning simultaneously across the state gave the Bay Area the worst air quality in the world at one point.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Spotter reported lightning struck a redwood tree shearing off about 20 feet of it this morning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of showers and thunderstorms shifted southeast into Southeast Oklahoma, Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana during the morning hours of August 5th, along a weak upper level shortwave trough that progressed southeast over Arkansas. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Remnant tropical moisture from former Hurricane Genevieve in the Pacific brought thunderstorms to the Bay Area and Central Valley one week after the historic lightning storms that sparked hundreds of wildfires across the state. The Bay Area and Central Coast were mostly spared from the worst of this system with only a few thunderstorms producing lightning near the SCU Complex Fires and along the coast of Monterey County while the bulk of the moisture was carried elsewhere. Winds were also less erratic, though gusts of 25-45 mph were still observed around the region, and increases in fire activity were observed on some of the active wildfires.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Return flow into New Mexico ushered in deeper moisture across the state on August 2, 2020. Showers and thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain during the early afternoon hours then moved south with upper level high pressure centered over Arizona. The combination of northerly steering flow with strong shear, instability, and deep moisture allowed a few of these storms to become severe across central and eastern New Mexico through the early evening. Hail, severe microburst winds, heavy rainfall, and frequent lightning occurred with the strongest storms. Socorro and Roswell both reported peak wind gusts near 60 mph. A lightning strike destroyed an abandoned mobile home northeast of Roswell.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire from a lightning strike northeast of Roswell destroyed a residential structure. Structure was an abandoned mobile home so fortunately, no injuries were reported. Damage amounts are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon in northeast Alabama, with activity shifting slowly west through north central Alabama during the early evening hours. The strongest storms knocked down a few trees and damaged a chicken house.  Also, hail of dime to nickel sized was reported. Lightning struck a middle school in Decatur damaging a portion of brick tower structure and shattering a window from falling debris.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A school official reported a lightning strike damaged Austin Middle School in Decatur. From photos on social media, it appears siding from a brick tower at the front of the building was significantly damaged. A window was also shattered by falling debris. A newspaper reported that a radio link antenna was damaged, broken windows, and roof damage from falling bricks.

On the 16th, a weak cold front approached the area late in the afternoon accompanied by a line of thunderstorms. Near the town of Eagle Mills, a man was struck by lightning. Trees were also downed nearby. The next day featured storms transpired by a weak disturbance passing through the Ohio Valley. Storms once again weakened on approach, but did inflict a few trees to be blown down in Neelysville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Near the town of Eagle Mills, a man was struck by lightning. He was taken to the hospital in critical condition, but fortunately did recover from his injuries.

Given sufficient daytime heating, scattered thunderstorms developed across the east coast metro, one producing lightning that striked a construction worker.

Other workers at the school reported that the man was thrown about 15 feet by the lightning strike. He was taken to the hospital, but thankfully, listed in stable condition.||Time of the event is based on lightning strike archive data courtesy of Vaisala's lightning detection network which showed a cloud-to-ground strike in close proximity.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe winds gusting up to near eighty mph along with lightning caused some damage in north central and northeast South Dakota.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of a garage, putting a large hole in it. There was smoke, but no fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through portions of Central New York during the afternoon of the 25th ahead of a cold front. Some of these storms became severe and produced mainly tree and powerline damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm struck a car and resulted in a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 14-year old male was struck by lightning at the 1500 block of Neel School Road.  Little information was available.  Time and location of strike were confirmed by NOAA's NCEI Severe Weather Data Inventory.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14-year old male was struck by lightning at the 1500 block of Neel School Road.  Little information was available, but the injury was not believed to be serious.  Time and location of strike were confirmed by NOAA's NCEI Severe Weather Data Inventory.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An oppressively hot afternoon was followed by a raucous evening of thunderstorms for parts of the area. Some of these storms produced wind damage, especially across parts of Tarrant County where excessive wind damage occurred. A second round of storms moved in overnight, producing lightning damage to a few homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Frisco, TX fire department reported a house fire caused by a lightning strike at the 13881 block of Round Prairie Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered clusters of thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and early evening hours across portions of southeast Georgia near a stationary front and a weak area of low pressure. Some of the thunderstorms produced damaging winds and lightning strikes to structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Chatham County Emergency Management reported a lightning strike at a home on Barnacle Court. The extent of damage was unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered clusters of thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and early evening hours across portions of southeast Georgia near a stationary front and a weak area of low pressure. Some of the thunderstorms produced damaging winds and lightning strikes to structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Chatham County Emergency Management reported that a male was struck by lightning on Tropical Way. The extent of injury was unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered clusters of thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and early evening hours across portions of southeast Georgia near a stationary front and a weak area of low pressure. Some of the thunderstorms produced damaging winds and lightning strikes to structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Chatham County Emergency Management reported that lightning struck a home in the 300 block of Westbrook Lane, resulting in an appliance fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered clusters of thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon and early evening hours across portions of southeast Georgia near a stationary front and a weak area of low pressure. Some of the thunderstorms produced damaging winds and lightning strikes to structures.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Chatham County Emergency Management reported that a house was struck by lightning in the 100 block of Lagoon View Crossing, resulting in a structure fire.

Some of these storms produced wind damage, especially across parts of Tarrant County where excessive wind damage occurred. A second round of storms moved in overnight, producing lightning damage to a few homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Frisco, TX fire department reported a house fire caused by a lightning strike at the 5105 block of Promise Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: While on the western side of an upper trough, a surface low with associated fronts moved south through west-central Kentucky. This produced thunderstorms along the front, stretching west to east through Kentucky. As this line moved south through the Bluegrass region of Kentucky, areas of severe damage resulted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which brought down power lines and landed on a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very moist and unstable atmosphere combined with a weak upper level disturbance led to the development of showers and thunderstorms. Some of the storms became strong to severe with strong winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was hit by lightning and sustained minor smoke damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze storms produced lightning across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused fire to a child's playhouse. The structure was completely burned. The cost of damage was estimated for Storm Data inclusion. The time of damage was approximated by radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through the Ozarks producing scattered reports of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole causing a transformer to fail and power outages.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A small complex of storms that moved out of northeast South Dakota late Saturday morning caused a concentrated area of straight-line wind damage. The Canby, Minnesota airport measured a wind gust of 72 mph. These type of wind speeds continued across portions of Yellow Medicine and Lac Qui Parle counties where hundreds of trees and power lines were blown down. There was another wind gust of 68 mph at the Department of Transportation road sensor (Near Hanley Falls, MN) that went offline as the gust was recorded. ||The worst area occurred in the city of Granite Falls where winds tore open two roofs and allowed water to pour through ventilation ducts into classrooms and hallways, causing hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage to the Yellow Medicine East School District building. The Granite Fun restaurant and golf course also sustained damage with 55 to 60 trees blown down. Due to the extensive damage, the city of Granite Falls declared a state of emergency. ||Although wind damage occurred east of Granite Falls, mainly between Sacred Heart to Renville, this storm weakened as it moved eastward toward the western part of the Twin Cities.||A secondary area of storms developed across south central Minnesota during the mid-late afternoon near New Ulm, and produced another area of significant wind damage eastward toward Cannon Falls, and Red Wing. There was a swath of tree damage around Cannon Falls where one house lost its roof, with other having minor roof damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt struck a park shelter where 40 people were attending a birthday party. Three individuals were injured, but with non-life-threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening hours of August 3rd, widespread thunderstorms moved over much of Indiana.  One of these thunderstorms damaged a large tree via a lightning strike.  The 1 to 3 inches of rain caused brief flooding, but only limited impacts were noted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 18 inch tree was downed due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms resulted in a damaging lightning strike in central Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Baldwin County Emergency Manager reported a home struck by lightning in the 100 block of Wildwood Lane NE, resulting in a 6-inch hole in the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon on August 22nd. Lightning struck a home leading to damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 6000 block of SE Tater Peeler Road causing roof damage and destroying part of a chimney. Damage was estimated at $1,000 dollars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across western Wisconsin during the early morning of August 31st. A lightning strike from one of these storms started a fire at a apartment building in La Crosse (La Crosse County). One unit in the apartment building sustained heavy fire and smoke damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at an apartment building in La Crosse. One unit sustained heavy fire and smoke damage as a result.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved very slowly from the Rockies into the Plains during the first week of September, resulting in several days of showers and thunderstorms. Many storms became strong with gusty winds and hail, but the primary result was heavy rain and flooding. Unfortunately, a couple died in Temple Texas in a house fire that was started by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in the 7000 block of Rainbow Falls Drive in Frisco. The origin of the fire was from the roof. There was fire damage to the roof, attic, and second floor.  There was smoke and water damage throughout the structure. The damage is estimated at $500,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two days after Isaias made landfall, lightning caused two deaths.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were clearing debris after Hurricane Isaias when lightning struck and killed the two men. The lightning also sparked an attic fire at a neighboring house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved very slowly from the Rockies into the Plains during the first week of September, resulting in several days of showers and thunderstorms. Many storms became strong with gusty winds and hail, but the primary result was heavy rain and flooding. Unfortunately, a couple died in Temple Texas in a house fire that was started by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in the Boyd area of Wise County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved very slowly from the Rockies into the Plains during the first week of September, resulting in several days of showers and thunderstorms. Many storms became strong with gusty winds and hail, but the primary result was heavy rain and flooding. Unfortunately, a couple died in Temple Texas in a house fire that was started by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A couple died in an early morning house fire that fire investigators determined was started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a trough of low pressure produced damaging winds and a lightning strike across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused the Gabriel Chapel at Long Ridge Road to completely burn down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A home caught on fire and was destroyed in Sebastian after being struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Indian River County Emergency Management relayed a report of a home near the 1500th block of Crowberry Lane in Sebastian caught fire and was destroyed after being struck by lightning. There were no injuries or fatalities.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong lightning storm developed during the early afternoon a few miles southeast of Apopka. A lightning strike from this storm caused the fatality of a man in Apopka.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 58 year old man was struck and killed by a lightning strike while grilling outdoors next to a tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid-level impulse moved over the mid-Atlantic on August 24. A moist and moderate to strongly unstable environment was present as this disturbance moved through, which led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms. Weak shear prevented storms from becoming well organized, but the instability allowed a couple of storms to become strong to severe and produce a few instances of damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The local fire department responded to a house fire on Creek Rd due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the late morning hours across portions of southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms produced dangerous cloud-to-ground lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Beaufort County Emergency Manager reported that a male was struck by lightning in a house at 324 Old Oak Road. The individual was working inside a house under construction when lightning struck the house, causing moderate damage to an exterior wall. The individual was leaning against the wall, had no visible injuries, but was shaken up. He walked to the ambulance under his own power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Nocturnal storms became very electrically active as they moved through the lower Missouri River corridor.  Several positively charged cloud-to-ground strikes were noted in the area of the damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two homes in northern portions of Sioux City on the 3600 block of Jackson Street in the early morning hours. A small attic fire was started in one home, with significant damage to the electrical system of the other home. Property damage amounts are rough estimates.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A prefrontal trough ahead of a slow moving cold front led to a few thunderstorms developing on the afternoon of August 17. Moderate instability and weak shear generally limited storm coverage and severity, but a cluster of severe thunderstorms with damaging winds impacted portions of the Pennsylvania Poconos and northern New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church in North Catasauqua.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushing across central South Dakota and Nebraska ignited severe storms overnight. With elevated instability of 1000-1500 J/kg and an increasing low-level jet, numerous storms formed along the 700 hPa baroclinic zone with a few taking on bowing characteristics.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a single-story apartment building and initiated a fire which burned through the entire attic of the building. Crews from North Sioux City and three nearby cities attacked the fire for around two hours. All twenty apartments were severely damaged, displacing all residents. Property damage costs are rough estimates.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak front draped across the area along with an upper level disturbance shifting off the Southeast Coast led to the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Beaufort County emergency manager reported a lightning strike to a residence along Farnsleigh Road which produced minor roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 61 year old female was admitted to a hospital in Dallas on June 28th with injuries sustained from a lightning strike. She died from her injuries on July 2nd. No other information was provided or could be found.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Per hospital personnel, a 61 year old female was admitted to a hospital in Dallas on June 28th with injuries sustained from a lightning strike. She died from her injuries on July 2nd. No other information was provided or could be found.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms formed during the afternoon hours and caused wind damage across parts of the Metroplex. Lightning struck a teenager in Dallas County, and the male passed away a week later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16 year old male was struck by lightning while under a tree in a yard. He died from his injuries on July 9th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A sea breeze circulation developing within a moderately unstable environment led to a few severe thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina during afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Beaufort County emergency manager reported a tree struck by lightning and starting a small brush fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During a time without any major weather systems moving through the region, a moist atmosphere with differential heating and remaining outflows from earlier thunderstorms was enough for thunderstorms and heavy rain to develop across central Kentucky. This resulted in widespread wind damage, flooding, and even fires from lightning. An elderly man drowned and his wife was injured trying to drive through flood waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in a small building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms produced hail and heavy rain across portions of the Wasatch Front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck behind a man and a woman walking in Eagle Mountain City. The man was knocked unconscious and flown to a nearby hospital. The woman was also impacted, but not hurt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A sea breeze circulation along with a moderately unstable atmosphere led to the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law enforcement relayed a report of a structure fire resulting from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak stationary front along with a moderately unstable atmosphere between an upper trough of low pressure inland and a ridge of high pressure offshore led to severe thunderstorms across Southeast Georgia during afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Effingham 911 Call Center reported a tree down by a lightning strike along Highway 119 North.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southeast Minnesota was hit with two rounds of severe storms during the afternoon and evening of June 2nd. The first round developed in the late afternoon and produced large hail that reached 2 inches in diameter in and around Winona and Pickwick (Winona County). The second round produced some sporadic wind damage. Three trees were blown down onto a house in Houston (Houston County), a semi was blown over north of Austin (Mower County) and an estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred southwest of Dover (Olmsted County). A fire at a Rochester (Olmsted County) apartment complex was started by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at an apartment building on the east side of Rochester.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of forcing associated with a mid-level shortwave and ample moisture/instability led to the development of thunderstorms across Southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A report relayed via amateur radio indicated lightning struck and brought down a tree off Highway 196.

The first round developed in the late afternoon and produced large hail that reached 2 inches in diameter in and around Winona and Pickwick (Winona County). EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a transformer fire in Lyle that led to a power outage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front and string mid-level disturbance moved across a marginally unstable air mass across the region during the afternoon of October 10th. Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed and moved across northern NY into VT, some of these storms produced a brief burst of damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was the determined cause of a 4 acre wildfire on Arrowhead mountain.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front along with a rigorous mid level disturbance triggered thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House struck by lightning on Cimorelli Drive with fire department on scene confirming a fire in the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level impulse moving through the area combined with plenty of heat and humidity to allow for the development of afternoon thunderstorms. A few of these storms produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a barn fire, resulting in hay bales and tractor trailers full of lumber stored within the barn to completely burn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Remnants of a tropical cyclone produced numerous showers and thunderstorms over east Alabama.  Some of the storms produced winds gusts of 40 to 50 mph and frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Home located on Lee Road 2087 struck by lightning with ensuing fire.  Two women struck by lightning on the same road.  Both survived with unknown injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed north of a warm front draped across northern Illinois during the afternoon hours across central and east-central Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced marginally severe hail and a lighting strike caused a power pole to become engulfed in flames in Appleton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a power pole to become engulfed in flames on Appleview and Fuji Drive in Appleton.  The power pole and attached light were damaged due to the fire and had to be replaced.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mid-level troughing advanced eastward across the region, with a frontal boundary to the north, keeping South Florida well within an unstable airmass. Several perturbations aloft brought cooler temperatures that aided in the potential for stronger convection. As daytime heating increased, storms developed across Palm Beach. Lightning from one of these storms that struck a home, causing damage. Thankfully, no injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house at the intersection of Lucky Lane and Southridge Road in Delray Beach. There was some charring to the roof and attic as well as electrical damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak front along with ample moisture and instability led to a few strong/severe thunderstorms across Southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported lightning struck a transformer and brought a tree down on Salt Creek Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread thunderstorms moved across central Indiana during the afternoon and early evening hours of October 23rd.  Some of these storms briefly produced isolated damaging wind gusts and large hail with the strongest storms across south central Indiana.  Several rounds of storms moved over the same areas at times, but no significant flooding impacts were noted other than some minor flooding in areas that easily flood.  One particularly strong storm produced a wall cloud that was seen south of Brownstown where a tornado warning was in place.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two non-life threatening injuries after lightning struck an asphalt roller. The driver and a nearby worker were checked out by first responders and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface low to the northwest of Iowa allowed for convection to develop in the warm sector and along the surface boundary as it pushed across northern Iowa through the afternoon and evening of the 21st. These storms caused damaging winds and large hail across northern and central Iowa. Localized areas received heavy rain that resulted in flooding overnight. Another shortwave embedded within the parent longwave trough allowed for additional rain across the state on the 22nd that lasted through the afternoon. This second round of rain exacerbated the ongoing flooded areas, resulting in flooding that lingered into the morning of the 24th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Coop observer reported that lightning hit a walnut tree 100 ft. from the house and fried the well pump.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With moist, unstable air in advance of a late season cold front, showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the frontal boundary. Some of these thunderstorms brought strong winds, lightning and hail to the Rio Grande Valley, and as the front slowed and stalled, heavy rainfall brought flooding to Hidalgo County during the afternoon of June 3rd.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damage was reported to a house and adjacent cinder block pole on the property near US 281 in Edinburg with no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a trough of low pressure produced damaging winds across portions of central, south central and eastern Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire on North Oaks Drive in Hanover.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed in response to an upper level low situated over the region. A few of these storms became severe with a few reports of downed trees and a report of a destroyed barn due to lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn on Cottrell Road was destroyed by a fire caused by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm passed over Manassas, Virginia shortly after 1:30 PM producing frequent lightning. A man was struck by lightning in a parking lot.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One man was struck by lightning in a parking lot outside of a grocery store.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms moving through DC produced lightning. One of the strikes hit two people, leading to non-life threatening injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two military personnel were struck by lightning shortly after midnight local time, leading to non-life threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving through the region sparked showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours of Sunday, June 28th, 2020. A few storms became severe with two reports of hail and one report of a barn roof being damaged in Montgomery county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A portion of a barn roof was damaged due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 18th in Central New York around the northern periphery of an upper level low. Lightning strikes from some of these storms caused some trees and homes to catch on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm caused a tree to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 18th in Central New York around the northern periphery of an upper level low. Lightning strikes from some of these storms caused some trees and homes to catch on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm caused a house to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 18th in Central New York around the northern periphery of an upper level low. Lightning strikes from some of these storms caused some trees and homes to catch on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm caused a house to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 18th in Central New York around the northern periphery of an upper level low. Lightning strikes from some of these storms caused some trees and homes to catch on fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm caused a tree to catch on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northward retreating frontal boundary allowed for generally east to southeasterly flow to keep abundant moisture in place across South Florida. Morning thunderstorms developed over Miami-Dade, with lightning striking a home, causing some damage. Thankfully no one was injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An article from Local 10 News reported a house near the intersection of Bryon Ave and 92nd Street was struck by lightning from a thunderstorm that pushed across the town of Surfside in the morning.  Lightning struck a tall structure on the roof, blowing up the concrete, which landed in six or seven different places and even hit his SUV, though it only caused a few scratches. Thankfully, no one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple periods of heavy rainfall occurred across eastern Kentucky as an upper level disturbance nudged westward toward the western Appalachians. This resulted in flash flooding across portions of Pulaski and McCreary Counties, while a locally strong to severe thunderstorm occurred near Williamsburg. Additionally, a commercial vehicle was struck by lightning in Whitley County along Interstate 75.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet reported a commercial vehicle struck by lightning just south of Williamsburg on Interstate 75. This resulted in the vehicle taking out 150 feet of guardrail before going into an embankment and blocking the right southbound lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot, humid conditions prevailed across the region.  Without much atmospheric forcing, it took a sea breeze boundary to set off strong thunderstorms, which became severe in eastern Massachusetts during the afternoon hours.  Localized flooding also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 62-year old woman was struck by lightning. She endured a side flash after lightning struck a tree near her.  She was alert and breathing at the scene but was transported to a hospital for further evaluation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed one person and injured another in a Durango subdivision.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 65-year-old woman was killed and her friend was injured when struck by lightning while walking in the 200 block of Silver Queen South in the Edgemont subdivision. The lightning bolt first struck a tree and moved laterally to strike the woman.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were struck by lightning and critically injured while fishing at Hobe Sound Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Martin County Fire Rescue and local broadcast media reported that two men were struck by lightning while fishing at Hobe Sound Beach. The lightning strike occurred at approximately 1530 LST, 200 yards north of a lifeguard tower. First responders arrived to find the two men injured and both were transported to local hospitals in critical conditions.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms rolled across western Wisconsin during the late afternoon and evening of June 2nd. Some of these storms produced very large hail ranging in size from 1 inch up to 2.5 inches in diameter. One of the hardest hit areas by the hail was Holmen (La Crosse County) where it was estimated that between 4,000 and 5,000 homes would need new roofs. Up to golf ball sized hail also fell near Pray (Jackson County) and near Dodge (Buffalo County). The storms also produced damaging winds with trees blown down across parts of Jackson, Monroe, Vernon, Adams and Juneau Counties. In Tomah (Monroe County), the roof canopy was blown off a grandstand at the county fairgrounds. The metal siding was ripped off a grain mill southeast of Ontario (Vernon County). More than 6,600 customers in the La Crosse area (La Crosse County) were without power after the storms moved through.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a garage just southwest of Sparta. The resulting fire destroyed the garage. The fire spread to a nearby house along a downed tree with the house suffering moderate fire and smoke damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms moved over Gunnison, Colorado with lightning striking near a campground. The lightning directly impacted a local campground where 3 campers were injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three individuals camping near Gunnison Colorado were struck by lightning as a thunderstorms passed through. All three were injured, with one 15 year old male seeking medical treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A major severe weather event by Pacific Northwest standards occurred over central and northeast Oregon and southeast Washington on May 30th. A powerful upper level storm system moved across the area during the afternoon and evening helping to trigger severe thunderstorms. The airmass was unusually unstable for this area of the country with surface dewpoints well into the 60s. With strong upper level winds in place the stage was set for numerous fast moving intense storms through the afternoon and early evening. Numerous reports of damaging winds were received across southeast Washington as the storms moved through.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Cattle company near Pasco lost 6 registered Charolais cattle during a lightning storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level disturbance interacted with a moist and unstable airmass to produce numerous thunderstorms across West Tennessee during the afternoon hours on August 31st. A lightning strike resulted in an injury in Henderson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike occurred near the NIDEC plant in northeast Lexington.  One injury resulted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary stalled over the mid-Atlantic on the overnight of September 2 and lifted northward slightly during the day on September 3. A robust shortwave trough was also approaching during the day. This combination caused a high shear environment to develop, with good moisture also present. However, instability was marginal due to considerable cloud cover over the area. In addition, multiple rounds of storms associated with different sources of lift tended to work against each other, as storms generally struggled to organize and become dominant. However, given the high shear some storms still became strong to severe and produced instances of damaging wind.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A residential fire occurred due to a lightning strike on Barksdale Court. Time estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another in a series of strong upper level troughs pushed through the southeast states, resulting in another enhanced risk of severe storms from the Storm Prediction Center.  The tri-state area was hit fairly hard again, with numerous reports of wind damage documented along with several tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and unstable air mass was advected into the area ahead of a weak cold front. A weak disturbance aloft triggered a round of strong to severe storms during an afternoon followed by another round of strong storms the following morning with the passage of a front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a fire at the Congregation Gates of Prayer Synagogue on North Weeks Street in New Iberia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and unstable air mass was advected into the area ahead of a weak cold front. A weak disturbance aloft triggered a round of strong to severe storms during an afternoon followed by another round of strong storms the following morning with the passage of a front.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Acadia Parish Sheriff's Department reported lightning struck a oil tank on Old Spanish Trail in the Midland/Mermentau area. The strike resulted in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed across eastern parts of the Phoenix metro during the early morning hours of the 20th. While these thunderstorms were isolated in nature, some produced cloud to ground lightning strikes, one of which struck a tree and resulted in some damage to a home in Mesa around 0400 MST. No injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Early morning isolated thunderstorms produced cloud to ground lightning strikes, one of which struck a tree and a house in Mesa near Main Street and Horne. The lightning resulted in a bedroom window being shattered along with a shutter being torn off from the house. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After some isolated thunderstorms moved across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on December 5, a line of severe thunderstorms moved across Middle Tennessee during the early morning hours on December. This line of thunderstorms produced 5 tornadoes and numerous reports of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two structure fires from lightning strikes were reported in the Martins Chapel area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a moviegoer at an east metro drive-in theater as storms moved through the area. The man was hit about 10:25 p.m at the Vali-Hi Drive-In on just north of Interstate 94 in Lake Elmo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a moviegoer at an east metro drive-in theater as storms moved through the area. The man was struck about 10:25 p.m CDT, Thursday, August, 5th at the Vali-Hi Drive-In just north of Interstate 94 in Lake Elmo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms resulted in widespread severe weather and flash flooding over eastern New York on Wednesday September 15, 2021.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree reportedly caught on fire due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe storms moved across the state on April 7th and again on April 9th and 10th associated with the passage two cold fronts. Large hail and damaging winds were the main impacts noted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house setting it on fire. The home was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In the overnight hours on May 17th into the early morning on May 18th, a cluster of slow moving severe thunderstorms associated with a weak mid-level disturbance drifted east across southeastern Louisiana. Ample overnight instability and weak steering flow resulted in damaging wind gusts, flash flooding and a few isolated weak tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on El Ranchitos Avenue causing a gas line to ignite on a water heater.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable environment brought scattered thunderstorms producing frequent cloud-to-ground lightning to the San Juan Mountains in Southwest Colorado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three firefighters working during the mopping up stages on the Johnny Canyon Fire east of Baldy Mountain were caught in a thunderstorm near the 9500 foot level. The thunderstorm intensified overhead with heavy rain, hail and continuous lightning. The crew decided to hunker down in place and wait for the storm to pass. After hearing a large thunderclap, the crew decided they needed to move down the mountain to a safer location. While hiking out, the crew passed through a metal fence gate when one firefighter saw a lightning strike very close by. He saw it split between a tree and the metal fence and immediately felt tingling and cramping in his feet and lower back. Another firefighter was in the process of latching the metal fence gate when he felt a jolt go through his harm and his arm tingling. There were no serious injuries between the three firefighters and all refused treatment, even though they were shivering badly and were experiencing the early stages of hypothermia from being exposed to the heavy rain and hail.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in damage over southern Vermont on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a fire and leveled a home in Woodford, VT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms with heavy rain produced flash flooding across portions of northern Arizona.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning stuck near the Bright Angel Trailhead. Four people were injured and two of them were hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina throughout the afternoon. A number of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts and some hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported a lightning strike caused a boat to catch on fire at a marina on Lake Hartwell.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Fred made landfall in the Florida Panhandle on the 16th and lifted steadily north through Georgia and into the southern Appalachians during the 16th and throughout the 17th. Tropical moisture and strong southeast upslope flow into the Blue Ridge mountains resulted in widespread showers and some thunderstorms producing extremely heavy rainfall rates. By the time the rain tapered off by the end of the 17th, 24-hour rainfall amounts of 5-12 inches were reported across portions of the mountains and foothills. This was in addition to a small area of 5-10 inch amounts that fell across portions of the southern North Carolina mountains during the morning of the 16th. The result of this rainfall was significant to catastrophic flash flooding across portions of the French Broad and Pigeon River basins, including some of the worst flooding to impact these areas in almost 20 years. The most severe flooding occurred in portions of southern and central Haywood County, where a number of fatalities and hundreds of millions of dollars and damage occurred. In addition, a brief tornado touched down in Iredell County and tracked into Alexander County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire dept reported lightning struck a roof causing a fire and roof collapse. Significant interior damage was caused due to the fire and torrential rain falling in the open roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted north through the Mid-South during the day on April 9th. As a result, moist and unstable air pushed into the region ahead of a potent upper-level disturbance approaching from the Central Plains. A couple of lines of severe storms with large hail ignited and pushed across Northeast Arkansas and West Tennessee during the early evening hours. Another line developed across North Mississippi and rolled through later in the evening with damaging winds, large hail, and some flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple fire departments called in to extinguish a fire at a business on Mulberry Avenue in Selmer. The fire was believed to be started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Elsa approached the mid-Atlantic states from the south on July 8. Downstream of Elsa, a warm and moist environment was present. A slow moving frontal boundary also resided over northern New Jersey, northern Pennsylvania, and into New York. This frontal system provided forcing for convective development over the mid-Atlantic, in fairly close proximity but unrelated to Tropical Storm Elsa. With strong instability and weak to moderate wind shear, some of the storms became severe as they organized into linear and multi-cellular clusters. Deep layer southerly flow in advance of Elsa caused storms to move northward as opposed to a more typical eastward motion. Damaging wind was the main hazard associated with these storms, with several strong downbursts noted. Storm activity eventually weakened and moved north of the region by evening as Elsa moved in.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole and started a fire on Mount Vernon Rd. Time estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorm associated with a cold front produced a lightning strike which caused damage to a home across portions of southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused damage to a home along Sunbeam Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: One of two severe weather events occurred across the state from the late night hours of Nov 10th into the early morning hours of the 11th. A weakening line of storms progressed across Arkansas during that time. A severe storm impacted portions of Cleburne County shortly after 1 am CST on the 11th when strong winds blew a mobile home off its foundation and a nearby home sustained roof damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on north Cedar Street was struck by lightning, causing a fire. The residents were displaced , but no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Veering southerly flow ahead of an approaching cold front helped to advect a rich plume of low-level moisture across South Florida. As showers and thunderstorms associated with the front pushed through the area and stalled, this translated into heavy rainfall and flooding across east coast metro. Also, lightning strikes from one storm struck and damaged the Broward Water Treatment Plant.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Broward County 2A Water Treatment Plant located on Copans Road in Pompano Beach. The lightning damaged a number of mechanical, electrical, and instrumentation components including a high service pump, the control modules for two electronically actuated valves, and two programable logic controllers. The failure of this combination of items impeded their ability to fully pressurize the potable water distribution system, resulting in a precautionary boil water order to portions of Broward County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable airmass in place across the Mid-South helped to fuel severe storms ahead of an advancing cold front and deep upper-level trough swinging into the Central Plains. A line of severe storms moved from Arkansas across northern parts of the Mid-South during the early morning hours of May 4th. There was widespread wind damage and a few weak tornadoes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning and caught fire on Country Club Lane near Paris.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the late evening hours of June 12th, a series of thunderstorms slowly moved through central Indiana from the north.  An outflow boundary in eastern Marion county led to additional thunderstorm growth north of Indianapolis that eventually would bring damaging winds and large hail to portions of Indianapolis and western Hancock County. Slow storm motions and backbuilding led to some areas to receive up to 3 inches of rain which caused isolated flash flooding.  Over 20,000 power outages were caused by the thunderstorms with some noted to be from lightning strikes and others from tree and power pole damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a large tree near the intersection of Westview St and Taft Avenue. This and other tree damage in town caused over 1500 power outages in Muncie.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into Louisiana with scattered storms. A few tornadoes occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire resulted from a lightning strike near Mansura.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very hot and humid air mass remained in place over the mid-Atlantic on June 9, following several days of unusually hot and humid conditions for the season. Similar to the previous day, afternoon thunderstorm development occurred in the mid-Atlantic mainly due to the influence of a weak cold front to the north and a weak surface trough. Like the previous day, storms were disorganized due to weak wind fields and a lack of forcing. However, the strong to extreme instability allowed some storms to briefly become severe with a threat for damaging winds, hail, and torrential rain. Convection gradually dissipated during the evening hours with the loss of daytime heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man in his 70s was struck and killed by lightning at Burlington Country Club. This was the first documented case of a fatal lightning strike in the United States in 2021. Time estimated from radar and dispatch calls.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Light southwesterly flow coupled with abundant moisture brought widespread showers and storms to West Central Florida. Unfortunately, one of those thunderstorms produced a fatal lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast Media reported a fatal lightning strike that hit a man working on a roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary became the focus of a line of strong to severe thunderstorms across the area. This line was long-lived and produced dozens of reports of wind damage, flash flooding and even multiple house fires caused by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire on Enterprise Road in Liberty.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon hours, a band of thunderstorms produced a lightning strike causing damage in a residential neighborhood of Madison. During the evening hours, a second broken line of thunderstorms, along with clusters of thunderstorms moved through north Alabama and and southern middle Tennessee during the late afternoon through mid evening hours. The line of thunderstorms produced pockets of higher winds that produced sporadic damage to trees and power lines.  Power outages resulted in parts of the area, including northern Madison County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and a residence at the corner of Hickory Ridge Road and Miller Road in Madison.  The tree exploded and the home's front windows were blown out.  Also, electronics were reportedly damaged at several of the surrounding homes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved in and stalled while multiple upper level disturbances moved through. High moisture levels and ample lift provided a few days of flooding and severe thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer resulting in a fire of a near by tree and fence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms brought a few impacts to the Florida panhandle with a report of a power line blown down in Calhoun county, as well as lightning striking a road in Walton county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An accident occurred on I-10 near mile marker 81 due to lightning striking the road and sending debris through the windshield of a pickup truck.  Two injuries resulted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours within a tropical airmass ahead of newly formed Tropical Storm Mindy centered in the northeast Gulf of Mexico. A few storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Beaufort County Sheriff's Office reported a couple of homes struck by lightning around the Beaufort area. One home that was struck was located on Isabelle Boulevard near Parris Island Gateway and the other was at 3060 Mink Point Boulevard. The degree of damage to the homes is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into the Mid-South and interacted with an unstable airmass to produce a broken line of showers and thunderstorms that moved across the area from late afternoon into the evening on May 9th.  The line interacted with an old outflow boundary to produce a weak tornado in Tipton County. Further south, a bowing segment within the line produced a swath of wind damage across North Mississippi.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A farmer was inside a milk barn on Reed Road near Dyer. The farmer was milking cows when lightning struck the barn. He was holding a metal railing attached to the barn. The farmer was transported to the local hospital and only suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms generated gusty outflow winds, heavy rain and frequent lightning across eastern Utah on June 24th. Two people were struck by lightning while recreating in Dead Horse State Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck by lightning while recreating on the West Rim Trail at Dead Horse State Park. Crews found both individuals in critical but stable condition before they were transported to Moab Regional Hospital for care.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms caused a lightning strike which resulted in damage to a home in Calhoun county.  In addition, there was isolated minor flooding reported in Bay county due to heavy rainfall.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Nettle Ridge Fire Department Facebook page reported a structure fire due to lightning on NW County Road 375 North.  Damage cost was estimated.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Highway 110 in Fremont during the late evening hours, causing it to burn to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak disturbance moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania, producing some showers and thunderstorms. One storm in Susquehanna County became severe and knocked down trees and powerlines.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a passing thunderstorm struck an animal hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low and a cold front near the surface resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms across much of North and Central Texas. Several storms produced very large hail and damaging winds west of I-35. The northern portions of Tarrant County were hit the hardest with large hail up to 3.25 in diameter. Hail damage estimates from this storm were over $500 million. The large hail damaged and/or shattered roofs, windows and cars.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged several lift station pumps for the City of Comanche.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few isolated thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the late evening hours of the 16th. One of these storms passed over the Duluth area bringing a few reports of nickel-sized hail along with a lightning strike that hit a parked vehicle and caused extensive damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A message was received via Facebook reporting that lightning struck a vehicle or near a vehicle that was parked in the lot at a local warehouse store. The strike caused the battery to burn causing extensive damage to the vehicle and rendering it inoperable. The car belonged to a manager at the store and surveillance video was used to confirm how the fire started and the time the strike occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Warm and unstable air in advance of a cold front led to thunderstorms developing across southeast Georgia and near Tybee Island Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The city of Tybee Island reported a fatality of a female teenager who was struck by lightning while swimming in the water near 17th Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front collided with warm and humid conditions, which then triggered scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening across Central New York. Many storms became severe and produced damaging winds as well as 1 inch hail. While fallen trees and utility wires made up most of the damage, there was also some minor structural damage as well. One storm became tornadic as a weak, short-lived tornado passed near Dryden in Thompkins County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a tree, blowing out the bottom. The top of the tree caught on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A number of severe thunderstorms developed across the area on the evening of June 15, resulting in many reports of tree damage, 1-inch hail, and building damage due to both winds and lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home in Fort Bend County caught fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few thunderstorms developed over eastern New Jersey on August 30. Marginal environmental conditions precluded any severe weather in association with these storms. However, they approached several locations along the New Jersey Shore during the mid to late afternoon. Beaches were crowded on what had previously been a sunny and warm day, creating a dangerous situation due to the lightning being produced by the approaching storms. Sadly, a Seaside Park lifeguard was killed and several others in the same area were injured by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Seven individuals were struck by lightning in South Seaside Park, with one fatality.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across northeast Iowa during the early morning of April 6th. A lightning strike from one of these storms started a house fire outside of Charles City (Floyd County). The damage to the home was contained to the attic and roof. No injuries occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire outside of Charles City was started by a lightning strike as thunderstorms moved across northeast Iowa during the morning of April 6th. The damage from the fire was limited to the attic and roof of the home and no injuries occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow-moving warm front lifted north into the Mid-South during the morning hours of March 17th with numerous showers and thunderstorms. Heavy rain produced some flash flooding and there were a couple of severe weather reports along with a couple of damaging lightning strikes. The front stalled across the area during the day with southern parts of the Mid-South, especially northeast Mississippi, becoming quite unstable during the afternoon hours. Additional storms developed during the late afternoon and evening as a cold front pushed into the region resulting in numerous severe storms, including a few tornadoes, across Northeast Mississippi along with flash flooding across the Memphis and Jonesboro areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Killough Street causing exterior damage and blowing out an interior wall.
