EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three homes were struck by lightning within a one-hour period in the Bruton Branch and Pickwick areas. Two homes had a fire in the wall and received minor damage and the third smelled of smoke.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters and line segments of heavy thunderstorms, a couple of which turned severe, overspread north Alabama during the predawn hours of the 25th.  These storms produced 2 to 3 inches of rain, mainly south of the Tennessee River, resulting in excessive runoff and flash flooding. Flash flooding closed a portion of I-65 in Cullman and several other roads were flooded or washed out in Cullman County. Also, isolated large hail and damaging winds were reported with a couple of these thunderstorms in northeast Alabama.  During the afternoon hours, additional strong thunderstorms produced additional excessive rainfall resulting in more flooding.  Rainfall totals were in the 3 to 5 inch range, generally south of the Tennessee River corridor.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A law enforcement officer was struck by lightning while evaluating flooding at Mars Hill Bible School and putting up barricades at the intersection of Chisolm Road and Gresham Road. The officer suffered burns and was treated at a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted north across the Mid-South during the morning hours of March 27th. Numerous thunderstorms resulted in heavy rain near the Tennessee/Mississippi line and some flash flooding along with an isolated damaging wind report. The front continued to lift north during the morning along with the complex of showers of thunderstorms. After a brief break during the early afternoon, thunderstorms started to redevelop in the moist and unstable airmass across east-central Arkansas, Southwest Tennessee, and Northeast Mississippi. Initially, storms developed in clusters with large hail, several weak tornadoes, and flash flooding from eastern Arkansas to the Tennesee River in West Tennessee. The clusters of storms gradually transitioned into a line with mainly damaging winds stretching from the Tennessee/Mississippi line into Northeast Mississisppi from the evening of March 27th into the early morning hours of March 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a structure fire in Gibson County.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A quasi-stationary front meandered north of the local area with zonal flow aloft. A dominant west coast sea breeze regime focused higher thunderstorm potential across the eastern portion of NE FL in the afternoon and evening hours, with a few pulse severe storms producing lightning and some wind damage near sea breeze and outflow boundary mergers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pine tree, which fell onto a home. The home then caught fire. The event was at 10733 Orchard Walk Place near Hartley Road in Mandarin. The time of the event was based on radar and lightning data. The cost of the damage was unknown but it was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data. The estimate is likely underestimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front across central Florida on 2/6 lifted northward as a surface low developed along the front in the eastern Gulf of Mexico. The warm front progressed northward to just south of the I-10 corridor during the night 2/6 into the early morning hours of 2/7 as the surface low track east along the front and then offshore of the local Atlantic coast early in the morning 2/7. Very strong shear was in place across the area with elevated instability with mid level lapse rates 7-7.5 deg C/km.  Some wind damage with gusts of 40-50 mph was reported as well as hail as large as quarter size. Widespread rainfall of 2-4 inches occurred in a couple of swaths across NE FL within 24 hrs which produced some localized flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that caused part of the tree to fall onto a home in Marion Oaks. The caused minor roof damage. The time of damage was based on radar. The cost of damage was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms caused a lightning strike which resulted in significant damage to a home in Houston county.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Lucy Fire Department Facebook page reported a residential structure fire due to lightning with significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused minor damage to a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Trained spotter reported a lightning strike to a mobile home on Railroad Ave. There were no injuries.  No structural damage occurred but an electrical box was damaged.  Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of thunderstorms moved across eastern New York during the afternoon and evening of the 26th. There were several reports of trees and wires downed due to thunderstorm winds. Power outages totaled around 2,100 in Albany and Schenectady Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which fell on a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very hot and humid conditions were in place.  Scattered thunderstorms occurred in the afternoon and early evening hours.  A few became severe and also produced localized flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Hatfield, lightning hit a power pole at Main Street and Maple Street, knocking out power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very hot and humid conditions were in place.  Scattered thunderstorms occurred in the afternoon and early evening hours.  A few became severe and also produced localized flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Georgetown, a house was struck by lightning on Lakeshore Drive, resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very hot and humid conditions were in place.  Scattered thunderstorms occurred in the afternoon and early evening hours.  A few became severe and also produced localized flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Webster, lightning caused a 2.5-story house to catch fire on School Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms moved across the area in the evening through late night hours and produced wind damage, lightning damage and some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire that produced severe damage to a home on Golden Sunset Circle near The Woodlands Country Club.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were  a few reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A transformer was struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An embedded shortwave within a longwave western US trough moved across the midwest, merging with a plume of increasing moisture transport out of the south. While no severe weather was reported, thunderstorms developed in the afternoon. Unfortunately one storm produced lightning that struck the Calhoun County court house and produced many thousands of dollars in damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported a lightning strike to the the county court house, resulting in over 20,000 dollars in damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe storms with heavy rainfall developed during the late morning of the 27th in association with an upper low pressure system. Widespread flash flooding and wind damage occurred over the region through the late afternoon. There were two brief tornadoes that developed along the leading edge of a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) to the southwest and southeast of Bolivar. Numerous reports of heavy rainfall between 1 and 4 inches were received across southwestern Missouri. Rainfall accumulations over 5 inches occurred in Joplin and led to flash flooding in the city. Another round of flash flooding occurred along Kelly Creek in Monett and several roadways were closed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home causing minor electrical and structural damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms moved across central, north-central, northeast, and east-central Wisconsin during the evening hours. The strongest storms produced hail up to ping pong size and wind damage. A lightning strike caused $300,000 worth of damage to a Wisconsin Rapids paper mill.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Verso Paper Mill at 7:30 pm CDT, producing $300,000 worth of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee during the early morning hours of March 17th, a few of which became strong. A report of lightning that resulted in damage to a shed was received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, which caused the tree to fall onto a shed and destroy it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure deepened over eastern Colorado and moved eastward along a stationary front into southern Illinois through the morning of the 9th before the front moved south of the Ozarks. Strong to severe storms moved over the region during the early morning of the 9th. Hail up the golf ball size occurred in Barry County southeast of Cassville, and several locations along the south of Highway 60 reported wind damage to trees and powerlines. Several rounds of rainfall led to flooding near Ava and Mountain Grove in Douglas County, near Sycamore and Hardenville in Ozark County, and near Bradleyville in Taney County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the Ava High School damaging seven network switches.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with a frontal system moving through the region. Some of these storms produced a few tornadoes, hail, and damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A mobile home was struck by lightning and destroyed by the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface front and drier air was settling southward across SE GA, with a differential heating boundary across NE FL near I-10 due to cirrus blow-off from storms in Appalachee Bay. Strong to severe storms formed across NE FL due to heating and interactions with the differential heating boundary and sea breezes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck a home in Dinsmore and caused a fire with significant damage and losses. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for Storm Data. It is likely a gross underestimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface front and drier air was settling southward across SE GA, with a differential heating boundary across NE FL near I-10 due to cirrus blow-off from storms in Appalachee Bay. Strong to severe storms formed across NE FL due to heating and interactions with the differential heating boundary and sea breezes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning fire caused damage at the Legends Condo complex in the World Golf Village. A portion of the roof had severe fire damage. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for inclusion in Storm Data. It is likely a gross underestimate of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep west to southwest flow prevailed throughout the column and widespread|showers and storms quickly moved inland from the Gulf coast in the late|morning to early afternoon hours toward the east coast. A weak east coast sea breeze was near the Atlantic coast, and convergence of the sea breezes and outflow boundaries resulted in storm to storm storms with enhancement from a passing shortwave aloft.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting struck a 2 story storage shed along Bay Drive and caused a fire. The cost of damage was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a local power substation and caused power outages in L'anse in the early morning of the 7th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused damage to a local power substation and caused power outages in L'anse in the early morning of the 7th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late season cold front moved into South Central Texas and generated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house to catch fire in Manchaca.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late season cold front moved into South Central Texas and generated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house to catch fire in South Austin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes resulted in two structure fires and a tree fire in Escanaba on the 5th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Delta County Sherriff's Department reported two structures fires and a tree fire in Escanaba as a result of lightning strikes.  It took over three and a half hours for firefighters to extinguish the first fire which occurred in the attic of a house at 514 South 12th Street.  A man and his dog were rescued from one of the apartments at this residence.  Fire fighter fatigue was reported to be a major difficulty at this fire due to the heat and humidity, and one firefighter sustained a minor injury while fighting the blaze.  Escanaba Public Safety was assisted on the scene by Delta County Central Dispatch, the Escanaba Township and Ford River Township fire departments, Gladstone Public Safety Volunteer Fire Fighters, MSP 84, the Delta County Sheriff's Department, Rampart EMS, DTE, Escanaba City Electric and the Red Cross.  ||While responding to the fire on South 12th Street, firefighters had to extinguish a tree fire and a second structure fire at an abandoned residence on 1612 North 20th Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold pool aloft caused numerous showers and an isolated thunderstorm across eastern MA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Brockton, a house was struck by lightning on Pine Grove Drive, resulting in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms moved across the area in the evening through late night hours and produced wind damage, lightning damage and some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and set fire to an empty apartment unit near the intersection of Westview Drive and Caywood Lane in the Spring Branch East area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms moved across the area in the evening through late night hours and produced wind damage, lightning damage and some flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the second floor of an apartment complex near the intersection of FM 528 and Blackhawk Blvd in Friendswood and set fire to several units.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With hot and humid air in place over the region, the approach of a wind shift trough from upstate New York triggered scattered severe thunderstorms in the mid to late afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Auburn. a small house fire resulted from a lightning strike on the 20 block of Curtis Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long lasting and multi faceted storm system moved through central Indiana beginning during the late afternoon hours of June 18th and continued through the evening hours with widespread damaging winds and very large hail before transitioning into a flash flooding event during the overnight hours with significant flash flooding occurring across portions of Owen and Monroe counties.  Unfortunately, one person lost their life due to the flood waters. Across Owen county, roads had suffered severe damage, 23 culverts had been washed out and 2 bridges have significant damage.  In all, over 30 Owen County roads were closed. A local emergency disaster declaration was created later in the day. Power outages across the state peaked at nearly 150,000.  A 3.4 inch hailstone fell in New Castle late afternoon which was the largest hailstone to fall across the state since mid 2019.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike led to a fire on Sage Meadow Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow-moving surface trough, heading east to west, and an upper disturbance triggered heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms that caused flash flooding in some instances.  Damages occurred to public and private property, including roads and bridges washed out. Nine homes were destroyed, 44 suffered major damage, and 55 suffered minor damage.  No significant injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes on Oahu led to power outages from Honolulu to Hauula.  Power was restored after several hours for most locales as lines were repaired.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced heavy rain and severe wind gusts across the Inland Empire, mountains and deserts on Thursday, September 9, leading to flooding, debris flows and rock slides. Elevated convection also made it to the coast on September 9. On September 10, severe thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall impacted the lower deserts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Department of Highways reported a tree was on fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms produced heavy rain and severe wind gusts across the Inland Empire, mountains and deserts on Thursday, September 9, leading to flooding, debris flows and rock slides. Elevated convection also made it to the coast on September 9. On September 10, severe thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall impacted the lower deserts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Widespread convection across the San Bernardino and Riverside County Mountains as well as coastal San Diego and Orange Counties. Earth Networks lightning strike data provided.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A passing mid-level shortwave along with the interaction of a sea breeze circulation and outflow boundaries from ongoing convection led to a few stronger thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Long County 911 Call Center reported a house fire caused by a lightning strike along Rye Patch Road, which led to minor siding and roof damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms impacted the desert to the coast on September 24. Locally heavy rainfall occurred across San Diego County with rainfall of 0.5 to 1 inch occurring, locally higher 1 to 2 inches near Palomar Mountain. A rare Severe Thunderstorm Warning was issued for downtown San Diego. Widespread hail and strong winds were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Brush fire in Palm Springs after lightning struck a palm tree.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several impulses embedded within a positively tilted mid-level trough across the region worked in concert with sufficient moisture to produce widespread thunderstorms across South Florida. A few storms resulted in damaging wind gusts across Broward County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Florida Highway Patrol trooper reported a vehicle struck by lightning traveling westbound on Alligator Alley near Mile Marker 31. Lightning struck the rear antenna of a vehicle where it then discharged through the ground. The road received damage, with a reported 7 ft x 4 ft x 2 in deep hole in the road. No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms developed along a dryline during the afternoon hours on March 24th. These storms advanced east into North and Central Texas, producing hail and a couple of EF-Unknown tornadoes. Large hail up to the size of 3 was reported in Tarrant and Denton counties. Hail-producing storms continued overnight as a cold front made its way through the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire on Vera Cruz in Frisco. Damage was to the roof and second floor. Lightning also struck an outdoor warning siren on Donnie Mayfield Way.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Danny initially developed as a tropical depression approximately 110 miles off the Southeast United States coast during the morning of June 28th, 2021, slowly tracking west-northwest across warmer gulf stream waters and eventually reaching tropical storm strength at 305 PM on June 28th, 2021 approximately 40 miles off the South Carolina coast. Danny made landfall at 8:00 PM just north of Hilton Head on Pritchards Island, South Carolina with a minimum central pressure of 1010 MB or 29.82 inches. After landfall, Danny continued moving to the west-northwest, eventually weakening to a tropical depression near the South Carolina/Georgia state line and following a path across central Georgia.  The primary impacts from Danny included gusty winds and heavy rainfall. Across Jasper and Beaufort counties, rainfall total amounts ranged approximately 3.50 to 6.25 inches, causing minor flooding issues across highways. Winds peaked over the Atlantic coastal waters with a 41 knot wind gust measured at Buoy 41029. Otherwise, wind gusts generally ranged between  the 25 to 40 mph across coastal counties of southeast South Carolina, producing isolated/minor wind damage across Charleston County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A picture via social media indicated a tree down and blocking one lane on Highway 170 about 2 miles east of the Savannah River.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Danny initially developed as a tropical depression approximately 110 miles off the Southeast United States coast during the late morning of June 28th, 2021, slowly tracking west-northwest across warmer gulf stream waters and eventually reaching tropical storm strength at 305 PM on June 28th, 2021 approximately 70 miles off the Georgia coast. Danny made landfall at 8:00 PM just north of Hilton Head on Pritchards Island, South Carolina with a minimum central pressure of 1010 MB or 29.82 inches. After landfall, Danny continued moving to the west-northwest, eventually weakening to a tropical depression near the South Carolina/Georgia state line and following a path across central Georgia. The primary impacts from Danny included gusty winds and heavy rainfall. Across Chatham and Effingham counties, rainfall total amounts ranged approximately 3.25 to 5.50 inches. Winds peaked over the Atlantic coastal waters with a 41 knot wind gust measured at Buoy 41029. Otherwise, wind gusts generally ranged between 25 to 40 mph across Chatham County, producing isolated/minor wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Chatham County emergency manager reported lightning striking the clubhouse of the Rice Hope subdivision in the Port Wentworth area. Smoke was also reported in the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Monsoon moisture slowly seeped into the region under the big dome of high pressure which was causing record-breaking temperatures, fueling isolated to scattered thunderstorms. As the moisture increased, the main thunderstorm impact transitioned from high winds to flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, snapping it and throwing the top into power lines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced widely scattered instances of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike broke a branch that fell onto wires causing a small fire in the 14400 block of MD-25 Falls Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Enhanced monsoonal moisture surged into Southern California, producing heavy thunderstorms across the San Bernardino County Mountains, the Riverside County Mountains and the San Diego County Mountains. A significant debris flow occurred on July 30 across northern portions of the El Dorado Burn Scar, with debris covering Highway 38.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 200 year old Jeffery pine tree was struck by lightning. It burned later in the evening until extinguished. The large tree split in half while burning. The thunderstorm on radar appeared to be during several cloud to ground strikes near Big Bear airport around 1230 pm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Elsa approached the mid-Atlantic states from the south on July 8. Downstream of Elsa, a warm and moist environment was present. A slow moving frontal boundary also resided over northern New Jersey, northern Pennsylvania, and into New York. This frontal system provided forcing for convective development over the mid-Atlantic, in fairly close proximity but unrelated to Tropical Storm Elsa. With strong instability and weak to moderate wind shear, some of the storms became severe as they organized into linear and multi-cellular clusters. Deep layer southerly flow in advance of Elsa caused storms to move northward as opposed to a more typical eastward motion. Damaging wind was the main hazard associated with these storms, with several strong downbursts noted. Storm activity eventually weakened and moved north of the region by evening as Elsa moved in.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning on Indian Trail with smoke reported in the house. This occurred from a morning round of sub-severe convection which preceded severe thunderstorms later in the day. Time estimated from dispatch report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved across parts of northeast Illinois during the early morning of July 28th producing localized wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 700 block of Miami Street and started a fire.  An 85 year old man in the house was unable to get out and died of smoke inhalation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front west and northwest of the Appalachian mountains tracked east into central North Carolina. A pre-frontal trough ahead of the cold front forced showers and thunderstorms during the evening hours, with several damaging wind reports and one lightning related house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported a house was struck by lightning, causing a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of fronts spawned two clusters of severe thunderstorms that produced localized considerable wind damage near Staunton, Virginia, Silver Spring, Maryland, and Washington, DC.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire in the 300 block of Greenhill Way.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man on Melbourne Beach was struck by lightning as a thunderstorm moved from the mainland to the barrier island and offshore. The man was injured, but survived.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while fishing on the beach at Spessard Holland South Beach Park in Melbourne Beach. The man was taken to a local hospital with injuries. The associated isolated thunderstorm moved from the mainland across the barrier island to the Atlantic while producing occasional cloud to ground lightning strikes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Seven lightning injuries occurred at Flint Creek Waterpark in Wiggins, MS during an afternoon thunderstorm.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Seven people were injured by a lightning strike while boating and swimming at Flint Creek Waterpark in Wiggins, MS.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A family of four was on the beach at Sanibel Island as a thunderstorm moved overhead. Unfortunately a lightning strike hit the father and he died of his injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A family of four was on the beach at Sanibel Island as a thunderstorm moved overhead. Unfortunately a lightning strike hit the father and he died of his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm and humid air mass ahead of an approaching cold front brought a couple of rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across the region, mainly along and north of Interstate 90. A few individual thunderstorms became severe across the Lake George Saratoga region during the early afternoon hours before the main line of thunderstorms progressed from west to east from the Adirondacks and Mohawk Valley to the Hudson River during the late afternoon and early evening hours. There were a couple of reports of hail, but these storms brought mostly damaging winds with downed trees and power lines, a couple of which fell onto homes or vehicles. Lightning also struck a house, resulting in a fire near West Glens Falls. Minor flooding occurred across southern Herkimer County, near Poland.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit a house resulting in a fire. There were no injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Subtropical moisture continued to stream into central California on July 30. Once again, afternoon thunderstorms developed over the Sierra Nevada. One thunderstorm produced a fatal lightning strike over the Sierra Nevada during the early afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Fresno County Sherrifs Office reported a 37 year old male hiker on the John Muir Trail near Muir Trail Ranch was struck by lightning and killed during a thunderstorm around 200 pm PDT on July 30.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Light steering flow and sufficient low-level moisture combined with strong daytime heating and local effects to generate heavy showers and thunderstorms across most of interior Puerto Rico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck City Hall, damaging a part of the facade of the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system (MCS) developed during the late afternoon and evening hours across Central and Eastern Oklahoma on July 10th, ahead of a weak cold front and associated upper level trough digging through the Central Plains into the Mid Mississippi Valley. The air mass ahead of this front and associated trough was moderately unstable even through the evening, with this complex of storms developing a strong cold pool as it shifted south through Southern Oklahoma, Southern Arkansas, and into East Texas and North Louisiana. Low level southerly winds ahead of this thunderstorm complex was sufficient enough to sustain this storm organization as it moved south through East Texas and North Louisiana during the morning hours of July 11th, which brought about gusty winds of 30-40 mph, heavy rainfall, and frequent lightning. As these storms moved through Lindale in Northern Smith County, Texas, lightning struck the roof of a Posada's Mexican Restaurant, causing a small fire which resulted in localized damage in the building.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of the Posadas Mexican Restaurant in Lindale, causing a small fire which was contained to an isolated area. Only minimal damage was caused to the business.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary boundary in a warm and humid air mass triggered a thunderstorm that had evidence of rotation via radar signatures across Northeastern New Jersey, mainly Passaic County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported that struck a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of thunderstorms developed across northeast Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours.  The strongest storms produced hail up to ping pong size, damaging wind gusts, along with heavy rain and flash flooding.  Portions of east-central Wisconsin received 2 to 5 inches of rain through the overnight hours. Lightning struck a hour in Kiel, causing a fire, as well as a pole in Green Bay, which damaged 2 garages.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on 10th Street in Kiel and causing a fire and extensive damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of thunderstorms developed across northeast Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours.  The strongest storms produced hail up to ping pong size, damaging wind gusts, along with heavy rain and flash flooding.  Portions of east-central Wisconsin received 2 to 5 inches of rain through the overnight hours. Lightning struck a hour in Kiel, causing a fire, as well as a pole in Green Bay, which damaged 2 garages.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a pole on South Oakland Street in Green Bay and fell on two garages causing damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed near the Detroit River.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four men were injured by a lightning strike as they worked in a field in Iosco Township. |The lightning struck a field along Weller Road in Gregory around 9 am EDT. One of local workers were transported to local hospital, while the other three workers declined medical treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In an environment with temperatures in the upper 80s to low 90s, dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s, and strong low level instability, a subtle surface trough was able to produce scattered storms across north-central Kentucky. This resulted in downed trees and power lines. Lightning started a fire on a power pole and there was one report of severe hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A power pole was on fire after being struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The continuation of a hot and humid air mass caused the development of another batch of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours across eastern New York, mainly impacting the Capital District. Damaging wind gusts knocked down trees and power lines as a result. Lightning also struck a house on Old Loudonville Road in the Hamlet of Loudonville, causing a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Old Niskayuna Road near the Hamlet of Loudonville causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of thunderstorms moved southeastward across southeast Missouri, accompanied by locally strong winds and frequent lightning. The storms followed the general location of a warm front that extended southeastward from a low pressure center over central Missouri to extreme northwest Tennessee. The air mass was very unstable with strong diurnal heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two persons were struck by lightning while recreating on the Current River.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: South of a slow moving front across Illinois and Indiana, scattered convection initiated across central Kentucky in the warm sector. A few of the stronger storms caused scattered wind damage, isolated flash flooding, and a fire caused by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A transformer was struck by lightning and caught on fire. Power lines were down across Lakeview Drive. Cost of damage is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Forward propagating MCS through western/southern Upper Great Lakes produced damaging wind. Most of SVRs and severe reports focused from Laporte into Allen/Dekalb County Indiana in the zone of a long-lived cold pool balance before gradually becoming outflow dominant into northwest Ohio.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused structural fire that destroyed a garage and damaged a house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated  thunderstorms developed across portions of Douglas, Grand and Morgan counties.  Microburst winds damaged boats on Grand Lake.  One pontoon boat was lifted off the water and landed upside down near a home.  In Larimer County, a brief period of heavy rain caused minor flash flooding in the Cameron Peak burn area near Glen Haven, along Miller Fork.  In Douglas County, nickel size hail was observed.  Lightning sparked a small grass fire near Wiggins in Morgan County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning sparked a grass fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough in an increasingly warm and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms across Northeastern New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damage to home at 42 Bloomfield Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms developed as an upper trough moved into the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire to the exterior of a home on Darrow Drive in the Grayson Park neighborhood.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire in Chester.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical summertime pattern for South FL, with showers and scattered to an isolated storm along the east coast through the first half of the day - transitioning to the interior and southwest Florida with storms becoming more numerous and robust by the afternoon hours. Lightning was the main hazard, and unfortunately struck a teenage boy on Marco Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media relayed a report of a 17-year-old teenage boy from Georgia struck by lightning at Residents Beach on Marco Island due to a thunderstorm in the vicinity. Injuries were severe and the teen was airlifted to a hospital in Miami. Eleven (11) days later on July 28th, he unfortunately passed away due to his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A persistent ridge across the Desert Southwest allowed for enhanced monsoonal moisture across Southern California from July 17-19. A Flash Flood Watch was issued for the Riverside County Mountains and the San Diego County Mountains for July 18. Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall in the mountains, where several flood advisories were issued on July 17 and July 18. A cluster of elevated thunderstorms formed across northern San Diego County and progressed westward to the coast early on the morning of July 18.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Retransmit. FOX5 reported 2 palm trees (with photos) on fire from lightning strike. 15 cloud to ground strikes detected from 4 am to 530 am in Vista and 95 total in San Diego county and open waters. Fire burned for 20 minutes until fire agency put out. Unconfirmed report of another palm tree burned in Oceanside. Damage cost is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical summertime pattern for South FL, with showers and scattered to an isolated storm along the east coast through the first half of the day - transitioning to the interior and southwest Florida with storms becoming more numerous and robust by the afternoon hours. Lightning was the main hazard, and unfortunately struck two people on a beach near Naples.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media relayed a report of two people, one adult and one child, struck by lightning on Clam Pass Beach in Naples. Injuries were minor to moderate and both persons were taken to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the morning hours on July 26. An isolated wind damage report was received as well as damage to a home from a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Carefree Lane was struck by lightning causing a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough moved over a warm, moist airmass and generated thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank battery southwest of Hallettsville. The lightning strike caused an explosion and fire. Of the eight tanks on site, three were destroyed and five severely damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very hot and humid air mass was in place over the mid-Atlantic on June 8. A weak upper level disturbance helped to initiate thunderstorms over the area during the afternoon hours. Storms were lacking in organization due to weak wind fields and limited forcing, and mainly took the form of single cells and disorganized multi-cells. However, due to the strong to extreme instability present, some of the storms did become strong to severe and produced downbursts containing damaging winds and some hail. Storms also produced torrential rain and areas of flash flooding.Convection waned during the evening hours with the loss of daytime heating.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Somerset Dr. The local fire department responded for a smell of smoke in the basement. Time estimated from radar and dispatch report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning bolt blew a four foot wide hole through the roof of a St. George home starting a fire. No one was hurt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widespread severe thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening within an environment of moderate CAPE and moderate shear. A shortwave moved across the Ohio Valley giving support for multiple rounds of convection, primarily in the form of multicell clusters and linear segments. Although damaging winds were the main impact, a few storms also created large hail.  Flash flooding was reported from slow moving thunderstorms in Lycoming and Tioga Counties.

Despite weak shear, the high instability and subtle forcing from a surface trough allowed convection to develop during the peak heating hours. Storms generally lacked organization, but some cells did become strong to severe and produced locally damaging winds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front and associated weak area of surface low pressure approached the mid-Atlantic on June 14. A seasonably warm air mass was present ahead of the front, allowing a moderate amount of instability to build over the mid-Atlantic. Moderate to strong wind shear was also present thanks to the presence of a robust upper level disturbance approaching the region. This disturbance, along with the front, provided sufficient forcing for scattered to widespread convection to develop in the interior mid-Atlantic and propagate towards the coast. Some storms became strong to severe in the rather favorable convective environment, posing a primary risk of damaging winds along with some hail. Convection also continued well into the overnight over portions of the area thanks to the good shear and forcing, with convection eventually moving offshore in the pre-dawn hours of the 15th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a fire, damaging a transformer and bringing wires down near Matthewstown Rd. Time estimated from radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front and prefrontal trough tracking from the Ohio and Tennessee River Valleys dove southeast into our region Saturday afternoon. These two features triggered numerous showers and storms that feed off of CAPE values greater than 1,500 j/kg and  PWATs that approach 1.5 to 1.7 inches. The storm mode started as multicellular clusters then transitioned into organized line segments as deep layer shear strengthened. This promoted areas of wind damage along with instances of large hail and localized flash flooding during the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning in the community of Laurel Fork, VA.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front stalled along the Virginia and North Carolina border combined with heat and moisture triggered another round of thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced damaging winds and large hail, especially along and east of the Blue Ridge mountains.   Single cell to multicell clusters develop between Lexington, VA and Galax, VA late in the afternoon and evening before slowly shifting south and east overnight.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home caught fire from a lightning strike during a thunderstorm along the 1100 block of South Oak Lawn Drive.  The home sustained fire and smoke damage to the roof, but no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid level shortwave trough provided the focus for storm development late in the evening of August 30th. Initial disorganized convection across northern Iowa became more organized moving across central and into southern Iowa where better instability and steep lapse rates allowed deeper convection. Storms grew upscale into a bowing line that produced damaging gusts from 55 to 65 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Story County emergency manager reported lightning striking a house causing a small fire with fire department investigating to confirm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front combined with shortwave energy pushed through the region during the afternoon of July 26th, 2021. Widespread showers and storms develop as a result of an unstable airmass supported by CAPE values of 2,000-4000 j/kg. This contributed to the storms producing damaging winds through much of the afternoon and into the overnight hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strikes an 18 year old individual and a 50 year old individual along Sharps Creek Road. Two injuries were reported as a result with one of the individuals receiving medical attention for burns to the leg.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of July 11th.  A few of the storms proved capable of producing sporadic damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall, supported by strong instability with CAPE values reaching as high as 2,000 J/Kg across the mountains by late afternoon.  Precipitable water values at 1.5 inches, was an indication of a moist enough atmosphere to support heavy rain.  The stronger storms were observed producing rainfall amounts as high as 5 inches per hour.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home caught fire from a lightning strike during a thunderstorm in the community of Altavista, Virginia.  The home sustained heavy fire and smoke damage, but no injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An influx of monsoonal moisture impacted portions of the southwestern U.S. from August 29th through 31st. This brought multiple thunderstorms from the deserts of Southern California all the way to the coast, where areas saw gusty winds, heavy rain, and frequent lightning. On August 30 and 31, severe thunderstorms impacted the Salton Sea and produce heavy rainfall. On August 31 a significant dust storm moved through the Coachella Valley and into the Borrego Deserts. On both days trees were reported downed in the lower Coachella Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning reached the beaches of San Diego County late in the afternoon August 29. This caused some beach closures and cancellation of outdoor activities. This photo captured by Del Mar lifeguards.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front swept through Northeastern Pennsylvania with multiple storms forming along it. Many storms became severe due to instability ahead of the front, resulting in multiple reports of trees and wires down. Lightning struck a house, resulting in the house catching on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convection initiated in Central Illinois and developed into a convective line as it approached Indiana. Thunderstorms developed in the warm sector ahead of the initial line and produced multiple outflow interactions. Embedded rear inflow jets within the line of storms resulted in several swaths of wind damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system descended from the Gulf of Alaska southward along the entire Pacific Coast and tapped into sub-tropical moisture originating from the Central Pacific to drop heavy rain throughout the state. A stalled frontal boundary over the Santa Cruz Mountains along with strong southerly winds from a coastal low-level jet, enhanced orographic rainfall over this region, leading to rainfall totals over a 2 day period (Dec 12th-13th) of up to ten inches in the coastal mountains. The stalled boundary was reinvigorated by a secondary boundary bringing in a cold unstable airmass that set off convective showers and lowered snow levels below 2000 ft. A wind advisory, later upgraded to a high wind warning was issued for the southern half of the region from the SF Peninsula down to the Big Sur Coast including the inland zones due to the coastal jet bringing sustained winds up to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph. A high surf advisory was issued for the entire coast due to the arrival of a strong NW swell train, along with Gale Warning throughout the coastal waters. A flash flood watch was issued for the Santa Lucia Mountains and Dolan Burn Scar area, where up to 12 inches of rain fell.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The area of high pressure that had been centered over the Four Corners shifted slightly westward on July 6, 2021. Meanwhile, low level return flow continued which aided in keeping moisture values high across New Mexico. With sufficient instability and shear, another crop of thunderstorms developed first across the high terrain before becoming more widespread across lower elevations. With numerous days of widespread thunderstorms and heavy rainfall, soils across northern and central New Mexico were saturated and primed for more flash flooding. Numerous flash floods were reported across the area with the most significant flash flooding occurring in the Belen area and farther south into Socorro County. Several inches of rainfall breached a canal in Belen which flooded low-water crossings as well as numerous homes and businesses. A State of Emergency was declared in Valencia County due to the flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a structure fire in Edgewood during the early morning hours of July 6th. The fire destroyed a shed, a porch, and a fifth wheel RV. Damages are estimated for the loss of the property.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front pushed into an unstable and very moist airmass to produce numerous showers and thunderstorms north of Interstate 40 during the afternoon of February 28th. Storms eventually evolved into a line and pushed southeast across the Mid-South. A few severe storms occurred. Heavy rainfall over already saturated soils resulting in some flash flooding.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective system (organized thunderstorms) producing a dust storm (haboob) in the Imperial Valley, Salton Sea and Borrego deserts on the evening of August 10th. Visibility was reported as low as 1/2 mile to 1 mile observed. This was followed by hours of lightning and heavy rain in the deserts, mountains and even reaching the coast at the city of San Diego.  The system brought wind gusts 40 to 50 mph, heavy rainfall up to 2 inches in the San Diego mountains and desert slopes, and copious amounts of lightning with parts of the desert with localized flash flooding.  The southern coastal San Diego County received near one quarter of an inch.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused 6 wildfires starts despite heavy rain. The wildfires were contained and kept to small acreage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface low lifted NNE across SE GA through the day with a moist and unstable airmass across portions of northeast Florida, roughly from Gainesville to St. Augustine southward, within the warm sector of the system. A strong low level 850 mb jet of 40-50 kts  produced gusty winds in thunderstorm downdrafts where enough surface instability enabled mixing down of stronger winds.

Around 900 customers were without power across northern Clark County following the passage of the storm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of storms moved across northeast Iowa during the late afternoon and evening of August 27th. These storms produced two tornadoes in the vicinity of Marble Rock (Floyd County). The first tornado was an EF0 west of Marble Rock that only caused some minor crop and structural damage to a farm. The second tornado was rated as an EF1 that passed just to the south of Marble Rock as it moved southeast. Nearly all the buildings on one farm were destroyed and several other farm buildings and homes sustained some damage. The storms also produced heavy rain with totals ranging from 3 to 8 inches. Flash flooding from this rain closed several roads, including U.S. Highway 18 near New Hampton (Chickasaw County) and some homes sustained water damage. A train derailment southwest of New Hampton resulted from flooding along the Wapsipinicon River prompted officials to evacuate nearby residents when a tank car leaked anhydrous ammonia. The Chickasaw County Sheriff issued a no travel advisory for parts of the county because of the flooding. The Governor of Iowa issued a disaster proclamation for Allamakee, Chickasaw, Clayton, Floyd, Howard, Mitchell and Winneshiek Counties. A previous disaster proclamation was still in effect for Fayette County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Ionia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Early morning thunderstorms resulted in outflow that left a remnant boundary across the forecast area. Visible satellite clearly marked a corridor with developing cumulus and associated thunderstorms, which stretched from central Illinois through Rolla, MO.  Mesoanalysis depicted 4000-5000+ J/kg of SBCAPE along this line, dew points well into the 70s, PWATs pushing near 2 inches, and DCAPE between 1000 and 1600 J/kg. The biggest limitation was the lackluster shear, less than 20 knots covering this region. This environment suggested frequent lightning, locally very heavy rain with rainfall rates of 1-2+ inches per hour, and downburst winds that could reach 50-60 mph through the early evening. There were numerous reports of damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At approximately 315 pm, lightning struck a house on Joyceridge Drive in Clarkson Valley. The strike ignited a fire in the attic. Fortunately a construction crew was working on a nearby house and saw the fire.  They were able to spray water on the fire and put most of it out until the fire department arrived on scene. No one was home at the time of the lightning strike. No injuries or deaths were reported.

Storms were developing in the area at that time and one of these storms produced a lightning bolt that hit near the 5th hole's tee box where the four were standing. All four were taken to an area hospital for treatment and were alert when first responders arrived. Two were released that day while the other two remained in the hospital for an unknown length of time. All four of the victims were male and their ages were 14, 19, 38, and 72.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm moved over Duluth during the evening of the 28th. While not strong or severe, it did produce lightning that struck one of the steeples of the Hope City Church near downtown Duluth. The steeple exploded from the direct strike, but a fire did not start. In addition to the extensive damage to the steeple, the strike also led to a water main break in front of the church as well, sending a river of water down the adjacent street.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire crews were dispatched to the Hope City Church at approximately 7:45 PM on the evening of August 28th. One of the steeples of the church had taken a direct strike from a bolt of lightning and exploded, raining debris onto the street below and causing extensive damage to the steeple and the roof of the church that impacted the structural integrity of the building. In addition to the steeple damage, the lighting strike also led to a water main break at the intersection in front of the church. This sent a river of water down North 3rd Avenue East. Fortunately, the lightning strike did not start a fire at the church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the western Atlantic waters allowed for an easterly wind flow to set up across South FL. This allowed for the Atlantic sea breeze to push westward across South FL while the Gulf sea breeze remained pinned across the west coast metro areas. This allowed for strong showers and storms to develop during the afternoon and evening hours across interior sections and the Gulf coast, including the Lake Okeechobee and Gulf waters. Strong wind gusts and frequent lightning were the main hazards. In fact, lightning struck a utility pole in Collier County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported via social media a lightning strike that caused a utility pole to burst into flames in Naples. Witnesses say a lightning bolt struck the pole outside of Paragon Pavilion on Vanderbilt Road. The pole popped a couple of times before catching fire. No injuries reported. Time based on National Lightning Detection Network data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and early evening hours. Thunderstorm winds produced considerable damage in Safford. Sporadic wind and lightning damage also occurred the greater Tucson Metro Area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a roof fire in a house near Sahuarita and Wentworth Rds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system tracked across the Central Plains into the Midwest, a trailing dry line and cold front interacted with an unstable air mass in a highly sheared environment to spark strong to severe storms during the afternoon and evening of the 24th. Two EF-1 tornadoes were produced from the strongest storms that moved across Camden County near Richland and in Dent County near Gladden.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large hay barn was witnessed being struck by lightning. The structure was destroyed by a subsequent fire as a result of the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from an unusual early morning October thunderstorm damaged a home in Clear Lake.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of mesoscale convective complexes developed over western portions of the Southern Plains and dived southeast through North and Central Texas, producing isolated instances of flooding and wind damage. On June 6th, a female died in her vehicle while crossing a flooded creek in Garland.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while under a tree in the Woodway area. He lost some teeth and had burns on his hands.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms occurred over the Mojave Desert. One produced damage from a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power pole along Interstate 40 1/2 mile east of Hector Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An early season monsoon weather pattern led to areas of lightning and wind, as well as some small wildfires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency manager relayed a report of a tree struck by lightning in Cathedral City as reported by KESQ media. Radar detected rain cells and lightning was also detected in the Coachella Valley. The Cathedral City fire department received reports at the 36000 block of Bankside Drive. The palm tree was immediately next to at least 2 home residences.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong southern winds brought warm temperatures and plenty of moisture into an environment of strong wind shear ahead of an advancing cold front. This resulted in unusually warm temperatures for a December day and the ingredients to produce a historic tornado outbreak and flash flooding. This included multiple long track tornadoes. Central Kentucky saw 18 tornadoes that injured 96 and killed 18. An additional death occurred in a flash flood.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house which caused a fire on the 4500 block of Chenwood Lane. The cost of damage is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As a cold front moved through the region, showers and storms developed across the ArkLaMiss ahead of the front during the morning and afternoon of December 6th. Some storms brought gusty winds which resulted in a few instances of wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment complex in Starkville. It also struck and split a tree on campus on the drill field.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With the help of an overnight storm complex in Oklahoma, a cold front was able to sag south and become stationary across the forecast area on Friday May 28. The front provided a focus for additional showers and storms, a few of which were either severe or produced heavy rain. The notable events from this episode was a large swath of damaging winds across part of Wise County and flooding in McLennan County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a fire in the attic of Brookdale Senior Living Solutions. No one was hurt.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In Arkansas, the fireworks started early (during the predawn hours) on the 17th. Isolated storms unloaded large hail, including golf ball size hail just east of Scranton (Logan County), and quarter size hail at Atkins (Pope County) and Johnsville (Bradley County). After that, it turned into a bunch of heavy rain.||Two to more than three inches of rain dumped from Newport (Jackson County) to North Little Rock (Pulaski County). Vehicles stalled in high water, and people had to be rescued. Several roads were closed. Water was also over roads in North Little Rock and Sherwood (both in Pulaski County). At the latter location, a pond near a police station overflowed, and there was water everywhere.||At Searcy (White County), lightning struck a clinic and caused damage to electronic equipment. Power was knocked out to the facility temporarily.||In southeast Arkansas, rotation ramped up in one storm, and a Tornado Warning was disseminated at 430 pm CDT for eastern Drew and southern Desha Counties. At 437 pm CDT, a brief tornado (rated EF0) was witnessed in a farm field about a mile southeast of McGehee (Desha County). It was the first tornado of 2021 in the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: We received a report of a lightning strike to a clinic on Beebe Capps. There was damage reported to electronic equipment inside the clinic and power was knocked out as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over the Mogollon Rim and moved southwest across Greenlee and Graham counties.  One storm caused lightning and wind damage in Central.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a partially constructed home, causing it to burn to the ground.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure trough in a hot and humid air mass triggered severe thunderstorms across Southeastern New York.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Six people were struck by lightning at Orchard Beach. They were all transported to the hospital. One of them, a 13-year-old boy died due to his injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and t'storms developed on August 18th producing some heavy downpours at times. These heavy downpours led to isolated flooding reports.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two adults were reportedly struck by lightning at Hickman Elementary School on Stewarts Ferry Pike, but only suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina throughout the afternoon and evening. Cloud to ground lightning from one of the storms caused injuries in the Grandfather Mountain area during the early afternoon. An isolated severe storm produced damaging wind gusts in Rowan County during the late evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike near Macrae Peak in Grandfather Mountain State Park injured seven people. One individual fell, resulting in a head injury which required them to be airlifted to a nearby hospital. Another suffered burns, while other injuries were minor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot and humid conditions helped create an unstable environment during the afternoon hours. Storms triggered along a passing disturbance as it moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania with many storms becoming severe. The main hazard was damaging wind gusts that knocked down trees and utility wires. A couple of storms had lightning strikes that resulted in damage. The most notable was a church that caught on fire after the steeple was struck by lightning. The fire caused extensive damage to the church's structure.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a steeple of a church, which created a fire. The church was heavily damaged due to the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front marching across the Northland acted as the catalyst for the development of severe thunderstorms. Storms were initially delayed due to a lingering stratus deck but once convective initiation took hold of the region, the strong ingredients in place lead to numerous severe storms across northeastern Minnesota that produced damaging winds and hail as large as 3 inches in diameter.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on the 200 block of 5th Street South in Virginia was struck by lightning around 4:55AM CDT causing extensive damage. The home's electrical system was heavily damaged along with heavy damage to the exterior of the home. Firefighters were on scene for about 3 hours surveying the extent of the damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot and humid conditions helped create an unstable environment during the afternoon hours. Storms triggered along a passing disturbance as it moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania with many storms becoming severe. The main hazard was damaging wind gusts that knocked down trees and utility wires. A couple of storms had lightning strikes that resulted in damage. The most notable was a church that caught on fire after the steeple was struck by lightning. The fire caused extensive damage to the church's structure.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, knocking it down onto a roadway while taking utility lines and a pole with it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Individuals struck by lightning during afternoon storms in Clearwater and Safety Harbor.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas 911 reports that lightning struck a person in Safety Harbor causing minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms developed and drifted slowly across southeast Arizona from the early morning hours of August 10 through the late night/early morning hours of August 12. Individual storms produced rain of 1 to 2 inches per hour, but some locations where multiple thunderstorm events occurred received 3 to 5 inches of rain during the period.  The result was numerous reports of flash flooding, road closures and swift water rescues, especially in Pima and Cochise counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on N Sweet Heather Way in Green Valley causing a small attic fire, which was quickly extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The local sheriff in Dunn County reported two individuals that were working at a construction site in Menomonie, Wisconsin, Tuesday morning, August 24th, were struck by lightning.||A 60-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene. A 20-year-old man was taken to Mayo in Eau Claire with serious injuries.||Dunn County authorities said the crew was working on a pole shed under a partial roof on ladders when the lightning struck.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two construction workers. One died and the other was transported to a local hospital with serious injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across eastern Pinal and Pima counties during the early morning hours. Flash flooding occurred in northern and western parts of the Tucson Metro area. Lightning also started a small house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a small fire at a residence in the Saddlebrooke area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in an unstable atmosphere in the afternoon of the 22nd. Storms initially developed over the high terrain of northern and eastern Arizona as well as near the Table Top mesa area south of Phoenix. High DCAPE promoted strong thunderstorm downbursts. The downbursts generated outflows that progressed into the greater Phoenix metro area and led to the development of additional scattered thunderstorm. The thunderstorms in the metro area produced damaging winds that led to numerous downed trees, downed power poles, and other property damage. The storms were also nearly stationary, under weak steering flow, and produced very heavy rainfall with rain rates around 1.5-2.0 inches per hour and briefly higher in the strongest storms. This led to considerable flash flooding around Phoenix with several road closure and significant flow in major washes. Even after the strongest storms in Phoenix subsided in the late evening of the 22nd, areas of moderate to heavy rain continued from northeast to southwest through the night and through mid-afternoon on the 23rd. The continued rain through the 23rd was aided by a strengthening diffluent flow regime between the monsoon high to the north and a retrograding upper low moving west through New Mexico. Additional significant flash flooding was observed on the 23rd, mostly in the foothills north of the Phoenix metro, with many road closures, flowing washes and creeks, and some water rescues.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and sparked a fire in in the attic. No one was home at the time of the strike. Fire crews were able to keep the damage at a minimum. Time estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon storms produce strong wind gusts downing power lines and producing minor damage in Pinellas and Lee counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Pinellas County Medical Examiner documented a lightning victim that passed away in hospice 26 days after the strike.  The gentleman was golfing at the time of the strike.  Time and location estimated as no additional information was found.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in widespread damage over eastern New York on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire at a residence near Route 29 in Middle Falls.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms produce damage in Manatee County and lightning strikes two in Pinellas County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pinellas 911 reported 2 individuals struck by lightning near Tradewinds Island Grand Resort in St. Pete Beach. They were transported to the hospital with unknown extent of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in widespread damage over eastern New York on Wednesday September 8, 2021.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a fire at a private residence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms developed and moved across southeast Arizona from mid morning of August 16 through the early evening of August 17. Individual storms produced heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches per hour, but some locations where multiple thunderstorm events occurred received 3 to 4 inches of rain during the period. The result was numerous reports of flash flooding, road closures and swift water rescues, especially in Pima and Cochise counties. Longer term flooding occurred in the Brawley Wash and downstream in Greene Wash. Damage from thunderstorm winds and lightning also occurred in the Tucson Metro.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a water heater at one home starting a fire, and caused damage to an adjacent house near Sweetwater and Silverbell Dr. in west Tucson.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak shortwave trough moving across the state aided in the development of showers and thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the morning of the 14th. With anomalously high amounts of moisture in place, showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall which led to some flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported in northern Pinal County near Florence where Maricopa County Flood Control gages recorded over 1.50 of rainfall. Flash flooding was also reported in the Globe area as heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph burn scar led to enhanced runoff in Pinal Creek. No injuries or damage were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have struck a 3-inch above-ground gas line near 35th Avenue and Durango causing a fire. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak shortwave trough moving across the state aided in the development of showers and thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the morning of the 14th. With anomalously high amounts of moisture in place, showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall which led to some flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported in northern Pinal County near Florence where Maricopa County Flood Control gages recorded over 1.50 of rainfall. Flash flooding was also reported in the Globe area as heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph burn scar led to enhanced runoff in Pinal Creek. No injuries or damage were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have started a house fire in a neighborhood near 91st Avenue and Lower Buckeye Road. Firefighters discovered a small fire in the attic of the home, which was quickly extinguished. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave trough rotating through the region led to steepening lapse rates and increasingly unstable conditions across central Arizona on the 16th. With abundant moisture and high CAPE values in place, the environment was favorable for the development of strong to severe thunderstorms. Thunderstorms initially developed over the high terrain of eastern Arizona before racing toward the west/southwest into the lower deserts of south-central Arizona as a line of strong to severe thunderstorms. The main impacts associated with these thunderstorms occurred as they moved into the Phoenix metro, producing widespread damaging wind gusts. Multiple observations recorded wind gusts in excess of 60 mph with a few approaching 80 mph. Recently implemented damage threat categories for Severe Thunderstorm Warnings were put to the test with one destructive Severe Thunderstorm Warning being issued for 80 mph wind gusts for much of Phoenix. There were numerous reports of downed trees across the Valley as a result of the severe wind gusts. The strong winds also led to several reports of dense blowing dust in dust prone areas. Additionally, thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall that led to several instances of flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Photos on social media show a charred pickup truck after catching on fire from being struck by lightning in a neighborhood near Ocotillo Road and Schnepf Road. No injuries were reported. Timing was estimated using radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front was draped across northern Pennsylvania and far northern New Jersey on July 12. South of the front, a very warm and unstable air mass was present. An approaching trough also helped spur the development of a weak wave of low pressure, which tracked along the front during the afternoon and evening hours. This helped add some forcing and shear to an already unstable air mass. The result was scattered to widespread thunderstorm development along and south of the front during the peak heating hours. Some of the storms became severe, with a number of instances of damaging wind across the region. This event was also better known for producing prolific flash flooding near the Delaware River just northeast of Philadelphia, along the Pennsylvania and New Jersey border. Storm coverage gradually decreased in the evening hours as heating and forcing were lost.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A scanner report of a lightning strike to a house with smoke, but no visible flames.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a cold front from the Big Country to the Red River. A couple of storms produced hail in Grayson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was believed to be the cause of a small house fire in Frisco.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low topped convection ahead of a cold front produced isolated strong to severe wind gusts over portions of eastern Pennsylvania.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large power outage occurred near downtown Stroudsburg due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak area of low surface low pressure formed along a frontal boundary that was draped across the local area. Aloft, shortwave impulses traversed with the better dynamic |forcing over southeast GA. The entire airmass was primed (PWAT over 2 inches) and prevailing westerly steering flow focused the strongest convection along the sea breezes mergers toward the I-95 corridor in the afternoon and into the evening. A cluster of storms formed along the front across NE FL and Duval county. When these slow moving storms encountered the east coast sea breeze as it moved inland, very heavy rainfall rates produced local flooding across portions of downtown Jacksonville, including the Hogans Creek basin near UF Shands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning. The cost of damage was unknown and was estimated (likely low estimate) for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the southern Appalachians during the afternoon. One of the storms resulted in a lightning fatality in the Mountain City area, while another storm produced damaging wind gusts near Clayton.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency manager reported a lightning strike killed a 39-year-old construction worker on Blacks Creek Dr.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave trough moving eastward from the eastern Great Lakes, triggered strong thunderstorms in New York state, which moved into southern New England overnight.  The atmosphere was very unstable and surface dewpoints were near 70 degrees. The result was strong to locally severe thunderstorms before daybreak in southeast MA.  Sunshine boosted temperatures in the afternoon, then a cold front swept through in the evening hours, triggering a second round of strong to severe thunderstorms, mainly in western and central MA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Norton, a NWS Employee discovered a tree which was struck by lightning at the intersection of Route 123 and Newland Street.  The trees was debarked and exploded, with bark strewn on Newland Street.  Time radar estimated.
