EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of an upper level trough and above normal moisture resulted in a very active afternoon along the municipalities of the interior, north and west of Puerto Rico. The wind gusts associated with the thunderstorm activity caused some trees to fall down on the roads.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residence, causing damage to the roof.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable airmass was over the area with diurnally driven sea and river breezes triggering convection in the afternoon and evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple lightning events were reported across northeastern Clay county Wednesday night. Two houses were hit by lightning on Azalea Fields Court and Claremont Drive. The houses did not catch fire. Lightning also caused a wildfire in the woods near the 4500 block of County Road 218. There was no estimate on the size of the fire. There were also transformer fires on Moody Avenue and Blanding Boulevard. About 1,500 Clay Electric customers were without power.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southwesterly flow and increased moisture with divergence over the area ahead of an approaching mid level trough enhanced sea breeze convection across the area in the afternoon and evening. The sea breezes merged near the Atlantic coast where a few strong to severe storms developed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was damaged due to a lightning strike. Time was estimated by radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of storms moved across portions of western Wisconsin during the morning and afternoon of June 13th. Runoff from these storms caused some street flooding to occur in La Crosse (La Crosse County). A small shed fire was caused by a lightning strike near Sparta (Monroe County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A small shed was started on fire by a lightning strike near Sparta.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surge of moisture from Tropical Storm Celia which was off the west coast of Mexico near 17N moved over a hot and unstable airmass which was situated over central California. This resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms over the area on June 22 which was also the first significant precipitation event for the area in two months.  Due to the convective nature of the precipitation, rainfall amounts varied; but a few thunderstorms produced one to two tenths of an inch of rainfall in the San Joaquin Valley.  Some stations in the Tehachapi Mountains and the south end of the upper Sierra picked up between a  quarter and three quarters of an inch of rainfall.  Some of the thunderstorms produced strong outflow winds and dry microbursts which resulted in several trees and power lines being downed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Bakersfield television station reported that a man in Ridgecrest was hospitalized due to lightning injuries sustained while walking his dog and pushing his child in a stroller.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through southern New England during the late morning and early afternoon triggering scattered thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Charlton, a lightning strike caused a house fire on H Foote Rd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through southern New England during the late morning and early afternoon triggering scattered thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Swansea, a house was struck by lightning on Midwood Dr. resulting in a small fire and minor damage. Report relayed by amateur radio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were scattered reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a storage shed and resulted in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of showers and thunderstorms moved across central North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. The line produced numerous damaging wind gusts along with marginally severe hail. One fatality occurred as the line moved through Franklin County, as a tree fell on and killed a person who was outside.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while working outside and was taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were scattered reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of slow moving thunderstorms developed in the Valdosta area with rainfall amounts between 3 and 6 inches falling in a short period of time. This resulted in flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a gas line near 816 S Gordon Ave resulted in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A short wave trough produced a band of showers and thunderstorms, with locally torrential rainfall, that moved quickly through during the pre-dawn hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At 353 AM EDT (253 AM EST), a lightning strike caused a house fire on Harrison Avenue in Barrington.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep southerly flow brought sufficient instability and shear to the region. An approaching trough provided sufficient forcing for ascent, resulting in a few severe thunderstorms across western portions of North-central Montana. One supercell dominated, beginning near Lincoln, travelling northeastward, finally crossing the Canadian border at the Blaine/Hill County border.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 34 year old female struck by lightning, which also injured a 40 year old male and another male of unknown age. Individuals were driving a vehicle that had a kayak strapped to top of vehicle. Strap came loose and the group pulled over and got out to tighten the strap when they were struck. Female was flung six feet, struck head on rocks, and stopped breathing. CPR was performed before individual was air lifted to salt lake city where she remains in the icu. The 40 year old male suffered burns and other individual suffered minor injuries. Time of event is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi on August 7th and 8th. A few of these storms were severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree in the Bridgewater area was destroyed by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed two people in a jetski near Cayo Matias just off the coastal waters of Salinas. Hurricane Earl was moving about 100 miles north-northeast of the islands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a jetski in Cayo Matias, just south of Salinas. There were two fatalities and a third person was taken to a hospital. A marine weather statement due to thunderstorms was in effect for nearby waters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms produced large hail, damaging wind gusts, and tornadoes through the day on April 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few rounds of severe thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Louisiana from late in the evening of April 12th through the evening of April 13th. These storms produced wind damage and several tornadoes before a cold front brought an end to storms from west to east.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home along LA Highway 589, and the home burned down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pre-frontal trough out ahead of a cold front was able to spark severe thunderstorms over an unstable environment in southeast NY.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Traffic lights out from Glen Cove Road to near Route 107 on Northern Boulevard in Glen Head NY.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe thunderstorms moved across Mississippi during the evening and overnight hours of the 13th into the 14th, with flash flooding across areas of the Delta and several tornadoes. Severe storm coverage diminished during the night, but storms became severe again during the afternoon of the 14th as a cold front interacted with a warm and unstable air mass in the region. Tornadoes on the 14th were generally along and south of the Interstate 20 corridor with severe storms continuing into the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire in the Bay Pointe area was started by lightning, and two people had to be rescued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As Hurricane Earl continued to lift well north of the islands, moisture was still being pulled from the Caribbean into the islands. Therefore, the active weather period continued.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A social media post showed that a lightning stroke a light post and it caught fire. This was around road PR-199, close to Paseos Veterinary Center.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An influx of high moisture values in a south-southwest wind flow pattern led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms over SE Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck several units in the Players Place townhouse complex on Winners Circle in North Lauderdale during a heavy thunderstorm, igniting a fire which caused extensive roof damage. Four units were affected, two of which appeared to have sustained total damage. At least 12 people were displaced due to the damage. Time is based on National Lightning Detection network data which showed several lightning strikes in the immediate area. Damage totals are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Under a classic setup for storm motion from the Northern Arizona high terrain to Southern Arizona lower deserts, with the monsoon 500mb high positioned over Nevada and Utah, a few multicell storm clusters developed and progressed west-southwest through the lower deserts in the afternoon and evening hours of the 2nd. Increased east-northeast steering flow resulted in relatively high shear values for the monsoon (Sfc-6km shear around 25-30 kts) and very steep mid-level lapse rate (8-8.5 C/km) supported the organized multicellular storm mode with robust updrafts. Inversely, very high DCAPE values, up to 1500-1800 J/kg, supported very strong downbursts. Moisture levels were also above normal which, in combination with the strong updrafts, supported high rainfall rates (1.5-2 inches per hour average). There were a few multicell clusters that moved through Southern Arizona. One through the southeast parts of the greater Phoenix area, another that developed in Yavapai County before descending southwest along US-60 in Maricopa and La Paz Counties, and a third that developed off the Kofa Wilderness terrain south of Quartzsite before being caught by the cluster descending along US-60. Each cluster produced damaging winds, dense blowing dust, small to severe hail, and localized flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local media reported a home was struck by lightning near Hunt Highway and Peace Pipe Place. The home caught fire and was fully destroyed. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large thunderstorm complex developed and tracked into south-central Arizona during the early morning hours on the 4th with widespread heavy rainfall activity across the Phoenix area, leading to flash flooding. The thunderstorm complex continued to track westward through southwest Arizona and into the Lower Colorado River Valley through the morning hours while at the same time weakening in the process.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning was reported to have struck a generator at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, causing a server to go down and delay dozens of Southwest Airlines' flights for several hours. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm and moist airmass developed ahead of a strong cold front. Thunderstorms developed ahead of the front and produced damaging winds along with a EF3 tornado that tracked from Greene County Mississippi into Washington County in Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved north into southern New England, producing showers and scattered strong thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Westport, police reported a tree down on Briggs Road, caused by a lightning strike.  Report relayed by amateur radio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hot and unstable southwest winds led to the formation of thunderstorms across parts of SE Florida as the Atlantic seabreeze moved inland.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, causing the tree to break in half and fall on a home in the 7400 block of Hope Street in Hollywood. The tree left a large hole in the roof over the bathroom. Time of the lightning strike is based on National Lightning Detection Network data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Seabreeze thunderstorm over Sumter County resulted in a lightning strike that caused a fire in the attic and damage to the water main.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Crego Court. It started a small fire in the attic and blew  the water main which lifted up the driveway and part of the roadway.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tree in Sumter County was struck by lightning and fell on house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which fell on a home in Lake Panasoffkee, causing the bathroom to| collapse.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered storms developed across the eastern part of the state and evolved southward and produced damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A barn was struck and caught fire off county road 210.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Dangerously high heat index values combined with forcing from a passing mid-level short wave trough and approaching surface front triggered late day severe storms across SE GA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a power line which caused a brush fire at 270 Village Drive. The time of the event was based on lightning data. The cost of damage was estimated for inclusion in the Storm Data database.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southerly flow brought elevated dewpoints in the 70s to southern New England leading to a heat advisory. All the heat and humidity led to good instability which, along with forcing from a strong mid level jet produced severe storms in Massachusetts and Connecticut and some flash flooding in Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Amherst, there was a tree down due to lightning on Meadow St.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms moved across Upstate South Carolina during the morning in association with a cold front. One storm producing intense lightning caused a minor injury in Gaffney.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved through ahead of a cold front. Isolated severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Police and EMS report that a person was struck by lightning in a soccer field.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An initial round of storms developed in the morning of June 26 near a warm front. Later in the day as the warm front lifted north and a cold front approached from the west, additional storms developed and moved over the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in Lambertville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass across northern NY during the afternoon of August 4th. Scattered thunderstorms developed in the Adirondacks and moved into the Champlain Valley.  A few storms produced locally large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people struck by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: From January 8th to January 9th, a strong atmospheric river led to widespread flooding across the San Francisco Bay Area and Central Coast. This was followed by convection on the 10th that resulted in flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Monterey, resulting in an electrical surge and the oven sparking and overheating. Several homes on the same block also experienced power surges.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low traveled across the Lower Mississippi Valley during the afternoon hours of May 11, 2023. The feature combined with peak heating produced an arc of showers and thunderstorms that swept across northeast Mississippi resulting in isolated wind damage near Tupelo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at a business located at Highway 30 and Bankhead Street in New Albany.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southerly flow brought elevated dewpoints in the 70s to southern New England leading to a heat advisory. All the heat and humidity led to good instability which, along with forcing from a strong mid level jet produced severe storms in Massachusetts and Connecticut and some flash flooding in Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Millbury there was a house fire on Stone Rd due to lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple thunderstorms developed along a stalled frontal boundary as an upper level trough approached the area. One of these thunderstorms was severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House fire caused by lightning strike on Chestnut Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak cold front was approaching southern New England from the west. Showers and thunderstorms formed ahead of it.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Westhampton, a lightning strike caused a garage fire at a residence on Tipping Rock Road.  Report relayed by amateur radio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In the midst of very warm and humid weather a hand full of thunderstorms caused some wind damage and flooding. The environment had very weak forcing so even though there was a good amount of CAPE there were only a few storms that became severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Boston, a woman was struck by lightning at Malibu Beach in the Dorchester section of Boston and was listed in critical condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front approached the region, with a line of strong showers and thunderstorms developing out ahead of the front. Storms produced damaging winds, multiple tornadoes, and small to medium-sized hail in New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Structure fire caused by lightning. Time estimated via radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front stalled across Connecticut and Rhode Island, producing thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall.  This caused significant flash flooding.  Also, wind shear was just strong enough for a few thunderstorms to become severe, with locally damaging wind gusts.  A Tornado Warning was even issued for a storm in northern Worcester County, but no tornado damage was reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Wellesley, lightning struck a tree on Schaller Street, igniting it, per Police Twitter account.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical summer afternoon convection formed.  There were many heavy showers and thunderstorms with gusts to 30-45 mph (non-severe).  Lightning from one storm caused a power pole fire in Hatfield, MA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Hatfield, a power pole was struck by lightning on King Street at Prospect Street, causing a pole fire, with wires down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Outer bands from Tropical Storm Philippe, which passed northeast of the islands resulted in heavy rain, river rises, lightning strikes and flooding across various sectors of the islands. Around up to 5 to 10 inches of rain fell over mainly eastern Puerto Rico from Oct 1st through October 5th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency Managers indicated that the power station at Culebra was struck by lightning, causing a fire and thus, a power outage across the island. Electrical workers restored service before sunrise on Tuesday.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deep upper level low pressure system moved across Texas and brought a frontal system across South Texas. Thunderstorms developed ahead of the front. One of these storms produced lightning that started a fire at an oil tank battery.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm ignited a fire at an oil tank battery northeast of Cuero.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moisture from the Gulf of Mexico combined with a dynamic frontal system to produce a prolonged period of moderate to heavy rain across northeast Georgia throughout the third and into the morning of the fourth. By the time the rain tapered off, 3 to 4.5 inches had fallen across much of the Piedmont. This resulted in flooding along Beaverdam Creek in Elbert County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Spotter reported a lightning strike ignited a house fire southeast of Toccoa.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong spring storm system moved through the area with ample instability and shear for severe weather. Numerous reports of severe weather were received across the tri-state area.  Two tornadoes occurred across southwest Georgia, and seven tornadoes occurred across the eastern Florida panhandle and big bend.  An EF2 tornado produced significant damage in the town of Hosford, FL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning in the Panama City area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large complex of thunderstorms moved slowly southeast across southeast Missouri into southwest Illinois, producing torrential downpours. The storms occurred south of a stationary front that extended from east central Missouri to southwest Indiana. A very moist low-level wind flow from the south-southwest fed plenty of moisture into the storms. Precipitable water values were up to 2.25 inches. A weak disturbance in the upper levels of the atmosphere over central Missouri moved east-southeast, helping to foster new storm growth.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at a church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple of bands of precipitation tracked from west to east across the region on February 7, 2023. Within these bands, one thunderstorm developed across Fulton County as a lightning bolt struck a church causing some damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Broadalbin Baptist Church was struck by lightning causing some damage to the steeple and some of the electrical equipment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed in advance of an approaching cold front. Some of these increased to severe levels and produced very large hail, some stones up to tennis ball size, and also localized damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree causing the tree to fall on the road. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In advance of an approaching cold front, showers and thunderstorms developed during the morning hours. A couple of these storms reached severe thresholds and produced damaging winds over parts of Henry, Franklin, and Bedford Counties. Additionally, lightning struck and set fire to a home in Forest, VA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and set a home on fire within the Farmington Subdivision of Forest. Firefighters encountered the home filled with smoke with a small fire in the attic.  Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A storm system and its associated cold front racing across the Great Plains combined with moist southerly flow at the surface resulted in a line of thunderstorms that impacted Middle Tennessee on February 16, 2023. As this line moved into the area that provided abundant wind shear and sufficient instability, they strengthened and quickly turned severe. Several reports of large hail and damaging winds were received, and three tornadoes were confirmed across southern Middle Tennessee. While these three tornadoes were weak with 2 EF0s and 1 EF1, they were the first tornadoes in Middle Tennessee since January 1, 2022.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Highland Place Way in Hermitage was struck by lightning during the afternoon. Firefighters quickly responded after reports were received of fire coming out of the roof. The lightning strike set the attic on fire. Fortunately, firefighters were able to keep the fire from spreading beyond the attic, but the homeowner's second floor was also badly damaged by water. Damages are a rough estimate for the damaged roof, destroyed attic, and water damage to the second floor. Nobody was hurt in the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front was draped across the Mid-South on April 27, 2023. A mid-level shortwave trough interacted with the front to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms. Steep mid-level lapse rates aided large hail development across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a large fire at a natural gas pipeline off of Kendrick Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moist and unstable air generated some thunderstorms across the Hawaiian Islands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media relayed a report that a lightning strike in the Ewa Beach area split a tree. No other damage was reported from this event.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms formed on the Big Island and generated several lightning strikes. The strikes hit in a location that is typically the island's dry side.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media initially reported that lightning strikes sparked two brush fires near  the Keamuku Maneuver Area in the Pohakuloa Training Area. Based on hot-spot satellite imagery taken from FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System), the fires were extinguished Feb 20th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Morning non-severe thunderstorms were common across Middle Tennessee on February 25, 2023. However, lightning did strike a home in Franklin which caused minor siding damage. Nobody was injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from a thunderstorm struck a home in Fieldstone Farms, causing minor siding damage. No injuries were reported. Damages are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WAVY television station reported a residential structure fire occurred due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad upper trough set the stage for a round of scattered showers and thunderstorms the afternoon of Tuesday May 30. One storm in Collin County contained frequent to continuous lightning. Multiple homes were hit by cloud to ground strikes, and a few of these homes sustained fire damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire and rescue along with broadcast media reported that 3 homes were struck by lightning on Silverbrook Lane, Norwich Lane, and Old Province Way in west Frisco. One of these homes was all but destroyed by fire, while the other two sustained severe damage. Six additional homes were struck by lightning but did not catch fire. One firefighter was injured while battling the fire on Silverbrook Lane, and was hospitalized with non-life threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front brought once incidence of wind damage and one funnel cloud report.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire Marshall reported structure fires due to lightning near the intersection of Gordo Road and Mission Hiills Drive with little to no damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Cloud to ground lightning was observed throughout multiple areas of Tutuila Island on April 15th from 1300 to 1500SST. Strong cells within the South Pacific Convergence Zone (SPCZ) produced thunderstorms at this time.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused an island wide power outage around 1400 SST that impacted all businesses, homes, and government facilities. The American Samoa Power Authority (ASPA) restored power for each section of the island through the evening hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Warm air advection above a cooler airmass generated elevated thunderstorms. Training of storms led to locally heavy rainfall and minor flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank battery along Hwy 87 between Smiley and Westhoff and started a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike killed a boat captain and injured a passenger on the Indian River.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported a 39 year old man was struck and killed by lightning while boating on the Indian River near US-1 and the Pineda Causeway. Another person on board was injured and taken to the hospital. Time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple thunderstorms turned severe during the very early morning hours of April 28, 2023. The strongest of these thunderstorms was near Columbia where one inch hail was reported. The most significant damage, however, was from lightning. Near Cookeville, a lightning strike severely damaged an apartment building while another home in Williamson County was also damaged from lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building at Eagle Summit Apartments at Tennessee Tech University along Willow Avenue near Cookeville, causing a fire. All occupants were evacuated, and firefighters put out the fire just after 7 AM local time. Four apartments were destroyed, impacting eleven occupants. No injuries were reported, and damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple thunderstorms turned severe during the very early morning hours of April 28, 2023. The strongest of these thunderstorms was near Columbia where one inch hail was reported. The most significant damage, however, was from lightning. Near Cookeville, a lightning strike severely damaged an apartment building while another home in Williamson County was also damaged from lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a Williamson County home in The Grove subdivision in College Grove. Officials reported that the fire began in the attic, and the home was severely damaged. No injuries were reported, and damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front resulted in the development of slow-moving thunderstorms with very heavy rain across portions of the Triangle. This resulted in multiple road and highway closures, particularly around Fuquay-Varina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house fire was reported due to a lightning strike, which burned the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused some damage to a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lighting caused a house fire on Knoboak Drive near the intersection of Hammerly Blvd and Gessner Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of showers and thunderstorms moved eastward across southwest Indiana. The storms were associated with a warm front that extended from Missouri eastward to the middle Ohio Valley. A lightning strike resulted in one injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 20-year-old maintenance worker was struck by lightning while working on a piece of equipment at a fabricating company. The man was taken to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved across the area and produced hail, damaging winds and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tall pine tree in a residential area. Electronics inside the nearby home and garage were damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of heavy rain showers and thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced severe weather, the most notable of which produced wind damage and a rare brief tornado in  the southern mountains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: County comms reported house fire caused by a lightning strike in the Etowah area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon through early evening thunderstorms produced some damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An historic Dickinson home caught on fire and was destroyed after a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave trough approaching from the eastern Great Lakes helped strengthen wind fields just enough to cause an isolated severe thunderstorm in the slopes of the Berkshires during the evening.  Elsewhere, there were scattered afternoon thunderstorms with localized heavy rainfall in north-central into northeastern Massachusetts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Westford, a lightning strike caused damage to the side of a house on River Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system, stacked vertically from the surface through the upper levels, was located over the Gulf of Maine and the Canadian Maritimes.  An upper level disturbance rotating around this low moved southeastward from Quebec to New England, triggering scattered afternoon thunderstorms in southern New England, a few of which were strong to severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Pelham on Amherst Road, the Fire Dept. reported an individual struck by lightning, with a reported foot injury.  Report relayed by amateur radio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered supercell thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the 28th and persisted through the evening producing several severe storms despite weak background forcing. Strong instability developed while the atmosphere became uncapped which allowed these supercell thunderstorms to develop. A slow moving storm near Vigo Park produced a brief tornado over an open field. More widespread thunderstorms evolved late in the evening while tracking from west to east over much of the South Plains and Rolling Plains. In Lubbock, a tree hit by lightning fell on a vehicle. These widespread slow moving storms produced extensive flash flooding especially over Lubbock County. Several roads were closed due to flooding with numerous stranded vehicles. After the cluster of thunderstorms moved east of Lubbock, a heat burst was observed at Reese Center (Lubbock County) within a stratiform region. A peak wind gust of 67 mph was observed with this heat burst as well as a 15 degree temperature increase.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media relayed photographs of a tree that fell on a car from a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the late evening and early overnight hours of May 6th a few severe storms moved into Indiana producing large to significant sized hail.  Instability parameters were less than usual for an event of this magnitude, but effective shear and a buoyant elevated area of instability was enough for a few storms to produce the large hail.||Additional strong, yet decaying thunderstorms crossed central Indiana through pre-dawn hours on the 7th.  Lightning from one cell caused a fire in an Elementary School in Hendricks County, before a downburst damaged a barn in Daviess County around dawn.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire in the attic area of Brownsburg Cardinal Elementary School was caused by a thunderstorm's cloud to ground lightning strike.  The school was closed on Monday, May 8th;  clean up of water damage from the fire suppression system continued into at least Tuesday May 9th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold pool aloft help trigger diurnal afternoon showers and thunderstorms.  One storm, in northeast MA struck a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Lawrence at 511 PM EDT (411 PM EST), a house was struck by lightning, causing damage to the electrical system.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An anomalous closed low over southern New England caused numerous showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening.  One storm caused lightning damage in Rhode Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Hopkinton, a house on Highview Avenue was struck by lightning, reportedly causing a small fire, which was quickly extinguished.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Near-record heat and a strong short-wave trough digging southeastward across Quebec led to the development of afternoon thunderstorms, mainly along the higher terrain in central MA and northeast CT.  A few of these storms produced isolated wind damage and some large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Mansfield, lightning caused a house fire on Hickory Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms dived southward into Middle Tennessee during the evening hours of May 7, 2023, strengthening as they did so. Several reports of hail were received as this system tracked through the area with the largest hail found near Vanleer. Elsewhere, a lightning strike damaged a home in south Nashville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house along Glen Echo Road in south Nashville, causing a house fire. No injuries are known, and damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of showers developed along a strong cold front in western Ohio the morning of April 1st and advanced through eastern Ohio/western Pennsylvania. Widespread damage was recorded across the region. Gusts up 75mph were also reported in some areas. Despite little lightning in the line convection, the environment was favorable for strong wind gusts with CAPE values ranging between 100 to 400J/kg and a 50 to 65kt low-level jet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported that lightning struck an apartment building, blowing a hole in the 3rd floor. Residents were displaced, moved to a warming shelter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong through moved through the region on the evening of February 20th over Tutuila. WSO Pago Pago observed cloud to ground lightning at times between 9 PM and 11 PM.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: After the Hawaiian Airlines flight landed at the Pago Pago International Airport from Honolulu, Hawaii, passengers remained onboard for two hours before being able to deplane. Due to heavy rainfall and lightning in the area, the captain decided to keep the passengers onboard due to safety reasons. The outbound flight was delayed through late in the afternoon on the 21st.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough, surface low pressure center, stationary front, and a Pacific cold front all aided in the development of thunderstorms on Wednesday April 26 across much of the region. Several storms became severe with mainly large hail. Up to softball sized hail occurred in McLennan County. A few storms also produced wind damage, and two very brief tornadoes were caught on camera. Unfortunately two children were injured from anvil lighting strikes in the DFW area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two boys, a 13 year old and a 9 year old, were injured in south Fort Worth when lightning struck a tree they were near. The lightning strike occurred out of the anvil from storms well to the south. Both survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from snow showers struck near an oil battery.  The lightning strike damaged the oil battery and a trailer next to the oil tanks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from snow showers caused damage to an oil battery and a trailer next to the oil tanks.  The trailer was used for fracking.  Damage to the trailer included lights and tires being burned.  Three of the tanks were completely destroyed, while the fire in two others had burned out.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed over the Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of May 30th. As they tracked east into the eastern panhandle and western Sandhills, they became severe. Hail up to quarter size and thunderstorm wind gusts to around 70 MPH was reported with the strongest storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another Low brought thunderstorms to the region bringing heavy rains and lightning for May 27, 2023.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at the Fairmont Cemetery in Northwest Spokane. Tree was spit in pieces on the ground with wood splinters scattered across the ground. No injuries were reported. Exact time of the lightning strike was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of severe thunderstorms produced large hail and strong, damaging winds during the overnight hours of March 27 as a cold front drifted southward toward the coastline.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a fire in a church along FM 518 in League City, causing damage to the building.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of rain with embedded thunderstorms developed across the central North Carolina during the early morning hours of March 2nd in the area of a stalled surface front. While the thunderstorms remained below severe limits a couple of homes were struck by lighting, resulting in significant damage to the homes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was reported on fire from a lightning strike along Walnut Cove Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front supported scattered showers and thunderstorms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. Multiple storms became severe with damaging wind gusts being the main threat. Minor damage of downed trees and wires was reported across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which fell onto powerlines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed near a cold front across portions of North and Central Texas. An isolated severe storm produced quarter size hail in Dallas County. Unfortunately, a dad and his son lost their lives due to a lighting strike in the Valley Mills area of Bosque County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A father and his son were struck by lightning walking home from the bus stop. The father died the same day but the son died weeks later, in June.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and strong to severe thunderstorms sprouted in the afternoon and evening of June 3rd as a backdoor cold front approached and then pushed across the area. One inch hail fell in the towns of Pennsboro and Middlebourne, and damaging wind gusts resulted in multiple downed trees in the Pennsboro, French Creek, and Rock Cave areas. A tree struck by lightning in Salem fell on power lines. Later in the evening, another tree was struck in Parkersburg and split in two. One intersection in Beckley also flooded due to heavy rain.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was split in half by a lightning strike at the 600 block of Bird Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms produced localized wind damage over eastern Howard County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house in the 6300 block of Sandchain Road causing a fire along the roof line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Near-record heat and a strong short-wave trough digging southeastward across Quebec led to the development of afternoon thunderstorms, mainly along the higher terrain in central MA and northeast CT.  A few of these storms produced isolated wind damage and some large hail.  One storm caused flash flooding in North Chelmsford, MA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a massive 6-alarm fire that destroyed a 160-year old church in Spencer, MA.  The steeple of the First Congregational United Church came crashing down and this made national news.  The rest of the building was destroyed.  A detailed analysis of lightning strike data showed that one strike a little north of the church occurred at 2:24:47 PM EDT but a closer one occurred at 2:29:16 PM EDT.  That was most likely the one that caused the blaze.  No injuries were reported.  Damage figure is estimated.

The storms formed over the eastern Piedmont, then became more clustered as they moved southeast and south through portions of Edgecombe, Wilson, Franklin, Wake, Wilson, Nash, Wayne, Harnett, Johnston, and Sampson Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home near the intersection of Bucksport Ln and Boothbay Ct.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a shed setting it ablaze.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A shed was struck by lightning and burned to the ground near the intersection of Daniel and Borne Lanes in Grand Lake.

An upper level disturbance rotating around this low moved southeastward from Quebec to New England, triggering scattered afternoon thunderstorms in southern New England, a few of which were strong to severe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Webster at 411 PM EDT (311 PM EST), lightning caused a house fire on Colonial Road. Subsequent follow-up with the fire department revealed that there was $100,000 in water damage to the home from extinguishing the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A remnant upper level low spun near the area aloft and interacted with a surface trough. A severe thunderstorm was able to develop and produced damaging winds in northeast New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was shocked during a passing thunderstorm while using a power tool in his garage. The man was taken to a nearby hospital with non-life threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical disturbance over the region coupled with an upper level low pressure over the Gulf of Mexico led to several strong thunderstorms over the South Florida Atlantic waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast Media reported that a man was hospitalized after a lightning strike Thursday afternoon at a construction site along Tamiami Trail in western Miami-Dade County.      Time based on archived lightning data from NOAA NCEI.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon through evening severe thunderstorms produced numerous wind damage and hail reports. A lightning strike and some flash flooding occured too.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire at an apartment complex near the 14500 block of Bammel North Houston Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A short wave trough moved across southern New England overnight, triggering a few severe thunderstorms in a very warm and moist environment.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Portsmouth, a house was hit by lightning on Slocum Road, causing a basement fire. Report relayed by amateur radio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Individuals near Helena were playing disc golf outside while a thunderstorm was located nearby. A lightning strike from the nearby storm struck two men, injuring both of them. One had to be resuscitated with CPR. As of early July 2023, both were recovering from their injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two male individuals (ages 22 and 21) were struck by lightning while playing disc golf.             Both were knocked unconscious. One of the individuals regained consciousness and             performed CPR on the other, who was later flown to Salt Lake City for advanced medical             care. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Low pressure over Southern California brought significant amounts of atmospheric moisture northward over the mountains, producing showers and thunderstorms with locally heavy rain and small hail. A period of heavy rain from thunderstorms over western Plumas County produced a debris flow over Feather River Canyon. Heavy rain also led to minor street and poor drainage flooding in the Quincy area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was a report of a lightning strike that hit a tree, causing a branch to penetrate the roof of the building in the Shasta View neighborhood in eastern Redding, next to Mountain View. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In semi similar fashion to the strong and severe storms experienced on the previous morning (29th of June), storms initiated over portions of northern Kansas and southern Nebraska in conjunction with the low level jet in the very early hours of the 29th. These storms, steered by easterly mean flow, progressed across far southern Iowa and northern Missouri within an environment consisting of around 2000 J/kg MUCAPE, 30 to 40+ kts of effective shear, and a very tight north-south gradient of DCAPE (most favorably into Missouri). Storms grew upscale through the early morning hours and primarily produced strong and damaging winds. There were a couple of severe hail reports as well along with a reported lightning strike that effective blew a tree apart.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Public relayed photo of a tree blown apart by a lightning strike. No other apparent damage to the residence at the time. Time matched to CG lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure trough and sea breeze circulation within an environment displaying favorable instability and shear led to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Beaufort County 911 Call Center relayed a report of a tree on fire due to a lightning strike.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Colleton County 911 Call Center reported a tree struck by lightning falling down and taking three other trees down with it on Moselle Road near Barnes Road.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wires were reported down on a house struck by lightning in South Whitehall Township.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The first significant event to produce widespread severe weather across the Mid-South for 2023 occurred on March 24, during the afternoon and evening hours.  This severe weather episode occurred mainly over portions of the Lower Mississippi and Tennessee Valleys. Surface analysis for this day depicted a quasi-stationary boundary from the Mid-Atlantic States and Ohio Valley through northern portions of West Tennessee and Arkansas and stretching back through Central Texas. Low pressure tracked along the stalled front into southeast Missouri during the evening. Meanwhile, a potent mid-level trough ejected out of the southwest U.S. Upper air analysis indicated the Lower Mississippi Valley was in the right entrance region of a strong 300 mb upper-level jet streak. This produced sufficient upper-level divergence and lift needed for severe thunderstorm development. ||Moderate instability combined with strong wind shear resulted in a QLCS (Quasi-Linear Convective System) convective mode. This northern part of the QLCS initially started over Western Arkansas Friday afternoon and moved east into Eastern Arkansas by early evening and then across West Tennessee. The northern part of QLCS produced scattered wind damage, flash flooding, and a weak tornado.  The southern end of this QLCS scraped across north Mississippi with numerous reports of flash flooding, damaging winds, and several weak tornadoes. ||The most significant storm of the night occurred during the late evening hours of March 24, as thunderstorms developing in advance of the QLCS streamed northeast Calhoun and Chickasaw Counties. A tight and small circulation developed in Chickasaw County (MS) about 5 miles east-northeast of Trebloc and quickly grew in strength as it moved into Monroe County (MS), producing significant damage from New Wren to Amory and Smithville, with the most significant damage occurring in Amory.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A structure on Threadgill Road caught on fire due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moving across Oklahoma toward Arkansas interacted with a stalled front across southern Arkansas. Strong to severe storms were triggered along the boundary and the setup along the cold front prompted the development of clusters of thunderstorms which produced damaging winds and multiple tornadoes.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a vehicle fire around the 6700 block of Cypresswood Drive near Spring.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) developed in southern Michigan the evening of June 15th and tracked southeast into eastern Ohio. Damaging wind gusts, heavy rain, and hail were reported across the Ohio River Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home. Damage unknown.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tank at Calcasieu Refining Company igniting naphtha. The fire prompted evacuations for an area of 1.5 miles from the site including Graywood. A shelter in place was ordered for residents within 5 miles. The fire burned into the early morning of the next day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system brought showers and thunderstorms to Central New York. Daytime heating helped provide instability for strong to severe thunderstorms. Multiple severe storms developed across the region. Strong wind gusts and large hail caused some minor damage.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Spotter reported lightning strike that destroyed pole and downed wires. Time estimated via radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Daytime heating combined with a nearby stationary front, caused a few strong thunderstorms to develop over northeast Montana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained spotter reported a direct lightning strike on a new series model tractor. The lightning strike fried the electronics and smoke was seen rising from the tractor cab.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed within the proximity of an upper-level low pressure system off the coast of New England. Hail fell out of many of these storms and ranged from pea size (around 0.25 inches) to as large as ping-pong balls (1.50 inches). In some locations, hail fell long enough to accumulate on ground surfaces.

This resulted in multiple wind damage and hail reports with limited flash flooding reports. A barn fire was also started by a lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a barn fire. Damage cost unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: With the influence of a mid-level trough to the north, South Florida was provided with a source of lift, which combined with surface instability from diurnal heating to develop strong to severe thunderstorms on the afternoon of July 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported a house fire in North Lauderdale along SW 81 Ave and 4th Court as a thunderstorm was affecting the area. Lightning data showed at least 2 strikes in very close proximity to the location at around 420 PM EDT.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms moved northward into Connecticut during the morning ahead of a short-wave trough southwest of southern New England.  The showers and thunderstorms spread northeastward into the early afternoon.  One storm produced a lightning strike that started a house fire in northeast Massachusetts. Several roads were flooded in Worcester County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Tewksbury, a lightning strike started a house fire on the 20 block of Sheridan Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Supercell thunderstorms developed toward midday across the middle Red River Valley along and south of a stalled frontal boundary. These thunderstorms progressed east southeast with upper 80s temperatures on the warm side of the boundary with dew points exceeding 75 degrees. Mid-level lapse rates of 7-8 C/km overspread this very moist low-level air mass over a rather broad west-to-east corridor, supporting extreme instability upwards of 4500 J/kg well downstream of the upscale-growing convection. Coinciding this corridor of extreme buoyancy was very strong effective bulk shear near 65 kts along with hodographs that were modestly curved at the low levels and elongated above 3 km AGL. Numerous local storm reports were documented of large hail and damaging wind gusts across parts of North Louisiana throughout the event. Unfortunately, a 73 year old male was killed in a fire ignited after lightning struck his home near Shongaloo in Northern Webster Parish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike from overnight storms started a fire at the home of the 73-year old victim, who was found deceased in his bedroom. Two cats also perished in the home. Following an assessment from fire investigators and nearby surveillance cameras, the fire was confirmed to be started by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Despite the presence of a high pressure ridge over the Southern Plains, a plume of Gulf moisture extending north into the region allowed some afternoon convection to overcome subsidence provided by the ridge. Multiple thunderstorms developed, some of which produced large hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Seventeen Lakes neighborhood in far north Fort Worth. The fire damaged the attic and upper story, but water and smoke damage rendered the house unlivable for a few months.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An closed upper low moving through a southern jet stream produced several waves of strong to severe thunderstorms over Central Alabama.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire on County Road 79. The home was a total loss.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house sustained significant damage from a lightning strike. Two automobiles were heavily damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered-to-numerous showers and thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a frontal boundary across the western Carolinas during the evening. A couple of the storms produced isolated damaging wind gusts in upstate South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported a lightning strike caused a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains and foothills during the late afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced large hail and brief damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: County comms reported a person was struck by lightning and transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms moved into upstate South Carolina from northeast Georgia during the evening. A few of the embedded cells produced brief damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: County comms reported lightning struck a house, causing a structure fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of thunderstorms moved into upstate South Carolina from northeast Georgia during the evening. A few of the embedded cells produced brief damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported lightning caused a structure fire that destroyed a church at Camp Creek Rd and North Blue Ridge Dr.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred within a favorable environment for downbursts.  Several reports of damaging winds were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a vehicle in the middle of I-75 southbound around Mile Marker 10.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms tracked eastward across Middle Tennessee early in the afternoon of July 1, 2023. With an abundant amount of instability in place, these thunderstorms quickly became severe with damaging winds the primary threat. Wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were common as they marched eastward and numerous reports were received of downed trees and powerlines. Fortunately, no injuries were reported. Otherwise, excessive heat across portions of the area continued as a few locations reported heat index values exceeding 110 degrees until the thunderstorms arrived.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a structure fire along Mann Road near Oakland. No injuries were reported. Damages are a rough estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms dropped southeast through the Tennessee Valley during the evening hours of the 11th. A thunderstorm in Madison County produced numerous reports of wind damage, resulting in power outages across central and north Huntsville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree between Clopton Street and Triana Blvd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An isolated severe thunderstorm cell moved southward across the Ozark foothills during the late evening hours. Strong winds brought down tree limbs in the path of the storm. The storm occurred near a weak stationary front that extended from the Ozark Mountains east to western Kentucky.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning set a barn on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds, lightning damage and one tornado across portions of northeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire off of Carolina Highway 343 South.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds, lightning damage and one tornado across portions of northeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a house fire off of Bayshore Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds, lightning damage and one tornado across portions of northeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike caused a tree fire at 300 Sandy Hook Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm developed west of Cheyenne during the afternoon of the 27th producing a lightning strike injuring an individual at Francis E. Warren Air Force Base.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An active-duty member of the U.S. Air Force was struck by lightning while outdoors on the grounds at Francis E. Warren Air Force Base. The lightning strike hit a military vehicle while the individual was in contact with the vehicle frame.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level disturbance in westerly winds aloft helped to intensify storms over the High Plains and carry these storms east during the night of July 6th and into the morning hours of July 7th. Instability had increased across central and south central Nebraska during the overnight period. A line of thunderstorms had moved across central Nebraska during the early morning hours of July 7th. This line of storms moved through Polk County around 8 AM CDT. The front end and strongest part of the line of storms had already moved through the area when lightning struck a grain elevator on the northeastern fringe of the town of Shelby. Six employees who were working on the construction of the grain elevator were sent to the hospital with non-life threatening injuries due to the lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Six employees working on the construction of a new grain elevator on the northeastern fringe of Shelby were sent to the hospital with non-life threatening injuries when lightning struck the structure.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Slocomb Fire Department Facebook page reported that a new, two story home at 546 South County Road 49 in Malvern was struck by lightning with major fire damage. Damage cost was estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms tracked eastward across Middle Tennessee early in the afternoon of July 1, 2023. With an abundant amount of instability in place, these thunderstorms quickly became severe with damaging winds the primary threat. Wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were common as they marched eastward and numerous reports were received of downed trees and powerlines. Fortunately, no injuries were reported. Otherwise, excessive heat across portions of the area continued as a few locations reported heat index values exceeding 110 degrees until the thunderstorms arrived.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structure fire along Barnett Road in Ethridge. No injuries or fatalities were reported. Damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On July 9th, a weak disturbance, followed by a cold front, resulted in rounds of showers and thunderstorms throughout the day. One early morning storm produced a lightning strike that caused an apartment fire in Putnam County. The majority of the three story building was gutted. Numerous showers and storms then developed in the afternoon, resulting in flash flooding in Fayette County. A few downed trees also occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local fire department responded to a 3:15 A.M. structure fire at the Devonshire Apartment Complex in Scott Depot. The three-story building, with 22 apartments (19 occupied) and 27 occupants, was gutted. Initial report mentioned a lightning strike. No injuries were reported. Everyone evacuated safely and were accounted for.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal passage spawned a few organized storm clusters that produced severe  thunderstorm wind gusts within a marginal shear and very moist airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A cloud to ground lightning strike caused a structure fire.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed a home on Brown Road near Hamptonville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered mostly dry thunderstorms developed on the afternoon on the 28th with subsequent lightning leading to a fire that damaged a local hay crop.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning caused fire consumed hay stored for winter cattle feeding at the Double K Ranch. More than 400 bales each weighting 1000 pounds were lost, which is a year's worth of feed for this ranch. Fencing was also lost in the fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms raced west to east at 50-65 mph across north Alabama. Numerous reports of trees and power lines being knocked down were received, knocking at power to tens of thousands in north central Alabama. Injuries were reported in DeKalb County when a tree was knocked down onto a residence, collapsing it. Lightning strikes may have also sparked a grass fire or other fires. At least 21,000 utility customers in Madison County were without power.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a grass fire at this location on Elk River Mills road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms developed over south-central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of July 28, 2023, just south of a frontal boundary that was draped from northwest to southeast across Pennsylvania. This cluster of storms produced sporadic wind damage as it progressed eastward across the Cumberland and Lower Susquehanna valleys. Additional showers and storms developed just north of the track of this initial cluster of storms, coagulating into a line that pushed northeastward across the central mountains during the evening hours producing sporadic wind damage in Centre County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A building was struck by lightning, resulting in a electrical damage and a fire west of Dickinson.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over Middle Tennessee on July 13, 2023 and into the early morning hours of July 14th. One of these thunderstorms in southeast Wilson County produced locally heavy rainfall, causing minor flooding in the Watertown area. Elsewhere, a lightning strike struck a gas line in west Brentwood.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Nashville emergency manager reported that a gas line was struck by lightning along Old Hickory Boulevard in west Brentwood. The fire department was called to the scene, but extent of damages is unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mesoscale vorticity maximum triggered thunderstorms in the eastern Carolinas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree at the Man O' War Golf Club in Myrtle Beach, catching it on fire. The strike traveled down the trunk and underground, where it damaged golf course irrigation water lines. No injuries or other damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted during the midday hours lasting through the afternoon across much of north Alabama. The thunderstorms produced wind damage at multiple locations.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which sparked a fire on Mulberry Lane.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms entered north Alabama during the late morning and early afternoon hours, moving east-southeast through the area. One of the thunderstorms produced a lightning strike, fatally injuring a male in north Florence in Lauderdale County. Lightning also killed 19 cattle at a farm in Ruth in Marshall County. As the thunderstorms progressed, several reports of wind damage were received, mainly south of Tennessee River in Morgan, Cullman, Marshall and DeKalb Counties.  Over 13,000 were left without power in north Alabama from the thunderstorms, including over 11,000 alone in Cullman County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a farm and killed 19 cattle near Ruth, including one bull. Location and time estimated by the Severe Weather Data Inventory from NCEI.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A sharp low pressure trough crossed western New York in the afternoon. Thunderstorms first occurred along the Niagara Frontier lake breeze convergence zone with additional clusters of thunderstorms later across the Finger Lakes to the eastern Lake Ontario region. Multiple reports of wind damage were received. An additional round of thunderstorms crossed the Niagara River later in the evening and produced wind damage near Youngstown.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning and set on fire in the town of Champion.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree which then collapsed onto a patio.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Typical summertime thunderstorms produced some minor wind damage, localized flooding, and two injuries due to lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 13 year-old female and 15 year-old female were struck by lightning at a ballpark in Vance.  Both females were underneath a tent next to a chain link fence.  Both sustained minor injuries and were taken to a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 28 year old woman walking her dog was struck and severely injured by lightning in Lake Nona.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 28 year old woman was struck and severely injured by lightning while walking her dog in the 9000 block of Dowden Road in Lake Nona.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous thunderstorms and storm clusters moved across western North Carolina throughout the afternoon. Many of these storms produced severe weather, mainly in the form of damaging wind gusts, some of which were fairly long-lived. A couple of weak tornadoes also developed in the Piedmont, including a long-track EF1.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency manager reported a person was struck and injured by lightning in the Vale area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Eastern Pacific Hurricane Hilary made landfall on the Baja Peninsula early on the morning of the 20th and reached Southern California as a tropical storm that afternoon. The cyclone brought widespread flash flooding to southeast California, along with isolated high winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole next to I-15, closing the highway for a period.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms moved through Middle Tennessee during the early afternoon hours of August 12, 2023. Damaging straight-line winds were the main hazard with this line with numerous reports received of downed trees and powerlines. One weak tornado also occurred in Franklin, causing minor tree damage. This activity was produced a lot of lightning with notably caused a large apartment fire in Mount Juliet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning about two miles south of Greenbrier. This caused the tree to fall onto a transformer and cause power outages in the area. Damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moved across the Northland during the day on the 19th setting the stage for severe storms during the afternoon and evening across the region. The storms that developed were prolific hail producers with hail to the size of baseballs reported in northern Itasca County. A few isolated reported of tree damage were received, but hail was the primary threat from these storms. Additionally, lightning struck a barn that was over 100 years old starting a fire that completely destroyed the barn.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 100-year-old barn in Blackhoof Township leading to a fire that completely destroyed the barn. No injuries or fatalities were reported and no other structures were impacted, but the barn was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A young girl was struck and critically injured by a lightning strike near Sebastian Inlet. Her mom was also injured but was later released from the hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 11 year old girl visiting from Minnesota was struck and severely injured by a lightning strike at Sebastian Inlet State Park. As of a September 1st news report, the girl was still unconscious and is expected to be permanently disabled. Her mom was also injured but was later released from the hospital. Time estimated via lightning strike data.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the 400 building at the Glass Creek Apartments in Mount Juliet. A fire began on the roof and quickly spread. The residents of all 24 units were safely evacuated, but one firefighter was critically injured when a part of the building collapsed. The 400 building was a total loss. Damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low pressure system which contained the remnant moisture from former Tropical Storm Eugene was situated off the California coast on August 12. This moisture helped fuel scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours over the Sierra Nevada. A lightning strike from one of the thunderstorms downed a large tree and started a small fire near Shaver Lake during the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Public report that that a lightning strike hit a tree, started a small fire; and downed the tree blocking both lanes of Dinkey Creek Rd. near the SR 168 exchange.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two strong systems moved through during the afternoon and evening on August 12th, with strong to severe thunderstorms producing damaging wind gusts and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House struck by lightning and set on fire on Twin Brook Road in Hilltown Township. Time estimated from lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A potent mid level shortwave moved in from the Great Lakes bringing widespread wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Springfield, lightning hit a pole on the roof of a college building, which is likely what started a fire there.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary was the focus for storms that produced lightning that caused a church fire in Barnwell.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Hagood Avenue Baptist Church in the town of Barnwell was struck by lightning and caught fire. The fire caused extensive damage to the church.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow-moving cold front dropping south from the Ohio Valley. As this front encountered an airmass with modest shear and very unstable conditions, it allowed allowed for afternoon thunderstorms to develop. Some of these storms were discrete and produced large hail. After the storms began to merge into bowing segments, damaging winds resulted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, that then caught fire, at a private residence in the 7800 block of Red House Road in Gladys.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A frontal boundary and low pressure system located to the west and east of eastern New York was the focus for rounds of showers and thunderstorms each day September 7-9. Strong to severe thunderstorms were more widespread on September 7-8. These storms resulted in numerous reports of tree and powerline damage, as well as thousands without power and several road closures. Some school districts across Columbia County delayed classes or closed on September 8 as a result of the severe thunderstorms on September 7.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Allen Teator Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms entered north Alabama during the late morning and early afternoon hours, moving east-southeast through the area. One of the thunderstorms produced a lightning strike, fatally injuring a male in north Florence in Lauderdale County. Lightning also killed 19 cattle at a farm in Ruth in Marshall County. As the thunderstorms progressed, several reports of wind damage were received, mainly south of Tennessee River in Morgan, Cullman, Marshall and DeKalb Counties.  Over 13,000 were left without power in north Alabama from the thunderstorms, including over 11,000 alone in Cullman County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At approximately 13:09 LST, lightning fatally injured a 28 year old male in the parking lot of a business at 3155 Kendall Drive in Florence.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Aside from far eastern Kentucky (roughly US-23 and eastward) where showers and storms lingered through much of the morning, the combination of dew points in the mid 70s to lower 80s and temperatures climbing well into the 80s and lower 90s led to an oppressively muggy and highly unstable environment by the midday hours of the 25th. Thunderstorms began to fire off by early afternoon near the I-64 corridor. These storms struggled to organize due to limited shear and lack of focusing mechanism. However, the stronger storms still produced multiple instances of severe wind gust damage, particularly over Morgan, Menifee, Powell and Estill counties. The thunderstorms also produced a considerable amount of lightning, one instance of which caused the death of a 39-year old male in Bath County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 39-year old male was struck and killed by lightning just south of Sherburne.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms that featured frequent lightning struck a house, causing a house fire in Botetourt County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning, which resulted in a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slowly southward-moving front was draped across central Ohio and Pennsylvania on July 13th.  Warm air aloft initially kept storm development muted, but a mesoscaled convective vortex fired thunderstorms by early to mid-afternoon over the Middle Ohio Valley.  These storms lifted northeastward into an environment characterized by 40 to 50 knots of deep-layer shear and up to 2500 J/kg of mixed layer CAPE.  Dry air aloft also enhanced the downburst wind threat.  As a result, many reports of tree damage were received across southwest Pennsylvania, along with several instances of marginally severe hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree and a house, with minor damage sustained inside the house.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A passing cold front brought strong storms to northern Illinois during the morning of July 26th. While these storms mostly remained sub-severe, they produced several instances of tree and power line damage. One man was also injured when he was reportedly struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was injured when he was struck by lightning while visiting a Rockford cemetery. His condition was reported as unknown, but the man was responsive when paramedics arrived on scene.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms developed over central Missouri and southeast Kansas ahead of an approaching cold front during the evening of the 12th and moved across southwest and south central Missouri through the early morning of the 13th. Sporadic wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph downed trees and power poles from Arcadia and Fort Scott in Kansas eastward to near Joplin, Billings, Marshfield, and Cabool. Widespread rainfall accumulations over an inch occurred across the entire region, with a band of two to five inches extending along and north of a line from Pittsburg, Kansas to Bolivar to Salem. Flash flooding was reported in Pittsburg, Kansas where water rescues and stranded vehicles were reported. Flash flooding also occurred near Couch in Oregon County when Townfork Creek rose rapidly out of its banks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Mountain Grove fire department responded to at least 3 lightning-related fires. One was at a residence while the others were tree related.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unusually strong upper level disturbance dropped southward from the northern Plains into western Missouri during the evening of the 30th and continued southward through the early morning of the 31st. Widespread wind gusts measured over 70 mph affected locations from Fort Scott to Lamar to South Springfield to Branson, resulting in widespread power outages from downed trees and powerlines. Some locations were without power for several days as a result of these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning causing a minor house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large complex of thunderstorms moved across northern Kansas into central Kansas and southeast Kansas during the evening hours of July 4th, 2023.  The line of thunderstorms produced damaging wind reports and a few large hail reports. The complex of storms also brought heavy rainfall to some areas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fire and rescue reported a lightning strike caused a house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of storms from the Midwest continued east into the Mid-Atlantic within a very unstable atmosphere conducive for damaging winds. Numerous downed trees and powerlines occurred in southwest Virginia from this line of storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in front of Clifton Forge Baptist Church, causing it to fall on nearby powerlines.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a house fire on Long Left Pine Drive in Conway, SC.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary over the area provided a focus for convection to develop and move over southeast NY. One storm produced frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Reported lightning strike to a house in Marine Park Brooklyn.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary over the area provided a focus for convection to develop and move over southeast NY. One storm produced frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two injuries from lightning at Coney Island Beach in Brooklyn.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was a report of a structure on fire at a house on Derek Van Brummel Circle due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of thunderstorms passed across Tazewell County during the early morning hours of July 19th, producing anywhere from 1.75 inches to 2.25 inches of rainfall within a hour. Automated rain gages indicated that rainfall rates at times were in excess of 3 inches per hour.  Further east, a thunderstorm over Pittsylvania County produced frequent cloud to ground lightning.  One of these strikes triggered a chimney fire to a house.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike ignited a chimney fire to a house on Climax Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convection developed during the day and was enhanced by the sea breeze. The storms intensified briefly to severe limits before weakening near the coast late in the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was downed and blocked Barney Coe rd. in Kelly, NC. Most likely due to lightning strike. Time estimated based on radar and NLDN data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tree and brush caught fire from a lightning strike along the westbound side of I-40 near exit 408. The fire was immediately contained by emergency responders.
