EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a 58 year-old man in an open area as he was gathering firewood. He suffered critical injuries and was transported to the hospital. A 62 year-old male companion also suffered minor injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered wind damage was observed from thunderstorms mainly across portions of SC.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structural fire in Longs.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, causing the wood to split and fall onto a person near Lake Waccamaw.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reports indicate a man in his 40s was taken the hospital after lightning struck a tree which fell on him.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Horry county lightning strike.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Horry County Fire Rescue was dispatched to a residential structure fire on Ashboro Ct.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Evening thunderstorms cause a fatality when lightning strikes a woman outdoors on Sand Key near Clearwater Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The body of a 73-year-old woman was discovered on a sidewalk at the Bayside Gardens IV condominiums along Gulf Boulevard on Sand Key in Clearwater after being struck by lightning.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a set of wood pallets in the 780 Block of Pigeon Run Road in Gladys, which then caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon of July 11, a broken line of strong thunderstorms moved across the Chicago metro. While most of these storms remained sub-severe, one cell stood out among the rest producing a 68 mph wind gust recorded by the ASOS at Chicago Midway Airport and downing nearby trees and power lines. One home was also damaged when an attached garage was struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the attached garage of a home in Naperville starting a fire that spread throughout the garage and into the living space above. No injuries were reported, but damages were estimated at $40,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of strong thunderstorms brought damaging winds, torrential rainfall, and flash flooding to parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening of July 5. Several rain gauges around the area recorded one to two inches of rain within a 30 minute period underneath some of these storms. The city of Chicago and its near-south and near-west suburbs were the areas hit hardest. Numerous reports were received of flooded roads, including a number of residential streets. Additionally, two firefighters were injured battling a fire caused by lightning striking a townhouse.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a townhouse in St Charles causing a fire to break out. The fire spread into the next townhouse severely damaging both buildings. Two firefighters were injured while battling the fire. The exact extent of their injuries is unknown, but both of them were released from the hospital within the next day. Damages were estimated at more than $700,000.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed and moved through Eastern NC during the early evening hours. A few storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts. In addition, a lightning strike cause major structural damage to a home in Duck.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in Duck, resulting in a major house fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving low pressure system brought multiple rounds of scattered showers and thunderstorms across eastern New York from August 3 to August 4, 2023. Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on August 3 in the system's warm sector producing locally damaging wind gusts, small hail and also a funnel cloud. Additional thunderstorm activity developed ahead of a cold front during the morning hours on August 4, especially across Herkimer County, with activity shifting eastward into the Hudson Valley during the afternoon and evening. Additional wind damage and large hail was observed with these storms as well as localized areas of flooding and flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was downed due to a lightning strike along Route 423 near Stillwater.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over southwestern Kansas during the evening of the 4th. These thunderstorms moved east and southeast across northern Oklahoma and into northeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 5th. The strongest storms produced hail up to penny size and damaging wind gusts across portions of northeastern Oklahoma.||Scattered thunderstorms continued across northeastern Oklahoma through much of the morning. Lightning from one of these thunderstorms struck four teenage girls at a swimming hole in eastern Mayes County. All four girls were taken to the hospital with injuries, and one of the girls later died from her injuries.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and injured four girls who were swimming. All of the girls were taken to local hospitals. One of the girls died from her injuries on August 7th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active northwest upper flow pattern produced several waves of convective storms during the first week of August.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Female struck by lightning.  Extent of injuries unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon thunderstorms produce lightning strike that downed a power line causing a fire that closed a highway near East Lake-Orient Park in Hillsborough County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local EM reported lane closures of State Route 574 near the intersection of MLK Boulevard due to a fire caused by a lightning strike that collapsed part of a tree onto a nearby power line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of the Big Country during the late afternoon and evening of August 9th and across portions of the Big Country and the Concho Valley during late afternoon and evening of August 10th. A few storms were severe and produced wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An airport director reported a runway at San Angelo Regional Airport was damaged by a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An embedded upper wave traversing the Central Plains, combined with increasing isentropic lift near a warm front, lead to widespread storm development across northern and central Oklahoma early on the 8th. Sufficient instability and wind shear lead to scattered reports of wind damage across central portions of the forecast area. In addition, a lightning strike to a residence under construction lead to a fire start. ||By the evening, high-based convection across the Texas Panhandle organized into a small mesoscale convective system (MCS) and entered western/southwestern Oklahoma. Despite increasing stability in the boundary layer, storm organization and internal processes were sufficient to yield damaging wind events across west-central Oklahoma.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected lightning strike caused a fire at a house under construction. Time is estimated from radar and media reports.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trough of low pressure across the Midlands was the focus for widely scattered strong to severe thunderstorms. The storms produced strong damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Dispatchers reported that lightning struck a home on Queen Chapel Road and caused a fire which produced minor damage. Exact monetary value of damage unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Across the Lower Ohio Valley, it was a warm summer day with temperatures in the 80s. There wasn't much shear in the atmosphere, but enough moisture and strong instability caused a line of convection to develop and intensify as an outflow boundary from earlier convection dropped south through southern Indiana and north central Kentucky. Severe winds from the storms caused widespread tree and power line damage, and two unlucky brothers were injured when they were struck by lightning in Lexington at a golf course.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two boys sustained injuries from a lightning strike on Meadowbrook Golf Course in Lexington.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lingering cold front, weak meso low and remnant outflow boundaries along with an environment displaying deep moisture and modest instability led to strong thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds and flooding across southeast South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Colleton County emergency manager reported a tree down due to a lightning strike near the 7800 Block of Round O Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front stalled across Connecticut and Rhode Island, producing thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall.  This caused significant flash flooding.  Also, wind shear was just strong enough for a few thunderstorms to become severe, with locally damaging wind gusts.  A Tornado Warning was even issued for a storm in northern Worcester County, but no tornado damage was reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Oxford, a lightning strike caused damage to the electrical system of a house on Hillcrest Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of storms developed in an unstable environment along with some shear. The storms became more linear with time and led to several instances of damaging winds all the way to the coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike resulted in a house fire in the Myrtle Beach International Club community in Murrells Inlet, SC.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours on the sea breeze along the southeast Georgia coast. One thunderstorm produced frequent lightning, striking a building in Savannah.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media shared a story of a lightning strike at Central Missionary Baptist Church in Savannah. The lightning strike produced a fire in the building and caused a large portion of the roof to collapse.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wavering surface boundary across SE Georgia, the dominant Gulf Coast sea breeze and steep mid and upper-level lapse rates combined with some dry pockets of low-level air produced scattered diurnally enhanced strong to severe storms that produced wind gusts of 40-60 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A teenager under a tree was injured by a lightning strike in Switzerland. The time of injury was based on radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak mesoscale convective vortex (MCV), leftover from showers and thunderstorms that developed during the afternoon and evening across North Texas on May 7th, drifted east into Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana during the late morning and afternoon hours on May 8th. This disturbance interacted with a moist and moderately unstable air mass in place during the period of peak heating and generated adequate forcing for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. Some of these storms became severe across extreme Southeast Oklahoma, East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana, producing large hail and damaging winds before weakening during the evening with the loss of heating and reduced instability.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an oil tank at the Delek Refinery in El Dorado, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size near Parker.  Brief heavy rainfall was also observed, with nearly one inch in less than one hour.  Lightning struck a home near 38th and Everett in Wheat Ridge.  Lightning blasted a hole in the roof as well as the ceiling inside.  Electrical outlets were damaged and one of the interior walls was charred. Severe thunderstorms produced quarter to half dollar size hail in Douglas County.  A tornado briefly touched down in open country in Lincoln County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a home in Wheat Ridge.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep seasonal moisture move northward over northern Arizona with numerous showers and thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a Monsoon thunderstorm destroyed a house in Baderville, north of Flagstaff Monday. Summit Fire and Medical crews arrived at the home just after 12:30 p.m. on a report of the roof of the home on fire. As crews got closer to the scene, firefighters could see smoke from Highway 180 and the fire was moved to a first alarm. Initial crews arrived to find heavy smoke coming from the attic of the home. More crews arrived to work the fire, including two water tenders. In all a total of 11 units and two battalion chiefs responded to the fire. There were no injuries to civilians or fire personnel and the home is a total loss (KAFF Country News).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Pacific system brought some severe weather mainly in the Upper Snake River Highlands region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Rocky Mountain Power reported lightning knocked out power to 75 customers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low crossed the region during the 5th. Instability due to diurnal heating and the cold pool aloft supported the development of thunderstorms during the afternoon. Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms occurred across portions of Downeast Maine with hail and damaging winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were struck by lightning and transported to the hospital. The extent of the injuries is uncertain. The time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours of July 8th two clusters of storms moved across central Indiana with prolific lightning and an isolated gust of wind in Rushville. Several lightning strikes caused fires across Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on the west side of Brownsburg and caused a fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the early morning hours of July 8th two clusters of storms moved across central Indiana with prolific lightning and an isolated gust of wind in Rushville. Several lightning strikes caused fires across Indiana.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an apartment building on the campus of Marian University causing a fire.  Two firefighters had minor injuries with one being related to the fire itself and the other caused by falling debris.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of strong thunderstorms moved into southeast South Carolina from the South Carolina Midlands and southeast Georgia in the late afternoon hours ahead of a cold front. These thunderstorms then tracked to the east through the evening and produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Beaufort County dispatch reported a portion of a tree down partially covering the roadway due to a lightning strike in the 6800 block of Sunset Circle North.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of strong thunderstorms moved into southeast South Carolina from the South Carolina Midlands and southeast Georgia in the late afternoon hours ahead of a cold front. These thunderstorms then tracked to the east through the evening and produced damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Beaufort County dispatch reported that lightning knocked down a tree at 1613 Sunset Circle North. The tree was blocking the roadway.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front approached the region, with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing out ahead of it, producing damaging wind gusts across parts of Delaware.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House struck by lightning on the east side of Newark resulting in a fire and significant damage. Time estimated by radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Prevailing SW steering with near record high precipitable water of 2.2 to 2.4 inches produced numerous diurnally enhanced thunderstorms along the sea breeze boundaries. A few locally strong pulse storms produced heavy rainfall and gusty wet downburst winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Meadows subdivision west of Kingland and cause minor injuries and a house fire. The number of injured was unknown. The extent of fire damage to the home was unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: SW steering flow pushed the dominant west coast sea breeze inland with a merger between the Highway 301 and St. Johns River basin during the evening. A moist and unstable airmass near the collision produced a few strong to pulse severe storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a large fire at the Summer Grove condo complex near the intersection of San Jose Blvd and Old St Augustine Road. Eight units were damaged and 20 people affected. There were no injuries reported. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data. With 8 units being damage, an estimated $5 of damage to each unit was used in Storm Data (this is likely a gross underestimate).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours along a stationary front across portions of southeast South Carolina. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house on Daniel Island was struck by lightning. The strike did not produce a fire but did damage the electrical system in the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A severe line of thunderstorms rolled through north Alabama during the late evening hours of the 24th into the early morning hours of the 25th, producing 7 tornadoes. An embedded supercell thunderstorm with a history of tornadoes in Mississippi moved east-northeast across northwest Alabama, yielding another two tornadoes in Lauderdale County in Florence and near Anderson. Associated with this line, multiple narrow swaths of intense damaging winds of 60 to 90 mph occurred across the Shoals metro area, including Sheffield, Tuscumbia, Muscle Shoals and Florence.  The winds caused widespread power outages, damaged numerous structures, and toppled or snapped numerous trees, power poles and power lines. A few trees and power poles were dropped onto residences and vehicles, either destroying or heavily damaging them. Roof damages were reported at many locations as well. All told, an estimated #### million in damages occurred, the majority in northwest Alabama in Colbert and Lauderdale Counties.  As the line continued east, additional tornadoes were spawned in Lawrence, Morgan, Jackson and DeKalb Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residence at 313 Kimberly Avenue sparking a fire and causing significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak front extended across SE GA while SW steering flow across NE FL brought a progressive west coast sea breeze inland through the afternoon. The sea breeze merger occurred near the St. Johns River basin and I-95 corridor. A few pulse strong to severe storms produced wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home attic in Orange Park during the afternoon which resulted in a fire. Extensive damage occurred to the home and the structure was deemed uninhabitable. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved through Central New York throughout daytime hours. Many storms became severe with strong wind gusts being the main hazard. Two NWS surveys confirmed strong microbursts. Both microbursts resulted in widespread damage that included damage to structures. Unfortunately on this day, three roofers were struck by lightning after taking shelter under a tree while waiting for a storm to pass. One of them succumbed to their injuries a few days after the incident.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three construction workers were struck by lightning in the town of Lincoln while sheltering under a tree and waiting for a storm to pass. Unfortunately, all sustained injuries with one  of them later passing away due to their injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning damaged a dock at Big Coppitt Key as a tropical wave moved west through the Florida Keys, accompanied by scattered thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike to a dock damaged a concrete piling.  Photos relayed through social media showed cracks and missing pieces of the plastic casing, as well as to an interior concrete post in two separate areas above and below the wooden dock level.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms occurred on November 15, producing widespread lightning and moderate to locally heavy rain. Reports of minor flooding and minor wind damage were received. A lightning strike resulted in a small wildfire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Barona Fire reports power pole struck by lightning, and transformer caught fire and burned 1/8 acre of vegetation at the end of Mapleview Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms in Minnesota lead to some lightning damage in northwestern Minnesota.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Mayor of Thief River Falls, MN reports a tree in his backyard took a direct strike from lightning. Still standing but damaged. No fatalities or injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On October 17th, a mid-level high pressure was weakening as an upper-level low was approaching the area, a surface trough was also helping to promote afternoon showers and thunderstorms. Lightning from one of these thunderstorms caused a fire in Morovis which mainly affected vegetation.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Social media post from reporter showed a fire that started with a lightning strike affecting mainly vegetation.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Convection developed along a quasi-stationary surface front extending from Central and Southwest Arkansas into Southeast Oklahoma on September 6th. Ahead of this activity, low-level lapse rates continued to steepen with rich pre-frontal boundary-layer moisture (mid to upper 70s surface dew points) in place. While large-scale ascent was generally lacking across the region, strong surface heating and destabilization amid the low-level frontal circulation further supported additional convective initiation along the front with a belt of moderate northwesterly mid-level flow over the frontal zone (around 30 knots of bulk shear). This resulted in some weakly organized thunderstorms after updrafts became established and sustained. One report of hail of undetermined size was reported in Panola County along with a fire sparked by lightning striking a tree near De Berry.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree near De Berry and ignited a fire nearby. Hail was also observed, but a size was not reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On September 19th, a robust storm produced some hail and damaging winds in Denton County, moving into Dallas County. Later that evening, a cluster of storms developed to our west and northwest, producing some hail and damaging winds in our western counties. On September 21st, another cluster of storms skirted along the Red River producing large hail in Denton County and flash flooding in Grayson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fully built but unoccupied home in Northlake partially burned due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stationary front across portions of southeast South Carolina from the afternoon into the early evening hours. The thunderstorms produced strong, gusty winds and cloud-to-ground lightning strikes.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Bluffton Fire Department reported that lightning struck a home on Pine View Drive as well as a nearby tree. The lightning strike started a fire in the attic of the home and produced significant damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lingering frontal boundary initiates convection over northeast New Jersey, with an upper level trough axis remaining just to the west. Some storms became severe and produced damaging winds over northeast NJ.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on West 4th Street in Plainfield NJ.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the early evening hours across southeast Georgia ahead of a nearby stationary front. One cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and cloud-to-ground lightning strikes across Effingham County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Effingham County dispatch reported a couple of trees down due to a lightning strike near the intersection of Low Ground Road and Country Estates Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the early evening hours across southeast Georgia ahead of a nearby stationary front. One cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and cloud-to-ground lightning strikes across Effingham County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Effingham County dispatch reported a home struck by lightning along Shirley Drive. Though there was no fire, the home did sustain significant damage to the attic.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the early evening hours across southeast Georgia ahead of a nearby stationary front. One cluster of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and cloud-to-ground lightning strikes across Effingham County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Effingham County dispatch reported a home struck by lightning along Brookfield Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front associated with an upper trough moved through central California on September 21. This system brought cooler temperatures to the area along with a period of increased winds to the area during the afternoon and evening hours. A few thunderstorms popped up ahead of the cold front during the afternoon over the Sierra Nevada. One thunderstorm over Yosemite Park produced a lightning strike which injured two hikers near Half Dome.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper article mentioned that two hikers were injured by a lightning strike while taking shelter in a cave near Half Dome.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An influx of high moisture values in a south-southwest wind flow pattern led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms over SE Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a mobile home in Davie during a heavy thunderstorm, igniting a fire, which resulted in a complete loss of the structure. Three people were displaced due to the damage. Time is based on National Lightning Detection Network data which showed several lightning strikes in the immediate area. Damage totals are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front remained over the Mid Atlantic region and led to multiple rounds of thunderstorms. While wind shear was weak, instability was high creating a favorable environment for localized damaging winds during the late morning and afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck two residences and caused extensive damage to appliances.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stationary front remained over the Mid Atlantic region and led to multiple rounds of thunderstorms. While wind shear was weak, instability was high creating a favorable environment for localized damaging winds during the late morning and afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree on Dogwood Circle and caused it to catch fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front approached from the west with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing late in the night on September 12th. Storms produced frequent lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 911 Call Center reported a house fire caused by a lightning strike in Cordova. Time estimated via radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cluster of severe thunderstorms formed over northwest Kentucky and the Pennyrile region during the late evening hours. These storms produced numerous reports of large hail and a couple of marginally severe wind gusts. The storms developed near and south of a warm front that extended eastward across the lower Ohio Valley from weak low pressure over southwest Illinois. As surface temperatures cooled with the onset of nocturnal cooling, the storms became mostly elevated in nature. Aloft, a layer of more unstable air persisted due to moist south-southeasterly flow aloft. Most-unstable layer capes in the 1000 to 850 mb layer remained near 1000 j/kg at night. The primary severe weather hazard with these elevated storms was large hail. Effective bulk wind shear values near 30 to 35 knots were marginally favorable for organized convection. The main hazard late in the night and early the following morning was heavy rain. A slow-moving cluster of storms regenerated during the very early morning hours, producing some road flooding in the Hopkinsville area as well as minor flooding of the Little River.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning, starting a damaging fire. While firefighters were battling the fire, another lightning strike occurred about 300 feet away. A firefighter who was next to a fire truck was thrown backward when the lightning struck. The firefighter was shocked and thrown to the ground, causing minor injuries that required treatment at a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed along a stalled boundary and moved through southeast NY in an environment with 3000 to 4000 J/kg of SBCAPE. Some of these storms were severe and produced damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Light started a house fire in Chester NY.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lingering frontal boundary initiates convection over northeast New Jersey, with an upper level trough axis remaining just to the west. Some storms became severe and produced damaging winds over northeast NJ.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike resulting in a power outage on Morningside Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous severe thunderstorms developed amidst an increasing low-level jet/isentropic ascent regime during the early morning hours of the 11th. Sufficient wind shear and instability allowed for organized modes (both cells and small lines) from west-central into southeastern Oklahoma. The strongest storms produced reports of wind damage and large hail. Given favorable antecedent conditions for flash flooding, a few reports of urban and creek flooding were noted across the central and southern forecast area. A lightning induced fire at a residence near the community of Edmond also lead to one indirect injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house causing a fire start in the attic. Broadcast media reports that an adult male was transported to the hospital with critical injuries as a result of the fire. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: In a 4-6 hour period during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 25th, a large-scale MCS/damaging wind event moved nearly due south, slamming much of north and central Georgia, including the Atlanta metro area. More than 170 storm reports, mainly wind damage were documented across the 96-county forecast area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency manager reported that lightning struck a transformer, resulting in nearby trees being set on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper-level system brought widespread rounds of showers and thunderstorms to eastern New York on July 9-11, 2023. The steadiest and heaviest rainfall occurred during the afternoon hours on July 9, the early morning hours on July 10 and during the evening hours on July 10 into the overnight hours on July 11. Rainfall totals varied greatly from region to region but the hardest hit areas (Hudson Valley and into northeastern Hamilton County) received 3 to 6 inches of rainfall.||Areal and flash flooding was primarily focused across areas along the Hudson River on July 9-10. Damage consisted of closed and washed out roads. A section of Metro-North's railroad tracks were washed out due to flood waters from Poughkeepsie southward.||The combination of heavy rain and beaver dam failures resulted in destruction of roads, bridges and sidewalks across northeastern Hamilton County during the early morning hours on July 11 focused on the areas of Long Lake and Blue Mountain Lake. A State of Emergency was declared for the towns of Long Lake and Indian Lake. New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a State of Emergency for Hamilton County. Hamilton County Emergency Manager estimated damage to be in the millions of dollars.||In addition to the heavy rainfall, a few severe thunderstorms also developed across portions of the Hudson Valley leading to downed trees and wires. A lightning strike caused an auto body shop to catch fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a propane tank and caused an automotive body shop to catch fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A scattered line of thunderstorms moved into a moderately unstable airmass south of I20. Several storms became strong with damaging winds. A few reports of particularly large hail were also noted in East Central GA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck tree which fell on powerlines at Lees Lake Rd and Buckeye Rd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and storms developed within a moisture rich atmosphere. Three homes in Wilkes County were struck by lightning from these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees in Oro Valley. In Sierra Vista, heavy rain caused a roof to collapse in a commercial building and lightning sparked a fire at a nearby apartment complex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck the roof of the Canyon Vista Homes apartment complex. The fire smoldered for several hours until rainfall evaporated, then spread through six apartments, causing extensive smoke damage and displacing six tenants.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front crossed western North Carolina during the early morning hours on August 15th with associated showers and storms. Some of these storms reached severe levels, producing damaging winds over the mountains and foothills of Northwest North Carolina and a tornado in Watauga County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck in the 100-block of Sumerset Lane, North Wilkesboro, NC. The strike damaged a metal shed and underground wiring to an old satellite dish. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and storms developed within a moisture rich atmosphere. Three homes in Wilkes County were struck by lightning from these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and storms developed within a moisture rich atmosphere. Three homes in Wilkes County were struck by lightning from these storms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Beginning on the 14th of June, numerous thunderstorms tracked across north and central Georgia. A cluster of severe storms resulted in widespread reports of damaging wind and large hail in a swath from northern Troup county to Henry/Butts County (south of Atlanta). Additional strong to severe storms moved across our far southern counties in central GA during the morning hours of June 15th. Little to no damage was reported in these more rural areas. Later on the 15th, scattered severe storms over far north GA produced localized wind damage and large hail from Whitfield County to White County, and isolated flash flooding in Gainesville.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House fire due to lightning strike. Structure was a total loss.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the northwest central Virginia to the south of a stationary front draped across northern Virginia into central West Virginia. By early afternoon, a surface trough had developed along the lee side of the Blue Ridge Mountains, providing the lower atmospheric convergence needed to aid in thunderstorm development. Surface-based CAPE values were estimated to be in the 1,500 to 2,000 J/Kg range by noon just east of the Blue Ridge, while precipitable water values had risen into the 1.7 inch to 1.8 inch range, both of which supported heavy downpours and wet microbursts. A couple of the storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds which downed trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree 2300 block of Walker Road. The lightning then traveled across the ground and impacted a breaker box of a neighboring residence. Emergency services were contacted and arrived on the scene to find a smoky haze inside. The local electric company also inspected the home, and electrician was needed to restore power to the residence. Damage values are estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through the area in the morning of the 11th. Moist flow behind the line in the afternoon was strong enough to initiate isolated thunderstorms which became strong to severe. Localized gusty winds and hail up to 1 was reported. Another line of thunderstorms moved into the area through the middle of the night and early morning of the 12th, bringing localized damaging wind-gusts to parts of North GA. Storms then redeveloped with afternoon instability in the afternoon across the far SE CWA.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House fire along the 400 block of Knight Rd due to possible lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On June 23rd, several thunderstorms moved through the Interior bringing small hail, frequent lighting and heavy downpours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a truck causing a barrel of gas in the back to ignite, blowing out the car's window. The driver of the truck sustained facial injures due to the incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lone supercell thunderstorm moved across Bolivar County and produced a swath of large hail and damaging wind. The largest hail was around 3 inches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike resulted in a shed catching fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A meandering boundary that extended across FL during the afternoon provided a focus for scattered strong to isolated severe storms to develop near sea breeze convergence and outflows over a moist and unstable airmass.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and caused a fire. The extent of damage was unknown. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak surface front was near the FL-GA state-line with moist, unstable conditions south of the boundary across NE FL. Diurnally enhanced storms further intensified into the afternoon and early evening as a short-wave trough moved across the area from the west. Storm motion was slow, so locally heavy rainfall was a concern near storm mergers.

Lightning struck the tree, knocking both unconscious. The teen was hospitalized, but she passed away 2 days later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An approaching cold front brought scattered thunderstorms to southeastern Massachusetts. Robust instability developed by mid morning leading to t-storms with heavy rain and gusty winds. Nantucket saw a good amount of damage as did Easton and Raynham.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Nantucket, a house was struck by lightning on Goose Pond Ln. Shingles on the roof were thrown off by the strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front crossed the region and generated showers and a few storms. Lightning from one of the storms struck a home on Surfside Drive near Smith Mountain Lake.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Surfside Drive near Smith Mountain Lake. The bolt struck the roof and set fire to the attic. The Moneta Fire Department was able to extinguish the blaze, confining its spread to only a portion of the attic.

The biggest impact was a microburst near the Carlsbad Airport, where a wind gust of 48 knots/55 mph was measured via ASOS. Signs at the airport were damaged in additional to several other reports of tree damage nearby. Several reports of street and flash flooding were also received across areas from the coast to as far east as Anza-Borrego State Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning snapped a large tree about two thirds of the way down near the base. Photo             received via Facebook of a tree near intersection of Douglas Dr and River Rd. This occurred during a line of storms moving through Oceanside around 11:30pm.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low and associated cold pool aloft crossed the region during the afternoon of the 5th. Steep lapse rates with diurnal heating and the cold pool aloft supported thunderstorm development during the afternoon. Some of the thunderstorms produced hail. Several individuals were also struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person doing yard work at their home was struck by lightning and injured. The person was transported to the hospital in stable condition. The person was conscious and talking while being transported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms in the morning of March 23 resulted in a pickup truck being struck by lightning in Van Wert County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Surveillance video shows a pickup truck was struck by lightning this morning in a parking lot.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Respectable instability and moderate lift from a digging upper-level trough initiated scattered thunderstorms across portions of North and Central GA. A couple of storms in the Northwest ATL Metro were able to become strong with damaging winds and large hail.

Very little media attention existed at the time of occurrence. A reporter from St. Louis was doing a follow-up story on this with the family and notified the appropriate NWS personnel months later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front and upper low crossed the region during the 13th. Steepening lapse rates with the upper low and increasing shear along the front supported afternoon thunderstorm development across northern and eastern Maine. Some of the thunderstorms became severe...producing large hail and damaging winds. Heavy rains also accompanied some of the storms leading to flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike injured 2 people. The individuals experienced electric shock through their refrigerator. Extent of injuries unknown.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning from thunderstorms produced one fatality in Garden County on June 21st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An individual was struck by lightning resulting in death. Reported by the Garden County Sheriff's Department.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck and killed a 24 year-old man while he was working on a roof in Volusia County, causing him to fall off of the roof.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 24 year-old man was working on the roof of a home on Sterling Pointe Drive in Deltona when coworkers reported he was struck by lightning, causing him to fall off of the roof. He was transported to a hospital, where he was pronounced deceased. Time estimated via lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weakening frontal system moved southeast into an unstable airmass over Central GA. Steep lapse rates and instability meant scattered thunderstorms over Central and East-Central GA developed damaging winds and some hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Structure struck by lightning along the 900 block of Mathis Rd near Sandersville Ga. Structure was destroyed by resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening of June 15th, an upper-level disturbance triggered a cluster of thunderstorms along a stationary front boundary around the Texas and Oklahoma border. These storms intensified and grew upscale into an intense mesoscale convective system (MCS) as they moved east-southeast along an axis of increased moisture and strong instability that extended toward the Central Gulf Coast. As the MCS moved into western Mississippi with a bow and arrow structure, it exhibited an unusually intense rear-inflow jet with velocities as high as 80 to 100 mph descending to around 1,000 feet above the ground, as viewed by the KDGX NEXRAD site. A wide swath of significant severe wind gusts at the surface caused widespread wind damage including snapped and uprooted trees, downed tree limbs and power lines, and damage to homes and other structures. Surveys of the wind damage indicated that peak wind gusts of 90 to 100 mph likely occurred in the most intense portions of the line. Over 240,000 power outages resulted in portions of the area and many continued for several days following these and other storms that occurred during the middle of June. Two embedded EF-1 tornadoes occurred with the squall line.  There was one fatality in Madison County due to the straight line winds, and several other injuries were due to fallen trees across the state. Later in the evening, additional severe thunderstorms produced hail up to the size of grapefruits and caused scattered wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home in the Shady Grove area along Trace Road. The home sustained minor structural damage from the lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mid-level shortwave trough moving across the Southern Plains triggered a line of thunderstorms to develop across Arkansas and Louisiana on June 10th. As these storms intensified and spread east into Mississippi during the afternoon hours, additional scattered strong to severe storms developed in the unstable air mass over Mississippi. These thunderstorms produced hail and wind damage including some swaths of significant wind damage associated with microbursts.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning caused a structural fire near Purvis.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A closed upper level low lifted north just to the west of our region, bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few severe storms produced damaging winds and small to medium sized hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Pennsylvania State police reported that lightning struck a tree, causing a large branch to fall on a vehicle on Limestone Road just north of Highland Road in Highland Township, PA. Time estimated via radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper low and associated cold pool aloft crossed the region during the afternoon of the 5th. Steep lapse rates with diurnal heating and the cold pool aloft supported thunderstorm development during the afternoon. Some of the thunderstorms produced hail. Several individuals were also struck by lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A family of 3 was struck by lightning at the Patten Pond Campground. All the victims were checked by EMT's who determined that no injuries had occurred. Hospitalization was not required. The time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A relatively small thunderstorm complex moved southeast across southern Illinois into far western Kentucky during the early morning hours. The storms occurred in association with a mesoscale convective vorticity center moving across Missouri. The storms produced another round of heavy rainfall on top of saturated ground, resulting in flooding of roads and creeks in the Mississippi River counties. A couple of lightning strikes started damaging structure fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house caught fire due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A relatively small thunderstorm complex moved southeast across southern Illinois into far western Kentucky during the early morning hours. The storms occurred in association with a mesoscale convective vorticity center moving across Missouri. The storms produced another round of heavy rainfall on top of saturated ground, resulting in flooding of roads and creeks in the Mississippi River counties. A couple of lightning strikes started damaging structure fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A fire in a small retail complex on the far west side of Paducah was likely started by a lightning strike. Very heavy damage was reported at an olive oil company.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm complex known as a Mesoscale Convective System developed across southern Arizona and migrated westward into southern California during the evening and overnight hours on the 30th-31st. The mesoscale convective system developed in an environment characterized by MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/KG as well as around 30 knots of deep-layer shear from an inverted mid-level trough that was situated over northern Sonora in Mexico. Isolated damaging winds were reported in the Yuma area as well as a lightning induced fire in a tree farm located southwest of the City of Maricopa.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike sparked a fire in a tree farm located in the area of Ralston and Peters & Nall Roads southwest of Maricopa. The fire burned for nearly 24 hours after the lightning strike. No property damage nor injuries were reported with this fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The overall pattern featured an upper-level low pressure situated along the west coast and the subtropical high pressure centered over New Mexico. This overall pattern configuration resulted in southerly flow across Arizona, which helped transport moisture into the region. Thus, the environment became conducive for thunderstorm activity as PWATs rose to 1.3-1.5 and MLCAPE values ranged between 1000-2000 J/kg across most of central and southern AZ. DCAPE values were very high, on the order of 2000 J/kg, which resulted in a very favorable setup for strong to severe winds. Thunderstorms first developed over southeast Arizona and then, with the southerly flow, were steered into south-central AZ. There were widespread reports of dense blowing dust with visibilities reduced to 1/4 mile or less as well as wind damage as winds were in excess of 60 mph. In addition, a training thunderstorm over northern Maricopa County, in the Anthem area, resulted in 2-4 of rain according to doppler radar estimates and led to significant flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A palm tree caught on fire due to a lightning strike in the area of North Timberland Drive located in the Gainey Ranch area of Scottsdale. No injuries were reported.
