EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled boundary over New Jersey resulted in a few isolated sub-severe thunderstorms developing over the state. Frequent lightning was observed with some thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was 1 fatality and 14 injuries reported at an archery range in Jackson Township due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Unstable and wet weather conditions were anticipated in early May due to a combination of abundant tropical moisture and a series of upper-level troughs moving over the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported via social media that lightning struck a house in Sector Borinquen. Pieces of the roof came off, and the electricity in the residence was interrupted.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong upper-level trough brought an unsettled weather pattern, heightening the risk of excessive rainfall across the islands from May 17th to the 20th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An emergency manager reported a lightning strike incident involving a 17-year-old female in Bo, Santa Rosa sector La 15. The individual was stable and conscious at the regional hospital in Arecibo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A late day short wave trough triggered scattered storms over an unstable airmass. Localized gusty winds and lightning occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two males, 18 and 19 years old, were killed by lightning in an open field near a vehicle during a thunderstorm Thursday evening along Lejuene Road and Alton Circle after fishing. The time of the event was based on county official information and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong cold front crossed the Appalachian Mountains on March 5. Strong winds aloft were mixed down to the surface from showers and thunderstorms, which caused notable reports of damaging winds that blew down numerous trees and power lines. Lightning from one of the storms struck a tree that knocked over a transformer and caused power outages at Liberty University.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree that knocked over a transformer and caused power outages at Liberty University.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A round of severe storms developed during the afternoon of March 23rd and persisted into the evening hours mainly across the northern half of the area. Several supercell storms developed initially, then grew upscale into more storm clusters and ultimately dissipated as a linear system. This main hazard from this event was hail, some large up to 2 inches, then a few instances of wind damage and a lone tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning and caught fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very warm, moist, and unstable airmass was in place across the Mid-South ahead of an approaching cold front. Dewpoints ranged from 75 to 80 degrees across the area. As the cold front sagged south, an upper-level disturbance pushed into the region, causing an increase in shear. Convection developed along an old outflow boundary during the late afternoon and evening hours on June 18, 2025. Additional development occurred as the front and additional outflow boundaries pushed south into the area. Storm mode was generally clusters and segments at first. Robust instability and high DCAPE values supported large hail and damaging winds initially. After midnight and during the early morning hours of June 19, 2025, the front nearly stalled and became parallel to the upper-level flow. As a result, convection became more east-west oriented with very heavy rainfall rates. Training storms caused significant flash flooding over parts of West Tennessee.

One cell in far north Georgia became strong with damaging winds and a strong enough rotation to warrant a tornado warning. No tornado was generated by the storm. Conditions became more favorable for severe thunderstorms as the front moved across the area. Damaging winds and an EF1 tornado were generated west of the ATL metro before weakening. The QLCS continue in strength across central GA mostly posing a damaging wind threat, however conditions reinvigorated across east-central GA necessitating further tornado warnings. Brief EF0 tornadic damage was found with those northeast of Milledgeville.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of May 2, 2025. With abundant instability and moisture and with the help of a front moving through the area, all the ingredients were present to allow for these thunderstorms to become severe. Several reports of large hail were received, especially near the Nashville metro area. The most significant damage was reported near Monterey were very strong winds caused tree and house damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A unique event impacted the region on Friday May 16th.  Showers and thunderstorms developed across central Illinois and tracked into northern Indiana. Rain cooled downdrafts in a dry environment allowed strong gusty winds of 40 to 70 mph to spread out in advance of the precipitation. These strong winds resulted in numerous reports of tree damage and power outages. In addition, these strong winds preceding the rain led dust and dirt being kicked up into the atmosphere with limited visibility at times.

Left moving northern cell moved across the northern metro, generating significant and prolonged hail ranging from 1 to 2.5 inches in size. The right moving cell moved southeast across the southern metro, causing some hail up to 1 inch and widespread wind damage down through Macon. Other areas which experience large hail included the Dade, Walker and Catoosa counties as well as the Dawson county area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the night of April 2nd, 2025, a cold front approached the lower Ohio Valley. Along and ahead of the cold front, numerous supercells developed over southern Illinois and western Kentucky. These storms tracked eastward and occasionally grew upscale into a QLCS with bowing segments. Storms lasted all night and into the morning hours, as the cold front began to stall over the lower Ohio Valley. These storms left behind a wake of damage in many counties in central Kentucky. Over the next few days, waves of showers and storms rode along the cold front bringing lots of rain which lead to widespread flash and areal flooding. Showers and storms came through daily, until the evening of April 6th. Later, this flooding turned into historic and near-record breaking river flooding along many river basins.||Overall, 6 tornadoes touched down from late evening into the overnight on April 2nd and 3rd, including one EF-3, one EF-2's, and four EF-1's. Many additional pockets of wind damage occurred, as well as widespread areal and flash flooding through late week into the weekend. Some river crests were historic, including a new record crest at Camp Nelson on the Kentucky River and the #2 all time crest at Frankfort. The crest at McAlpine Upper on the Ohio River was #8 all time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A major and historic multi-day severe weather event unfolded across Middle Tennessee during early April 2025. This event began during the afternoon hours of April 2nd and continued through April 6th. These first couple rounds of thunderstorms brought damaging winds and large hail along with a tornado risk. The corridor from southwest Middle Tennessee into the Nashville metro area was hit particularly hard with multiple supercells training for several hours. Large hail was reported, particularly with the early thunderstorms, with hail sizes nearing three inches. A couple of tornadoes were also confirmed with the strongest being an EF-1 tornado in Wilson County. A brief break was received on April 4th, but the event ended with a potent line of thunderstorms sweeping east through the area April 5th and into the early morning hours of April 6th. This final round of thunderstorms brought a wide swath of damaging winds to several Middle Tennessee counties, including Perry, Humphreys, Dickson, Cheatham, Davidson, Sumner, Wilson, Macon, and Trousdale counties. Widespread 60-70 mph winds were common, however, embedded microbursts likely produced winds up to 90 mph in some spots. Before this line exited the area, it was responsible for producing one last EF-1 tornado in Grundy County. ||These multiple rounds of thunderstorms were also responsible for widespread flooding and flash flooding. By the end of this event, highest rainfall totals were received across the northwest corner of Middle Tennessee and into the Nashville metro area where observations and radar estimates showed 6 to 12 inches of rain. Fortunately, the brief break in activity on April 4th likely prevented more significant flooding, but widespread reports of road closures and streams and creeks spilling out of banks were still received. River flooding was also a widespread issue with sixteen river gauges reaching minor flood stage and six river gauges reaching moderate flood stage. ||Fortunately, no reports of injuries or fatalities were received over this prolonged severe weather event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reports Metro Police dispatch confirms the victim was outside when they were struck at the Hilton on Cleghorn Avenue in Nashville's Green Hills neighborhood. Victim was awake and alert, and did not require medical transport to a hospital.

All of the homes on the cul-de-sac had some degree of damage, ranging from blown outlets to warped soffit pieces to blown out wells.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: During the afternoon and evening hours of the fifth, an intense supercell thunderstorm moved over the South Plains region of West Texas, producing several tornadoes over portions of Cochran, Hockley, and Lubbock Counties. This thunderstorm also produced widespread damage from very strong straight-line winds and large hail across western and southwestern portions of the City of Lubbock (Lubbock County) before it exited into Crosby and Garza Counties and weakened late in the evening. A cold front stalled south of the South Plains early in the afternoon before returning northward as a warm front. Very humid air returned to the region as the front moved northward and contributed to extreme atmospheric instability by the afternoon. This allowed for explosive thunderstorm development from far east-central New Mexico into the South Plains. This supercell initially produced a brief tornado over far northwestern Cochran County that moved over open country and produced no known damage. Shortly thereafter, the supercell produced a strong wedge-type tornado several miles northwest of Morton (Cochran County), which destroyed multiple large wooden power poles as it tracked eastward, eventually crossing Texas State Highway 214 about four miles north of Morton before dissipating over northeastern Cochran County. The supercell then produced another strong tornado over far northwestern Hockley County, about five miles northwest of the community of Pettit (Hockley County), which was directly observed by mobile research radar. A separate and very brief cone-type tornado was then observed only two miles north of Pettit. The supercell then began to track more southeastward, with no tornadoes observed for a period of approximately 15 minutes. Just as the supercell approached US Highway 385 in north-central Hockley County, it produced another strong tornado which crossed US Highway 385 about three miles south of the community of Whitharral (Hockley County). This tornado destroyed several additional wooden power poles, rolled a semi-truck traveling on the highway, and damaged buildings and trees along its path before dissipating about seven miles east of US Highway 385. The final three tornadoes produced by this supercell were observed as the storm crossed from eastern Hockley County into western Lubbock County. The first tornado developed approximately three miles northeast of Texas State Highway 114 and the community of Smyer (Hockley County), damaging and destroying multiple manufactured homes as it moved eastward before dissipating along the Hockley/Lubbock County line. The second tornado developed very close to the termination of the previous tornado, and damaged and destroyed several homes and buildings as it tracked southeastward and dissipated only about a quarter mile north of Texas State Highway 114. The final tornado produced during this event developed and tracked over southern portions of Reese Center (Lubbock County), toppling large trees and damaging roofs before dissipating just outside the Lubbock city limits. Although the storm did not produce any additional tornadoes after this point, the supercell did continue to produce very strong straight-line winds and large hail, which resulted in widespread damage to homes and businesses across western and southwestern portions of the City of Lubbock. Many buildings within the city experienced significant damage to roofs and windows, and hail up to the size of tennis balls was observed within the city limits. The supercell continued to produce large hail and severe wind gusts as it moved over the community of Slaton in southeastern Lubbock County, with the storm finally weakening over Crosby and Garza Counties with no additional severe weather reports after it moved to the east of the Caprock Escarpment. After the initial supercell thunderstorm moved east, additional thunderstorms developed over far eastern New Mexico and the South Plains bringing more severe storms late in the evening through the early morning hours of the sixth.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of the subtropical high over the Four Corners/Rockies and an area of low pressure near the southern CA coastline resulted in a modest southeasterly flow that advected modest amounts of moisture across much of central and southern AZ. With the moisture advection, PWAT values increased upwards of 1.3-1.5. This moisture quantity in combination with strong daytime heating led to moderate instability as MLCAPE increased upwards of 1000 J/KG. Thunderstorm activity during the early to mid afternoon hours on the 2nd developed across the higher terrain areas of south-central and southeast AZ with outflow boundaries migrating west to northwestward into the lower deserts, where additional thunderstorm activity developed, with the heaviest activity observed across the western half of Maricopa County through the western side of the Phoenix metro area. Another isolated cluster of thunderstorms developed across central La Paz County as well. The increasing upper-level forcing from the approaching low pressure system likely enhanced the thunderstorm activity. During the afternoon hours on the 3rd, additional thunderstorm activity, although much more isolated in nature, developed across portions of south-central AZ. This activity was aided by moderate instability as MLCAPE values were around 1000-1500 J/KG and the presence of the upper-level forcing from the aforementioned low pressure system as it was traversing the region. With DCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/KG throughout the entire time period, conditions were favorable for the generation of strong downburst winds as well as dense blowing dust. With PWATs values approaching 1.5, the environment was moist enough for heavy rainfall producing thunderstorms that would result in isolated flash flooding.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms pummeled the Lower Rio Grande Valley, especially during the afternoon and overnight hours of March 27th into early on March 28th, resulting in historic seasonal rainfall and widespread flash and areal flooding across the RGV.  Total rainfall ranged from 8 to nearly 19 inches based on trusted observations, with 10 inches or more falling across some of the highest populated locations from south McAllen through the south side of Interstate Highway 2 in Hidalgo County, then farther north in Cameron County, where 12 to nearly 19 inches fell between La Feria and Rio Hondo, including Harlingen and San Benito. Trusted radar estimates indicated up to 20.5 inches in east Harlingen, but as of this writing there were no verified values this high from trusted observers.||Initial rainfall began late on March 26th in eastern and southern Cameron County, with flooding in east Brownsville toward Port Isabel around sunrise on the 27th. ||Nearly five thousand homes and other structures were impacted, with more than two thousand having major damage or destruction due to 2 or more feet of water in them. Hundreds of local roads were flooded with up to 4 feet of water in some places, and at least one thousand vehicles trapped on flooded roads were damaged or totaled. Unfortunately, there were fatalities, with five dead on the U.S. side of the Rio Grande due to drowning and a lightning-induced fire, and one on the Mexican side of the border in Reynosa.||In addition to the flooding, wind damage occurred in several locations, with two small tornadoes touching down during the late afternoon of the 27th near Edcouch, and just after midnight on the 28th in Port Isabel.||Though damage estimates were still unknown as of late May, it is estimated that total damage was upwards of $100 million.  By early July, damage estimates had risen to $157 million; these numbers only included initial values of Public Assistance (PA) of $94 million, and $63 million in Individual Assistance in much of the Rio Grande Valley.  These values did not include privately-insured damage, and totals were likely to exceed $200 million. Additional damage estimates will be available by the end of 2025.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unseasonably hot and humid air mass beneath a strong upper ridge in place across the Midwest led to the development of storms late on the evening of the 20th across the Northern Plains. These congealed into a thunderstorm complex over the Upper Midwest, tracking eastward along the perimeter of the ridge, into the Upper Great Lakes on the morning of the 21st. A NW-SE oriented broken line of storms developed along a warm advection axis ahead of the initial line of storms; this produced hail up to the size of golf balls across parts of northern Lower Michigan, including the Traverse City metro area. Meanwhile, a strong mesolow developed at the heart of the slowly decaying thunderstorm complex, ultimately driving a meteotsunami across the length of Lake Superior, resulting in significant water level changes of as much as 2-4ft on Whitefish Bay and the Upper St. Mary's River during the morning hours. This resulted in delays in freighter traffic through the Soo Locks, the waterway through which nearly 100 percent of America's domestic iron ore passes. Periodic water level fluctuations up to 2 feet remained present on the eastern end of Lake Superior through the next couple days, and water levels did not settle back down to normal for several days through the end of June.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple reports of lightning damage in the Traverse City, MI metro area, including significant damage to a large oak tree leading to some structural damage, and a possible structure fire caused by lightning near Long Lake west of Traverse City.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Following a fairly active June, unsettled conditions rolled right on into the month of July with bands of rain and thunderstorms springing up ahead of a cold front on the 1st. Activity continued until the front pushed east of the Appalachians early on the 2nd, then drier conditions took hold for southeast Ohio, northeast Kentucky, southwest Virginia, and much of West Virginia while the front stalled across central Virginia, Maryland, and the Carolinas.||Much of the area received between a half inch and two inches of rain, with pockets of locally higher amounts. One strip of 2.5 to 4 inches of rain resulted in flash flooding in Cabell, Kanawha, Mason, and Putnam counties. This resulted in flooding that impacted several roads within these counties. Within the strongest thunderstorms, damaging wind gusts yielded downed trees and power lines across several counties west of the I-79 corridor. Storms tapered off and pushed eastward by the late afternoon, bringing the threat for severe weather and flooding to an end.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house on Pike Street south of Parkersburg. No fire or smoke was seen but locals reported a burning smell.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Mid-level shortwave approaching the region, coupled with a low-level warm front, allowed for ample lift across central Pennsylvania during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 16, 2025. Ample moisture in place, with precipitable water values in the 1.80 to 2.20 range and very little deep-layer shear promoted slow-moving showers and thunderstorms with efficient rainfall rates across much of the area. Flooding across the hydrologically sensitive areas of northern Pennsylvania resulted in multiple instances of flash flooding across Potter County, with flooding also observed across the western highlands of Pennsylvania. Ample instability brought upon a secondary thunderstorm risk during the late evening hours, with lightning causing a structural fire in Cambria County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residence on the 500 block of East Horner Street in Ebensburg,  causing a fire. No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Showers and thunderstorms across eastern Ohio and western PA associated with a weak shortwave continued approaching portions of central Pennsylvania during the early morning hours of July 26, 2025. As showers and thunderstorms continued progressing eastward across the Commonwealth, interactions with a quasi-stationary boundary in an increasingly unstable and moist environment allowed for intensification of showers and thunderstorms. Severe thunderstorms began to produce tree damage in Blair County before continuing to produce tree damage into the south-central mountains during the afternoon hours. Later in the evening, an isolated cell began to pop up across the Middle Susquehanna Valley in a corridor of enhanced instability and shear, causing tree damage in northern Lancaster County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm produced lightning that struck a garage and started a fire on the 7900 block of Woodland Drive in Paradise Township, York County. The fire began to spread rapidly, damaging portions of the residence before crews were able to put out the fire. No injuries were reported.

Some of these storms became severe, causing multiple downbursts with strong, damaging winds which downed numerous trees and power lines across Ouachita Parish before diminishing by early evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front was tracking southeast towards Kentucky during the early morning hours of Thursday, May 8th. But by the time it got into the state, it began to stall. It remained stalled, with a spot low across western Kentucky, for much of the day. It wasn't until about 0Z that WPC analyzed it starting to sink back southward again, quickly reaching the TN border just a few hours later, where it continued to sink into the overnight.  A upper level low and shortwave were also moving through the state during this time, amplifying the instability and lift in the warm sector - which is where eastern Kentucky was located. Hail seemed to be the most common mode of severe weather, not just in Kentucky but in sourrounding states to our south and east, with several 2 inch stones reported in eastern Kentucky.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface low was centered over Nebraska with an associated boundary stretching into Minnesota. Early on the morning of August 9th this boundary had stalled across northwest to west central Iowa. Storms were elevated, but the low level jet helped to erode the cap through the early morning hours and storms were able to tap into 3500+ J/kg of MLCAPE. With 30 kts of 0-6 km shear, storm storms were able to persist but the mode was a messy linear and multi cell hybrid.  Storms produced wind damage many communities in west central and northwest Iowa, mainly to trees and outbuildings. Storms were also efficient rain producers with 3+ inches reported in many locations, though no flooding occurred.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree was struck by lightning at 833 am. Delayed report.

Several reports of wind gust damage, along with reports of high surf, flooding and debris flow were received between August 16 to 18.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media through social media reported a lightning strike that impacted a residence in the Bo. Lagunas sector of Aguada. Residents reported a loud explosion-like sound and a bright flash that woke people from sleep. Minor structural damage to a wall was observed. No injuries were reported. Lightning strike occurred within outer bands associated with Hurricane Erin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Late afternoon storms under easterly flow sea breeze regime produce lightning strikes that injure one person near Lealman in Pinellas County, cause an apartment fire near Holiday in Pasco County, and produce a gustnado near Pinellas Park in Pinellas County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Social media post relayed a drone video of a lightning-caused fire at an apartment complex in Holiday. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front over northern Alabama ahead of an approaching cold front during the late  morning and afternoon hours.  Tragically, a boater on Lake Guntersville was struck by lightning while fishing and was seriously injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guntersville Fire/Rescue personnel responded to an incident where a man was struck by lightning on a boat on Lake Guntersville near Honeyomb Cemetery. The victim had serious injuries and burns in several areas.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front slowly moved into New Jersey, with showers and thunderstorms developing in a very unstable and tropical airmass. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed, producing damaging wind gusts and large hail across portions of the state.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local news reports that a 28 year old man was injured from a lightning strike while  golfing. He later died from his injuries. Time estimated from radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved into a very moist and unstable environment. Damaging wind gusts were observed in portions of New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A commercial building fire on Oberlin Ave due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Afternoon and evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce a lightning strike that injures one person near Seminole in Pinellas County, and produce street flooding stranding vehicles near Wildwood in Sumter County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: FDEM relayed report from Pinellas County 911 dispatch of an individual injured by a lightning strike near Seminole, requiring transport for treatment following initial on-scene attention from local fire department personnel.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Training thunderstorms brought several rounds of torrential rainfall to portions of northeast Illinois on the 12th, especially around the interior Chicago metro area. Street flooding was reported around a number of municipalities. Nearly 500 service requests were made to the city of Chicago for water in basements. One person was also injured at Montrose Beach as lightning struck nearby.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Chicago Park District lifeguard is believed to have been impacted by a nearby lightning strike. The man sustained minor injuries as storms were passing over just before 3 PM CST. He was transported to a local hospital and kept overnight as a precaution and was released the following morning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The front eventually sagged south back into the Mid-South during the early morning hours of April 5th. Strong low-level moisture transport into the frontal zone resulted in heavy rain and training storms across northern sections of the Mid-South, mainly north of I-40. A bow echo developed along and just south of the slowly advancing front. This feature crossed the entire forecast area producing 13 tornadoes, including an EF-2, and wind damage. Heavy rain continued through the morning hours with flash flooding increasing across the Mid-South. ||The final round of severe weather occurred during the afternoon and evening of April 5th. The slow-moving cold front combined with an increasingly unstable airmass, strong upper-level divergence, and 0-6 km bulk shear values of 50-60 knots provided the ingredients for more severe storms. A QLCS with a bookend vortex pushed into east Arkansas and West TN with a good deal of wind damage. The southern end of the line became more supercellular during the afternoon and evening and produced seven tornadoes, including an EF-2. The combination of continued abundant moisture with precipitable water values greater than 1.75 inches and strong low-level moisture transport into the frontal zone resulted in very heavy rainfall and considerable flash flooding across much of the Mid-South. ||The severe weather threat finally wound down by late evening on April 5th with the flash flood threat ending a few hours later. Total rainfall amounts of 10-15 inches occurred across parts of east Arkansas, the Missouri Bootheel, West Tennessee, and extreme northwest Mississippi during this event. This resulted in widespread river flooding for several days following the event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A structure fire caused by lightning was reported on CR 265.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front with strong shortwave energy moved into a hot, humid, and unstable airmass, triggering the development thunderstorms in eastern Pennsylvania. These storms produced frequent lightning with damage from a lightning strike reported.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: State Route 309 was closed in North Whitehall Township due to a lightning strike that downed several utility poles and trapped several cars.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were were reportedly killed by an afternoon lightning strike in far southern Highlands County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Highlands County Sheriff and Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission officers discovered the vehicle and bodies of two men and their hunting dogs on a levee along a canal near Rucks Dairy Road southeast of Brighton in Highlands County. The men had reportedly gone hunting but had not returned, and were discovered two days later. Investigators suspected the fatal lightning strike likely occurred on Monday, September 22, as the men attempted to return to their car for shelter, with the time of the incident estimated from radar and satellite data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical wave moving south of the islands, moisture, local effects, excessive diurnal heating, and sea breeze variations, promoted the formation of showers and thunderstorms over the islands during the last two days of the month. Flooding was reported in Yauco and Carolina, while a fatal lightning strike was reported in Toa Vaca Lake, Villalba.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The 911 Call Center reported that at approximately 3:20 PM AST, a lightning strike impacted two individuals in a boat near the fishing club by the dam at Lago Toa Vaca. One individual was reported conscious with burns to the hands but breathing. The second individual, a 48 year old male, was thrown into the water by the impact; his body was found at around 8 PM ast.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of forcing associated with a surface front and mid-level energy along with deep moisture residing across the area led to an environment capable of producing heavy rainfall across Southeast South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported power lines down and transformer blown due to a lightning strike along Highway 17 between South Shellmore Boulevard and Dragoon Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A shortwave passing across the region encountered an environment displaying deep moisture and warm temperatures, supporting thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management and local media reports indicated a lightning strike causing a house fire to a townhome on Pine Shadow Drive in Goose Creek. Damage to a chimney could be seen on a video.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weakening line of showers and thunderstorms produced hail across portions of central Wisconsin during the morning on Saturday (8/09).  ||A stronger line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and tracked through central, east-central Wisconsin and the lakeshore ahead of an approaching cold front. These storms produced widespread wind damage with Door County included in a disaster declaration due to the significant storm damage.  The Door County Emergency Manager indicated there was $431,938 worth of damage and debris clean up across central and northern Door County.  Egg Harbor and Ephraim experienced significant damage, with Sister Bay and Baileys Harbor notably affected. ||The storms also produced a weak, brief tornado in Peninsula State Park (Door Co.) with lightning causing a house fire and significant damage to a home in Casco (Kewaunee Co.), producing around $125,000 worth of damage. In total, this event produced over a half a million worth of damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house was struck by lightning and started on fire. The fire produced around $125,000 worth of damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A tropical wave, southeasterly flow and abundant tropical moisture over the islands promoted t-storm formation. A lightning strike impacted electrical lines in Aibonito, causing a utility pole to fall and result in a power outage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A NWS employee and emergency managers, reported a lightning strike that impacted electrical lines near KM 3.0 of PR-725 in the Los Pinos sector of Barrio Llanos. The incident caused a utility pole to fall and scattered debris in the area, resulting in a power outage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A series of thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall and widespread flooding to much of the Chicago metro area, namely the south and west suburbs and up into the city of Chicago. Several Oswego District 308 schools received water and storm damage. Flood damages were estimated at around $288 million across the metro area, most of which came from the city of Chicago which alone accounted for roughly $230 million in damages with roughly 40,000 individual structures flooded around the city. The remainder of Cook County accounted for roughly $57 million in flood damages with more than 10,000 additional structures flooded. Several instances of wind damage were also reported, mostly damage to trees.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike impacted Oswego East High School knocking out electrical systems including telephones. The time of the strike is unknown and was estimated using radar and lightning data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moist southwest steering flow focused the afternoon and early evening sea breeze merger toward the I-95 corridor. Storm produced locally heavy rainfall, gusty winds and lightning. Three people were struck and injured by lighting in St. Augustine Beach FL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three individuals were struck by lightning at the Saint Augustine Beach Pier. Officials said an elderly man was transported in critical condition to a local trauma center and the other person was transported with minor injuries to a local hospital. All three survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An embedded shortwave rounded the top of thermal ridging across Iowa. Storms across Nebraska and South Dakota earlier in the day moved into Iowa by afternoon, moving along the instability gradient across northern Iowa with over 4000 J/kg of MPCAPE to the south. An elevated mixed layer prevented more robust storm development initially, but eventually increasing cold pool strength pulled those stronger gusts to the surface and storms continued to push east. Severe gusts were common along the line of storms with several reports of tree and power line damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home and the fire department confirmed a hole in the roof with a small area of smoldering material in the attic. Reported by emergency manager, time estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A complex of thunderstorms developed over the Red River Valley region during the early morning hours of the 8th and pushed into central and northeastern Minnesota during the mid to late morning hours. The storms intensified as they moved into the Brainerd Lakes region with bowing segments producing strong winds. By the late morning hours, the storms outran their support leading to a quick drop in intensity as they reached Lake Superior and northwestern Wisconsin. Numerous reports of tree damage were received from the Brainerd Lakes area into Aitkin and St. Louis counties. A lightning strike at a cemetery damaged headstones as well.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large white pine was hit by lightning and exploded causing damage to headstones and  grave markers at the Thorp Cemetery.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered scattered strong to severe thunderstorms in the Illinois River Valley during the evening of August 18th.  A few of the cells produced 60-70mph wind gusts and minor wind damage, as well as prolific lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a utility pole and caused it to shatter at the intersection of North East Street and East Court Street in Farmington.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front triggered scattered strong to severe thunderstorms in the Illinois River Valley during the evening of August 18th.  A few of the cells produced 60-70mph wind gusts and minor wind damage, as well as prolific lightning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a transformer on East Washington Street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak upper-level low moving through the Desert Southwest combined with above normal moisture (PWATs upwards of 0.8) to generate scattered showers and a few embedded thunderstorms across portions of south-central AZ during the early morning hours of the 22nd. Even though the shower activity was not impactful at all, an isolated thunderstorm moving through the Avondale area just after 0400MST generated cloud to ground lightning that sparked a small house fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning strike resulted in a small house fire near the area of El Mirage and Lower Buckeye Roads in Avondale. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wet, unstable weather pattern due to Tropical Storm Jerry's proximity supports periods of heavy rain and thunderstorm activity across PR.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency management reported that a lightning strike impacted a power pole and associated electrical lines along Calle 59 in the Rexville area of Bayam��n. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A wet, unstable weather pattern due to Tropical Storm Jerry's proximity supports periods of heavy rain and thunderstorm activity across PR.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trained weather spotter reported a lightning strike on a pine tree in Vega Baja. No injuries or additional damage were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An unstable weather pattern supported periods of enhanced shower and thunderstorm activity across Puerto Rico. Thunderstorms developed mainly during the afternoon, resulting in localized impacts, including flooding, hail, and lightning-related incidents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Members of the public reported that a pine tree was struck by lightning along PR-878 near Beltran Auto Parts in Naranjito. The lightning strike damaged the tree, breaking several branches and affecting the trunk.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level trough shifted east through the Central and Southern Plains during the afternoon/evening of October 18th, reinforcing a cold front southeast into Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and North Louisiana. A hot and humid air mass was present ahead of the front, with temperatures climbing into the mid 80s to near 90 degrees. When combined with ample low level moisture present, moderate instability was in place, with increasing wind shear ahead of the front/trough resulting in multi-cell thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms became severe, with damaging winds downing trees and power lines across portions of extreme Eastern Texas, Southern Arkansas, and North Louisiana before the storms exited the region into the Lower Mississippi Valley after midnight. Unfortunately, one fatality was reported in Union Parish after lightning struck a deer stand, setting it on fire and killing a 17 year old male hunter inside.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck an elevated deer stand south of Highway 2 just southeast of the Weldon community. A 17 year old male hunter was in the stand when it was struck and caught fire, and did not survive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The remnants of Pacific Hurricane Priscilla pushed tropical moisture into southern Nevada, fueling scattered thunderstorms. Several produced heavy rain and flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a brush fire near Highway 160 and Trout Canyon Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The remnants of Pacific Hurricane Priscilla pushed tropical moisture into southern Nevada, fueling scattered thunderstorms. Several produced heavy rain and flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A house near Mae Road was struck by lightning, knocking off the siding and scorching the house, but not setting fire to it.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak, cut-off low pressure system moved over Arizona bringing numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Law Enforcement reported 2 hikers injured from a lightning strike on Humphreys Peak.  Time of event estimated on radar.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level trough with a period of light winds contributed to the development of strong thunderstorms across PR between October 5 and 9.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At approximately 12:05 PM AST, a lightning strike occurred at Condominio San Cipriani in Carolina. A 53-year-old male was exiting his vehicle while holding an umbrella when lightning struck his left arm. The individual sustained injuries and was transported to a regional hospital, where he was reported to be in stable condition. No additional injuries or property damage were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level trough with a period of light winds contributed to the development of strong thunderstorms across PR between October 5 and 9.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The 911 Call Center reported that a tree struck by lightning fell along Avenida Baldorioty in Carolina, just past Plaza Carolina. The fallen tree landed on a vehicle, causing a roadway obstruction. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A storm system of mainly multi-cluster strong to severe storms moved across the Ozarks producing localized reports of quarter sized hail. Additionally, strong winds downed several trees and caused power outages with limbs and trees on powerlines. At least one structure was struck by lightning causing damage by fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two barns and a home were reported to have been struck by lightning. Small fires occurred with the barns and the front porch of the home partially collapsed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level low brought two main rounds of thunderstorms to North and Central Texas during the last week of October 2025. The first, and most severe, was a large storm complex on the evening of October 24, followed by isolated activity on the afternoon of October 25. Severe weather primarily consisted of thunderstorm wind damage and isolated instances of flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Denton Co EDS reported on Facebook that they responded to a house fire in the 1800 block of Elm Place in Northlake where the roof of a home was on fire. The fire was quickly put out but some damage occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper-level low brought two main rounds of thunderstorms to North and Central Texas during the last week of October 2025. The first, and most severe, was a large storm complex on the evening of October 24, followed by isolated activity on the afternoon of October 25. Severe weather primarily consisted of thunderstorm wind damage and isolated instances of flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Denton Co EDS reported on Facebook that they responded to a house fire in the 700 block of Plaza Lane in Argyle where the attic of a home was on fire. The fire was quickly put out but some damage occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of showers and strong to severe thunderstorms (a few exhibiting embedded supercell structures) pushed east into northwestern Alabama during the early evening hours.  This line became more organized and stronger as it pushed quickly east as it approached the I-65 corridor producing more widespread 50 to 70 mph wind gusts.  The winds resulted in trees and power lines being knocked down at numerous locations and several thousand without power.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree, causing it to fall and block both lanes of traffic near the intersection of highway 157 and CR 237.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface boundary was positioned west to east across the Quad State during the early afternoon with convective activity increasing with daytime heating. Scattered convection primarily occurred south of the boundary mid to late afternoon. MLCAPE reached 2000J/kg but effective bulk shear was very limited. Precipitable water values over 2 allowed for torrential rainfall rates. Training storm occurrence was limited, leaving flash flooding south of Harrisburg as the one flood report out of Southern Illinois.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a barn on Mermet Rd, which resulted in a fire that fully engulfed the barn and burned it down.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An active day of thunderstorms impacted much of North and Central Texas on November 20, triggered by the passage of a Pacific cold front and an upper trough. The day brought several instances of damaging winds, large hail, and flooding. Frequent cloud to ground lightning also took place, resulting in multiple house fires in the DFW Metroplex.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A public report inticated a house fire caused by lightning on Alta Sierra Dr in Benbrook.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A seasonably humid and unstable environment allowed for widespread storms to develop across portions of central and eastern Virginia during the afternoon of July 27. These storms produced damaging winds and isolated hail as they congealed into a line while moving generally southeast to south.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A couple of trees were knocked down likely due to a lightning strike in the Lago Mar subdivision in Virginia Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was struck by lightning while boating on the Intracoastal Waterway on the Pender County coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man who was struck by lightning on June 29 while boating on the Intracoastal Waterway succumbed to his injuries and died on July 10.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved southwestward into the Tucson Metro area causing power outages and fire starts due to lightning. Additionally, the storms produced heavy rainfall causing running water over roadways in the Tucson Metro. Heavy rainfall also caused a roadway to close for roughly 24 hours in Benson.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike damaged utility equipment and caused 200 customers to loose power for an unknown amount of time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong thunderstorms moved southwestward into the Tucson Metro area causing power outages and fire starts due to lightning. Additionally, the storms produced heavy rainfall causing running water over roadways in the Tucson Metro. Heavy rainfall also caused a roadway to close for roughly 24 hours in Benson.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike hit power company equipment and caused power outages at the Pima  County Election Headquarters and several other areas in Midtown Tucson.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms in the early morning hours produced between 0.25 to 0.80 inches of rainfall in the lower valley floor and between 1.0 to 2.80 inches in the Catalina and Rincon Foothills. This rainfall caused multiple roads to close in the Tucson Metro and in Benson, AZ. Additionally, utility equipment was damaged due to lightning and caused a power outage for 183 customers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Utility equipment was damaged due to lightning and caused a power outage for 183 customers for an unknown duration of time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms produced occasionally severe wind gusts across parts of Mississippi on July 1st. On July 3rd, a brief landspout tornado occurred in Bolivar County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tree was struck by lightning and fell onto a home along Greenfield Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms produced occasionally severe wind gusts across parts of Mississippi on July 1st. On July 3rd, a brief landspout tornado occurred in Bolivar County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home along Slade Road.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A power pole was struck by lightning and then fell onto a car. No one was injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low and remnant MCVs produced several rounds of heavy rain and training storms that produced flash flooding for a few day across the region, mainly across Central Texas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency manager reported a house fire caused by a lightning strike between Waco and McGregor.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On June 3 and 4, a cold front and a dryline served as focal points for thunderstorm development across North and Central Texas. These storms were associated with several instances of severe weather and flooding. Unfortunately Unfortunately one person died due to flooding in Dallas County, and a lightning strike killed one person and severely injured another person in Grayson County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning and set on fire on County Road 286 in Lamkin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Isolated thunderstorms developed over Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of September 3, 2025. While these thunderstorms remained non-severe due to poor lapse rates, other ingredients were enough to still allow for strong winds. These thunderstorms also produced frequent lightning which was the cause for a structure fire in Mt. Juliet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a structure fire in the 500 building of Glass Creek Apartments. The fire was contained to a small portion of the roof. No injuries were reported, and no residents were displaced. Damages are a rough estimate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms due to a cold front and upper level disturbance produced large hail and damaging winds to portions of southeast WI. A lightning fatality also occurred to a man on a hiking trail in the Township of Kewaskum.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An employee of the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources was struck by lightning when working outside near the New Fane hiking trail. The lightning strike was fatal.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A typical summertime pattern of numerous afternoon thunderstorms occurred. These storms produced many lightning strikes, one of them hitting a house and starting a fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: St. Tammany Fire Department responded to a house fire on Sunset Drive in Slidell. No  injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of showers and storms, associated with a cold front and lee trough, moved into central and southern Virginia in the late afternoon and evening hours of September 4. While weak instability generally limited storm intensity, the strongest storms produced isolated areas of wind damage as well as lightning. An isolated lightning strike occurred in central Virginia.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A reported lightning strike caused a crawl space fire in a single-family home on the 4600 block of Lee Street in Chester, VA.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning injuries were reported with afternoon thunderstorms that developed along the Gulf sea breeze in Southwest Florida on June 21, 2025.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Marco Island Police Department reported three minor injuries associated with lightning striking a tiki hut along Marco Island Beach. All three individuals were transported for further assessment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of September 21, North Texas experienced explosive thunderstorm development due to a shortwave trough and a meandering front interacting with a warm, unstable environment. These storms persisted through the evening and dissipated overnight into the morning of September 22. Multiple storms produced reports of large hail and damaging winds, with some isolated instances of flash flooding also occurring.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two house fires were caused by lightning in the Brookside community in Princeton.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cool front entered the region during the early afternoon hours of September 24th, ahead of an approaching upper trough that traversed the Southern Plains. Strong heating ahead of the front and attendant trough contributed to increased instability, with large scale forcing from these surface and upper level features contributing to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms containing heavy rainfall across portions of extreme Eastern Texas and portions of Northwest Louisiana. Damaging winds and localized flash flooding were observed across portions of Caddo and Bossier Parishes, with an isolated tornado also touching down just southeast of Benton, before these storms weakened during the mid-afternoon hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Longfellow Trace in the Southern Trace subdivision, causing a  fire which significantly damaged the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moist and unstable airmass was in place on September 27. Meanwhile, a surface low lingered across south central Virginia along the North Carolina border with a stationary front extending east along the state border. While this primarily resulted in heavy rain and flash flooding, an isolated lightning strike occurred in southeast Virginia early on the morning of September 27.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caught a house on fire in Smithfield early in the morning. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A highly unstable and strongly sheared environment set the stage for an evening of severe weather, as a line of thunderstorms pushed south from the Southern Plains into North Texas on June 8. Widespread wind damage, scattered large hail reports and a few tornadoes occurred as storms continued south overnight into the early morning hours of June 9.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that two men were struck by lightning at The Bridges golf  course in Gunter. One man was killed and another injured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Thunderstorms developed north of the Iron Range into the Minnesota Arrowhead during the afternoon of the 8th. Aside from some small hail and a lightning strike damaging some fiber optic lines, the storms remained below severe limits.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike near the Gunflint Trail and Soderberg Lane damaged about 2,000 feet of underground fiber optic cable causing a loss of phone and internet service to customers from that point to the end of the Gunflint Trail. Service was restored after about 14 hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon through early evening hours of the 27th, ahead of an approaching upper level disturbance. The atmosphere became moderately unstable during the afternoon across the area, but wind shear was weak. This combination resulted in intense thunderstorm development that was fairly short-lived and unorganized. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging downburst wind. A woman was struck and killed by lightning near Eufaula during the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman was walking through Greenwood cemetery, and took shelter under a tree when a thunderstorm moved into the area. She was struck and killed by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of June 1st, an outflow boundary from morning thunderstorms, combined with a strong shortwave trough moving south from the Southern Plains into North Texas, created a focus for thunderstorm development. These storms began near the I-20 corridor and moved south throughout the afternoon, eventually dissipating over Central Texas by evening. The most significant severe weather event associated with this system was large hail, up to 3, in Parker and Tarrant counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person suffered severe injuries from electrocution due to a lightning strike on Circle Court in the Willow Park area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On the afternoon of June 1st, an outflow boundary from morning thunderstorms, combined with a strong shortwave trough moving south from the Southern Plains into North Texas, created a focus for thunderstorm development. These storms began near the I-20 corridor and moved south throughout the afternoon, eventually dissipating over Central Texas by evening. The most significant severe weather event associated with this system was large hail, up to 3, in Parker and Tarrant counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a canopy at Mustang Park with 14 people underneath it. Twelve people were treated on the scene for minor injuries and two others were transported to the hospital. A vehicle parked near the tree was damaged.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A north/south oriented trough axis extended from the Great Lakes to the Florida Panhandle and a ridge was centered over the Desert Southwest encompasses the rest of the country. That put the CWA right between both features. The frontal boundary associated with the trough stalled along the northern Gulf Coast. That front was the initial focal point for convection to begin developing early in the afternoon. That activity was been able to capitalize on very high instability. Quite robust thunderstorms produced several damaging wind events.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike caused a fire on a home along Dutch Lane between Ponchatoula and  Springfield.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper trough approached the Mid-Atlantic region from the west on June 19th. Strong solar heating and rich low level moisture combined for robust instability across the area. Moderate wind shear ahead of the upper trough resulted in sufficient shear for thunderstorm organization and resulted in widespread damaging winds across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a tree in Wyndham.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two storms caused damage in North Texas: one from a lightning strike, and the other with strong winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A media article reported that a lightning strike likely caused a house fire on Lakewood Drive in Grand Prairie near Joe Pool Lake. Notable damage could be seen to the roof and second story of the home. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Lorena's remnants, a late-summer cold front, and an upper-level trough collectively contributed to significant thunderstorm activity across North Texas during the afternoon and evening of September 5th and into the morning of September 6th. Several of these storms generated damaging wind gusts and hail, while frequent cloud-to-ground lightning resulted in multiple residential fires.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home on Wynfield Drive near Analea Lane in Little Elm was struck by lightning and heavily damaged by the resulting fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface cold front stationed across northern Pennsylvania allowed for scattered showers and thunderstorms to form in an environment with ample instability and limited shear during the afternoon and evening hours of June 25, 2025. These slow-moving showers and thunderstorms quickly became strong-to-severe with the aforementioned instability and were able to sustain and produce isolated instances of thunderstorm wind damage across Schuylkill and Clinton counties. Ample moisture in place, allowed for heavy rain with these showers and thunderstorms with water over roadways in urban areas of Centre County. A couple of lightning strikes from thunderstorms also caused structure fires during the evening, with one near Lock Haven and the other northwest of McConnellsburg.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning from a thunderstorm struck a building and caused a structure fire on Farrandsville Road northwest of Lock Haven.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a residence in Licking Creek Township, causing a house fire. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front moving across central Pennsylvania during the morning hours of June 28, 2025 with a surface cold front stationed in the Great Lake region allowed for much of central Pennsylvania to reside in the warm sector during the early afternoon and evening hours. Increasing instability, shear, and moisture due to this residence time primed the atmosphere ahead of a prefrontal trough allowing for ample lift to produce showers and thunderstorms. Thunderstorms in western Pennsylvania during the late morning hours quickly grew strong-to-severe, producing an isolated instance of tree damage in Elk County, continuing eastward and producing damage in southern Clinton and southern Lycoming counties. Scattered thunderstorms also began to form across southern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours with slow-moving, severe thunderstorms producing large hail, tree damage, and flash flooding across Lancaster County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a house near the intersection of Hahnstown Road and Glenwood Drive in Ephrata Township. No report of injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line swept through the tri-state area ahead of a cold front on March 16th. Numerous reports of severe weather were received.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The historic Beadel House at Tall Timbers was destroyed in a fire caused by lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: From April 24 to April 27, daily thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening, triggered by a dryline and a meandering frontal boundary. These long-lasting supercells were fueled by a highly unstable and sheared environment, resulting in several tornadoes, damaging winds, and very large hail. Two fatalities occurred on April 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning started a house fire in Colleyville that was contained to the attic of the home, however a female adult and a child under the age of 3 died in the fire. Another child was transported with injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: From March 12th through March 14th of 2026, a large and powerful kona storm setup over the northern central Pacific, and brought numerous impacts across the state. This low was supported by a broad and potent upper level trough that lingered for many days. Impacts included flash flooding, wind damage, large surf, and strong thunderstorms.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike destroyed a transmission pole in the Campbell Industrial area at about 2 am.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak mid-level impulse moved through the Lower Mississippi Valley on March 9th. As the system approached the local area, mid-level temperatures cooled, increasing atmospheric instability. These cooler temperatures aloft, combined with near-record surface temperatures in the mid 80s, supported robust thunderstorm development during the afternoon hours. One thunderstorm became severe and produced large hail across portions of East Feliciana Parish.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck Twin Steeples Creative Arts Center, a historic art gallery in Ponchatoula. A fire started as a result of this strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong low pressure (991 millibars) moving across the Upper Midwest lifted a warm front northward into the Altamaha River in southeast Georgia. Deeper moisture surged northward into northern Florida in the wake of the warm frontal passage. This combined with a warm and unstable air mass resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developing in the afternoon into evening along the inland moving sea breezes mainly south of the I-10 corridor. Cool mid-level temperatures, steep lapse rates and ML CAPE values in excess of 2,000 j/kg caused strong storms to briefly severe to develop in the late afternoon into the evening hours. The Storm Prediction Center had a Marginal (level 1 out of 5) Risk for severe thunderstorm development across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Clay County EM Reported An Electrical Outage Likely Due To Lightning which Impacted Approximately 1,400 Customers In The Middleburg Area. No Infrastructure Damage was Reported.

The roof caught on fire and quickly destroyed much of the inside of the home. The lightning caused a large hole in the roof. The family has been displaced. No injuries or fatalities.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike led to the total loss of two sheds to fire.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The total loss of a small shed and a Tobacco Shed to a fire was attributed to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A home was damaged by lightning in Socastee, SC.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a home on Farrier Drive, causing damage and displacing three people.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A line of strong to severe storms developed over central Wisconsin as warm, moist and unstable air aloft surged into the region. The line of storms then moved southeast across southern Wisconsin.  Widespread wind damage occurred across much of south central to southeast Wisconsin, with two tornadoes documented along with the high winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Home struck by lightning and followed by a fire. The Fort Atkinson Fire Department reported it took 45 minutes to get the fire under control. No injuries, but structural and smoke and water damage displaced the 4 residents from the home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An organized area of low pressure tracked along a stationary over the region and brought lines and clusters of strong thunderstorms and heavy rainfall to southern WI. Flash flooding occurred in spots from Rock County to the Milwaukee area. One storm produced a tornado in Walworth county with a brief path.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Report of a lightning-related fatality in a gas station parking lot.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Severe storms moved across the state of Mississippi during the morning, afternoon and evening hours of April 26 through April 29 2026. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts that downed trees and powerlines. Some of these storms produced hail and a brief tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Camper struck by lightning and burned up. The camper was along Plum Nellie Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A vigorous low-pressure system and cold front pushed through the Plains and the Ozarks, interacting with a warm, moist air mass as a strong upper-level trough and a veered wind profile created high wind shear and instability. This set the stage for supercellular development that evolved into bowing line segments. This setup brought destructive straight-line wind gusts of 60-70 mph, with isolated gusts reaching up to 75 mph. Hail up to 2 inches occurred and 5 tornadoes touched down in Benton and Morgan Counties.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A home was struck by lightning causing a structure fire on the south side of Versailles.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front attendant to a southern Canada low pressure center moved slowly through northwest North Carolina, causing showers and storms to form. Bulk shear of around 30kts in the North Carolina High Country encouraged some isolated severe thunderstorms to form during the afternoon of May 21st.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lightning struck a church steeple, setting it on fire.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed on a daily basis across the region over Memorial Day weekend as a result of several passing upper level disturbances. Some storms produced severe hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding. Significant flash flooding occurred in North Richland Hills in Tarrant County on May 25th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency manager reported a lightning-caused house fire in Colleyville that damaged the roof and attic of the house. Another 4 houses were also reported struck by lightning, but no major damage was reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slowly advancing cold front was positioned beneath strong west-southwesterly flow downstream of a broad upper-level trough with embedded shortwaves. A moist low level layer and strong instability combined with strengthening deep-layer and low-level wind shear to support discrete supercells across southwest and southern Mississippi during the late afternoon and evening. These storms produced large hail and multiple tornadoes over southwest Mississippi, one EF1 and one EF2 tornado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: House fire reported as started by lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A diffuse frontal boundary stalled across the northern forecast area 5/22 with broad troughing present. Areas south of the boundary saw generous heating with MLCAPE values nearing 1500-2000 J/kg and weak deep layer shear near 25-30 kts. This heating across the boundary lead to a couple strong storms, but one that produced tree damage near Thomson GA and started a fire at McCormick High School in McCormick County SC.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: McCormick County Emergency Services reported a structure fire at the McCormick County  High School gym due to a lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broad upper level low centered offshore from northern California produced numerous thunderstorms in southern Oregon. One thunderstorm produced a lightning strike that burned a hole through the roof of a home.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm in the city of Ashland produced  a lightning strike that burned a hole in the roof of a home.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold upper level low approached the Hawaiian islands and led to thunderstorms and flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm brought frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes across Oahu. Some of the lightning struck utility poles which led to power outages for about 35000 customers. The outage areas included, but were not limited to,  Makaha, Aiea, Ewa, Kapolei, Makakilo, Mililani, Pearl City, Waikele, Waimalu and Waipahu. According to HECO, a lightning strike ignited a fire in the switchyard at Kahe Power Plant shortly after 3 p.m., which damaged equipment. Flights at the Daniel K. Inouye International Airport were also delayed due to the lightning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A stalled frontal boundary north of the region, as well as Gulf Coast and Atlantic Coast sea breezes, combined with usual early summer high instability and PWATs close to 2 inches to produce numerous showers and thunderstorms across the region, as well as isolated severe downbursts. Slow storm motion attributed to localized heavy rainfall and minor flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Putnam County Emergency  Management reported that lightning sparked a  wildfire that was approximately 6.65 acres in  size located along West River Road near Palatka. Time of event was based on lightning strike data.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few severe thunderstorms produced large hail across the Concho Valley and Northern Edwards Plateau. Also, a lightning strike destroyed a hotel in Brady.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A lightning strike started a fire at a hotel in Brady. The Texas State Fire Marshal has ruled the building a total loss due to the extensive fire, smoke, and water damage.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Scattered thunderstorms occurred ahead of a frontal boundary on May 23-25. However, on May 25, a mesoscale convective system developed west of the area and enhanced the low level wind field.  This resulted in two tornadoes across the tri-state area. One tornado affected the Villa Tasso area in Walton county in Florida, and the other tornado affected Houston and Henry counties in Alabama.  Both tornadoes were rated EF1.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Franklin County dispatch and the local fire dept reported fried wiring, phone lines down, and compromised security gate at a home from a likely lightning strike at the St George Island Plantation around Hawthorne.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Franklin County dispatch and the local fire dept confirmed a palmetto that caught fire at the Gramercy Plantation from a likely lightning strike.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Lightning hit a fisherman that was standing under a pine tree.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A nineteen-year-old male survived a lightning strike while fishing with his mother at the Bevilport boat ramp on the Angelina River. Lightning hit a nearby pine tree he stood under, throwing him several feet away, destroying his fishing rod, and leaving him briefly unconscious before he was treated at Christus Jasper Memorial Hospital. He returned to fish at the same spot the next day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A broken line of thunderstorms associated with an upper trough and Pacific cold front pushed through North and Central Texas on February 14. Storms were mostly below severe thresholds, but a few became strong enough to produce wind damage and isolated instances of flash flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Videos and articles from social and news media reported that a wind turbine south of Caddo was struck by lightning the morning of February 14th and caught on fire as a result. As per pictures, the shell at the top of the turbine was destroyed along with one of the blades.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fast-moving quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) swept across portions of central, southern and eastern Oklahoma on the morning of the 8th. This convective system was tied to the passage of a compact upper wave across the region, resulting in very strong wind fields within a weakly unstable boundary layer. In addition to sporadic pockets of thunderstorm wind damage, and generally sub-severe hail, a few tornadoes occurred in a corridor from near Purcell, OK to Shawnee, OK.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A suspected lightning strike caused a tree to fall onto a car, just north of the Broadway and Covell Road intersection. An occupant in the vehicle was injured. The event location is approximate.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A front brough a messy line of convection to western and central Massachusetts Tuesday evening which caused some limited wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: In Gill, lightning struck a tree which downed powerlines on Main Rd.
